Overall, our calculations suggest that the covalent 2A − g state lies below the ionic 1B + u at the Franck-Condon point. Our analysis provides general insight into the electronic structure of xanthophylls, including the interplay between covalent and ionic configurations induced by structural distortions and environmental effects. The MPD framework enables a direct comparison of state character, highlighting the similarities between methods and clarifying the origin of remaining differences. This work establishes a consistent framework for understanding xanthophyll photophysics, and offers practical guidance for modeling their excited states with cost-effective methods.

papers.title: Copper-Catalyzed, Photoinduced Carbonylative Cross-Coupling of Alkyl Iodides with Amines, Alcohols and Water.
papers.abstract: A general photoinduced copper-catalyzed carbonylative cross-coupling of alkyl iodides with amines for the synthesis of amides under mild conditions is reported. Using a readily accessible, inexpensive copper complex, [Cu(bcp)DPEphos]PF 6 , the reaction proceeds at room temperature and accommodates a broad range of amines, delivering the corresponding amides in good to excellent yields. Notably, the transformation can also be performed - for the first time - under ambient carbon monoxide pressure, enhancing its practicality. The procedure also extends to hydrazines, alcohols, and water, enabling an efficient and divergent access to hydrazides, esters, and carboxylic acids and providing a versatile and sustainable approach to the catalytic carbonylative functionalization of alkyl electrophiles.

papers.title: Container material and matrix effects on the adsorption and recovery of longchain perfluoroalkyl acids: a case study of PFTeA
papers.abstract: Per-and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) adsorb to laboratory containers, potentially causing significant under-reporting of solution concentrations. While adsorption has been examined for shorter-chain PFAS, far less attention has been given to longer-chain species, which are expected to adhere more strongly. This study focuses on the adsorption of the C14 compound perfluorotetradecanoic acid (PFTeA) on different container materials in aqueous solutions with varying salinity, evaluates both storage solvent composition (water vs. water-acetonitrile mixtures) and solvent-assisted desorption (acetonitrile vs. methanol). Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA, C8) is included for comparison. Adsorption losses were quantified by electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS), with an internal standard added post-sampling to assess instrument response. PFTeA showed the greatest adsorption to plastics (HDPE), followed by stainless steel, with adsorption lowest on borosilicate glass and aluminum. In saline media, PFTeA adsorption on containers was delayed within the first 24 hours. Acetonitrile was markedly more effective than methanol at recovering adsorbed PFTeA. These results highlight the elevated adsorption risk posed by long-chain PFAS, particularly in plastic containers, and provide guidance for improving PFAS quantification, degradation studies, and sample storage and handling protocols. Relative PFTeA remaining in solution after storage over 7 days (C/C₀), demonstrating strong adsorption to HDPE and less adsorption to aluminum.

papers.title: Direct Anodic Decarboxylative Alkylation Reaction to Pharmaceutically Relevant Quinones
papers.abstract: We established an electrochemical platform for the direct decarboxylative coupling of various carboxylic acids with para -quinones. This single-step approach rapidly constructs complex molecular architectures without pre-functionalization and offers a handle for accessing drug-like scaffolds. By generating radicals via direct anodic oxidation of carboxylic acids, this approach expands the synthetic toolbox for electrochemical sp 3 –sp 2 decarboxylative couplings. The method demonstrates excellent functional group tolerance across diverse carboxylic acids, including both aromatic and aliphatic substrates. Furthermore, it enables synthesis of various antimalarial scaffolds and pharmaceutical precursors for east coast fever treatment. The method was successfully scaled up 16-fold, confirming its robustness. This electrochemical approach preserves halide moieties such as bromide on the para -quinone core and therefore allows further modification of the derived product, demonstrating the formation of a platform compound. The protocol further enables transfer of fully deuterated methyl groups from acetic acid- d 4 to pharmaceutically relevant target molecules while preserving the deuterium content without the use of hazardous methyl group transfer agents. A selectively deuterated antimalarial lead structure was synthesized successfully in two electrochemical steps from readily available starting materials.

papers.title: Structure-Induced Optical Function from Molecular Organization in Imine-Based Crystals
papers.abstract: text. Molecular science has traditionally advanced optoelectronic materials through single-molecule structure–property relationships. However, in organic optoelectronics, device performance is largely governed by solid-state aggregation and molecular packing. This shift highlights the need to resolve structure–property relationships at the supramolecular scale, where material functionality emerges from intermolecular interactions, spatial organization, and aggregate geometry. Here, experimental characterization combined with computational studies is used to investigate how molecular structure controls aggregation, packing, and the resulting optical properties of (E)-N,1-bis(4-(phenylethynyl)phenyl)methanimine derivatives. While molecular substitution induces only minor changes in optical properties in dilute solution, aggregation and especially solid-state lead to pronounced differences across the derivatives, including the formation of distinct polymorphic structures with markedly different emissive responses. These results demonstrate how crystal packing modulates excitonic coupling and enables organic optical waveguiding, highlighting the potential of these materials for crystalline organic photonic architectures and underscoring the importance of aggregation and packing in the design of organic photonic materials. Such insights provide a framework for rationally engineering solid-state order to achieve predictable and tunable photonic functionality in advanced optoelectronic systems.

papers.title: The Ballad of LLM Agents: Philosophical Reasoning for Chemistry
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show remarkable potential for scientific reasoning but often produce unreliable or scientifically unactionable outputs when faced with multi-step logic, domain grounding, and interpretability challenges, especially in complex fields like chemistry and materials science. Here, we introduce a framework of philosophical reasoning agents, inspired by canonical thinkers such as Socrates, Descartes, Kant, and Hume, to guide LLM behavior via structured prompt engineering. These agents embody distinct reasoning paradigms,(dialectical inquiry, deductive logic, rule-based judgment, and empirical validation),and are evaluated across multiple chemistry subdomains (such as physical, organic, and general chemistry) using the ChemBench benchmark. Our agentic prompting approach yields substantial accuracy gains on open-ended numerical chemistry questions, with up to +18.4% for GPT-4o using the Hume agent, +14.1% for GPT-5 with Kant, and +11.7% for GPT-5.1 with Descartes, relative to zero-shot baselines. Beyond accuracy, we reveal distinct “reasoning signatures” across models, reflecting latent epistemic biases in how LLMs approach scientific problem solving. These findings demonstrate that embedding philosophy-of-science principles into multi-agent frameworks can improve and produce interpretable, adaptive, and domain-aligned scientific LLMs.

papers.title: Do humans and large language models agree on the quality of synthesis plans?
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have seen a widespread adoption in all spheres of science including chemistry and cheminformatics. Nevertheless, our knowledge of how they operate is limited, giving rise to exploration of their capabilities in different areas of science and different operation modes. Here, we investigated whether LLMs could mimic human experts on the challenging task of assessing retrosynthetic path feasibility in routes generated by a popular computer-aided synthesis planning tool (AiZynthFinder). We evaluated the agreement between LLMs and expert chemists on holistic evaluations of the proposed routes as well as the individual chemical reactions in them. We used four frontier LLMs (Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-4.1, GPT-o3, and Gemini 2.5 Pro) and employed 17 expert chemists to grade 50 retrosynthetic paths. We found out that when instructed with clear possible categories for the evaluation of a given reaction in a retrosynthetic tree, human experts tend to converge in their opinions. Another important finding was that Gemini 2.5 Pro performs remarkably well out of all the LLMs explored, GPT-o3 tends to be more pessimistic, and Claude and GPT-4.1 tend to be overly optimistic when compared to the majority vote of human experts.

papers.title: How Fe(II)/2-Oxoglutarate Oxygenase Chooses Chlorination Over Hydroxylation: Electric Field-Driven Ligand Exchange Governs C–Cl Formation
papers.abstract: Non-heme Fe(II)/2-Oxoglutarate (2OG) dependent halogenases catalyze highly selective C-H halogenation. BesD is a non-heme Fe(II)/2OG halogenase that performs regio- and stereoselective chlorination of L-lysine (L-Lys) substrate. Understanding the mechanism by which halogenation is favored over canonical hydroxylation is essential for guiding enzyme engineering efforts aimed at converting hydroxylases into halogenases. Here, we combine molecular dynamics (MD) and hybrid quantum mechanics / molecular mechanics (QM/MM) calculations to elucidate the origin of chlorination selectivity in BesD and variants derived from a homologous hydroxylase. Our results indicate that, although the initial inline Cl-Fe(III)-OH intermediate is inherently predisposed toward hydroxylation, it undergoes a two-step isomerization in which the -Cl and -OH ligands exchange coordination positions. This rearrangement positions the chloride ligand trans to H207, where the protein’s intrinsic electric field (IEF) enhances Fe-Cl bond polarization and promotes C-Cl bond formation, ultimately enabling the selective chlorination of L-Lys. Comparative analysis of the homologous hydroxylase and two halogenation-competent variants (Hydrox-3R and Chimera14) reveals halogenase-specific correlated motions between substituted second coordination sphere, long-range residues with the active-site, particularly the coordinated succinate, and the substrate. Notably, these collective motions mirror those observed in the native halogenase BesD. Furthermore, the Hydrox-3R and Chimera14 variants employ a two-step isomerization strategy analogous to that of BesD, enabling efficient chlorination through IEF alignment along the Fe-Cl bond. These results highlight the critical roles of collective correlated motions, the second coordination sphere, and long-range interactions, as well as enzyme-generated electric fields, in determining halogenation selectivity in non-heme Fe(II)/2OG-dependent oxygenases. Ultimately, halogenation is achieved not due to a new catalytic mechanism, but rather due to subtle electronic, geometric, and dynamic perturbations of a hydroxylase scaffold. These insights provide a mechanistic framework for engineering hydroxylases into halogenases with enhanced activity.

papers.title: Catalytic Turnover by Matrix Metalloproteinase-1: Sequential Collagen L-Chain Release, Active-Site Regeneration, and M-Chain Insertion Governed by Intrinsic Electric Fields and Conformational Dynamics
papers.abstract: Matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) are Zn(II)-dependent endopeptidases central to extracellular matrix remodeling and are therapeutic targets in cancer and arthritis. While the peptide-bond hydrolysis mechanism of MMPs is established, the subsequent catalytic steps governing product release and active-site regeneration, which regulate catalytic turnover, remain poorly understood. Here, we combine molecular dynamics (MD), well-tempered metadynamics (MetD), and hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations on the full MMP-1–triple-helical peptide (THP) complex to elucidate the mechanism of product release and collagen middle (M)-chain insertion, key steps in catalytic turnover. Our results show that intrinsic electric fields (IEFs) drive reaction-pathway selectivity for Zn(II)-coordinated carboxylate product dissociation, where the field projected along the Zn→COO⁻ axis stabilizes transition-state charge separation, lowering the ligand-exchange barrier for the two-water pathway and favoring formation of a five-coordinate (5C) Zn cat (II) state over the higher-energy single-water pathway leading to a four-coordinate (4C) state. Interdomain flexibility and loop motions promote solvent influx, enabling further product release. As the leading (L)-chain fragments dissociate, interactions redistribute to the M and trailing (T) chains, and Zn cat (II) relaxes from 5C to 4C. Insertion of the M-chain scissile bond becomes favorable only after L-chain displacement, establishing a sequential release–insertion mechanism. M-chain scissile carbonyl coordination proceeds with a lower barrier than the L-chain, as weaker IEFs stabilize C=O polarization, and thereby favor Zn cat (II) coordination. These findings highlight how IEFs, in concert with Zn cat (II) coordination changes, second-sphere interactions, and protein motions, regulate catalytic turnover in MMP-1, with implications for metalloprotease engineering and selective inhibitor design.

papers.title: ChemVLMate: a multimodal, dual-arm, seeing robotic chemist for adaptive synthesis
papers.abstract: Chemical synthesis is a dynamic process. Chemists rely on a perception-reasoning-manipulation loop to interpret evolving experimental environments and states and adapt operations real-time. Yet most robotic chemistry platforms remain perception-blind, executing static scripts that assume nominal behaviours and fixed environments. Here we introduce ChemVLMate, a multimodal dualarm robotic chemist that closes the perception–reasoning–manipulation loop by grounding decision making in real-time vision. An open-vocabulary vision–language model converts an overhead image into a structured semantic observation of tools, reagents and instrument readouts; a language-model policy selects the next parameterized laboratory action from a constrained API; and coordinated bimanual manipulation executes it with force-aware control. Across diverse bench chemistry tasks, ChemVLMate autonomously performs solution preparation, precision weighing, hydrogel synthesis and colouring, and room-temperature crystallizations, adapting online under partial observability. Integrated within a self-driving laboratory, it completes an end-to-end synthesis-to-X-ray diffraction characterization workflow. ChemVLMate provides a general framework for reliable, visually grounded laboratory autonomy and adaptive synthesis.

papers.title: Advancing the CL&Pol Polarizable Force Field for Accurate Modeling of Mg2+, Ca2+ and Zn2+ Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Divalent cations such as Mg2+, Ca2+ or Zn2+ are promising candidates for powerful and affordable post-Li batteries due to their high natural abundance and an expected two-electron transfer per charge carrier. But an accurate representation of divalent cations in electrolytes by molecular dynamics simulations remains challenging due to effects of their high charge density. For ionic systems such as the ones studied here, a molecular interaction model with explicit polarization terms, using Drude induced dipoles, largely improves the representation of equilibrium and transport properties when compared to fixed-charge models. Some issues regarding over-polarization of the induced dipoles require attention. Thole and Tang-Toennies screening (or damping) functions are parameterized to avoid the over-polarization effects, and were validated by simulating MgCl2, CaCl2 and ZnCl2 salts in aqueous solutions. Followingly this, simulations with model electrolytes based on two commonly used solvents — dimethoxyethane (G1) and ethylene carbonate (EC) — were performed. The simulations of the G1 and EC electrolytes highlight significant differences in structural and dynamic behaviors between Ca2+, Mg2+, and Zn2+, depending on the scaling of the Lennard-Jones well-depth, which is performed when adding explicit induced dipoles to a non-polarizable force field. The study of the impact of this scaling, investigated for both systems G1 and EC, provides a framework for future simulations involving divalent cations with the CL&Pol force field. These results, coupled with the transferability of the CL&Pol model, offer an efficient tool to simulate a broad range of systems involving divalent ions, from biological media to electrolytes for novel energy storage devices.

papers.title: Direct evidence of a lanthanide-tellurium bond in [K(18-crown 6)(Cp′′2LnTe3)] with Ln = La, Ce, and Nd
papers.abstract: Using non-classical divalent lanthanide precursors as multi-electron reducing agents, complexes, [K(18-crown-6)(Cp” 2 LnTe 3 )], with Ln = La, Ce, and Nd, Cp” = 1,3-bis-(trimethylsilyl)cyclopentadienyl, were synthesized and investigated to elucidate the mechanism of lanthanide-tellurium bonding and the role of 4 f -element electron density in stabilizing small chalcogenide chains. Density-Functional Theory (DFT) reveals that the frontier molecular orbitals of these complexes are predominantly localized on the [Te 3 ] 2- fragment, while the trivalent lanthanide ions stabilize the tellurium chain through weak but measurable metal-ligand interactions. To experimentally resolve these interactions, we focus on complementary ligand- and metal-centered X-ray spectroscopic approaches. Ln L 3 -edge high-resolution XANES (HR-XANES) and valence-band resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (VB-RIXS) demonstrate that the Ln-Te/C interaction has substantial Ln 5 d orbitals contribution, particularly for the Ln-Te bond, and remains largely constant across the three complexes. DFT-based bond analysis provides a mechanistic interpretation of these trends. The Ln–C interaction exhibits increasing electron density at the bond critical point and a higher delocalization index (QTAIM analysis) from the lighter to the heavier lanthanides, reflecting enhanced Ln 4 f participation within an energy-driven covalency regime. The Ln–Te interaction is predominantly electrostatic, with meaningful orbital contributions arising mainly from Ln 5 d participation within an orbital-overlap driven covalency regime. These results demonstrate that the Ln-C and Ln-Te bonding in the present complexes follow fundamentally distinct covalency mechanisms, which together enable the stabilization and isolation of the small [Te 3 ] 2- fragment chain.

papers.title: The synergistic effects of aqueous solution, temperature, and mutagenesis on Syntaxin-1a-Munc-18a complex formation
papers.abstract: In the nervous system vesicular fusion is a physiological event regulated by several proteins, particularly Syntaxin-1a and Munc-18a. Although these proteins are known to form the molecular assembly, affording the neurotransmitter release, the synergistic effect of ions, temperature, and mutagenesis on its interaction remain a conundrum. To remedy this, we characterized the energetic properties of both wild-type and mutant Munc-18a, when they form a complex with Syntaxin1a within an artificial aqueous solution mimicking the cytosolic conditions. Applying molecular dynamics simulations at three temperatures (room, physiological, and febrile), we assessed ionic influences on the complexes given by the interaction energies. Our results demonstrate strong coupling between calcium and hydrogen ions in the wild-type complexes, which suggests a novel ionic role influencing the Syntaxin1a-Munc-18a interplay. Furthermore, in the mutant complex, distinct ionic interactions were observed between Syntaxin-1a and ions. In fact, beyond the strong energetic interplay with hydrogen ions, weaker, but still significant interaction was documented with potassium, sodium, and chloride as well. Moreover, the results also clearly show how the mutation changes the binding energy of the complexes as a function of temperature. Last, but not least, the structural analyses revealed greater separation between domains 3a and 1 of Munc-18a in the mutant compared to wild-type across all temperatures. Based on these results we discuss a biophysical substrate in the context of vesicular fusion.

papers.title: Comparing numerical treatments for drug classification using IR spectra
papers.abstract: In this article, we investigate the numerical relationships between illicit drugs based on IR spectra from a publicly available library. Classification models were trained to test how well single component drugs can be classified using their IR spectra alone. Two challenges were considered: classifying spectra representing various amphetamine, fentanyl, and cocaine compounds, and classifying spectra specifically of fentanyl analogs. All spectra were sourced from the most recent version of the SWGDRUG IR library (Version 3.1). Multiple classification models with varied parameters were created for each task. The models for challenge 1 performed very well, with several models having a median reported accuracy of 100% The models did not perform well with the appreciably more difficult challenge 2, with median classification accuracies ranging between 50% and 75%. Our results demonstrate the appropriateness of classifying drugs based on IR spectra at the major class level, while confirming the limitation of trying to use IR spectroscopy for analog level discrimination. Efforts to determine the “bounds” of drug classification using IR spectra is on-going in our lab. All source code used to generate the results presented in this article are available at https://github.com/Brandon12G/GiotisNumericalTreatments.

papers.title: Fluctuation-driven chemistry at aqueous interfaces and beyond
papers.abstract: Interfacial electric fields at gas–water, oil–water, and solid–water boundaries are frequently invoked to explain radical formation under ambient conditions. Field strengths of 10 7 –10 9 V m⁻ 1 are often cited as sufficient for this purpose. Yet the electrostatic work accessible from such fields over molecular distances is orders of magnitude smaller than the energies required for homolytic bond dissociation or one-electron ionization. This discrepancy raises the question of whether interfacial electric fields directly drive chemistry or modulate an intrinsic mechanism of liquid water. We argue that equilibrium interfacial electric fields bias molecular orientation and reaction kinetics but do not constitute a primary energetic input for bond-breaking chemistry. Instead, we propose a fluctuation-driven model in which transient, partially charge-separated configurations (H 2 O⁺ δ ···H 2 O⁻ δ ) arise from cooperative hydrogen-bond fluctuations, which can be kinetically trapped by solutes (e.g., H + , DMPO, crown ethers, or catalytic surfaces) to yield measurable radical products. In this picture, interfaces, ions, and weak perturbations reshape the free-energy landscape and alter fluctuation statistics.

papers.title: Atomic Periodicity as Spectral Structure
papers.abstract: The periodic system was established from trends in atomic weight and chemical behavior and later explained through electronic structure models, but it has not been derived directly from atomic observables without prior chemical or theoretical knowledge. Here we show that atomic spectra alone encode the full organization of the periodic table. Frequency-domain analysis reveals that elements occupy a bounded spectral space governed by hierarchical scaling between K-edge (𝜈 𝑚𝑎𝑥 ) and first ionization frequencies. Elements organize into spectral bands (periods) and parallel trajectories (groups). Periodic differentiation emerges from bifurcation of spectral modes, and periodic bandwidth (Δ 𝑝 ) contracts following Δ 𝑝 ∝ 𝜈 𝑚𝑎𝑥 −1.19 (R 2 = 0.9995), establishing a fundamental limit on elemental differentiation. Substituting atomic number for K-edge does not reproduce this organization, indicating that the spectral domain represents the natural scaling coordinate for periodic structure. This two-parameter framework provides an empirical resolution to longstanding classification questions and enables prediction using spectral scaling relations. Leave-one-out cross-validation yields median prediction errors of 1.1% for measured first ionization frequencies and 2.1% for covalent radii, with lanthanide-series prediction errors below 0.3%. Extending these predictions to atoms with experimentally unknown properties yields new K-edge frequencies and covalent radii for actinium and lawrencium, and ionization frequency for praseodymium, while predicting superconducting behavior for Chromium and Silver.

papers.title: Investigating CO electrolysis on cobalt at elevated temperatures to produce C4+ hydrocarbons
papers.abstract: CO2 electrolysis has emerged as a promising route to carbon-neutral fuels, but Cu-based catalysts are largely limited to producing short-chain (< C3) products. In contrast, strong *CO-binding metals that underpin thermochemical Fischer-Tropsch (FT) catalysis remain largely unexplored under electrochemical conditions. Here, we investigate Co catalyst for producing C4+ hydrocarbons in membrane electrode assembly (MEA) reactors operated at elevated temperatures (30-80 °C) and industrially relevant current densities. At 80 °C and 250 mA/cm 2 , Co produces a complex spectrum of 28 distinct C₁-C₆+ products, with hydrocarbon partial current densities increasing linearly with temperature. Density functional theory calculations reveal that direct *CO dissociation on Co remains kinetically inaccessible under these reaction conditions, pointing instead to protonation-mediated pathways in CC bond formation. Strong adsorption of unsaturated hydrocarbons leads to surface coking and progressive deactivation, which is mitigated through pulsed electrolysis. Unlike Cu, the activity and selectivity trends on Co are only weakly dependent on alkali-metal cation identity, highlighting a mechanistic regime more closely analogous to FT catalysis than to classical *CO-*CO dimerization. Together, these findings establish Co as a prototype strong *CO-binding catalyst for electrochemical long-chain hydrocarbon synthesis and provide mechanistic design principles for developing high-temperature electrochemical routes to sustainable, naphtha-range fuels.

papers.title: AI-Driven Electrocatalysis: Adaptive Control of the Glycerol Oxidation Reaction via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: In this work, we present the full development process of a reinforcement-learning-based controller deployed in a closed-loop experimental setup to optimize the glycerol electrooxidation reaction. The conversion of glycerol to valuable products on platinum has attracted attention as a substitute for the oxygen evolution reaction in hydrogen-producing electrolyzers, motivated by the availability of glycerol as an inexpensive byproduct of biodiesel production. However, the glycerol oxidation reaction is known to poison platinum requiring an intelligent operation procedure to sustain high conversion rates. The employed AI controller autonomously discovered a non-periodic pulsing strategy, which achieved on average a 30% higher charge transfer rate over the human-engineered pulsing protocol. In addition, we analyzed its decision making using first-order Markov-chain modelling. This analysis revealed that the AI employs two distinct surface reactivation procedures: most of the time it uses a short cycle, pulsing from the glycerol-oxidation potential to a relaxation potential of 0.3 V vs. RHE, while it periodically performs a longer cycle by pulsing first to 1.0 V vs. RHE and then to 0.3 V vs. RHE to revitalize the system. To further support these findings, we developed an interpretable physics-inspired AI model that simulates surface dynamics during glycerol oxidation and captures the evolving distribution of active and poisoned sites. Although demonstrated for glycerol oxidation, both the AI-control framework and the physics-inspired AI model are broadly applicable to other electrochemical systems, offering a general pathway for integrating AI methods into experimental electrocatalytic research.

papers.title: Upconverted Nanoparticle for 2D Nano-mapping of Excitation Energy Transfer in Conjugated Polymer
papers.abstract: Real-space evaluation of exciton migration in nano-domain potentially provides significant information in advanced material design; that is however still challenging as optical excitation and detection are diffraction limited to submicrometer resolutions. To achieve the real-space evaluation, we utilized rare-earth upconverting nanoparticles with thulium ions as emitters (TmUCNP) for nanometric photoexcitation of conducting polymer, MEH-PPV. The TmUCNPs in MEH-PPV solid were photoexcited with a near-infrared laser. The visible emission of the Tm ions allowed for the production of excited states of the MEH-PPV through excitation energy transfer. The emission of MEH-PPV spectrally separatable from Tm ions permitted individual imaging of their emission spots and single-particle emission dynamics measurement. The luminescence images of the TmUCNPs and MEH-PPV film, analyzed using the localization method, provided 2D nanoscale distributions of the emissive trap sites in the MEH-PPV surrounding the TmUCNPs. From the 2D map of the emissive sites, we determined the length of EET in the MEH-PPV solid to be < 40 nm.

papers.title: On the Role of Hydroxide Ions as the Mediators of Cathodic Cu Corrosion
papers.abstract: Understanding changes and degradation of the copper cathode during the electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO2RR) is a fundamental challenge. Advances in operando experimental methods and computational tools have shed light on the degradation mechanisms. However, the role of the hydroxide ions formed from the alkaline Volmer reaction remains under-studied. Here we report a computational investigation of Cu(OH) n adatom complexes that can form on a roughened surface as possible intermediates that can lead to cathodic copper corrosion. Series of constant-potential density functional theory calculations are utilized to compute the voltage-dependent free energy surfaces of Cu(OH) n electrodissolution from adatom defects on a Cu(100) surface. The results show that the dissolution of a Cu(OH) adatom complex is endergonic by ∼ 1 eV at an electrode bias of −1.59 V vs. the Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE) and thus quite unfavorable. In contrast, the dissolution of [Cu(OH) 2 ] - at the same bias only requires ~ 0.2 eV. The Cu oxidation states of both complexes are +1 regardless of the applied potential. The atomic partial charges and their change show that two hydroxides of surface-bound *Cu(OH) 2 induce an image quadrupole which allows facile dissociation. Pathways to form these two complexes are analyzed using transition state calculations evaluated at constant potential. The presence of oxygen adatoms, for example from subsurface oxygen, is identified to facilitate the formation of Cu(OH) n via dissociative chemisorption of water. Including both pathways to form Cu(OH) n with and without subsurface oxygens, the stochastic simulation model predicts approximately 6 monolayers per hour of Cu loss through Cu(OH) n formation. The results show that hydroxide-ion mediated cathodic Cu dissolution is viable. Remaining questions and further work that could validate the proposed mechanism are discussed.

papers.title: Investigation of Ligand-to-Ligand Charge-Transfer in Heteroleptic Zinc(II) 4'-Substituted 2,2':6',2''-Terpyridine Complexes
papers.abstract: Molecular photosensitizers can use a donor-chromophore-acceptor architecture to achieve long-lived charge separated states that may more efficiently initiate the single electron transfer processes involved in photocatalysis or photovoltaic devices. These photosensitizers are typically metal complexes wherein the dominant lowest energy photon-absorbing state is a metal-to-ligand charge-transfer, having molar absorptivities on the order of 10 4 cm -1 M -1 , and charge separation is achieved through careful redox leveling of ancillary electron donating and accepting groups. Taking advantage of direct ligand-to-ligand charge-transfer states introduces new excited state pathways that can also lead to charge separated states. In this work, we present a series of heteroleptic zinc(II) 2,2':6',2''-terpyridine photosensitizers containing a pendant pyridyl group and carbazole or diphenylamine electron donating groups capable of undergoing direct ligand-to-ligand charge-transfer with up to 42% photoluminescence quantum yields in solution or solid state, and up to 86% when arrested in a polymer matrix due to overcoming aggregation induced quenching effects.

papers.title: A Correlative Microscopy Dataset for Multimodal Data Fusion and Image Matching in Materials Science
papers.abstract: Gaining understanding of process-structure-property relationships in materials at a mechanistic level relies on correlative microscopy workflows. These workflows, in turn, fundamentally depend on image matching, i.e., a computer vision task with the objective of finding point correspondences in pairs of images. Matching models are difficult to evaluate quantitatively in the materials field due to a shortage of representative benchmark datasets. Nonetheless, prior research indicates that traditional rule-based image matching techniques such as the surface-invariant feature transform currently fall short on such matching tasks. We present a dataset for cross-modal image matching and data fusion in the materials microscopy domain, which we coin AmalgaMatch, to support model benchmarking and fine-tuning efforts. All images are micrographs captured using the most widely applied imaging techniques in materials science including light-optical, scanning electron, and transmission electron microscopy, as well as electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD). Therein, various detectors and imaging modes are employed to capture micrographs of diverse materials. While the majority of images are raw images, some underwent typical processing routes using digital image correlation or EBSD indexing. Common regions in image pairs are populated with hand-annotated keypoint correspondences. While mutual information is limited in cross-modal, multi-scale image pairs, we relied on characteristic defects such as dislocations, grain boundaries, triple junctions, inclusions, pores or topographic features for annotation. Furthermore, the dataset is divided into groups, defined by distinct registration use cases, and further into subsets, defined by the imaged material. The dataset covers many typical use cases for image matching in materials science, including slip partitioning, dislocation characterization, and surface fractography. In total, it comprises 6 groups and 19 subsets with 35 scenes and 187 annotated image pairs to support autonomous multi-modal materials data fusion. For each image, we provide structured metadata to facilitate training of hybrid matching models which process textual alongside image-based inputs to improve the matching quality and robustness. A formal ontological model for correlative microscopy and image matching processes is proposed to express image contents, relationships, and transformations through knowledge graphs and to enable aligning with FAIR data principles.

papers.title: Quantum-Accurate Enhanced Sampling and Mini-Protein Folding through Replica Exchange for Multiscale Neural Network Potentials
papers.abstract: Neural network potentials (NNPs) have emerged as efficient alternatives to computationally demanding quantum-mechanical (QM) methods. AMPv3-BMS25 (short AMP-BMS) is an equivariant NNP designed for multiscale ML/MM simulations that captures directional and long-range interactions. In classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, enhanced-sampling techniques are applied to cross large energy barriers and improve convergence. Among those, replica exchange with solute scaling (REST2) is an efficient method that selectively scales solute interactions while keeping the bath temperature fixed, thereby reducing the number of replicas required. Here, we present a REST2-like algorithm compatible with multiscale ML/MM simulations. This algorithm is combined with AMP-BMS by exploiting the simple separability of its Hamiltonian into solute–solute, solute–solvent, and solvent–solvent contributions. We validate the REST2–AMP approach on several peptidic systems in explicit solvent and demonstrate folding of the mini-proteins chignolin and CLN025 from extended conformations. Thus, our REST2 approach for ML/MM enables access to biologically relevant timescales while maintaining near-DFT accuracy.

papers.title: Scalable and Generalizable Analog Design via Learning Medicinal Chemistry Intuition from Matched Molecular Pair Transformations
papers.abstract: Chemical analog design in the hit-to-lead and lead optimization stages of drug discovery relies on systematic structural modifications often guided by medicinal chemistry intuition. Although a matched molecular pair (MMP) provides an interpretable framework to capture the intuition, models trained on individual MMP instances face significant limitations, such as bias toward frequent transformations in historical data. This work introduces a novel approach to transform the concept of ”how to design chemical analogs like a medicinal chemist” into a primary training objective for generative models by focusing on matched molecular pair transformations (MMPTs) as the fundamental unit of chemical modifications. This allows for a more generalizable and context-independent representation of medicinal chemistry intuition, enabling the application of the same transformation priors across different projects, regardless of the target or indication. Using a consistently curated ChEMBL-derived dataset, we compared a transformationcentric foundation model (MMPT-FM) with multiple MMP-based generative formulations trained on the same underlying data. Furthermore, performance is assessed through challenging within-patent and cross-patent real-world test cases derived from drug discovery patents. The MMPT-FM model achieves comparable or improved recall and novel metrics across all test cases, demonstrating particularly strong performance for low-frequency and previously unseen transformations This work not only shifts the paradigm of learning and utilizes medicinal chemistry intuition in an efficient and scalable manner in the AI for drug discovery era, but also establishes a significant competitive advantage by enabling the drug discover industry to encode decades of collective medicinal chemistry knowledge—both public and proprietary—into a scalable foundation generative model that could help researchers design chemical analogs.

papers.title: A novel and comprehensive CH4/NH3/H2 mechanism incorporating new physics
papers.abstract: Ammonia is a promising carbon-free energy carrier; however, its low reactivity and strong tendency to form nitrogen oxides remain major challenges for practical combustion applications. Blending ammonia with hydrogen and/or methane is one strategy to facilitate ammonia combustion, but this changes the radical pool and introduces cross chemistry that is not fully understood. Thus, it remains unclear how different fuel blends promote or suppress the formation of pollutants such as NOx and N2O. In this work, we expand our recently developed NH3/H2 mechanism to model NH3/H2/CH4 blends using an automated reaction-mechanism generator. For many important reactions, kinetic and thermochemical parameters are sourced from existing libraries, whereas rate rules and groupadditivity rules are applied when no data are available. To treat the composition dependence of key reactions, the linear-mixture rule in reduced pressure (Burke rule) is applied. Importantly, no kinetic and thermochemical parameters are tuned to reproduce specific modeling targets. The mechanisms are validated against laminarburning velocities and species profiles from jet-stirred and flow reactors across binary and ternary fuel blends, and good agreement with experiment is observed. Reaction-path and rate-of-production analyses reveal that blending H2 or CH4 enhances fuel-driven NOx formation primarily by increasing H, O, and OH concentrations rather than introducing new NOx-forming reaction pathways. We present a detailed analysis in which we demonstrate how different ternary blends affect NOx emissions.

papers.title: Programmable Uniform Gel Networks Amplify Weak Interactions via Multiple Anchoring for In Situ Growth of Gold Nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Synthesizing ultrasmall thermoresponsive nanoparticles within poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPA) hydrogels without the use of strong ligands remains challenging, as intrinsically weak interfacial interactions and structural heterogeneity in conventional networks often lead to poor size control and aggregation. Here, we report a programmable PNIPA-based hydrogel constructed from star-shaped polymers via living radical polymerization, in which a homogeneous network containing locally reinforced crosslinking domains enables ligand-free in situ formation of ultrasmall metal nanoparticles. The uniform network provides a spatially consistent reaction environment, allowing synchronized and controllable particle growth across length scales. Nanoparticle size is governed by network architecture rather than by synthetic conditions, and the resulting hydrogel composites exhibit exceptional stability under thermal cycling and harsh chemical environments, despite relying solely on amide functionalities. Stabilization does not arise from rigid immobilization or strong ligand coordination along the polymer chains; instead, it emerges from the collective engagement of multiple spatially distributed, amide-enriched crosslinking domains. These reinforced domains generate a cooperative multiple-anchoring effect, creating a soft yet adaptive chelation-like confinement. This work establishes a versatile platform for strong-ligand-free yet robust and controllable nanoparticle synthesis, extendable to colloidal dispersions, diverse polymer matrices, and various metal nanoparticles.

papers.title: Topological Decoupling of Mechanical Robustness and Hydration Dynamics in Biocompatible Polymer Networks
papers.abstract: Poly(2-methoxyethyl acrylate) (PMEA) is widely recognized as a polymer exhibiting excellent biocompatibility. However, because PMEA behaves as a viscous liquid at room and physiological temperatures, its practical use has been largely limited to coating materials. Polymerizing its monomer, 2-methoxyethyl acrylate (MEA), with crosslinkers via conventional free-radical polymerization can produce free-standing polymer network films suitable for biomaterials. Yet, the resulting networks are topologically disordered and mechanically fragile. Increasing the crosslinker concentration improves stiffness but simultaneously reduces the amount of “intermediate water”—a key factor governing the biocompatibility of PMEA—and raises the glass transition temperature, ultimately compromising biological performance. Here we show that these limitations can be overcome through topological design of the polymer network. By synthesizing MEA-based star polymers via living radical polymerization and subsequently connecting their chain ends with a common crosslinker, topology-defined and highly ordered networks can be constructed. These networks exhibit mechanical properties approaching theoretical limits while maintaining hydration structures and glass transition temperatures favorable for biocompatible materials. These results demonstrate that controlling network topology enables decoupling of mechanical performance from hydration structure, even with identical monomers and crosslinkers, providing a general design strategy for high-performance biomaterials.

papers.title: Thickness-dependent Chromatic Inversion via Absorption–Bragg Competition in Hybrid Photonic Films
papers.abstract: In nature, structural and pigmentary colors frequently coexist to produce vivid complementary contrasts without compromising saturation. Inspired by this biological strategy, we demonstrate a "programmable transition of color dominance" in photonic crystal films formed by the self-assembly of monodisperse polystyrene microspheres containing internal pigments. When designing a film exhibiting blue Bragg reflection using particles with yellow pigments, we observed a sharp visual transition from pigment-dominant yellow to structure-dominant blue as thickness increased. Remarkably, this transition bypassed achromatic phases despite the complementary colors. We elucidated that this discontinuous hue switching stems from "spectral competition" between pigment absorption, which increases linearly with thickness, and Bragg reflection, which scales non-linearly with the number of layers. Furthermore, introducing broadband absorbers to suppress multiple scattering successfully enhanced structural color saturation. In contrast, a system combining red pigments with blue reflection showed strong spectral masking due to overlapping bands and shorter hue distance; consequently, no distinct transition occurred. However, by diluting absorption, structural color was recovered, confirming that final coloration is governed by the "coupling of absorption and reflection." These findings propose "spectral competition design" as a general principle for controlling color dominance within a single material system, providing a blueprint for sustainable, high-saturation biomimetic colorants.

papers.title: Solvent Permittivity and Polarity as Practical Design Parameters for Perovskite Processing
papers.abstract: Solution processing has enabled metal halide perovskites to emerge as one of the most versatile material platforms for next-generation optoelectronic devices. Techniques such as spin coating, blade coating, slot-die coating, and inkjet printing enable low-temperature fabrication, compositional tunability, and compatibility with large-area manufacturing. Yet, despite impressive laboratory efficiencies, perovskite technologies continue to face challenges in reproducibility, scalability, and long-term stability. In many cases, these challenges can be traced to a factor that is often underestimated: solvent choice.

papers.title: Mono-material polydisulfides for pressure sensitive adhesive tapes with closed-loop recyclability
papers.abstract: Pressure-sensitive adhesives (PSAs) are indispensable components across all sectors of modern society, ranging from packaging to aerospace or construction. However, conventional PSAs are non-recyclable multi-layer materials that contain numerous additives, and they often hamper the recycling of other materials such as plastics or metals when they are applied. Furthermore, most research on sustainable PSA development has focused on the adhesive layer with less attention on the non-adhesive plastic backing layer which typically uses petroleum-derived plastics. Herein, we report a strategy to create ‘mono-material’ PSA tapes from biogenic polydisulfide copolymers where both the plastic backing and adhesive layer are chemically recyclable. The cationic ring-opening copolymerization of lipoic acid and its ester derivative, ethyl lipoate, yields high-molecular-weight polydisulfides ( M w > 400 kDa) with low glass transition temperatures (< −30 °C) and unique viscoelastic properties including extremely low moduli (< 100 kPa). When paired with a polyester backing layer, these polydisulfides displayed excellent adhesion strengths (up to 400 N·m −1 ) that were superior to commercial PSA tapes. After treating the adhesive disulfide copolymer with an alkaline solution to form an ionomer, the polymer became 1000-fold stiffer with plastic-like mechanical properties and was non-adhesive. The plastic-like backing and elastomeric adhesive layers were then adhered without additives or compatibilizers to form a complete PSA tape with performance comparable to the polyester-disulfide tapes. Furthermore, the disulfide copolymers in both layers of the tape were fully depolymerized to recover the original monomeric components in high purity. The reclaimed comonomers were subsequently repolymerized to regenerate polydisulfides, thereby verifying closed-loop recyclability. Overall, this work represents one of the first demonstrations of a fully closed-loop, additive-free PSA system in which both the adhesive layer and backing originate from a single dynamic polymer platform.

Overall, this work represents one of the first demonstrations of a fully closed-loop, additive-free PSA system in which both the adhesive layer and backing originate from a single dynamic polymer platform.

papers.title: Production of bottle fermented sparkling wine using nano and micro filters
papers.abstract: The article presents a new method of bottle fermentation of sparkling wine. This method integrates two processes — microfiltration and nanofiltration. A microfilter is employed to effectively separate the majority of wine from yeast cells. This significantly simplifies the process of removing yeast from bottles after fermentation is complete. This process is analogous to the method of removing tea leaves from a prepared infusion using a tea bag. The use of a microfilter also provides the ability to interrupt the fermentation process at any point after the desired level of residual sugar has been achieved. The nano filter is employed for the separation of carbon dioxide from volatile aromas present in gaseous fermentation products. Nanofilters are able to pass small carbon dioxide molecules through them, which are contained in the fermentation gas. At the same time, nanofilters prevent the exit of large aromatic molecules. This process allows the wine to retain the full flavour potential of the grapes, which may be partially lost during the winemaking process. Various options for producing sparkling wines using the proposed method are being considered. The proposed method does not require the use of expensive equipment, which makes it affordable for small-scale production and even for use at home.

papers.title: LeukemIA: A Machine Learning Pipeline for Patient-Specific Molecular Generation in Acute Myeloid Leukemia via Latent Diffusion and Multi-Target Docking
papers.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) remains one of the deadliest hematologic malignancies, with a 5-year overall survival below 30%. We present LeukemIA, a computational pipeline integrating four complementary approaches: (1) a Random Forest model achieving rho=0.824 [95%CI: 0.802-0.843] in 5-fold cross-validation (N=1,458) for AML IC50 prediction; (2) a Fourier Transformer Variational Autoencoder coupled to a Latent Diffusion module with Classifier-Free Guidance for patient-guided de novo molecular generation; (3) a patient encoder trained on real BeatAML data (636 patients, 132 drugs ex vivo, mean rho=0.151, 55/132 drugs significant p<0.05); and (4) molecular docking validation on FLT3 (PDB: 4RT7) and BCL2 (PDB: 2W3L). The generative pipeline identified novel molecules with predicted BCL2 affinity of -8.6 kcal/mol on average (clinical threshold: -7.0 kcal/mol), with optimal ADMET profiles (10/10, no hERG cardiotoxicity, no AMES mutagenicity). Molecular candidates and full technical details available upon request.

papers.title: Chasing the “Holy Grail” of Low‑Dimensional Ice: Intrinsically Stable Freestanding One‑Dimensional Ice Crystals
papers.abstract: “Does intrinsically stable one‑dimensional ice exist without external support?” This question has long been the “Holy Grail” of low‑dimensional water science. Using first‑principles calculations, this work provides the first affirmative answer, predicting two families of freestanding intrinsically stable one‑dimensional ice crystals: polygonal nanotubes (S4‑INT to T14‑INT) and polar helical multi‑stranded nanotubes (P3H‑INT to P7H‑INT). In all structures, water molecules strictly obey the Bernal–Fowler ice rules, forming closed, saturated hydrogen‑bond networks through four hydrogen bonds per molecule. No dangling bonds exist, eliminating the large surface energy penalty – this is the microscopic origin of intrinsic stability and the key to unlocking the “Holy Grail”. Phonon spectra and molecular dynamics simulations confirm their dynamical and thermodynamic stability (the helical family remains intact below 100 K). The polygonal family is non‑polar and a wide‑band‑gap insulator, whereas the helical family exhibits macroscopic polarization (≈0.01 C/m 2 ) due to symmetry breaking, suggesting potential ferroelectricity. We also provide vibrational spectra, XRD fingerprints, a rolling mechanism from two‑dimensional ice to one‑dimensional nanotubes, and Python generation codes. This discovery expands one‑dimensional ice research from the “confined‑stabilized” to the “intrinsically stable” paradigm, offers a clear theoretical answer to the long‑standing “Holy Grail” question, and provides new theoretical models and material motifs for designing pure‑water‑based nanoscale functional materials (e.g., ferroelectrics, proton conductors, chiral devices).

papers.title: Intersite Geometry Controls Activity and Selectivity in the Oxygen Reduction Reaction on Dual-Atom-Site Catalysts
papers.abstract: Dual-atom site catalysts (DACs), unlike bulk and single-atom site catalysts (SACs), enable precise control over the interatomic distance between catalytic centres. This study illustrates how variation in molecular spacers (i.e., phenylene and naphthalene) alter interatomic distances and influences the electrocatalytic behaviour of bisalphen complexes. Corresponding DACs were first synthesised through a straightforward Schiff-base condensation reaction and then immobilised onto edge-functionalised graphene (EFG) support. Catalytic activity towards the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) was evaluated for two cobalt DACs. Under identical conditions, the phenylene-bridged cobalt complex Co2PG achieves a significantly lower alkaline ORR overpotential (η = 0.26 V) than both its naphthalene counterpart Co2NG (η = 0.48 V) and commercial 20% Pt/C (η = 0.37 V). Rotating ring-disk electrode analysis, combined with in situ Raman spectroscopy and theoretical modelling, suggests a new correlation between catalyst structure, reaction pathway, and selectivity. Namely, the results demonstrate that breaking of the scaling relations can be achieved through an optimal interatomic distance – neither too far nor too close – a geometric design principle complementary to the Sabatier principle.

papers.title: From Data to Design: Physics-Informed Symbolic Regression Reveals Ionic Mobility Descriptors in Batteries
papers.abstract: Large, high-quality datasets are essential for accelerating materials discovery. However, challenges related to data accessibility and analysis often prevent these datasets from having full impact. Here, we introduce DISCOVER, an open-source descriptor analysis framework designed to facilitate systematic data exploration and descriptor identification for desired or undesired material functions. Using this framework, descriptors can be identified even for complex materials properties, enabling interpretable and data-driven optimization of targeted materials. Alongside the framework, we present an open-access database containing 765 spinel compounds that are relevant to battery applications. These compounds were derived from periodic density functional theory (DFT) simulations, which provide the structural, electronic, and electrochemical properties necessary for understanding and optimizing spinel materials for use in energy storage technologies. Applying this database together with DISCOVER, we uncover a universal, physics-informed descriptor for ionic mobility across oxide, sulfide, and selenide spinels. Specifically, we demonstrate that the migration barrier is fundamentally governed by a direct competition between the thermodynamic site preference and the geometric anion positional parameter. By providing this open-access resource coupled with analytical tools, we aim to promote reproducibility and accelerate the data-driven design of high-performance energy storage materials.

papers.title: Interfacial lithium redox kinetics regulated by solvent asymmetry and moment of inertia in Li-metal batteries
papers.abstract: Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) offer high energy density, but interfacial charge transfer kinetics remain a bottleneck for high-rate operation. In this work, we construct a library of 12 ether solvents with systematic variations in symmetry and fluorination, confirming that molecular asymmetry is an important molecular feature that results in enhanced Li + redox kinetics and more stable solid electrolyte interphases on Li 0 . Furthermore, we develop a mechanistic understanding of the underlying process. We show that more tilted dipoles and lower moments of inertia strongly correlate with higher exchange current densities. Among the solvents in our study, the asymmetric F5MPE (1-methoxy-2-(2,2,3,3,3-pentafluoroepropoxy) ethane) molecule, a previously unreported solvent molecule, enabled >170 stable cycles in high-rate Li||NMC full cells, outperforming the previously reported best single-salt-single-solvent ether solvent, F5DEE molecule. Overall, this work links molecular-level information with the behavior at electrochemical interfaces and provides an understanding of molecular design considerations for next-generation electrolytes tailored for high-power, fast-charging LMBs.

papers.title: Recyclable electron donor mediated defluorination of per- and poly-fluoroalkyl substances
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are among the most persistent anthropogenic contaminants, widely distributed in the environment and biota owing to the exceptional strength of C–F bonds. Despite extensive efforts to degrade and defluorinate PFAS, existing technologies remain fundamentally constrained by high energy demands, inefficient C–F bond cleavage, and interfacial mass- and electron-transport limitations, which are particularly severe for solid fluoropolymers. Here we report a rapid and general destruction strategy under ambient conditions in nonaqueous media using recyclable and storable organic mediators that generate highly reducing aromatic radical anions or dianions upon (electro)chemical activation. These soluble electron donors enable effective defluorination of both solubilized and solid PFAS within minutes with high electron transfer efficiencies, producing inorganic fluoride salts and defluorinated amorphous carbon without detectable short-chain PFAS byproducts. Mechanistic investigations support a radical chain defluorination process in which electron injection into σ*(C–F) orbitals propagates successive C–F bond scission, circumventing the kinetic and interfacial barriers that limit conventional treatments. We further translate this chemistry into an electrochemical platform that enables controlled in situ mediator regeneration and sustained operation. This work redefines reductive PFAS destruction by replacing heterogeneous charge transfer at solid reductant or electrode surfaces with mediator-enabled homogeneous reaction, thereby enabling rapid and complete mineralization under mild conditions.

papers.title: Catalytic Carbon-Atom Transfer Enables Spiro-Fusion of C–C σ-Bonds
papers.abstract: The catalytic transfer of a single carbon atom offers a powerful means to reconfigure molecular frameworks, yet controlled insertion of a carbon atom into C–C σ-bonds remains a longstanding challenge. Here we report a rhodium-catalyzed spiro-carbon-atom transfer that converts planar biphenylene feedstocks into rigid three-dimensional architectures. Using N -isocyanoiminophosphorane (PINC) as an atomic carbon equivalent, the reaction forms four new covalent bonds at a single spiro center through sequential C–C bond activation. The transformation enables both homo- and cross-spiro-fusion of biphenylenes that are otherwise difficult to access. The strategy can be further extended to reactions involving combined σ- and π-bond activation, providing complementary molecular frameworks. These results establish catalytic carbon-atom transfer as a general approach for transforming simple monocyclic feedstocks into structurally complex spirocyclic molecules, with a single carbon atom serving as a central linchpin.

papers.title: Control of Circularly Polarized Luminescence through Hydrogen-Bond-Assisted Atropisomer Resolution in a Dinuclear Boron Difluoride Complex
papers.abstract: Controlling the sign and magnitude of circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) through conformational chirality remains a challenging yet attractive strategy for the developing chiral photo-functional materials. In this study, hydrogen-bond-assisted control of CPL is reported in a dinuclear boron difluoride complex co-crystallize with organic salts. Two atropisomers, (SC,SC,Ra,Ra) and (SC,SC,Sa,Sa), are separately obtained under different recrystallization conditions. Importantly, each crystalline form exhibits opposite CPL handedness and distinct luminescence efficiencies. These findings provide novel design principles for the development of conformationally flexible CPL emitters.

papers.title: Stabilization of a Molecular Beryllium Electride via Interstitial Electron Localization: A Multi-Topological and NBO Investigation
papers.abstract: We report the computational characterization of a stable molecular beryllium electride featuring a dimeric beryllium core (Be2) encapsulated within a rigid sulphur-rich tetradentate ligand framework. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations at the TPSS/def2-TZVP level reveal a Be-Be bond distance of 2.089 Å, significantly shorter than standard van der Waals dimers. A multi-faceted topological analysis of the electron density provide definitive evidence for the electride nature of the complex. Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM) identifies a (3,-1) bond critical point (BCP) at the interstitial midpoint, while Electron Localization Function (ELF) and Localized Orbital Locator (LOL) maps reveal isolated high-localization basins (η≈ 0.85) detached from the nuclear positions. Interaction Region Indicator (IRI) and Laplacian (∇2ρ < 0$) analyses further identify a non-nuclear attractor that serves as the "anionic" glue of the system. Natural Bond Orbital (NBO) analysis quantifies the electronic environment, revealing highly cationic beryllium centres (+1.1e) and significant sulphur-to-beryllium back-donation (E2 > 20 kcal/mol), which provides the electrostatic confinement necessary to stabilize the interstitial electron cloud. With a HOMO-LUMO gap of 1.58 eV and demonstrated vibrational stability, this complex represents a novel class of alkaline-earth electrides with potential applications in non-linear optics and multi-electron redox catalysis.

papers.title: Emergent in-plane dynamics in two-dimensional porous molecular materials
papers.abstract: Dimensionality reduction profoundly reshapes the phase landscapes of crystalline materials, thereby opening access to novel and metastable states that are inaccessible in the bulk. While this concept is well established for inorganic two-dimensional (2D) materials, its extension to 2D molecular materials remains largely unexplored. Here we present a new crystalline phase of porous molecular materials that exists exclusively in a 2D regime and exhibits emergent in-plane structural dynamics. Shape-persistent triangular metal–organic polygons (MOPGs) self-assemble via directional van der Waals interactions into tessellated 2D lattices, which are then stacked to form threedimensional porous structures. Removal of guest molecules induces densification of the tessellations while preserving permanent porosity, as evidenced by a type I nitrogen sorption isotherm. Exfoliation via decoupling between in-plane and out-of-plane interactions generates nanometer-thin 2D MOPG crystals, termed MOPhene, a phase inaccessible in bulk crystals. Despite having the highest packing density among MOPG tessellations, MOPhene undergoes dynamic molecular rearrangements upon gas adsorption. These results demonstrate the potential of 2D molecular materials as a platform for responsive low-dimensional solids.

papers.title: A Simplified Architecture of a Neural Network for Improved Performance on Small Datasets in Photovoltaic Applications
papers.abstract: Oxide perovskites (ABO3) have emerged as chemically robust and environmentally benign alternatives to halide perovskites for photovoltaic applications. However, the vast compositional space of oxide perovskites makes systematic experimental or first-principles exploration impractical. In this work, we present a machine-learning (ML) based screening framework to identify ABO3 oxide perovskites with favourable photovoltaic characteristics, focusing on two key descriptors: electronic band gap and intrinsic carrier concentration. While conventional ML models such as Random Forest and XGBoost achieve reasonable classification accuracy, they often struggle with imbalanced datasets and fail to capture the physically meaningful ordering of intermediate classes. Similarly, standard neural networks tend to overfit small datasets and underperform in representing borderline semiconductor regions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a modified neural-network architecture, MOIMNet, which integrates a dual head design with a margin-based loss function. This innovation enforces structured separation between extreme classes while preserving the continuum of electronic properties in the latent space, thereby enhancing discrimination of the physically critical middle class. MOIMNet achieves balanced accuracy exceeding 0.83 and area-under-the-curve (AUC) values above >0.90 across all classes, outperforming conventional ML and standard neural networks in handling small, imbalanced datasets. Selected predictions were validated using density functional theory calculations performed with Quantum ESPRESSO, demonstrating strong agreement between ML screening and first-principles results. This integrated ML DFT framework, anchored by MOIMNet, provides a reliable and physics-aware strategy for accelerating the discovery of oxide perovskites for solar-cell applications.

papers.title: Comparative Study of Bayesian Optimization Strategies for Batch Optimization of Heterogeneous Catalysts in CO2 Hydrogenation
papers.abstract: High-throughput and automated experimentation platforms combined with artificial intelligence are increasingly used to accelerate catalyst discovery. Batch Bayesian optimization (BO) (i.e., the simultaneous selection of multiple candidate experiments per iteration) is widely adopted for navigating large compositional spaces; however, its practical behavior under realistic high-throughput and batch constraints remains poorly understood. In this work, we systematically evaluate four BO strategies to optimize the catalyst composition for the hydrogenation of CO2 to methanol. For each BO method, 48 catalysts were synthesized by co-precipitation, utilizing an automated synthesis platform, and evaluated in high-throughput fixed-bed reactors over seven batch iterations. The composition space comprised up to four metallic elements selected from a pool of nine. Although all BO approaches identified competitive catalyst formulations, most optimization trajectories rapidly converged toward distinct local optima that were strongly influenced by the initial random design and exhibited limited global exploration of the compositional space. This case study provides practical insights into the limitations of BO for batch catalyst optimization and highlights their strong dependence on the initial random design, parameter space definition, and batch execution strategy.

papers.title: A general framework for optimal load transfer in SWCNT-polymer composites
papers.abstract: The design of functional nanocomposites depends critically on the engineering of the interface between the nanofiller and the matrix. Despite the exceptional intrinsic mechanical properties of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs), their integration into polymers typically results in mediocre bulk properties due to bundling and poor interfacial bonding. Here we show that using macrocycles mechanically interlocked to SWCNTs and further connecting the rings covalently to the polymer matrix enables near-optimal load transfer. We illustrate this general strategy with both rigid (polystyrene) and flexible (polyurethane) polymer matrices. With polystyrene, we achieve composite materials with very high SWCNT loading, while preserving nanotube individualization. Films of these composites are 11 times stiffer and 37 times harder than the parent polymer while remaining fully solution-processable. In elastomeric systems, this architecture increases fatigue resistance by nearly two orders of magnitude and enhances rain erosion protection by 41% in standardized industrial tests. Our approach provides a universal and scalable chemical solution to overcome the interfacial bottleneck in SWCNT composites, opening the door to a new generation of high-performance nanocomposites.

papers.title: ZeoAgent: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automated Zeolite Design and Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is transforming scientific research, yet most materials discovery approaches remain limited to isolated tasks. A key next step is therefore to develop agentic systems that can autonomously coordinate these tasks within iterative scientific workflows. Despite their broad industrial importance, the discovery of new zeolite frameworks remains highly challenging because of the lack of efficient discovery workflows and rational design strategies. Here we present ZeoAgent, a large language-model-driven agent system that autonomously coordinates zeolite structure analysis, property prediction, and framework design through natural-language interaction. Equipped with a suite of computational tools, ZeoAgent performs structure analysis and property prediction with results consistent with manual calculations. To enable autonomous, goal-directed design, ZeoAgent further incorporates a newly developed point-cloud-based generative method that converts natural-language objectives into physically plausible framework candidates by learning from existing structures. Representative case studies demonstrate ZeoAgent’s ability to address three increasingly challenging design tasks, including generating frameworks under user defined structural constraints, modifying existing topologies to enhance transport performance, and designing frameworks for CO 2 /CH 4 separation. This work provides a promising strategy for computational zeolite research and establishes a practical foundation for goal-directed, LLM-assisted zeolite design.

papers.title: The impact of FDM infill parameters on tensile mechanical properties
papers.abstract: The mechanical properties of printed parts from additive manufacturing depend on the 3D printing method, the material used, and the specific parameters of the 3D printing process. While the method and material may not be easily switched, the printing parameters are relatively easy to adjust during the printing preparation process, known as slicing. This study investigates the influence of infill patterns and density on 3D printed parts using a Fused Deposition Modelling (FDM) printer with common white polylactic acid (PLA) filament, the most widely accessible 3D printing material today. Specimens with all 16 patterns offered by the software PrusaSlicer were tested, each with 15 or 16 infill densities ranging from 5% to 95% or 100%, as well as specimens without infill (0% density). This study aimed to measure and compare the tensile mechanical properties of FDM-printed parts with varying infill parameters. It was found that infill patterns and increasing infill density significantly affected the tensile strength of printed parts, and that the effect of increasing infill density varied across patterns.

papers.title: Straightforward assessment of structural disorder in Ti3C2Tx MXene using Raman spectroscopy.
papers.abstract: MXenes, a large family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides, have attracted considerable interest owing to their physical-chemical properties. It is now well established that structural defects play a key role in these properties with possible significant improvement but also detrimental impact when uncontrolled. This issue is particularly important for MXenes due to the potentially harsh chemical etching conditions used for their exfoliation from the MAX phase precursors. Despite their important role, characterization defects remains highly challenging. Herein, we employ Raman spectroscopy as the primary probe to systematically investigate defect formation in carefully defect-engineered Ti3C2Tx MXenes derived from ion-implanted Ti3AlC2 MAX phases and exfoliated via a mild LiF/HCl route. Controlled ion implantation in the MAX precursor is used to generate well-defined defect densities, enabling direct correlation between implantation dose and Raman response in the resulting MXenes, together with improved exfoliation efficiency. In particular, we demonstrate the high sensitivity of the A1g mode at 206 cm—1, characteristic of Ti-C vibrational modes, to structural disorder with a peak broadening linearly scaling with defect density. This sensitivity is also confirmed for samples obtained with increasingly harsh etching conditions. Raman characterizations were corroborated by complementary spectroscopic analysis at various scales based on XPS/HAXPES and TEM-EELS. Together, these results demonstrate that Raman spectroscopy is a robust, accessible and reliable technique for mapping defects in MXenes, and provide a practical spectroscopic workflow for correlating vibrational, chemical and electronic signatures of disorder in Ti3C2Tx layers.

papers.title: A Zwitterionic Azo Posolyte for Long-Lifetime Aqueous Redox Flow Batteries
papers.abstract: A growing share of variable renewable generation requires low-cost, long-duration grid-level energy storage. Aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) offer tunable molecular chemistry and scalable flow architecture; acidic systems enable high power and leverage mature vanadium-flow hardware. A central challenge is designing posolytes that combine high redox potential, solubility, capacity density, and stability. Here, we report a 2-electron azo-based zwitterionic molecule 4,4′-azo-bis(1-pyridinium-3-propane-sulfonate) (ABPS) that addresses these constraints through intrinsic structural features. The zwitterionic character dramatically enhances water solubility (1.30 M in 2.00 M H 2 SO 4 ) while maintaining overall electroneutrality, thereby intrinsically reducing molecule crossover and suppressing capacity decay during cycling. Symmetric cell testing confirms outstanding stability over 3800 cycles (~ 100 days) with an average coulombic efficiency of 99.98% and nearly zero capacity loss (0.198% year -1 ). In the full cell demonstration, ABPS delivers a high voltage of 1.14 V (paired with V 2+ /V 3+ ). A capacity density of 48.5 Ah L -1 and the corresponding posolyte energy density of 55.3 Wh L -1 are achieved (1.00 M molecule concentration), and an ultralow capacity decay rate of 0.125% year -1 over 1,100 hours of operation. The rational design of azo-based zwitterionic structure thus offers a promising universal route to durable, high-power acidic AORFB posolytes.

papers.title: A Reduced Dynamical Systems Model of PARP Inhibitor-Induced Nascent Strand Gap Formation and BRCA1-BRCA2-RAD51-Dependent Repair During DNA Replication
papers.abstract: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase, PARP, inhibitors are widely recognized for their selective toxicity in homologous recombination-deficient cells, particularly in tumors carrying defects in BRCA1 or BRCA2. Although classical models emphasized unrepaired single-strand breaks and replication fork collapse, more recent evidence has highlighted unligated Okazaki fragment intermediates, PARP trapping, post-replicative daughter-strand gaps, and BRCA-dependent rescue as key determinants of PARP inhibitor response. Here, a reduced mathematical proof-ofconcept framework was developed to formalize these interactions as a coupled dynamical system. The model links ligatable nascent lagging-strand discontinuities, trapped PARP-DNA complexes, persistent daughter-strand gaps, RAD51 repair intermediates, mature nascent DNA, secondary double-strand breaks, and survival. Across baseline conditions, the model reproduced an interpretable hierarchy of replication-associated stress, with untreated wild-type cells showing the lowest lesion burden and the combined LIG1↓ BRCA2−/− + PARPi state showing the most severe phenotype. Together, these results support a coherent mechanistic interpretation in which PARP inhibitor response is governed by the balance between lagging-strand lesion generation, PARP trapping, and BRCA1-BRCA2-RAD51-dependent rescue of daughterstrand gaps.

papers.title: A Computationally Efficient and Accurate Method for Predicting Conductance of Single-Molecule Junctions
papers.abstract: The conductance of single-molecule junctions has been extensively investigated over the past two decades across a wide range of molecular structures, yet efficient predictions of their conductances quantitatively remain a challenge. These junctions typically consist of an organic molecule composed primarily of light atoms, coupled to heavy-atom metal electrodes, most commonly gold. The standard ab initio framework for calculating the junction transmission combines density functional theory (DFT) with non-equilibrium Green’s functions (NEGF). In practice, these calculations use low-rung exchange-correlation functionals such as PBE, which underestimate the gap between the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and the lowest unoccupied molecular orbitals (LUMO) and overestimate the conductances. Although more advanced methods have been developed to correct these systematic errors, they often require nontrivial, multi-step workflows and substantial computational efforts, which limit their use as accessible tools for widespread adoption. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a physically motivated, low-cost approach that closely approximates results obtained with high-rung functionals, such as the hybrid B3LYP and PBE0 functionals. Our method fits the PBE-calculated transmission to a Breit-Wigner form and subsequently refines the fit parameters using molecular orbital energies and metal densities of states computed for the isolated subsystems with high-rung functionals.
