In contrast, catalytic strategies have recently advanced, with desymmetric substitution emerging as a powerful method for generating P(V) stereocenters. However, current strategies are predominantly restricted to acyclic systems, where control is exerted solely over the P(V) stereogenic center. Herein, we report the first N- heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-catalyzed desymmetric annulation for the enantio- and diastereoselective synthesis of phosphacycles bearing P(V) and C-stereogenic center at 1,4-positions. The control over remote chirality and multiple stereogenic center are the key challenges of the present strategy, which was successfully achieved by choosing the suitable NHC precursor and substrate. DFT studies shed light on the importance of the annulation step, rather than the initial NHC addition to the aldehyde, as the crucial step for the enantio- and diastereoselectivity control of the reaction. The derivatization of the synthesized seven membered phosphacycles emphasizes the practical utility of the present methodology.

papers.title: Topological and Energetic Landscapes of a Binuclear Beryllium Complex: Identifying Non-Nuclear Attractors and Correlation-Driven Stability
papers.abstract: The nature of metal-metal bonding in main-group elements remains a significant challenge for electronic structure theory. In this work, we present a comprehensive computational study of a binuclear beryllium complex, Be2C12N2H14, utilizing Density Functional Theory (DFT) and high-level DLPNO-CCSD(T) calculations. The complex features a remarkably short Be–Be bond of 1.884 Å. Natural Bond Orbital (NBO) and Energy Decomposition Analysis (EDA-NOCV) confirm a strong covalent σ-bond stabilized by significant electron correlation and electrostatic interactions. Topological analysis via the Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM) reveals the presence of non-nuclear attractors, characterizing a unique electron-trapping bonding environment. Time-Dependent DFT (TD-DFT) predicts an intense absorption peak at 399.8 nm, suggesting potential applications in optoelectronic materials.

papers.title: From Fluorine to Chlorine: How Atomic Vibrations Enable Efficient Triplet Harvesting in Crystalline TADF Scintillators
papers.abstract: Thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) offers a powerful route for harvesting triplet excitons in organic scintillators, yet achieving simultaneously small singlet–triplet gaps and efficient spin–orbit coupling (SOC) in rigid molecular crystals remains a fundamental challenge. Here we demonstrate that targeted halogen substitution can activate vibrationally assisted spin-flip channels that dramatically enhance triplet harvesting in crystalline donor-acceptor emitters, tailoring them for scintillators with higher light yield and faster response times. Using DMAC-TRZ derivatives bearing fluorine or chlorine substituents, we combine single-crystal structural analysis, temperature-resolved photoluminescence, radioluminescence spectroscopy, and quantum-chemical calculations to reveal how subtle changes in halogen chemistry control excited-state dynamics. While fluorination reduces sharply the singlet-triplet energy gap, chlorine additionally introduces dynamic SOC enhancement mediated by the vibrations of Cl atoms within the crystal lattice. As a result, the chlorinated crystal exhibits an exceptionally small activation energy (Ea = 3.9 meV), (sub)microsecond-scale delayed fluorescence, and a scintillation yield of 26 000 photons MeV-1. These results reveal a powerful, atom-economical approach to achieving near S1-T1 degeneracy combined with vibrationally activated heavy-atom effects, enabling high-performance TADF scintillators in organic crystals.

papers.title: Computational Methods in Physical Virology: A Critical Perspective Across Lengths and Timescales
papers.abstract: Physical virology investigates viral particles by focusing on their assembly, stability, mechanics, and interactions with host cells, neutralizing antibodies, and surfaces. Within this field, computational virology is becoming an indispensable pillar, serving as a “computational microscope” that bridges the spatio-temporal scales of viral processes, from individual protein dynamics to capsid assembly and cellular entry. This perspective article offers a critical overview of the current state, challenges, and future directions of computational approaches in physical virology. Our vision is anchored in the research presented at the 2025 EMBO/FEBS Lecture Course on Physical Virology held in Sant Feliu de Guixols, Spain, and complemented by a targeted survey among attendees. We survey the principal methodological frameworks in use, from all-atom to multiscale molecular simulations, mesoscale simulations, and growing integration of artificial intelligence tools. We also critically examine the central obstacles impeding the field's progress, including the computational–experimental interface gap, limited accessibility to simulation data, reproducibility concerns, and systemic gender and geographic inequities. Finally, we outline future perspectives, proposing that integrating physics-aware AI with multiscale simulation frameworks, combined with community-driven data-sharing initiatives, will transform the computational microscope from a descriptive tool into a predictive engine for antiviral therapies, rational vaccine design, and biotechnological innovation.

papers.title: Crosslinking of Linear Polyimines into Aminal-Linked Porous Organic Polymers for Efficient Hydrocarbon Separation
papers.abstract: Hypercrosslinked polymers, a class of porous organic polymers (POPs), are constructed by crosslinking linear polymers or knitting small aromatic molecules with a molecular crosslinker, typically via Friedel–Crafts alkylation. In this study, we report a new approach for the synthesis of POPs via the crosslinking of linear polyimines with m‑phenylenediamine through nucleophilic addition of amines to imines, forming aminal linkages. The resulting aminallinked POPs, with an estimated low cost of 16 USD/kg, exhibited high surface areas up to 650 m2/g and abundant microporosity, in contrast to the ~100 m2/g observed for the linear polyimine. This method demonstrated good generality: four linear polyimines with different structures were successfully crosslinked into POPs with high porosity. Both experimental results and theoretical calculations indicate that the use of diamines at the meta-position is critical for efficient crosslinking, whereas para-diamines did not initiate crosslinking. With their high surface area and rich microporosity, these POPs displayed high adsorption capacities for C2 hydrocarbons and CO2, but significantly lower capacity for CH4. Dynamic breakthrough experiments confirmed excellent separation performance for C2 hydrocarbons/CH4 mixtures, highlighting their potential for hydrocarbon separation. This study provides a new strategy for the synthesis of cost-effective POPs and demonstrates their promising applications in gas separation.

papers.title: Amphiphilic Diketopyrrolopyrrole Polymers Enable Intrinsic Selective Perchlorate Transduction in Organic Electrochemical Transistors
papers.abstract: Controlling ion-specific interactions in organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs) is essential and challenging for the development of high-gain analytical sensors. This challenge is particularly acute in aqueous environments, where the detection of emerging contaminants such as perchlorate (ClO 4 - ) is often hindered by high kinetic barriers to ion ingress and by complex dehydration-rehydration dynamics associated with volumetric doping. Herein, we introduce a ‘membrane-less’ organic electrochemical transistor (OECT) platform based on a methoxylated diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP)-based amphiphilic copolymer. By strategically incorporating 100% methoxy functionalization into the polymer backbone, we provide high-density oxygen-donor sites for facile injection of chaotropic perchlorate ions. Our multimodal investigation reveals that this structural modification enables a nearly five-fold surge in volumetric charge (QV) to 32 C/cm 3 and a four-fold increase in the doping level (y = 0.38) per repeating unit relative to non-methoxylated analogues. When integrated into OECTs, this enhanced ionic-electronic coupling yields a 300-fold increase in detectivity, reaching 21 (±1) ppb in pristine media and 30 (±2) ppb in complex ionic backgrounds, among the lowest reported for membrane-free OECTs. Mixed-interference protocols yield a 140-fold selective preference for perchlorate over common environmental interferents (F - , Cl - , NO 3 - , SO 4 2- ), supported by a high signal recovery of 86.5%. This performance is further corroborated by control experiments and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, which demonstrate that the methoxy units enhance aqueous wettability and function via an "auxiliary glycol" effect to transduce trace levels of analytes.

papers.title: CyRxnOpt: Generalized Interface for Benchmarking Reaction Optimization Algorithms
papers.abstract: Numerous cutting-edge machine learning algorithms have been developed in recent years for efficiently optimizing chemical processes. While many are open-source, evaluating and applying them to chemical processes remains challenging due to varying, non-standard implementations and interfaces. Additionally, comprehensive comparisons of optimization algorithms are crucial for researchers to make informed decisions about which algorithm will perform best for their process, but there is little information comparing how each algorithm performs on differing chemical processes. CyRxnOpt has been developed as a general, Python-based interface to install, use, and switch between reaction optimization algorithms under a single software interface. By integrating optimizers with the CyRxnOpt interface, many state-of-the-art reaction optimization algorithms can be more easily used in other software and workflows. To demonstrate the use and flexibility of CyRxnOpt, it was used to access four optimization algorithms and benchmark their performance on standard optimization functions and reaction models built from experimental datasets, providing a benchmarking framework which we plan to expand to more optimization algorithms. The initial benchmarking for this limited set of models show that EDBO+ and AMLRO demonstrate robust performance.

papers.title: Supervised multi-agent discovery of high-entropy layered double hydroxides for selective ethanol-to-acetate electrooxidation
papers.abstract: Autonomous materials discovery platforms must deliver not only efficient optimization across high-dimensional chemical spaces, but also trustworthy system design that ensures safety, traceability, and robust scientific decision-making. Here we present AIChemist-Alpha, a hierarchical supervised multi-agent framework for scalable autonomous materials discovery. The framework separates orchestration, validation, and execution into distinct functional layers and integrates three reproducible system capabilities: traceable decision chains, data-flood governance that converts raw electrochemical signals into validated decision-grade abstractions, and supervised safety gates for risk-tiered experimental actions. We apply AIChemist-Alpha to the discovery of high-entropy layered double hydroxide (HE-LDH) electrocatalysts for alkaline ethanol oxidation, a challenging optimization problem defined by a large combinatorial composition space. Through supervised closed-loop exploration, the system identifies Co0.35Fe0.23Mn0.05Ni0.32Zn0.05-LDH as an optimized catalyst. It delivers an operating potential of 1.3447 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) at 10 mA cm-2 with acetate selectivity exceeding 97%, and furthermore the assembled device demonstrates a durability of over 300 h at 100 mA cm-2. These results demonstrate how trustworthy multiagent autonomy can accelerate catalyst discovery while maintaining scientific rigor, operational safety, and practical reproducibility.

papers.title: Framework-Templated Gas Lattices in Metal-Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: A gas lattice is a crystalline-like arrangement of adsorbates stabilized inside a porous host by confinement and periodic binding, providing a structurally defined adsorption state that links uptake and transport. Here, we present an end-to-end pipeline to discover and design framework-templated gas lattices in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) using Xenon as a proof-of-concept guest. High-throughput screening with a lattice-aware descriptor identified Co-CAU-36 as a host that stabilizes a pore-spanning Xenon lattice, while isotherm analysis resolved shell formation, pore filling, and cooperative lattice establishment under application-relevant conditions. In Xenon/Krypton mixtures, Co-CAU-36 exhibited strong pore-scale core–shell segregation, and NEB calculations indicated a low-barrier core diffusion pathway for Krypton, implying separation relevance. Finally, ML-guided genetic optimization over a pillared-MOF space yielded candidates with Xenon lattice signatures. Here, we show that framework-templated gas lattices constitute a distinct adsorbed phase, characterized by long-range periodic order, collective transport pathways, and non-additive mixture behavior.

papers.title: Transfer of Discrete Spin Crossover Complexes into Structurally Infinite Architectures using the Metalloligand Approach
papers.abstract: High-density data storage systems, molecular switches and other spintronic devices show promise for application in the next generation of electronics; however, precise control of electronic states in extended architectures remains a significant challenge. Spin crossover (SCO) materials are promising candidates for the development of such devices due to their intrinsic electronic and magnetic bistability. In this context, the use of pre-existing SCO complexes as building blocks to generate extended coordination polymer (CP)/metal-organic framework (MOF)-type architectures remains largely unexplored, owing to the difficulty of preserving SCO behavior following network formation. To this end, we now demonstrate the use of the metalloligand approach as a general strategy for enabling the transfer of SCO behaviors into new extended CP/MOF architectures following the coordination of Ag(I) ions to the secondary coordination domains of the parent metalloligand. In general, integration of the parent metalloligand, [FeL](BF4)2 (where L = tris((((1-(pyridin-4-yl)-1H-imidazole-4-yl)methylene)amino)ethyl)ethane-1,2-diamine), in this fashion was found to enhance cooperativity and structural robustness by introducing additional metal-ligand and ligand-ligand interactions. Detailed structure-function relationships for various solvatomorphs of the parent metalloligand highlight potential mechanisms of action altering both the completeness and cooperativity of the corresponding spin-profiles. Further, structural augmentation of the parent metalloligand enables additional tunability of the SCO behavior following simple variation of the secondary metal ion species. This work reports a general strategy for the rational design of multifunctional SCO materials and represents, to the best of our knowledge, a very rare demonstration of the transfer of a SCO metalloligand into SCO-active CP/MOF-type architectures.

papers.title: Triazenyl Furans as Diels–Alder Dienes
papers.abstract: 2-Triazenyl furans are introduced as bench-stable, electron-rich Diels–Alder dienes, enabling convergent and divergent access to highly substituted arenes under redox-neutral conditions. The triazene substituent activates the furan toward cycloaddition, promotes i n situ aromatization, and serves as a versatile handle for downstream functionalization. Diels–Alder reactions are demonstrated with a broad range of dienophiles, including alkenes, alkynes, allenes, and benzyne, in both inter- and intramolecular settings. Chemoselective derivatizations highlight the synthetic versatility of this platform, culminating in concise annulative syntheses of pomalidomide, ( S )-apremilast, and related analogues.

papers.title: Development and Scale-Up of a Regioselective Functionalization of 2-Cyano-3-Fluoropyridine in a Flow Reactor
papers.abstract: A continuous-flow process was developed for the regioselective functionalization of 2-cyano-3-fluoropyridine using Corning® Advanced-Flow™ reactors. The flow set-up enabled the controlled generation of a pyridyllithium intermediate through deprotonation with lithium diisopropylamide (LDA) under noncryogenic conditions (-20 °C) with a short residence time of 6 s. Subsequent in-line trapping with electrophiles afforded the corresponding highly functionalized pyridine derivatives in high yields and excellent selectivity. The optimized process was seamlessly scaled up using a Corning® Advanced-Flow™ Reactor G1, maintaining high selectivity while achieving a throughput of 83 g.h-1.

papers.title: Seeing Like a Structural Biologist: EyeCue, a Multimodal AI Agent for Interpreting MD Trajectories with Audio-Visual Explanations
papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations capture atomic interactions that govern molecular binding, stability, and conformational changes. However, interpreting trajectories typically requires labor-intensive inspection by expert structural biologists and bespoke analysis workflows. We introduce EyeCue, a multimodal AI agent that analyzes MD trajectories to generate narrated video explanations highlighting key molecular behaviors, including binding, dissociation, and conformational transitions. Across protein–ligand and interfacial systems, EyeCue’s interpretations show strong agreement with established quantitative metrics for binding stability and conformational dynamics. These results establish EyeCue as an expert-level interpreter of MD simulation outputs in R&D workflows, enabling scalable analysis of large design spaces. A gallery of EyeCue generated videos is available online at https://eyecue-gallery.aganitha.ai/.

papers.title: Unmodified Levoglucosenone as a Dual-Reactive Monomer for Degradable Biobased Resins: A Preliminar Study
papers.abstract: This study presents a direct, water-based, catalyst-free polymerization of levoglucosenone (LGO) with tris(2-aminoethyl)amine (TREN), exploiting both the α,β-unsaturation and the ketone of LGO. Initial studies with Cyrene™, containing only a ketone, confirmed rapid imine formation under neutral aqueous conditions, demonstrating that TREN efficiently reacts with carbonyl groups in water. In contrast, the dual reactivity of LGO enables step-growth polymerization via aza-Michael addition and imine formation, yielding crosslinked poly(aza-Michael-imine) networks with tunable structural and thermal properties. Systematic variation of the LGO:TREN ratio revealed that lower TREN content promotes highly crosslinked, thermally stable resins, whereas higher TREN content results in less crosslinked, water-soluble networks with increased flexibility. The choice of solvent was also found to significantly influence polymer architecture: polar aprotic solvents led to initially precipitated, moisture-sensitive resins, while polar protic or weakly polar aprotic solvents produced fully dissolved, stable resins. Thermal analysis showed Td5% values up to 255 °C and glass transition temperatures ranging from 23 °C to 72 °C depending on the solvent, highlighting the tunable thermal behavior of these materials. The imine-based networks can also be depolymerized under acidic conditions, highlighting their potential recyclability. This approach provides a versatile platform for functional, water-processable resins with applications ranging from coatings and adhesives to drug delivery and enzyme immobilization.

papers.title: A 4D-STEM Approach to Serial Crystallography of Advanced Nanomaterials
papers.abstract: Advanced crystalline materials are increasingly engineered at the nanoscale, where precise atomic arrangements govern macroscopic functionality. Yet, structure determination often remains limited by intrinsically weak diffraction from small, structurally complex, and radiation-sensitive nanocrystals, as well as signal overlap arising from aggregation or intergrowth. Here, we present a serial electron diffraction (SerialED) strategy based on four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) that addresses both limitations. By acquiring diffraction snapshots via raster scanning, this approach maximizes the information content while enabling high-throughput access to individual nanocrystalline regions and selective inclusion of high-quality measurements. We demonstrate the approach across representative nanocrystalline systems including zeolites, metal-organic frameworks, and small-molecule pharmaceuticals, resolving all structures at atomic resolution. Importantly, the workflow requires minimal instrument alignment and no prior structural knowledge. Our 4D-STEM SerialED approach establishes a general platform for nanoscale serial crystallography, broadening access to high-quality structure determination and opening new opportunities for understanding and designing advanced functional materials.

papers.title: Continuous Flow Synthesis of Diglycolamides for Rare-Earth Elements Recovery: Algorithm-Accelerated Reaction Optimization Coupled with Automated Extraction Evaluation
papers.abstract: A first example of diglycolamide flow synthesis was developed, showcasing algorithm-accelerated reaction optimization and its potential to accelerate ligand discovery and enable autonomous, AIcontrolled manufacturing of critical materials. 3 ABSTRACT The increasing demand for manufacturing rare-earth elements (REEs) as critical materials has intensified research on sustainable synthesis of advanced extractants such as diglycolamides (DGAs). The development of ligands involves substrate scope development, process optimization, at-scale production, and separation evaluation. These components are typically disconnected in a conventional workflow, which is therefore time-consuming and labor-intensive. To accelerate extractant development and impact manufacturing, we present a streamlined workflow for DGAs that includes continuous-flow ligand synthesis and automated evaluation for REEs solvent extraction. The synthesis of DGAs is achieved using a digitized flow reactor, which enables online spectroscopic monitoring and control of residence time, temperature, and reactant stoichiometry. The use of Rxn Rover automation software enables artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm supervision to minimize the steps and time for process optimization by over 40%. A substrate scope of 7 structurally diverse DGAs was synthesized in yields up to 90% upon optimization. The process optimization mode can be seamlessly scaled up to mass production, yielding 19 grams of the high-extraction-efficiency ligand N,N′-dimethyl-N,N′-dioctyldiglycolamide (DMDODGA) over 48 hours of continuous operation. The ligands synthesized at scale can be used for highthroughput evaluation of liquid-liquid (L-L) extraction against 14 lanthanides (Ln) on a robotic platform. This work highlights the power of combining automated synthesis with applicationdriven testing to accelerate the discovery of functional ligands, laying the foundation for fully closed-loop, AI-controlled platforms for the smart and autonomous manufacturing of critical materials.

papers.title: Modular Synthesis of Bis(triazole)s by Sequential Triazole Formation and Michael Addition
papers.abstract: An efficient modular assembly method using bis(2-azidoacrylamide)s as tetravalent platforms is described. A broad range of bis(triazole)s are easily synthesized by triazole formations and subsequent Michael additions. Sequential conjugation enables the facile construction of bis(triazole)s from readily available modules. Furthermore, following mono(triazole) formation, selective Michael addition of the resulting 2-triazolyl acrylamide moiety proceeds smoothly leaving 2-azidoacrylamide moiety intact.

papers.title: Leveraging E/Z Isomerization to Enhance Ring Opening Polymerization Thermodynamics of a CO2/Butadiene Derived δ-Lactone
papers.abstract: 3-ethylidene-6-vinyltetrahydro-2H-pyran-2-one (EVP), a δ-lactone with 28 wt % CO2, has been shown to valorize cheap and abundant waste products into commercially competitive polyester products which are non-toxic and potentially biodegradable. Here, our team reports the photochemical E/Z isomerization of EVP through irradiation with 245 nm light. Selective ringopening polymerization of (Z)EVP is achieved through ureate-anion catalysis, where unwanted Michael addition reaction is suppressed at low temperature (<-10 ºC). Further, competitive ureate-anion catalyzed Z to E isomerization of the monomer is suppressed through high initiator loading where poly(Z)EVP is obtained at 69 % yield at -40 ºC (98 % selective). Importantly, the ceiling temperature (Tc) significantly increased from -141 ºC to -60 ºC from (E)EVP to (Z)EVP, resulting in a six-fold increase in polymer yield at -10 ºC (8 vs. 48 %). The increase in Tc is rationalized by leveraging a repulsive non-covalent interaction between the methyl group on the ethylidene functional group and the carbonyl oxygen. A reactivity ratio of r(Z)EVP 1.36 and r(E)EVP 0.73 is measured, resulting in a polymeric material with gradient architecture in copolymerizations of the stereoisomers. The increased insertion rate of (Z)EVP is rationalized by a reduction in the steric hinderance along the Flippin-Lodge trajectory of the lactone.

papers.title: Contra-thermodynamic α,β- to β,γ-Photodeconjugation of an Inert CO2 Derived δ-Lactone Enables Facile Ring-Opening Polymerization
papers.abstract: The ring opening polymerization (ROP) of δ-lactones derived from the telomerization of CO2 and butadiene offers a platform to valorize cheap and abundant waste products into commercially competitive products. However, ROP of multisubstituted δ-lactones is often limited by a lack of exergonicity. Here, our team reports the photochemical activation of 3-ethylidene-6-vinyltetrahydro-2H-pyran-2-one (EVP) through base-catalyzed α,β- to β,γ-photodeconjugation affording 3,6-divinyltetrahydro-2H-pyran-2-one (DVP) with yields up to 97 %, where yields are dependent on the pKa of the catalyst’s conjugate acid. Ti(OiPr)4-catalyzed selective ring opening polymerization results in well controlled polymerizations with polymer molar masses up to 5 kDa. Thermodynamic analysis of DVP polymerization reveals a ceiling temperature (Tc) of 58 ºC, ~200 ºC higher than for EVP, demonstrating how photodeconjugation can be used as a simple tool to improve the polymerization thermodynamics of β-substituted-α,β-conjugated lactones.

papers.title: A Continuous-Space Analytical Framework for Committor Functions from Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: Many biomolecular processes, including protein conformational changes, ligand binding, and allosteric regulation, are governed by rare transitions between metastable states on complex freeenergy landscapes. The committor function, the probability that a trajectory initiated from a given configuration reaches one metastable state before another, is widely regarded as the optimal reaction coordinate for describing such transitions. In practice, committor functions are often computed using Transition Path Theory combined with Markov State Models (MSMs), which discretize configuration space into states and therefore limit spatial resolution. Here we introduce an analytical framework for computing continuous-space committor functions directly from molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories using a Liouville propagator formulated in a basis-function representation. The key insight is that the slow eigenmodes of the propagator can be represented as linear combinations of basis functions, yet the resulting committor equations do not depend explicitly on the unknown expansion coefficients. As a consequence, the Liouville propagator and committor functions can be constructed directly from an arbitrary set of basis functions without explicitly solving for eigenfunctions. This formulation enables continuous committor functions, iso-committor surfaces, and other kinetic quantities such as mean first passage times (MFPTs) to be computed without discretizing configuration space. Applications to a two-dimensional model potential, alanine dipeptide, and the FIP35 WW domain demonstrate that the resulting committor functions agree with MSM-TPT results while providing substantially higher spatial resolution, enabling precise identification of transition states. Because our theoretical framework accommodates general basis representations, including polynomial or Fourier expansions of physical coordinates, tensor-based collective variables (CVs), and machine-learning-derived CVs, it provides a versatile foundation for analyzing dynamics in biomolecular systems and other complex dynamical processes.

papers.title: Machine-learned nonadiabatic couplings enable reactive photochemical reaction dynamics simulations
papers.abstract: Photochemical reactions proceed through complex excited-state pathways; direct atomistic resolution on subnanosecond timescales remains experimentally inaccessible, obscuring mechanistic insight. Capturing these dynamics requires explicit treatment of coupled nuclear and electronic motion via nonadiabatic molecular dynamics (NAMD); its high computational cost restricts applications to small molecules and short timescales. While ML-photodynamics has accelerated NAMD, non-adiabatic couplings remain approximated due to their vectorial nature, arbitrary phase, and singularities near state crossings. Here, we present the first direct machine-learning prediction of NAC vectors for complex photochemical reactions in gas-phase and explicitly solvated environments. We achieve NAC MAEs of 0.09-0.12 eV/Å and speedups exceeding 3 orders of magnitude over multiconfigurational methods, while matching experimental quantum yields and stereoselectivity, reproducing QM-NAMD half-lives, bond-breaking mechanisms, and crossing regions. Out-of-sample evaluation establishes training-set diversity as critical for generalization and physically accurate ML-NAMD. This framework unlocks predictive modeling of complex photodynamics and rational design in photochemistry.

papers.title: Click’n ROPISA: One-pot Synthesis of Ultrabright Fluorescent Nanoparticles made of polypeptides
papers.abstract: Fluorescent nanoparticles are widely used in bioimaging and sensing, yet their preparation relies on multistep synthetic routes that limit scalability and structural control. Here we introduce a one-pot strategy that couples aqueous ring-opening polymerization-induced self-assembly (ROPISA) of γ-propargyl-L-glutamate N-carboxyanhydride with copper-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) to produce fluorescent polypep- tide nanoparticles. This synchronized “Click’n ROPISA” process enables the si multaneous formation of polypeptide nano-objects and covalent incorporation of diverse azido-functionalized fluorophores. The resulting assemblies exhibit tunable emission across the visible spectrum and are accessible at high solids content while maintaining high brightness and structural uniformity. Dense fluorophore incorporation enables efficient Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) both within the assemblies and with dye-labeled proteins, supporting sensing applications. The intense brightness of t he red-emitting nanoparticles further enables single-particle tracking in microscopy toward advanced bioimaging.

papers.title: Spin Crossover in a Fe(II) Complex with a Radical Iminosemiquinonate Ligand
Precision Profiling of α-1,4-vs α-1,6-glycosidase activity using synthetic linear and branched glycogen tetramers using HPLC-MS
Diameter-controlled synthesis of horizontally aligned carbon nanotube arrays via S-apphire interface engineering
papers.abstract: Precise control over the size and dispersion of supported metal nanoparticles is a fundamental issue in heterogeneous catalysis, governing both reaction activity and selectivity. However, regulating these parameters remains challenging due to thermodynamically driven sintering, particularly under high-temperature conditions. This challenge is acutely exemplified in the growth of horizontally aligned carbon nanotube (HACNT) arrays, where the catalyst size strictly dictates the CNT diameter, and consequently the electronic properties for integrated circuit applications. Here, we report a deterministic sulfur-modified sapphire (S-apphire) interface engineering strategy to regulate catalyst dispersion and the resulting CNT diameter. We establish cohesive energy ( E coh ) as a quantitative descriptor of metal-metal versus metal-support interactions and show that sulfur modification selectively tunes E coh to control nanoparticle size predictably. This strategy achieves a diameter reduction to ~1.26 nm using Ti catalysts, meeting the requirements for the 3 nm technology node of CNT integrated circuits, while preserving high array density and good alignment. Top-gated field-effect transistors fabricated on these arrays exhibit on/off current ratios approaching 10 7 , superior to devices with uncontrolled diameters. Beyond CNT electronics, this work offers a generalizable thermodynamic framework for designing stable, size-controlled metal nanostructures via interface engineering.

papers.title: Convergent Synthesis of Natural-Mimetic Glycerophospholipids: New Tools for Biological Studies and Cancer Cells Labelling
papers.abstract: Glycerophosphlipids (GPLs) constitute the most important subclass of phospholipids. These biomolecules play multiple roles at the cellular level and are involved as major constituents in membrane bilayers, cellular compartmentalization and as intramolecular signaling molecules. We have recently demonstrated that, to preserve the native biological behavior of phosphatidic acids (PA, a GPL) probes, no modifications should be made to their fatty acid chains nor phosphate head, whereas only the addition of a clickable moiety on the glycerol backbone is acceptable. Since PA represent only a tiny fraction of GPLs, we have extended our synthetic methodology to more challenging families of GPLs such as phosphatidylethanolamine, phosphatidylcholine or phosphatidylserine by using an innovative and convergent approach. Moreover, the clickable moiety was used to allowed flexible grafting in cellulo of different molecules to GPLs analogues for various biological applications. This innovation thus provides powerful tools for selectively labeling cancer cells by exploiting the difference of composition of the membrane leaflets between normal and cancer cells.

papers.title: Novelty-Aware Evolutionary Bayesian Optimisation for Multi-Objective Discovery Science
papers.abstract: Efficient optimisation of complex experimental systems is a central challenge in modern discovery science, particularly in settings characterised by high-dimensional design spaces, expensive evaluations, and multiple competing objectives. Multi-objective Bayesian optimisation (MOBO) has emerged as a leading approach for such problems due to its sample efficiency, but can suffer from limited exploration and reduced diversity, especially in many-objective, multimodal, and constrained settings. Evolutionary algorithms, by contrast, excel at maintaining diversity across the Pareto front but typically require large evaluation budgets. Here, we systematically investigate hybrid evolutionary-Bayesian optimisation strategies that combine the strengths of both approaches. Building on the Evolutionary Guided Bayesian Optimisation (EGBO) framework, we benchmark multiple evolutionary generators within a unified acquisition-driven pipeline across ten synthetic test problems spanning multimodal, many-objective, and constrained regimes. We further introduce a novelty-aware batch selection strategy that explicitly promotes diversity within candidate batches while retaining model-guided prioritisation. Across benchmarks, hybrid methods consistently outperform acquisition-only MOBO in challenging optimisation regimes, achieving improved hypervolume, lower inverted generational distance, and more reliable convergence. Gains are most pronounced in many-objective and multimodal problems, as well as in feasibility-limited search spaces. However, performance advantages diminish in very high-dimensional feature spaces, where evolutionary exploration reduces sample efficiency. The proposed novelty-aware selection further improves performance by reducing redundancy within batches and mitigating optimisation stagnation. Importantly, these trends translate to real-world experimental datasets spanning reaction optimisation, pharmaceutical formulation, materials design, and drug screening. Together, these results demonstrate that hybrid evolutionary–Bayesian optimisation provides a robust and practical strategy for improving optimisation performance in autonomous and data-driven discovery workflows.

papers.title: Tailored Biochar with B, N Co-Doping: Theoretical and Experimental Insights into Dual-Sided Dye Adsorption and High-Performance Supercapacitor Applications
papers.abstract: The present work addresses two pressing global challenges: (i) Water purification and (ii) Eenergy storage by developing a multifunctional, sustainable material aligned with key Sustainable Development Goals. We report the synthesis of boron and nitrogen co-doped biochar (B-BC), obtained via a scalable, single-step carbonization (700-900 °C) of Bambusa Tulda bamboo using boric acid as a dopant precursor. Comprehensive physicochemical characterization like XRD, SEM, FTIR, XPS, and BET were performed to understand the biochar properties. Boron and nitrogen co-doping effectively modulate surface polarity, enhances electronic conductivity, and increases the surface area of the biochar matrix, enabling dual adsorption capabilities. The optimized B-BC800 sample exhibited exceptional adsorption capacities of 492.61 ± 39.37 mg/g for Crystal Violet (cationic dye) and 178.56 ± 17.46 mg/g for Congo Red (anionic dye). Meanwhile, the B-BC700 sample demonstrated a high specific capacitance of 296.0 ± 6.6 F/g at 0.5 A/g and excellent cycling stability (89% retention after 5000 cycles), underscoring its potential in energy storage. Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations, including band structure, density of states (DOS), and Bader charge analyses indicates the mechanistic insights into how heteroatom doping tailors the electronic structure and surface charge distribution, supporting the observed adsorption and capacitive behavior. This study highlights the 2 effect of rational tuning of the doping levels and carbonization temperature to optimize the surface functionality and multifunctional performance, paving the way for nextgeneration materials in environmental and energy applications.

papers.title: «Just ask»: Agentic Pilot to empower chemists
papers.abstract: Large Language Model agents capable of using software tools have recently surged in capability and popularity in the data science domain, but remain under-used in the physical sciences. We develop Agentic Pilot, a visual user interface built on LangGraph, to help fill this gap. Agentic Pilot enables the intuitive development of complex agentic workflows, allowing even small LLMs to perform industrially relevant tasks such as executing computational screening calculations or querying electronic lab notebook databases via natural language. In this work, we present Agentic Pilot and provide an industrial perspective on the future of LLM-based agentic workflows in chemistry.

papers.title: Aromaticity Switching via Rearrangement of a Pyrrolyl Substituted Phosphenium Cation
Beyond Capacitive Attribution: Rethinking Sloping Capacity in Hard Carbon for Sodium–Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Hard carbon underpins sodium–ion battery negative electrodes, yet the origin of its sloping capacity remains debated. This capacity is frequently attributed to capacitive storage based on kinetic analyses, although such attribution is not mechanistically unique. Here, we argue that commonly observed electrochemical signatures—including near–linear current scan–rate scaling and b–values approaching unity—can arise from multiple storage processes in structurally heterogeneous carbon, rather than exclusively from surface–confined capacitive charging. Using hard carbon as a model system, we propose a structure–coupled description of sodium storage in the sloping region and outline experimental criteria required to distinguish capacitive and non–capacitive contributions. Recognising this distinction is important, as interpretations based solely on apparent kinetics may bias materials design towards optimising rate response at the expense of efficiency and durability. This work highlights the need to interpret kinetic metrics as phenomenological descriptors rather than direct mechanistic identifiers in disordered electrode materials.

papers.title: Beyond Apparent Rate Capability: Interpreting Fast Sodium Storage in Hard Carbon Negative Electrodes for Practical Sodium–Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Hard carbon remains the most widely studied negative electrode for sodium–ion batteries, and recent work has increasingly highlighted materials capable of sustaining rapid charge–discharge operation. Electrodes that exhibit fast sodium uptake and strong capacity retention at elevated current densities are often regarded as promising candidates for high–power sodium–ion systems. Yet the electrochemical response measured under laboratory conditions does not always translate directly into reversible, durable, or practically relevant sodium–storage behaviour. In many cases, the apparent kinetic response reflects a coupled interplay between carbon microstructure, interfacial chemistry, electrode architecture, and the testing conditions used during evaluation. This work examines how fast sodium storage in hard carbon negative electrodes is commonly interpreted and discusses three issues that complicate rate–centred performance assessment. The first is the potential decoupling between rapid sodium uptake and true electrochemical reversibility. The second is the divergence that may arise between short–term rate performance and long–term cycling durability. The third is the strong sensitivity of laboratory rate metrics to electrode configuration, particularly mass loading and electrode thickness. In many published studies, rate capability is evaluated using electrodes with mass loadings below approximately 0.5–1.5 mg cm−2, whereas practical electrodes typically require loadings of about 3–6 mg cm−2 to achieve areal capacities above 2 mAh cm−2. Under such conditions, simplified laboratory testing can favour optimistic interpretations of material behaviour. Viewed in a broader electrochemical and engineering context, rate capability provides useful but incomplete information about electrode quality. A more reliable assessment of fast sodium storage should therefore consider rate performance together with initial coulombic efficiency, interphase stability, long–term durability, and electrode–scale transport under realistic loading conditions. Such a multidimensional framework offers a sounder basis for evaluating hard carbon negative electrodes and for guiding the design of materials relevant to practical sodium–ion battery technologies.

papers.title: Secure and Distributed Cloud Platforms for Large-Scale Genomic Data Processing in Biotechnology
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of high-throughput sequencing technologies has generated unprecedented volumes of genomic data, creating significant computational and security challenges for biotechnology research and industrial applications. Large-scale genomic analysis requires scalable computing infrastructure, efficient data storage architectures, and robust mechanisms to safeguard sensitive biological information. Secure and distributed cloud platforms have emerged as a practical solution by integrating elastic computing resources, parallel processing frameworks, and advanced cryptographic protocols within virtualized environments. This paper examines the architectural foundations, security models, and performance considerations of distributed cloud systems tailored for genomic data processing. It discusses containerized workflows, distributed file systems, and workflow orchestration tools that enable reproducible and high-throughput bioinformatics pipelines. Particular attention is given to data confidentiality, integrity, and access control through encryption standards, federated identity management, and compliance-aware infrastructure. The study also evaluates the trade-offs between public, private, and hybrid cloud deployments in terms of cost efficiency, scalability, regulatory adherence, and latency. By synthesizing recent technological developments and practical deployment strategies, this work highlights how secure cloud-based infrastructures can accelerate genomic research while maintaining ethical and legal standards. The findings underscore the importance of integrating cybersecurity principles with distributed computing design to support precision medicine, agricultural biotechnology, and large-scale population genomics initiatives.

papers.title: High-entropy molecular mixing arrests crystallization in molecular glasses
papers.abstract: Crystallization from the supercooled liquid is the central obstacle to forming stable molecular glasses, yet no general physical principle exists for suppressing it. Here we show that increasing configurational entropy through multicomponent molecular mixing provides such a principle. In equimolar mixtures of small biocompatible molecules, increasing component number markedly reduces liquid fragility without changing the glass-transition temperature. Above a critical component count, crystallization is arrested entirely, yielding stable amorphous phases upon cooling and reheating. Applying this principle to pharmaceutical systems, we stabilize drugs that crystallize readily in isolation in the amorphous state at loadings as high as 50 mol%, forming what we term high-entropy amorphous drugs (HEADs). At high drug loadings, crystallization remains arrested even as fragility rises above values at which low-component mixtures crystallize readily, revealing that configurational entropy suppresses nucleation through a thermodynamic mechanism independent of fragility reduction. The invariance of the glass-transition temperature further distinguishes molecular systems from high-entropy metallic glasses, where accessible mixing entropy depresses the glass transition. These results establish configurational entropy as a design parameter for controlling crystallization in molecular glasses, operating through separable kinetic and thermodynamic channels.

papers.title: Kilogram-scale Stereoselective Synthesis of an N-methylprolinol Derivative by Enzymatic Transformation
papers.abstract: A scalable method for the manufacture of (S)-1-((2S,4R)-4-methoxy-1-methylpyrrolidin-2-yl)ethan-1-ol, a key intermediate for KRAS inhibitor candidates, was established. This method simplifies the process by performing the decarboxylation of the β-keto ester and the stereoselective reduction of the resulting ketone in a one-pot enzymatic reaction. Furthermore, the direct methylation via Boc group reduction using lithium aluminum hydride was replaced with the safer Eschweiler-Clarke reaction. The resulting prolinol derivative was isolated as its tartrate salt, yielding a high-quality target compound.

papers.title: Anti-Kasha electroluminescence in carbene-gold-arylacetylide complexes
papers.abstract: Kasha's rule states that luminescence occurs from the lowest excited state; violating this rule could enable radiative release of excess electronic energy, otherwise lost as heat in electroluminescent devices. Here we demonstrate anti-Kasha narrowband electroluminescence from carbene-gold(I)-arylacetylide complexes. A rigid acetylide bridge links a (carbene)gold(I) moiety to a multiple-resonance chromophore, thereby spatially separating frontier orbitals to produce a dark long-range charge-transfer S1 and bright short-range charge-transfer S2 states. Optical spectroscopy and theory show that S2 is populated by reverse intersystem crossing from T1 and T2 triplets, enabled by gold-mediated spin-orbit coupling. Proof-of-concept solutionprocessed OLEDs exhibit narrowband (26 nm) anti-Kasha electroluminescence with 20.4% maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE), and 13% EQE at 10,000 cd m-2 .

papers.title: Biomass-Derived 2-Cycloolefin-1-ones: A Key to Depolymerizable and Degradable Polymeric Materials
Generative Artificial Intelligence for Biology: Toward Unifying Models, Algorithms, and Modalities
papers.abstract: Rapid advances in generative artificial intelligence have revolutionized biological modeling across domains such as protein, genetics, and single-cell. However, existing works often organize applications by molecule types or specific research tasks, overlooking the methodological convergence and cross-modal innovations. This paper aims to present a unified methodological perspective that highlights the fundamental technical commonalities across biological modalities. We systematically organize recent advances in generative modeling for biology through the lens of core machine learning paradigms, from language models (LMs) and diffusion models to their emerging hybrid architectures. Our work reveals how techniques initially developed for one molecular type (e.g., protein design) can be effectively transferred to others (e.g., RNA engineering), and identifies the convergence trend where discrete diffusion models and iterative language models represent different facets of a unified generative framework. We cover the evolution from domain-specific models to multi-modal biological foundation models and agent-based systems. By emphasizing methodological connections rather than applications, this paper aims to accelerate cross-domain innovation and make the field more accessible to the broader machine learning community. We conclude by identifying promising research directions where successful techniques in one biological domain remain unexplored in others, offering a roadmap for future advances in generative biology.

papers.title: Synthesis and Physicochemical Properties of trans-2-Fluoroalkyl-Substituted Cyclopentane Building Blocks
Development of Rare-earth-Copolymerized Polystyrene Particles for Traceable Microplastic Quantification and Imaging in Environmental and Biological Systems
Emission of Photons by Near-infrared PbS Quantum Dot Nanocrystals for a Large Diameter Range
papers.abstract: In pursuit of the functionalization of 3D silicon nanophotonics with optically active building blocks, we investigate as candidates near-infrared (NIR) emitting semiconductor quantum dot (QDot) nanocrystals. We present continuous-wave and time-resolved spectral emission of different commercially obtained lead sulfide (PbS) quantum dots with considerable 2-fold variations in diameters, with two different cappings—polyethylene glycol (PEG) and oleic acid (OA)—that are suspended in three different solvents water, chloroform, or toluene. The emission spectra reveal maxima at different photon energies, as set by the nanocrystals average diameters. Timeresolved emission histograms reveal varying amounts of non-single exponential decay, all of which are successfully modeled with a log-normal distribution of decay rates. We observe for quantum dots with OA surface groups that the most frequent decay rate varies slightly with photon energy and concomitant quantum dot diameter. The rates agree with a two-level exciton model, especially if we assume the transition dipole moment to vary proportionally to the quantum dot diameter, but not with an atomic-like dipole emitter. For quantum dots with PEG surface groups, the most frequent decay rate decreases remarkably beyond photon energies 8000 cm −1 or conversely nanocrystal diameters below 4.4 nm. A hypothesis for this observation is that the protonation of the terminal amine groups of the thiol–PEG–NH 2 ligands generates an enhanced local electric field, which enhances the quantum-confined Stark effect (QCSE). This leads to a greater spatial separation of the electron and hole wavefunctions and thus reduces the radiative rate, particularly in smaller dots. Other mechanisms such as quenching, solvent polarity, solvent resonance (vibrational or electronic), nanoparticle acoustics, and electron or hole wavefunction trapping are also evaluated. As a preliminary concrete step towards silicon photonics, we study quantum dots dip-coated on a silicon surface, and observe that the emission rates are markedly increased 5- to 10-fold, which is attributed to the higher dielectric function near to the silicon surface compared to suspensions.

papers.title: Stereoselective photometallobiocatalytic radical C–C coupling of organoboron reagents and diazo compounds via an outer-sphere mechanism
papers.abstract: Designing and developing synthetically useful biocatalytic reactions that operate via novel mechanisms represent a central challenge in modern biocatalysis research. By coupling photoredox catalysis and metalloenzyme catalysis, we harness cooperative photometallobiocatalysis to merge enzymatically generated, open-shell iron carbenoids with reactive radical intermediates formed via excited-state chemistry. This strategy enables a new class of intermolecular radical C–C coupling reactions with excellent enantio- and diastereoselectivities. Central to the successful implementation of this design is the directed evolution of a small metalloprotein catalyst, derived from a thermophilic cytochrome c, to achieve challenging stereocontrol in radical C–C coupling via an outersphere mechanism. These photobiocatalytic, formal metal carbenoid-radical coupling reactions advance a new form of stereoselective outer-sphere metal carbenoid chemistry, providing a powerful strategy to design and evolve biocatalytic C–C bond forming reactions through otherwise challenging intermolecular asymmetric radical couplings.

papers.title: Isoreticular Expansion in Porous Al(III) and Ga(III) Phosphonates: Synthesis, Structure, and Properties
papers.abstract: We report the synthesis and structural elucidation of two metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), [M(OH)(H₂BPD)]·xH₂O (M = Al 3+ , Ga 3+ ), denoted as M-CAU-67, employing the ditopic linker molecule N,N’ 4,4’ bipiperidine bis(methylenephosphonic acid) (H 4 BPD). The title compounds can be synthesised on a milligram scale under hydrothermal conditions, while gram-scale synthesis was realised under reflux conditions. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD) revealed an isoreticular, expanded MIL-91 type structure, representing a rare case of isoreticular expansion in porous metal phosphonates. The framework structure was confirmed by Rietveld refinement against powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) data and further validated by solid-state NMR spectroscopy ( 31 P MAS, 27 Al 3Q MAS). Solvent-exchange experiments and variable-humidity/temperature PXRD data revealed high framework flexibility. The compounds show permanent microporosity and a complex, polarity- and size-dependent sorption behaviour toward gases and vapours.

papers.title: Thermal Properties of Binary Chlorides Relevant to Molten Salt Nuclear Chemistry
papers.abstract: Among proposed Generation IV nuclear reactors, the molten salt fast reactor (MSFR) has some of the most promising inherent safety features available. This includes isolation and solidification of the salt matrix in emergency situations preventing runaway. Other convenient features include online reprocessing and increased fuel variety. A major hurdle for MSFR design is the lack of fundamental data on the component salts, and the resulting fission and corrosion product species. While current MSFRs design research and development is focused on fluoride salts, chloride salts have shown promise and have received increased interest in recent years. A better understanding of the fundamental thermodynamic properties of chlorides would aid in the design of more efficient and precise separations of the spent fuel salt mixture for recycling of fissile isotopes. This review has collected and analyzed existing literature data on the relevant thermochemical and thermophysical properties including: boiling / melting / sublimation points, molar heat capacity, vapor pressure expressions, enthalpic / entropic / free energy formation and phase change values. The elements of interest include those of the fuel salts (actinides), the solvent/cooling salts (alkali and alkaline earth metals), and contamination salts, namely fission and corrosion products (main group, transition metal, and rare earth element).

papers.title: A Gentle Push: Data-Efficiency in Fine-Tuning Foundation Models for Complex Oxide Surface Reconstructions
papers.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are powerful tools for atomistic modeling, yet evolutionary structure searches routinely sample highly distorted and far-from-equilibrium configurations that challenge model robustness. To ensure search stability, conventional exploratory workflows rely on including unphysical local atomic environments in training data. We show that foundation models eliminate this requirement when fine-tuned exclusively on physically reasonable minima. We benchmark different degrees of parameter restriction on limited data, identify the optimal strategy, and apply gradient-free evolutionary searches to SrTiO3(110) and BaTiO3(001) surfaces, yielding new low-energy reconstructions at minimal computational cost. For BaTiO3(001), we further show that a two-step active learning approach outperforms single-shot fine-tuning by enabling efficient potential energy surface exploration without requiring large increases in training data.

papers.title: Viscous solvent embrittles long-chain polymer networks
papers.abstract: The toughness of polymer networks is commonly attributed to energy dissipation arising from viscoelastic deformation, leading to a design principle: higher viscosity increases toughness. Here, we show that this relationship can be reversed when polymer chains are sufficiently long. To demonstrate, we prepare polyacrylamide hydrogels with identical network structures, fully dry them, and reswell them in glycerol-water mixtures to the same polymer content, thereby varying the solvent viscosity by three orders of magnitude while preserving the network structure. Although the mechanical response under homogeneous deformation does not change significantly, toughness measured by pure shear and trouser tests markedly decreases with solvent viscosity. In particular, toughness collapses onto a master curve when plotted as a function of the product of viscosity and velocity, with a scaling relation consistent with the shear-lag model. Stick-slip occurs under conditions for which the slope of the master curve is negative, corroborating the presence of a master curve. We attribute this embrittlement to limited transmission of tension along polymer chains at the crack tip due to solvent viscosity, which reduces the fraction of load-bearing chain segments at rupture. In contrast, in short-chain networks, the tension can readily be transmitted to the entire polymer chains, resulting in a non-negative slope. At sufficiently high viscosity and velocity, energy dissipation by viscosity dominates the tension transmission, resulting in a positive slope regardless of the chain length. These results advance the understanding of toughness dynamics through tension transmission and viscous dissipation.

papers.title: Reactions of a uranium(III) complex with N-heterocycles to form diuranium(IV) ketimides
papers.abstract: The chemistry of the classical uranium(III) complex [U(N′′) 3 ] (N′′ = {N(SiMe 3 ) 2 } – ) is well-developed, but there have been surprisingly few studies of its reactivity towards N -heterocycles. Here we report the separate reactions of [U(N′′) 3 ] with pyrazine, 4-azido-pyridine, and the methylene transfer agent N -(9,10-dihydro-9,10-epiminoanthracen-11-yl)methanimine (C 14 H 10 N 2 CH 2 ) to give the respective diuranium(IV) products [{U(N′′) 3 } 2 (μ-NC 4 H 4 N-1κ N ,2κ N ′)] ( 1 ), [{U(N′′) 3 } 2 (μ-NC 5 H 4 N-1κ N ,2κ N ′)] ( 2 ) and [{U(N′′) 3 } 2 (m-NC 14 H 10 N-1κ N ,2κ N ′)] ( 3 ). The solid-state structures of complexes 2 and 3 respectively revealed bent U–N=C angles of 167.6(5) and 155.3(4)°, short U–N bond lengths of 2.070(5) and 2.104(4) Å, and diagnostic C=N ketimide distances of 1.297(7) and 1.364(7) Å. A combination of structural, spectroscopic, magnetic, and quantum-chemical calculations was required to confidently assign U(IV) ions exclusively in complexes 1-3 , and to prove that 2 and 3 are ketimides rather than iminyls or nitrenes. Together, this study underscores the need for comprehensive analysis for the correct interpretation of the electronic structures of actinide complexes.

papers.title: Predictive Reaction Screening in Quantum Chemistry: Branch-Resolved Free-Energy and Spectral Wave-PacketTransfer Theoryon Coupled Potential-Energy Surfaces for Low-Cost Molecular Prioritization
papers.abstract: Predicting which molecular transformation is worth synthesizing, optimizing, or validating experimentally is rarely a single-surface problem. In realistic quantum-chemical workflows, multiple physically plausible microregimes coexist: conformer basins, protonation states, spin manifolds, solvent-shell organizations, vibronically accessible excited surfaces, and near-degenerate charge-transfer arrangements. A calculation that reports one electronic energy and one barrier therefore compresses an intrinsically branched physical object into a single number. This manuscript develops a dense theoretical framework that keeps the branching structure explicit. The first layer is a Gaussian-basis electronic-structure model built from Born–Oppenheimer Hamiltonians, Hartree–Fock or Kohn–Sham reference states, and finite-temperature free-energy corrections. The second layer is a branch-resolved statistical mechanics in which latent microenvironmental states contribute through an exact log-sum-exp free-energy aggregation. The third layer is a bounded-domain spectral representation of nuclear motion on coupled potential-energy surfaces, where Gaussian wave packets are decomposed into sine modes and transferred between neighboring surfaces by a resolvent-weighted cross-surface operator. The resulting theory unifies thermodynamics, kinetics, and nonadiabatic spectral structure in a single screening formalism. Branch-specific Eyring rates map corrected free-energy barriers to observable time scales; multi-fidelity Gaussian-process residuals map low-level surfaces toward higher-level reference data; posterior Bayesian updates reweight branch priors after sparse historical outcomes; and a spectral transfer norm quantifies whether amplitude that fails on one surface may be redirected onto a neighboring surface with more favorable free-energy descent. Several mathematically explicit results are given: an exact decomposition for the effective free energy of a latent branch ensemble, a rate-error bound induced by barrier uncertainty, boundedness and truncation estimates for the spectral transfer operator on coupled surfaces, and a contraction criterion for epoch-wise coefficient refinement. The manuscript is intentionally written as a research-style theoretical chemistry paper: long-form, equation-dense, fully mechanistic in tone, and organized so that a reader can translate the theory into an implementable computational protocol without importing biological assumptions into the core model.

papers.title: Electron donor-acceptor mediated hydrosulfonylation of olefins from N-hydroxymethylphthalimide sulfones
papers.abstract: Sulfones are widely used sulfur-(VI) motifs in pharmaceuticals, yet their synthesis often relies on harsh oxidation conditions and limited precursor availability. We report a hydrosulfonylation strategy that employs N-hydroxymethylphthalimide (NHMP) sulfones as versatile sulfinyl radical precursors. In the presence of tertiary amines, NHMP sulfones form electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes that undergo light-induced single-electron transfer to generate sulfinyl radicals in the absence of a photocatalyst. The resulting radicals add efficiently to activated olefins, affording structurally diverse sulfones under mild conditions.

papers.title: Decarbonizing Complex Chemical Processes via Heat Electrification: A Case Study on Acetic Acid Hydrogenation to Ethanol
papers.abstract: Low-temperature process heat (<400°C) electrification is a promising decarbonization pathway, yet its effectiveness depends on process design, grid carbon intensity (CI), and electricity costs. Here, we evaluate electrification of ethanol production via acetic acid hydrogenation — involving complex azeotropic separations and reaction–separation coupling — across three process layouts, with similar ethanol carbon recoveries (≥95%). We compare a fossil fuel baseline process against: a) simple electrification, where electric resistance heating (ERH) replaces natural gas as the hot utility, and b) advanced electrification, that combines ERH and electricity-powered vapor recompression cycles while also redesigning the process heat integration scheme. Under the reference grid scenario, advanced electrification achieves greater emissions reductions (74–87%) than simple electrification (42–46%), reflecting its lower electricity intensity. Despite higher capital investment, advanced electrification yields lower levelized costs than simple electrification and limits cost increases versus baseline process to 16–23%. This results in carbon abatement costs (CAC) of 32–57 $/tonneCO 2 versus ~170 $/tonneCO 2 for simple electrification. Advanced electrification also resolves a cost–emissions trade-off present under simple electrification and the baseline process, making lower-capital, lower-per-pass-conversion layouts preferable on both metrics. Sensitivity analysis confirms advanced electrification's greater robustness to electricity price and grid CI variations versus simple electrification.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Investigation of Oil Wetting on Synthetic Polymer Substrates
papers.abstract: Understanding polymer oleophobicity, or the interaction of polymer surfaces with nonpolar liquids, is critical for applications ranging from anti-fingerprint coatings to oil–water separation membranes. Despite its technological importance, the molecular mechanisms underpinning polymer–oil wetting are not well characterized. Here, we employ molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the behavior of n-hexadecane in contact with chemically distinct polymer surfaces, spanning eight constitutional unit chemistries as well as amorphous and crystalline morphologies. This permits critical examination of both thermodynamic and dynamic descriptors of oleophobicity, including oil contact angle, dewetting free energy, interfacial diffusivity, and a proposed “ghost probe energy,” which does not require explicit simulation of oil-polymer interactions. We find that the oil contact angle does not reliably distinguish oleophobic behavior across polymer chemistries, whereas other metrics provide clearer and more consistent differentiation. Analysis of the results reveals that polymer oleophobicity is primarily governed by interfacial van der Waals interactions and modulated by surface flexibility and morphology. Collectively, this work establishes a computational framework for characterizing oil wetting and provides additional insight into what molecular-level factors dictate trends in oleophobicity.

papers.title: Universal Scaling and Many-Body Resurrection of Polaritonic Double-Quantum Coherences
papers.abstract: The ultrafast nonlinear optical response of molecular ensembles is fundamentally altered under strong light-matter coupling. To rigorously isolate the genuine many-body contributions, an exact time-domain field-subtraction protocol is developed within a fully non-perturbative Maxwell-Liouville framework explicitly incorporating the two-exciton manifold in real space and time. This approach reveals that while collective cavity delocalization drives the macroscopic nonlinear signal toward a severe harmonic cancellation (an effect termed ”spectral starvation”), intrinsic many-body molecular interactions robustly resurrect genuine polaritonic double-quantum coherences (DQCs). This many-body resurrection is governed by a universal two-photon matching rule, ∆B +4J = ΩR, linking molecular anharmonicity (∆B) to the macroscopic Rabi splitting (ΩR) and excitonic coupling (J). Crucially, this dictates that J-aggregates (J < 0) uniquely isolate the resonant many-body state below the dense two-exciton scattering continuum, protecting the macroscopic coherence from spatial fragmentation. This predictive framework establishes a direct phase diagram to engineer and protect optical nonlinearities across diverse strongly coupled platforms.

papers.title: When Thermochemistry Limits Electrocatalysis: Insights from CO Electroreduction
papers.abstract: Electrocatalysis modulates interfacial charge-transfer kinetics through potential control, yet how thermochemical processes such as adsorption influence electrocatalytic kinetics remains unclear. Here, we determine CO-reduction limiting currents through measurements of CO-oxidation limiting currents, thus allowing mass-transport effects in CO reduction to be deconvoluted. Using CO-to-methanol conversion on molecular catalysts as a model system, we show that while the reaction rate is limited by an electrochemical step at low overpotentials, the thermochemical CO adsorption step becomes rate-limiting at high overpotentials. Cation-dependent variations in CO adsorption energies and activation energies can be interpreted within the framework of the Brønsted-Evans-Polanyi principle, suggesting CO adsorption energy as a kinetic descriptor. We further demonstrate that cobalt phthalocyanine supported on carbon nanotubes enables appreciable CO-to-methanol conversion due to its stronger CO adsorption compared to other metal phthalocyanines. These findings illuminate possible thermodynamic constraints in electrolysis and provide a kinetic framework to identify when such limitations become rate-defining.

papers.title: An Aerobic Kolbe Pathway to Aldehydes from Carboxylic Acids
papers.abstract: Kolbe electrolysis has long converted carboxylic acids into hydrocarbons via C–C coupling of decarboxylative radicals, with molecular oxygen regarded as detrimental. Here, we show that oxygen instead redirects this reaction, establishing an aerobic Kolbe pathway that selectively produces aldehydes from long-chain carboxylic acids. Isotopic labeling, kinetics, and theory reveal that selectivity is governed by competition between radical dimerization and oxygen interception to alkylperoxy intermediates (ROO•). By maintaining low surface concentrations of alkyl radicals and high oxygen availability, radical dimerization is suppressed in favor of oxygen interception. The resulting ROO• intermediates rapidly evolve to aldehydes with concomitant hydroxyl radical formation, leading to minor alcohol production. The reaction achieves >97% selectivity to oxygenates, redefining Kolbe electrolysis as a route to value-added aldehydes.

papers.title: High-Throughput Screening for Accelerated Oxide Glass Discovery
papers.abstract: Despite millennia of research and development, glass discovery remained largely reliant on manual, trial-and-error methodologies. A major impediment for accelerated glass discovery is its dependence on the processing conditions that is rarely documented, often complicating meaningful comparisons across independent studies. Here, a high-throughput screening platform is presented that allows for up to one hundred cm3-scale glass specimens to be produced per run through multicomponent stereolithographic printing, and be evaluated automatically via Raman spectroscopy without any sample preparation. The approach is demonstrated through its application to mixtures of representative yet chemically diverse glass systems, specifically, borosilicate, aluminosilicate and rare-earth doped materials. The proposed strategy provides a scalable, accessible, systematic and quantitative framework for accelerated glass exploration with relevance across both academic and industrial research environments. Conventional laboratory synthesis throughput is exceeded by two orders of magnitude, while the reproducibility and compositional control that accelerated discovery demands are preserved.

papers.title: Towards a Formal Definition of Kinase Inhibitor Selectivity: Empirical Characterization of Definitional Instability and Proposed Desiderata
papers.abstract: Kinase inhibitor selectivity is routinely quantified using one of several definitionsincluding the S-score, selectivity entropy, Gini coefficient, and ratio-based measuresyet these definitions are applied interchangeably without systematic justification. We characterize, across two large kinase inhibitor profiling datasets (Davis, n = 68; Klaeger, n = 222), the extent and structural sources of disagreement between definitions as their parameters vary. Spearman correlations between median rankings reveal that ratiobased definitions cluster separately from entropy-and distribution-based definitions (r = 0.27–0.48 vs. r = 0.75–0.91). Rank instability is not random: three mechanistically distinct sources are identified. Drugs with no detected binding above a minimum affinity threshold exhibit maximal instability (mean rank σ ≈ 74) due to definitional noise. Among active compounds, near-tied top targets drive ratio-specific instability (r = −0.293, p < 0.001), while broad flat binding profiles drive instability within distribution-based families. Attempts to correlate selectivity scores with clinical adverse event rates from FAERS (n = 46) and FDA label discontinuation rates (n = 33) yield null results, which we attribute to confounding by indication severity and prescription volume. From these findings we derive four desiderata toward a well-formed selectivity measure: a reliability threshold condition, bounded gap sensitivity, distributional consistency under parameter perturbation, and monotonicity under weak off-target

papers.title: MolDockLab: a data‑driven workflow for balanced consensus docking in hit identification
papers.abstract: Structure-based virtual screening (SBVS) is a cornerstone of modern computer-aided drug design, yet its success is highly dependent on selecting an appropriate combination of docking tools, scoring functions (SFs), and ranking strategies from the vast array of available options. MolDockLab addresses this challenge by providing an automated, data-driven framework that optimizes SBVS workflows for a given protein target, for balanced predictive performance and computational efficiency, ultimately improving hit identification.MolDockLab systematically explores all combinations of five docking engines, fifteen SFs, and three consensus ranking strategies using a calibration set of approximately 200 compounds with known bioactivity. The SBVS workflow showing the highest correlation with experimental data is then applied to the larger screening library. Final hit selection from the top 1% integrates protein–ligand interaction profiler (PLIP)-derived protein–ligand interaction fingerprints, structural diversity assessment, and expert manual inspection.MolDockLab was validated through both a retrospective and a prospective case study. In the retrospective evaluation on epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), the chosen pipeline achieved a Spearman correlation of 0.35 and an enrichment factor at 10% (EF₁₀%) of 1.51, both consistent with the calibration set, used for pipeline selection. In the prospective application to the energy coupling factor transporters (ECF-T), a challenging transmembrane target featuring a dynamic, membrane-embedded cryptic binding site and no co-crystallized ligand, the optimal pipeline on the calibration set reached a Spearman correlation of 0.45 and an EF₁₀% of 3.13. Subsequent post-processing enabled the identification and in vitro confirmation of two chemically novel active compounds, which their potencies rival those of the best ECF-T inhibitors reported to date.Application to a challenging case study demonstrates that MolDockLab effectively enhances hit identification by tailoring SBVS workflows to individual targets. While the framework improves robustness and reproducibility, its performance remains dependent on the availability of an adequate calibration set for pipeline selection.

papers.title: BigMixSolDB: Extraction of a solubility database in solvent mixtures with an uncertainty-quantified large language model-based pipeline
papers.abstract: The rapidly expanding body of chemical literature contains physical data scattered across unstructured text and complex tables in thousands of publications. Translating this information into machinereadable formats is essential for training data-driven chemical models. The lack of uncertainty quantification in computationally extracted datasets make manual extraction and curation still necessary. We here address this challenge and present an uncertainty-quantified data extraction pipeline. Our fully automated pipeline utilizes large language models (LLMs) to extract complex tabular and textual chemical data directly from scientific PDFs. We systematically assess several modern LLMs and document-to-text conversion frameworks. We benchmark the uncertainty in extracted data by comparison of our computationally extracted databases with large, existing databases on solubility that are manually curated. Our pipeline achieve between 93 and 79% of the literature contained data, with extraction errors being on par with aleatoric limits that exist in the manually curated databases. We showcase the utility of our pipeline by deploying the optimized pipeline across a diverse corpus of 2,793 articles to generate BigMixSolDB, a comprehensive database on solubility in complex mixtures. BigMixSolDB comprises over 325,000 filtered solubility entries spanning single, binary, and ternary solvent systems. Our results demonstrate how integrated LLM-based pipelines can be used for literature data extraction that is comparable with manual curation. We envision these frameworks can be used for large-scale, accurate extraction of literature data into datasets for machine learning applications.

papers.title: One-Shot Reaction: Controlling Ultrafast Reactions in Coexistence Flow Conditions
Hydrogen-Bond Networks and Proton Transfer in Choline Geranate: Insights from IR Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Choline–geranate (CAGE) systems have attracted considerable interest due to their remarkable performance in biomedical and drug-delivery applications, yet their microscopic structure remains incompletely understood.
