In particular, the nature of the interaction between geranate (GE) and geranic acid (AGE) in CAGE formulations with excess acid has been the subject of ongoing debates, with spectroscopic evidence suggesting proton transfer but not resolving whether the proton is symmetrically shared or dynamically exchanged between the carboxylate groups. In this work, we combine experimental attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared (ATR–FTIR) spectroscopy with theoretical vibrational spectra derived from ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations to elucidate the hydrogen-bond network and local structural organization in CAGE at 1:1 and 1:2 choline-to-acid ratios. The simulations are performed at a representative water content of 8 wt%, while the experimental IR spectra are recorded over a range of water contents to assess the effect of hydration. Structural analysis of the AIMD trajectories reveals a dynamic hydrogen-bond network in which proton transfer between AGE and GE occurs intermittently, consistent with a rattling proton rather than a symmetrically shared configuration. The calculated infrared (IR) spectra reflect this behavior through the coexistence of vibrational signatures characteristic of both carboxylate and carboxylic acid groups. Experimental IR spectra corroborate these findings, showing persistent carboxylate and carboxylic acid features across compositions and water contents, with no evidence for a delocalized proton-bound dicarboxylate species. Together, the combined experimental and theoretical results provide a consistent structural picture of CAGE, reconciling previously reported nuclear magnetic resonance observations of proton transfer with the vibrational signatures observed in IR spectroscopy and clarifying the role of proton dynamics in these systems.

papers.title: Stepwise Ring Expansion as a Biosynthetic Strategy for Macrocycle Construction
papers.abstract: Macrocyclic formation in natural products is typically understood to proceed through direct macrocyclization reactions. Here we demonstrate that complex macrocycles can instead be constructed through stepwise ring expansion of a pre-formed smaller scaffold. Genetic and biochemical analyses of luminamicin (1) biosynthesis revealed that a 10-membered ring is progressively transformed into a 14-membered macrocycle through two mechanistically distinct ring expansion steps. This process involves a cofactor-independent intramolecular acyl transfer and a radical-mediated oxidative rearrangement, which together reorganize a pre-assembled intermediate into the final macrocyclic framework. This stepwise remodeling strategy contrasts with canonical macrocyclization logic and provides a solution to the entropic and conformational constraints associated with the formation of large rings. More broadly, these findings establish stepwise ring expansion as a previously unrecognized biosynthetic strategy for constructing complex macrocycles and suggest new strategies for their chemical synthesis.

papers.title: Regulation of Fast Reversible Electronic Energy Transfer in Rotaxane through Zn(II) Ion-Driven Ring Shuttling
papers.abstract: We report the synthesis of a Zn(II)-ions-switchable [2]rotaxane which can modulate an intramolecular reversible electronic energy transfer (REET) between two mechanically linked pyrene- and ruthenium complex-based chromophores. This system was designed to control this photophysical process through the mechanical bond by increasing/decreasing chromophores distance following addition/removal of metallic ions. NMR spectroscopy analyses showed it can exist as a dynamically locked Zn(II)-containing system, where both chromophores are far apart in space, and a metal-free co-conformers mixture in a biased dynamic equilibrium, where both chromophores are closer in space, by subsequent addition of Zn(II) ions and KCN. Additional spectroscopic analyses highlighted how ruthenium complex triplet excited state lifetime is highly dependent of chromophores distance with an approximate 1.8-fold increase of ruthenium complex 615 nm emission upon Zn(II) ions excess addition. More specifically, it revealed how the excitation energy is more distributed to the ruthenium complex upon Zn(II) ions addition and less toward the pyrene unit, which can stock part of this energy as a quasi-isoenergetic “reservoir” in metal-free rotaxane. This research work represents an advancement towards the development of new tools for lifetime-based chemosensing and photosensitizer.

papers.title: defermi: A tool for computing and visualizing point-defect equilibria, bridging computational and experimental users
papers.abstract: Using computational methods to study defect thermodynamics is a powerful alternative to the assumptions-based defect chemistry approach. Currently available tools for the computation and visualization of point-defect equilibria primarily focus on DFT high-throughput schemes, resulting in a significant entry barrier. To bridge the gap between computational applications and the more experimentally focused defect chemistry approach, we report defermi, a Python package with a graphical user interface. The GUI is designed to provide fast and consistent workflows for plotting formation energies and charge transition levels, and for computing Brouwer and doping diagrams. The Python API provides the same high-level interface, while offering additional customization capabilities, including full control over the routines used to compute formation energies and defect concentrations. This opens the door to extending the current computational approach to include temperature and volume dependence in defect formation energies, which are generally neglected in ab initio approaches.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Chimeric Switching (NEX) Stabilizes Binding Free Energy Calculations Across Chemical Space
papers.abstract: Accurate and efficient prediction of protein–ligand binding free energies remains a barrier to the routine use of physics-based modeling in drug discovery. Although alchemical free energy methods can achieve high accuracy, their applicability is often limited by computational cost and chemical diversity. Here we present Nonequilibrium Chimeric Switching (NEX), a general free energy framework that leverages nonphysical states as endpoints in nonequilibrium transformations. In this work, we investigate one realization of NEX that integrates nonequilibrium statistical mechanics with a dual-topology alchemical transfer formulation for relative binding free energy calculations. By routing bidirectional nonequilibrium switches through a chimeric intermediate, NEX improves phase-space overlap and stabilizes free energy estimation. NEX achieves accurate and reproducible predictions across protein–ligand benchmarks, with most results within 1 kcal mol −1 of experiment. Comparative analysis shows that the chimeric intermediate is critical, reducing work-distribution variance, improving numerical stability, and outperforming direct nonequilibrium switching at equivalent cost. NEX also delivers competitive performance on a challenging scaffold hopping benchmark without manual intervention or system-specific tuning. The chemical flexibility and numerical stability of NEX position it as a scalable engine for hit-to-lead and lead optimization workflows, enabling reliable deployment in future autonomous, agentic drug discovery systems.

papers.title: From 2D Graphs to Sub-Unit pKa: Nine Iterations to Beat MolGpKa on Both Scaffolds and Sulfonamides
papers.abstract: Accurate pKa prediction for drug-like molecules remains a significant gap between com- mercial tools (Epik ∼0.5 RMSE, MoKa ∼0.4 RMSE) and open-source methods, particularly for sulfonamides and heterocyclic N–H compounds prevalent in medicinal chemistry. We present a systematic nine-iteration ablation converging on a routed ensemble that outperforms MolGpKa on both general scaffolds and sulfonamides simultaneously—the first open-source model to do so. Starting from a 2D molecular graph baseline (v1, SAMPL7 RMSE 3.48), we isolate each variable: global xTB descriptors help scaffolds but not sulfonamides (v2); data augmentation fails (v2-aug); per-atom Mulliken charges help sulfonamides but hurt scaffolds (v3); routing combines both (v4, SAMPL7 2.19). We then identify the architectural gap with MolGpKa: per-atom pKa output targets trained on microscopic data. Per-atom output alone fails with macroscopic labels (v5). Microscopic labels from Uni-pKa improve scaffolds but not sulfonamides (v6). Merging microscopic and macroscopic data with a mixed loss produces the first model with no tradeoff (v7, scaffold 1.31, SAMPL7 1.32). Adding full xTB charge coverage solves sulfonamides (v8, SAMPL7 0.535) but hurts scaffolds. The final routed ensemble (v9) achieves scaffold RMSE 1.255 (R2 0.878) and SAMPL7 RMSE 0.535 (R2 0.948)—beating MolGpKa by 62% on scaffolds and 45% on sulfonamides, with calibrated uncertainty and zero failure rate. All models trained on open data (IUPAC, ChEMBL, Uni-pKa) with open-source tools (xTB, RDKit, Chemprop).

papers.title: QFlux: An Open-Source Toolkit for Quantum Dynamics Simulations on Quantum Computers. Part V - Adaptive Variational Quantum Algorithms for Open Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Simulating open quantum systems remains one of the most demanding problems in quantum dynamics, as environmental interactions lead to non-unitary evolution that challenges standard quantum simulation techniques. Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) offer a practical way forward by combining classical optimization with quantum hardware, making them well suited for near-term devices. Here, in Part V of the QFlux implementation series, we introduce adaptive variational-ansatz methods for solving the Lindblad master equation. This tutorial presents the Python-based qmad module of the QFlux toolkit, which is designed to help students and researchers easily build and explore adaptive VQA strategies. The tutorial walks through each step of the workflow and applies the methods to two illustrative examples. The first is the amplitude-damping channel, which models spontaneous emission in a two-level system. The second is the Fenna-Matthews-Olson (FMO) complex, a prominent model for excitonic energy transfer in photosynthesis. The two workflows utilizing adaptive variational approaches implemented here are the unrestricted adaptive variational quantum dynamics (UAVQD) scheme and the stochastic Schrödinger equation (SSE) based trajectory method. By working through these examples, readers gain both intuition and hands-on experience with variational techniques for simulating dissipative quantum dynamics.

papers.title: Water molecular dynamics during dough heating by Fast Field Cycling Nuclear Magnetic Resonance
Ultrasound-Assisted Extraction of Alkaloids: Comparison and Key Process Parameters.
papers.abstract: Alkaloids are nitrogen-containing secondary metabolites produced by organisms such as plants and fungi, as a defence mechanism. Besides preventing prey from attack, these alkaloids also have important therapeutic properties such as for treating Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases in human beings. They are primarily extracted from plants using different extraction techniques. Among several methods, ultrasonic-assisted extraction (UAE) employs cavitation to extract bioactive compounds. This technique possesses several benefits such as short extraction time and low energy consumption over others methods. The main objectives of this review are: 1. Comparison of the UAE for evaluating its advantages and disadvantages relative to other methods, such as microwave-assisted extraction, Soxhlet extraction, percolation, and maceration, 2. The use of greener solvents such as ionic liquids (ILs) and deep eutectic solvents (DES) to enhance the effectiveness of extraction using this technique, and 3. To study the parameters affecting the extraction efficiency of UAE for alkaloids.

papers.title: Enzymatic synthesis of glyco-DNA equipped with oligosaccharides and charged monosaccharides
papers.abstract: The therapeutic and biotechnological utility of synthetic oligonucleotides is constrained by the limited chemical diversity of canonical nucleotides and their susceptibility to nuclease degradation. Inspired by the hypermodified genomes of bacteriophages, where 5-glycosylated pyrimidines confer protection against host restriction enzymes, we report the design and synthesis of a library of 5-glycosylated 2′-deoxyuridine triphosphates (dNTPs 1-7) bearing mono- (either neutral or charged moieties) and oligosaccharides affixed to position 5 of the nucleobase. The resulting glyco-modified nucleotides were well incorporated into DNA by different template-dependent polymerases but much less by template-independent polymerases. While the presence of charged residues did not affect incorporation efficiency, longer side-chains of the oligosaccharide moiety considerably reduced the incorporation yield of nucleotides. On the other hand, the presence of the saccharides did not affect the serum stability of the 71-mer sequences containing the glyco-modified dNTPs, and were only slightly destabilizing duplex DNA. Interestingly, the presence of oligosaccharides highly increased the stability against the effect of the BfaI endonuclease. These findings show that 5-glycosylation with oligosaccharides expands the chemical alphabet of DNA without disrupting the base-pairing, offering a robust strategy for developing next-generation glyco-aptamers with enhanced endonuclease-stability and novel saccharides-mediated recognition capabilities.

papers.title: Fine-Tuning the Pressure Response and Mechanical Properties of Azobenzene‑ and Stilbene‑Based Zr‑Metal-Organic Frameworks Through Multivariate Design
papers.abstract: The rich chemistry of molecular framework materials allows for precise control of physicochemical properties by structural design of the framework topology and the underlying building blocks. In this contribution, we demonstrate for the first time the manipulation of mechanical properties in a series of mixed-linker Zr-based MOFs incorporating azobenzene- and stilbenebased linkers. We synthesized a series of mixed-linker MOFs with high porosity and investigated the formation of solid-solutions with random linker mixing by hyper spectral Raman imaging, and powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD). We further investigate for the first time linker disorder in a mixedlinker system by single crystal X-ray diffraction. Within this series of mixed-linker MOFs, we investigate the pressure response by in situ PXRD and molecular simulations and show that the bulk modulus can be finely tuned in the range of 9 to 5 GPa by varying the linker composition. Our multivariate design strategy provides a versatile tool to tune the pressure response of framework materials and may give rise to counterintuitive mechanical properties in future systems.

papers.title: Coordination Interference for Overcoming Catalyst Poisoning in Asymmetric Hydrophosphinylation
papers.abstract: Transition-metal-catalyzed carbon–phosphorus (C−P) bond formation stands as a pivotal and promising frontier in modern organic synthesis. However, its progress has long been hindered by a critical bottleneck: the competitive coordination of phosphorus species to metal active sites, which induces irreversible catalyst deactivation and severely constrains breakthroughs in this field. Herein, we report an innovative, general "coordination-interference" strategy that employs oxophilic Lewis acids such as lanthanum triflate (La(OTf) 3 ) and cobalt triflate (Co(OTf) 2 ) to address this core challenge. This approach effectively overcomes palladium catalyst poisoning in the asymmetric hydrophosphinylation of 1,3-enynes and conjugated dienes with secondary phosphine oxides (SPOs). Mechanistic studies reveal that oxophilic Lewis acids selectively bind to the oxygen atom of SPOs, dynamically tuning their coordination capacity while markedly lowering the concentration of free SPOs in the reaction mixture. Consequently, unproductive coordination of SPOs to palladium active sites is suppressed, fundamentally mitigating catalyst poisoning and ensuring efficient reaction progression. This strategy exhibits a broad substrate scope, excellent functional group tolerance, and maintains high efficiency even at ultralow palladium catalyst loadings, offering a versatile solution to advance C−P bond construction.

papers.title: Architectural Evolution in In Silico Biopharmaceutical Engineering Methods:
authors: David Ferguson, BS, MS, MRSB MRSC
papers.abstract: Background. Deep learning methods and structural prediction algorithms have expanded the scope of in silico antibody engineering. However, the computational requirements for residue-level structural optimization differ substantially from those required for formulation design, delivery system modeling, and pharmacokinetic simulation. This paper describes and compares two successive versions of a web-based biopharmaceutical engineering platform, AntibodyForge Pro, which address these two stages of the drug development workflow. Methods. The computational architectures, mathematical frameworks, and AI pipelines of AntibodyForge Pro v26.0 (BioNeMo Edition) and AntibodyForge Pro v36 were systematically analyzed. Version 26.0 uses a v16 3000-atom NeRF engine, SpatialHash O(n) collision detection, and a 12-step NVIDIA BioNeMo pipeline incorporating ESM-2, AlphaFold2, ProteinMPNN, DiffDock, and MolMIM. Version 36 employs a 15-step formulation-centric pipeline introducing the Reaction Coordinate (RC) Engine, PDB Family GeoMapper, and Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) Continuum, alongside modules for Antibody-Drug Conjugate (ADC) design, nanocarrier formulation, and multi-compartmental PK/PD simulation. Results. Version 26.0 is designed for residue-level geometric optimization, with explicit Ramachandran backbone editing and high-fidelity multimeric assembly. Version 36 extends this architecture to encompass formulation and delivery, supporting Drug-to-Antibody Ratio (DAR) prediction via Poisson distributions, Critical Packing Parameter (CPP) calculations for vesicle geometry, and Target-Mediated Drug Disposition (TMDD) modeling via ordinary differential equations. Conclusions. The two versions are complementary. Version 26.0 is well-suited for early-stage structural design and quality control. Version 36 extends the design environment to encompass formulation, delivery, and in vivo pharmacological behavior, providing a more complete assessment of translational feasibility prior to experimental validation.

papers.title: Ion–Polymer Interactions Control Energetic Elasticity in TetraPEG Ion Gels
papers.abstract: Energetic elasticity arising from polymer–solvent interactions governs the mechanical response of polymer networks; however, its molecular origin in ion gels, i.e., polymer networks swollen with ionic liquids (ILs), remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the role of ion–polymer interactions in tetra-arm poly(ethylene glycol) (TetraPEG) ion gels prepared in ILs. By separating the elastic modulus into energetic ( G E ) and entropic ( G S ) contributions, we found that the ion gels exhibit negative energetic elasticity, similar to TetraPEG hydrogels. Comparative experiments using imidazolium- and pyrrolidinium-based ILs revealed that hydrogen bonding between PEG ether oxygen atoms and the imidazolium cations enhances the energetic contribution, whereas non-hydrogen-bonding pyrrolidinium cations provide only a minor contribution. Addition of Li salt decreased the shear modulus and changed both G E and G S through preferential Li + –PEG complexation, replacing hydrogen-bonding solvation and yielding more compact polymer conformations. At high Li salt concentrations, coordination of most ether oxygens to Li + suppresses conformational changes of the polymer chains upon deformation, leading to nearly constant G E and G S . These findings strongly support the view that the elasticity of ion gels is governed by molecular-level ion–polymer interactions and provide guidelines for tuning the mechanical properties of polymer gel electrolytes through ion coordination.

papers.title: Ligand Engineering of Dithiolate-Protected Au24Pt Nanoclusters for Improved Thermocatalytic Activity
papers.abstract: Thiolate-protected gold (Au) nanoclusters (NCs) are a well-established class of model NCs that have been extensively studied as catalysts for various reactions. However, many Au NCs feature surfaces completely passivated by ligands, leaving no exposed metal sites to serve as active centers. To address this issue, researchers have searched for methods to remove the ligands. However, simply introducing weakly bound ligands often compromises the structural stability of the NCs. In this study, we identified a novel Au NC that remains stable even with relatively weakly bound thiolate ligands by reinforcing the staple motifs through the introduction of dithiolate ligands. This Au NC exhibits excellent CO oxidation activity at relatively low temperatures, because the ligands can dissociate under relatively mild conditions. These findings show that advanced ligand engineering, beyond the metal core structure, significantly affects catalytic activity, providing a robust strategy for the design of diverse metal NC catalysts.

papers.title: Surface Decoration with Li Ions Enables Superprotonic Conductivity in Zr-Based Metal-Organic Polyhedra
papers.abstract: Proton conductors are essential for sustainable energy technologies, enabling efficient ion transport in electrochemical devices. Zr-based metal–organic polyhedra (MOPs) offer a distinctive platform as charge-neutral assemblies of cationic cages and Cl− counterions, creating intrinsic ionic microenvironment without acid doping. Here, we establish surface decoration as a powerful strategy to enhance proton transport in structurally distinct Zr-MOP solids, with the magnitude of enhancement dictated by packing structure. Li@UMOP-1 and Li@UMOP-11 exhibit superprotonic conductivities of 2.43 and 4.19 × 10−2 S cm−1, respectively, at 90% relative humidity (RH) and 95 °C, with Li@UMOP-11 representing the highest value reported to date for MOP-based proton conductors. Structural analyses and computations reveal that the topology-dependent positioning of Li+ ions governs water accessibility to the ionic sites. These findings establish packing-guided surface decoration as a design strategy for high-performance proton-conducting MOP solids.

papers.title: Computational Druggability Assessment of Mitochondrial Targets: Structure-Function Constraints and Binding Site Characterization
papers.abstract: Background : Precision drug design for mitochondrial disease requires a systematic evaluation of whether each drug target possesses a pharmacologically tractable binding site. Druggability is determined by the intersection of structural accessibility, ligand efficiency evidence, pharmacological precedent, and mitochondrial delivery feasibility. No comprehensive druggability map exists for the curated mitochondrial target landscape defined by the MitoCorex Chapter 2A.1 compendium. Methods : We performed computational and literature-based druggability assessment for all 25 targets from the MitoCorex pathway registry (Chapter 2A.2). Assessment integrated five dimensions: binding site type and geometry (from PDB structures and homology models), pocket accessibility (solvent exposure versus transmembrane embedding), ligand efficiency evidence (ChEMBL bioactivity database), pharmacological precedent (approved drugs, clinical-stage compounds, and validated tool compounds), and mitochondrial delivery feasibility (encoding locus, subcellular compartment, and known delivery strategies). Targets were stratified into three druggability tiers. Results : Fifteen targets achieved Tier 1 (high druggability), nine achieved Tier 2 (moderate druggability), and one achieved Tier 3 (low druggability). Five highest-priority targets were identified: DNM1L (DRP1; cytoplasmic GTPase, no delivery barrier, Mdivi-1 scaffold), PINK1 (kinase domain, clinical-stage kinetin), NFE2L2/Nrf2 (PPI target, bardoxolone Phase III), NDUFV1 (FMN enzyme, IACS-010759 clinical scaffold), and SDHA (FAD enzyme, dual TCA/OXPHOS relevance). Delivery analysis identified six targets requiring no mitochondrial targeting, nine requiring standard matrix-targeting peptide conjugation, and three for which gene therapy is the primary therapeutic strategy (mtDNA-encoded structural subunits). Mechanism of action classes covered GTPase modulators, kinase modulators, serine proteases, PPI disruptors, enzyme active sites, nucleotide analogs, transporters, and upstream transcriptional regulators. Conclusions : The MitoCorex target landscape is pharmacologically tractable: 60% of targets achieve high druggability and 36% achieve moderate druggability. The five highest-priority targets share favorable structural, delivery, and precedent profiles that support immediate molecule design by DrugSynth AI. The druggability registry (druggability_registry_v1.yaml) is deposited at Zenodo and functions as a structured input for Chapter 3.1 (defect modeling) and Chapter 4.1 (DrugSynth AI design engine specification).

papers.title: Unlocking the Chemical Space for Rechargeable Batteries with a Generative Solvent Design System
papers.abstract: Electrolyte discovery for rechargeable batteries today relies on heuristic trial-and-error or high-throughput screening of existing molecules. Here, we introduce a Generative Solvent Design System (GSDS) that integrates a graph-based deep molecular generator with machine-learning (ML) property predictors to design new rechargeable battery solvents de novo . We enable this by constructing a battery-specific prior dataset (Batt-SLM, 115,756 molecules) and fine-tuning a graph-based molecular generator using physics-informed ML surrogates for redox potential, viscosity, melting point, donor number, and dielectric constant. We validated the real-world performance of GSDS on the rediscovery of both fluorinated and phosphorus-containing compounds not seen during training. This allows us to propose application-specific candidates (top 0.2 ‰) fluorinated diluents and non-fluorinated weakly solvating electrolytes—that pass a posterior verification funnel including property evaluation, synthetic accessibility, novelty prioritization, and literature checks. We conclude that GSDS establishes a tractable first layer of a broader electrolyte-design framework and can be expanded toward salt-aware, interface-informed, and mixture-included optimization for next-generation rechargeable batteries.

papers.title: Porous Ionic Liquids for Sustainable Ammonia Synthesis
papers.abstract: Ammonia is a key chemical for agriculture and an emerging energy carrier, yet its conventional production via the Haber-Bosch process is energy intensive and contributes significantly to global CO2 emissions. The electrochemical synthesis of ammonia via the reduction of N2 offers a sustainable alternative but remains limited by low N2 solubility and competing hydrogen evolution in aqueous systems. In this context, enhancing N2 availability within a non aqueous electrolyte while maintaining suitable transport and electrochemical properties is critical. Here, we investigate porous ionic liquids formed by dispersing ZIF-8 nanoparticles into ionic liquids to enhance nitrogen solubility. These materials combine permanent porosity with the intrinsic properties of ionic liquids, including low volatility, tuneable solubility, and wide electrochemical stability. Gas sorption and electrochemical measurements, reported in this work, confirm pore accessibility and the stability of these heterogeneous electrolytes. Using polarizable molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate the solvation, partitioning and mobility of N2, isopropanol (proton source) and NH3 at the interface between the ionic liquid and the porous particles into three different porous ionic liqquids. We show that the incorporation of ZIF-8 provides accessible free volume for both N2 and NH3, while isopropanol is excluded from the pores. The simulations further reveal that N2 and NH3 remain mobile across the solid-liquid interface, highlighting the role of the pores as reversible gas reservoirs without hindering the reaction or product recovery. The choice of cation and anion of the ionic liquid strongly influences the ordering of the ions near the interface, creating a distinct solvation environment within the accessible surface cavities. This affects solute distribution and mobility across the interface, and therefore the transport properties. In particular, the pyrrolidinium cation promotes greater accessibility of the pores and mobility of solutes compared to the bulkier phosphonium cation. Overall, this work shows that polarizable molecular simulations are key to understand and to rationally design porous ionic liquids tailored to be used as electrolytes for the electrochemical synthesis of ammonia.

papers.title: AI-Assisted De Novo Design of Small Molecule Candidates Targeting Five Priority Mitochondrial Proteins: A MitoCorex Proof of Concept
papers.abstract: Background : Precision drug design for genetically defined mitochondrial disease requires generation of candidate molecules with specific rescue mechanisms directed at the molecular defect produced by each pathogenic variant. Prior chapters of the MitoCorex pipeline established five priority targets with complete design briefs: DNM1L (DRP1; GOF A395D stalk inhibitor), PINK1 (LOF G309D kinase activator), NFE2L2/Nrf2 (Keap1-GOF PPI disruptor), NDUFV1 (LOF R94C FMN-binding stabilizer), and SDHA (LOF R589W FAD-binding stabilizer). This chapter reports the first-wave de novo molecule design for these five targets using the DrugSynth AI pipeline. Methods: Fifteen candidate molecules (three per target) were designed using the DrugSynth AI sevenmodality generative chemistry framework operating on the design briefs from Chapter 3.1 and structural profiles from Chapter 3.2. Design modalities applied include scaffold-based optimization (M1), fragment growing (M2), bioisosteric replacement (M3), pharmacophore-constrained generation (M4), and mutantselective design (M6). For NDUFV1 and SDHA candidates, mitochondria-targeted prodrug design (M7) was applied. All candidates were evaluated by RDKit for physicochemical properties and screened for PAINS (pan-assay interference). Results: All 15 candidates passed Lipinski Rule of Five criteria and PAINS screening. Molecular weights ranged 215 to 380 Da (target ceiling 480 Da); cLogP ranged -0.26 to 3.68; QED ranged 0.356 to 0.895. Three rescue classes are represented by mechanistically distinct design strategies: three DRP1 stalkdomain inhibitors (DSA series) exploiting the oligomerization interface inaccessible to prior GTPasedomain inhibitors; three PINK1 G309D-selective activators (PKA series) built on the kinetin purine scaffold with mutant-selective modifications; three Keap1 kelch domain PPI disruptors (KND series) with molecular weight 267-327 Da representing the most compact reported non-covalent Keap1 binders; three NDUFV1 FMN-binding stabilizers (NDS series) employing phosphonate, methylphosphonate, and carboxylate bioisosteres of the FMN phosphate group; and three SDHA FAD-binding stabilizers (SDA series) addressing the R589W pyrophosphate coordination loss. Conclusions: The 15 first-wave candidates demonstrate the DrugSynth AI pipeline's capacity to generate structurally diverse, pharmacologically grounded, and computationally validated molecules across four distinct rescue mechanism classes. Ten candidates are designated for advancement to Stage 7 in silico validation (Chapter 5.1). The molecule candidates registry (molecule_candidates_v1.yaml) is deposited at Harvard Dataverse with full provenance documentation linking each candidate to its upstream design brief, variant model, and pathway context.

papers.title: A Unified Topological Framework for Representation and Construction of Generalized Carbon Nanobelts
papers.abstract: The expanding structural and topological diversity of macrocyclic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, including carbon nanobelts (CNBs), cycloarenes, and their twisted analogs, demands a unified framework to overcome fragmented nomenclature schemes. Here, we present a topology-driven framework that unifies these systems as generalized CNBs by conceptualizing them as segments excised from generalized carbon nanocones with varying opening angles, spanning tubular, conical, and flat geometries within a single descriptive space. Central to this approach is the introduction of compact, bijective path codes that provide a mathematically rigorous, machine-tractable representation of annulation patterns. We further establish a simple topological parity rule, whereby the parity of positive path segments serves as a robust invariant distinguishing Hückel and Möbius topologies. Building on this representation, we develop an automated construction protocol, implemented in the open-source beltopkit package, that converts path codes directly into three-dimensional geometries. To this end, a novel topology-constrained optimization algorithm is devised, allowing reliable generation of highly strained and multiply twisted macrocycles. As a representative demonstration of our approach, exhaustive enumeration of 12-ring generalized CNB topoisomers reveals a rich isomeric landscape and identifies multiple previously unrecognized low-energy structures competitive with experimentally synthesized infinitene. This framework provides a computationally tractable foundation for integrating complex macrocyclic nanocarbons into cheminformatics and machine learning workflows, enabling large-scale, data-driven exploration of new structures and synthetic targets.

papers.title: In Situ Polymerized Polyaniline in Redox-Active Metal–Organic Polyhedra for Supercapacitors
papers.abstract: The introduction of porosity into polyaniline (PANI) is key for enhancing its capacitive performance because both electrons and counterions need to migrate through the whole material during the charge-discharge process. Here, we demonstrated the incorporation of redox-active metal-organic polyhedra (MOPs) as intrinsic porous materials into PANI. Two redox-active and structurally stable ruthenium-based MOPs, SO3-RuMOP and t-Bu-RuMOP, were employed as additives during the solution-phase oxidative polymerization of aniline. This approach produced two series of nanocomposites with various ratios between MOPs and PANI. Dynamic light scattering measurements were used to trace the hydrodynamic diameters of solid products formed during the polymerization process and to investigate the effect of different MOPs on the process. Electron microscopy and infrared spectroscopy were used to quantify the MOPs loading in each composite. Electrochemical measurements of pristine materials and all PANI@MOP composites were conducted in acidic aqueous electrolytes to study the electrochemistry of both MOPs and PANI in the composites. Composites with the optimal capacitive performance in both series, PANI@SO3-RuMOP (1:0.035) and PANI@t-Bu-RuMOP (1:0.07), achieve specific capacitances of 425 F/g and 414 F/g at 0.5 mA/cm2, respectively. These capacitive performances significantly outperform the pristine PANI (339 F/g). The PANI@SO3-RuMOP (1:0.035) composite also exhibited better rate capability and higher long-term capacitance retention than pristine PANI. Findings here shed light on the use of redox-active MOPs as the minor additive during in situ polymerization to synthesize conducting polymers with enhanced capacitive performance for electrochemical energy storage devices.

papers.title: Balancing Data Quantity and Quality: Evaluating Curation Strategies for Bioactivity Prediction
papers.abstract: Building good machine-learning (ML) models to predict the bioactivity of novel chemical matter remains a challenging task. Accurate models require a training set with a large number of diverse compounds and a low level of noise. When extracting data from public databases such as ChEMBL, different levels of curation rigor may be applied, resulting in training sets of varying size, diversity, and, presumably, noise levels. It is not possible to know a priori whether increasing the size of the dataset at the cost of adding more noise improves model generalization. To assess this trade-off, we compare three data curation and modeling approaches: (1) models trained on data for a single target, (2) models trained on target-specific data further restricted to a single set of assay conditions, and (3) multitask learning (MTL) models where each assay condition is treated as a separate task. This MTL approach was designed to bridge the gap between data quantity and quality. Graph neural networks (GNN) and random forests (RF) regressors are evaluated via a leave-assay-out strategy to minimize noise in the test sets. Our results show no meaningful performance differences between these curation strategies, suggesting that for lead-optimization tasks, increasing data quantity at the expense of label consistency does not improve generalization. Notably, the MTL approach also failed to provide a performance advantage. Additionally, we find that GNNs exhibit high seed-dependent variability in connection with the comparatively small training sets common for bioactivity measurements, highlighting the necessity of multi-seed evaluation for robust model assessment.

papers.title: Advancing the CL&Pol Polarizable Force Field for Accurate Modeling of Mg2+, Ca2+ and Zn2+ Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Divalent cations such as Mg2+, Ca2+ or Zn2+ are promising candidates for powerful and affordable post-Li batteries due to their high natural abundance and an expected two-electron transfer per charge carrier. But an accurate representation of divalent cations in electrolytes by molecular dynamics simulations remains challenging due to effects of their high charge density. For ionic systems such as the ones studied here, a molecular interaction model with explicit polarization terms, using Drude induced dipoles, largely improves the representation of equilibrium and transport properties when compared to fixed-charge models. Some issues regarding over-polarization of the induced dipoles require attention. Thole and Tang-Toennies screening (or damping) functions are parameterized to avoid the over-polarization effects, and were validated by simulating MgCl2, CaCl2 and ZnCl2 salts in aqueous solutions. Followingly this, simulations with model electrolytes based on two commonly used solvents — dimethoxyethane (G1) and ethylene carbonate (EC) — were performed. The simulations of the G1 and EC electrolytes highlight significant differences in structural and dynamic behaviors between Ca2+, Mg2+, and Zn2+, depending on the scaling of the Lennard-Jones well-depth, which is performed when adding explicit induced dipoles to a non-polarizable force field. The study of the impact of this scaling, investigated for both systems G1 and EC, provides a framework for future simulations involving divalent cations with the CL&Pol force field. These results, coupled with the transferability of the CL&Pol model, offer an efficient tool to simulate a broad range of systems involving divalent ions, from biological media to electrolytes for novel energy storage devices.

papers.title: Emergent Synthesis of Life’s Molecular Toolkit from Bare Atoms via Free-Market Agent-Based Modeling
papers.abstract: We present a computational "time machine" that replays prebiotic chemistry: starting from bare C, H, O, and N atoms, a free-market agent-based model grounded in physics — Bond Dissociation Energies (BDE) and Universal Force Field (UFF) strain evaluation — discovers thermodynamically favorable reaction pathways and spontaneously initiates the synthesis of life’s molecular toolkit: all 12 feasible amino acids, all 5 nucleobases (the letters of RNA and DNA), the complete formose sugar chain from formaldehyde to ribose to glucose, Krebs cycle intermediates (pyruvate, succinate, malate), and the first tripeptide (Gly-Gly-Gly). The simulation runs on a standard laptop in under 5 minutes, discovering up to 260 independent synthesis routes for a single amino acid. No target molecules are specified; all products emerge purely from thermodynamic drive. Amino acid formulas appear 14× earlier than random chance would predict, confirming the thermodynamic inevitability hypothesis. Beyond origins-of-life research, the framework offers a rapid exploration tool for novel synthesis pathway design in modern chemistry.

papers.title: Direct evidence of a lanthanide-tellurium bond in [K(18-crown 6)(Cp′′2LnTe3)] with Ln = La, Ce, and Nd
papers.abstract: Using non-classical divalent lanthanide precursors as multi-electron reducing agents, complexes, [K(18-crown-6)(Cp” 2 LnTe 3 )], with Ln = La, Ce, and Nd, Cp” = 1,3-bis-(trimethylsilyl)cyclopentadienyl, were synthesized and investigated to elucidate the mechanism of lanthanide-tellurium bonding and the role of 4 f -element electron density in stabilizing small chalcogenide chains. Density-Functional Theory (DFT) reveals that the frontier molecular orbitals of these complexes are predominantly localized on the [Te 3 ] 2- fragment, while the trivalent lanthanide ions stabilize the tellurium chain through weak but measurable metal-ligand interactions. To experimentally resolve these interactions, we focus on complementary ligand- and metal-centered X-ray spectroscopic approaches. Ln L 3 -edge high-resolution XANES (HR-XANES) and valence-band resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (VB-RIXS) demonstrate that the Ln-Te/C interaction has substantial Ln 5 d orbitals contribution, particularly for the Ln-Te bond, and remains largely constant across the three complexes. DFT-based bond analysis provides a mechanistic interpretation of these trends. The Ln–C interaction exhibits increasing electron density at the bond critical point and a higher delocalization index (QTAIM analysis) from the lighter to the heavier lanthanides, reflecting enhanced Ln 4 f participation within an energy-driven covalency regime. The Ln–Te interaction is predominantly electrostatic, with meaningful orbital contributions arising mainly from Ln 5 d participation within an orbital-overlap driven covalency regime. These results demonstrate that the Ln-C and Ln-Te bonding in the present complexes follow fundamentally distinct covalency mechanisms, which together enable the stabilization and isolation of the small [Te 3 ] 2- fragment chain.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Chimeric Switching (NEX) Stabilizes Binding Free Energy Calculations Across Chemical Space
papers.abstract: Accurate and efficient prediction of protein–ligand binding free energies remains a barrier to the routine use of physics-based modeling in drug discovery. Although alchemical free energy methods can achieve high accuracy, their applicability is often limited by computational cost and chemical diversity. Here we present Nonequilibrium Chimeric Switching (NEX), a general free energy framework that leverages nonphysical states as endpoints in nonequilibrium transformations. In this work, we investigate one realization of NEX that integrates nonequilibrium statistical mechanics with a dual-topology alchemical transfer formulation for relative binding free energy calculations. By routing bidirectional nonequilibrium switches through a chimeric intermediate, NEX improves phase-space overlap and stabilizes free energy estimation. NEX achieves accurate and reproducible predictions across protein–ligand benchmarks, with most results within 1 kcal mol −1 of experiment. Comparative analysis shows that the chimeric intermediate is critical, reducing work-distribution variance, improving numerical stability, and outperforming direct nonequilibrium switching at equivalent cost. NEX also delivers competitive performance on a challenging scaffold-hopping benchmark without manual intervention or system-specific tuning. The chemical flexibility and numerical stability of NEX position it as a scalable engine for hit-to-lead and lead optimization workflows, enabling reliable deployment in future autonomous, agentic drug discovery systems.

papers.title: Pre-Analytical Integrity in Ignitable Liquid Residue Casework: Decision-Grade Reporting
papers.abstract: In ignitable liquid residue (ILR) casework, the credibility of chromatographic interpretation is often determined before a sample reaches the instrument, through how exhibits are recognised, recovered, packaged, sealed, transported, stored, and documented. This article argues that standards, guidance, and relevant literature converge on a common forensic consequence: claim strength in ILR reporting should not exceed the pre-analytical integrity demonstrably preserved in the case record. It therefore offers a harmonised governance reading of continuity, contamination control, preservation, representativeness, and documented deviation across the scene-to-laboratory pathway. Where identity, continuity, condition, or control evidence is missing, weakened, or not retrievable, reporting language should narrow accordingly rather than absorb the gap into analytical confidence. Operational categories are used only as shorthand for bounded reporting consequences. The manuscript develops the ILR threat model, traces the critical control points from scene recovery to laboratory receipt and analysis, links pre-analytical limits to uncertainty and decision-rule discipline, and shows how compact implementation tools can translate this governance logic into routine casework. The central claim is straightforward: decision-grade ILR reporting depends on auditable control of the pre-analytical chain and explicit restraint when that chain is incomplete.

papers.title: Protein titration benchmark of CHARMM36, Amber99sb-ildn, OPLS-AA/M, and Martini 2 force fields for constant pH molecular dynamics in GROMACS
papers.abstract: Constant pH molecular dynamics (CpHMD) has emerged as a powerful method for simulating pH-dependent processes in proteins and other biomolecules. The original implementation of the PME-based CpHMD in the GROMACS software included the CHARMM36 and Martini 2 force fields for treating the titratable amino acids in proteins. As requested by the user community, this work contains the parameterization of titratable residues for the Amber99sb-ildn and OPLS-AA/M force fields. In addition to carefully carrying out the parameterization process, the performance of the different force fields in the scope of CpHMD is evaluated by performing computational titrations for a set of benchmark proteins. The calculated pKa values obtained using all force fields yield an average root mean square error of about 1 pH unit in comparison to experimental pKa values, which is in line with previous CpHMD benchmarks. The presented work expands the applicability of the PME-based CpHMD method in GROMACS, and guides the researchers aiming to perform accurate and efficient CpHMD simulations.

papers.title: A Physically Informed QUBO Model for π-Stacking Interactions in Molecular Docking Problems
papers.abstract: In Computer Aided Drug Discovery (CADD), Molecular Docking (MD) is a computational technique aiming at predicting the most energetically favorable conformation of a ligand to its target macromolecule. Recent advances in quantum computing have led to the development of new molecular docking models. In particular, quantum annealing has motivated the formulation of physically informed docking frameworks that can be encoded within discrete optimization paradigms such as QUBO formulations. This work introduces a new Hamiltonian term that captures π-stacking interactions between aromatic systems, a class of non-covalent forces essential in biomolecular recognition yet often oversimplified in traditional docking approaches. High-level computational chemistry simulations were performed on HPC infrastructures to obtain reference interaction energy profiles for benzene dimers, which were then used to guide the formulation of the proposed term. The extended model was tested through simulated annealing on systems involving benzene and aromatic amino-acid residues (tyrosine, phenylalanine, and tryptophan). The results show that the new term consistently drives the optimization toward correct binding conformations, demonstrating the importance of explicitly incorporating πstacking effects in discrete docking formulations and supporting future developments in quantum-enhanced molecular optimization.

papers.title: Text-to-Flowsheet: An Automated LLM-Pipeline for Digitization and Simulation of Chemical Processes with Expert-Level Accuracy
papers.abstract: Converting unstructured natural language descriptions into structured process flowsheets is a fundamental bottleneck in chemical engineering, traditionally requiring years of expert training. While large language models (LLMs) show promise in text comprehension, their ability to match human expertise in modeling complex chemical process flowsheets remains unproven. Here, we present a rigorous benchmark comparing a fully automated LLM-powered digitization pipeline against the collective performance of 50 chemical engineering experts. Our pipeline leverages LLMs to extract process structures from text and formalize them as flowsheet graphs. To handle the inherent ambiguities of natural language, we utilize constrained, step-by-step prompting augmented with thermodynamic property calculations. Subsequently, the digitized flowsheet graphs are automatically translated into the flowsheeting software Aspen Plus to compute rigorous mass and energy balances. Black-box optimization on subprocess structures is used to estimate unknown parameters and ensure simulation convergence, completing the pipeline from text to converged process simulation. For the first time, we demonstrate that an automated pipeline can achieve expert-level accuracy in process digitization. Using a unique, newly-generated dataset of 101 expert-drawn flowsheets, we show that our LLM-assisted approach faithfully captures process topology and operating conditions even in the face of incomplete information. This work provides a robust, validated framework for the large-scale digitization of chemical production literature, contributing a transformative tool and dataset for the community to accelerate automated process design and assessment.

papers.title: Harnessing Iodonium Ylides as Metalloradicophiles in Metalloradical Catalysis: Fe(TPP)Cl-Catalyzed Doyle-Kirmse Rearrangement and Transylidation
papers.abstract: We report a simple and efficient process for generating homoallyl sulfides and selenides through the Fe(TPP)Cl-catalyzed formation of S,C-sulfonium ylides, which subsequently undergo the Doyle-Kirmse reaction, utilizing iodonium ylides as safer metalloradicophiles, an alternative to construct valuable C–S, C–Se, and C–C bonds. The reaction was performed under benign conditions, with a short reaction time, broad substrate scope, and good tolerance of diverse functional groups. The mechanistic and computational investigation revealed that the reactions follow a metalloradical catalytic pathway to form sulfonium ylides, which then undergo a [2,3]-Sigmatropic rearrangement to yield homoallylic sulfanes, while transylidation was achieved with benzyl(phenyl)sulfanes, and N-(phenylthio)benzamides to afford sulfonium ylides.

papers.title: Lateral Cyano Substitution as a Tool for Tuning Negative Dielectric Anisotropy in High-Birefringence Liquid Crystals
papers.abstract: A series of ten novel liquid crystalline compounds based on oligophenyl and tolane cores bearing laterally positioned cyano groups has been designed, synthesised and systematically investigated. The molecular architecture was tailored by varying the number and position of lateral nitrile substituents, as well as the degree of core extension and terminal functionalisation, in order to elucidate structure - property relationships governing mesomorphic, optical and dielectric behaviour. The majority of the compounds exhibit exclusively nematic phases, while no smectic ordering was observed, indicating that lateral cyano substitution effectively disrupts layered packing. The introduction of cyano groups significantly enhances dielectric permittivity and induces negative dielectric anisotropy, with its magnitude strongly dependent on both the number and location of nitrile substituents. At the same time, extended π-conjugated cores provide relatively high birefringence (Δn ≈ 0.24), despite the presence of strong transverse dipoles, which typically reduce optical anisotropy. Comparative analysis reveals that excessive lateral polarity destabilises the nematic phase and narrows its temperature range, highlighting the need for a balance between dipolar interactions and molecular anisotropy. The obtained results demonstrate that lateral cyano substitution constitutes an effective strategy for tuning negative dielectric anisotropy while retaining favourable optical properties. These materials show promise for applications in high-frequency (GHz) electro-optical and microwave devices.

papers.title: Metadata Analysis to Reveal Environmental Effects in Large-Area Molecular Tunneling Junctions
papers.abstract: Data fidelity and/or irreproducibility in experimental science is often attributed to rarely quantified/qualified adventitious perturbations. This challenge is exacerbated by the stochastic nature and/or lack of requisite infrastructure to capture and analyze such interferences. Selfassembled monolayer (SAM) tunneling junctions provide a particularly sensitive test case: current density measurements can vary substantially across laboratories and operators, but conventional transport models such as the Simmons decay model account for molecular structure alone and explain as little as 37% of the variance of experimental data. Here, we demonstrate that automated curation and analysis of data and metadata can convert this unexplained scatter into interpretable, structured information. Starting from 18,834 I–V measurements on n-alkanethiol SAMs collected across two laboratories, we built an automated pipeline for data cleaning, variance decomposition, and enrichment with historically reconstructed environmental variables including temperature and humidity. A delta-learning framework, pairing the Simmons model as a physics-based baseline with metadata-trained Lasso regression, achieved an uncertainty-weighted R2 of 0.97. Feature analysis reveals that measurement location, time-of-day activity patterns, temperature, and humidity are the dominant drivers of residual variability, each with physically interpretable mechanisms. Beyond the specific findings for molecular junctions, this work argues that treating metadata as a first-class scientific output, and building automated workflows to capture and analyze it, is a practical, scalable strategy for diagnosing error hence improved reproducibility across readily perturbed interface materials research.

papers.title: Synthetic control over the electron-beam stability of upconverting nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Electron microscopy is fundamental to nanocrystal characterization, but some structures are quickly degraded in electron beams, limiting advanced structural characterization. Here, we introduce a synthetic strategy that combines layer-by-layer shell growth with in situ annealing to produce NaYbErF4 alloyed upconverting nanoparticles (UCNPs) with enhanced structural stability and optical properties. Using an automated synthesis platform to precisely control precursor delivery and annealing cycles, high rare earth ion concentrations are maintained during shell growth and annealing at high temperature, reducing luminescence quenching and degradation under electron beams. This in situ annealing layer-by-layer (ISA-LBL) approach gives rise to alloyed UCNPs with exceptional electron beam stability, reducing beam-induced fractures and voids by over 90% compared to conventionally synthesized aUCNPs. ISA-LBL aUCNPs also exhibit enhanced photoluminescence intensity and extended lifetimes, consistent with fewer quenching defects. This demonstrates a synthetic route to nanocrystals with enhanced structural integrity, increasing their compatibility with EM studies and their utility in highly ionizing environments.

papers.title: An Energy-Gradient Strategy for Triplet-Pair Separation in Singlet-Fission Oligomers
papers.abstract: Singlet fission (SF) offers a pathway to surpass the Shockley-Queisser limit by converting one photoexcited singlet exciton into two triplet excitons. However, in molecular assemblies, this process commonly yields a strongly exchange-coupled correlated triplet pair, 1 (TT), where inter-triplet interactions facilitate geminate recombination and back-transfer to the singlet manifold. Here we implement an energy-gradient strategy in linear diphenylhexatriene (DPH) hetero-oligomers to guide post-fission dynamics toward triplet-pair separation while minimizing thermodynamic loss. The hetero-oligomer series is constructed from two DPH-based building blocks with matched chromophore frameworks but offset triplet energies: a TIPS-substituted unit (T-DPH) and an alkyl-substituted unit (P-DPH). By positioning T-DPH at the termini of the hetero-oligomers, we encode a modest downhill triplet-energy gradient (~60 meV) that drives the migration of the triplet population away from the initially formed 1 (TT) configuration toward the chain periphery. Using femtosecond and nanosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, we track the kinetic evolution from the singlet manifold through 1 (TT) formation to a spatially separated, weakly exchange-coupled (T⋅⋅T) state. Magnetic-field-dependent transient absorption and photoluminescence measurements provide an independent experimental signature of the weak-exchange triplet-pair regime. Comparison with a homotrimer (PPP-DPH 3 ) lacking energetic asymmetry directly isolates the role of this design lever, demonstrating that a ~60 meV offset is sufficient to accelerate 1 (TT)→(T⋅⋅T) separation. This energy-gradient strategy enhances the yield of harvestable free triplets while maintaining the high triplet energy required for device-relevant SF-based optoelectronics, offering a simple and transferable design principle for singlet-fission materials that favour productive triplet-pair separation over geminate loss.

papers.title: Methionine Sulfoxide as a Reversible Handle Enhances Peptide Synthesis and Alters pH‑Dependent Amyloid Formation of GLP‑2
papers.abstract: Methionine sulfoxide [Met(O)] emerges as a powerful, versatile, and reversible masking group, which we here deploy in the synthesis of glucagon-like peptide-2 (GLP-2), a therapeutically important peptide hormone well known for its notoriously challenging solidphase peptide synthesis due to severe aggregation. i) Incorporation of Fmoc-Met(O)-OH during SPPS increased crude purity to 62%. After purification, reduction with TMSBr/EDT restored native methionine, yielding GLP-2 at 79% purity. ii) Beyond synthesis, methionine oxidation reshapes aggregation in a pH‑dependent manner. Native GLP‑2 rapidly forms 2 amorphous aggregates at pH 4 and sparse protofilaments at pH 7, whereas the oxidized variant, GLP-2-M(O) shows delayed nucleation followed by robust fibril elongation into well‑defined amyloid structures. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that oxidation disrupts the hydrophobic “methionine cage” at Met10, increasing solvent exposure and effectively decoupling nucleation from fibril growth and elongation. Together, these results establish methionine sulfoxide as a generalizable design element that enables both efficient synthesis and programmable control over peptide aggregation.

papers.title: Biomimetic Synthesis of Seven Halenaquinone Meroterpenoids
papers.abstract: Structurally similar natural products arising in phylogenetically distant organisms may reflect convergent evolutionary pressure toward privileged biological scaffolds. The marine sponge-derived halenaquinone meroterpenoids exemplify this phenomenon, sharing a highly electrophilic and strained diketofuran motif with both the viridin/wortmannin and hibiscone families of natural products. Guided by biosynthetic reasoning, we report herein a biomimetic route to the halenaquinone family. Central to the strategy is an aryne–furan Diels–Alder reaction that rapidly constructs the tetracyclic carbon framework, together with oxidative decarboxylation of a diosphenol intermediate followed by divergent late-stage oxidative cyclizations to furnish either xestoquinone or halenaquinone. This platform enabled the synthesis of seven natural products, three structural revisions, and the discovery of potent cytotoxic activity for several family members.

papers.title: Context-Guided Equivariant Diffusion Model for Efficient and Physics-Aware 3D Molecular Generation and Editing
papers.abstract: The advancement of Structure-Based Drug Design (SBDD) critically relies on efficient and accurate three-dimensional molecular generation. While diffusion models show great promise in this domain, existing methods frequently encounter challenges related to computational efficiency, ensuring chemical and physical reasonableness, adequately leveraging target-specific contextual information, and expanding beyond de novo generation to support nuanced tasks like molecular editing. Inspired by progress in point cloud processing, we propose Context-Guided Equivariant Diffusion (CGED), a novel framework that integrates an SE(3)-equivariant diffusion backbone with innovative mechanisms to address these limitations. CGED incorporates a Multi-scale Context-Aware module for enhanced target specificity, a Dynamic Physics-Informed Prior Injection module to ensure chemical realism, and an Adaptive Sampling Acceleration strategy for significant efficiency gains. Extensive experiments on the PDBbind-2020 and QM9 datasets, comparing against state-of-the-art baselines, demonstrate CGED’s superior performance. Our method achieves high molecular validity, favorable QED scores, strong binding affinity, and high docking success rates, alongside significantly reduced sampling steps. Ablation studies quantitatively confirm the efficacy of each proposed module, while qualitative evaluations by medicinal chemists further underscore CGED’s ability to generate novel, synthesizable, and therapeutically promising molecular designs.

papers.title: SuzukiMe: A Tactically Mild Methylation Reagent
authors: Luiz Paulo Melchior de Oliveira Leão
papers.abstract: A mild, efficient, and practical method for the methylation of aryl bromides and triflates utilizing activated boronate nucleophiles is described. The mildness of this cross-coupling reaction relies on the unique utilization of a preactivated, but stable mixed lithium dialkyl boronate salt that displays high reactivity and selectivity in B-alkyl Suzuki coupling events. The reaction requires no exogenous hydroxide or alkoxide base, rendering it tolerant of substrates that would typically undergo degradation under canonical Suzuki alkylation events. Amidst a broad scope that includes the late-stage methylation of natural products and drug scaffolds, this reaction also improves upon tactically similar Suzuki alkylations that suffer from low yields and/or conversion. In addition, applications in isotopic labeling were explored along with a high-throughput substrate screening assay that further unveils the breadth of this transformation, demonstrating the immense potential for these unique nucleophiles in programmatic cross-coupling.

papers.title: Exploring the potential anticancer activity of Ruthenium(II)-Arene and Copper(I) complexes bearing N-heterocyclic carbene ligands containing azido, pyridinium and ethisterone-derived triazole groups
papers.abstract: The design and functionalization of N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) ligands provide a versatile platform for tuning the chemical and biological properties of metallodrugs. Herein, we report the synthesis of a series of backbone-functionalized imidazolium precursors incorporating chloromethyl, azidomethyl, triazole–steroid, and pyridinium motifs, enabling the introduction of biologically relevant functionalities while maintaining steric protection around the metal-binding site. These precursors were efficiently converted into linear Cu(I)–NHC complexes via a weak-base protocol and into Ru(II)–arene carbonato and dichloro NHC complexes using an analogous methodology, highlighting operationally simple, scalable approaches suitable for sensitive or multifunctional ligands. Structural characterization confirmed the formation of well-defined metal–carbene species. Biological evaluation revealed that Cu(I)–NHC complexes exhibit potent antiproliferative activity against ovarian (A2780, A2780cis) and breast (MCF-7) cancer cells, including cisplatin-resistant models, and induce apoptosis with moderate selectivity over non-tumorigenic keratinocytes. In contrast, Ru(II)–NHC complexes displayed moderate cytotoxicity but are consistent with profiles favouring anti-metastatic and mechanistically distinct actions. These results underscore the potential of backbonefunctionalized NHC ligands to fine-tune metallodrug activity and highlight Cu(I)–NHC complexes as promising candidates for further development against resistant cancers.

papers.title: TOWARD HIGH-THROUGHPUT VIRTUAL SCREENING VIA QUASI-ADIABATIC QUANTUM GEOMETRY OPTIMIZATION WORKFLOW
papers.abstract: This work addresses the challenge of molecular geometry optimization at post-Hartree-Fock levels of theory using quantum computing methodologies. We present a novel potentially quasi-adiabatic approach based on the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) algorithm for efficient exploration of potential energy surfaces. The method combines quantum-circuit emulators with classical optimization routines and uses the Hellmann–Feynman theorem, including Pulay corrections, together with a finite-difference scheme to compute forces. Our implementation uses GPU-accelerated quantum-circuit operations within a parallelized framework, achieving computational efficiency by warm-starting the wavefunction and reoptimizing it at each subsequent geometry-optimization step. Benchmark results on small molecular systems demonstrate the feasibility of this hybrid quantumclassical approach, with detailed comparisons against established quantum chemistry methods, including CASCI and DFT optimizations. We discuss the current limitations, computational advan-tages, and potential future developments of this methodology in the context of quantum chemistry for drug discovery applications.

papers.title: Spatial Arrangement Controls Activity and Selectivity in Bifunctional Zeolite-Oxide Catalyst for Hydrogen Engine Exhaust
papers.abstract: Hydrogen-fueled internal combustion engines generate nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions that require aftertreatment technologies. Hydrogen fuel introduces challenges for conventional aftertreatment catalysts but simultaneously creates opportunities to repurpose mature diesel technologies. Commercial ammonia slip catalysts (ASC) designed to oxidize unreacted ammonia contain platinum that can also catalyze low-temperature NOx reduction using hydrogen. Establishing design principles for bifunctional operation of these existing catalyst architectures is essential for developing effective H2-ICE aftertreatment systems. We demonstrate that spatial arrangement of ASC catalyst phases is a critical design parameter governing NOx reduction activity and selectivity in mixed hydrogen-ammonia environments. Using a bifunctional catalyst system combining copper-containing zeolite with a platinum-containing oxide, we systematically varied the degree of spatial homogeneity from complete phase separation to intimate interfacial contact. A physically mixed composite with modest phase proximity between zeolite and oxide emerged as the optimal architecture for low-temperature NOx conversion. This configuration achieved synergistic NOx reduction through cooperative utilization of both reductants while preserving the independent catalytic functions of each phase. In contrast, forced homogenization through mechanical ball milling caused complete deactivation of platinum functionality. Analysis of ammonia formation and consumption profiles revealed that in situ generation of ammonia on platinum followed by its utilization on copper sites drives the enhanced low-temperature activity. However, the benefits of spatial proximity for low-temperature NOx conversion introduced selectivity trade-offs. These structure-performance relationships establish that multifunctional catalyst architectures for hydrogen-containing exhaust require precise control over phase arrangement to balance activity enhancement against selectivity.

papers.title: Twist to Upconvert: Conformational Control of DSA Governs Photon Upconversion Properties
papers.abstract: Using a reverse “solid-state-first” approach, we investigate the upconversion-relevant properties of 9,10-distyrylanthracene (DSA) in solution and solid phases to identify the parameters governing its performance as an aggregation-induced emission (AIE)-active triplet annihilator. By systematically comparing the photophysics of the palladium(II) mesotetraphenyltetrabenzoporphyrin (PdTPTBP)/DSA sensitizer/annihilator pair in solution, nanocrystals, and crystalline thin films, we clarify the triplet and singlet state dynamics underlying triplet–triplet annihilation upconversion (TTA-UC). Our results show that the lack of TTA-UC in DSA solutions is not simply a consequence of reduced fluorescence quantum yield from vinyl-group rotation. Rather, conformational flexibility allows DSA to planarize in the triplet excited state, lowering its triplet energy below the level required to satisfy the 2E(T1) ≥ E(S1) criterion for e\icient upconversion. In contrast, in the solid state the vinyl groups are locked at an approximately 75° dihedral angle, preserving a higher triplet energy and providing su\icient driving force for TTA to generate the excited singlet state, consistent with the intense upconversion observed in nanocrystal and thin-film samples. These findings establish dihedral-angle control as a key molecular design principle for tuning excited-state energetics and developing e\icient, structurally rigid, solid-state TTA-UC materials.

papers.title: InF3 Surface Passivation on InAs Quantum Dots Enhances Photoluminescence and Reduces Trap-Induced Dark Current in Shortwave Infrared Photodetectors
papers.abstract: Shortwave infrared (SWIR) photodetectors are crucial for emerging technologies such as autonomous driving, smart agriculture, industrial inspection, and eye-safe LiDAR. Colloidal indium arsenide (InAs) quantum dots (QDs) offer a low-cost, RoHS-compliant alternative to epitaxial III–V semiconductors. But their performance is limited by a high density of surface trap states that induce nonradiative recombination and potentially give rise to a high dark current in photodiodes. Here, we demonstrate that InF 3 can effectively passivate these surface traps, significantly improving both optical and electronic properties. In non-polar solvents, a simple InF 3 treatment on oleylamine/chloride-capped In(As,P) and oleate-capped InAs QDs increases the photoluminescence quantum yield to 13% and 4%, respectively—the highest reported for core-only InAs QDs. In polar media, the InF 3 treatment remains effective but reduces colloidal stability. To overcome this limitation, a solid-state in situ InF 3 treatment of QD films was used. The treatment doubles the carrier lifetime and lowers the dark carrier density, confirmed by ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy, microwave conductivity, and electrochemically gated transistor measurements. In SWIR photodetectors, this leads to an order-of-magnitude reduction in dark current density and a three-fold increase in the calculated specific detectivity assuming it is shot-noise-limited. Temperature-dependent dark current density and thermal admittance spectroscopy measurements reveal that deep trap states dominate the dark current in InAs QDs photodetectors. The InF 3 treatment strongly suppresses these traps. These findings establish InF 3 passivation as a powerful, versatile strategy for mitigating surface-trap-induced dark current and advancing high-performance, RoHS-compliant SWIR photodetectors.

papers.title: The synergistic effects of aqueous solution, temperature, and mutagenesis on Syntaxin-1a-Munc-18a complex formation
papers.abstract: In the nervous system vesicular fusion is a physiological event regulated by several proteins, particularly Syntaxin-1a and Munc-18a. Although these proteins are known to form the molecular assembly, affording the neurotransmitter release, the synergistic effect of ions, temperature, and mutagenesis on its interaction remain a conundrum. To remedy this, we characterized the energetic properties of both wild-type and mutant Munc-18a, when they form a complex with Syntaxin1a within an artificial aqueous solution mimicking the cytosolic conditions. Applying molecular dynamics simulations at three temperatures (room, physiological, and febrile), we assessed ionic influences on the complexes given by the interaction energies. Our results demonstrate strong coupling between calcium and hydrogen ions in the wild-type complexes, which suggests a novel ionic role influencing the Syntaxin1a-Munc-18a interplay. Furthermore, in the mutant complex, distinct ionic interactions were observed between Syntaxin-1a and ions. In fact, beyond the strong energetic interplay with hydrogen ions, weaker, but still significant interaction was documented with potassium, sodium, and chloride as well. Moreover, the results also clearly show how the mutation changes the binding energy of the complexes as a function of temperature. Last, but not least, the structural analyses revealed greater separation between domains 3a and 1 of Munc-18a in the mutant compared to wild-type across all temperatures. Based on these results we discuss a biophysical substrate in the context of vesicular fusion.

papers.title: Discovery of Potent and Non-Cytotoxic HDAC3-Selective Degraders Featuring a Propyl Hydrazide Zinc-Binding Group
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylase 3 (HDAC3) is an important therapeutic target in cancer, yet selective HDAC3 degraders remain limited. In this study, we report the development of novel class I HDAC degraders derived from the HDAC3-preferential inhibitor FL-007 . Two linker exit vectors were investigated, leading to the identification of a series of potent compounds ( 2a-d ) exhibiting low micromolar inhibition of HDAC2 and submicromolar inhibition of HDAC1 and HDAC3, together with selective HDAC3 degradation. Degradation activity was confirmed in MM.1S, HCT116, A2780-HDAC3-HiBiT, and Cal27CisR cells using immunoblotting and HiBiT/LgBiT assays, achieving Dmax values of up to 92%. Notably, these compounds showed no cytotoxicity up to 100 µM in both cancerous and non-cancerous cell lines. Selective HDAC3 degradation resulted in moderate chemosensitization of cisplatin-resistant Cal27CisR cells, in contrast to the stronger effects observed with cytotoxic HDAC inhibitors. For compound 2b , the chemosensitizing effect was associated with increased histone H3 acetylation and increased p21 expression.

papers.title: A small molecule dual inhibitor of agr quorum sensing and ATP synthase blocks acute and chronic virulence phenotypes in Staphylococcus aureus
papers.abstract: The accessory gene regulator (agr) quorum sensing system in Staphylococcus aureus plays a prominent role in acute infections caused by this common pathogen. In contrast, ATP synthase affects the ability of S. aureus to establish chronic infections and persist as small colony variants. In this study, we report that a synthetic small molecule, CP-20, is capable of dually inhibiting agr and ATP synthase. We demonstrate CP-20’s ability to counteract key virulence phenotypes associated with both pathways, including hemolysis, biofilm formation, and antibiotic resistance. We also show that CP-20 facilitates more efficient clearance of S. aureus by murine macrophages than genetic inactivation of either agr or ATP synthase alone, suggesting that dual inhibition may have an additive effect on ablating intracellular survival. This work demonstrates the utility of a single chemical modulator to attenuate S. aureus pathogenesis via two non-essential pathways and suggests a pathway toward non-bactericidal virulence control.

papers.title: Effects of 6PPD-Q and Its Hydroxylated Metabolites on function in the Rainbow Trout Cell Line RTgill-W1
papers.abstract: The tire rubber-derived contaminant 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) exhibits high acute toxicity to salmonid species, yet the toxicological profiles of its hydroxylated metabolites and the underlying mitochondrial mechanisms remain poorly characterized. This study investigated the cytotoxicity and mitochondrial function in rainbow trout gill cells (RTgill-W1) exposed to 6PPD-Q and three mono-hydroxylated metabolites (p-hydroxy 6PPD-Q, 6PPD-Q-1-OH, and 6PPD-Q-4-OH). Using OECD Test Guideline 249 in combination with complementary physiological assays, we demonstrate a clear structure–toxicity relationship (STR). Among the tested compounds, p-hydroxy 6PPD-Q exhibited the greatest toxicity, exceeding that of 6PPD-Q, whereas the alkyl-hydroxylated metabolite showed little to no detectable toxicity. Mechanistic analysis revealed that the toxic variants induced a concentration-dependent collapse of mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) and severe ATP depletion, concurrent with a significant disruption of intracellular calcium homeostasis. Although no statistically significant differences in total oxygen consumption were observed, likely due to uncoupling-like effects or compensatory cellular dynamics, these results demonstrate that 6PPD-Q and its active transformation products compromise rainbow trout cell viability primarily by targeting the mitochondrial bioenergetic axis.

papers.title: From 2D Graphs to Sub-Unit pKa: Nine Iterations to BeatMolGpKa on Both Scaffolds and Sulfonamides
papers.abstract: Accurate pKa prediction for drug-like molecules remains a significant gap between com- mercial tools (Epik ∼0.5 RMSE, MoKa ∼0.4 RMSE) and open-source methods, particularly for sulfonamides and heterocyclic N–H compounds prevalent in medicinal chemistry. We present a systematic nine-iteration ablation converging on a routed ensemble that outperforms MolGpKa on both general scaffolds and sulfonamides simultaneously—the first open-source model to do so. Starting from a 2D molecular graph baseline (v1, SAMPL7 RMSE 3.48), we isolate each variable: global xTB descriptors help scaffolds but not sulfonamides (v2); data augmentation fails (v2-aug); per-atom Mulliken charges help sulfonamides but hurt scaffolds (v3); routing combines both (v4, SAMPL7 2.19). We then identify the architectural gap with MolGpKa: per-atom pKa output targets trained on microscopic data. Per-atom output alone fails with macroscopic labels (v5). Microscopic labels from Uni-pKa improve scaffolds but not sulfonamides (v6). Merging microscopic and macroscopic data with a mixed loss produces the first model with no tradeoff (v7, scaffold 1.31, SAMPL7 1.32).
