papers.title: pH-Inverted Histidine-Rich Nanochelants for Trapping Furin-Processed Polycationic Nanotoxins: A Quantum-Classical Platform for Dual Heavy-Metal Detoxification and Broad-Spectrum Countermeasures
papers.abstract: Furin cleaves polybasic sites in endosomes and the secretory pathway, releasing linear (>3 net positive charges) and concentric (metal-coordinating) nanotoxins that drive metabolic disease, cytokine storms, neurodegeneration, autoimmunity, cancer immune evasion, and infection. We introduce 5H-EAF, an erythritol-capped linear penta-histidine nanochelant (MW ≈ 880 Da) that activates to +4–5 net charge at endosomal pH 5.5–6.5, trapping these species via electrostatic clamping and coordination, then deprotonates and releases harmlessly at neutral pH. DFT (B3LYP-D3/def2-TZVP, explicit solvation) yields Pb²⁺ ΔG = –11 to –16 kcal/mol (low pH) → –3 to –6 kcal/mol (neutral); SARS-CoV-2 PRRAR⁺ motif clamping ΔG ≈ –8 to –13 kcal/mol; and anthrax PA63 pore blockade analogous to validated cationic blockers (Kd nM–µM, planar-bilayer literature) supported by all-atom MD simulations (MM-PBSA ΔG = −28.7 kcal/mol at pH 5.5). The platform speaks furin’s native pH/Ca²⁺/charge language without global inhibition. It unifies GLP-1 optimization, cytokine control, α-syn/amyloid management, Pb neuroprotection, and biodefense against furin-dependent pathogens (anthrax, Ebola, H5N1, SARS-CoV-2, Dengue).

papers.title: Theoretical characterization of hydroxyfuranones related to biomass burning and their tautomers
Direct electrochemistry of hydrogenase, formatedehydrogenase, CO dehydrogenase and nitrogenase: Wiring strategies and mechanistic insights into metalloenzymes that produce solar fuels.
papers.abstract: Direct electrochemistry (DET), whereby a redox enzyme exchanges electrons with an electrode without the intervention of any mediator, has emerged at the turn of the XXIth century as a powerful tool to investigate redox enzymes. In this review we focus on the electrochemistry of metalloenzymes that are involved in the recycling of biological solar fuels. We summarize the strategies that made it possible to wire them to electrodes, from their mere physisorption onto friendly electrodes to more sophisticated covalent attachment. We then describe a number of qualitative and quantitative electrochemical investigations of their mechanisms. These studies have disclosed the functional diversity within each family of enzymes considered here, suggesting that structural features that are remote from the active site play a major role in determining catalytic properties such as catalytic directionality, reversibility, and resistance to oxygen. DET electrochemistry contributed to elucidating some of these outer sphere effects, which are crucial in molecular catalysis, and also to discovering and characterizing new enzymes, which have the properties and robustness required in solar fuel devices.

papers.title: Acidic local environments inhibit CO2 reduction catalysis on coinage metals
papers.abstract: The carbon-efficient electrochemical reduction of CO 2 (CO 2 RR) requires acidic electrolytes to mitigate irreversible CO 2 capture via non-faradaic CO 2 uptake and (bi)carbonate formation. However, CO 2 RR only takes place in acidic electrolytes upon addition of spectator cations and the mechanistic basis for this requirement remains unclear. Herein, we present scanning voltammetry experiments conducted in bulk acidic electrolytes in conjunction with differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS) analysis of CO 2 consumption and product formation. By quantifying both faradaic CO 2 consumption via CO 2 RR, and non-faradaic CO 2 consumption via the formation of (bi)carbonate in real-time, we deconvolute the direct role of the added electrolyte cations from their indirect role in fostering a transient local pH swing. We find that across coinage metals and electrolyte compositions, CO 2 RR commences only upon substantial depletion of hydronium and coincides with non-faradaic CO 2 uptake. Doping Ag with Pt to promote hydronium consumption via efficient H 2 evolution serves to lower the overpotential for CO 2 RR onset in scanning voltammetry experiments by ~1 V. These findings together indicate that an interfacial pH swing is a pre-requisite for, rather than merely a consequence of CO 2 RR, and that the primary role of the supporting electrolyte cations is to establish a non-equilibrium interfacial ionic environment depleted in hydronium ions. To rationalize these findings, we propose that acidic pH environments foster the formation of *COOH, rather than *COO − , and that this protonated intermediate undergoes unproductive fragmentation to CO 2 and H*, contributing to H 2 evolution, but not CO 2 RR. This work highlights the value of pre-steady state real-time analysis of both faradaic and non-faradaic interfacial reactions and establishes a self-consistent mechanistic picture for CO 2 RR in bulk acidic electrolyte.

papers.title: Balancing redox-mediated cytotoxicity and catalysis in natural product biosynthesis
papers.abstract: Redox-mediated chemistry is central to both the biosynthesis and cytotoxicity of many natural products, yet how microbes balance these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we uncover a conserved mechanism that coordinates three redox-mediated processes in secondary metabolite biosynthesis: self-protection, prevention of substrate degradation, and late-stage biocatalysis. Using the antitumor antibiotic doxorubicin as a model system, we show that the Vicinal Oxygen Chelate (VOC) protein DnrV prevents reactive oxygen species formation and substrate degradation while promoting P450 catalysis. We expand this paradigm to a conserved family of VOC-fold proteins, REdox-Associated CytoToxin binding proteins (REACT), found across bacteria, fungi, and plants. REACT represents a multifunctional protein class that balances antibiotic assembly, self-protection, and prevention of metabolite destruction, providing a foundational understanding of production of redox-active natural products.

papers.title: Reversible Droplet Bridging and Tunable Viscoelasticity in Emulsions Using Biocompatible PLA-b-PEO-b-PLA Telechelic Block Copolymers: Implications for Injectable Emulsion Gels
papers.abstract: Telechelic polymers are known to form reversible networks through end-group association; however, their application as structuring agents in emulsion-based soft materials remains underexplored. Herein, we systematically investigate the biocompatible amphiphilic triblock copolymer poly(DL-lactic acid)-block-poly(ethylene oxide)-block-poly(DL-lactic acid)(PLA- b -PEO- b -PLA) as a rheology modifier in toluene-in-water model emulsions. Owing to the selective adsorption of PLA end blocks at the oil–water interface and the solvation of the PEO midblock in the aqueous phase, this polymer is expected to form reversible droplet-bridging networks. During the process, the polymer concentration, molecular weight of the mid and end blocks, and the dispersed phase volume fraction were adjusted, and the factors governing network formation were elucidated using oscillatory rheology and stress-relaxation measurements. The results show that anchoring of the PLA end blocks and PEO-mediated bridging predominantly control the strength and dynamic reversibility of the network. Step-strain experiments further reveal that the droplet-bridging interactions can be disrupted under large deformation and partially recover when small-strain conditions are restored, confirming the presence of reversible physical associations. These findings establish a molecular design strategy for biodegradable telechelic copolymers as effective and reprocessable structuring agents in emulsion gels. The shear-responsive, tunable, and reversible nature of the droplet-bridging network makes this material platform particularly suitable for injectable emulsion gels for advanced soft matter and biomedical engineering applications.

papers.title: Synthesis of 4-Quinolone N-Oxides via Controlled Partial Hydrogenation of 2-Nitrobenzoyl Enamines
papers.abstract: An operationally simple procedure for the synthesis of 2-alkyl-4-quinolone N-oxides, relying on controlled platinum-catalyzed partial hydrogenation of 2-nitrobenzoyl enamines, has been demonstrated. The P. aeruginosa metabolite 2-heptyl-4-quinolone-N-oxide (HQNO) and four analogous products have been prepared in good yield and high purity by this method.

papers.title: Breaking the strength-activity tradeoff in high-temperature CO2 electrolysis with a hybrid solid oxide cell
papers.abstract: Electrochemical conversion of CO2 into chemicals and fuels offers a promising route towards a circular carbon economy. High-temperature CO2 electroreduction in solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) delivers high selectivity and energy efficiency, but suffers from a tradeoff between mechanical robustness and electrochemical activity. Here we resolve this constraint using a hybrid ionic-conductor architecture that decouples electrocatalysis, ionic transport and mechanical support into function-specific layers. The resulting cell achieves one of the highest reported mechanical strengths (fracture load >7 N), while delivering 1.5-3.0fold higher CO2-to-CO activity than state-of-the-art SOECs over operating temperatures of 600-800 °C. Stable operation is maintained for over 1,000 hours at a current density of 1.0 A cm-2. Furthermore, we demonstrate scalability with a single-cell area of 100 cm 2 , achieving total currents up to 120 A and powers up to 200 W. This work establishes a general strategy for developing mechanically resilient, efficient, and scalable energy conversion devices.

papers.title: When Do Models Win? A Learning Curve Benchmark for Molecular Property Prediction in Low-Data Regimes
papers.abstract: In many molecular property prediction tasks, such as drug discovery and OLED material design, labeled data are often limited to only tens to thousands of samples due to high experimental costs. Despite the rapid development of machine learning models, it remains unclear which model classes are most effective under such low-data regimes and how their performance evolves with increasing data. In this work, we present a comprehensive learning curve benchmark across traditional machine learning methods, graph neural networks (GNNs), transformer-based molecular language models, and hybrid architectures. We systematically vary the training data size from 50 to 3,000 samples and evaluate performance on QM9, ESOL, Lipophilicity, and BACE datasets using scaffold splits with repeated trials for statistical robustness. We further propose two hybrid models combining GCN and ChemBERTa with different fusion strategies-concatenation (GTCA-Cat) and cross-attention (GTCA-CA)-and analyze their data efficiency through ablation studies. Our results reveal that (1) hybrid models substantially improve over single-modality GCN in low-data regimes for physicochemical property targets (e.g., 32% RMSE reduction on ESOL at N=50), (2) simple concatenation fusion generally outperforms or matches cross-attention due to reduced overfitting and improved stability, and (3) clear crossover points exist where traditional kernel-based methods outperform deep learning models depending on the task type. Importantly, we identify regimedependent model optimality: deep learning models dominate continuous physicochemical property prediction, while kernel-based methods can be more effective for bioactivity prediction across most data scales. Our findings provide actionable guidelines for model selection under data scarcity and highlight the importance of learning curve analysis as a principled tool for understanding model behavior.

papers.title: Selective Post-Synthetic Reduction of Pyridinium Hydrazone Cages
papers.abstract: Post-synthetic modification of a series of hexacationic organic cages containing pyridinium and hydrazone groups gave a new family of neutral organic cages through a high-yielding single step reduction reaction. The reduction selectively reduces all six pyridinium rings to 1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridines but leaves the hydrazone C=N bond untouched. The neutral cages display strong and cooperative sulfate binding to give cage•(SO4 2-)2 complexes in DMSO.

papers.title: Surface-Neutralized HgCdSe Quantum Dots for High-Detectivity Infrared Photodetectors
When Three-Body Interactions Become Redundant: Scaling Graph Neural Network Potentials
papers.abstract: Graph neural networks (GNN) are currently the vehicle for large scale molecular dynamics at quantum accuracy, but their practical scalability remains limited by the rapidly increasing size of graph representations required for large atomistic systems. In particular, the construction of higherorder interactions such as triplets leads to substantial memory and computational overhead during both training and inference. In this work, we investigate strategies to improve the scalability of GNNbased potentials while preserving predictive accuracy. We show that pruning triplet interactions during training and inference has minimal impact on regression accuracy for formation energies, band gaps, and elastic moduli. For molecular dynamics simulations, we find that pruning triplets during inference preserves structural fidelity while significantly reducing computational cost. This allows for upscaling of GNNs to large structures (beyond 30k atoms). To further extend scalability, we introduce a spatial chunking scheme that decomposes large atomistic systems into padded subgraphs, enabling efficient evaluation of forces for systems containing hundreds of thousands of atoms. Using this approach, we perform molecular dynamics simulations of a 400,000-atom LGPS supercell on a single GPU using the M3GNet and DIEP models. Our results demonstrate that fully trained manybody GNN potentials contain significant redundancy that can be exploited to improve scalability, providing a practical pathway toward large-scale atomistic simulations with universal machinelearning potentials.

papers.title: Mapping the Applicability Domain of Lipophilicity Models Through Chemical Space Topology
papers.abstract: The applicability domain (AD) of a QSAR model defines the boundary of chemical space within which its predictions are statistically valid. For large-scale lipophilicity (logP) modeling, conventional AD formulations produce a binary in-domain/out-of-domain classification that conceals the internal topology of prediction uncertainty. This paper presents a PCAbased spatial error analysis over a 426,850-molecule bioactive dataset assembled from three independent chemical databases. The seven-dimensional descriptor space reduces to a 2D manifold capturing 76.83% of total variance (PC1: 52.85%; PC2: 23.98%), revealing a bimodal topology: Lipinski-compliant drug-like molecules form a dense central core, while pharmacologically extreme molecules scatter at the periphery. Overlaying ElasticNet prediction residuals (computed exclusively on held-out test molecules) demonstrates that mean absolute error (MAE) is 2.73× higher at the periphery than at the central manifold (1.567 vs. 0.574 logP units), with non-overlapping bootstrap 95% confidence intervals confirming significance at α=0.01. A Lipinski-stratified dual-model strategy motivated by this topology achieves RMSE=0.838 for the Drug-Like population and R²=0.767 for the Extreme population, the latter surpassing the global XGBoost baseline (R²=0.765). The contribution is primarily methodological: PCA-based error topology provides an interpretable, quantitative diagnostic for AD characterization that directly informs production deployment decisions. The approach is general and not specific to logP.

papers.title: Identification of Roasting Reaction Products of Catechin Exhibiting Xanthine Oxidase Inhibitory Activity
papers.abstract: Food processing and cooking methods that involve high-temperature heating (such as roasting) alter the composition of raw food materials. Even polyphenols, which are generally considered thermally stable, undergo changes in their chemical structure during roasting. This study investigated the roasting reaction of catechin, a functional polyphenol, at a temperature of approximately 200 ℃ and found that it enhanced xanthine oxidase inhibitory activity. Purification and separation of the products derived from the catechin roasting reaction revealed two types of moderately active compounds: dimeric products with a linkage between the C and A rings, and an aurone-like benzofuran product. Additionally, several fractions containing oligomeric products were identified as highly active fractions. These results suggest that catechin enhances xanthine oxidase inhibitory activity by transforming into dimeric, aurone-type, and probably oligomeric products.

papers.title: MgCl2-Mediated Mechanisms of Oxygen Solubility in Molten Salt Reactor Fuels
papers.abstract: In molten salt reactors, oxygen impurities accelerate structural material corrosion. Moreover, the ingress of oxide species may promote the formation of insoluble actinide oxychlorides or oxides, potentially raising safety concerns. To limit the undesired precipitation of such phases, MgCl 2 has been proposed as a complementary fuel component to sequester oxygen by enhancing the solubility of actinide oxide species. In this study, we provide direct, molecularlevel evidence of an MgCl 2 -mediated oxygen solubility mechanism. This was achieved through high-temperature 17 O nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy on NaCl-MgCl 2 -LaCl 3 melts with various amounts of dissolved 17 O-enriched LaOCl, corroborated by classical molecular dynamics with the polarizable ion model and first-principles NMR calculations. Experiment and simulation both show that adding MgCl 2 drives Mg 2+ to compete with La 3+ for O 2- coordination, disrupting La-O clustering that facilitates oxide precipitation. Altogether, these results establish a mechanistic framework for tuning oxygen speciation and solubility through compositional design in high-temperature molten salt systems.

papers.title: A new equation for the calculation of activity coefficients in non-ideal solutions
papers.abstract: Based on the thermodynamic expression of excess volume, a new equation is derived to calculate the activity coefficients of components in a non-ideal solution. For an ideal binary solution, it is proved that this equation is valid. For non-ideal binary solutions, the damped Newton method is applied to find the roots of this equation iteratively. The iterative process is not dependent on the initial guesses of activity coefficients. The convergence of iterative process is always reached. For two negative and three positive deviation solutions, the activity coefficients of components are calculated iteratively. They are in good agreement with the activity coefficients reported in literature. The total activity coefficient is also calculated to show the deviation of the entire solution from the hypothetic ideal solution. Based on the activity coefficients calculated in this work, the total activity coefficients γ of five non-ideal solutions are in very good agreement with the total active coefficients calculated with activity coefficients reported in literatures. The magnitude of γ can be understood from intermolecular interaction. This interaction is estimated qualitatively with the interaction of the molecular dipole moments calculated with the density functional theory.

papers.title: Lithium plating and stripping facilitated by thin sputtered silver and carbon interlayers in anode-free all-solid-state batteries
Unlocking a shortcut: Active machine learning in non-aqueous battery electrolyte development for sodium-based batteries
papers.abstract: Sodium-based batteries are promising candidates for sustainable large-scale energy storage, yet systematic electrolyte design remains challenging due to the high dimensionality and physical constraints of formulation space. Here, we present a data-driven workflow that combines high-throughput experimentation with batch-wise active learning to efficiently map and model non-aqueous sodium-based electrolyte formulations. Rather than targeting a single optimal composition, the approach constructs predictive surrogate models over the full space of physically admissible formulations, which in the present case corresponds to a three-dimensional, compositionally constrained feature space defined by salt content and solvent mixing ratios. Training identical models on sodium-and lithium-based data sets enables a direct, composition-wide comparison of both cations within the same solvent framework, revealing largely similar conductivity landscapes with modest but systematic differences that can be rationalized by differences in ionic size and solvation characteristics. The formulation space can be reliably described using only 72 electrolyte compositions acquired in two active learning iterations, corresponding to a reduction in required experiments by a factor of 4-7 compared to random sampling. Conductivity-guided electrolyte selection leads to improved rate capability and low-temperature performance in sodium-ion full cells, while also highlighting the limitations of ionic conductivity as a sole performance descriptor. Overall, this work establishes a transferable, physics-informed framework for data-efficient electrolyte exploration.

papers.title: Dispersion from polarizabilities of atoms in molecule: DPAIM
papers.abstract: A new atom-atom pairwise dispersion function DPAIM (dispersion from polarizabilities of atoms in molecules) has been developed. The dynamic polarizabilities, both dipole-dipole and quadrupole-quadrupole, of a set of reference molecules obtained from the time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) are first spherically averaged and then split into AIM atomic contributions using the generalized effective atomic sizes based on Hirshfeld's partitioning of DFT molecular density. The polarizability

papers.title: When Do Simple Models Win? Machine Learning Architectures for UV Absorption Prediction and Insights for General Molecular Property Prediction
papers.abstract: What determines which machine learning architecture wins for molecular property prediction? We address this question through a controlled comparison of five models spanning four architecture families: fingerprint-based ensembles (Random Forest, XGBoost), a directed message-passing graph neural network (GNN), a bidirectional gated recurrent network (BiGRU), and a pretrained Transformer, using UV absorption wavelength (λ max) prediction as a testbed across 18,755 solute-solvent pairs with stratified 5-fold cross-validation and two external datasets totaling over 40,000 molecules. The answer depends on the task. For screening within known chemical space, RF with Morgan fingerprints is optimal: it matches the GNN (RMSE = 31.34 ± 1.82 vs. 31.69 ± 3.18 nm, p = 0.77), trains in 15 minutes on a CPU with no hyperparameter tuning, and outperforms all sequence-based models. For exploring novel scaffolds, deep learning is superior: experimental validation on 16 novel UV-absorbing 1 compounds shows that the GNN (MAE = 26.2 nm), Transformer (26.3 nm), and Bi-GRU (28.6 nm) all outperform RF (38.5 nm), as learned representations generalize where fixed fingerprints cannot. In either case, encoding solvent identity improves all models: a simple SMILES/fingerprint concatenation strategy yields 6-8% RMSE reductions across fingerprint, graph, and recurrent architectures (p < 0.02), without domain-specific descriptor engineering. Interpretability analysis confirms that both RF feature importance and BiGRU gradient saliency independently highlight the same chromophore motifs, and that architectures with local inductive bias systematically outperform global-attention Transformers on this locally determined property. These findings provide general guidance for molecular property prediction: the largest or most complex model is not always the best choice. Instead, optimal model selection depends on the locality of the target property and the relationship between target compounds and available training data. When the target property is governed by local molecular features and the prediction task is interpolation within known chemical space, simple fingerprint-based models offer an efficient and accurate alternative to deep learning.

papers.title: Open-Source Computational Workflows for Drug Repurposing: A Methodological Strategy Against Arterial Hypertension
papers.abstract: Arterial hypertension remains a leading global risk factor for cardiovascular mortality. The traditional de novo drug discovery pipeline is hindered by exorbitant costs and prolonged developmental timelines. Drug repurposing-identifying new therapeutic indications for existing approved drugs-presents a highly efficient alternative. This methodological essay critically evaluates the implementation of completely open-source computational workflows for in silico drug repurposing against key hypertensive targets, such as the Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme (ACE) and the Angiotensin II Type 1 Receptor (AT1R). We systematically dissect a generalized Computer-Aided Drug Design (CADD) pipeline utilizing freely available software: RDKit for cheminformatics library preparation, AutoDock Vina for high-throughput virtual screening (HTVS), and GROMACS for molecular dynamics (MD) trajectory analysis. Consolidating literature data, we demonstrate how open-source automation frameworks (like KNIME and Python/Jupyter) democratize pharmacological research, enabling academic laboratories to execute complex polypharmacological screenings. Our analysis highlights that open-source pipelines can achieve hit-identification accuracies comparable to proprietary software, reducing computational screening costs by 100% while compressing the preclinical target validation timeline by over 60%.

papers.title: Cationic Imidazolium Macrocycles Enable Array-based, Site-Selective Optical Detection of Peptide Phosphorylation
papers.abstract: Simple polycationic imidazolium macrocycles, formed in one step from commercial precursors, show strong affinity for peptide strands with anionic and hydrophobic character, and can be paired with styrylpyridinium dyes in an arrayed format to enable site-and state-selective optical detection of phosphorylation at serine residues. Even though they show affinity for anions in aqueous solution, the cationic macrocyclic hosts do not bind the modified serine phosphate residues themselves, rather they exploit π-stacking interactions with the native peptide backbone and different sidechains, allowing interaction with both modified and unmodified peptides. When combined with cationic indicators that can also bind the peptide targets, a complex equilibrium is established consisting of peptide:host, peptide:dye and dye:host assemblies, as well as peptide:dye:host ternary complexes. These multiple equilibria enable differentiation of miniscule changes in peptide target, differentiating phosphate residues at different sites on otherwise identical peptide strands.

papers.title: Transparent Reporting for Agentic Catalysis Enabled by Artificial Intelligence (TRACE-AI): Community Guidelines and A Publication Checklist
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into catalysis science, enabling agentic workflows in which AI systems perceive inputs, reason under constraints, plan, and autonomously execute in silico or physical experiments with minimal human intervention. While these closed-loop capabilities hold promise to accelerate knowledge generation and technological innovation, they inevitably introduce new sources of variability in data lineage, model specification, and agent policies that can undermine FAIRness, rigor, and reproducibility. These risks are particularly pronounced in heterogeneous catalysis, where subtleties in catalyst synthesis and pretreatment, dynamic restructuring under operating conditions, and transport-mediated local environments can largely determine catalytic outcomes. To address these challenges, we introduce TRACE-AI (Transparent Reporting for Agentic Catalysis Enabled by Artificial Intelligence) as a set of community guidelines paired with a publication checklist. TRACE-AI emphasizes end-to-end traceability across the full lifecycle of an agentic catalysis campaign, linking research objectives to data and models, agent reasoning and action, and the knowledge acquired. By promoting standardized and accountable reporting, TRACE-AI aims to cultivate a shared foundation for accelerating scientific discovery while reinforcing safety and trust as autonomous catalysis laboratories continue to emerge.

papers.title: Application of machine learning to identify key physicochemical predictors for mimicking UHT cow milk
papers.abstract: Plant-based milk alternatives (PBMAs) differ from cow milk in their physicochemical properties, creating a significant challenge in their ability to replicate dairy-like functionality. In this study, machine learning was applied to identify the key physicochemical predictors associated with dairy-like properties in PBMAs. Two models, Random Forest Regression (RFR) and Gradient Boosting Regression (GBR), were trained using physicochemical, chemical composition and ingredients data from cow (10), soy (10), oat (10), almond (10), coconut (10), rice (3), and plant-hybrid (1) milk types. Model performance was evaluated using the coefficient of determination (R²), root mean square error (RMSE), learning curves, and compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Both models demonstrated strong predictive performance on testing data, RFR (R² = 0.80 ± 0.05; RMSE = 1.29 ± 0.19), and GBR (R² = 0.76 ± 0.05; RMSE = 1.46 ± 0.27), with no statistical difference in predictive accuracy. Permutation feature importance identified fat, carbohydrate, and xanthan gum content as the key predictors of physicochemical similarity to cow milk, reflecting their roles in determining volatile compounds, viscosity, particle size, whiteness, and physical stability. Volatile compounds, including δ-octalactone, also contributed to predictive accuracy. The performance of the models was limited by the small dataset size, the absence of sensory data, and commercial formulations. This study demonstrated the value of machine learning in predicting key physicochemical predictors in PBMAs mimicry of dairy. Future work should focus on formulation prediction, increasing dataset size, and the integration of sensory data to improve model robustness.

papers.title: A theoretical analysis of propargyl oxidation by the hydroperoxyl radical
papers.abstract: The kinetics of the C 3 H 3 + HO 2 reaction system were investigated theoretically using high-level quantum chemical methods combined with statistical rate theory. The potential energy surface (PES) was explored to identify intermediates and transition states using reactive molecular dynamics with ChemTraYzer-TAD. The resulting thermochemical data and energy barriers for products P0 to P13 were used in RRKM/master equation calculations to determine the temperature-and pressure-dependent rate constants suitable for incorporation into chemical kinetic models. Implications for chemical kinetic model predictions and future model development were assessed by representative jet-stirred reactor simulations of stoichiometric propyne/air mixtures at 10 atm and 800-1200 K. These simulations show that the widely employed allyl + HO 2 analogy overestimates propargyl consumption. In the jet-stirred reactor case considered here, replacing the analogy-based treatment with the theory-based update reduces the contribution of C 3 H 3 + HO 2 reactions to the overall consumption of C 3 H 3 from up to 26 % to no more than 15 %. The corresponding changes in benzene predictions are visible, but remain within the experimental uncertainty. Based on these findings, a compact reduced three-reaction submodel is proposed for future chemical kinetic model development. Novelty and significance statement We present the first comprehensive ab initio and master equation-based kinetic investigation of the C 3 H 3 + HO 2 reaction system. Barrierless and new low-barrier channels were identified using potential energy surface exploration with ChemTraYzer-TAD, and the resulting temperature-and pressuredependent rate coefficients provide a substantially more reliable description of this chemistry than the allyl + HO 2 analogy commonly used in chemical kinetic models. Jet-stirred reactor simulations show that replacing the analogy-based treatment reduces predicted C 3 H 3 consumption via reactions with HO 2 and leads to visible changes in benzene predictions that remain within the experimental uncertainty. Brute force sensitivity analysis further shows that only the OH-forming channel, C 3 H 3 + HO 2 = P-C 3 H 3 O + OH, noticeably affects the predicted C 3 H 3 and benzene mole fractions. Based on these findings, a compact reduced three-reaction submodel is proposed for future chemical kinetic model development. Because C 3 H 3 is a key C0-C4 core species, the refined kinetics are relevant beyond aromatic chemistry.

papers.title: Gas6-Enriched NIR-II Nanodecoys for Chemo-Photothermal Therapy and Preemptive Inhibition of Lung Metastasis in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
papers.abstract: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a highly aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis, and preventing its metastasis remains a major clinical challenge. In this work, we developed biomimetic nanodecoys (NDs) capable of precise diagnosis and effective treatment of NPC while concurrently preventing lung metastasis. The NDs were synthesized via precipitation polymerization to form a pH-and thermal-responsive poly(N-isopropylacrylamide-co-acrylic acid) nanogels (PA NGs), followed by encapsulation a newly developed aggregation-induced emission luminogen (AIEgen), NDA-N, for strong near-infrared (NIR) fluorescence imaging (FLI) and remarkable photothermal therapy (PTT) performance. In combination with the 2 chemotherapeutic drug doxorubicin (Dox), these NDs achieved effective chemo-photothermal combinatorial therapy. Triggered by the acidic tumor microenvironment, the NDs released Dox, and this release was further accelerated under NIR irradiation due to the generated heat. Moreover, we demonstrate that growth arrest-specific 6 (Gas6)-camouflaged NDs (PND@Gas6(+)) could function as a prophylactic agent to bind Axl receptor in lung metastatic niches, thereby preemptively blocking the Gas6/Axl axis and preventing metastatic colonization. This study presents an innovative strategy that integrates real-time NIR-II monitoring and synergistic chemo-PTT therapy for NPC, while also providing a rational design for metastasis inhibition, offering substantial promise for improving NPC treatment.

papers.title: Diclofenac Aptasensor Based on Graphene Field-Effect Transistor
papers.abstract: Biosensors are analytical tools whose performance is highly influenced by the transducing method and the construction protocol. Graphene field-effect transistors (GFETs) are recognized as sensitive sensors owing to their strong response to changes in surface charge, but their use is limited by complex fabrication and integration processes. In this work, we employ a straightforward method to modify commercially available GFET surfaces via diazonium salt reduction, yielding reproducible and robust interfaces. Using a protective-deprotective strategy to form controlled nanostructured monolayers, a GFET aptamer-based sensor was developed for the detection of diclofenac (DCF). For that purpose, an azide-modified aptamer sensitive to DCF was immobilized on the surface of the functionalized graphene by click chemistry, an orthogonal and biocompatible covalent immobilization strategy. The sensor had a linearity range from 5 to 100 nM, reaching a satisfactory limit of detection of 3.1 nM, comparable to the concentrations of the analyte found in the environment. Moreover, the sensor has good selectivity, stability, repeatability, and performance in river water. This strategy marks the first attempt to develop an aptamer-based GFET sensor for DCF detection.

papers.title: Biaryl Tetrazines as Chemoselective Double-Click Reagents
papers.abstract: Biaryl 1,2,4,5-tetrazines are established as a new class of bench-stable bifunctional click reagents for chemoselective double Diels-Alder reaction sequences. A unified approach to both symmetric and unsymmetric biaryl tetrazines via Pd-catalyzed coupling of bromotetrazines is described, providing derivatives amenable to further functionalization, including via mutually orthogonal Cu-catalyzed azide-alkyne Huisgen click reactions. Diels-Alder studies reveal that biaryl tetrazines undergo chemoselective mono-cycloaddition reactions with strained alkynes as dienophiles, which can be followed by a second Diels-Alder reaction with a dienophile at either the alkyne or alkene oxidation level. Computational analysis reveals that a subtle interplay between electronic interactions and substrate distortion energies governs cycloaddition chemoselectivity. Leveraging this reactivity, we demonstrate a model bioconjugative double Diels-Alder sequence that exhibits advantageous proximity-enabled fluorescence quenching properties.

papers.title: Long-Term Release Behavior and Cytotoxicity Assessment of Therapeutic Agents from Nanostructured Laser-Modified Titanium Niobium Zirconium Tin Implants
papers.abstract: The development of advanced biomaterials for implantable devices has increasingly focused on improving both therapeutic functionality and biocompatibility. In this study, nanostructured surfaces were engineered on titanium-niobium-zirconium-tin (Ti-Nb-Zr-Sn) alloys using laser modification techniques to enable controlled drug delivery and enhanced cellular response. The laser processing generated hierarchical surface features that significantly increased surface area and facilitated the incorporation of therapeutic agents within the nanostructures. The long-term release behavior of the loaded agents was systematically evaluated under physiological conditions, revealing a sustained and predictable release profile over extended periods without significant burst effects. Cytotoxicity assessment was conducted using relevant in vitro cell models to evaluate the biological safety of the modified implants. The results demonstrated high cell viability, minimal inflammatory response, and improved cell adhesion and proliferation compared to untreated surfaces. The synergy between the nanostructured topology and controlled drug release contributed to a favorable microenvironment for tissue integration. Furthermore, the Ti-Nb-Zr-Sn alloy exhibited excellent corrosion resistance and mechanical stability, supporting its suitability for long-term biomedical applications. Overall, the findings highlight the potential of laser-modified nanostructured Ti-Nb-Zr-Sn implants as multifunctional platforms for localized therapy and improved osseointegration. This approach offers a promising pathway for next-generation implantable devices with enhanced therapeutic efficiency and reduced adverse effects.

papers.title: Co-Al LDH nanoclusters for enhanced visible-light-driven photocatalytic H2 production
papers.abstract: The efficient conversion of solar energy into chemical energy represents one of the most significant challenges in contemporary society. Photocatalytic systems combining a catalyst, a photosensitizer (PS), and a sacrificial electron donor (ED) are widely explored for this purpose. Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) have shown great potential as catalysts. In this study, we demonstrate efficient photocatalytic hydrogen evolution using Co-Al LDH nanoclusters synthesized by the epoxide method in the presence of fluorescein as the photosensitizer and triethanolamine as the electron donor. Colloidal nanosized LDH display a remarkable hydrogen production of 28863 µmol H 2 g –1 after 3.5 h, while redispersed solid reached 12567 µmol H 2 g –1 . Increasing PS concentration to 1 mM further enhances the activity to 54105 µmol H 2 g –1 . By contrast, micrometric LDHs synthesized by the urea hydrolysis method produce only 2065 µmol H 2 g –1 . PL studies suggest that the acac layer on the nanosized LDH surface confers a hydrophobic environment, mitigating aggregation-induced quenching. Electrochemical experiments confirm a lower charge-transfer resistance in nanometric LDHs, explaining their superior charge transport and catalytic efficiency.

papers.title: Chemical vapour deposition of high-purity, heavily boron-doped diamond in a low-cost, custom-built microwave plasma reactor
papers.abstract: Boron-doped diamond, an outstanding electrode material, is commonly synthesised via chemical vapour deposition (CVD) using expensive and toxic boron-containing gases. Alternative boron sources are therefore attractive; however, their use in the growth of phase-pure diamond films is so far limited. This study presents how trimethyl borate (TMBT; B(OCH 3) 3) can be used as a liquid precursor of boron for the growth of high-quality, heavily boron-doped diamond films in a custom-made, microwave plasmaassisted CVD system. These polycrystalline films were deposited on Si plates at a very high boron-tocarbon molar ratio (105,000 ppm) with homogeneous distribution throughout the film. The films exhibit an atypical surface morphology, composed of {110} and {100} crystallographic facets. Typical growth rates of about 1.5 μm/h were achieved for the process carried out without enhancements. The average concentration of boron in the films was determined to be 6.48×10 21 cm-3. Moreover, the films are characterised by negative electron affinity. The availability of these diamond films from a highly reproducible and very accessible procedure is opening new possibilities for electrochemistry, sensing and photo-electrocatalytic applications.

papers.title: Substitution-Driven Control of Excited-State Dynamics in Mono-Annulated Indigos
papers.abstract: A series of mono-annulated indigo (MAI) derivatives was synthesized and systematically investigated to elucidate the role of structural asymmetry on excited-state dynamics. The synthesized MAIs exhibit pronounced solvatochromism, large Stokes shifts, and base-induced NIR absorption. Transient absorption measurements showed ns-lived singlet states and ms-lived triplet states, demonstrating substitution-controlled ISC and relaxation pathways.

papers.title: Face saturation at ρ * = 4 ln 2: a universal threshold separating cooperative from individual relaxation in hydrogen-bonded liquids
papers.abstract: The non-Arrhenius crossover in the dielectric relaxation of liquid water near 35-45 • C has been documented for four decades. No existing model predicts the crossover temperature without a fitted parameter. We show that the crossover occurs at a topological threshold ρ * = 4 ln 2, derived from the 4-simplex (K5) and not adjusted. A periodic table of K5 hydrides (CH4, NH3, H2O, HF and their third-row analogues) reveals that water is the only simple hydride combining a permanent dipole with an effective hydrogen-bond density ρ above the threshold. The crossover at ∼ 40 • C is a direct consequence of this unique position. We test the universality of ρ * on a database of 11 hydrogen-bonding liquids with published temperature-dependent dielectric relaxation data. Using the measured number of hydrogen bonds per molecule nHB as the effective density ρ, the threshold classifies 10 of 11 liquids correctly: B19 • Regime II (ρ * < ρ < 2ρ *): cooperative. Water, formamide: 2/2. • Regime I (ρ < ρ *): individual. DMF, DMA, MeOH, EtOH, PrOH, DMSO, CH3CN: 7/7. • Regime III (ρ > 2ρ *): vitrification. Glycerol: 1/1. The single exception is N-methylformamide (NMF, nHB = 2.0 < ρ * , cooperative). Neutron diffraction shows NMF forms linear chains, not triangular clusters: its cooperativity arises from sequential bond breakage, a mechanism distinct from K5 face saturation. The gap between the lowest cooperative ρ (formamide, 3.08) and the highest individual ρ (ethanol, 1.5) straddles ρ * = 2.773 with no overlap. All nHB values are sourced from neutron diffraction or molecular dynamics; all τ (T) classifications are from the original authors. No existing model (Tanaka, Stanley, Poole) extends beyond water. D2O (nHB = 3.76) and ethylene glycol (nHB = 3.0-3.7) are predicted to show cooperative relaxation. Both are testable immediately. The threshold also predicts a critical concentration in water-alcohol mixtures: the non-Arrhenius crossover in τ (T) should disappear at x * MeOH ≈ 0.35 (25 • C) in water-methanol, and x * EtOH ≈ 0.39 in water-ethanol. B20 In the (T, nHB) plane, the cooperative-individual boundary is a horizontal line at nHB = ρ * , regardless of how nHB is varied (temperature, concentration, or pressure). Four K5 constants, together with one measured input (f coord), predict the relaxation time τ of 6 hydrides with τ free derived from geometry, and of 5 further molecules across three decades (3-1500 ps). All 11 predictions fall within a factor 3. B17 Companion script: 123 tests, 20 blocks, all PASS.

papers.title: A Columnar Liquid Crystalline Self-Assembly of a Donor-Acceptor TADF Emitter Design for Solution-Processed OLEDs
papers.abstract: The self-assembly of π-conjugated molecules into supramolecular columnar structures has become as an effective strategy for the creation of soft, durable, and adaptable materials with immense potential for application in organic optoelectronic devices. In this regard, the columnar organization of discotic liquid crystals (DLCs) is well-studied in terms of a quasi-1D charge transport medium, which can be exploited across a range of organic electronic device applications. There are relatively few examples of room temperature columnar DLCs emitting thermally activated delayed fluorescent (TADF). Herein, we demonstrate a molecular design strategy to deliver a material that simultaneously shows bright and efficient TADF and self-organizes into columnar DLCs at room temperature. The compound TCzTRZ-DLC contains three dendrimeric carbazole-based donors with mesogenic units decorating a central 1,3,5-triphenyltriazine acceptor. Notably, the system exhibited a desired homeotropic alignment resulting in preferential aromatic p-stacking among disc-like molecules, which is beneficial to boost the light out-coupling efficiency in solution-processed organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). The resulting green-emitting SP-OLEDs emitted at lEL of 488 nm and showed a maximum external quantum efficiency, EQEmax of 15.5%. This represents a significant improvement in OLED efficiency compared to other solution-processed devices using TADF emitters bearing mesogenic groups.

papers.title: Electrochemically Driven Phenazine Autoxidation Coupled with Supported Liquid Membrane Technology for Hydrogen Peroxide Production
papers.abstract: Green synthesis of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) using renewable electricity remains a substantial challenge due to strict requirements of complex catalysts and unavoidable H2O2 decomposition in electrochemical reactors. Here we report a compact electrified phenazine autoxidation (e-PAO) platform that couples an alkaline electrolyzer and a supported liquid membrane (SLM) reactor for continuous, high-purity H2O2 production. This electrified phenazine mediation system avoids the use of precious metal catalysts and gaseous reactants in electrocatalytic and conventional thermocatalytic H 2 O2 manufacture systems. The concept of SLM is applied to integrate hydrogenation, autoxidation and extraction into a single module, efficiently shuttling electrons from the aqueous electrolyte to H2O2 product across a fixed nonaqueous medium with Faradaic efficiency up to 80%. In this SLM architecture, separating electroreduction from H2O2 formation into distinct environments mitigates the H2O2 decomposition that is widespread in other electrochemical methods. We demonstrate direct applicability to advanced oxidation via in-situ Fenton treatment of organic pollutants, highlighting the potential of the e-PAO platform for modular, on demand H2O2 generation and wastewater remediation. This strategy provides an integrated and flexible reactor-construction framework for multiphase, electrochemically mediated synthetic processes.

papers.title: Electrochemical CO2 Mineralization and H2 Generation from Steel and Coal Waste
papers.abstract: This work introduces a novel electrochemical strategy that couples CO 2 capture and mineralization (CCM) with water electrolysis (WE). Leveraging the exothermicity of CO 2 mineralization, this process sustains a reverse pH gradient, reducing the potential required for water splitting by up to 0.39 V. Experimental validation using a three-chamber reactor achieved a steady state pH gradient of 4.4 between cathode and anode. Under this condition we demonstrate WE at an onset potential of 1.30 V and a Faradaic efficiency for CO 2 fixation of 93%. This equates to an energy efficiency for CCM of <0.5 kWh/kg CO 2 when considering the energy content of the generated H 2 . By combining water electrolysis with high CO 2 fixation efficiency, more CO 2 is captured than is emitted by the equivalent energy consumption from the electrical grid. Consequently, deploying this process using available electricity will immediately result in H 2 production at <1 USD/kg at net negative CO 2 emission. We further demonstrate that steel slag or coal ash can act as the CO 2 sorbent indicating that a byproduct of this process is valorization of industrial waste to phase-pure, synthetic calcite. At scale this process has capacity to mitigate >500M tonnes CO 2 emissions annually.

papers.title: ChemAgents: A Hybrid Agentic Framework Coupling Large Language Models, Molecular Transformers, and Physics-Based Simulations for Accessible Computational Chemistry
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence in chemistry has produced a powerful yet fragmented ecosystem of predictive models, creating a significant accessibility gap for domain experts who lack specialized machine learning expertise. To bridge this divide, we introduce ChemAgents, a practical, domain-specific agentic AI framework designed to make molecular property prediction and simulation more intuitive and reproducible. Expanding upon previous conversational agent architectures such as ChemCrow [1] and ChemToolAgent [2], ChemAgents employs a layered system of 13 specialized agents, a custom toolset integrating PubChem, LAMMPS molecular dynamics, and a novel Simulation-AI Coupler, alongside an aggressive duallayer caching architecture (in-memory LRU + persistent SQLite) that reduces repeated-query latency by up to 200×. The framework offers two complementary interaction modes: (i) a direct conversational agent for rapid task routing and (ii) a hybrid LLM-tool agent that leverages multistep ReAct reasoning for complex inquiries. A novel confidence-triggered hybrid prediction scheme dynamically routes molecules between fast AI screening and computationally expensive physics-based validation. The core specialist models were developed by fine-tuning the ChemBERTa-2 foundation model [3] on the MoleculeNet benchmarks ESOL, Tox21, and ClinTox [4], demonstrating competitive performance against established GCN baselines. By combining generalist LLM reasoning with domain-specialized transformer models and traditional simulation engines, ChemAgents demonstrates a practical path toward democratizing access to advanced computational chemistry workflows.

papers.title: Diradical Generation/Complexation via Relayed Single-Electron Transfer
papers.abstract: The concept of single-electron transfer (SET) has been widely employed to rationalize the generation and complexation of radical species, facilitating a wealth of efficient synthetic strategies with high atom economy. However, precisely locating a SET transition state has been and continues to be the holy grail of radical chemistry, and the electron transfer pictures during the SET process have not been captured in both theory and experiment by now. Herein, we proposed and confirmed a new mechanistic model named relayed single electron transfer (relayed-SET) for diradical generation/complexation, and located the relayed-SET transition state in case studies by performing quantum mechanical calculations for the first time. Further control experiments have shown that the reaction indeed undergo a SET process discovered through theoretical calculations, revealing the feasibility of designing free radical reactions based on the relayed-SET model. The calculated results indicate the orbital overlap is necessary for relayed-SET, yet the process is not accompanied by intermolecular bond formation or breaking. Analysis of π-electron number in key structures provides direct evidence that the SET process involves a single π-electron transfer. This work helps deepen the understanding of the nature for radical chemistry and combines experiments with theories demonstration that SET reactions is an electron transfer process via orbital overlap.

papers.title: Recent Advances and Perspectives of Artificial Intelligence in the Discovery of Enzyme Inhibitors for Metabolic Syndrome: A Focus on Computational Design and Data Platforms
papers.abstract: The discovery of enzyme inhibitors for Metabolic Syndrome (encompassing obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus) is undergoing a paradigm shift driven by data science and computational power. This review article systematically analyzes recent literature (2019-2024), focusing on Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted rational drug design, the exploitation of ultra-large chemical spaces, and the underlying database infrastructures. We examine how Deep Learning architectures-specifically molecular Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), Transformers, and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs)-have optimized the screening and de novo design of inhibitors targeting DPP-4, PTP1B, and Pancreatic Lipase. Our analysis indicates that integrating makeon-demand databases with AI platforms allows researchers to explore chemical spaces of up to 10 10 molecules, vastly outperforming traditional empirical methods. Consolidated metrics demonstrate that GNNs achieve ROC-AUC values exceeding 0.92 in classifying active compounds, drastically reducing false-positive rates. Furthermore, generative models have proven to compress the hit-to-lead timeline by up to 80%. Finally, current computational bottlenecks, such as training data bias and synthetic accessibility, are discussed alongside the future perspectives of autonomous laboratories and quantum machine learning.

papers.title: Multi-Task Attention Network for Elucidating Synergistic Effects of Multiple Vacancies on Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity in High-Entropy Layered Double Hydroxides: A Synthetic Data Study
papers.abstract: This study introduces and validates a novel Multi-Task Attention Network (MTAN) framework designed to predict and interpret the complex synergistic effects of "multiple vacancies" on Oxygen Evolution Reaction (OER) activity in High-Entropy Layered Double Hydroxides (HE-LDHs). Utilizing combined chemical and characterization data, MTAN employs a shared encoder and task-specific attention mechanisms. The framework was evaluated on a comprehensive synthetic dataset and benchmarked against established supervised learning models, including Random Forest, XGBoost, and Graph Neural Networks, for both regression (predicting overpotential) and binary classification (categorizing activity). Our results demonstrate that MTAN consistently achieves superior predictive performance across all metrics, substantially outperforming baselines for overpotential prediction and activity classification. An ablation study further confirmed the critical contributions of both the attention mechanism and the multi-task learning paradigm. Interpretability tools, including MTAN's attention weights and SHAP analysis, elucidated task-specific feature importance. This analysis highlighted the synergistic roles of oxygen vacancy density, Ni coordination number, metal vacancy density, and Bader charge of Ni, thereby offering precise data-driven guidance for rational materials design.

papers.title: Organolithiums reactivity: geometric and energetic characterization of the lithium bond, substituents effect and cooperativity
papers.abstract: Lithium bonding has recently attracted increasing attention as a directional noncovalent interaction analogous to hydrogen bonding, with potential implications in organolithium chemistry and lithiumbased energy technologies. In the present study, the nature, strength, and substituent effects of lithium bonds formed by organolithium compounds were investigated using density functional theory calculations at the ωB97XD/6-311++G(d,p) level of theory. A series of CH₂XLi molecules (X = H, F, Cl, Br, CH₃) interacting with water and ammonia were analyzed to characterize the C-Li⋯O and C-Li⋯N lithium bonds and to evaluate possible cooperativity with hydrogen bonding. Geometric, energetic, and electronic analyses reveal that the Li⋯N complexes are generally more stable than the Li⋯O counterparts, with binding energies ranging from 77-91 kJ mol⁻¹ for Li⋯N and 66-83 kJ mol⁻¹ for Li⋯O interactions. In Li⋯O complexes containing halogen substituents, additional O-H⋯X hydrogen bonds lead to cooperative stabilization and cyclic structures. Natural Bond Orbital (NBO) analysis shows that classical donor-acceptor charge transfer from LP(N/O) → σ*(C-Li) contributes modestly to stabilization, whereas a stronger LP(N/O) → LP*(Li) interaction involving the vacant p lithium orbital is observed. Molecular electrostatic potential maps reveal a pronounced σ-hole along the extension of the C-Li bond, supporting the directional nature of lithium bonding. The combined analyses suggest that lithium bonding in organolithium complexes exhibits a hybrid character, dominated by σ-hole electrostatic interactions but supplemented by orbital contributions resembling π-hole interactions. These findings provide new insights into the fundamental nature of lithium bonding and may contribute to a better understanding of lithium-containing systems in organic synthesis, catalysis, and lithium battery chemistry.

papers.title: Ensuring Physicochemical Fidelity of Generated Polymers with PoGE
papers.abstract: The computational design of polymers with targeted macroscopic properties is frequently limited by the tendency of generative models to produce structures that deviate from experimental reality. Standard evaluation metrics, originally derived for small drug-like molecules, often do not adequately capture the physicochemical constraints unique to polymeric materials. To address this, we introduce PoGE (Polymer Generation and Evaluation), a transformer-based framework trained on a hybrid corpus of generated and experimentally validated polymer representations. We propose a physics-driven evaluation suite that utilizes Wasserstein distance to quantify the alignment between generated and experimental property distributions, replacing traditional fragment-based scoring. PoGE demonstrates superior fidelity to the physicochemical attributes of real-world polymers-specifically regarding molecular weight, topological polar surface area, and chain flexibility-when compared to existing recurrent neural network and conditional generation baselines. Notably, this alignment is achieved through unconditional sequence modeling, indicating that the architecture implicitly captures the complex structural rules governing polymer synthesis without requiring explicit descriptor conditioning. By providing a rigorously validated pre-training corpus and a physics-informed benchmarking framework, this work establishes a reliable foundation for the on-demand inverse design of synthesizable materials for advanced applications.

papers.title: Biocatalytic Metal Hydrogen Atom Transfer for Asymmetric Olefin-Olefin Coupling
papers.abstract: Metal-mediated hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT) enables versatile radical hydrofunctionalization reactions, yet asymmetric variants, especially for olefin-olefin coupling, remain unknown. Here we report an enzymatic solution using engineered protoglobins, establishing a biocatalytic platform for asymmetric MHAT-triggered intramolecular cyclization. Directed evolution of a protoglobin furnished a variant that catalyzes 5-exo-trig radical cyclizations to generate 3,4-substituted pyrrolidines in high yields and up to 98:2 e.r. The reaction tolerates diverse donor and acceptor substituents, including esters, amides, nitriles, nitro groups, imines, and ketones. Mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations support a radical pathway with an ultrafast enantiodetermining radical cyclization. These results show that engineered heme proteins can support new-to-nature MHAT chemistry and exert stereocontrol over rapid radical steps, providing a powerful system for asymmetric MHAT reactions.

papers.title: Accelerating Reaction Generalization through Domain-Specific Transfer Learning
papers.abstract: Generality in synthetic chemistry is often equated with a single set of reaction conditions that performs uniformly across diverse substrates. In practice, however, widely adopted transformations achieve generality not through a universal protocol, but through a wellcharacterized reaction space that enables rapid substrate-specific optimization. Here we report a machine-learning-guided strategy that accelerates this generalization process through active transfer learning. Bayesian optimization was used to generate a compact dataset of 120 experiments that maps the reaction landscape for the decarboxylative olefination of malonic acid derivatives. This domain-specific dataset provides transferable prior knowledge that enables the rapid identification of optimal conditions for new coupling partners, including previously unseen substrates. The method extends across thioesters, esters, and amides, providing a mild and atomeconomical alternative to classical phosphonate-based olefinations. More broadly, this work shows how small, information-rich datasets coupled with accessible machine learning tools can enable practical reaction generality and accelerate the translation of new reactions into routine synthetic use.

papers.title: Pushing complexometric titrations in the nanomolar range through SERS monitoring
papers.abstract: Complexometric titrations have been developed in the 40's and 50's for virtually every metal cation. However, the colorimetric of spectrophotometric monitoring of their endpoints limit their sensitivity range to the µM to mM range. Hence, these methods were quickly replaced by atomic instrumental methods, which became the new benchmark, when the corresponding instruments became widely accessible. However, in the context of a global lack of water quality data, especially in low income or geographically isolated areas, these instrumental golden standards are out of reach. In this work, we revisit a popular complexometric titration of the heavy metal cation Cu 2+ through monitoring the endpoint in Surface Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (SERS). We demonstrate a sensitivity at environmentally relevant concentrations, from 1 µM and down to 250 nM, thanks to SERS titration curves that mirror those predicted by thermodynamics. Remarkably, the method is cheap and frugal: it can be run with moderate chemical training, on a simple benchtop, using an instrument worth 10 keuros that can be battery-operated on field. Trueness of at least 75 ± 1% for coarse titrations and 96 ± 3% for a finer-resolution were obtained, in 2 hrs for 6 to 9 readouts (including duplicates and blanks), and for a consolidated cost of 28 euros, demonstrating the frugality of the overall method.

papers.title: Regiodivergent Synthesis of gem-Difluoroalkenes Enabled by Electron Donor-Acceptor Complex-Mediated C–F Bond Photoreduction of α-Trifluoromethyl Styrenes
papers.abstract: gem -Difluoroalkenes are valuable carbonyl bioisosteres in medicinal chemistry. Conventional synthesis primarily involves nucleophilic addition to α-trifluoromethyl styrenes. In contrast, recent approaches leverage photocatalytic radical addition, followed by reduction and fluoride elimination. Reaction pathways utilizing gem-difluoroallyl radicals remain largely underdeveloped despite their potential to enhance synthetic diversity. We report herein an electron donor-acceptor (EDA) complex-mediated C-F bond photoreduction of αtrifluoromethyl styrenes for the synthesis of gem -difluoroalkenes via gem -difluoroallyl radical addition. Radical trapping experiments confirm the formation of gem -difluoroallyl radical intermediates. By integrating this radical pathway with a conventional nucleophilic addition strategy, regiodivergent synthesis of gem -difluoroalkenes is achieved. To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first example of C–F bond photoreduction and functionalization of α-trifluoromethyl styrenes via gem -difluoroallyl radicals, forming gem -difluoroalkenes.

papers.title: Two-step bubble printing for continuous nanoparticle assembly through a structured flow field
Effects of ″On-Water″ on Free Radical Polymerization of Methacrylates
papers.abstract: Water-organic interfaces, referred to as ″on-water″, have recently attracted considerable attention because of their ability to accelerate various organic reactions. In this study, the effects of ″on-water″ interface on conventional free radical polymerization of methacrylates were investigated. Polymerizations were carried out under various conditions, including variations in monomer, solvent, reaction time, and stirring speed, to evaluate the effects of heterogeneity and interfacial area at the water-monomer interface. The results clearly indicate that the ″on-water″ interface plays a significant role in increasing the polymer molecular weight. Specifically, the polymerizations of 2-methoxyethyl and 2-ethoxyethyl methacrylates in water/methanol mixtures at specific solvent volume ratios resulted in a bimodal molecular weight distribution, in which the higher-molecular-weight fraction increased as the polymerization proceeded. This polymerization behavior is attributed to a transition of the reaction medium from a homogeneous to a heterogeneous phase during polymerization, demonstrating the ″on-water″ interfacial effects.

papers.title: Natural Product-Inspired Peptidomimetic Design Reveals Aromatic Interaction Patterns in OX2R
papers.abstract: Natural products provide structurally diverse scaffolds for ligand design, yet the determinants of ligand recognition in the orexin 2 receptor (OX2R) remain unclear. Docking analysis of the bisbenzylisoquinoline alkaloid neferine revealed recurrent positioning of aromatic moieties near His350 within the OX2R pocket. A similar interaction pattern was observed for the simplified analogue laudanosine, suggesting that this region is accessible to reduced aromatic motifs. To probe this interaction, a constrained cyclic peptidomimetic scaffold was designed to reduce conformational flexibility while retaining minimal aromatic features. The resulting docking poses showed reproducible localization of aromatic groups in the same region. Suvorexant exhibited comparable positioning, whereas alixorexton adopted distinct poses without consistent proximity to His350, even under restricted conformational conditions. These results suggest that ligand recognition in OX2R may involve a recurring aromatic interaction region near His350, while also supporting the presence of multiple binding modes depending on scaffold architecture.

papers.title: Bioactive Enhancement of Fish Sauce Using Black Garlic: Chemical Characterization and In Vitro Antiproliferative Activity
papers.abstract: This study was conducted to evaluate the physicochemical changes, antioxidant activity, and ability to inhibit hepatocellular carcinoma (Hep-3B) cells of black garlic under in vitro conditions, while also investigating the process of applying black garlic to the production of functional fish sauce. Fresh garlic was thermally fermented at with humidity for 35 days to convert it into black garlic. The analysis results showed that the fermentation process increased the reducing sugar content by 11 times (from 20 mg/g to 220 mg/g) and increased the antioxidant activity by 5 times compared to fresh garlic, with a value of .In anti-cancer tests, black garlic extract and S-allylcysteine (SAC) at a concentration of (calculated as SAC) showed a marked inhibition of Hep-3B cell line proliferation after 72 hours of exposure , through a mechanism of cell cycle arrest without causing immediate direct toxicity. Based on biological indicators, the study optimized the black garlic fish sauce mixing ratio at 3g black garlic/15mL fish sauce, achieving the highest sensory evaluation score and ensuring microbiological safety standards. These results help prove the value of black garlic as a potential ingredient for functional foods that support cancer prevention and health protection.

papers.title: Sovereignty: A Lasso-Derived Composite Descriptor for Categorical Stability Classification of Pharmaceutical Compounds
papers.abstract: We introduce Sovereignty, a composite stability descriptor derived via Lasso regression from three pharmacokinetic variables (clearance resistance, BBB penetration, and their interaction), for classifying pharmaceutical compounds into four structural states: Stable, Threshold, Drift, and Collapse. Validated on 294 compounds with experimental half-life data, Sovereignty achieves Pearson r = 0.672 (p = 6.41 × 10⁻⁴⁰) with log₁₀(t½), the highest correlation among all single descriptors tested, though statistically significantly higher than logP (Fisher z-test, p < 0.0001). For categorical classification, the associated field capacity metric F_cap achieves 88% accuracy (58/66) on extreme half-life cases (binomial test p = 9.0 × 10⁻¹¹ vs. random). Y-randomization z = 11.64 (conclusive). A key finding from Lasso calibration is that plasma protein binding (PPB) contributes zero weight to Sovereignty, contradicting common assumptions. The framework, equations, and software are fully specified in this paper and publicly available.

papers.title: Accounting for Land Clearing Greatly Increases Minerals' Life-cycle Greenhouse Gas Emissions
papers.abstract: Life cycle assessments of the minerals used in decarbonization do not consider the greenhouse gas emissions that arise from land use change as mining sites increase to accommodate growing minerals demand. This omission could lead to underestimation of lithium-ion battery and electric vehicle life-cycle GHG emissions. We developed a consequential LCA-inspired model to account for land use change greenhouse gas emissions that predicts per ton mineral life-cycle GHG emissions can increase up to four-fold. Per kWh battery emissions increase by 20-29% for nickel manganese cobalt cathode chemistries. Increases for batteries with LFP cathodes range from 9-16%. This analysis demonstrates how these emissions, previously unaddressed in existing models, could increase the contributions to climate change from mining minerals used in decarbonization technologies.

papers.title: Orbital Mixing Induced Stabilisation of Divalent Scandium Sandwich Complexes
papers.abstract: The unusual electronic structure of low-oxidation-state rare-earth ions with d -orbital occupation has spurred major advances in molecular magnetism and molecular qubit design. While progress has been made in expanding the range of ligand types employed, first-row donors are used almost exclusively and heavier main-group counterparts remain largely unexplored. Using scandium as a model rare-earth, we report and compare two anionic divalent sandwich complexes supported by substituted cyclopentadienide or isolobal phospholide ligands. Spectroscopic and computational analyses show that the unpaired electron is stabilised by an in-plane σ+π-bonding interaction between the phospholide and the scandium metal centre, whereas in the cyclopentadienide analogue it is almost entirely metal-centred, leading to significant differences in stability and decomposition pathways. This work highlights the importance of ligand orbital energy and symmetry matching for divalent rare-earth ions, and, more broadly, constitutes a new avenue in divalent rare-earth chemistry.

papers.title: Organelle-targeting large-Stokes-shift fluorescent probes for confocal, fluorescence-lifetime and 2-photon excitation microscopy applications
papers.abstract: Subcellular multiplex imaging is fundamentally limited by spectral crowding, restricted photostability, and the modality-specific performance of conventional fluorophores, which constrain the simultaneous visualization of multiple organelles in living cells. Here, we report a modular class of organelle-targeting, coumarin-based fluorescent probes that overcome these limitations through a large (up to 150 nm) Stokes shift, high brightness, good photostability, and efficient twophoton excitation. Central to this platform is a synthetically accessible, sulfonamide-functionalized coumarin core that enables convenient late-stage attachment of diverse organelle-targeting motifs. This modular strategy allows selective labeling of mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, lysosomes, plasma membrane, and whole cells at nanomolar concentrations with high signal-to-background ratios. The large Stokes shift minimizes spectral crosstalk and enables straightforward multiplex imaging in combination with green-and red-emitting fluorophores using simplified excitation schemes. These probes perform robustly across multiple imaging modalities, including confocal microscopy, two-photon excitation microscopy, fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy, and flow cytometry. These new dyes provide a versatile toolkit for dynamic subcellular studies in basic research and disease modelling.

papers.title: Hydrothermally Stable Single Atom Cu Catalysts on CeO2
papers.abstract: Single atom catalysts are characterized by atomic dispersion of an active transition metal on a support by creating a stable bond between the two providing resistance to deactivation such as sintering or coking. Single atoms can achieve stability at high temperatures under oxidizing conditions but reducing conditions or steam can cause the single atoms to migrate forming nanoparticles, significantly impacting stability of the catalyst. In the context of bio-derived fuels such as upgrading ethanol to sustainable aviation fuel, Cu catalysts have garnered interest due to their ability to dehydrate alcohols, but deactivation poses a challenge due to the low melting temperature of Cu and the presence of steam/hydrogen during reaction. Here we demonstrate the synthesis of single atom Cu catalysts that provide hydrothermal stability under conditions encountered during biofuel upgrading reactions. The use of a facile PVP sol-gel method achieves a high loading of atomically dispersed Cu (~5wt%) capable of surviving under aggressive hydrothermal and reducing conditions. We used CO oxidation as a probe reaction to distinguish single site ionic Cu from metallic Cu or Cu oxide nanoparticles which demonstrate lower reactivity. Using XAS and operando DRIFTS during CO oxidation we confirm that the fresh catalyst contains single atom Cu 2+ species which remain unchanged after aging.

papers.title: Resolving the inner versus outer component of the 5 f radial wavefunction in the early actinides
Leveling up upconverting nanoparticles with machine learning
Bacterial headspace sampler for real-time volatilome monitoring
papers.abstract: The bacterial volatilome is rich in information that can be exploited for metabolic investigations and infectious disease diagnostics, including identification and, potentially, rapid antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Robust and reliable headspace sampling is critical for the capture of bacterial emissions. Here, we introduce a standardized bacterial headspace sampling technique for reproducible and real-time analysis of bacterial growth plates. The system is based on an inert volume sampler for the accumulation and triggered extraction of trace-level microbial volatile organic compounds (mVOCs) from inoculated samples under controlled temperature and relative humidity. Integrated sample dilution is achieved using high-resolution mass flow controllers to meet the dynamic range requirements of various analytical tools, for instance, mass spectrometers and chemical sensors. A built-in analyte gas standard enables calibration between measurements. The sampling characteristics are assessed for key mVOCs (acetaldehyde, acetone, benzene, and ethanol) within relevant concentration ranges, down to parts-per-billion by volume (ppb) levels. In vitro tests with Escherichia coli confirm accurate capture of mVOC dynamics reflecting physiological changes during bacterial growth, as monitored by soft-ionization mass spectrometry over 24 hours. This setup offers a standardized approach compatible with diverse analytical tools for exploring the microbial volatilome.

papers.title: Enhancing Relative Binding Free Energy Calculation with Grand Canonical Monte Carlo, Water Swap Monte Carlo, Terminal-Flip Monte Carlo and Replica Exchange Solute Tempering
papers.abstract: Alchemical free energy calculations, particularly free energy perturbation (FEP), have become routine in drug design. When molecular dynamics (MD) is employed as the sampling method in FEP, accurately sampling water molecules deeply buried in protein binding pockets remains challenging, despite their critical role in protein-ligand interactions. We implemented three enhanced sampling methods, Grand Canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC), water swap Monte Carlo (water MC), and replica exchange with solute tempering (REST2). GCMC or water MC accelerate the hydration state equilibration in buried pockets and REST2 accelerates the sampling of ligand conformations. Combining REST2 with GCMC or water MC enables accurate calculation of ligand relative binding free energies. In the benchmark on the water set, our package achieved an RMSE of 0.94 kcal/mol, compared to 0.86 kcal/mol from FEP+ and 1.60 kcal/mol from OpenFE. This development provides the scientific community with an open-source sampling engine for robust and accurate FEP calculations.

papers.title: Interlayer expansion of bulk MoS2 via top-down organic pillaring enables tunable Li+ intercalation and controlled solvent co-intercalation
papers.abstract: Interlayer engineering is widely used to improve charge storage in layered transition metal dichalcogenides, yet most studies rely on nanosized materials where the effects of interlayer expansion and particle downsizing are intertwined. Here, molecular pillaring is translated to bulk molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) using a top-down strategy. Chemical pre-reduction with butyllithium enables exfoliation and restacking in the presence of hexanediammonium (HDA) molecules, forming a pillared MoS2-HDA structure with an expanded interlayer spacing of 0.98 nm while preserving the bulk particle morphology and specific surface area. Electrochemical analysis reveals that improved rate capability primarily originates from the chemical activation associated with the pre-reduction step rather than from interlayer expansion itself.
