Operando X-ray diffraction and electrochemical dilatometry show that bulk MoS2 undergoes solvent co-intercalation in diglyme electrolyte, leading to pronounced lattice expansion and electrode swelling. In contrast, pillared MoS2-HDA suppresses solvent cointercalation despite its larger interlayer spacing, demonstrating that interlayer expansion alone does not dictate solvent co-intercalation in layered electrodes.

papers.title: Enantioselective Deaminative Cross-coupling of Amino Acid Derivatives with Alkylzirconocenes
papers.abstract: The enantioselective construction of C(sp 3 )-rich architectures from renewable feedstocks remains a formidable challenge in synthetic chemistry, particularly when targeting stereocenters with minimal steric differentiation. While radical chemistry provides access to C(sp 3 )-rich motifs under mild conditions, catalystcontrolled enantioselective radical−radical coupling for such subtly differentiated aliphatic stereocenters has remained elusive. Here, we disclose a visible-light-mediated, nickel-catalyzed enantioselective deaminative cross-coupling of naturally abundant amino acids with unactivated alkenes via in situ -generated alkylzirconocenes. This operationally simple protocol operates without external photocatalysts or stoichiometric reductants, leveraging the intrinsic photoreactivity of alkylzirconocenes to generate both alkyl radicals and the reducing Cp 2 Zr III Cl species. The method exhibits broad functional group tolerance and delivers a wide array of chiral amides with high efficiency and excellent enantioselectivity (up to 83% yield and 99% e.e.). Notably, it enables the asymmetric construction of stereogenic centers bearing minimally differentiated alkyl substituents that differ by a methylene unit or heteroatom, directly addressing a long-standing challenge in asymmetric catalysis. Mechanistic investigations support a radical-radical cross-coupling pathway controlled by a chiral nickel catalyst, with Cp 2 Zr III Cl serving as a key reductant to sustain the catalytic cycle. This work establishes alkylzirconocenes as versatile platforms for enantioselective radical transformations and offers a sustainable route to value-added chiral carbonyl compounds from amino acids.

papers.title: Molecular Adsorbing Host•Guest (MAHG) Crystals: A New Paradigm for Porous Materials?
papers.abstract: Since the discovery of host•guest complexes, we have assisted to huge developments of this part of chemistry, liquid state studies brightly leading the way. In this context, numerous macrocycles and cages have shown exceptional relevance for selective and controllable guest capture and release mainly based on 1:1 host•guest complexes. With such attributes, applications pertaining to sequestration, separation, catalysis, template synthesis and more generally to biology and materials science have flourished over time. Comparatively, the solid-state chemistry of host•guest complexes is less developed, especially that involving macrocyclic hosts. In this context, we recently reported the crystal structure of what could be the first of a series of Molecular Adsorbing Host•Guest (MAHG) crystals featured by several new properties. Whereas a rapidly growing field today exists about porous Hydrogen-bonded Organic Frameworks (HOFs), some composed of macrocyclic "hosts only", an unchartered territory appears within reach for (macrocyclic) "host•guest complexes". Given the huge diversity of host•guest complexes described in the liquid state, rapid developments of MAHG type materials are expected in the near future.

papers.title: Crystal Structure of the DMF-Coordinated Perovskite Precursor Intermediate (MA)₂(DMF)₂Pb₂I₄Cl₂
papers.abstract: (MA) 2 (DMF) 2 Pb 2 I 4 Cl 2 , a DMF-coordinated perovskite precursor intermediate, was isolated by dropwise addition of a 3MAI + PbCl 2 solution in DMF at room temperature. Its crystal structure, determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SC-XRD), reveals a triclinic space group P—1 (No. 2) with lattice parameters a = 4.54193(19) Å, b = 11.8019(6) Å, c = 12.4835(6) Å, α = 94.265(7)°, β = 97.666(7)°, γ = 96.042(7)°, V = 656.83(5) Å 3 . The structure features infinite one-dimensional [Pb₂I₄Cl₂]²⁻ chains in which iodide and chloride coexist at a crystallographically fixed I : Cl ratio of 2 : 1, stabilized by hydrogen-bonded methylammonium cations and coordinated DMF molecules. This is the first crystallographically characterized perovskite precursor phase incorporating both iodide and chloride, providing direct structural evidence for the role of chloride in one-step solution-processed MAPbI 3 deposition.

papers.title: A Hybrid GNN-QAOA Pipeline for Constrained Drug Repurposing Portfolio Selection with Topology-Aware Compilation on IBM Heavy-Hex Quantum Hardware
papers.abstract: Constrained portfolio selection in drug repurposing (choosing subsets of approved compounds that jointly satisfy interaction avoidance, toxicity ceilings, and target-coverage requirements) remains intractable for classical integer programming beyond ∼10,000 candidates, precisely the regime where combinatorial drug repositioning operates. Existing quantum formulations address pairwise drug-combination scoring but do not account for portfolio-level constraints or the mismatch between problem graph structure and physical qubit connectivity. We introduce a three-stage pipeline: a relational graph convolutional network (RGCN) narrows the candidate pool to ∼5,000 triples, a QUBO encoding extends the Complementary-Exposure framework [6], [36] with budget, diversity, and multitarget coverage penalties, and a topology-aware QAOA compiler maps constraint blocks onto natively connected heavy-hex qubit clusters. The compiler reduces two-qubit SWAP-gate counts by 23-41% relative to Qiskit optimization-level-3 transpilation on sub-problems of 20-100 qubits (Table IV), directly lowering accumulated gate error on IBM Heron r2 hardware. Retrospective validation on ten FDA-approved repurposed drugs yields 82.5% Recall@100 on a noiseless simulator versus 79.3% for ILP/Gurobi; on real IBM Heron hardware, recall drops to 69.8% (approximation ratio 0.64), falling 9.5 percentage points behind ILP and quantifying the noise gap that future errorcorrected processors must close. The central finding is negative: at current NISQ fidelities, classical ILP produces strictly superior solutions in less wall-clock time. The contribution is therefore architectural, not algorithmic; the topology-aware compilation strategy transfers directly to improved processors without redesign, positioning the pipeline for the p ≤ 10 −4 gate-error regime projected for 2028-2030. Code and QUBO encodings will be released upon acceptance.

papers.title: Armstrong's Hierarchical Molecular Graph Framework (AHMGF)
papers.abstract: Traditional molecular formulas and structural notations (e.g., SMILES, InChI) compress multi-scale or hierarchical chemical structures into flat strings, capturing composition and connectivity for discrete molecules while obscuring layering, surface oxidation, and multi-cluster assemblies. This paper presents Armstrong's Hierarchical Molecular Graph Framework (AHMGF), a nested notation that encodes hierarchical relationships between chemical units, permitting core-shell structures, molecular clusters, sheets, and surface layers to be represented independent of explicit spatial coordinates. AHMGF represents each chemical unit as a node, with nesting denoting hierarchical adjacency that may be chemically interpreted as containment without implying spatial enclosure, and includes multiplicities to quantify repeated subunits. I define the canonical syntax, demonstrate an algorithm for constructing nested representations from layered or clustered structures, and illustrate the framework with examples including oxidized iron sheets, nanoparticle clusters, and supramolecular assemblies. AHMGF is purely notational and hierarchical, yet fully computable, permitting automated parsing, analysis, and integration with materials-informatics workflows while preserving intuitive structural relationships that are inaccessible in traditional flat formulas.

papers.title: Fast computation of exact symmetry-corrected RMSD of conformers
A Sequence-Specific Theory for Charge-Regulating IDPs
papers.abstract: Intrinsically disordered proteins are an important class of biological polymers whose physico-chemical properties and biological functions are determined by an intricate interplay of chain connectivity, electrostatic interactions, the sequence of residues, and non-universal short-range interactions. An important phenomenon in these molecules is charge regulation, which arises because of weakly acidic and basic residues, but is often neglected in theoretical descriptions. In this work, we use the Edwards-Singh variational method to derive an approximate variational theory that describes sequence effects in the charge regulation and chain conformation of intrinsically disordered proteins. The main result of our theory is a set of coupled algebraic equations yielding a renormalized Kuhn length and residue-specific mean-fields that determine the respective ionization states. We discuss limiting cases of these equations that underline the internal consistency of our theory and connect our results to earlier studies. To solve the full set of equations, we propose a simple numerical scheme. As test cases, we calculate the conformation and ionization state of a weak polyelectrolyte and of thirty sequence variants of the polypeptide (EK) 25 . For the weak polyelectrolyte, we show that the theory predicts phenomena such as the overall suppressed ionization due to electrostatic interactions and the enhanced ionization at the chain ends. In the case of the polypeptide (EK) 25 , we find strong effects of the sequence on ionization, with well-mixed sequences exhibiting a broad pH range where the polypeptide is net neutral, while blockier sequences exhibit a steeper ionization response. Moreover, we also observe pronounced sequence effects on the swelling behavior of the chains.

papers.title: Linking solvation structure, activity, and electronic structure to electrochemical stability in lithium-ion battery electrolytes
papers.abstract: Electrolyte stability governs the performance and lifetime of Li-ion batteries, yet a quantitative molecular-level framework linking salt concentration to electrochemical stability remain absent. Here, we develop an integrated theoretical–experimental framework that quantitatively connects solvation structure, thermodynamic activities, and electronic structure to electrochemical stability for LiPF 6 :EC:EMC (3:7 v:v). Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, a lattice fluid theory, X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), and density functional theory (DFT) are combined to predict electrolyte stability across concentration. We derive simple, analytic expressions for the activities of species, which are then experimentally parameterized using Raman spectroscopy and validated against MD simulations and experiment. Increasing salt concentration is found to enhance PF 6 − participation in the Li + coordination shell while suppressing free solvent populations, leading to systematic shifts in the activities of species and an expanded electrochemical stability window. The lattice fluid theory directly links solvation structure to measurable shifts in redox potentials via the Nernst equation, which we confirm experimentally. DFT calculations predict concentration-dependent shifts in unoccupied electronic states, which are validated by O and F K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy. These shifts provide the physical origin for the activity changes predicted by lattice fluid theory, while frontier orbital analysis further rationalizes the evolution of interphase composition arising from enhanced PF 6 − reactivity at high concentrations. This work establishes a predictive protocol connecting solvation structure, thermodynamic activity, and electronic structure with electrolyte stability, enabling rational design of electrolytes with tailored stability windows.

papers.title: Sulfotransferases from Bacterial Secondary Metabolism Enable Access to N-Heterocycles
papers.abstract: In this communication, we report the characterization of a new subclass of cryptic sulfotransferases (STs) and demonstrate their broad potential for N -heterocycle formation. We find that the ST enzymes Fic28, Vzb21, and Azi31 enable stereospecific sulfation of a variety of natural and unnatural amino alcohol substrates. We report a novel one-pot chemoenzymatic cascade for the desymmetrization of serinol into enantioenriched N H-aziridines. Finally, we demonstrate the existence of additional cryptic STs in putative biosynthetic gene clusters of novel natural products through genome mining. Together, this work accesses previously untapped reactivity for STs, and describes their potential uses in biocatalysis and natural product discovery.

papers.title: Vibronic contributions to hyperfine-mediated spin kinetics
papers.abstract: The hyperfine interaction is a cornerstone of spin-dependent processes, yet the kinetic modelling of this mechanism remains limited by the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, obscuring the observation of coherent pathways that underpin many photophysical systems. Here, we introduce a unified theoretical framework that rigorously incorporates vibronic contributions through a phase-consistent Herzberg-Teller expansion of the hyperfine Hamiltonian. Application to the FMNH•-Cys• radical pair shows that second-order vibronic coupling enhances hyperfine-mediated electronic transitions between spin states by up to 10 8 − 10 9 -fold. The S◦ →T◦ rate increases from ~5− 40 s −1 (Franck-Condon) to ~2 × 10 8 − 1 × 10 9 s −1 (Herzberg-Teller), while the T◦ →S◦ rate increases from ~4 × 10 2 − 1 × 10 3 s −1 to ~1 × 10 10 − 5 × 10 10 s −1 . This observed nanosecond timescale correlates well with the microsecond lifetime photoadduct formation central to its function. Comparison to spin-orbit coupling (SOC) places these rates within the broader landscape of spin-mixing mechanisms, indicating that the hyperfine interaction operates on chemically relevant timescales. Despite the larger magnitude, SOC-mediated transitions are incoherent; the hyperfine interaction in contrast preserves coherence and is therefore crucial to spin evolution models. This work underscores the importance of incorporating a vibronic description in hyperfine-driven dynamics and provides a generalised methodology that captures essential non-Condon effects even at the single-structure level; thus serving as a complementary tool for systems where full ensemble sampling is impractical or not yet integrated into standard workflows.

papers.title: An Experimental and Theoretical Investigation of the Electrochemical Reactivity and Electron Transfer Kinetics of Perindopril Erbumine
papers.abstract: This study explores the electrochemical properties of Perindopril Erbumine (PE) via cyclic voltammetry (CV) and correlates with density functional theory (DFT) calculations at the CAM-B3LYP level. CV experiments, conducted with a three-electrode system (glassy carbon working electrode, Ag/AgCl reference, Pt counter), revealed distinct oxidation and reduction peaks, indicating sequential oxidation processes, with scan rate studies (10–100 mV s⁻¹) confirming diffusion-controlled yet kinetically hindered electron transfer. DFT results show that PE exists as a neutral COOH···N hydrogen-bonded complex in the gas phase. Frontier molecular orbital analysis indicates a large HOMO–LUMO gap (7.78 eV), reflecting high kinetic stability, with the HOMO localized over amine and carbonyl groups, identifying preferred oxidation sites. The first adiabatic ionization potential (6.54 eV) correlates with the initial anodic peak, while the higher second ionization potential (18.44 eV) explains oxidation at elevated potential. Low electron affinity values account for the weak reduction response. These findings establish a diffusion-assisted, kinetically controlled sequential oxidation mechanism governed by intrinsic electronic structure.

papers.title: Manipulation of Electrospray-Produced Biomolecular Ions with Acoustic Fields at Atmospheric Pressure
papers.abstract: The coupling of electrospray ionization (ESI) with the newly discovered acoustic ion manipulation (AIM) phenomenon is demonstrated for biopolymer analytes, including peptides, proteins, and oligonucleotides. It is shown that large (i.e., up to ca. 12 kDa) and multiply charged ions are influenced by the presence of the acoustic fields. Specifically, we demonstrate the ability to gate, modulate, redirect, and focus these biomolecular ions through the use of an acoustic field. To ensure effective acoustic-ion interactions, it was necessary to desolvate the electrospray droplets and ions prior to the AIM field, through optimization of a drying-tube temperature and spray-gas pressure. In general, small and highly charged ions were more readily deflected from the unstable antinode region towards the acoustic nodes. This trend extended to a charge-state dependent behavior for protein ions, where higher charge ions of the same molecule were redirected more easily than their lower charge counterparts. This work lays a foundation for the implementation of AIM in the study of biomolecules, as well as other analytes introduced by ESI to ion-based spectroscopic techniques, such as mass spectrometry and ion mobility spectrometry.

papers.title: Dynamics of Ce-O bond energy upon formation of O vacancies
papers.abstract: CeO2 offers excellent oxygen storage capacity for catalysis and energy applications. It accommodates a surprising number of oxygen vacancies (VO), yet the driving force and origin of these VO are rarely discussed. Through a combination of in situ techniques and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS), here, we discovered that upon formation of the VO, the remaining Ce4+-O2- bond energy increases by at least 0.2 eV. Such an increase in the bond energy provides an additional enthalpy change (ΔH) in the reaction of VO formation, stabilizes the reduced CeO2 phase and explains why CeO2 can host an extensive array of VO. This work demonstrates that RIXS is effective in probing metal-oxygen bond energy, possibly under working conditions, which is an ideal method to quantify electronic structures with material performance.

papers.title: LACAN: Leveraging adjacent co-occurrence of atomic neighborhoods for molecular scoring and generation Authors
papers.abstract: LACAN (Leveraging Adjacent Co-occurrence of Atomic Neighborhoods) is a bond-level statistical scoring function and filter based on adjacent atomic environment co-occurrence. When integrated into evolutionary search it enables chemically constrained molecular generation. It scores molecules by asking: how likely is each bond, given the chemical environments on both sides of it? Some common molecular fragments co-occur next to each other less than expected by random chance. We leverage this phenomenon for a data-driven method that assesses the extent to which the local environment around each bond in a molecule conforms to the norms of a reference data set such as ChEMBL. This approach is based on co-occurrence patterns of circular atomic environments centered on the two atoms involved in the bond. We show LACAN can be effectively used as a transparent and interpretable filter for certain unstable and uncommon molecular functionalities such as haloamines and peroxides, and we compare it to other commonly used molecular filters, such as SAScore, QED and MolSkill. We show this filter can be used for molecular mutations and molecular breeding, while providing an effective railguard against unfeasible structures. We apply these operations in an evolutionary algorithm and demonstrate good performance in various generative tasks. Scientific contribution: We present a novel molecular filter which filters atypical bonds using co-occurrence patterns of adjacent atomic environments. We show it enables the application of genetic operations like mutation and crossover with more chemically reasonable outcomes than known genetic algorithms. We present a lightweight molecular generator with a performance similar to state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Leveraging AI/ML-driven Tools for Material Discovery and Critical Mineral Separations †
papers.abstract: Critical materials and rare earth elements (CM/REEs) are essential components for modern energy technologies, communication systems, security, and defense applications. However, CM/REE recovery from complex mining wastes remains a challenge. Currently used processes, dominated by solvent extraction and precipitation, are not well suited to complex environmental feedstocks such as coal fly ash, phosphogypsum, and metal mine tailings. Although there is intense interest in extracting CM/REEs via adsorptive processes due to their attractive selectivity and low solvent usage, the discovery of novel ligands with well-defined structure-property correlations and fast cycling rates remains challenging, particularly through scientific experimental design. In this Perspective, we discuss the significant potential of artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) and self-driving laboratories (SDLs) for the design of selective and mass-transferefficient adsorbents for the sustainable separation of CM/REEs from complex mining wastes. 2 Some important examples of the application of AI/ML include accelerating calculations in quantum chemistry, molecular dynamics, and discovery science, for which SDLs can be harnessed to facilitate the rapid validation, optimization, and scale-up of material systems. In principle, the combination of AI-based material discovery, continuous-flow processing, analytics, and reinforcement learning is expected to yield novel material-processing methods for CM/REE separation.

papers.title: A Thermodynamically Consistent Multiscale Framework for Additive Transport in Pharmaceutical Polymers: The Pharm-PATIK Theory
papers.abstract: The incorporation of functional additives into pharmaceutical polymers underpins modern drug delivery systems, yet the predictive modeling of additive mass transfer during processing remains a fundamental challenge. Existing frameworks rely on decoupled Fickian diffusion models that fail to capture the complex interplay between polymer rheology, crystallization dynamics, and mechano-chemical degradation-phenomena critically important for pharmaceutical applications where additive uniformity directly impacts drug product safety and efficacy. Here, we present the Pharm-PATIK (Pharmaceutical Polymer Additive Transport and Interaction Kinetics) framework: a thermodynamically consistent, multiscale computational theory for additive mass transfer in polymer matrices. The framework is built upon the GENERIC (General Equation for Non-Equilibrium Reversible-Irreversible Coupling) formalism and integrates: (i) a multicomponent Maxwell-Stefan diffusion model with shear-dependent Flory-Huggins interaction parameters; (ii) a phase-field description of polymer crystallization with additive exclusion dynamics; (iii) a finite-strain viscoelastic model capturing stress-induced additive migration via configurational temperature theory; and (iv) mechano-chemical degradation kinetics for predictive assessment of leachables formation. The governing equations are formulated as a system of coupled nonlinear partial differential equations with degenerate mobility, for which we establish mathematical well-posedness under physically relevant conditions. Homogenization theory bridges molecular-scale free-volume effects to equipmentscale transport phenomena. Validation against experimental benchmarks including forced Rayleigh scattering diffusivity measurements, X-ray fluorescence mapping, and twin-screw extrusion trials demonstrates predictive accuracy with mean absolute percentage error below 7%. The framework provides a rigorous foundation for digital design of pharmaceutical polymer processing operations, enabling predictive control of additive fate from extrusion through shelflife storage under quality-by-design (QbD) paradigms.

papers.title: Adhesion of soft materials depends on interfacial strength
papers.abstract: In the conventional description, peeling of an adhesive from a solid substrate is characterized in terms of adhesion energies at adhesive-substrate interfaces. However, this energy based identification faced considerable difficulties in explaining why the adhesion energy, also known as peel strength /gamma p , is many orders of magnitude greater than Dupré's thermodynamic work of adhesion, sigma0. In this study we present experimental evidence to demonstrate that polymer adhesion is governed by interfacial strength formed between the adhesive and substrate whose surface energy /gamma s plays no explicit role in controlling the adhesion strength /sigma adh . On different substrates with widely varying surface energies, by carrying out both tensile-adhesion tests to demonstrate the dependence of /sigma adh on applied rate and temperature and conventional peeling tests to show the effects of peeling speed v p and temperature on /gamma p , we propose that /gamma p explicitly depends on /sigma adh through a characteristic length scale P instead of /gamma s and /gamma 0 . Here P is the distance of the adhesive layer away from the peeling front, beyond which the adhesive undergoes little deformation. Since P is a much larger length scale than a molecular scale and /sigma adh directly depends on polymer-substrate interfacial interactions rather than substrate surface energy, peel strength /gamma p has no relationship with /gamma 0 and its dependence on temperature and peeling speed stems from the time and temperature dependencies of interfacial strength /sigma adh . As activated processes, interfacial debonding on shorter time scales and lower temperature required higher interfacial stress. Consequently, /sigma adh is rate and temperature dependent.

papers.title: Newman-Kwart Rearrangement Enabled by Flavin Photoredox Catalysis
papers.abstract: The Newman-Kwart Rearrangement (NKR) is a valuable transformation for accessing thiophenol derivatives from readily available phenols. Traditional methods for conducting the NKR are often limited by harsh reaction conditions, operational scalability, and reactions run in primarily organic solvents. Herein, we introduce a bioinspired approach to perform the NKR using (-)-riboflavin as a cheap and effective photocatalyst. The reaction has been demonstrated on a broad range of substrates in high yield with low catalyst loadings in primarily aqueous media. A combination of mechanistic and spectroscopic experiments suggest that the reaction proceeds through flavin photoredox-mediated singlet oxygen generation for oxidation of the starting O-arylthiocarbamate. The developed NKR is demonstrated on gram-scale, performed with green light, and is compatible with a variety of biological buffers.

papers.title: Photogenerated Oxetanes as a Gateway to Uphill Cyclopropanation
papers.abstract: Despite their privileged status in pharmaceutical chemistry, the sustainable synthesis of cyclopropanes remains a fundamental challenge. Conventional methods rely on hazardous diazo precursors or pre-functionalized substrates that generate stoichiometric byproducts. Here, we report an overall endergonic, catalytic route to cyclopropanes from abundant, renewable starting materials. Furan oxetanes, readily formed by photochemical [2+2] cycloaddition of aldehydes and furan, undergo an intramolecular SN-type rearrangement under Lewis-acid catalysis, producing cyclopropanes with ideal atom economy. The strategy enables access to meso-cyclopropane dicarbaldehydes, which are versatile intermediates that streamline the preparation of otherwise challenging bioactive motifs. By harnessing photogenerated oxetanes as cyclopropane precursors, this work offers a sustainable way to densely functionalized cyclopropanes from simple feedstocks under mild conditions.

papers.title: Geometric Orthogonality of Competing Structural Memories in Glass: Temperature Controls Mechanical Erasure of Thermal History
papers.abstract: Glass retains memory of its entire processing history in the spatial arrangement of atomic bonds. Whether competing histories-thermal (cooling rate) and mechanical (cyclic fatigue)-encode in geometrically independent structural subspaces, or whether one erases the other, has not been systematically investigated. Here we address this question using Lennard-Jones model glasses subjected to a 2D parameter sweep: strain amplitude δ ∈ {4, 6, 8, 12}% and cycling temperature T cyc ∈ {0.35, 0.38, 0.40, 0.42, 0.44, 0.46} (in LJ reduced units, spanning 0.78

papers.title: Logical Reasoning Profiles and General Chemistry Performance at a Hispanic-Serving Institution
papers.abstract: Logical reasoning is important for success in introductory chemistry, yet the reasoning profiles of students at Hispanic-serving institutions remain underreported. This study used the Group Assessment of Logical Thinking (GALT) to characterize the reasoning skills of 140 students enrolled in General Chemistry I at the University of Puerto Rico at Cayey during the first semester of the 2018-2019 academic year. Internal consistency of the instrument was acceptable (Cronbach's α = 0.731, Spearman-Brown = 0.753, and Guttman split-half = 0.751). Based on total GALT scores, 25.7% of students were classified as formal reasoners, 29.3% as transitional reasoners, and 45.0% as concrete reasoners, indicating that most participants had not yet reached the formal operational level. Across reasoning modes, students performed best in mass/volume conservation and combinatorial reasoning, and weakest in proportional, probabilistic, and correlational reasoning. Descriptive comparisons by final course grade, gender, and academic year suggested that stronger logical reasoning tended to align with better course outcomes, whereas lowerperforming students were more frequently represented in the transitional and concrete groups. These findings provide a local profile of students' reasoning skills in General Chemistry and suggest that introductory chemistry instruction may benefit from more explicit support for abstract reasoning.

papers.title: A Polyacrylamide Hydrogel Platform with Physiological Stiffness for Cell Sheet Fabrication via Desthiobiotin-Streptavidin Functionalization
papers.abstract: Cell sheet engineering enables the harvest of scaffold-free, extracellular matrix (ECM)-rich cellular layers for regenerative medicine, yet most platforms rely on rigid substrates (~10⁶ kPa) that lack physiologically relevant stiffness (1-10² kPa). Integrating tunable substrate stiffness with reliable sheet detachment therefore remains a key challenge. Here, a polyacrylamide hydrogel functionalized with desthiobiotin-streptavidin (PAC-SAV) was developed to combine physiological stiffness with controllable cell sheet release. The hydrogel exhibited an elastic modulus of approximately 7 kPa. Desthiobiotin-mediated streptavidin immobilization promoted cell adhesion while enabling cells to sense the underlying substrate stiffness. Contrary to the initial hypothesis that competitive biotin displacement would trigger release, exposure to serum-containing medium induced rapid cell detachment at both single-cell and multicellular levels. To generate continuous cell sheets, the culture protocol was modified by using growth factor-supplemented serum-free medium during the late culture phase, enabling stable monolayer formation prior to detachment. Under these conditions, intact fibroblast sheets containing fibronectin-rich ECM and Ncadherin-junctions were released by serum exposure and successfully reattached to secondary substrates. These results establish desthiobiotin-streptavidin-modified polyacrylamide hydrogels as a platform for cell sheet engineering that integrates physiologically relevant mechanical cues with a mild and efficient detachment strategy.

papers.title: Reward Hacking in Materials Discovery: An Interpretable Inverse Design Framework and its Physical Limits
papers.abstract: The inverse design of tailored molecular materials is currently dominated by high-capacity generative models. The “black-box” nature of these models often obscures structure-property relationships and yields candidates with questionable physical transparency. In this work, we present an interpretable, feature-correlation-driven inverse engineering protocol that bridges robust statistical descriptor analysis with constrained genetic algorithms (GAs). By extracting structural primitives via hypergeometric Z-score and A-score analysis-subject to rigorous false discovery rate (FDR) corrections-we provide a physically grounded complement to latent-space sampling. The protocol successfully generated 2nd-generation libraries for high-refractive-index polyimides and high-density organic molecules. Critically, we employ first-principles DFT validation to diagnose the “extrapolation crisis” inherent in 2D surrogate models. The GA successfully optimized topological motifs, yielding a predicted RI max = 2.16 and ρ max = 1770 kg/m^3. DFT validation, however, revealed that 3D steric effects cap the realizable properties at RI = 1.58 and ρ = 1251 kg/m^3. This work establishes a transparent, motif-guided framework for constrained generative design. It also provides a rigorous methodology for identifying the physical boundaries where topological heuristics fail.

papers.title: The Factors Governing Metal Dependence of an Emergent Superfamily of Bimetallic Oxygenases
papers.abstract: Metalloenzyme superfamilies are typically defined by their protein scaffolds and active sites. Owing to the high tunability of protein structures, members of a single superfamily can catalyze diverse reactions with the same metallocofactor. Some superfamilies, such as Amidohydrolase-related dinuclear oxygenases (ARO), display further versatility by utilizing multiple metallocofactors. We have shown that certain AROs catalyze monooxygenation reactions with diiron, dimanganese and/or mixed manganese-iron cofactors, but the molecular factors governing the selection of a particular cofactor remain unknown and the extent of this superfamily in biology is unclear. Here, we report bioinformatic analyses that expand the ARO superfamily to approximately 17,000 unique UniProt sequences, far exceeding the number of previously characterized enzymes. Through the integration of structural, spectroscopic and thermodynamic analyses of representative proteins with a bioinformatic pipeline that identifies key secondary-and tertiary-sphere residues, we can predict in silico the metal preference for the majority of reported ARO sequences. These annotations were validated via the characterization of multiple new AROs, including ones implicated in key oxidative steps of natural product biosyntheses. This study establishes the key structure-function relationships governing metal preferences in AROs and highlights their vastly underappreciated role in myriad biological processes.

papers.title: Visible light-driven amide bond formation between carboxylic acids and amines
papers.abstract: Photosensitised direct coupling of carboxylic acids with amines, without prior functionalisation of the carboxylic acid, was achieved under ambient conditions via an in situ generated coupling mechanism using thiocyanate. Yields up to 63% were achieved in this one-pot redox-driven coupling process.

papers.title: Intramolecular Al/P Frustrated Lewis-pairs based on an Indoline backbone -Two Reaction Sites for Small molecule Activation and Hydrodefluorination
papers.abstract: The syntheses of compounds of the type Ph₂P(Ind)AlX₂ (with Ind = indoline and X = Cl, I, Me and C₆F₅) are reported. They can be accessed starting from the 7-diphenylphosphino indoline via deprotonation and subsequent salt metathesis or via in-situ deprotonation using precursors with basic ligands. While in case of X = Me X-ray crystallographic and solution studies confirmed that the connectivity and configuration is as envisaged, the latter was only true in case of X = C₆F₅ for the solid state. In solution ligand scrambling was observed, as was for X = I and Cl, which unlike the organometallic derivatives we found to have a dimeric structure. The dimers in solution are partly forming the scrambled compounds [Ph₂P(Ind)]₂AlX. However, upon contact with donors (D) all compounds were found to react as Ph₂P(Ind)AlX₂, forming Ph₂P(Ind)AlX₂(D). The reactivities of the representatives with X = Me and C₆F₅ were investigated, showing that diazo compound Ph2CN2 can be activated in the Al/P reaction space, while CO2 reacts with the aluminum-amide unit to give carbamates. The Al-N units can also be used to perform the dehydrofluorination of fluorocyclohexane. Subsequent investigations showed that achieving this reaction with alanes requires a fine balance and cooperation between a sufficiently Lewis-acidic aluminum center and a basic ligand.

papers.title: Decoupling Photon-Driven CO Desorption from Photothermal Heating on Pt Catalysts
papers.abstract: Illumination of metal nanoparticles can accelerate the rate of surface species desorption beyond what is achieved by purely thermal (dark) heating, but the extent to which this enhancement arises from a non-thermal (photon-enabled) desorption pathway versus concomitant photothermal heating remains debated. Using experimentally measured carbon monoxide temperature-programmed desorption from Pt/Al 2 O 3 under visible photon illumination, coverage-dependent thermal desorption kinetics and additional photon-enabled desorption channels were quantified. We compared two models to describe the influence of photon flux on CO desorption rate: (i) an additive photodesorption rate term superimposed on thermal desorption, and (ii) a heating-only model that maps photon absorption onto an elevated local temperature. While both models reproduce TPD traces as a function of photon flux, only the additive photodesorption model exhibited physically reasonable sensitivity to light intensity, resulting from purely photochemical events. In contrast, the heating-only model yielded ill-conditioned, superlinear sensitivities and unrealistic extrapolation behavior that would require extreme effective temperatures at higher flux. Moreover, the additive photochemical pathway provided a selective kinetic perturbation consistent with wavelength-dependent and bond-selective photokinetic signatures that cannot be explained by indiscriminate heating. At low temperatures, the additive photochemical desorption channel followed an Arrhenius dependence with an apparent activation barrier ~6–7× lower than in the dark. Our analyses support the rationalization of visible photon-assisted desorption via an additive, photodesorption event, providing a deployable module for microkinetic modeling of photo chemically accelerated catalytic cycles on non-semi conducting metal surfaces.

papers.title: Accelerating Quantum Chemistry Automation: Early Detection and Real-time Recovery of SCF Convergence Failure via Time Series Feature Extraction
papers.abstract: Self-consistent field (SCF) convergence failures bottleneck high-throughput quantum chemistry, particularly in open-shell systems. To address this, we introduce an autonomous pipeline treating the electronic structure descriptors from initial spin-unrestricted SCF iterations as a time series. Using statistical descriptors extracted from just the first ten iterations, a lightweight gradient-boosted classifier accurately predicts convergence failures. The model achieves 94.8% accuracy on 55,000 test molecules after training on only 10,000 examples. Coupling this early-warning predictor with a 𝛽-level-shift restart (𝛽-RST) heuristic, derived from Bayesian Optimization of the shift parameters, enables automated recovery. Across six diverse calculation settings, our pipeline successfully rescued 57.5% of inherently difficult-to-converge molecules while maintaining a 94.1% convergence rate for easy cases, resulting in a 460,000-iteration reduction across the 1200 calculations. Ultimately, this framework provides a highly transferable, data-efficient, and autonomous solution for largescale electronic structure calculations.

papers.title: A Chemist's Guide to Solid-State Qubits: Diamond Color Centers as Embedded Vacancy-Centered Molecules
papers.abstract: Diamond point defects or color centers are at the forefront of solid-state quantum technology applications, from computing to sensing. Their high degree of magnetic and optical manipulability without interference from the host underpins their functionality as qubits. The ability to understand and predict defects' (quantum) properties expeditiously via accurate quantum mechanical (QM) simulations can help accelerate their development. Modeling molecular qubits has made leaps and bounds mainly due to the advanced QM tools in the arsenal of quantum chemists for modeling (isolated) molecular systems and these concepts should be easily translatable for analogous systems in solid state. Here, enabled by chemistry principles and quantum chemical computational tools, we simulate a series of diamond defects: a carbon vacancy (V C ) and second row substitutions that are adjacent to a V C or D C V C , with D = B, N, and O, to evaluate their magnetic and optical properties. Because these defects have localized electronic structures, we model them as V C -centered molecules embedded in an optimized effective potential, which we derived quantum mechanically from defective periodic diamond crystals within the density functional embedding theory. We applied molecular orbital principles, an embedded cluster method, and the multi-configurational n-electron valence state second order perturbation theory to computationally characterize above-mentioned defects for a multitude of spin, charge, and excited states, comprehensively and expeditiously. We found our computational approach to be suitable for these types of defects, delivering high quality correlated wavefunction theory insights that compare well with experiments. Furthermore, with this framework, we confirm that the spin-triplets B C V C - and O C V C 0 to be promising alternatives to the well-known N C V C - . We calculated bright transitions that respectively correspond to UV (3.80 eV) and blue (2.65 eV) light absorption with emission lifetimes (τ) of 2.3 and 5.6 ns, which are higher-energy and shorter-lived (thus brighter) than what we calculated for N C V C - : green (2.26 eV), τ = 9.5 ns. Like N C V C - , both B C V C - and O C V C 0 have accessible spin singlets that may luminesce violet and infrared light, respectively, that may act as long-lived shelving states. B C V C - 's bright excitation at 3.8 eV is its second spin-triplet excited state (~ 8× brighter than the first at 3.05 eV) and has a similar character as the first excited states of N C V C - and O C V C 0 .

papers.title: Ruthenium-Mediated Phospha-Buchner Ring Expansion: Phosphorus Insertion into a Pendant Arene
papers.abstract: A ruthenium metalloligand platform enables formal phosphorus-atom insertion from NaOCP into a pendant electron-rich arene, affording a Ru-bound phosphepine. X-ray diffraction confirms a puckered, bond-localized seven-membered P-heterocycle formed without arene prefunctionalization. DFT supports dearomatizative [2+1] cycloaddition followed by facile electrocyclic ring opening.

papers.title: Tunable half-sandwich iridium coordination cages for PAH guest encapsulation
papers.abstract: Gaining control over the confinement dimensions and nature is key for a rational design of cages for specific guest molecules. In this work we synthesized three new iridium coordination cages enabling highly tunable cavities by systematically expanding the ligands. These cages have been fully characterized by the means of NMR spectroscopy, DOSY, HR-ESI-MS, and SCXRD. Density functional simulations indicate that the size expansion of the linkers leads to structurally analogous cages with a systematic variation of cavity size and shape. The large π-systems of the ligands enable guest binding of several polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH), including the well-known carcinogen Benzo[a]pyrene. 1 H NMR spectroscopic host-guest titrations and mass spectrometric experiments were carried out and revealed a 1:3 binding with pyrene. Density functional calculations further proved the 1:3 binding stoichiometry of the adducts, consistent with the symmetry of the cages. The corresponding binding constants decrease with expanding cage size, and therefore decreasing the packing coefficient, providing an example for Rebek’s rule of 55%.

papers.title: Artificial Coater: An In Situ Self-Driving Lab Reveals Design Rules and Mechanisms for Ambient Perovskite Film Fabrication
papers.abstract: Ambient solution-processing of metal halide perovskites remains highly sensitive to subtle variations in environment, formulation, and human technique, often leading to unpredictable outcomes and limited mechanistic understanding. Despite rapid advances in materials and device performance, researchers continue to rely heavily on manual and intuition-driven optimization, inconsistent fabrication protocols, and subjective film quality evaluation. These challenges persist across diverse coating methods, including but not limited to antisolvent dripping, which is especially sensitive to ambient manufacturing. In this work, we present the Artificial Coater, a self-driving laboratory platform that integrates closed-loop Bayesian optimization, in situ UV-Vis and photoluminescence spectroscopy, and machine vision to optimize thin film fabrication autonomously, reveal film formation mechanisms, and underlying root causes of unsuccessful fabrication. To enable scalable and unbiased interpretation of in situ spectral evolution, we apply non-negative matrix factorization across thousands of spectra, revealing latent spectral features associated with successful versus failed coatings. Using the benchmark composition FA₀.₈₃Cs₀.₁₇Pb(I₀.₈₃Br₀.₁₇)₃, we identify critical processing parameters governing crust formation, nucleation uniformity, and phase evolution. Our approach uncovers mechanistic insights into the formation of compact and uniformly converted perovskite thin films versus films exhibiting visibly rough morphologies across the coated area, links variations in morphology to solvent extractionmediated crystallization and reveals antisolvent drip design rules. This study establishes a dataintensive in situ framework with materials processing transparency, providing reusable and interpretable data for broader applications, including for potential transferability to other fabrication platforms and materials prepared using antisolvent drip.

papers.title: Assess first, route later: A multi-dimensional difficulty assessment framework for biopharmaceutical patent extraction
papers.abstract: The batch extraction of structure-activity relationship (SAR) data from global biopharmaceutical patents is a critical bottleneck in drug discovery. The extreme heterogeneity of these documents causes "one-size-fits-all" automated pipelines to either waste resources on simple patents or fail completely on complex ones. To solve this, we shift to an "assess first, then route" paradigm. This report introduces a multi-dimensional difficulty assessment framework that decomposes extraction complexity into 16 evaluation dimensions across four core categories: document physical quality, patent metadata, bioactivity data expression, and Markush structure complexity. Emphasizing engineering pragmatism at scale, our scoring engine uses a dual-track architecture-combining fast deterministic rules with Large Language Models (LLMs) for deep semantic evaluation. By dynamically grading patents from L1 to L4, the framework enables downstream pipelines to intelligently route tasks: maximizing Straight-Through Processing (STP) for L1/L2 patents while reserving Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) resources for L3/L4 cases. Validation on over 94,000 global patents across seven patent offices demonstrates that over 53% of these heterogeneous documents can be securely routed to STP pipelines. This effectively eliminates redundant manual review overhead for straightforward cases, while preemptively preventing pipeline failures on deeply complex structural formulations.

papers.title: Predictive Design of Fulvalene-Bridged Bimetallic Molecular Solar-Thermal Fuels
papers.abstract: Molecular solar-thermal (MOST) energy storage requires the simultaneous optimization of photocharging efficiency, energy density, and thermal persistence. The diruthenium fulvalene complex (Fv)Ru 2 (CO) 4 remains the only organometallic MOST fuel that supports fully closed photothermal cycle, enabled by triplet-mediated photocharging and singlet-surface thermal discharge. Isoelectronic metal substitution typically disrupts cyclability, either by quenching the essential triplet photocharging pathway or by kinetically trapping the high-energy isomer. Here, we introduce a dual-gate framework that elevates metal-pair selection from an empirical choice to a predictive design handle. The framework defines two complementary filters: a groundstate Storage-Stability Gate, in which stored free-energy and the thermal back-reaction barrier are intrinsically coupled, and an excited-state Photo Gate, requiring Franck-Condon-proximal access to the isomerizing triplet. Applying both gates to a 21member library identifies (Fv)OsW(CO) 5 as a previously unrecognized MOST fuel that combines photocharging, high energy storage, and day-to-week thermal persistence, while simultaneously providing a quantitative rationalization of the (Fv)Ru 2 (CO) 4 success. Our framework establishes transferable, mechanism-guided principles for rational MOST design beyond serendipity.

papers.title: Heavy-Atom Tunneling at Room Temperature
papers.abstract: Quantum-mechanical tunneling enables molecules to react through high-energy barriers. In chemistry, the effects of tunneling are normally assumed to be negligible except at very low temperatures, especially when heavy atoms are involved. This assumption is typically justified using one-dimensional theories of tunneling based on strong simplifying approximations. In this work, we employ a more advanced and recently developed computational approach (called nonadiabatic instanton theory) to capture the true multidimensional tunneling pathway. Surprisingly, we find that the tunneling of heavy carbon atoms significantly speeds up the spin-forbidden ring closing of various strained organic radicals to form housanes and caged diones (which are direct precursors for cubanes) even at room temperature. This highlights the importance of tunneling in spin-forbidden reactions and opens up possibilities for tunneling control in the synthesis of strained molecules, not just at cryogenic temperatures, but under ordinary laboratory conditions.

papers.title: Mechanistic Understanding of an Intermediate Time Scale (around 1 ps) in Orientational Relaxation Dynamics of Bulk Water
papers.abstract: The longer timescale of water reorientation is intimately coupled to hydrogen-bond (H-bond) exchange, as elucidated by the jump reorientation mechanism proposed by Laage and Hynes. In this study, we revisit this mechanism to probe the short to intermediate timescales of the reorientation process. Using atomistic molecular dynamics simulations and fitting of the OH reorientation time correlation function, we identify an intermediate timescale of ∼1.15 ps that contributes approximately 20% to the total decay. To elucidate its molecular origin, we analyze the time correlation function of the donor O*–H* vector over the interval preceding an H-bond exchange event, removing contributions from the transition-state region, which reveals the same ∼1.15 ps component accompanied by a slower ∼6 ps component attributable to frame tumbling motion. Further analysis of the trajectory reveals the presence of acceptor-free dangling states of the donor between two successful exchange events. A joint probability distribution of donor–acceptor distance and O···O*–H* angle reveals that short-lived dangling states (≤20 fs) arise primarily from angular fluctuations of the donor OH bond, whereas longerlived dangling states (≥50 fs) show a distinct population centered around ~3.5 Å and ~30°, characteristic of an average transition-state-like geometry. The average waiting time of such long-lived dangling events is ~1.10 ps. Taken together, our results suggest that the origin of the intermediate timescale of ~1.15 ps in bulk water reorientation is due to unsuccessful switching attempts of the donor. We believe that similar analysis will be useful for breaking down time scales observed in various confined systems.

papers.title: A Sensitive DNA Bowtie Sensor for Calibration-Free Sex Hormone Detection Using Analyte-DNA Conjugates and Multiple Redox Labels
papers.abstract: Using a modular and reconfigurable DNA-based bowtie sensor structure, several advancements in electrochemical (EC) biosensing are reported. Raw current and sensitivity were enhanced up to 16-fold using a novel redox reporter design, where a DNA strand was decorated with five methylene blue molecules (MB 5 ) instead of the typical single label (MB), and flexible spacers further improved signal. Leveraging the bowtie sensor's modularity, custom synthesized analyte-DNA conjugates (testosterone-DNA, estradiol-DNA, and progesterone-DNA) and a control strand (digoxigenin-DNA) were incorporated into the complete DNA structure on electrode surfaces by enzymatic ligation. Upon binding antibod ies, each of these sensors showed enhanced current with the MB 5 label, and responses consistently followed a Langmuir curve. A previously inaccessible signal-on response was observed at low square wave voltammetry frequencies using MB 5 , allowing differential signal corrections, and the limit of detection (LOD) for direct antibody sensing was as low as 0.08 nM (80 pM). A mathematical model was devised based on uncoupled equilibria among the analytes, antibodies, and the electrode surface. After training the model on binding curves, calibration-free measurements of small molecule hormones were possible, with observed LODs for testosterone, estradiol, and progesterone at 0.2, 0.8, and 1 nM, respectively, extending within human clinical ranges. For example, the testosterone sensor's range was 200 pM to 70 nM, covering the clinical range in both females (0.52 to 2.43 nM) and males (9.0 to 34.7 nM), and the sensor functions with 90% recovery in 50% human serum. This work expands the usage of the EC bowtie sensor, employing custom synthetic organic methods to introduce new analyte-DNA conjugates and further validate the sensor's generalizability, alongside developing a unique model of the binding mechanism. Beyond this, the newly introduced MB 5 label should be functional with a range of other DNA-based EC sensors or aptamer-based sensors.

papers.title: Conformational landscapes resolved by ion mobility mass spectrometry reveal differential mechanisms of polyubiquitin-controlled phase separation
papers.abstract: Polyubiquitin chains regulate phase separation of the ubiquitin-binding shuttle protein ubiquilin-2 (UBQLN2) in a manner that depends on the position of the isopeptide linkage and the length of the polyubiquitin chain. However, conformational heterogeneity of the non-covalent complexes formed between these proteins has rendered the molecular mechanisms underlying this regulation elusive. Here, we have used ion mobility mass spectrometry (IM-MS) to disentangle conformational features of the non-covalent complexes formed by UBQLN2 with different polyubiquitin chains. We demonstrate that the length of the polyubiquitin chain binding to UBQLN2 has a large effect on the conformational distribution of the complex, with increasing chain lengths (up to four ubiquitin subunits) allowing access to more extended conformations of the complex, and shorter chains promoting compaction. This provides the first evidence for differential mechanisms of phase separation regulation by ubiquitin chains of different lengths. We also compare polyubiquitin chains linked by lysine residue (K)48 and by K63, both alone and in complex with UBQLN2. By understanding how K48- and K63-linked tetraubiquitin chains behave in the gas phase, which differs to solution, we propose distinct molecular mechanisms for their regulation of UBQLN2 phase separation. This work, enabled by the unique ability of IM-MS to resolve conformational features of highly heterogeneous biomolecular systems, represents a conceptual breakthrough in understanding polyubiquitin-controlled phase separation mechanisms.

papers.title: Bridging Bioassay-Guided Isolation and Metabolomics: Toward Hybrid Strategies in Natural Product Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Natural product (NP) remains an important source of drug discovery, providing approximately 32% of newly introduced small molecule drugs between 1981 to 2019. Their unique chemical complexity presents an abundance of active novel chemical entities, but it also raises challenges in its identification and isolation. Two primary methods dominate these fields: the traditional bioassay-guided isolation (BGI) and the more recent metabolomics-based discovery approaches. Despite extensive use of both methods, a systematic framework that integrates their complementary strengths remain insufficiently developed. To address this gap, this review proposes an integrative framework that links metabolomics-based compound prioritization with subsequent BGI validation. This review critically evaluates findings from peer-reviewed studies published between 1958 to 2024 to compare the principles, technical capabilities, strengths limitations, and bridges their integrative applications in NP drug discovery. Our analysis shows that metabolomics excels in early-stage exploration by providing broad chemical coverage, high sensitivity, and efficient prioritization of active novel compounds, while BGI remains essential for definitive isolation, mechanistic evaluation, and biological activity confirmation. By framing metabolomics as a decision-support stage rather than a replacement for BGI workflows, this review emphasizes integrative discovery that improves efficiency, reduce rediscovery, and preserve chemical rigor. Such hybrid strategies could reduce the research timeline for the discovery of NP-based new chemical entity with improved precision and reproducibility.

papers.title: A General Strategy to Access Fluorogenic Heptamethine Cyanines through Polymethine Reactivity
papers.abstract: Fluorogenic heptamethine cyanines are highly desirable for biomedical imaging due to high signal-to-background ratio from region of interest, however, there are limited strategies to develop them. Here we report a general strategy to synthesize fluorogenic heptamethine cyanines using intrinsic reactivity of the polymethine scaffold. In our strategy, a meso-carboxylate group undergoes intramolecular nucleophilic attack at the γ-position of the polymethine chain to form a five-membered cyclized structure that disrupts π-conjugation and suppresses nearinfrared fluorescence; referred to as cyclizing-heptamethine cyanines (c-Cy7). This c-Cy7s have solvent dependent equilibrium between the open, conjugated form (polar solvent) and the closed, cyclized form (nonpolar solvent). A library of symmetrical and unsymmetrical c-Cy7s containing electron-withdrawing groups were synthesized to demonstrate that electronic substitution modulates the cyclization equilibrium. Collectively, this work demonstrates that polymethine reactivity can be harnessed for developing fluorogenic heptamethine cyanines.

papers.title: Low Temperature, Low Pressure Quasi-solidstate Transformation of Fused Silica to α-Quartz
papers.abstract: Synthesis of α-quartz typically involves transformation of amorphous silica, silicates or silanebased precursors under extreme conditions, such as high temperature of ~1000-1200 °C or via hydrothermal at a combination of high temperature (~300-400 °C) and high pressure (~2-3kbar). Chemistry behind direct transformation of fused silica bulk to α-quartz in vapor or quasi-solid environment yet to be well-explored. Here, we have shown an innovative hydrothermal method for transforming bulk amorphous fused silica into α-quartz phase at relatively lower temperatures of 240 °C under autogenic pressure. By taking advantage of alkali metal ion-transport and water vapor under hydrothermal conditions, a relatively faster amorphous to crystalline phase transformation kinetics has been achieved. While exploring the mechanism, an in-depth experimental and computational investigation showed that ion migration from sodalime to fused silica facilitated the crystallization, overcoming the activation barrier related to structural stability of the amorphous silica network. Our findings provide new and unexpected insights into energyefficient pathways for quartz formation from the amorphous state in silica. Notably, quartz crystallization in the Earth's crust remains a complex and not fully understood geological process, our approach also provides a plausible mechanistic analog for such natural phenomena.

papers.title: High-temperature carbonized PVC/RM (red mud) composite material for self-supplying NaCl electrolyte for supercapacitors
papers.abstract: Red mud (RM) is an industrial waste with high alkalinity and high corrosiveness. Appropriately removing the alkalinity from RM is crucial for the reuse and application of RM. This study attempts to composite RM with polyvinyl chloride (PVC) for self-supplying NaCl electrolyte for supercapacitors. The carbon structure and chemical state of Fe in RM/PVC composites after carbonization at different temperatures were studied. The results show that, compared with RM, the content of Fe 2+ in RM/PVC composites at 800 ℃ increased. The carbon in RM/PVC composites at 800 ℃ includes disordered and graphite carbon. Surprisingly, the specific capacitance of RM/PVC(1:1.67)-800 (1.59 F/g) under GCD test (5 mA/g) is two to three orders of magnitude higher than that of RM (1.7 mF/g) and PVC-800 (2.5 mF/g). It is worth noting that the electrolyte solution of this supercapacitor is 2 NaCl derived from the reaction between the alkalinity in RM and HCl generated from PVC during the high-temperature carbonization process, which improves the safety and environmental friendliness of RM utilization. Therefore, in this work, the industrial waste RM was ingeniously combined with PVC to turn waste into treasure, thus paving the way for the development of using RM.

papers.title: N-Heterocyclic Imines and Olefins as Stabilising Donors for Geminal Carbodications
papers.abstract: Geminal carbodications ( g CD) violate the electronic octet rule. We present a systematic quantum chemical analysis of diverse doubly cationic (hetero)cumulenes in a push towards identifying ideal frameworks for localizing and stabilizing the charges. Readily available N-heterocyclic imine (NHI) donors have recently successfully been used for the isolation of bis(iminyl) g CDs ((NHI) 2 C 2+ ). We herein analyze and compare their behavior to N-heterocyclic olefin (NHO) donors as promising stabilizing ligands to form bis(vinyl) carbodications ((NHO) 2 C 2+ ). Their geometry structures and bonding characteristics are analyzed by density functional theory (DFT) calculations at the r 2 scan-3c level, including geometry metrics, ion affinities, bond order analyses, topology approaches (QTAIM, ELF), together with IBO and NBO analysis. While both families exhibit pronounced Lewis superacidic character, they differ markedly in reactivity, charge distribution and delocalization. Our findings suggest that N -heterocyclic olefins are robust ligands to stabilize dicoordinate C 2+ centers through crucially allowing unpolar σ-bonds that avoid additional charge accumulation. The presented results support the design of further isolable g CDs which will help develop this class of compounds towards applicability.

papers.title: Latest Approaches in Enantiodivergent Organocatalysis
papers.abstract: This Minireview focuses on recent and most impactful contributions in enantiodivergent organocatalysed reactions. Four different approaches based on achiral stimuli were examined as inversion strategies: solvent-controlled inversion, achiral reagent or additive inducted inversion, and minimal catalyst modification, discussing in detail for each example the mechanistic insights behind the chiral inversion. Other strategies to achieve enantiodivergence are also briefly discussed.

papers.title: Molecular Reporters for Mammalian Sugars via Hydrogen Bonding Auxiliaries
papers.abstract: Glycans are essential transmitters of biological information. However, their complex and dynamic structures remain difficult to characterize, posing a major barrier to fully understanding their biological functions. Here, we demonstrate that hydrogen bonding auxiliaries positioned adjacent to the boron site of turn-on fluorogenic phenylboronic acid reporters serve as key modulators of sensitivity to mammalian sugars, providing a new design principle analogous to the hydrogen bonding networks found in lectin binding pockets. We show that these auxiliaries tune sensitivity both globally and for individual mammalian sugars and reveal a striking differential turn-on response between the anomeric forms of monosaccharides. The versatility of these selective and reversible molecular reporters is demonstrated through in-gel glycoprotein imaging, flow cytometry, and cell-surface visualization, establishing them as a generalizable chemical platform for interrogating mammalian glycans.

papers.title: UMA-ASE: A FAIR-Aware Environment for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential Workflows with UMA and ASE
papers.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are rapidly changing the operating regime of computational chemistry by narrowing the traditional gap between first-principles accuracy and large-scale atomistic simulation. UMA-ASE was developed to make this transition operational through a reproducible, FAIR-aware environment that couples the Universal Model for Atoms (UMA) with the Atomic Simulation Environment (ASE) and exposes the resulting workflows through both a command-line interface and a browser-based application. The platform combines structure intake and generation from SMILES, job submission, GeoOpt and TS search, molecular dynamics, vibrational analysis, visualization, post-processing, queue management, and integration with ioChem-BD. In this manuscript we position UMA-ASE within the current MLIP landscape and define the design goals of the new software. We emphasize reproducibility artifacts such as structured logs, machine-readable .use recipes, result bundles, and repository-oriented interoperability. We conclude that FAIR-aware scientific tools and user-friendly interfaces are becoming essential complements to modern ML methods, and that LLM-assisted software development is likely to accelerate this trend further.

papers.title: Novel hydroxyl-functionalized 1,2,4-triazole-based oligomers: synthetic approach, photoluminescence and coordination behaviour as uranyl chelators
papers.abstract: The management and recycling of accumulated depleted uranium may benefit from the development of novel organic heterocyclic systems that can be used as ligands for uranyl complexes in advanced materials. Although functionalised 1,2,4-triazoles have shown promise as ligand systems for a variety of transition metals, little is known about their coordination behaviour towards uranyl and the characteristics of the resultant complexes. In the present study, the synthetic strategy to construct functionalized oligo(1,2,4-triazoles) have been developed to prepare mono- ( H 2 L 1 ), bis- ( H 2 L 2 ) and tris-1,2,4-triazole-based oligomers ( H 2 L 3 ) bearing hydroxy-methyl and -phenyl substituents. Uranyl complexes [UO 2 (L 1 )(CH 3 OH)] 2 ·2CH 3 OH ( 1 ), [UO 2 (L 2 )] 2 ·4DMF ( 2 ) and [UO 2 (HL 3 )(CH 3 COO)]·CH 3 OH·H 2 O ( 3 ) were easily synthesized by combining UO 2 (CH 3 COO) 2 ∙2H 2 O with the ligand under suitable conditions. Two identical halves of the dinuclear molecules of 1 and 2 are bridged by two deprotonated alkoxy groups from the tri- and tetradentate ligands, respectively. In complex 3 , the pending hydroxymethyl group of ( HL 3 ) - stays protonated impeding dimerization of the molecule. Extensive N/O–H···O and C–H···N/O hydrogen bonding consolidates supramolecular 3D network structures of the uranyl complexes in the solid state. The behavior of the ligands and complexes in DMSO solution was investigated using 1 H NMR and 1 H DOSY NMR spectroscopy, complemented by DFT calculations. Under excitation with UV light (l ex = 310–311 nm), the ligands in solution give rise to strong broad bands centred at near 444 nm with Stokes shifts of ~133 nm. Photoluminescence quenching observed for 1 – 3 (1 x 10 -5 М, DMSO) as compared to the free ligands was rationalized with use of DFT calculations performed with ORCA 6.0.1 program package.

papers.title: High-Throughput Discovery of Conformation-Switching Mechanophores with Novel Response and Enhanced Reactivity
papers.abstract: Mechanophores offer unique opportunities in chemistry and material science, yet current mechanophores are often limited by low reactivity, irreversible transformation, or poor thermal stability. Here, we report the computational discovery of a new class of Cu 2+ complex mechanophores comprising two tridentate scorpionate ligands that reversibly switch from octahedral to square-planar coordination under mechanical load. We curate over 750 synthetically accessible candidates using ligands from the Cambridge Structural Database. Leveraging density functional theory (DFT) and external force explicitly included (EFEI) modeling, we find 393 coordination-switching complexes that undergo square-planar conversion through concerted dissociation of two load-aligned coordination bonds at low applied force. We analyze the data to identify trends and characterize the most reactive mechanophores using interpretable machine learning (ML) models. This analysis reveals the most reactive mechanophores to be those that have chemical compositions leading to longer load-aligned and shorter load-orthogonal bonds as well as lower ligand steric bulk. Finally, we find robust candidates that exhibit both mechanical lability and thermal stability, with complexes comprising tris(2-pyridyl) ligands emerging as promising lead candidates. Together, this work establishes coordination switching as a useful design strategy for mechanophores and demonstrates how high-throughput ab initio screening and ML can enable data-driven discovery of force-responsive polymer building blocks.

papers.title: ChemNetworks: New Capabilities for High-Throughput, Real-Time Chemical Graph Construction and Analysis
papers.abstract: A new release of ChemNetworks (Journal of Computational Chemistry, 2013, 35, 495-505), is described. Updates have made the software performant in supercomputing environments, capable of real-time graph construction and analysis with running simulations, and incorporate graph theory libraries for diverse and customizable analysis workflows. Here, we describe newly implemented algorithms (and examples) in ChemNetworks that include a recursive Z-matrix algorithm for structure identification and graph construction, the incorporation of the DataSpaces data staging framework as one of its optional I/O engines, and user-contributed graph theory analyses that leverage the igraph library. The new release of ChemNetworks better enables ongoing development through community contributions.

papers.title: Effective Removal of Microplastics and Nanoplastics with Cationic Cellulose Fibers in Wastewater Treatment
papers.abstract: The ubiquitous contamination of water supplies by microplastics and nanoplastics is a growing global concern, posing significant risks to aquatic ecosystems and human health. Wastewater treatment plants serve as critical barriers to reducing the concentration of plastic contaminants before their release into natural environments. In this study, we introduce cationically functionalized cellulose fibers as bridging agents for enhancing the removal of microplastics and nanoplastics in coagulation–flocculation processes. Cellulose fibers are modified with quaternary ammonium groups via periodate-induced oxidation, and extensive characterization confirms their successful cationization. The addition of cationic fibers achieves near-complete removal (>99%) of 1 µm and 200 nm model microplastics and nanoplastics and 93% removal of 20 nm model nanoplastics from synthetic wastewater, significantly outperforming both unmodified fibers and conventional treatment (i.e., without fiber addition). Fluorescence microscopy of the settled flocs reveals a surface-enhanced removal mechanism of cationic fibers, driven by electrostatic interactions during floc formation. Fiber reusability tests conducted with fibers extracted from sludge show that high performance of cationic fibers is maintained, achieving 94% and 81% removal of 1 µm and 20 nm particles, respectively, after five consecutive reuse cycles. Furthermore, cationic fiber effectiveness for plastic removal is validated in microplastic- and nanoplastic-spiked municipal wastewater influent, demonstrating their practical applicability. This comprehensive assessment of functionalized cellulose fibers underscores their potential as a highly effective and sustainable approach for mitigating widespread plastic pollution with primary wastewater treatment.

papers.title: Demonstration of Real-Time Autonomous Metal Additive Manufacturing
papers.abstract: Laser-directed energy deposition offers unique opportunities for fabricating and repairing high value metallic components. However, major barriers do exist for widespread adoption due to costly, modeldependent, trial-and-error experimentation-based qualification protocols. In this study, we demonstrated an autonomous framework for process optimization that integrates in-situ X-ray imaging with Gaussian Process-based active learning. Thin-wall structures of the Ni-base superalloy Mar-M247 were fabricated under systematically varied laser power and scan speed, and build quality was quantified using a new metric combining geometrical and structural conformity. Crack identification was achieved through a machine-learning pipeline by employing modern data science, AI and in-situ sensing. The autonomous system rapidly converged to optimal process parameters within 14 iterations, significantly fewer than conventional design-of-experiments approaches. Ex-situ x-ray diffraction (XRD) and scanning electron microscope (SEM) characterizations confirmed that cracking tendency and microstructural evolution are strongly correlated with thermal gradients and melt pool geometry. Thermomechanical simulations further validated the observed "Goldilocks" regime of laser power and scan speed required to minimize cracking while maintaining geometrical conformity. Importantly, we show that geometrical and structural conformity are coupled phenomena, governed by the same underlying thermal gradients and stress evolution. While current sensor resolution limits defect detection at the sub-micron scale, the framework demonstrates a scalable pathway for rapid qualification.

papers.title: Correlative Multimodal Framework Reveals Supramolecular Chirality Loss Precedes Fibrillar Rarefaction in Dermal Collagen
papers.abstract: Early-stage remodeling of collagen-rich tissues is commonly inferred from fibrillar thinning and loss of connectivity, yet the structural change that initiates this process has remained unclear. Here, we show that early collagen remodeling is first expressed as a loss of supramolecular chirality coherence, rather than a reduction in collagen density or network integrity. By correlating molecular-scale chiral order with mesoscale fibrillar organization across three independent adult skin sample donors (Samples 1-3 referred to as S1-S3), we identify an abrupt collapse of chirality coherence despite preserved collagen mass and coverage. Only at some stages do fibrillar fragmentation and directional reorganization become apparent, accompanied by a reduction in nonlinear optical response. These findings establish supramolecular chirality coherence as an early-failing order parameter in collagen assemblies and reveal a previously unrecognized precursor to dermal remodeling. More broadly, this work provides a framework for detecting incipient failure in hierarchical chiral biomaterials before macroscopic degradation becomes evident.

papers.title: Denitrogenative glycosylations of glycosyl sulfonohydrazides
papers.abstract: Radical glycosylation has emerged as a powerful strategy in carbohydrate synthesis, offering alternative disconnections and direct functionalization of protected and native sugar. Despite notable progress, the development of novel and efficient glycosyl radical precursors that are readily accessible, synthetically versatile, and compatible with stereoselective coupling platforms remains an ongoing challenge. Here we report a nickelcatalysed stereoselective denitrogenative glycosylation of redox-neutral glycosyl sulfonohydrazides via anomeric C-N bond homolysis. Bench-stable (un)protected glycosyl sulfonohydrazides are concisely and catalytically synthesized via an open-closed ring equilibrium without stoichiometric reagents, and intrinsically generate glycosyl radicals without external redox additives, offering remarkable practical utility. This operationally simple, nickelcatalysed denitrogenative glycosylation platform-proceeding without photocatalysis-enables highly stereoselective formation of diverse C(sp³)-C(sp³), C(sp³)-C(sp²), C(sp³)-C(sp), C(sp³)-S, C(sp³)-Se, and C(sp³)-Te bonds, with broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. Importantly, this protecting-groupfree denitrogenative glycosylation provides straightforward access to a wide range of metabolically robust glycosyl derivatives. Mechanistic investigations proposed a nickel-catalysed radical pathway involving redox-neutral homolysis of Ni(II)-isodiazene complexes and thermally induced N₂ extrusion. Collectively, this work demonstrates that glycosyl sulfonohydrazides function as N-based glycosyl radical precursors, notably establishing a new class of unprotected glycosyl radicals while broadening the "cap-and-glycosylate" platform for glycomimetic synthesis and the glycodiversification of bioactive molecules.

papers.title: STALAgent: A Multi-Agent System Based on Large Language Model (LLM) for Steel and Alloy Design
papers.abstract: The design of steel and alloy materials is of critical importance across a wide range of industrial applications; however, effective intelligent agent-based assistants for this domain remain limited. To address this gap, we introduce STALAgent, a large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent system specifically tailored for intelligent and automated design of steel and alloy materials.
