Using this robust method, we demonstrate the transesterification of geraniol and citronellol, the most prevalent terpenes in rose oil, directly within a rose oil mixture to yield their corresponding methacrylate derivatives. This work represents a step forward towards the green functionalisation of terpenes and the valorisation of flower waste biomass.

papers.title: Geometric Encoding of Cyclic Mechanical Fatigue in Model Glasses: Graph Neural Networks as Structural Probes for Battery-Relevant Degradation
papers.abstract: Solid-state battery glass electrolytes degrade under repeated charge and discharge cycling, yet the atomic-scale structural changes underlying this fatigue remain poorly characterised. Here we investigate whether cyclic mechanical fatigue—simulated as oscillatory volumetric strain applied to a Lennard-Jones model glass—encodes a learnable geometric signature detectable by graph neural networks (GNNs). Using a GATv2 architecture and a systematic four-way ablation study, we find that classification between pristine (cycle 0) and heavily fatigued (cycles 300–400) glasses reaches 91.67 ± 4.22% accuracy using 8-dimensional bond-length statistics as node features, rising to 98.33 ± 1.49% (AUC = 0.9975 ± 0.0022) when per-sample instance normalisation is applied. The improvement under normalisation—which explicitly removes all global magnitude information—establishes that the discriminative signal resides in the relational geometry of local bond networks, not in trivial density or volume changes. Ablating distribution-shape features (skewness, quartiles) reduces accuracy by 5.3 percentage points and collapses cycle-number regression to near-random performance (R² = 0.006), confirming that asymmetric bond-length damage is the dominant structural fingerprint of fatigue. Continuous degradation tracking via regression achieves R² = 0.311 ± 0.039 under instance normalisation, with all five cross-validation folds converging to R² ≈ 0.28–0.32 given extended training. Structural analysis reveals that fatigue accumulates as monotonically increasing bond-length disorder that saturates around cycle 300, consistent with a metastable fatigued equilibrium. Per-atom energy validation reveals a striking inversion: the dominant classification feature (r_max, ΔAUCdrop = 0.601) correlates negligibly with local potential energy (Spearman ρ = −0.093), while the strongest energy proxy (r_min, ρ = −0.812) ranks seventh in fatigue discrimination—establishing that the GATv2 probe detects irreversible structural history encoded in stretched-bond geometry rather than the instantaneous energy state. A Kovacs memory effect experiment further validates the 8D feature vector as a genuine structural probe: bond-length standard deviation and skewness track the NVT Kovacs relaxation signal with the same timescale as the macroscopic energy recovery, while mean non-affine displacement continues to grow linearly after bulk equilibration, confirming that the GNN features occupy the physically privileged space between thermodynamic observables and full microscopic configuration. These findings extend the geometric-encoding framework established for thermal history to mechanical cycling history, and provide a methodological foundation for applying GNN-based structural probes to experimentally characterised solid electrolyte fatigue.

papers.title: Armstrongs Probabilistic Electron Phase-Space Overlap Model (APEPM)
papers.abstract: Context Assessing whether a bonding interaction is geometrically possible , that is, whether the probabilistic electron clouds of two atoms spatially overlap at a given internuclear separation, is a fundamental yet often implicit aspect of molecular modeling. Conventional electronic structure methods address this question indirectly through wavefunction optimization and energetic analysis, which can obscure the underlying geometric constraints and limit scalability. Here, Armstrong’s Probabilistic Electron Phase-Space Overlap Model (APEPM) is introduced as a geometry-driven, wavefunction-free framework for evaluating geometric bond feasibility by explicitly determining whether nonzero electron cloud overlap exists for any specified atomic separation. The model provides closed-form expressions for the size and extent of the shared electron phase-space and tracks how this overlap evolves continuously under bond compression or extension. By mapping the overlap region onto radially partitioned orbital shells, APEPM identifies which atomic orbital regions are geometrically involved in the mandatory shared phase-space, yielding an interpretable description of spatial orbital involvement that is independent of energetic weighting or bond strength assignment. Methods APEPM represents bonded atoms as interacting probabilistic electron volumes characterized by effective electron cloud radii derived from atomic electron cloud extents. Geometric overlap is determined analytically using closed-form expressions for the intersection of two spheres as a function of internuclear distance, yielding overlap radius, cross-sectional area, and overlap volume, with zero overlap defining the geometric infeasibility limit. Orbital participation is evaluated by projecting the overlap region along the bond axis and identifying intersections with predefined radial orbital shells. All calculations are analytic and geometry-based and are implemented in Python using custom software developed for this work.

papers.title: Automated Structural Refinement of Docked Complexes in Cytochrome P450 Using Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: Molecular docking is a standard tool for predicting ligand binding, yet refining these poses via molecular dynamics (MD) remains challenging to automate for metalloproteins like Cytochrome P450 (CYP450). Here, we introduce DOCKTOPUS (Dock to P450) and CYCLOPS (CYtochrome Complex Ligand Optimization with Protein Simulation) Python packages designed to automate the docking and molecular dynamics setup for CYP450-ligand complexes. These tools integrate seamlessly with representative predictive engines AutoDock Vina, GNINA, GalaxyDock2-HEME, and RoseTTAFold All-Atom (RFAA) by automatically handling the complex parameterisation of the covalently bound heme-thiolate cofactor and ligand topologies, while also providing capabilities to filter out unphysical ligand geometries generated by RFAA. We validated the pipeline through a medium-sized case study to enable a rigorous statistical analysis. In crossdocking scenarios RFAA achieved a mean geometric drift relative to experiments approximately three times lower than that of AutoDock Vina. Our structural and pharmacophoric analyses revealed that subsequent MD simulations provide no statistically significant geometric refinement towards the experimental crystal structure. This behaviour was remarkably consistent: we observed no significant differences by specific interaction type or ligand flexibility. These findings suggest that short MD refinement with contemporary classical force fields for organometallic systems might have limited effects beyond pose validity. Furthermore the DOCKTOPUS and CYCLOPS packages offer a robust platform for statistical testing of docking and molecular dynamics effects.

papers.title: StereoMolGraph: Stereochemistry-Aware Molecular and Reaction Graphs
papers.abstract: Conventional molecular graphs often are unable to reliably encode stereochemistry, especially for symmetric molecules, non-tetrahedral centers, and transition states. To overcome this, we present StereoMolGraph, an open source Python library implementing a stereochemistry-aware graph representation for molecules and condensed graphs of reactions. Our method uses permutation invariant local stereodescriptors, grounded in group theory, to provide an extensible representation of chirality. Based on this we introduce methods allowing for robust comparison of stereoisomers, including the identification of enantiomerism and diastereomerism, and supports fleeting stereochemistry in transition states. We demonstrate the library's utility for complex organic molecules and metal complexes and analysis of distinct chiral reaction pathways. With RDKit interoperability and visualization features, StereoMolGraph offers a practical and transparent tool for advanced stereochemically aware chemoinformatics workflows.

papers.title: Water-Mediated Reconfigurable Topology and Mechanics in PorousPeptide Materials
papers.abstract: Biological systems, including proteins, employ water-mediated supramolecular interactions to adopt specific conformations for their functions. However, current solid-state supramolecular materials are typically stiff and fail to capture the dynamic behaviors observed in proteins. Here, we present dynamic crystal-hydrates of aliphatic dipeptides with sequence-isomers of leucine (L) and isoleucine (I). These crystals exhibit shallow conformational energy landscapes, with various reconfigurable crystal nano-architectures accessible through small changes in relative humidity and temperature. Specifically, for LI crystals, as water content changes, the solid-state supramolecular architecture rapidly and reversibly transitions between perpendicular and parallel honeycomb nano-architectures, as well as layered van der Waals structures, leading to significant and distinct variations in mechanical and photophysical properties. Our findings demonstrate the potential of leveraging aliphatic hydrophobic domains inspired by protein architectures to create dynamic solid-state materials with context-adaptive properties.

papers.title: Base-Catalyzed Hydroarsination at Ambient Temperature: Synthesis in Green Solvent
papers.abstract: A practical, transition-metal-free hydroarsination protocol using commercially available, air-stable catalytic NaOH in DMSO is described. Hydroarsination has been sorely underdeveloped , and these conditions enable regioselective anti-Markovnikov addition of diphenylarsine to vinylarenes, Michael acceptors, and alkynes at ambient temperature, affording previously unknown tertiary arsines in good to quantitative yields. Deuterium labeling studies support a nucleophilic mechanism initiated by arsine deprotonation. Because NaOH is not fully soluble in DMSO under conditions screened, the insoluble component provides water management during the reaction as well as additional base to (re)activate arsine, which explains the high activity relative to reported catalysts. This simple methodology expands access to previously inaccessible substrates and therefore structurally diverse tertiary arsines with a substantial improvement in activity and scope over prior catalysts while reducing cost, simplifying purification, and improving green aspects of the reaction.

papers.title: Repression of Virulence in S. aureus by 2-Aminothiol-mediated Quorum Quenching
papers.abstract: In this work, we present a novel strategy for the inhibition of quorum sensing in Staphylococcus bacteria. Previous work has focused on the development of peptides that can compete with native autoinducing peptides (AIPs), to antagonize the receptor histidine kinase responsible for activation of quorum sensing and thereby repress the expression of virulence genes. Here we report simple small molecules that can eliminate the native AIPs extracellularly, before they activate their receptor, and validate that this alternative strategy can also be applied to turn off quorum sensing in different S. aureus reporter strain assays. Further, we show that two selected compounds can reduce skin infection caused by MRSA in a murine model. This work provides impetus for the development of simple small molecules for the topical treatment of staphylococcal skin infections. We anticipate that further studies, including delivery strategies, will help illuminate this potential.

papers.title: Effect of Temperature and Aluminum Content on Diffusive Water Transport in Single-Walled Zeolitic Nanotubes
papers.abstract: Simulations of novel zeolitic nanotubes (ZNTs) have been performed in aqueous NaCl solutions. In addition to purely siliceous frameworks, various levels of aluminum substitution were also investigated. It was shown that these substitutions have an impact on the transport of both the water molecules and the solvated ions. The residence times of water molecules within the ZNT increase more than 100% at a 𝑆𝑖/𝐴𝑙 ratio of 12 with respect to a ZNT of pure silicon dioxide (~1.5 ns to ~3.5 ns). Radial distribution functions reveal that the local structure of the solution within the ZNT is also altered by the presence of the framework aluminum atoms. These differences and the electrostatic potential across the membrane introduced by the charge defects may yield the ability to pursue separation applications that can be tuned based by altering the local environment surrounding the ZNT.

papers.title: Metal-Ligand Chemistry and Hybrid Nanomaterials: AI/ML for Design, Separations, and Self-Driving Laboratories
Integrated Framework for Multi-Die Semiconductor Interconnect Systems: Hierarchical Signal Management Methodology and Coordinated Tessellation Architecture for Heterogeneous Chiplet Integration
papers.abstract: The progressive scaling limitations of monolithic semiconductor dies have driven the semiconductor industry toward heterogeneous multi-die integration, wherein multiple specialised chiplets are co-packaged on a shared substrate.[1,2] This work presents two complementary theoretical frameworks disclosed under Indian Patent Applications IN202521117751 and IN202521130431 that together constitute a full-stack co-design methodology for multi-die interconnect systems. The first framework, the Structured Electro-Interconnect Management Configuration (SEIMC),[11] addresses the algorithmic design layer through a three-module computational pipeline: a hierarchical signal distribution processor that decomposes extensively connected signal networks into spatially bounded regional subnetworks; a layout organisation processor that partitions the physical layout into thermally and electrically coherent regions; and an iterative design refinement engine whose convergence is guaranteed by mathematical bounds on the spatial extent of each modification step. Computational analysis predicts inter-die signal propagation below 5 ps, energy consumption below 1 pJ/bit,[10] and design closure for 10,000-signal systems within 5-60 seconds on standard computing hardware. The second framework introduces a multi-layer physical interconnect architecture employing coordinated geometric tessellation patterns:[12] a hexagonal primary routing layer (characteristic dimension L₁ = 15-45 µm), a triangular secondary layer with dimensional ratio L₂/L₁ ∈ [1.60, 1.85],[6] and a thermal via layer oriented at θ = 40-50°to the primary axis.[7] The geometric coordination between hexagonal and triangular layers causes triangular vertices to align naturally with hexagonal edge midpoints, creating electromagnetic partition boundaries without dedicated shielding structures.[8] Finite element analysis predicts electromagnetic isolation exceeding 50 dB at 10 GHz with partitionboundary area overhead below 10%, thermal resistance below 0.30 °C/W,[9] and die interconnection timing variation below 50 ps. Complete experimental validation methodology is disclosed in Section 6 to enable independent verification at qualified semiconductor packaging facilities. All energy implications of this work are quantified on a per-operation basis-joules per bit, watts per package-that are independent of electricity generation source; none of the predicted efficiency benefits require nuclear power, small modular reactors (SMRs), uranium fuel cycles, nuclear fusion, or any non-renewable energy infrastructure. Performance values cited for current technology are drawn from peer-reviewed experimental literature; all values for this work are computational predictions calibrated against that literature and require independent experimental validation before equivalence can be claimed.

papers.title: Magnesium(0) Complexes and their Reduction Reactions with Binary Transition Metal Carbonyls
papers.abstract: A new example of an anionic magnesium(0) complex, and two mixed oxidation state magnesium (Mg I /Mg 0) compounds have been stabilised by very bulky -diketiminate ligands. Reaction of the magnesium(0) compound with neutral group 6-8 metal carbonyls leads to their reduction, and the formation of a series of anionic transition metal carbonyl complexes.

papers.title: The missing link in H2 electrolysis on Pt surfaces: water networks
Cytotoxic Effects of Branched Cationic Peptides Derived from Bovine Lactoferricin on Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma
papers.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma is the most common type of oral cancer. In many cases, misdiagnosis leads to the progression of the disease to life-threatening stages. In this study, we evaluated a series of synthetic peptides derived from bovine lactoferricin (bLFcin) as potential strategies to treat oral carcinoma. Host defense peptides, such as bLFcin, interact with the negatively charged membranes of cancer cells through ionic and selective interactions. To enhance the cationic and amphiphilic properties of lactoferricin-derived peptides, we designed branched and palindromic sequences from bLFcin(6) (i.e., 20 RRWQWR 25). A total of 14 peptides were synthesized using solid support synthesis. We found that tetrameric and dimeric peptides with higher cationic charge and improved amphiphilic properties were cytotoxic to human oral carcinoma cell lines. Scanning electron microscopy revealed membrane disruption and pore formation induced by bLFcin(20-25)2. In addition, flow cytometric analyses of cells treated with fluorescently tagged bLFcin(20-25)2 confirmed selective interaction of the cationic peptide with the anionic cancer cell membranes. Lastly, the dimeric peptide bLFcin(20-25)2 inhibited tumor growth of chemically induced oral carcinoma in hamsters, demonstrating its in vivo efficacy. These results pave the way for the design of branched cationic peptides as potential oral cancer therapeutics.

papers.title: A 3-Fluoropyridine-Substituted Grubbs III Catalyst as a 19F NMR Probe for Chain Chelation in ROMP
papers.abstract: Propagation rates in ruthenium-catalyzed ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP) can be attenuated by transient back-coordination of the growing chain to the metal center. Direct spectroscopic observation of such chelation under catalytically relevant conditions remains challenging, owing to the fast exchange dynamics of propagating intermediates and spectral overlap in conventional 1 H NMR. Here, we report a Grubbs catalyst 3rd generation (GIII) in which the ancillary pyridine is substituted with 3- fluoropyridine (F-GIII), such that chain chelation may be observed using Variable Temperature 19 F nuclear magnetic resonance (VT-NMR) spectroscopy. F-GIII is readily prepared analogously to GIII from GII, giving a solid-state structure closely related to its 3-bromopyridine analogue, and exhibits comparable reactivity. A selection of chelation-prone or non-chelating norbornene and oxanorbornene-based monomers are investigated using 19 F VT-NMR and display either well-defined temperature-dependent equilibria between coordinated and dissociated pyridine or persistent dissociation consistent with chelating behavior. These results establish 19 F NMR as a convenient, non-invasive and direct probe for studying growing polymer chain-catalyst interactions during ROMP.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Prediction of Thermal Expansion in Complex Oxides via LLM-Curated Literature Data
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used in materials discovery, but its practical application is often limited by the time required to construct structured experimental datasets and by the lack of reliable uncertainty estimates. We introduce an integrated workflow that combines documentgrounded large language model (LLM) literature mining, human verification, and probabilistic modeling to enable uncertainty-aware prediction of the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) in complex oxides. Experimentally reported CTE values, compositions, and measurement temperature ranges are extracted from full-text articles using a document-grounded large language model and subsequently normalized and verified. Composition-derived descriptors and the reported temperature bounds are used as inputs to a probabilistic regression model that predicts both the expected CTE and a composition-dependent uncertainty, enabling prediction intervals for new compositions. On held-out tests, the model achieves competitive mean accuracy relative to deterministic baselines while producing uncertainty estimates that increase systematically for sparsely represented or chemically distinct compositions, enabling risk-aware screening and prioritization. The workflow supports comparative screening of compositions with targeted CTE behavior and helps guide experimental selection for detailed thermophysical characterization. This study illustrates how LLM-assisted literature curation can be combined with uncertainty-aware machine learning to construct property prediction workflows for materials systems where experimental data are sparse and primarily available in the literature.

papers.title: Spatial Mapping of Electrochemical Hole-Injection into Perovskite Supercrystals
papers.abstract: Lead halide perovskite nanocrystals are of interest for the application as emissive layer in light emitting diodes (LEDs) due to their high photoluminescence quantum yield, their color tunability and their defect tolerance. For the application in LEDs, charges need to be easily transferred from the charge transport layers to the nanocrystal core without compromising their optoelectronic properties. While charging of nanocrystals can be studied by spectroelectrochemistry (SEC) in general, in this work we combine SEC with diffraction-limited optical resolution. This allows studying hole injection into self-assembled supercrystals of CsPbBr3 nanocrystals and determining the spatially dependent potential for this action. We find an overall brightening of the photoluminescence, which is gradually shifting from the edges to the supercrystal center, and a generally greater resistance toward electrochemical degradation in the supercrystals.

papers.title: Advances in Air-Stable Perovskite Precursor Inks for Photovoltaics
papers.abstract: Perovskite photovoltaic has garnered widespread attentions from the scientific and industrial community for the exceptional power-conversion efficiency, low fabrication cost, straightforward processing, and structural versatility of the devices. However, conventional fabrication process of perovskite light-absorbing films requires strictly controlled low-humidity and low-oxygen inert environment, which poses significant challenges for large-area production and commercial scalability. Developing air-stable perovskite precursor inks provides a useful approach to overcome the constraints of traditional preparation conditions. The present review first highlights the properties of perovskite precursor colloids, then provides a systematic overview of recent advances in air-stable perovskite inks. A broad spectrum of strategies for bolstering the ambient stability of perovskite inks is comprehensively examined-encompassing solvent engineering, compositional optimization, and additive design. The review concludes by pinpointing the remaining challenges and charting future research pathways toward truly air-processable perovskite materials, with the goal of accelerating both the technological maturation and the industrial-scale deployment of perovskite photovoltaics.

papers.title: Extended Mixed-Reference Spin-Flip Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory (EMRSF-TDDFT) for Charge-Transfer State
papers.abstract: We propose a novel extended mixed-reference spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory (EMRSF-TDDFT). This approach extends MRSF-TDDFT by incorporating electronic configurations present in linear-response TDDFT but absent in conventional MRSF-TDDFT, which are essential for relaxation in charge-transfer excited states. The formulation is based on the connection between linear-response and MRSF time-dependent Hartree-Fock theory and is extended to TDDFT. Benchmark calculations for representative molecular systems show that EMRSF-TDDFT consistently stabilizes charge-transfer excited states relative to those of MRSF-TDDFT and improves agreement with reference theoretical best estimates. We expect that the new EMRSF-TDDFT model is applicable to problems where the relative energetics of charge-transfer and locally excited states are important, such as thermally activated delayed fluorescence, as well as to nonadiabatic dynamics involving charge-transfer processes.

papers.title: Surfactant-free NaBH4-mediated synthesis of AuxPd1-x nano-alloys for active electrocatalysts
papers.abstract: Nanomaterials with composition Au x Pd 1-x (x=0-1) in the size range 5-15 nm are easily obtained at room temperature using a surfactant-free NaBH 4 -mediated synthesis in water. The materials are readily active electrocatalysts suitable to timely study composition effects, as exemplified with the electrocatalytic ethanol oxidation reaction (EOR).

papers.title: Radical-Assisted Enhanced Intersystem Crossing Enables Efficient Triplet Photochemical Reactions: Application to BODIPY Photocages
papers.abstract: Photoreaction efficiency via the triplet states is often reduced by rapid singlet decay channels that can outcompete spin-forbidden intersystem crossing (ISC) when organic chromophores are photoexcited to the singlet excited states. A classical strategy to promote ISC is incorporation of heavy atoms (e.g. iodine), but halogenation may introduce undesirable photochemical R-X bond scissions. Here we demonstrate an alternative to the heavy-atom effect by appending a stable radical to a chromophore to induce radical-assisted enhanced intersystem crossing (RAE-ISC) for triplet photochemical reactions. Using a TEMPO-substituted BODIPY photocage as a model system, we show that RAE-ISC increases the photoreaction quantum yield by an order of magnitude. Transient absorption spectroscopy and computational calculations confirm that generation of the triplet excited state, enabled by RAE-ISC, is the key factor underlying the enhanced photochemical efficiency. These results provide proof of concept that RAE-ISC is a new and promising strategy for the future design of chromophores that promote triplet-state photochemical reactivity.

papers.title: Like-Charge Ion Pairing and Enhanced Interfacial Diffusion in Charged Aqueous Droplets
papers.abstract: Chemical reactions in charged aqueous microdroplets often proceed orders of magnitude faster than in bulk solution, yet the molecular origins of this acceleration remain unclear. Using molecular dynamics simulations of charged water nanodroplets containing Na + , Cl-, and OHions, we examine two molecular-level factors that may contribute to enhanced interfacial reactivity: ion pairing and radially dependent diffusion. Multiple hydroxide ions exhibit an enhanced tendency to form contact-ion pairs relative to Na + and Clions despite their like charge. These contact ion pairs are stabilized by hydrogen-bonded water bridges that form transient O 4 H 6 2structures. These correlations are most pronounced in the subsurface region, where ion density and orientational ordering of interfacial water are enhanced. Diffusion in this layer is moderately accelerated, with coefficients up to 1.5 times larger than in the droplet interior. Although this enhancement alone cannot explain the large reaction-rate increases reported in microdroplet experiments, the combination of increased encounter frequencies and stabilized ion pairs suggests a molecular mechanism by which interfacial confinement and fluctuating electric fields may promote reactive ion configurations in charged droplets. Finally, the larger depth of the OHions from the interface relative to alkali and halide ions may help rationalize differences in ionization efficiency between negative and positive modes in electro-spray ionization.

papers.title: Chirality Unlocks Sub-Terahertz Molecular Dynamics in Peptide Nanotubes
papers.abstract: Low-frequency modes in the picosecond range play a key role in molecular recognition and biomolecular function. Here, we investigate how these dynamics at the interfaces of self-assembled peptide biomaterials relate to fine structural details of the supramolecular assembly. We resolve terahertz and mid-infrared modes in individual diphenylalanine nanotubes by nanoscale microspectroscopy, uncovering a direct correlation between supramolecular chirality, molecular arrangement, and picosecond dynamics at the nanotube-environment boundary. By combining THz and mid-IR nanoscopy with a multiscale strategy spanning single nanotubes and ensemble measurements, supported by density functional theory calculations, we access the intrinsic picosecond response of peptide assemblies beyond the limits of conventional microscopy and ensemble averaging. Heterochiral (D-L) nanotubes display sharp resonances, whereas homochiral (L-L) nanotubes exhibit a comparatively featureless sub-THz profile, revealing a clear chirality-dependent contrast. Mode assignments show that the heterochiral features are dominated by localized torsional and bending motions of phenyl rings relative to the peptide backbone. Overall, chirality-dependent THz fingerprints emerge as sensitive descriptors of peptide nanotube architecture, while low-frequency nanospectroscopy provides a route to interrogate biomaterial interfaces under biologically relevant conditions.

papers.title: EOSH-Closure: An Oxidation-State-Anchored Electron-Counting Framework for Main-Group Structure Prediction
papers.abstract: We present EOSH-Closure (Electron Ownership via Shell Hierarchy), a parameterfree, arithmetic electron-counting framework that predicts AX m E n molecular geometry from a binary formula and total charge alone. The method applies a single operationclosure-core subtraction-to the IUPAC ionic-limit electron count e i = Z i −O i , yielding an integer valence descriptor n val (i) from which lone pairs, steric number, and geometry follow without free parameters or Lewis-structure drawing. Validated against 23 binary fluorides (interhalogen, noble-gas, and hypervalent p-block; steric numbers 2-7) and a further 15 non-fluoride compounds (Cl, Br, O, S, N ligands; Table S4 †), the framework recovers all 38 experimentally established geometries correctly (38/38). Three supplementary descriptors-the Closure Nuclear Charge Ratio η (D8), the Closure Compatibility Index Γ (D9), and the LCP minimum central-atom radius r ion,min (D10)-extend the electronic gate to a three-gate hierarchy (electronic, compatibility, steric) that correctly predicts the existence of [SiF 6 ] 2and the non-existence of [SiCl 6 ] 2from first principles. A systematic 5 733-entry AB m atlas maps electronic admissibility across seven ligand families, and a four-level routing protocol identifies when VSEPR localisation fails and higher-level theory is required. The linear combination δ(i) = λ • OS(i) + (1 − λ) • FC(i) unifies formal charge and oxidation state on a single ionicity continuum; six prospective computational tasks define explicit falsification criteria connecting the framework to ab initio electronic structure.

papers.title: Interplay of Iron Coordination Dynamics and Second-Sphere H-Bonding Machinery Governs the Selective Halogenation by α-KG/Fe-dependent SyrB2
papers.abstract: In this study, we elucidate the halogenation mechanism catalyzed by SyrB2 through an integrated computational approach, which combines simulated annealing (SA), molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical-molecular dynamics (QM/MM MD) simulations. Our investigations reveal an alternative binding mode of α-ketoglutarate (α-KG), which corroborates the inferred substrate positioning from 2 H-HYSCORE spectroscopic data and promotes the formation of a five-coordinate equatorial Fe(IV)-oxo intermediate. Key findings highlight that the coordination dynamics of the iron center governs SyrB2's chlorination selectivity. The transformation of the Fe(IV)oxo species from an equatorial to an axial conformation facilitates hydrogen-atom abstraction from the C−H bond of the substrate. Subsequent re-isomerization of the Fe(III)-OH intermediate to the equatorial conformation is critical for selective chlorination while minimizing competitive hydroxylation. This mechanistic scheme is further validated by the reactivity of the non-native substrate L-Nva. As L-Nva has an extended carbon chain and lacks the constraints of the hydroxyl-mediated hydrogen-bonding interactions, the corresponding C5 radical intermediate is positioned closer to the OH-ligand than the Clligand, leading to preferential hydroxylation, in accord with experimental observations. Our modeled structure is consistent with the resolved SyrB1-PPant-SyrB2 crystal structure, supporting the reliability of our modeling protocol. Altogether, our work reveals that an interplay between iron-ligand dynamics and second-sphere hydrogen-bonding networks governs selective chlorination in the SyrB1-SyrB2 complex.

papers.title: Pharmaceutical Contamination in European Groundwater and Drinking Water
papers.abstract: Pharmaceuticals and their transformation products (TPs) are especially relevant contaminants of emerging concern (CECs) due to their engineered bioactivity and their widespread presence in diverse environments. Trace levels of pollution from pharmaceutical compounds is a global problem, and the presence of these chemicals in drinking water is particularly concerning as this is an important pathway for human exposure. Additionally, contamination in groundwater is particularly relevant, as many countries, including Denmark, rely on it as a critical drinking water source. Thus, understanding the nature of pharmaceutical pollution in aquatic matrices is crucial. With this goal in mind, this paper aims to summarize the extent of pharmaceutical pollution in European drinking and groundwater by conducting a literature review, which includes 25 studies that detected pharmaceutical compounds via either gas chromatographymass spectrometry (GC-MS) or liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS). This review highlights concentration ranges and detection frequencies. It also discusses key pharmaceuticals, including carbamazepine, sulfamethoxazole, metformin, ibuprofen, diclofenac and phenazone. Additionally, publicly available data published by the German Environment Agency, Umweltbundesamt in the PHARMS-UBA database, is utilized to expand the overview of medicine residue pollution in European groundwater and drinking water and consider the toxicological implications of these findings for public health. Lastly, research gaps are identified and a path forward using advanced analytical methods to expand the evaluated chemical space and improve toxicological and ecotoxicological insights is proposed with the overall aim of improving protection for human and environmental health.

papers.title: Photocatalytic Amino and Alkoxy Carbonylation Reactions in Flow Using [Co2(CO)8]
papers.abstract: A cobalt mediated photocarbonylation reaction, whereby [Co2(CO)8] acts as a catalyst and carbon monoxide surrogate, has been developed and translated to flow for the preparation of amides and esters. The flow process is technically straightforward, does not require CO gas handling, includes a membrane separator to facilitate in-line purification and can produce amides in multi-gram quantities. Modest-to-high yields of amides and esters were achieved within 1-2 h residence times. A competitive hydrodebromination side-reaction was observed and quantified under these conditions, relative to desired carbonyl-containing products. This presents the first demonstration of an eIective cobalt photocatalysed carbonylation reaction in flow.

papers.title: Order-disorder phase transition and orientational defect formation in a hybrid organic-inorganic piezoelectric material
papers.abstract: Hybrid organic-inorganic materials offer an alternative to Pb-based ceramics for ferroelectric and piezoelectric applications. However, these materials suffer from ferroelectric-to-paraelectric phase transitions above which the piezoelectric response disappears. For most hybrid materials, this occurs below room temperature. Here, we investigate a notable exception, TMCMCdCl3 (TMCM = trimethylchloromethyl ammonium), which features an order-disorder phase transition at 400 K. By training a machine learning force field based on the scalable Allegro architecture and performing large scale molecular dynamics simulations, we show that the phase transition temperature can be predicted in close agreement with experiments, provided that dispersion interactions are included, and that the high temperature phase is dominated by dynamical disorder of the molecular cations. We uncover an unexpected molecular orientation in the high temperature phase, not following the expectations from the symmetry relations between ferroelectric and paraelectric phases, which contributes to entropic stabilisation of the high temperature phase. This demonstrates the shortcomings of previous model Hamiltonian based approaches, which did not include the unexpected molecular orientations. Finally, we show that orientational defects of the molecular cations are present in significant concentrations in the low temperature phase, suggesting that these can act as nucleation sites for polarisation switching. This paves the way for accurate modelling of ferroelectric-to-paraelectic phase transitions and design of hybrid organic-inorganic materials with exceptional room temperature piezoelectric response.

papers.title: Substrate-Programmed Selectivity in Sequential Transpeptidase Ligation
papers.abstract: Enzymes that process two substrates through sequential steps recognize structural motifs on the substrates that define selectivity at each reaction step. However, whether and how selectivity emerges in sequential, multi-substrate reactions remains incompletely understood. Here, we hypothesized that first-substrate binding reshapes the enzyme-substrate intermediate to program second-substrate selectivity. Using a transpeptidase, ancestral sortase variant (AcSE5), as a model to test the hypothesis, we developed a Contact Reporter assay that enables rapid and quantitative profiling of ligation across systematically diversified first-second substrate combinations. This comprehensive analysis revealed that single-residue changes in the first substrate generate distinct selectivity profiles for subsequent nucleophiles. To extend this analysis beyond peptide-based substrates, we further established a fluorescence readout and visualized selectivity across a chemically diverse set of 79 primary amines. Together, our findings reveal how selectivity emerges in sequential, multi-substrate reactions: first-substrate binding biases second-substrate preference via the enzyme–substrate intermediate, offering a generalizable framework for directing ligation outcomes in transpeptidases and related bioconjugation platforms

papers.title: Fluorination as a Molecular Design Parameter for Programming Peptide Nanocarriers
papers.abstract: Peptide-based nanocarriers offer unique opportunities for programmable self-assembly, yet rational design strategies that couple structural control with biological function remain limited. In particular, fluoropeptides have been largely inaccessible as modular building blocks until the recent availability of enantiomerically pure fluorinated amino acids in gram-scale quantities, preventing their systematic use in functional nanomaterials. Here, we introduce fluorination as a quantitative molecular design parameter to program peptide self-assembly, morphology, and biological performance. A homologous series of amphiphilic fluoropeptide-RGD conjugates was constructed in which the degree of side-chain fluorination is precisely controlled. We show that fluorination does not monotonically enhance assembly, but instead defines a narrow design window in which compact, non-amyloid fibrillar architectures emerge. Mechanistic insight from molecular dynamics simulations reveals how fluorineinduced modulation of hydrophobic interactions and hydration disrupts classical β-sheet packing. The optimized trifluorinated conjugate exhibits high drug-loading capacity, pH-triggered release, receptor-specific cellular uptake, and low cytotoxicity, while remaining enzymatically degradable. Together, these results establish fluorinated peptide segments as a previously inaccessible and programmable handle for the rational design of peptide-based nanocarriers.

papers.title: Catalytic Surface Degradation of (CF2H)2O to CF3H at a Si-Teflate Doped Aluminium Chlorofluoride Lewis Superacid
papers.abstract: The synthesis and characterisation of ACF-Si-teflate (teflate: pentafluoroorthotellurate) is reported, which is a solid super Lewis acid generated by incorporating teflate-functionalised silicon containin entities into an aluminium chlorofluoride (ACF) matrix. ATR IR analysis confirmed its super acidic nature, with a blueshift Δν(CN) of 69 cm −1 for ACF-Si-teflate•CD 3 CN, adduct exceeding that of SbF 5 •CD 3 CN. This material catalytically degrades the persistent fluorinated ether bis(difluoromethyl) ether (CF₂H₂O) into CF₃H, with Et3SiH serving as an HF scavenger. More than 95 % conversion to generate CF 3 H was achieved within 24 h. The scavenger is crucial to ensure continuous catalytic activity, preventing HF from blocking the active sites at the catalyst. This heterogeneous catalysis approach provides a strategy for remediating stable fluorinated pollutants.

papers.title: Tensorization over Factorization: Rethinking Permutation Invariant Polynomials in JAX
papers.abstract: Permutation invariant polynomials have been the gold standard descriptor for constructing high-precision potential energy surfaces (PESs) for over two decades. The monomial symmetrization approach (MSA) has long served as the dominant engine for this task, primarily by minimizing floating-point operations (FLOPs) through algebraic factorization. While the common sub-expression factorization leads to non-contiguous memory access and explosion of intermediate monomials, causing deep and scattered computational graph for automatic differentiation (AD) engines. To resolve these issues, we introduce JaxPIP, a library implemented in JAX and Equinox, that advocates the paradigm shift from factorization to tensorization. JaxPIP reformulates PIPs evaluation into dense, hardware-friendly tensor operations via log-exp fusion and segmented summation. Benchmarks show that JaxPIP achieves orders-of-magnitude faster JIT compilation and superior throughput compared to existing implementations such as MOLPIPx on both CPUs and GPUs. The tensorized architecture naturally supports massive batching, enabling efficient high-throughput simulations such as path-integral molecular dynamics (PIMD), ring-polymer molecular dynamics (RPMD) and vibrational diffusion Monte Carlo (VibDMC). Our practice confirms that on modern architectures, the cost of redundant FLOPs is tiny compared to the benefits of memory continuity and computational graph simplicity.

papers.title: Is a support always needed in heterogeneous catalysis mediated by metal nanoparticles? The case of metal-organic alloys NiGraf and rNiGraf
papers.abstract: Is a support always needed in heterogeneous catalysis mediated by metal nanoparticles? To answer the question, this study investigates metal-organic alloys NiGraf and its reduced version rNiGraf and their sol-gel entrapped versions in the catalytic reduction of nitroaromatics under ultramild conditions. Both NiGraf and rNiGraf consisting of jamborite nanoparticles entrapping graphene oxide and graphene within the crystal lattice and the ORMOSIL-entrapped NiGraf and rNiGraf are able to selectively mediate nitroaromatics selective hydrogenation. The sol-gel entrapped catalysts, however, employed in consecutive reaction runs rapidly lose the initial excellent activity. These findings are important in the quest for catalytic materials that can selectively convert nitroaromatic compounds to amines under mild conditions viable for upscaling and practical uptake.

papers.title: Adiabatic Connection Methods Applied to Molecular Crystals
papers.abstract: We extend adiabatic connection models (ACMs) derived from the Møller-Plesset adiabatic connection (MPAC) formalism, previously applied only to finite systems, to periodic molecular crystals. Lattice energies for 19 representative systems are computed and compared with periodic MP2, high-level reference, and experimental data. The tested ACMs achieve accuracies comparable to state-of-the-art dispersioncorrected hybrid density functionals and come close to those of correlated wave-function methods. Among them, the HFAC24 model, which is a post-Hartree-Fock parameterfree correlation expression that correctly recovers both the uniform-electron-gas and strong-interaction limits, is the only one with accurate binding energies and accuarate total energies. The results in this work demonstrate that MPAC-based ACMs provide 1 an accurate and transferable framework for modeling molecular-crystal energetics and represent a robust, systematically improvable route for developing correlation models for extended systems.

papers.title: Time-resolved IR and X-ray spectroscopy as complementary electronic structure probes of photoinduced ligand-exchange
papers.abstract: Photoinduced ligand-exchange dynamics in molybdenum hexacarbonyl have been studied using time-resolved IR and X-ray spectroscopy. We find that the energies of the unoccupied molybdenum 4d-derived orbitals that are accessed through X-ray transitions correlate with red-shifts in CO stretching modes. This provides complementary electronic structure information from the metal and the ligand perspective.

papers.title: Oral Administration of Cannabidiol via Zirconium-Based Metal-Organic Frameworks: In Vivo Neuroprotective Effects in a C. elegans Alzheimer's Model
papers.abstract: Cannabidiol (CBD) holds significant therapeutic promise for neurodegenerative pathologies. However, its clinical translation is severely restricted by poor aqueous solubility and susceptibility to degradation in the acidic gastric environment. To overcome these limitations, this study reports the encapsulation of CBD within NU-1000, a zirconium-based metal-organic framework (MOF) distinguished by exceptional acid stability and biocompatibility. The resulting composite, CBD@NU-1000, was optimized to attain a high drug loading capacity of approximately 50 wt% while maintaining the structural integrity of the MOF. Under simulated gastrointestinal fluids, NU-1000 effectively shielded CBD from gastric degradation and facilitated controlled release within the intestinal milieu. In vivo efficacy was assessed using a transgenic Caenorhabditis elegans model of Alzheimer's disease expressing human β-amyloid. Oral administration of CBD@NU-1000 significantly delayed the onset of β-amyloid-induced paralysis, demonstrating neuroprotective potency comparable to free CBD but with a superior, sustained therapeutic effect attributable to controlled release kinetics. Toxicological evaluations confirmed the biosafety of NU-1000 at therapeutic doses, evidencing efficient internalization and excretion without bioaccumulation risks. Consequently, this study establishes the potential of MOF-mediated encapsulation as a viable strategy to enhance the oral bioavailability and long-term efficacy of CBD in treating neurodegenerative disorders.

papers.title: Variational Quantum Circuits for Pesticide Environmental Fate Prediction: A Comparative Study with Classical Machine Learning on the EU SPIN Database
papers.abstract: Predicting pesticide environmental fate properties specifically soil degradation half-life (DegT50) and organic carbon sorption coefficient (K oc)-is essential for regulatory risk assessment under EC 1107/2009. Classical QSAR models achieve moderate predictive power for K oc but struggle with DegT50 due to its dependence on complex soil microbial processes. This work investigates whether variational quantum circuits (VQCs) can capture non-linear molecular descriptor relationships that elude classical regressors. We encode 17 physicochemical descriptors for 111 EU-registered pesticides into a 12-qubit IQP-style quantum circuit with data re-uploading and 8 variational layers (301 trainable parameters). Leave-one-out cross-validation benchmarks reveal that Random Forest (RF) achieves R 2 = 0.194 for DegT50 and 0.726 for K oc (on a circularity-free 16-feature set excluding the bioaccessibility proxy), while Gradient Boosting (GB) reaches 0.223 and 0.764, respectively. The VQC underperforms classical baselines on DegT50 (R 2 < 0, 5-fold CV), consistent with severe overfitting expected from the unfavorable parameter-to-sample ratio (N params /N data ≈ 2.7). A hybrid stacking framework blending QML and RF predictions yields α = 0.20, but the resulting R 2 improvement (+0.02) is not statistically significant. We also assess adverse outcome pathway (AOP) features derived from AOP-Wiki data as additional descriptors, finding no improvement over structural features alone. These results provide a rigorous benchmark for near-term quantum machine learning applied to regulatory chemistry and highlight the critical role of dataset size in VQC generalization.

papers.title: Managing the Anthropogenic Carbon Cycle - Technologies, Pathways, Emissions
papers.abstract: Effective decarbonization and carbon removal require tools that facilitate holistic yet detailed decisionmaking across interconnected carbon pathways; however, existing research often isolates technologies and focuses on linear process chains. To bridge this gap, we present a systemic framework for the anthropogenic carbon cycle encompassing capture, conversion, utilization, and storage. Through an iterative synthesis and multi-level abstraction process, we decompose the cycle into 46 technological building blocks. These blocks can be assembled into diverse pathway configurations (Carbon Capture and Storage, CCS; Carbon Capture and Utilization, CCU; Carbon Capture Utilization and Storage, CCUS) and categorized by their resulting emission balances (net-negative, net-zero, netpositive). This modular representation enables flexible navigation between emerging technologies and established circular value chains, revealing synergies and emission trade-offs. The framework equips decision-makers with a practical tool to design and assess systemic circular carbon strategies.

papers.title: Practical and Sustainable Synthesis of Fluorinated Amino Acids: Process Optimization
papers.abstract: Chiral Ni(II) complexes have emerged as powerful platforms for the synthesis of noncanonical amino acids. Recent advances have enabled gram-scale access to structurally diverse fluorinated amino acids. Nevertheless, the process reported earlier still suffers from practical limitations, including multistep manipulations, prolonged reaction times, and substantial solvent consumption. In this work, we streamline existing methodologies by developing an operationally simple, time-efficient, and more sustainable protocol. Using an (R)-glycine Schiff base Ni(II) complex as the chiral auxiliary, we successfully prepared a series of Fmoc-protected fluorinated R-amino acids for the first time. This strategy provides a practical route for accessing fluorinated numerous new building blocks and facilitates their broader application in peptide synthesis.

papers.title: Mixed-linker Zn(II) coordination polymer with structurally accessible binding sites for efficient and recyclable trimethoprim removal from wastewater
papers.abstract: The persistence of pharmaceutical residues in aquatic systems necessitates the development of robust and recyclable adsorbents for efficient removal. In this work, a Zn(II)-based mixed-linker coordination polymer, [Zn(Phen)(5-NIP)]ₙ (Zn-CP), was synthesized via a solvothermal method and evaluated for the adsorption of the antibiotic trimethoprim (TMP) from aqueous media. Structural characterization by single-crystal X-ray diffraction revealed a one-dimensional zigzag chain architecture featuring periodically exposed aromatic and carboxylate moieties that provide accessible adsorption sites. Batch adsorption experiments demonstrated high removal efficiency (up to ~97%) under optimized conditions. Adsorption kinetics followed a pseudo-second-order model, indicating that surface interactions govern the uptake process, while isotherm analysis confirmed favorable adsorption behavior. Thermodynamic parameters suggested a spontaneous and predominantly physisorption-driven interaction. The material exhibited excellent chemical stability and maintained its adsorption performance over ten regeneration cycles, highlighting its reusability. Mechanistic investigations indicate that hydrogen bonding and π-π interactions between TMP and the exposed functional groups of Zn-CP play a key role in adsorption. These results demonstrate that mixed-linker coordination polymers with structurally accessible binding sites represent promising candidates for the removal of pharmaceutical contaminants from water systems.

papers.title: 1H, 13C, 15N, and 19F Random Coil NMR Shifts of Trifluoromethyl-Bearing Amino Acids
papers.abstract: Fluorine-labeling is a powerful technique in biomolecular NMR, yet its application is often hindered by a lack of standardized reference data for non-natural residues. In this work, we report the multinuclear random coil chemical shifts (1H, 13C, 15N, and 19F) for three commercially available, trifluoromethyl-bearing amino acids: trifluoromethylaminobutyric acid (TfAbu), trifluoronorvaline (TfNva), and 2-trifluoromethyltryptophan ((2-Tfm)Trp). These residues exhibit steric profiles comparable to the canonical amino acids Val, Leu, and Trp, respectively, making them suitable reporters for on-site 19F-labeling of proteins. Random coil data was recorded using a well-established hexapeptide model (Gly-Gly-X-Ala-Gly-Gly). The obtained chemical shifts are highly consistent with the dataset established by Wishart et al. (1995), thereby providing the foundational framework for NMR-based structure elucidation of complex, fluorine-labeled biomolecules.

papers.title: EOSH-Closure in the d-Block: Full-Graph Derivation of d n Counts, Ligand Donation, and the 18-Electron Rule
papers.abstract: The EOSH-Closure framework,[1] introduced for main-group structure prediction, applies a single arithmetic operation to every atom in the molecular graph: n val (i) = (Z i − OS i) − max{c ∈ C ext : c ≤ Z i − OS i }. Here we show that applying this operation simultaneously to the metal centre and all ligand donor atoms in a coordination compound derives-without external input-the d-electron count (d n), the ligand electron donation (n lig), and the 18-electron rule as a noble-gas closure condition. The covalent-bond-classification (CBC) lookup table for n lig emerges as a consequence of EOSH, not a prerequisite. A 23-complex arithmetic panel (spanning carbonyls, halides, aqua, ammine, and cyano ligands across 3d/4d/5d metals) validates all three derived quantities without exception. Scope boundaries are stated precisely: σ-donor atoms yield n lig by direct D5/D6 application; π-ring systems (Cp − , arene) require the Hückel-count correction where the donor pair is not Lewis-localisable on a single atom. The non-innocent-ligand case is handled by branch-enumeration: all integer oxidationstate assignments consistent with the molecular charge are generated; charge-consistent branches converge to a unique answer (C2 confidence); genuinely divergent branches report alternative outputs (C1). RHF/def2-SVP calculations confirm that QM partial charges carry the correct sign relative to EOSH oxidation states in 14 of 14 atoms across 7 molecules (ionicity ratio λ = 0.06-0.42), validating the sign and ordering of the ionic partition without overclaiming quantitative charge magnitudes.

papers.title: Computational hole mobilities in (pseudo-)amorphous organic semiconductors
papers.abstract: The development of novel organic semiconductors with enhanced conducting properties is often hindered by the challenge of accurately describing and modeling charge transport within the (pseudo-)amorphous films typically found in optoelectronic devices. In this study, we present a multiscale computational protocol to accurately predict hole mobilities of non-crystalline hole-transporting materials. Our approach, which integrates density functional theory, molecular dynamics, docking, and kinetic Monte Carlo simulations, reveals the impact of modeling different film morphologiesamorphous, pseudo-amorphous, and paracrystalline-on the charge transport properties of these materials. In particular, we demonstrate that experimentally observed mobility trends across a family of ten hole-transporting molecules, including the enhancement associated with increased aromatic core planarity and extended π-conjugation, can only be reproduced when both amorphous disorder and locally ordered molecular aggregates are explicitly considered. This work establishes a robust, morphology-aware framework for the rational, in silico design and optimization of next-generation organic semiconductors.

papers.title: Cyclo-Polyproline: Chameleonic All-Peptide Macrocycles with Induced-Fit Host-Guest Recognition
papers.abstract: We report the design, synthesis and characterization of a novel class of allpeptide macrocycle, Cyclo-Polyprolines (CP). Exploiting the precision of Fmocbased solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS) and head-to-tail macrocyclization, this platform grants unparalleled control over the macrocycle's primary sequence and secondary structure, offering a viable route towards exo-/endo-functionalization and addressing a bottleneck of traditional synthetic host macrocycles. The resulting CP scaffold is highly amphiphilic, exhibiting excellent solubility in both organic and aqueous media. Structural analysis via NMR spectroscopy and single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals a distinct chameleonic character: the macrocycle shifts from an all-cis conformation in organic solvents to a predominantly all-trans isomer in water. We demonstrate that this transition is driven by a cooperative hydration effect, wherein water molecules stabilize the expanded framework through precise two-point hydrogen bonding. Demonstrating responsive host-guest capabilities, CP undergoes induced-fit isomerization to bind ligands, successfully forming, among other species, an all-peptide pseudo-rotaxane. This methodology establishes a robust platform for creating functionalized, proline-based hosts with significant potential in medicinal chemistry, drug delivery, and organocatalysis, thereby bridging the gap between supramolecular systems and enzyme mimetics.

papers.title: Targeting the RNA-binding Site of SARS-CoV-2 NSP13 by FRASE-bot in CACHE Challenge #2
papers.abstract: The Critical Assessment of Computational Hit-Finding Experiments (CACHE) Challenges came forward as real-world stress tests for virtual screening methods. In Challenge #2, the focus was on SARS-CoV-2 NSP13 helicase - the most conserved protein across Coronaviridae and a prime target for broad-spectrum antivirals. We brought in FRASE-based hit-finding robot (FRASE-bot), our fragment-based screening engine that delimits target-relevant chemical space and identifies likely binding sites. Guided by FRASE-bot, 79 compounds were selected over two rounds. Round 1 delivered four confirmed binders of NSP13 with dissociation constants between 11 and 61 μM. Round 2 pushed further: five analogs bound in the micromolar range, with compounds 8 and 9 (derived from the parent hit 2) showing clear gains over other CACHE participants. With successful runs in both CACHE #1 and #2, FRASE-bot is proving its ability to tackle tough protein targets. The identification of validated binders targeting the RNA-binding groove of SARS-CoV-2 NSP13 holds significant promise for antiviral drug discovery.

papers.title: Deciphering Infrared Difference Spectra of Bovine Rhodopsin in the Amide I Region by Localized Anharmonic Vibrational Calculations
papers.abstract: Vibrational quasi-degenerate perturbation theory (VQDPT2) based on localized vibrational modes is combined with quantum mechanics / molecular mechanics (QM/MM) calculations to investigate the amide bands of bovine rhodopsin in dark (inactive) and Meta II (active) states. The total vibrational spectrum is reconstructed by partitioning the protein into individual amide-group subsystems. Our approach reproduces the experimental IR difference spectrum upon photoactivation across the amide I, II, and III regions, demonstrating the importance of accounting for anharmonicity. Detailed analysis has revealed that the amide I band signals are not localized to a single domain; rather, the higher-wavenumber shifts are primarily driven by helical regions, while lower-wavenumber shifts stem from loop regions. We identified specific residues, such as Thr118 and Trp265, whose significant frequency shifts are coupled with local structural rearrangements. This subsystem-based anharmonic vibrational approach provides a powerful tool for the microscopic interpretation of vibrational spectra in large biomolecular systems.

papers.title: pH-Inverted Histidine-Rich Nanochelants for Trapping Furin-Processed Polycationic Nanotoxins: A Quantum-Classical Platform for Dual Heavy-Metal Detoxification and Broad-Spectrum Countermeasures
papers.abstract: Furin cleaves polybasic sites in endosomes and the secretory pathway, releasing linear (>3 net positive charges) and concentric (metal-coordinating) nanotoxins that drive metabolic disease, cytokine storms, neurodegeneration, autoimmunity, cancer immune evasion, and infection. We introduce 5H-EAF, an erythritol-capped linear penta-histidine nanochelant (MW ≈ 880 Da) that activates to +4–5 net charge at endosomal pH 5.5–6.5, trapping these species via electrostatic clamping and coordination, then deprotonates and releases harmlessly at neutral pH. DFT (B3LYP-D3/def2-TZVP, explicit solvation) yields Pb²⁺ ΔG = –11 to –16 kcal/mol (low pH) → –3 to –6 kcal/mol (neutral); SARS-CoV-2 PRRAR⁺ motif clamping ΔG ≈ –8 to –13 kcal/mol; and anthrax PA63 pore blockade analogous to validated cationic blockers (Kd nM–µM, planar-bilayer literature) supported by all-atom MD simulations (MM-PBSA ΔG = −28.7 kcal/mol at pH 5.5). The platform speaks furin’s native pH/Ca²⁺/charge language without global inhibition. It unifies GLP-1 optimization, cytokine control, α-syn/amyloid management, Pb neuroprotection, and biodefense against furin-dependent pathogens (anthrax, Ebola, H5N1, SARS-CoV-2, Dengue).

papers.title: Color-Changing Hydrogels for Visual pH Monitoring of Confined Living Systems
papers.abstract: Maintaining pH homeostasis is essential for sustaining cell viability, yet confined culture systems such as bioreactors can experience unexpected pH drift despite a controlled nutrient supply. To enable noninvasive, real‑time monitoring of these changes, we developed dual‑dye hydrogel materials that can sense and respond to pH changes in inducible microbial cultures. Image‑based detection and numerical processing of the hydrogel response yield continuous quantitative pH measurements without perturbing the biological system. This platform achieves accuracy within ±0.1 pH units relative to conventional electrochemical probes, demonstrating a robust system‑level approach for dynamic tracking of physicochemical parameters in engineered living systems.

papers.title: Configurational entropy suppresses crystallization in multicomponent molecular glasses
papers.abstract: The formation of stable amorphous molecular solids is fundamentally limited by crystallization from the supercooled liquid, yet no general physical principle exists for suppressing it. Here we demonstrate that increasing configurational entropy through multicomponent molecular mixing provides such a principle. Using equimolar mixtures of small biocompatible molecules, we show that increasing component number markedly reduces liquid fragility without changing the glass-transition temperature. Above a critical component count, crystallization is arrested, yielding stable amorphous phases upon cooling and reheating. Applying this principle to pharmaceutical systems, we show that drugs crystallizing readily in isolation can be stabilized in the amorphous state at loadings as high as 50 mol%, forming what we term high-entropy amorphous drugs (HEADs). At high drug loadings, crystallization remains arrested even as fragility rises above values at which low-component mixtures crystallize readily, revealing that configurational entropy suppresses nucleation through a thermodynamic mechanism independent of fragility reduction. The invariance of the glass-transition temperature further distinguishes molecular systems from high-entropy metallic glasses, where accessible mixing entropy depresses the glass transition impairing glass-forming ability. These results establish configurational entropy as a design parameter for controlling crystallization in molecular glasses, operating through separable kinetic and thermodynamic channels.

papers.title: Measurement of the Critical Ionization Level for Resist Polymer Dissolution Using a Polypeptoid Platform
Measurement of the Critical Ionization Level for Resist Polymer Dissolution Using a Polypeptoid Platform
AnnoMe: User-defined classification of HR-MS/MS spectra for natural product discovery
papers.abstract: Summary: Annotation of HR-MS/MS spectra is a complex task that can be tackled either by expert interpretation or machine learning models that rely on large spectral/structural databases for training. Frequently, users want to find novel compounds of a particular substance class they are already familiar with. This requires the classification of detected compounds as 'relevant' (i.e., belonging to the compound class of interest) or not (i.e., 'other'). For such applications, the python-based AnnoMe software is presented that allows users to classify their experimental HR-MS/MS spectra according to their aims. By leveraging a user-curated dataset of 'relevant' and 'other' reference HR-MS/MS spectra alongside structure-informed embeddings (MS2DeepScore), the package enables rapid and accurate prediction of 'relevant' compounds with custom-trained classification models and a majority vote, facilitating exploration of the complex chemical space inherent to LC-HRMS/MS data. This software is demonstrated by predicting putative prenylated flavonoids for prioritization in natural product discovery. Availability and Implementation: Code, documentation, and datasets are available at https://github.com/chrboku/AnnoMe and https://zenodo.org/records/16322488 .

papers.title: RECOMPENSE: A Student-Led Open Science Initiative for Sustainable Polystyrene Waste Upcycling in Academic Labs
papers.abstract: Plastic waste is a global challenge, with polystyrene (PS) among the least recycled polymers despite its widespread use in laboratories. Conventional recycling routes for PS remain economically and technically limited, creating an urgent need for accessible, sustainable alternatives. Here, we introduce RECOMPENSE, a student-led open science initiative designed to upcycle PS waste into polystyrene sulfonic acid (u-PSSA), a heterogeneous catalyst for green organic synthesis. Developed through MSc research projects at UCL, RECOMPENSE combines technical innovation with educational engagement, offering detailed protocols and video resources freely available online. We report a reproducible method for sulfonating expanded PS under simple laboratory conditions, yielding u-PSSA with up to 45% sulfonation. Its catalytic performance was validated in Friedel–Crafts reactions using biobased substrates, achieving quantitative yields of a biofuel precursor under mild conditions. Comparative studies with commercial PSSA confirmed the viability of waste-derived catalysts, while additional tests with aromatic aldehydes demonstrated broad applicability. Beyond experimental results, RECOMPENSE exemplifies co-creation in sustainable chemistry education. By involving students in research and resource development, the project fosters practical skills, systems thinking, and global collaboration. demonstrating how academic labs can transform plastic waste into valuable resources while preparing future scientists to lead sustainability transitions.

papers.title: In situ observation of ultra-giant spherulites in perovskite hydrates
A Zn4L4 cage with guest-programmable stereochemistry
papers.abstract: Supramolecular hosts with flexible and controllable shapes offer the prospect of generating new technologies, for example in selective chemical purifications. However, balancing flexibility with the rigidity and fidelity required for successful assembly and guest recognition needed for purification applications remains challenging. Here we report a Zn4L4 tetrahedral cage that interconverts between four diastereomers, driven by binding different guest molecules. The truxene-based cage backbone features inward-pointing methyl groups that enclose guests and differentiate the cavities of otherwise similar diastereomers. The cage switches quantitatively between two T-symmetric diastereomers when exposed to adamantane in varying stoichiometry, and adopts C3-or C2-symmetric diastereomers in the presence of lower-symmetry guests. Cyclic ion-mobility mass spectrometry (cIMS-MS) provided insights into the structure and dynamics of these diastereomeric host-guest complexes, indicating that the cage can retain its stereochemistry following guest release. We leveraged this "shape-memory" effect to achieve the programmable binding of different guests from a mixture, as controlled by pre-programmed host stereochemistry.

papers.title: Peroxide Triplet Sensitization and Copper Catalysis for Expanding the Scope of Oand N-Methylation to Late-Stage Diversification
papers.abstract: A practical multicatalytic strategy that merges triplet energy-transfer (EnT) sensitization of di-tert-butyl peroxide with copper catalysis enables efficient O-and N-methylation of protic nucleophiles under mild and neutral conditions. A key design element of this system is the bifunctional reactivity of DTBP. Photoinduced O-O homolysis generates tert-butoxyl radicals, one of which undergoes β-methyl scission to furnish Me • with acetone as a low-boiling byproduct, while the complementary fragment participates in copper-mediated formation of alkoxide-type species (e.g., Cu-O t Bu) that promote in situ activation of O-H and N-H nucleophiles. This redox balanced, synchronized generation of a carbon-centered radical and a catalytic basic component obviates the need for externally added base and enables efficient heteroatom methylation at room temperature using low catalyst loadings. The transformation exhibits broad substrate scope, high functional-group tolerance, and excellent chemoselectivity governed by the interplay between nucleophile acidity and its coordination ability to copper. These features allow late-stage methylation of structurally complex molecules, including drug-like compounds, peptides, and nucleotides bearing acid-or base-sensitive functionalities. Mechanistic studies, supported by experimental and DFT investigations, reveal that methyl radicals are generated through EnT-sensitized peroxide activation, while the copper catalyst selectively orchestrates radical capture and C-heteroatom bond formation.

papers.title: Intramolecular through-space heavy-atom effect in multiresonant thermally activated delayed fluorescence emitters with [2.2]paracyclophane
papers.abstract: The heavy-atom effect (HAE) is a powerful strategy to enhance spin-orbit coupling (SOC) for accelerating reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) in multiresonant thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters, which is relevant to the performance of organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). Here, we demonstrate the effectiveness of a through-space HAE using a [2.2]paracyclophane (PCP) scaffold with a co-facially aligned MR-TADF emitter and bromine atom. By placing a bromine atom at pseudo-ortho (po) or pseudo-meta (pm) positions relative to the tCzBN MR-TADF core, po-PCP-tCzBN-Br and pm-PCP-tCzBN-Br were obtained. The two emitters have nearly identical emission spectra to the reference PCP-tCzBN, yet exhibit faster kRISC: 5.3×10 4 s-1 (po) 2 and 4.1×10 4 s-1 (pm) compared to 2.8×10 4 s-1 (PCP-tCzBN). Despite this improvement in kRISC, OLEDs fabricated with these emitters show no alleviation in efficiency roll-off and display lower maximum external quantum efficiency (EQEmax). The results highlight the promise of through-space HAE as a strategy to accelerate RISC while evidencing that C-Br bond stability adversely affects OLED performance.

papers.title: Green Methacrylation of Geraniol and Citronellol in Rose Oil Enabled by Amano Lipase from Pseudomonas fluorescens: A Step Toward Waste
papers.abstract: Devising bio-synthetic routes based on well-known, simple organic transformations and utilising non-edible and waste feedstocks to create novel bio-derived alternatives to traditional materials is an attractive solution to the current unsustainable synthetic polymer economy. Terpenes have emerged as suitable feedstock alternatives to fossil-based building blocks for polymer synthesis, as they can be obtained from renewable resources and various waste streams. Herein, we report enzymatic, solvent-free, scalable, and operationally simple transformations of alcohol terpenoids into the corresponding methacrylates using Pseudomonas fluorescens lipase (PFL), affording products with full conversion and quantitative yields without the need for further purification. Using this robust method, we demonstrate the transesterification of geraniol and citronellol, the most prevalent terpenes in rose oil, directly within a rose oil mixture to yield their corresponding methacrylate derivatives. This work represents a step forward towards the green functionalisation of terpenes and the valorisation of flower waste biomass.

papers.title: Investigating Glycosylation of the HIV-1 Envelope Protein by Charge Detection Mass Spectrometry and Mass Photometry
papers.abstract: Composed of three heterodimers, the heavily glycosylated trimeric HIV-1 envelope protein (Env) gains entry into host cells by binding CD4 and CCR5 co-receptors, earmarking Env as the main target for neutralizing antibodies and making it a key focus for development of vaccines and inhibitors. Charge detection mass spectrometry (CDMS) was utilized to investigate the glycan processing of Env, which contains up to 90 N-glycan sites per trimer. The methodology was applied to the gp120 and gp140 components, with the gp140 construct exhibiting a higher propensity for gas-phase trimerization, though glycan processing remained comparable across both gp120 and gp140 trimeric forms. CDMS revealed clade-specific differences, with clade B species exhibiting higher molecular weights and greater inter-strain variability than clade C. Investigation into expression systems indicated that CHO cells consistently produced heavier monomeric units than HEK systems. Enzymatic deglycosylation via PNGase F demonstrated that N-glycosylation is critical to the stability of the trimeric complex, while collisional activation revealed distinct variations in gas-phase stability across samples. Finally, CDMS results correlated closely with mass photometry data, validating the ability of CDMS to reflect liquid-phase protein distributions. Collectively, this study underscores the glycosylation complexity of the HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein and demonstrates the ability of CDMS as a robust tool for analysis of highly heterogeneous systems.

papers.title: Solvent-controlled ion transport and electric double-layer stability in nanoporous carbon-based supercapacitors
papers.abstract: The solvent properties play a critical role in determining the power, energy, and long-term stability of energy storage devices. This study elucidates the influence of methanolic versus aqueous solvation environments on EDL formation by comparing 2 mol•kg-1 potassium acetate (KAc) in bulk solutions and nanoporous carbon electrodes. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations reveal important differences in diffusion coefficients, ionicity, coordination numbers, and the potential of mean force for the ions with different solvation shells. These findings are corroborated by Raman spectroscopy, which confirms a high degree of ion pairing in the methanol-based KAc electrolyte. While this strong association results in slower ion transport kinetics compared to the rapid dynamics in water, electrochemical measurements demonstrate that the methanolic environment provides a more stable interface owing to higher ion-solvent stabilization energy and ion desolvation to saturate carbon nanopores. The thermodynamic barrier in methanol also suppresses parasitic side reactions, ensuring that EDL charging remains the dominant storage mechanism even at high voltages. Our findings are validated by the electrochemical potential distribution investigations of symmetric capacitors using these electrolytes and nanoporous carbon electrodes. Potentiostatic floating tests conducted at 1.2 V, 1.6 V, and 2.0 V show that methanolbased capacitors retain 65% energy efficiency after 100 h at 2.0 V, along with significantly lower leakage energy losses, compared to only 13% for the aqueous counterpart. This work confirms that the charge storage at the EDL and ion transport in carbon electrode pores are governed by solvation structure, and in the case of methanol-based KAc electrolyte, lead to long-term stability and high performance metrics.

papers.title: Ozonolysis of strontium-adducted phosphatidylcholines in the gas phase: expanding the isomeric coverage of ozone-induced dissociation
papers.abstract: The structural complexity of lipids, encompassing stereoisomerism, double-bond position, and acyl tail regioisomerism, presents persistent challenges for mass spectrometric analysis. Ozone-induced dissociation (OzID) directly targets carbon-carbon double bonds, but its utility has been limited by relatively slow kinetics. Herein, we show that multivalent metal adduction of phosphatidylcholines, particularly with strontium, markedly accelerates ozonolysis, enabling rapid E/Z stereoisomer differentiation on sub-second timescales. In addition to enhanced reaction efficiency, Sr 2+-adduction promotes charge-splitting fragmentation that selectively cleaves the sn-2 acyl chain. Because this pathway occurs under standard OzID conditions, double-bond position (from OzID) and acyl tail regioisomerism (from charge splitting) can be obtained simultaneously within a single mass spectrum. Mixture analysis confirms accurate quantification of E/Z composition, while the diagnostic sn-specific fragments expand structural resolution beyond conventional OzID.
