Subsequent OzID of sn-specific fragments allows double-bond localization to specific acyl tails, further enhancing structural information. Together, these results establish multivalent metal adduction as a dual strategy to accelerate ozonolysis and broaden its structural coverage, providing a powerful new approach for comprehensive lipid isomer characterization.

papers.title: In Crystallo Synthesis of a Triplet Silver Nitrene
Dissociation behavior of photocatalyst-substrate complexes investigated with quantum mechanically derived force-fields
papers.abstract: Chiral thioxanthones were shown to be promising energy transfer catalysts for the photoinduced catalysis of organic molecules. In recent years, they were successfully applied in photocatalytic deracemization and kinetic resolution reactions with high enantiomeric excess rates. Previous computational investigations have focused on static investigation mostly using density functional theory (DFT). In this study, we use force field-based molecular dynamics to explore the dissociation dynamics of the substrate-catalyst complexes at different potential energy surfaces. Leveraging the quantum mechanically derived force-field (QMdFF) framework enables the efficient simulation of the molecules in the ground and the excited states. We derive kinetic parameters for the complex dissociation and use them in a kinetic reaction model. Our study indicates that the experimentally observed temperature optimum results from a different temperature dependence of the photo-induced energy transfer and the dissociation and association processes of the substrate-catalyst complexes.

papers.title: Predicting Reactivity and Reaction Yields in Parallel Synthesis: Meeting of Expectations and Reality
papers.abstract: This study focuses on the essential problem in modern machine learning in chemistry: data quality and its impact on ML predictions. We explored a dataset of Biginelli reactions, obtained via a parallel synthesis protocol at Enamine LTD over more than 20 years. Prediction models, both classification (feasibility) and regression (estimated yield), were developed. We observed a relatively uniform performance of different ML methods, representations, and descriptor types. The performance of regression models is limited by the inaccuracies in the reported yield values, which were explored in depth (model outlier identification, resynthesis, and structural analysis). Our findings highlight the potential of machine learning models not only for predictive tasks but also as tools for quality control and deeper insights into the synthetic process-particularly when results deviate from expectations. They also demonstrate the critical impact of input data quality on the excellence of prediction models. Our models were finally evaluated on a set of newly synthesized molecules, selected from Enamine's REAL database, and found to be of satisfactory quality.

papers.title: The Electrostatic "Leash" and Coupling Effects in Diffusion of Ionic Species
papers.abstract: Using the thermodynamics of irreversible processes as starting point, the Maxwell-Stefan (M-S) formulation for diffusion of charged species under the influence of electrostatic force fields is derived. The M-S diffusion formulation, that is generally applicable to concentrated ionic solutions, simplifies to yield the Nernst-Planck equations for systems in which the ionic species are present in dilute solutions. The requirements of electro-neutrality and the no-current prescription, combined with the differences in the mobilities of individual ionic species results in the creation of an electrostatic potential gradient, that acts as a "leash" in a manner so as to speed-up or slowdown an ionic species, depending on the sign of the charges. The net result is that diffusion of ionic species is, in general, strongly coupled to one another. Published experimental data for a wide variety of systems are used to highlight several features of ionic diffusion such as transient overshoots, and uphill diffusion during equilibration in bulk electrolyte solutions, permeation across cation-exchange membranes, and uptake in ion-exchange particles.

papers.title: Electrochemical Generation of an Open-Shell Gold(III)-Dithiolene Porous Coordination Polymer
Tailoring Roof-Shaped Nematogens -Alignment and Biaxial Packing in a Nematic LC Phase
papers.abstract: Inspired by a recently postulated nematogen design, two molecules with an inverted substitution pattern of lateral chains were synthesised, for which one realises an optimum biaxial aspect ratio and improved interdigitation of hexyl groups along the minor molecular axis. The impact of the substitution pattern on the packing along the minor director is confirmed by increased order parameters (XRD) and the local packing of defined conformers (solid-state NMR spectroscopy). Molecular dynamics predicts a rather high biaxiality parameter for the nematic phase of the correctly substituted mesogen. Temperature variable polarised optical microscopy studies on homogeneous and homeotropic aligned samples and investigations of the capacitance and resistance provide evidence for a phase transition in the nematic region from a uniaxial nematic N 1 to a new N 2 phase with biaxial order.

papers.title: Universal Design for Learning Case Study: Engaging medical students with chemistry through enhancing relevance and diversifying assessment
papers.abstract: An inorganic chemistry module for undergraduate medicine students was redesigned based on student feedback, using Universal Design for Learning principles to improve student experiences. The main aim was to boost engagement by maximising chemistry's relevance to medicine, while minimising distractions and accessibility-barriers. Structural supports built into large modules reduce need for once-off accommodations. Redesign choices included pre-scheduled communications, accessible learning materials, videos, varying assessment (including peer-assessment), and linking learning to student-generated examples of medicinal applications. Redesign ensured most prior critiques did not recur in post-implementation feedback. Focus group comments and a general uplift of grades largely supported positive impact of interventions.

papers.title: 102No2+ as a soft metal ion: Extraction of 255No using crown ethers
papers.abstract: The chemical properties of transfermium with atomic numbers >100 are largely unknown. Element 102, nobelium, is an actinide and forms stable +2 valent cations in aqueous solutions, unlike other heavy actinide. In previous experiments, No 2+ exhibits similar behavior to alkaline earth metal ions, particularly Ca 2+ and Sr 2+ , suggesting hard-acid character. In this study, the soft metal ion behavior of No 2+ was demonstrated through complex with crown ethers. In the solid-liquid extraction of 255 No using di- t Bu-dicyclohexano-18-crown-6 in HNO 3 , No 2+ was extracted as much as Sr 2+ . Density functional theory calculations confirmed higher stability of the No 2+ -DtBuCH18C6 complex, with covalent bonding involving the 6d orbitals. Theoretical studies also revealed strong relativistic effects on the atomic orbitals of No 2+ , rendering No 2+ a soft ion similar to Pb 2+ .

papers.title: AIEE, optical-waveguide, and latent fingerprint detection behaviors of rutaecarpine, an alkaloid isolated from the medicinal herb Evodia rutaecarpa
papers.abstract: Traditional medicinal herbs Evodia rutaecarpa has long been utilized for treatment of abdominal pain, postpartum hemorrhage, amenorrhea, dysentery, and headache in traditional medical practice. Rutaecarpine (Rut) is an indolopyridoquinazolinone alkaloid isolated from Evodia rutaecarpa having cardiovascular actions. In this work, Rut was found to be a novel luminogen having aggregation-induced emission enhancement (AIEE) property. AIEE phenomenon of Rut was studied by single crystal structure analysis, optical property, viscosity, concentration, and host-guest interaction. Interestingly, crystals of Rut under UV light showing self-waveguiding of the fluorescence. Finally, Rut was used for latent fingerprint visualization. In short, Rut provides a new direction for obtaining novel AIEE-active luminogens, and exhibiting great potential in latent fingerprint detection.

papers.title: Reaction of Phosphiranide Complex with Bunte Salts: Synthesis of 1-Thiophosphirane Complex
papers.abstract: We have developed a tandem protocol starting from β-chloroethylphosphine W(CO)5 complex to access 1-thiophosphiranes bearing a keto group. This strategy capitalizes on the nucleophilicity of phosphiranide complexes toward Bunte salts, establishing a novel platform for P-S bond construction. Two series of Bunte salts were examined in the reaction, affording the phosphirane complexes in moderate yield.

papers.title: Experimental Identification of Oxygen Dissociation Bottleneck in Proton-Conducting Ceramic Fuel Cells
papers.abstract: Proton-conducting ceramic fuel cells (PCFCs) enable efficient electrochemical energy conversion, yet further performance improvements are limited by sluggish cathodic oxygen reduction kinetics and the lack of direct identification of the rate-determining step under operating conditions. Here, we experimentally identified that oxygen dissociation from superoxide intermediates (O 2 2− ) limits cathodic polarization in PCFC devices with a PrBa 0.5 Sr 0.5 Co 1.5 Fe 0.5 O 5+δ (PBSCF) cathode. Modulation-excitation infrared spectroscopy directly observes that superoxide is the major intermediate for the oxygen reduction reaction. We also isolate the intrinsic cathodic kinetics of PBSCF using hydrogen–deuterium isotope effects combined with impedance spectroscopy on working PCFC devices, which achieves peak power densities of 517-1077 mWcm −2 at 550-650 °C under a fuel-oxidant combination of H 2 -air. The cathodic polarization resistance exhibits an oxygen partial pressure dependence with characteristic exponents above 0.5 and shows no measurable dependence on water vapor pressure. This kinetic signature is uniquely consistent with oxygen dissociation via O⁻ formation from O 2 2− intermediates, assisted by oxygen vacancies at the cathode–gas interface. These results provide experimental evidence that oxygen dissociation constitutes the dominant kinetic bottleneck in the PCFC device, establishing a clear design principle: strong electron-donating character coupled with a high density of surface oxygen vacancies is essential to accelerate cathodic kinetics.

papers.title: Accelerated Langevin Dynamics Simulation via Neural Network-Driven Importance Sampling
papers.abstract: Atomistic simulations are powerful tools for understanding the dynamical processes that control material behavior at the molecular scale. Yet the study of many important processes is currently limited by the timescales achievable by direct simulation. This limitation often arises from potential energy landscapes featuring deep energy basins, corresponding to metastable states, in which the system remains trapped for extended periods of time. The long-term evolution of such systems is governed by the transitions between these metastable states, which are rare events that are very inefficient to capture by brute-force simulations. We present an importance sampling framework to accelerate the time scale of Langevin dynamics simulations. Using an importance function to bias the dynamics, this approach significantly enhances the efficiency of sampling the rare transitions, while preserving the relative probabilities between different transition paths. The importance function is parameterized using a neural network for scalability to high-dimensional systems. We also provide a rigorous mathematical formulation to compute the original transition rates between metastable states from the biased dynamics. To control the statistical variance of the estimated transition rates, we introduce a branching random walk (BRW) algorithm to manage the weights of the sampled transition paths. We validate the proposed importance sampling framework on a two-dimensional system and a fourteen-dimensional system to demonstrate its robustness and scalability.

papers.title: Structure-Activity-based Amyloid Trafficking to Suitable Electrode and Electrochemical Disassembly of Insulin Fibrils via ROS-Mediated Structural Collapse
papers.abstract: The pathological aggregation of misfolded proteins into β-sheet-rich amyloid fibrils underlies a broad spectrum of debilitating disorders, yet strategies capable of safely and effectively reversing these supramolecular assemblies remain limited. Here, we present a reagent-free, tunable electrochemical platform for the controlled disintegration of amyloid fibrils using lowintensity electrical stimulation. Employing an electrode-based setup operating at a minimal current of 1 mA, we demonstrate efficient disruption of preformed insulin amyloid fibrils without the need for chemical denaturants or external catalysts. Mechanistic inspection reveals a preferential and specific interaction between insulin amyloid fibrils and graphite electrodes compared to platinum, enabling targeted degradation of β-sheet-rich amyloid fibrils through localized electrochemical reactions. Thus, the electrode interface facilitates structural degradation, leading to a significant reduction in fibrillar morphology. Importantly, electrochemical stimulation not only disassembles amyloid fibrils but also reduces their cytotoxicity and restores insulin's biological activity. Our findings establish electrochemical stimulation as a precise, reagent-free therapeutic strategy, highlighting the critical role of electrode-fibril interaction for amyloid disaggregation. This work advances the emerging field of external electrical stimulation can be a reagent free controllable platform for the development of clinically transformable course of targeting amyloid-associated pathologies.

papers.title: Defying Antiaromaticity - The Curious Case of Pentalenopentalenes
papers.abstract: Antiaromatic molecules possess unique electronic properties attractive for various applications, yet their inherent instability poses a fundamental challenge. Extended annelation with arenes can stabilize antiaromatic cores, but often attenuates the very properties of interest. Here, we systematically investigate the (anti)aromatic character of two families of pentalenopentalene-based polycyclic hydrocarbons: bisbenzannelated and biscycloheptatriene-annelated, in both the S 0 and T 1 states. At first glance, the two families exhibit strikingly different behavior, diverging in symmetry, open-shell character, and magnetic response. The bisbenzannelated isomers form distinct pairs, with the annelation pattern governing their properties. The biscycloheptatriene-annelated form two separate groups, with the type of pentalenopentalene core dictating the properties. However, we show that a single unifying principle underlies all of these seemingly disparate observations: a persistent preference for retaining local aromatic character. In T 1 , the same principle manifests through preferential localization of spin density, preserving local aromaticity and resulting in a local reversal of aromatic character. Resonance structure analysis combined with the Randić conjugated circuit model provide a general framework for rationalization. These findings underscore that neither the Hückel nor Baird rules can be naïvely applied to polycyclic systems and offer guiding principles for the design of persistent antiaromatic molecules.

papers.title: A Hybrid GNN-QAOA Pipeline for Constrained Drug Repurposing Portfolio Selection with Topology-Aware Compilation on IBM Heavy-Hex Quantum Hardware
papers.abstract: Constrained portfolio selection in drug repurposing (choosing subsets of approved compounds that jointly satisfy interaction avoidance, toxicity ceilings, and target-coverage requirements) remains intractable for classical integer programming beyond ∼10,000 candidates, precisely the regime where combinatorial drug repositioning operates. Existing quantum formulations address pairwise drug-combination scoring but do not account for portfolio-level constraints or the mismatch between problem graph structure and physical qubit connectivity. We introduce a three-stage pipeline: a relational graph convolutional network (RGCN) narrows the candidate pool to ∼5,000 triples, a QUBO encoding extends the Complementary-Exposure framework [6], [36] with budget, diversity, and multitarget coverage penalties, and a topology-aware QAOA compiler maps constraint blocks onto natively connected heavy-hex qubit clusters. The compiler reduces two-qubit SWAP-gate counts by 23-41% relative to Qiskit optimization-level-3 transpilation on sub-problems of 20-100 qubits (Table IV), directly lowering accumulated gate error on IBM Heron r2 hardware. Retrospective validation on ten FDA-approved repurposed drugs yields 82.5% Recall@100 on a noiseless simulator versus 79.3% for ILP/Gurobi; on real IBM Heron hardware, recall drops to 69.8% (approximation ratio 0.64), falling 9.5 percentage points behind ILP and quantifying the noise gap that future errorcorrected processors must close. The central finding is negative: at current NISQ fidelities, classical ILP produces strictly superior solutions in less wall-clock time. The contribution is therefore architectural, not algorithmic; the topology-aware compilation strategy transfers directly to improved processors without redesign, positioning the pipeline for the p ≤ 10 −4 gate-error regime projected for 2028-2030. Code and QUBO encodings will be released upon acceptance.

papers.title: Isoelectric Point-Dependent Adsorption of SAMs on Metal Oxides: Selective Modification of TiO 2 -NiO Composite
papers.abstract: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) on metal oxides play a pivotal role in tailoring surfaces for advanced hybrid and nanoscale architectures; however, their adsorption behavior is strongly governed by the interfacial chemistry of the underlying oxide. In this study, we systematically investigate the adsorption characteristics of two model acidic and basic SAM

papers.title: RVGrow A Fragment Efficiency-Based Scoring Strategy for Rational and Efficient Fragment-to-Lead Optimization
papers.abstract: Fragment-based drug design (FBDD) seeks to optimize fragment hits into potent lead compounds by maximizing their three-dimensional interactions with the target binding site. However, designing efficient fragment-to-lead growth strategies remains a core challenge in de novo drug discovery. Here, we introduce RVGrow, a novel algorithm incorporating a Fragment Efficiency Score (FE-score) that guides rational fragment elaboration based on interaction efficiency. RVGrow was systematically applied to evaluate the correlation between FE-score and experimental inhibition data across multiple protein targets. Furthermore, its integration with deep generative models demonstrates RVGrow's adaptability and utility in AI-driven molecular design pipelines. The work presents RVGrow in the context of fragment-to-lead optimization, highlighting its use of interpretable, efficiency-based scoring.

papers.title: Synthetic anionophores enhance the activity of anionic drugs
papers.abstract: Lipid bilayers pose a major barrier to the passive diffusion of anionic species, including many carboxylate-containing drugs. This limited membrane permeability can reduce drug efficacy and allow bacteria to deploy various defense mechanisms. Herein, we show that small synthetic anionophores can significantly enhance antibacterial activity of anionic antibiotics by accelerating their transmembrane transport. In liposomes, these anionophores increase the transmembrane transport rate of carboxylate drugs by over two orders of magnitude, even when present in catalytic amounts. In bacteria, the same artificial carriers synergistically amplify the activity of clinically used anionic antibiotics, markedly enhancing their antimicrobial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative strains. Notably, the extent of this activity enhancement directly correlates with the carrier-induced increase in drug permeability. These results demonstrate that synthetic anion carriers can improve not only membrane permeability but also the therapeutic performance of anionic drugs, offering a promising strategy for overcoming permeability-related resistance in drug design.

papers.title: Position Specific 15 N Isotope Analysis at Natural Abundance by 1 H NMR
papers.abstract: Stable isotope analysis of nitrogen (N) at natural abundance provides key insights into biochemical processes. However, position-specific isotope analysis (PSIA) of 15 N remains technically challenging due to the low sensitivity of conventional approaches. Here, we present a novel method that exploits scalar coupling patterns in conventional 1 H NMR spectra to directly extract 15 N/ 14 N ratios at natural abundance. This approach relies on resolving the 1 H-15 N doublets

papers.title: Solid-State Structural Chemistry of Gold Corroles: Nonplanar Distortions, Crystal Packing, and Aurophilic Interaction
papers.abstract: Gold(III) corroles are often close to planar, the factors governing their deviations from planarity in the solid state remain poorly understood due to the limited number of available crystal structures. Herein, we report a combined single-crystal X-ray diffraction and density functional theory study of a series of meso-phenyl-substituted gold corroles bearing electron-donating and electron-withdrawing substituents. The structures exhibit modest out-of-plane distortions dominated by saddle-type deformations, with amplitudes and symmetry influenced by substituent identity, lattice environment, and asymmetric unit contents (Z′ > 1). Normal-coordinate structural decomposition and relaxed potential energy scans indicate that saddling corresponds to a shallow deformation mode, with planar and distorted conformers separated by < 0.3 kcal/mol and exhibiting nearly invariant force constants across the series. Notably, a short unsupported Au III •••Au III contact (< 3.55 Å) is observed exclusively for AuT[3,5-diOMe]PC; for which NBO and QTAIM analyses provide electronic evidence of a weak but stabilizing aurophilic interaction, representing the first such example in gold corroles. Molecular electrostatic potential analysis further shows that substituent-dependent polarization influences the preferred distortion pattern without significantly perturbing the frontier electronic structure, highlighting how peripheral substitution and crystal packing together shape the supramolecular organization of these metallomacrocycles.

papers.title: Unified Thermodynamic Framework for Speciation-Gated Mass Transfer at Liquid-Liquid Interfaces
papers.abstract: The behavior of ionizable surfactants at oil/water interfaces is central to applications from emulsification to liquid-liquid extraction, yet predictive control remains a challenge. Current models often decouple interfacial adsorption from the underlying acid-base chemistry that inevitably will influence surfactant availability. Here, we establish a unified thermodynamic framework demonstrating that interfacial phenomena are controlled by speciation-gated mass transfer. Using a homologous series of linear carboxylic acids (C5-C16), we combine dynamic interfacial tension measurements with kinetic phenotyping and a phase-resolved speciation/partitioning model to show that the flux of surface-active species is gated by the acidbase equilibrium. Two kinetic regimes emerge across the series: long-chain acids relax monotonically toward equilibrium, whereas short-chain acids display pronounced non-monotonic behavior, consistent with initial interfacial activity followed by depletion through organic-toaqueous transfer and dissociation in water. Our framework, which explicitly couples partitioning (logP) and dissociation (pKa) parameters, quantitatively predicts the time-dependent interfacial tension, including non-monotonic behavior driven by mass transfer, and the corresponding pH control of the aqueous phase. The model predicts interfacial-tension dynamics and captures the pH switching gate at which the system switches from oil-favored to water-favored behavior. We validate these predictions across concentrations, pHs, and chain lengths, as well as in weak bases (decylamine). This work transforms the design of responsive liquid-liquid interfaces from empirical trial-and-error to a predictive, thermodynamically guided approach, in which pH and molecular structure (pKa and logP) serve as explicit design levers to control interfacial energy and dynamics.

papers.title: Atomically Precise Bismuth Oxido Nanoclusters as Hosts for Ln3+: Effects of Doping on Optical and Magnetic Properties of a Soluble Metal Oxide
papers.abstract: Lanthanide doping in bismuth-based oxides and coordination polymers is known to modify the materials properties significantly while preserving their principal structure. Herein we report a series of lanthanide doped bismuth oxido nanoclusters (BiO-NCs) of the type [Bi 38 O 45 (NO 3 ) 24 (dmso) y ]:Ln ( C-1:Ln ; Ln 3+ = La, Pr, Nd, Sm, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Tm, Yb, Lu; y = 26–28) including isostructural host and doped structures. The dopants are statistically distributed on the lattice position of Bi 3+ and changing the optical and magnetic properties of the BiO-NCs host material. Successful doping of the BiO-NCs was demonstrated by electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS) and exemplarily by single crystal X-ray diffraction (SC XRD) analysis for C-1:Gd and C-1:Dy . The respective amount of doping (≈ 1 ω %) was determined using inductive coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES). Altered optical properties in the UV–vis absorption and photoluminescence (PL) emission were demonstrated with special focus on C-1:Er , C-1:Yb and C-2 d :Dy . PL emission studies showed dual emission based on Bi 3+ and the Ln 3+ specific emissions, resulting in characteristic emission combinations over a wide wavelength range from visible to the NIR region. Starting from C-1:Gd and C-1:Dy the methacrylate substituted BiO-NCs [Bi 38 O 45 (OMc) 24 (EtOH) 14 ]:Gd ( C-2 E :Dy ) and [Bi 38 O 45 (OMc) 24 (EtOH) 14 ]:Dy ( C-2 E :Dy ) were synthesized to finally give solvent-free [Bi 38 O 45 (OMc) 24 ]:Ln ( C-2 d :Gd, C-2 d :Dy ) after drying. The introduction of paramagnetic behavior in the BiO-NC diamagnetic host structure was confirmed by superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) measurements, with molar susceptibilities of χ mol T = 5.10 cm 3 ·K·mol –1 for C-2 d :Gd and χ mol T = 10.00 cm 3 ·K·mol –1 for C-2 d :Dy . The core composition aligns well with the data obtained by ICP-OES analysis. We further investigated the suitability of Gd 3+ in C‑2 d :Gd as polarization agent (PA) for dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP)-enhanced magic-angle spinning nuclear magnetic resonance (MAS-NMR) experiments, which resulted in a proton enhancement of approximately 10.

papers.title: Excited-State Proton Transfer in Solution under Vibrational Strong Coupling
papers.abstract: Proton transfer reactions are ubiquitous in chemistry and biology. Here we explore the consequences of vibrational strong coupling (VSC) on excited state proton transfer in solution. The rates of proton transfer as well as the internal dynamics and quantum yields are significantly modified when the solvent and the photoacid are coupled cooperatively. These findings confirm that VSC can act on excited state reactivity and not just on ground state processes reported so far.

papers.title: Photochemistry of the Energy-Storing Isomer of a Norbornadiene-Based Molecular Switch: Ring Opening, Rehybridized Intramolecular Charge Transfer, and Isomerization into a Carbene Photoproduct
papers.abstract: Photoswitches based on the norbornadiene-quadricyclane (NBD-QC) isomer pair capture solar energy by undergoing the NBD→QC photoisomerization reaction. The energy-storing QC isomer contains two highly strained three-membered rings, which implies that it may be susceptible to photodegradation through exposure to the ultraviolet (UV) component of sunlight. In the present study, we use nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the UV-induced photochemistry of the QC isomer of a representative NBD-QC photoswitch with a push-pull substitution motif. A pattern recognition algorithm is employed to analyze and systematize the simulation results. We find that the predominant outcome of UV absorption, observed in 75 out of the 100 simulated trajectories, is the opening of the four-membered ring which belongs to the QC moiety, although in about half of the trajectories which follow this relaxation pathway, the ring promptly closes again. However, in a small fraction of trajectories, the QC moiety instead breaks up, leading to the formation of a carbene photoproduct. We hypothesize that that the breakup of the QC moiety is the first step in a reaction pathway which leads to the decomposition of the photoswitch.

papers.title: Probing the Role of Copper Dislocation Density in Electrochemical CO2 Conversion
papers.abstract: The electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) is a promising pathway for sustainable carbon utilization with the potential to produce valuable multi-carbon (C2+) products, including platform chemicals, like ethanol and ethylene, to replace fossil-fuel-derived sources. While structural defects on catalysts, such as dislocations, have been linked to enhanced CO2RR activity, a deep understanding of the connection between defect structure and selectivity remains elusive. In this work, we directly observe the relationship between dislocation density, catalytic activity, and selectivity in CO2RR on Cu. To investigate this, we synthesized (100)-oriented Cu thin films with systematically controlled dislocation densities spanning a ninefold range (6.40 × 10-14 m-2 to 58.56 × 10-14 m-2), measured over the bulk catalyst via X-ray diffraction θ/2θ scans. Dislocation densities were quantified via the Scherrer equation in combination with Le Bail full profile decomposition. In our carefully controlled thin-film samples, the CO2RR and C2 partial current densities did not increase with dislocation density under H-cell testing conditions, indicative of a null result. Overall, we suggest that these findings clarify that higher dislocation density alone does not guarantee greater C2+ activity or selectivity on copper. Our findings suggest that C2+ production may depend on the combination of copper defect structure together with other factors, such as local microenvironment conditions or specific active-site features, which together influence C2+ selectivity. These insights clarify to what extent lattice dislocations alone can influence reaction pathways, resolve discrepancies in the existing literature, and guide the design of CO2RR systems to produce desirable C2+ products.

papers.title: Solid-state Luminescence Intermittency Unlocks in situ Label-free Super-Resolution Imaging of Supramolecular Fiber Growth
papers.abstract: Understanding how supramolecular structures grow requires imaging methods that combine nanometer-scale resolution with real-time operation under native conditions, yet super-resolution microscopy typically relies on extrinsic dyes that may perturb assembly pathways. Here, we show that supramolecular fibers from a saccharide-derived benzaldehyde (SachCHO) exhibit both Solid-state Luminescence Enhancement (SLE) and Solid-state Luminescence Intermittency (SLI), enabling label-free stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy (STORM). Crucially, the SLI is not imparted by external labelling but is fundamentally linked to the assembly process itself, localizing at structural defects within the fibers via a defect-mediated redox-blinking mechanism. Using SLI-STORM, we visualize fiber self-assembly with ~25 nm resolution and identify these defects as hotspots of heterogeneous growth, revealing intermittent elongation and non-classical kinetic growth regimes. Analogous behavior in amyloid fibrils suggests this phenomenon is general. By leveraging the material's own photo-physics/chemistry, SLI-STORM transforms the assembling structure into its own dynamic reporter, offering a minimally invasive strategy to probe growth and defect formation in both synthetic and biological supramolecular materials.

papers.title: An intramolecular frustrated Lewis-Pair based on a bismuth(III) acid site
papers.abstract: An FLP is reported that makes use of a Lewis acidic bismuth(III) site. Lewis acidity is generated by the substitution of the two chloride ligands in ((Ph2P)C6H4)BiCl2(THF) against triflate ligands, which due to their internal polarisation bind predominantly in an ionic way. DFT calculations show that in contrast to simpler substituents like halides, that are bound in a more covalent way, this leads to acceptor orbitals with predominant Bi(6p) character that undergo strong interaction with the phosphine donor function. For this the linker unit has to distort, however. Accordingly, ((Ph2P)C6H4)Bi(OTf)2(THF) is capable of binding/converting substrates in an FLP type manner. It abstracts an S atom from Ph-NCS to yield ((Ph2PS)C6H4)Bi(OTf)2 and Ph-NC. Ph-NC in turn is bound as a 1,1 adduct complex.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Guided Discovery and Free Energy Validation of Genotype-Selective NOD2 Binders for the R702W Crohn's Disease Variant
papers.abstract: Crohn's disease affects over 3 million individuals globally, yet no approved therapy directly targets NOD2, the gene most strongly associated with disease susceptibility. The R702W missense variant (rs2066844), carried by 4-11% of patients, confers a 2.2-2.4-fold increase in disease risk, but its impact on drug binding remains unexplored. Here we report a seven-stage computational pipeline that screens 9,566 compounds from the eDrug3D (n = 2,152) and COCONUT (n = 7,414) libraries against the AlphaFold2-predicted NOD2 leucine-rich repeat domain. GNINA CNN docking retained 2,129 compounds, which were re-ranked by NOD2-Scout, an XGBoost consensus re-scoring classifier (held-out test AUROC = 0.901; scaffold cross-validation AUROC = 0.890 +/-0.03). Following ADMET filtering, eight Tier-1 compounds were identified; three Tier-1 compounds, one Tier-2 natural product, and one negative control were selected for molecular dynamics (520 ns; OpenMM/AMBER14/OpenFF-2.1.0). Absolute binding free energies via free energy perturbation (120 lambda windows; MBAR) identified two distinct candidates: Febuxostat (FDAapproved; delta-Gbind,WT =-2.77 +/-0.64 kcal/mol) and Bufadienolide/CID 10120 (natural product; delta-Gbind,WT =-7.67 +/-0.26 kcal/mol). The R702W mutation exerted opposite effects: Febuxostat binding weakened significantly (delta-delta-G = +2.34 +/-0.26 kcal/mol; 9.0σ, p < 0.001), whereas Bufadienolide binding showed no statistically significant change (delta-delta-G =-0.44 +/-0.37 kcal/mol; 1.2σ, not significant). This differential mutation sensitivity, invisible to conventional docking, demonstrates the necessity of free energy methods. These computational hypotheses illustrate how genotype-stratified compound triage could inform future Crohn's drug discovery: Febuxostat serves as a proof-of-concept for mutation-sensitive binding, while the Bufadienolide chemotype identifies a mutation-insensitive scaffold class. Both compounds are computationally prioritized tool compounds requiring extensive experimental validation and medicinal chemistry optimization before any therapeutic application; Bufadienolide carries significant cardiac glycoside toxicity liability, and Febuxostat's primary xanthine oxidase activity precludes straightforward repurposing.

papers.title: An LLM-Driven Pipeline for Automated Quantitative Drug-Target Interaction Data Extraction and Curation from Biomedical Literature
papers.abstract: The accurate understanding of quantitative drug-target interactions (DTIs) is crucial for modern drug discovery, yet a vast amount of essential affinity data (IC 50 , K i , K d , EC 50) remains embedded within unstructured biomedical literature, leading to sparse and biased datasets for machine learning models. To overcome this challenge, we introduce PharmExtract, an automated, endto-end pipeline leveraging large language models (LLMs), optical character recognition (OCR), and advanced table parsing to systematically extract, standardize, and curate high-quality quantitative DTI data. Processing hundreds of thousands of full-text articles, PharmExtract yields a comprehensive collection of unique DTI entries after rigorous quality control, notably including a significant proportion of novel data absent from existing databases. Our evaluation demonstrates PharmExtract achieves significantly higher extraction accuracy and precision compared to baseline methods. Furthermore, retraining established DTI prediction models (GraphDTA, DeepDTA, MolTrans) with PharmExtractDB consistently demonstrates substantial performance improvements. These results highlight PharmExtractDB's transformative potential in providing enriched, high-quality DTI data, thereby accelerating the development of more accurate DTI prediction models and advancing computational drug discovery.

papers.title: Cyclo-Polyproline: Chameleonic All-Peptide Macrocycles with Induced-Fit Host-Guest Recognition
papers.abstract: We report the design, synthesis and characterization of a novel class of allpeptide macrocycle, Cyclo-Polyprolines (CP). Exploiting the precision of Fmocbased solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS) and head-to-tail macrocyclization, this platform grants unparalleled control over the macrocycle's primary sequence and secondary structure, offering a viable route towards exo-/endo-functionalization and addressing a bottleneck of traditional synthetic host macrocycles. The resulting CP scaffold is highly amphiphilic, exhibiting excellent solubility in both organic and aqueous media. Structural analysis via NMR spectroscopy and single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals a distinct chameleonic character: the macrocycle shifts from an all-cis conformation in organic solvents to a predominantly all-trans isomer in water. We demonstrate that this transition is driven by a cooperative hydration effect, wherein water molecules stabilize the expanded framework through precise two-point hydrogen bonding. Demonstrating responsive host-guest capabilities, CP undergoes induced-fit isomerization to bind ligands, successfully forming, among other species, an all-peptide pseudo-rotaxane. This methodology establishes a robust platform for creating functionalized, proline-based hosts with significant potential in medicinal chemistry, drug delivery, and organocatalysis, thereby bridging the gap between supramolecular systems and enzyme mimetics.

papers.title: Development of log P and log D models using a hierarchical linear regression approach
papers.abstract: We present a hierarchical linear regression approach for the prediction of log P and log D, two key physicochemical properties in drug discovery. Molecular structures are described using radial substructure fragments of increasing complexity derived from Morgan count vectors, organized into three layers of features corresponding to radii of 0, 1, and 2. Starting with the simplest layer, a series of Bayesian ridge regression models are trained sequentially, where each successive model corrects the residuals of the previous one. The final prediction is obtained by summing the predictions of all three models. The final models employ approximately 1000 features in total and are trained on datasets of about 40,000 log P and 50,000 log D values compiled from public sources. Model performance was assessed by 5-fold cross-validation, yielding MAE of 0.35 and RMSE of 0.55 for log P, and MAE of 0.47 and RMSE of 0.69 for log D, which is competitive with results reported in the literature. External validation on two independent OpenADMET datasets confirmed that the model generalizes well to new data, while also demonstrating that retraining with even a small number of novel chemotypes can substantially improve performance on structurally distinct compound series. The hierarchical design, combined with the use of linear models, results in an interpretable and computationally lightweight approach suitable for deployment in browser-based applications via WebAssembly.

papers.title: Composition-Dependent Li-Ion Transport in Mixed-Metal ZIF-62 Glasses Revealed by Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: Understanding ion transport in metal-organic frameworks requires resolving the interplay between framework dynamics, local disorder, and thermally activated hopping on extended time and length scales. Here, we develop a robust deep neural network (DNN) interatomic potential, trained and validated against density functional theory data using the DP-GEN framework, to investigate Li-ion transport in pure and mixed-metal ZIF-62 across a wide range of Co/(Co+Zn) ratios. Large-scale deep potential molecular dynamics simulations at 450 K reveal that Li-ion motion is governed by localized vibrational dynamics within metastable cages, punctuated by activated hopping events through the interconnected pore network. Van Hove correlation analysis reveals that intermediate metal substitution [Co/(Co+Zn) ≈0.25-0.50] optimizes the spatial extent of Li displacements while maintaining a stable local coordination environment. Jump-resolved analysis further demonstrates that the 0.50-ZIF-62 composition exhibits the lowest effective activation energy (∼0.093 eV) and the highest ionic conductivity (∼6.0 ×10 −3 S cm −1), arising from a dynamically evolving, composition-dependent energy landscape. Correlated-motion analysis indicates that long-range diffusion proceeds predominantly via independent hopping rather than sustained collective migration. Together, these results establish a unified and dynamic picture of Li-ion transport in mixed-metal MOF electrolytes, demonstrating the predictive capability of machine-learning interatomic potentials for the rational design of highconductivity solid-state ion conductors.

papers.title: Vibrational Power Spectra as a Tool to Benchmark Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials for Molecular Systems: The OMOL-1k-MD Data Set
papers.abstract: We present OMOL-1k-MD, a new data set for the benchmark and training of universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs). It contains three independent ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) trajectories of 10 ps each for 1000 arbitrarily chosen neutral closed shell molecular systems from the OMOL25 dataset, calculated at the PBE level of theory at 300 K. In contrast to most other MLIP training or benchmark data sets, which are predominantly focused on local minimum structures or geometry optimization trajectories, OMOL-1k-MD contains a total of 30 million structures sampled from all parts of the potential energy surface that are accessible at room temperature. In this paper, we use the new data set to benchmark several popular uMLIPs towards their ability to reasonably reproduce the DFT dynamics. To this end, we compare vibrational power spectra of the OMOL-1k-MD trajectories, obtained from the velocity autocorrelation function, with uMLIP trajectories for the same set 1 of 1000 molecular structures. The comparison can be done in detail by looking at the relative positions of different vibrations, or cumulatively by calculating vibrational free energies, obtained by integrating the power spectra. This procedure enables a thorough benchmark and ranking of uMLIP performances apart from local minima. We found that the MACE MP-0 uMLIP performed best, followed by SevenNet and Orb OMat. The physics-based GFN2-xTB semiempirical method, however, performed better than all tested uMLIPs.

papers.title: Non-equilibrium Relaxation in Water No Man's Land
papers.abstract: Determining how supercooled water relaxes in the deeply metastable regime remains a central challenge in liquid-state physics, because direct equilibrium measurements are experimentally inaccessible in the temperature range known as no man's land. To probe this regime, experiments have turned to driven approaches that repeatedly perturb the liquid while avoiding crystallization, such as nanosecond pulsed-heating procedures (PHP). Here, we use molecular dynamics simulations of TIP4P/Ice water to investigate the relaxation kinetics probed by PHP and to clarify how the relaxation times extracted from PHP relate to intrinsic isothermal relaxation and equilibrium molecular diffusion. The simulations reproduce key experimental observations, including stretched-exponential relaxation, strong kinetic asymmetry between hyperquenched water and low-density amorphous ice, and the temperature dependence of relaxation across no man's land. We show that PHP-derived relaxation times are robust descriptors of collective structural reorganization but systematically decouple from equilibrium diffusion upon cooling. This decoupling arises because PHP probes a driven relaxation pathway characterized by smaller effective activation energies than those governing molecular mobility. Consequently, PHP relaxation times exhibit a shallower temperature dependence and do not provide a reliable proxy for equilibrium molecular diffusion.

papers.title: Targeting the RNA-binding Site of SARS-CoV-2 NSP13 by FRASE-bot in CACHE Challenge #2
papers.abstract: The Critical Assessment of Computational Hit-Finding Experiments (CACHE) Challenges came forward as real-world stress tests for virtual screening methods. In Challenge #2, the focus was on SARS-CoV-2 NSP13 helicase - the most conserved protein across Coronaviridae and a prime target for broad-spectrum antivirals. We brought in FRASE-based hit-finding robot (FRASE-bot), our fragment-based screening engine that delimits target-relevant chemical space and identifies likely binding sites. Guided by FRASE-bot, 79 compounds were selected over two rounds. Round 1 delivered four confirmed binders of NSP13 with dissociation constants between 11 and 61 μM. Round 2 pushed further: five analogs bound in the micromolar range, with compounds 8 and 9 (derived from the parent hit 2) showing clear gains over other CACHE participants. With successful runs in both CACHE #1 and #2, FRASE-bot is proving its ability to tackle tough protein targets. The identification of validated binders targeting the RNA-binding groove of SARS-CoV-2 NSP13 holds significant promise for antiviral drug discovery.

papers.title: Excited state anti-homoaromaticity
papers.abstract: Homoaromatic molecules bear an interrupted π system, yet behave as well-known aromatic compounds in the ground state. However, the photophysical properties of homoaromatics are largely unknown despite their substantial potential for molecular optoelectronic materials. This report features a series of fluorescent, structurally adaptable neutral homoaromatic molecules with Stokes shifts up to 247 nm; their inherent structural flexibility enables excited-state molecular changes upon irradiation. Our experiment-theory approach identifies an anti-homoaromatic excited, which provides the missing analogy of aromatic and homoaromatic molecules' behavior in the excited state. We show that facile synthetic modification of the homoaromatic π system allows for significant structural changes in the excited state, leading to large Stokes shifts upon systematic variation in a library approach. The luminescence behavior is corroborated by multiconfigurational quantum mechanical calculations' analysis of the complete homoannulene library. This study advances arylated homoannulenes as structurally and mechanistically unique novel building blocks with direct applications in molecular optoelectronics.

papers.title: High-Throughput Experimentation on Oxide Photocatalyst: From Large-Scale Screening to Kinetic Insights
A minimal machine-learning correction of DFTB Mulliken charges towards DFT-level MBIS populations
papers.abstract: Density-functional tight binding (DFTB) enables efficient quantum-based simulations for large molecular systems, but atomic charges are typically reported via Mulliken population analysis and often deviate from density-based charge definitions at the density functional theory (DFT) level. Minimal basis iterative stockholder (MBIS) charges are attractive due to numerical stability and reduced basis-set sensitivity, yet MBIS is not available in standard DFTB workflows due to the lack of an explicit real-space electron density. Here we develop a minimal, physics-informed machine-learning (ML) correction that maps DFTB Mulliken charges to DFT reference MBIS charges at the atom-wise level. The model uses only atomic identity, DFTB Mulliken charge, and inexpensive local-geometry descriptors derived from the molecular structure, while enforcing exact molecular charge conservation at inference by a per-molecule shift. Using 5000 molecules from the QM9 database split into 4000/500/500 for training, validation, and testing, we show that nonlinearity alone provides limited improvement over an element-wise linear baseline, whereas incorporating local geometric descriptors yields a substantial accuracy gain, particularly for carbon and nitrogen. The proposed correction provides DFT-level charge quality at a computational cost comparable to standard DFTB calculations and can be readily integrated into existing DFTB-based workflows.

papers.title: Food Informatics: Leveraging Data and Knowledge to Advance Food Systems
papers.abstract: The term Food Informatics has been increasingly used in scientific literature to describe the growing use of data-driven and computational approaches in food research. However, its definition and scope remain inconsistent across disciplines. This lack of conceptual clarity limits cumulative knowledge building and hinders the development of Food Informatics as a coherent interdisciplinary field. In this commentary, we review current definitions of Food Informatics and propose an updated definition with a clearer scope, aiming to provide a conceptual foundation for leveraging data, knowledge, and methods across food systems.

papers.title: Revisiting a Common Cobalt Chloride Equilibrium Experiment with Generative Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: We have developed and implemented a first-year undergraduate laboratory experiment at St. Bonaventure University that augments a well-established thermodynamics lab on the spectrophotometric determination of the equilibrium of cobalt(II) chloride hexahydrate with generative artificial intelligence (GenAI). Students utilized free ChatGPT accounts as a support tool in their analysis of laboratory data and iteratively refined their answers to chemical questions. Overall, the inclusion of GenAI in student workflow did not appear to negatively impact student performance, but there were instances where it struggled to produce correct answers for tasks. Descriptive analysis of student responses, chat logs, and instructor discussions suggests that students were resilient to incorrect GenAI output. This laboratory experiment is designed such that it can be easily adopted by faculty with an interest in exploring the use of GenAI in chemistry curricula.

papers.title: Lysine-Tolerant N-Terminal Amidination of UnprotectedPeptides
papers.abstract: Selective and late-stage modification of the N-terminus of unprotected peptides remains challenging due to competition from lysine ε-amines. Herein, we report a chlorooxime-mediated N-terminal amidination that provides a general and lysine- tolerant platform for peptide engineering. Operating under physiological conditions, this strategy enables efficient late-stage functionalization of complex unprotected peptides and peptide therapeutics and is extended to macrocyclization and protein labeling. We further identify an unexpected amidine-induced, site-specific amide bond cleavage that reveals previously unrecognized reactivity. These findings establish chlorooxime chemistry as a versatile platform for the structural manipulation of bioactive peptides.

papers.title: Molecule by Molecule Characterization of a Polymer Molecular Mass Distribution via Mass Photometry
papers.abstract: Polymer analysis tools form the backbone of modern polymer technology. However, traditional tools like size exclusion chromatography (SEC) fractionate based on hydrodynamic volume. This analysis assumes all molecules in a fraction are identical, an increasingly strained assumption for complex macromolecules. Importantly, characterization of the molecular mass distribution (MMD) is typically reduced to reporting several moments of the MMD, like number and weight-averaged molecular masses, a significant loss of information. In contrast, a molecule-by-molecule elucidation of the full MMD would yield an extremely informative new perspective on macromolecule diversity, while eliminating limitations and time commitment associated with fractionation. Here, we show that mass photometry (MP), whereby the interferometric scattering signal of individual molecules is correlated with mass, of high-molecular weight polyethylene oxide (PEO) allows elucidation of the full MMD. In some cases, multiple subpopulations are directly revealed. This effort provides the first single-molecule measurement of the MMD of a synthetic polymer, bypassing artifacts introduced by bulk-scale measurements. Further, we show that Dispersity (Đ) can be precisely determined in a manner that is largely calibration-free, allowing determination of Đ in functional polymers where monodisperse standards are unavailable. Integration of MP with SEC conspicuously shows how multiple populations are present in collected fractions.

papers.title: Multireference Methods for Chemistry and Materials Science: Automated Active Spaces, Efficient Dynamic Correlation, and Extended Systems
papers.abstract: While multiconfigurational approaches have long been relegated to expert practitioners working on a case-by-case basis, recent developments have increasingly made these methods more routine and applicable to broader sets of systems. This perspective outlines the state-of-the-art in multiconfigurational approaches, with an emphasis on moving from delicate hand-selected pathways through configuration space towards more robust and efficient approaches to treating a host of challenging chemical systems accurately. First, we overview recent work in automated active-space selection, which has enabled increasingly large-scale applications of multireference methods to modeling vertical excitations and reactivity. Second, we highlight the increasingly efficient methods for recovering correlation energy beyond the active space, as headlined by extensions of pair-density functional theory and its role in accurate and efficient treatment of excited-state dynamics and its utilization to train machine-learned potentials. Finally, we highlight recent efforts to treat extended systems that until recently have lied beyond the traditional limits of active-space methods, giving center stage to product-form wave functions of the localized active space family of methods that allow for the computation of multiconfigurational band structures. These recent advancements point to a broader use of multireference approaches for high-impact chemical and materials science applications.

papers.title: ChainSpace: Sequence-Aware Design for Machine Learning-Driven Polymer Engineering
papers.abstract: Sequence is the critical determinant of macromolecular function, yet current polymer design approaches often optimize monomer composition and ratios while ignoring sequence. This creates poorly defined design spaces for active learning that miss the vast combinatorial landscape of sequence possibilities. We introduce ChainSpace, a computational framework that maps synthetically accessible sequence space through four orthogonal control mechanisms: compositional (random copolymerization), kinetic (relative reactivity differences), temporal (staged monomer injection), and spatial (post-polymerization functionalization). Using three orthogonal descriptors (second eigenvalue λ₂, Shannon entropy, and mean run length), we characterize sequence statistics across experimentally achievable synthesis conditions. Parameter space exploration reveals that accessible sequences form a curved three-dimensional manifold with distinct regions accessed by different synthesis strategies. Kinetic control provides the broadest sequence access, temporal control enables highly blocky architectures, and spatial control favors alternating motifs. We demonstrate this framework using cationic polymers for gene delivery, where sequence statistics correlate with transfection efficiency and salt resistance. A top-performing, multi-component gene delivery polymer achieved 85% transfection efficiency, with sequence analysis revealing optimal blockiness and entropy values. This sequence-centric approach provides a systematic foundation for active learning design spaces, enabling rational navigation of sequence space that is especially useful for the advancement of multimonomeric polymers for industrially relevant end-use technologies.

papers.title: Deciphering Infrared Difference Spectra of Bovine Rhodopsin in the Amide I Region by Localized Anharmonic Vibrational Calculations
papers.abstract: Vibrational quasi-degenerate perturbation theory (VQDPT2) based on localized vibrational modes is combined with quantum mechanics / molecular mechanics (QM/MM) calculations to investigate the amide bands of bovine rhodopsin in dark (inactive) and Meta II (active) states. The total vibrational spectrum is reconstructed by partitioning the protein into individual amide-group subsystems. Our approach reproduces the experimental IR difference spectrum upon photoactivation across the amide I, II, and III regions, demonstrating the importance of accounting for anharmonicity. Detailed analysis has revealed that the amide I band signals are not localized to a single domain; rather, the higher-wavenumber shifts are primarily driven by helical regions, while lower-wavenumber shifts stem from loop regions. We identified specific residues, such as Thr118 and Trp265, whose significant frequency shifts are coupled with local structural rearrangements. This subsystem-based anharmonic vibrational approach provides a powerful tool for the microscopic interpretation of vibrational spectra in large biomolecular systems.

papers.title: Morphology-Controlled Silica Nanoparticle Coatings for Transparent Radiative Cooling
Formalizing structure-property relationships of highly-oxidizing and weakly-reducing organic cyanoarene photocatalysts
papers.abstract: This study investigates three new highly-oxidizing cyanoarene photocatalysts with modulated donors and acceptors via electrochemical and photophysical characterization. Comparing with previous reports, we determined the chlorinated acceptor shortens delayed fluorescent lifetimes and increases the excitedstate oxidation potential. Electron-deficient donors both weaken reduction and strengthen oxidation, which contradicts established design principles.

papers.title: Flow synthesis of C2-alkylated indoline enabled by convergent cation-anion direct reaction
papers.abstract: The synthesis of C2-alkylated indolines through the acidic activation of indoles is challenging owing to the instability of reac-tive species under reaction conditions. To address this problem, a flow microreactor (FMR) was utilized to handle highly un-stable reactive species, enabling instantaneous Csp3–Csp3 bond formation. Taking advantage of reaction integration in FMR sys-tems, we also achieved the rapid introduction of functional alkyl substituents using alkyllithium species generated via reductive lithiation.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Multi-Output Machine Learning for Predicting Nanozyme Kinetic Parameters
papers.abstract: Nanozymes-artificial nanomaterials with enzyme-like catalytic properties-offer superior durability compared to natural enzymes, enabling broad applications in biosensing and therapeutics. However, their rational design remains challenging due to immense structural heterogeneity and a reliance on trial-and-error. While machine learning (ML) accelerates materials discovery, conventional models often lack physicochemical grounding. We present a multi-output, physics-informed ML framework for predicting the core catalytic kinetics (Km, kcat, Vmax) of nanozymes. Using a curated dataset from NanozymeDB, we integrated the Arrhenius equation (activity-specific activation energies), pH-dependent Gaussian zones, and material properties (electronegativity, redox potential). Our model achieves robust predictive performance: R² = 0.555 for Km, 0.319 for kcat, and 0.524 for Vmax, with 55.6 of Vmax predictions falling within a factor of two of experimental values. Feature importance analysis confirmed that the Arrhenius factor (importance = 0.228) and pH zones (0.30 combined) dominate predictions, validating the physics-informed approach. This demonstrates that embedding thermodynamic constraints into ML enhances both predictive reliability and interpretability for rational nanozyme design.

papers.title: Advanced Carbon dioxide Valorization Using Samarium-Stabilized Aluminium Catalytic Frameworks in Continuous Flow Packed-Bed Reactors
papers.abstract: This work demonstrates the catalytic conversion of carbon dioxide (CO 2) to methane and methanol over samarium-doped alumina (Sm-Al 2 O 3 ) supported nickel catalysts in a continuous packed-bed reactor and establishes structure-performance correlations through complementary characterization and multi-modal performance measurements. Catalysts with varied Sm loadings were synthesized on high-surface-area alumina and evaluated using FTIR, XPS, XRD, BET, SEM, and EDX. FTIR confirmed surface hydroxyls and Sm-O moieties that promote CO 2 adsorption; XPS verified Sm 3+ as the dominant surface species; XRD revealed distinct NiO, Al 2 O 3, and Sm 2 O 3 phases; and BET/SEM showed that moderate Sm retains porosity and dispersion while excessive Sm induces agglomeration and pore coverage. EDX indicated uniform Ni/Sm distribution at moderate loading with segregation at higher Sm.

papers.title: Synergistic Magnetic, Piezoelectric, and Chiral Optical Effects in Fe-and Mn-Hybrid Metal Halides
Coupling Nanoscale Viscoelastic Measurements and Infrared Heating of Polymers with AFM-IR
papers.abstract: In heterogeneous polymer systems, the viscoelastic response of polymers around interfaces or with nanostructured morphology may deviate from bulk values. However, current measurement techniques tend to mask these local variations, which are crucial for understanding and developing these materials. Coupling the high spatial resolution of atomic force microscopy (AFM) with dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) offers an avenue to circumvent this limitation. We previously demonstrated the advantages of using a focused infrared (IR) laser on an AFM-IR system to locally heat a sample during nanomechanical measurements, with heating modulated by varying the IR repetition rate. [1] Herein, we present a brief demonstration of coupling nDMA with our previously demonstrated chemistry-selective IR heating. We first measured the storage and loss modulus of poly(propylene glycol) (PPG)-4,4′-methylenebis(phenyl urea) (MPU) at varying IR repetition rates, demonstrating a viscoelastic modulus response with typical heating characteristics upon crossing the glass transition temperature. We further demonstrated stress relaxation of an enaminelinked vitrimer possessing significant bond dynamicity at elevated temperatures. Overall, this method is in the preliminary stages of development, and this working paper aims to serve as a basis for feedback and discussion.

papers.title: A triangulenum-based biosensor platform for mapping kinase activity in T cells
papers.abstract: Monitoring protein kinases in their native environment is essential for understanding cellular signaling. This study introduces triangulenium-based peptide biosensors for the real-time detection of the activity of two key protein kinases involved in the T cell immune response: Akt1 and Src. The substrate biosensors incorporate a long-lifetime fluorophore from the triangulenium dye family, which undergoes photoinduced electron transfer (PET) quenching. Upon kinase-mediated phosphorylation, PET is suppressed, resulting in a significant "turn-on" of both fluorescence intensity and fluorescence lifetime (τ FL ). This lifetime extension (up to 15 ns) enables the use of fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) and time-gated filtering to effectively eliminate cellular autofluorescence. In vitro and in extracto assays confirmed the biosensors' high affinity and specificity for endogenous kinases. Furthermore, in cellulo FLIM experiments demonstrated efficient uptake, biocompatibility, and the ability to quantitatively report endogenous Src and Akt1 activities through robust, lifetime-based responses selectively modulated by kinase activators and inhibitors. Crucially, the Akt1 biosensor was successfully applied to isolated primary T cells, where it tracked dynamic signaling changes following T cell receptor (TCR) stimulation using confocal microscopy and flow cytometry. This integrated framework provides a robust, non-invasive platform for quantitative kinase analysis in living cells, with significant implications for immunological profiling and cancer research.
