papers.title: Geometric Encoding of Cyclic Mechanical Fatigue in Model Glasses: Graph Neural Networks as Structural Probes for Battery-Relevant Degradation
papers.abstract: Solid-state battery glass electrolytes degrade under repeated charge and discharge cycling, yet the atomic-scale structural changes underlying this fatigue remain poorly characterised. Here we investigate whether cyclic mechanical fatigue-simulated as oscillatory volumetric strain applied to a Lennard-Jones model glass-encodes a learnable geometric signature detectable by graph neural networks (GNNs). Using a GATv2 architecture and a systematic four-way ablation study, we find that classification between pristine (cycle 0) and heavily fatigued (cycles 300-400) glasses reaches 91.67 ± 4.22% accuracy using 8-dimensional bond-length statistics as node features, rising to 98.33 ± 1.49% (AUC = 0.9975 ± 0.0022) when per-sample instance normalisation is applied. The improvement under normalisation-which explicitly removes all global magnitude information-establishes that the discriminative signal resides in the relational geometry of local bond networks, not in trivial density or volume changes. Ablating distribution-shape features (skewness, quartiles) reduces accuracy by 5.3 percentage points and collapses cycle-number regression to near-random performance (R 2 = 0.006), confirming that asymmetric bond-length damage is the dominant structural fingerprint of fatigue. Continuous degradation tracking via regression achieves R 2 = 0.311 ± 0.039 under instance normalisation, with all five cross-validation folds converging to R 2 ≈ 0.28-0.32 given extended training. Structural analysis reveals that fatigue accumulates as monotonically increasing bond-length disorder that saturates around cycle 300, consistent with a metastable fatigued equilibrium. These findings extend the geometric-encoding framework established for thermal history to mechanical cycling history, and provide a methodological foundation for applying GNN-based structural probes to experimentally characterised solid electrolyte fatigue.

papers.title: Optically Active Yb3+ Spin Defects in Cerium Oxide Nanocrystals
papers.abstract: Nanocrystalline CeO 2 is a chemically tunable wide-bandgap host lattice of interest for quantum information technologies due to its ability to accommodate optically-and spin-active defects. Here, we investigate CeO 2 nanocrystals as hosts for near-infrared-compatible Yb 3+ ions as optically active spin quantum bits (qubits). We characterize the as-synthesized Yb 3+ -doped CeO 2 nanocrystals (0.01-10% Yb) by photoluminescence, which reveals short photoluminescence lifetimes dominated by non-radiative decay arising from surface and Ce 3+ -related defects. Thermal annealing at 700 °C increases crystalline domain sizes (from ~7 nm to ~20 nm) and reduces the concentration of Ce 3+ defects, yielding an enhancement in excited-state lifetimes. Low-temperature optical spectroscopy reveals at least two distinct Yb 3+ lattice sites with cubic and trigonal symmetries, and a ~5-fold difference in photoluminescence lifetimes between the two sites. Continuous-wave EPR measurements support these site assignments, while pulse EPR measurements further show that annealing the nanocrystals nearly doubles the spin-lattice relaxation time ( T 1 ) from 33.9 to 62.7 µs at 0.08% Yb. Phase memory times, however, remain relatively constant, indicating that coherence is limited by dephasing mechanisms (e.g., slowly fluctuating local fields or spectral diffusion) rather than by spin-lattice relaxation. Collectively, these results establish defect mitigation, rather than dopant identity alone, as a bottleneck in realizing nanocrystalline CeO 2 as a viable quantum host. This work provides quantitative benchmarks for optical and spin coherence in CeO 2 :Yb 3+ nanocrystals and highlights defect engineering as a critical pathway toward scalable rare-earth-based qubits.

papers.title: Tree Tensor Network Approach to Transport in Heavily-Doped Organic Materials with Coexisting Electron Correlation and Electron-Phonon Coupling
papers.abstract: Heavy doping in organic materials induces complex many-body interactions characterized by the coexistence of strong electron correlation and electron-phonon coupling, arising from their soft structures and low dielectric constants. Simulating charge transport and thermopower in this regime poses a significant computational challenge. In this work, we propose a finite-temperature time-dependent tree tensor network state (TTNS) method to calculate the conductivity and Seebeck coefficient of organic materials modeled by the Holstein-Hubbard Hamiltonian. Our TTNS ansatz features a tailored “bus-branch” structure, where the “bus” captures the electronic entanglement, and the “branches” encode the local electron-phonon correlations. Benchmarks against exact diagonalization (ED) on small clusters demonstrate that this network structure achieves numerically exact results with smaller bond dimensions than the Matrix Product States (MPS). Furthermore, the “branch” topology efficiently isolates the local electron-phonon entanglement, thereby avoiding the globally large bond dimensions required by MPS. These algorithmic advantages enable us to constrain the relative error of transport properties to within 10% across a wide range of parameter regimes. To validate the capability of this framework, we study the complex interplay between Hubbard repulsion and phonon-mediated attraction, successfully illustrating the roles of spin degrees of freedom and effective interactions in thermodynamics and charge transport, and reproducing the correlation-induced anomalous sign change of the Seebeck coefficient. Our work establishes the “bus-branch” TTNS as a powerful and efficient tool for exploring quantum dynamics in strongly correlated electron-phonon systems.

papers.title: Exploiting Cross-Reactivity for Selective Chemotherapy Monitoring: A Differential Electrochemical Aptamer Approach
papers.abstract: Despite its widespread use, high-dose methotrexate (MTX) regimen presents a risk of lifethreatening nephrotoxicity. Consequently, rigorous monitoring of MTX levels at predefined time points is highly recommended to assess toxicity and guide dosing of rescue therapy such as glucarpidase. Upon administration, glucarpidase rapidly converts MTX into its inactive metabolite 2,4-diamino-N10-methylpteroic acid (DAMPA) which displays structural similarity to MTX, causing an overestimation of the actual MTX levels. Therefore, patients receiving glucarpidase necessitate analytical methods capable of specifically monitoring MTX concentrations to inform the need for further rescue treatment. However, existing point-of-care tools lack this selectivity, leaving clinicians reliant on time-consuming and lab-bound chromatographic assays for decisionmaking. Here, we introduce a differential electrochemical aptamer-based biosensor that enables simultaneous real-time monitoring of MTX and DAMPA concentrations after glucarpidase intervention by exploiting, rather than avoiding, aptamer cross-reactivity. DAMPA levels are directly reported by a DAMPA-specific aptamer, whereas MTX concentrations are inferred via a mathematical deconvolution of the cross-reactive aptamer signal. We anticipate that our work will advance point-of-care MTX monitoring during glucarpidase-assisted rescue therapy and support informed clinical decision-making in chemotherapy. More broadly, we envision this work will also establish a translational framework for leveraging cross-reactive biosensors to monitor drug metabolism in real time.

papers.title: MatForge: Meta-Adaptive Trial Framework for Optimization via Trajectory-Guided Experimentation
papers.abstract: Sequential optimization in the sciences operates under extreme budget constraints: each experiment may cost thousands of dollars and days of effort. Bayesian optimization (BO) is the dominant paradigm, yet its acquisition function-the policy that decides where to evaluate next-is typically fixed before any data is observed. We introduce MatForge, a framework that replaces the fixed acquisition function with an adaptive portfolio: four acquisition strategies (EI, Thompson Sampling, UCB, Knowledge Gradient) governed by a trajectory-aware selector that monitors incumbent improvement, surrogate calibration, and exploration coverage at every trial. On a benchmark of 22 problems across five scientific domains (2-25 dimensions, 20 seeds, 50 trials, 132,000 total function evaluations), MatForge reaches 75% of optimal performance in 5.1 trials-the strongest baseline, SAASBO, requires 12.0 (p < 0.001, Wilcoxon signedrank). Final solution quality at trial 50 shows no significant difference (NS 0.934 vs. 0.934, p = 0.72, Cohen's d = 0.008). The convergence advantage scales with dimensionality, growing from 11.5× faster than SAASBO at 6D to 20.9× at 25D. An ablation confirms that deterministic rule-based switching matches LLM-augmented switching (p = 0.97): the adaptive architecture, not domain knowledge, drives the gains. Across 70 pairwise statistical tests (14 metrics × 5 baselines), MatForge records 48 significant wins, 2 losses, and 20 non-significant results.

papers.title: A3M-CIR: An Attention-Aware Adversarial Masking Based Self-Supervised Chemometric Framework for Robust Infrared Spectral Analysis
papers.abstract: Infrared (IR) spectroscopy provides rich molecular fingerprint information and is widely used for qualitative and quantitative chemical analysis across biomedical, environmental, and materials science applications. However, its practical utilization is often constrained by instrument-dependent variability, baseline drift, acquisition noise, and limited labeled data. While deep-learning-based chemometric methods have improved performance over traditional preprocessing-driven pipelines, their reliance on supervised learning limits robustness and transferability across heterogeneous measurement conditions. To address these challenges, we introduce A 3 M-CIR, an attention-aware adversarial masking-based self-supervised chemometric framework for robust infrared spectral analysis. The framework performs large-scale self-supervised pretraining on diverse unlabeled IR spectra to learn transferable representations without explicit calibration or manual annotation. Its core component, the Attention-Aware Adversarial Feature Masking Block (A 3 FMB), suppresses diagnostically salient absorption regions to generate informative contrastive views that emulate realistic perturbations, while a lightweight Dual-Mixing Attention (DMA) encoder captures both global spectral context and local continuity of one-dimensional vibrational signals. Extensive evaluations under linear-probing and fine-tuning protocols demonstrate consistent improvements over representative self-supervised baselines, and systematic signalto-noise ratio analyses further validate robustness and transferability under varying noise conditions. By explicitly addressing spectral variability, measurement noise, and limited supervision as intrinsic challenges of infrared spectroscopy, this work establishes A 3 M-CIR as a practical and extensible foundation for datadriven infrared spectral analysis. Source code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/Ak7210/A3M-CIR.git.

papers.title: Understanding molecular excited states at the metal–molecule interface via transition density matrix analysis — A case study of azobenzene thiols on gold
papers.abstract: Noble metal nanoparticles are rapidly gaining popularity as novel catalytic platforms to influence chemical reactions in various ways. Despite an increasingly large number of studies, many key processes especially at the metal–molecule interface are fundamentally still not fully understood up to this day. Throughout this work, we present a systematic study targeting the molecular excited states of covalently linked azobenzenes (ABs) on gold via a combination of time-dependent density functional theory and tight-binding calculations with transition density matrix analysis. We find that the optically bright ππ* state is strongly resonant to close-lying local gold excitations, which leads to a splitting and red-shift of the ππ* state and increased UV/Vis absorption around the ππ* excitation energy. We show that these findings hold true across different AB isomers and demonstrate, how a systematic variation of the AB–gold distance leads to a gradual localization of the ππ* excitation. Moreover, we discuss how a direct electronic interaction between the AB and gold surface leads to the formation of delocalized hybrid states and investigate the exciton formation of AB dimers at the metal interface. Our results are carefully verified across a wide range of computational parameters including a large number of different density functionals, basis sets and gold clusters of varying form and size. The presented workflow is easily applicable to other functional molecules on metal surfaces to further broaden the understanding of substrate–surface interactions at the interface.

papers.title: Rational Design of Lipidated Glycolipid-based Coacervates for Sequestration of Macromolecules and Enveloped Viruses: Supramolecular Strategy for Antiviral Defence
papers.abstract: Molecular self-assembly offers a powerful route to engineer sophisticated materials that mimic biological compartmentalisation. Inspired by liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS), which drives the formation of cellular membraneless organelles, we rationally designed glycolipid-based coacervates by tuning the attractive and repulsive intermolecular interactions. The low molecular weight glycolipid-based amphiphile (MWGSD-A4) self-assembles into stable coacervate droplets in aqueous media at low micromolar concentrations and exhibit dynamic encapsulation capabilities of sequestering dyes, proteins, and drug-like molecules. Interestingly, the glycolipid-based coacervates function as "viral magnets" by efficient sequestration of influenza and lentiviruses. Mechanistically, the coacervates appears to mask the influenza hemagglutinin, thereby blocking viral attachment to host cell surface receptors, inhibiting hemagglutination and preventing the virus from entering host cells. These glycolipid-based coacervate represent a novel therapeutic paradigm utilising supramolecular phase separation to entrap and neutralise pathogenic viruses.

papers.title: Method for quantifying trifluoroacetic acid in peptides by 1 H -19 F NMR spectral correlation
papers.abstract: Widely used in peptide synthesis and purification, trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) can affect properties of corresponding salts, which are challenging to characterize without weighing samples. We report a rapid, non-destructive NMR method to quantify TFA without sample weighing by correlating 1 H and 19 F integrations using a fluorinated alcohol as internal references. A fluorinated dipeptide model was first used to benchmark HFIP and TFE as probes in D 2 O at different temperatures. Different 1 H integration strategies were studied for optimal analysis of TFA content. Correlation of 1 H and 19 F signal integration was subsequently applied on a set of linear and cyclic peptides possessing up to four potential positive charges. The method was shown to quantify effectively TFA offering utility for the assessment of peptide salt composition without sample destruction.

papers.title: Low frequency (THz) Raman Spectroscopy - A green and versatile method to probe polymorphism, isomerism and solvent-induced dynamics in Fe-based metal-organic frameworks
Excited state anti-homoaromaticity
papers.abstract: Homoaromatic molecules bear an interrupted π system, yet behave as well-known aromatic compounds in the ground state. However, the photophysical properties of homoaromatics are largely unknown despite their substantial potential for molecular optoelectronic materials. This report features a series of fluorescent, structurally adaptable neutral homoaromatic molecules with Stokes shifts up to 247 nm; their inherent structural flexibility enables excited-state molecular changes upon irradiation. Our experiment-theory approach identifies an anti-homoaromatic excited, which provides the missing analogy of aromatic and homoaromatic molecules' behavior in the excited state. We show that facile synthetic modification of the homoaromatic π system allows for significant structural changes in the excited state, leading to large Stokes shifts upon systematic variation in a library approach. The luminescence behavior is corroborated by multiconfigurational quantum mechanical calculations' analysis of the complete homoannulene library. This study advances arylated homoannulenes as structurally and mechanistically unique novel building blocks with direct applications in molecular optoelectronics.

papers.title: Molecular Simulations with a Machine Learning Potential Reveal the Mechanism of Urea Macrocyclization at a Cavitand-Water Interface
papers.abstract: Urea formation is a fundamental transformation in biological, synthetic, and industrial chemistry. While its mechanism in bulk aqueous solution is well established, how supramolecular confinement modulates this reaction remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the macrocyclization of a α,ω-aminoisocyanate substrate in a water-soluble cavitand to uncover how confinement reshapes the reaction mechanism in water. Combining classical molecular dynamics, density functional theory, and machine learning interatomic potentials coupled to enhanced sampling simulations, we construct the free-energy landscape for both the confined and unconfined reactions. The cavitand exerts two mechanistically distinct confinement effects. First, it templates a compact reactant conformation that initiates the macrocyclization, stabilizing it relative to the unconfined system without lowering the ring-closure energy barrier. Second, when confined in the cavitand, ionic intermediates that are highly transient in bulk water are converted into longer-lived species occupying distinct free-energy minima. Both effects originate from spatially heterogeneous solvation at the cavity-water interface, where one nitrogen atom of the forming urea moiety remains exposed to bulk solvent while the other nitrogen is partially buried inside the hydrophobic pocket. This anisotropic solvation selectively promotes the basic proton-transfer pathway, shifting the reaction from nearly balanced acidic and basic routes observed in bulk water to a confinement-biased basic mechanism. These findings demonstrate that molecular containers do not merely preorganize substrates geometrically but can actively reshape reaction free-energy landscapes. The molecular-level insights into supramolecular control of reactivity in aqueous environments underline confinement as a powerful design principle for controlling chemical transformations.

papers.title: Disorder Tolerance in LED Phosphor Host CaAlSiN3 : Correlated Cation Disorder with Minimal Electronic Penalty
papers.abstract: In functional multinary nitrides, intrinsic cation disorder typically has severe electronic consequences, introducing gap states and driving band-gap reduction through local bonding irregularities. CaAlSiN 3 (CASN), a benchmark nitride phosphor host for phosphor-converted light-emitting diodes, therefore presents a paradox: despite substantial Al/Si disorder generated during high-temperature synthesis, it maintains exceptional optical performance. Understanding the fundamental effects of intrinsic disorder in this system could therefore provide broader insight into its performance as a phosphor and the electronic structure of disordertolerant nitrides. Experiments typically treat the Al/Si disorder in CASN as random, whereas prior theoretical studies have been limited to a narrow set of ordered configurations, leaving its thermodynamic origin and electronic consequences unresolved. Here, we combine cluster-expansion Monte Carlo simulations with hybrid density functional theory to characterise Al/Si disorder in CASN across a range of temperatures. Despite the emergence of disorder, the electronic structure remains resilient, with a maximum band-gap reduction of only 3.8% and minimal carrier localisation. This contrasts with related ternary nitrides such as ZnGeN 2 and ZnSnN 2 , in which less correlated cation disorder directly perturbs both band edges, driving pronounced band-gap collapse and carrier localisation. We attribute this tolerance to two features of CASN's crystal chemistry: a Ca d -dominated conduction band minimum decoupled from the disordered sublattice, and correlated disorder that suppresses the most electronically damaging local environments. These results establish CASN as a model system for disorder tolerance in multinary nitrides and suggest broader design principles for electronically robust phosphor hosts.

papers.title: Ab initio, Atomistic, Nonadiabatic Dynamics of the LH2 Complex. I. Distributed exciton model and modified ab initio multiple spawning for LH2.
papers.abstract: Light-harvesting complexes absorb light energy, then funnel it to reactive centers with remarkable efficiency. The LH2 complex in the purple bacterium Rhodoblastus acidophilus has received much experimental scrutiny. However, the size of LH2 has, up until now, precluded ab initio nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations. Past studies have employed parameterized Hamiltonians with system-bath approximations to reduce the nuclear degrees of freedom. In this work, we develop a parallel, GPU-accelerated Frenkel exciton model which allows us to build the exciton Hamiltonian from ab initio electronic structure calculations at every time step. We also implement the Norm-Preserving Implementation (NPI) and phasing within Ab Initio Multiple Spawning (AIMS) to simulate the nonadiabatic dynamics of LH2 with a trajectory-based, quantum mechanical formalism. This approach allows us to observe individual trajectory-resolved population transfer events (loosely speaking, "hops") between the excitonic states of LH2. We present the computed spectrum and a short nonadiabatic dynamics trajectory of LH2 in the B800 band, and we find that hopping between bright outer-ring states occurs via an indirect mechanism involving the dark inner-ring states.

papers.title: Terrestrial ecotoxicity of plastics: Effect factors for life cycle impact assessment
papers.abstract: Soils act as major sinks for plastic pollution, with potential implications for terrestrial ecosystem services. In life cycle assessment (LCA), such impacts are quantified using characterization factors that describe the fate, exposure, and effects of emitted substances. In this study, we develop terrestrial ecotoxicity exposure-and-effect factors (XEFs) for plastics in soil for application in LCA. We compiled 680 effect concentrations (ECs) from published ecotoxicity studies involving plants and invertebrates and converted them to EC 10eq. values. Following the USEtox framework, species-specific average EC 10eq. values were used to construct log-normal fitted species sensitivity distribution curves, from which XEFs were derived. The resulting XEF for plastics in soil equals 0.128 [0.07; 0.30] PAF•m 3 •kg -1 . Specific XEFs for nanoplastics ≤1µm and plastics >1µm were estimated at 0.921 [0.11; 13.10] and 0.126 [0.07; 0.29] PAF•m 3 •kg -1 , respectively. Specific XEFs for natural and agricultural soil were estimated at 0.159 [0.08; 0.40] and 0.236 [0.09; 0.77] PAF•m 3 •kg -1 , respectively. Compared to existing estimates, the derived XEFs fall within the range of previous soil-based values but are substantially lower than aquatic and sediment XEFs, indicating that direct read-across between compartments is not justified. Overall, the proposed XEFs are fully compatible with the USEtox methodology and enable improved inclusion of plastic-related terrestrial ecotoxicity impacts in LCA.

papers.title: Direct Electrografting of Long-Chain Carboxylates Forms Hydrophobic Films for Gold Nanocluster Assembly
papers.abstract: Controlling molecular organization at carbon-based electrochemical interfaces is essential for advancing electrocatalysis, energy conversion, and chemical sensing technologies. Electrochemical oxidation of tetrabutylammonium carboxylates offers a straightforward route for covalent modification of carbon electrodes, yet direct grafting of saturated alkyl chains has been considered impractical due to competing side pathways. Here we demonstrate that chain-length-driven preorganization through van der Waals interactions enables radicals generated upon decarboxylation to couple efficiently with glassy carbon surfaces, forming robust hydrophobic films with organized architectures. Film growth efficiency increases systematically with chain length from hexanoate to undecanoate, yielding interfaces that combine organized molecular packing with controlled porosity. These directly grafted electrodes selectively adsorb Au₂₅(SC₈H₁₇)₁₈ nanoclusters through hydrophobic templating, forming stable multilayer assemblies spanning three to five nanocluster layers that maintain exceptional electrochemical activity and stability. Electrochemical analysis reveals tunable electron transfer kinetics governed by grafted chain length and electrolyte ion size, while control experiments with disorganized films demonstrate that molecular organization, rather than simple hydrophobicity, enables multilayer formation. This chain-assisted direct electrografting strategy establishes a simple yet powerful platform for creating covalently anchored molecular interfaces capable of organizing sophisticated functional nanostructures on carbon electrodes, opening opportunities in nanocluster immobilization, interfacial catalysis, molecular sensing, and molecular electronics.

papers.title: MACE-MDP: A Foundation Model for Molecular Dipole Moments and Polarizabilities
On the acidity characterization of pristine and zinc-modified H-ZSM-5 zeolites: Comparison of adsorption-based characterization methods
papers.abstract: Unlike temperature-programmed desorption (TPD) of ammonia (NH 3 -TPD) and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy of adsorbed pyridine (pyridine-FTIR), where ammonia and pyridine adsorb and desorb without reaction, TPD of isopropylamine (IPAm-TPD) relies on a Brønsted-acid-catalyzed decomposition of isopropylamine to propylene and ammonia to selectively probe Brønsted acidity. Prior studies have reported altered IPAm-TPD responses for metals-modified zeolites relative to pristine zeolites, yet hypotheses on the cause have diverged. This work examined the acidity characterization results of pristine and zinc-modified H-ZSM-5 zeolites from IPAm-TPD against those from NH 3 -TPD, and pyridine-FTIR. For pristine zeolites, the IPAm-TPD data exhibited the expected Brønsted-site-related propylene desorption feature, with propylene amounts proportional to framework aluminium, strongly adsorbed ammonia in NH 3 -TPD, and Brønsted-associated pyridine in pyridine-FTIR. However, the IPAm-TPD data of the zinc-modified zeolites was more complex, with multiple desorption features. The mass spectrometry data and comparison of the quantitative IPAm-TPD results to those of NH 3 -TPD and pyridine-FTIR suggested contributions from a Brønsted-site-related propylene release, an additional, likely Lewis-site-related propylene release, and unidentified side products overlapping with typical propylene responses, possibly from dehydrogenation and aromatization reactions. When the Brønsted-site-related propylene response was quantified and compared to quantitative pyridine-FTIR results, the results seemed representative of Brønsted acidity despite the side reactions.

papers.title: pH-Inverted Histidine-Rich Nanochelants for Trapping Furin-Processed Polycationic Nanotoxins: A Quantum-Classical Platform for Dual Heavy-Metal Detoxification and Broad-Spectrum Countermeasures
papers.abstract: Furin cleaves polybasic sites in endosomes and the secretory pathway, releasing linear (> 3 net positive charges) and concentric (metal-coordinating) nanotoxins that drive metabolic disease, cytokine storms, neurodegeneration, autoimmunity, cancer immune evasion, and infection. We introduce 5H-EAF, an erythritol-capped linear penta-histidine nanochelant (MW ≈ 880 Da) that activates to +4-5 net charge at endosomal pH 5.5-6.5, trapping these species via electrostatic clamping and coordination, then deprotonates and releases harmlessly at neutral pH. DFT (B3LYP-D3/def2-TZVP, explicit solvation) yields Pb 2+ ∆G = −11 to −16 kcal/mol (low pH) → −3 to −6 kcal/mol (neutral); SARS-CoV-2 PRRAR + motif clamping ∆G ≈ −8 to −13 kcal/mol; and anthrax PA63 pore blockade analogous to validated cationic blockers (Kd nM-µM, planar-bilayer literature). The platform speaks furin's native pH/Ca 2+ /charge language without global inhibition. It unifies GLP-1 optimization, cytokine control, α-syn/amyloid management, Pb neuroprotection, and biodefense against furin-dependent pathogens (anthrax, Ebola, H5N1, SARS-CoV-2, Dengue).

papers.title: Isolation of Base-Stabilized 1,4-Disilaquinones
papers.abstract: Despite the importance of quinones in organic synthesis and materials chemistry, their silicon analogues remain largely unexplored until to date. Herein, we report the synthesis of two base-stabilized 1,4-disilaquinones through dimerization of ketenyl-substituted silylenes. These silylenes were obtained in high yields by reaction of two differently substituted metalated ketenes with the amidinato-stabilized chloro silylene (PhC(NtBu)2SiCl). X-ray crystallography combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed a planar, but unsymmetrical structure of the disilaquinone core, arising from its unusual bonding situation. The central heterocyclic motif is best described as a resonance hybrid of three principal forms: a silaquinone-type structure, or as a dimer of two enolates and carbanionic ketones, respectively. Despite its non-aromatic character, the disilaquinone core exhibits remarkable thermal and chemical stability, showing no tendency toward ring opening. Although unreactive toward nucleophiles, treatment with Lewis or Brønsted acids perturbs the π-electron density but preserves the integrity of the six-membered ring framework.

papers.title: Natural Product-Derived Acyl-Tryptamine Conjugates: A Systematic Series of Sixty-Nine Novel Dual-Release Prodrug Candidates Targeting Neuroinflammation, Senescence, Neuroprotection, and Serotonergic Modulation
papers.abstract: A novel series of sixty-nine N-acyl tryptamine conjugates is presented, organised into twentythree structural classes derived from natural product scaffolds: ergolin-8-oyl, berberin-9-oyl, resveratrol-3-oyl, pterostilben-3-oyl, hesperetin-2-oyl, naringenin-2-oyl, eriodictyol-2-oyl, taxifolin-2-oyl, quercetin-2-oyl, isorhamnetin-2-oyl, tamarixetin-2-oyl, rhamnetin-2-oyl, fisetin-2-oyl, kaempferol-2-oyl, galangin-2-oyl, apigenin-2-oyl, luteolin-2-oyl, diosmetin-2-oyl, baicalein-2-oyl, wogonin-2-oyl, chrysin-2-oyl, curcumin-4-oyl, and silibinin-oyl. All compounds share a secondary amide bond linking the acyl moiety to substituted tryptamine scaffolds bearing 4-hydroxy, 5-methoxy, or 4-acetoxy substitution, with enzymatic hydrolysis proposed to simultaneously release a pharmacologically active tryptamine and a bioactive natural product-derived acyl fragment. The twenty-three classes introduce mechanistically distinct secondary hypotheses including SIRT1/AMPK activation, Nrf2 induction, AhR modulation, NF-κB inhibition, MAO-B inhibition, senolytic activity, D2 receptor modulation, aromatase inhibition, and mitochondrial redox support. All sixty-nine compounds are new chemical entities; no synthesis or biological testing has been performed. SMILES strings, predicted physicochemical properties, and hypothetical pharmacological profiles are provided to stimulate further investigation. This series constitutes the fourth instalment of a systematic acyl-tryptamine prodrug platform, complementing three preceding publications describing heteroaromatic, endogenous, and phytochemical acyl classes across fifty-five additional compounds.

papers.title: Consequences of Monomer Impurities on Network Characteristics and Dynamic Mechanical Behavior of an Eugenol-based Covalent Adaptable Network
papers.abstract: Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) are an emerging class of polymers exhibiting the potential to introduce recyclability into polymer networks. For industrial applications, robustness of material properties and predictable dynamic behavior are highly desirable. In this study, diepoxides of varying purity were used to prepare hybrid CANs. Hybrid CANs are based on both dynamic vinylogous urethane bonds and permanent bonds formed by the reaction of amines and epoxides. We specifically investigate the robustness of the materials dynamic exchange behavior against impurities that impair or modify the network characteristics. Stress relaxation experiments reveal that the dynamic behavior remains relatively stable up to ca. 23 % monomer impurity. At higher impurity levels we observe pronounced changes of the exchange dynamics. All materials, regardless of purity, exhibit incomplete stress relaxation. Macroscopic manifestations of this fact are visible defects in the nominally purest materials upon reshaping. Thermal and dynamic-mechanical analyses further show that network density and glass transition temperature decrease with increasing impurity, while overall the thermal stability remains largely unaffected. The results demonstrate that hybrid CANs based on vinylogous urethane exchange chemistry can tolerate moderate monomer impurities without losing key dynamic properties, offering insights for industrial-scale processing and material design.

papers.title: Bridging MS2 Spectra and Chemical Space: Advances in Spectral Similarity, Molecular Retrieval, and De Novo Structure Discovery
papers.abstract: Mass spectrometry-based metabolomics increasingly relies on computational methods to translate information-rich MS/MS fragmentation patterns into chemical insight, yet assigning chemical identities to spectra ("annotation") remains a major bottleneck because reference libraries cover only a small fraction of plausible compounds. In this review, we frame the field through the lens of two interacting representation spaces: spectral space, where MS/MS data reside, and chemical space, where molecules are represented by fingerprints, descriptors, or learned embeddings. We discuss how different design choices induce different geometries, what it means for spectra or molecules to be "close", and survey methods for representing and comparing spectra, representing molecules, and mapping between both spaces. We highlight emerging deep-learning trends for cross-modal alignment and retrieval, and we outline where the analogy to text-image learning breaks due to peak ambiguity, noise, and the one-to-many nature of spectrum-to-structure relationships.

papers.title: Evaluation of Custom REINVENT Priors Trained on Synthetically Accessible Chemical Spaces for Generative Molecular Design
papers.abstract: Generative molecular design is increasingly popular as a promising way to create novel drug candidates with desired properties. The REINVENT approach, originally proposed by AstraZeneca, is a widely used framework for such generative design. However, the synthetic accessibility of generated molecules often remains uncertain. Combinatorial spaces provide access to hundreds of billions of molecules with guaranteed synthetic feasibility and a flat pricing model, making them attractive for planning and executing drug-discovery projects. This study addresses how generative molecular design can be used to ensure that generated molecules remain within a desired chemical space. To achieve this, we developed a new approach and demonstrated the feasibility of training REINVENT Priors on samples from Freedom Space 4.0 and REAL Space. We evaluated the performance of finetuned REINVENT Agent models derived from these Priors using both structure-based and ligand-based computational objectives. Our approach allows the generation of molecules that exhibit the desired activity and remain within the combinatorial space, ensuring synthetic accessibility. The Priors developed in this work are freely released to the community. We hope that the outcomes of this research will boost the practical applications of generative molecular design in academia and industry all over the world.

papers.title: Armstrongs Probabilistic Electron Phase-Space Overlap Model (APEPM)
papers.abstract: Context Assessing whether a bonding interaction is geometrically possible , that is, whether the probabilistic electron clouds of two atoms spatially overlap at a given internuclear separation, is a fundamental yet often implicit aspect of molecular modeling. Conventional electronic structure methods address this question indirectly through wavefunction optimization and energetic analysis, which can obscure the underlying geometric constraints and limit scalability. Here, Armstrong’s Probabilistic Electron Phase-Space Overlap Model (APEPM) is introduced as a geometry-driven, wavefunction-free framework for evaluating geometric bond feasibility by explicitly determining whether nonzero electron cloud overlap exists for any specified atomic separation. The model provides closed-form expressions for the size and extent of the shared electron phase-space and tracks how this overlap evolves continuously under bond compression or extension. By mapping the overlap region onto radially partitioned orbital shells, APEPM identifies which atomic orbital regions are geometrically involved in the mandatory shared phase-space, yielding an interpretable description of spatial orbital involvement that is independent of energetic weighting or bond strength assignment. Methods APEPM represents bonded atoms as interacting probabilistic electron volumes characterized by effective electron cloud radii derived from atomic electron cloud extents. Geometric overlap is determined analytically using closed-form expressions for the intersection of two spheres as a function of internuclear distance, yielding overlap radius, cross-sectional area, and overlap volume, with zero overlap defining the geometric infeasibility limit. Orbital participation is evaluated by projecting the overlap region along the bond axis and identifying intersections with predefined radial orbital shells. All calculations are analytic and geometry-based and are implemented in Python using custom software developed for this work.

papers.title: Phenoxy-Benzothiadiazole Donor-Acceptor Compounds Exhibit Solvatochromic Fluorescence and Are Precursors to Open-Shell Phenoxyl Radicals
papers.abstract: In this work, we present the synthesis of two highly fluorescent phenoxy-benzothiadiazole donor-acceptor (DA) compounds, which exhibit quantum yields of up to 84% in solution under an atmosphere of air. These compounds display solvatochromic fluorescence within the visible region of the electromagnetic spectrum, characteristic of DA exciplex behavior, and exhibit reversible reactivity under acidic conditions as monitored by UV-Vis spectroscopy. We demonstrate the reversible oxidation of compound to the open-shell phenoxy radical 5·. In contrast, compound 6 undergoes irreversible oxidation to bis(quinone) 7, despite the loss of aromaticity. We also observe the comproportionation of 6 and 7 to compound 6· upon UV light irradiation in solution, as evidenced by EPR spectroscopy. The structures of compounds 5, 6, and 7 were confirmed through X-ray crystallography.

papers.title: Non-Equilibrium Phase-Pure Synthesis and Thermal Transport Properties of Metallic Telluride Cu5Ge2Te7
papers.abstract: Tellurides are of increasing interest owing to their emerging applications in energy and electronics, as well as their diverse structural chemistry. We introduce Cu 5 Ge 2 Te 7 , a novel ternary telluride, synthesized using traditional high-temperature synthesis and non-equilibrium methods. This is the first report on the Ge-based phase of the Cu 5 Sn 2 Ch 7 ( Ch : S, Se, Te) family, which has been extensively studied. The phase-pure Cu 5 Ge 2 Te 7 was synthesized by heating for 30-120 seconds using Direct Joule heating Synthesis (DJS), followed by quenching. DJS was used to develop an ex - situ “panoramic” reaction map that provides insight into phase formation at different DJS temperatures. The structure of Cu 5 Ge 2 Te 7 was characterized by X-ray diffraction techniques on the crystals grown by traditional high-temperature synthesis. The structure consists of corner-sharing distorted Te 4 -tetrahedral units surrounding copper and germanium atoms. The germanium atoms reside in tellurium tetrahedra, which condense into [Ge 2 Te 7 ]-dimers, and such a Ge–Te interaction has been rarely reported in inorganic systems so far. Electronic structure calculation shows that Cu 5 Ge 2 Te 7 is a poor metal, as a finite density of states is present at the Fermi level. Bonding analysis displays that the [Ge 2 Te 7 ]-unit in the structure exhibits Zintl-phase-like electronic features, though the overall electronic structure indicates that this Cu 5 Ge 2 Te 7 is not a true Zintl phase. Transport measurements reveal an ultralow lattice thermal conductivity of 0.4 W·m -1 ·K -1 at 683 K, making it a suitable candidate for thermal insulation applications.

papers.title: Rapid screening platform for discovering novel peptide prenyltransferases to expand the structural diversity of pseudo-natural prenylated peptides
papers.abstract: Peptide lipidation can enhance stability and permeability, yet biocatalysts for late-stage, site- and mode-selective modification remain limited. We established a streamlined activity-profiling system that rapidly assesses peptide-prenylating activities using an artificial substrate set. Screening 19 recombinant, putative cyanobactin prenyltransferases (PTases) uncovered 14 active enzymes with diverse catalytic properties, including five unprecedented modes of prenylation, bifunctionality toward Trp/Tyr, and expanded donor utilization such as farnesylation. Co-crystal structures of seven PTases reveal how subtle active-site changes enable dual substrate recognition and accommodation of bulkier donors, highlighting the evolutionary diversification of catalytic functions. The enzymes tolerate non-native substrates, enabling late-stage, site- and mode-selective lipidation to construct pseudo-natural peptides. Together, these findings drastically expand the enzymatic and mechanistic landscape of cyanobactin PTases, substantially enlarging their functional repertoire and revealing the structural principles that govern the diversification of peptide prenylation chemistry.

papers.title: Large-Scale Virtual Screening Identifies Novel Allosteric Modulators of TIMP2: A Computational Approach to Enhancing Neuroplasticity
papers.abstract: TIMP2 (Tissue Inhibitor of Metalloproteinase-2) plays a crucial role in hippocampal neuroplasticity and cognitive function through MMP-independent signaling. Despite its therapeutic promise, TIMP2 has long been considered 'undruggable' due to its cryptic surface topology and lack of canonical active sites. We present a comprehensive computational pipeline integrating CNS-filtered virtual screening, orthogonal ADMET/toxicity validation, and allosteric site targeting to identify small-molecule modulators of TIMP2. Screening ~600,000 CNS-filtered compounds from ZINC20 against a cryptic N-terminal allosteric site (Val6, Leu100, Phe103) identified 178 compounds with favorable drug-like properties. Orthogonal validation using ProTox-III refined this to 154 highest-confidence candidates (Tier 1A) validated across multiple computational toxicology platforms. Site-selectivity analysis revealed a 99.5% preference for the primary allosteric pocket, establishing it as the dominant binding site for therapeutic intervention. Chemical diversity analysis identified 15 distinct scaffold families spanning both halogenated (26.6%) and non-halogenated (73.4%) chemotypes, demonstrating multiple viable strategies for achieving CNS penetration with clean safety profiles. This work represents the first systematic identification of small molecule TIMP2 modulators, revealing a previously unknown cryptic binding site that can accommodate diverse chemical scaffolds. Integration of ADMET-AI and ProTox-III predictions enabled refined risk stratification, yielding 154 highest-confidence candidates validated across orthogonal computational toxicology platforms. The dramatic variation in ADMET survival rates across chunks (0.3–9.3%) underscores the importance of broad sampling of chemical space. While halogenation enhances certain drug-like properties, our results demonstrate that both halogenated and non-halogenated compounds can achieve the demanding intersection of high affinity, CNS penetration, and drug safety. Structural validation using the AlphaFold v6 predicted structure confirmed the cryptic allosteric pocket with sub-angstrom accuracy (mean Cα deviation = 0.30 ˚A, triad pLDDT > 96), and cross-species conservation analysis revealed 100% pocket identity in mouse TIMP2, the primary translational model. Molecular dynamics simulation (50 ns explicit solvent) further confirmed pocket stability under physiological conditions with 92% area preservation and convergence of triad distances to within 0.01–0.32 ˚A of crystallographic values. These findings establish TIMP2 as a tractable drug target and provide 154 validated chemical starting points across diverse scaffolds for therapeutic development.

papers.title: Nanomolar Sensitivity Chirality Transfer from Designed Helical Repeat Proteins to Achiral CdS Nanorods
papers.abstract: Bridging chirality across length scales with inorganic-organic hybrid materials is a rapidly expanding area of research. Here, we establish asymmetry at CdS nanorod (NR) interfaces using a designed helical repeat protein bearing four cysteine residues (DHR-4Cys). Hydrophobic NRs are transferred into water with glycine, then glycine is displaced by DHR-4Cys, leveraging the thiophilicity of cadmium. Circular dichroism (CD) in the visible, coincident with CdS electronic transitions, reveals a chiral DHR-4Cys:CdS interface. The dissymmetry factor ( g = 4.5×10 -4 (short NRs), and 5.0×10 -4 (long NRs)) is weakly dependent on NR length, and CD persists at nanomolar protein loadings. Additionally, control experiments demonstrate that DHR-4Cys:CdS NR chirality is dictated by the local coordination of Cys with no significant contribution from the chiral secondary structure of the protein ( g -factor of short and long Cys:CdS NRs are 4.8×10 -4 and 4.0×10 -4 , respectively). Together with far-UV CD and TEM, which provide evidence of preserved protein structure, these results provide the first demonstration that a structurally defined protein can induce chirality in CdS nanocrystals while maintaining protein structure at biologically relevant concentrations.

papers.title: Balancing Chemical Equations via the Process of Difference Elimination
papers.abstract: While the method of manual inspection produces correct results at the introductory level, it can often appear untidy, unintuitive, and may lack structured, teachable depth. This paper presents an alternative approach, the concept of difference elimination, designed with transparency at its core. It serves as both a pedagogical and visualisation tool, offering a structured perspective on balancing chemical equations at the introductory level. This article aims to reinterpret the balancing workspace, contributing to ongoing discussions surrounding the limitations of manual inspection, suitable introductory alternatives, and the broader comprehension of what is often perceived as an abstract and somewhat unteachable process of balancing chemical equations.

papers.title: Lipid assembly on a polyphenyllactate droplet surface to form a hybrid protocell
papers.abstract: Deciphering how primitive, inanimate matter organized into living systems is a central challenge in origins of life research. In this context, protocells—primitive cell-like compartments—are widely considered as plausible intermediates linking nonliving chemistry with early biological systems. Among various protocell models, formation of polyester droplets through wet-dry cycle-induced polymerization of hydroxy acids, followed by hydration, provides a prebiotically plausible model of primitive compartment formation on early Earth, resulting in a membraneless protocell providing relevant functions such as biomolecule enrichment. However, these droplets, while functional to some extent, may have necessarily required incorporation of membrane boundaries to support their stability and their potential to evolve over extended timescales. Here, we report the construction of lipid-coated polyphenyllactate (polyPA) droplets, in which lipid layers spontaneously assemble onto droplets to form stable membrane-bound compartments. By integrating the robustness of lipid bilayers with the molecular enrichment properties of polyPA droplets, lipid-coated polyPA droplets exhibit permeability to small molecules as well as significantly enhanced stability compared to membraneless polyPA droplets. This hybrid model protocell system provides a plausible bridge providing a transition from membraneless to membrane-bound protocells, a potential essential step leading towards the emergence of early cellular life.

papers.title: Reversible Droplet Bridging and Tunable Viscoelasticity in Emulsions Using Biocompatible PLA-b-PEO-b-PLA Telechelic Block Copolymers: Implications for Injectable Emulsion Gels
papers.abstract: Telechelic polymers are known to form reversible networks through end-group association; however, their application as structuring agents in emulsion-based soft materials remains underexplored. Herein, we systematically investigate the biocompatible amphiphilic triblock copolymer poly(DL-lactic acid)-block-poly(ethylene oxide)-block-poly(DL-lactic acid)(PLA- b -PEO- b -PLA) as a rheology modifier in toluene-in-water model emulsions. Owing to the selective adsorption of PLA end blocks at the oil–water interface and the solvation of the PEO midblock in the aqueous phase, this polymer is expected to form reversible droplet-bridging networks. During the process, the polymer concentration, molecular weight of the mid and end blocks, and the dispersed phase volume fraction were adjusted, and the factors governing network formation were elucidated using oscillatory rheology and stress-relaxation measurements. The results show that anchoring of the PLA end blocks and PEO-mediated bridging predominantly control the strength and dynamic reversibility of the network. Step-strain experiments further reveal that the droplet-bridging interactions can be disrupted under large deformation and partially recover when small-strain conditions are restored, confirming the presence of reversible physical associations. These findings establish a molecular design strategy for biodegradable telechelic copolymers as effective and reprocessable structuring agents in emulsion gels. The shear-responsive, tunable, and reversible nature of the droplet-bridging network makes this material platform particularly suitable for injectable emulsion gels for advanced soft matter and biomedical engineering applications.

papers.title: A Toolkit for Phase Identification and Reproducible Synthesis of Fe-Terephthalate Metal-Organic Frameworks: MIL-88B, MIL-101, MIL-53, and MIL-68
papers.abstract: Iron-terephthalate metal-organic frameworks (Fe-BDC MOFs) are an important and abundant class of materials that exhibit rich polymorphism, making reproducible phase-pure synthesis and phase identification challenging. Here, we systematically examine how precursor type, solvent, temperature, and pH influence the formation of the four known Fe-BDC phases: MIL-88B, MIL-53, MIL-101, and MIL-68. We provide a wide range of complementary analyses of phase pure samples including powder Xray diffraction (PXRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Mössbauer spectroscopy, elemental (CHN) and ICP-OES analysis, nitrogen and water sorption analysis. We identify that solvent-depended PXRD measurements reveal fingerprints for respective Fe-BDC phases due to the different breathing behaviors, providing a rapid and reliable method for phase discrimination even in phase mixtures. This work, establishes robust synthesis protocols and experimental reference data for navigating the phase identification in 2 the Fe-BDC system and clarifies synthesis-structure-property relationships, with a focus on structural flexibility.

papers.title: Triethoxysilane-Catalyzed Hydroboration of Alkenes, Nitriles, Ketones and Esters: From Non-Covalent Interactions to a Hydrosilylation/Si-B Exchange Pathway
papers.abstract: Triethoxysilane was found an efficient precatalyst for the hydroboration of alkenes, nitriles, ketones and esters with pinacolborane (HBPin). The catalyst showed an excellent substrate scope including aromatic and aliphatic substrates affording the products in good to excellent yields. The system was found less efficient for the hydroboration of alkenes and Ealkenylboronate esters than that of alkynes, which could be traced back to the strength of the interactions between the multiple CC bonds of the substrates with HSi(OEt)3. The nature of the multiple CC bond (C=C vs C≡C) played the largest role in catalyst efficiency, the presence of a BPin substituent in the E-alkenylboronate esters not impacting the substrate conversion compared to that of terminal alkenes. The nature of aryl substituents in aromatic substrates exerted distinct effects on catalytic efficiency depending on the substrate class. Whereas the catalyst was sensitive to both the electronic and steric properties of terminal alkynes, catalytic efficiency in the hydroboration of aromatic nitriles was governed primarily by steric effects, with minimal sensitivity to electronic variation. Competition experiments allowed to unravel the catalyst preferences for the hydroboration of different types of functional groups, HSi(OEt)3 showing a significant preference for alkynes and alkenes over nitriles and ketones. Unlike in the HSi(OEt)3-catalyzed sequential hydroboration of alkynes, the fluorinated analog HSi(OCH2CF3)3 showed a comparable efficiency to HSi(OEt)3 for the hydroboration of nitriles, suggesting that the Lewis acidity at Si did not play a role in catalyst efficiency. The significant differences between alkynes and heteroatom-containing substrates could be traced back to the presence of a catalytically active species different from HSi(OEt)3 in the hydroboration of nitriles, ketones and esters. Additionally, intermediates from hydrosilylation of the multiple bond of nitriles were identified during catalytic turnover, supporting a mechanism involving H-Si bond addition across the multiple bond followed by Si-B exchange steps.

papers.title: Web-PackMol: A Molecular Packing Tool for the Web Browser
papers.abstract: Adequate initial configurations for molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are essential for preventing unphysical overlaps that disrupt integration algorithms. Most software packages for MD simulation already bring a "solvation" function that handles that specific part of the setup, producing regular boxes for MD. But these programs cannot deal with more complex molecule packing procedures. While the original PACKMOL package introduced a powerful gradient-based optimization for this purpose, its command-line nature and installation requirements can be a barrier for quick system setup or educational use. Here, we present Web-PackMol, a lightweight, zero-installation web application that employs a stochastic Monte Carlo approach for molecular packing. Web-PackMol allows users to pack complex molecules within arbitrary 3D regions defined by dual-constraint logic (e.g., inside a box AND outside a sphere). It includes built-in features such as real-time 3D visualization, automated density calculation on the generated systems, and session persistence through JSON exports. While algorithmically less efficient than PACKMOL (which stays the best choice to pack large, dense systems), Web-PackMol is far easier to use as it operates right in the web browser and through a regular graphical interface without scripting, while allowing to accomplish a vast majority of the most common procedures within seconds to minutes, as we demonstrate with examples similar to those presented in the PACKMOL paper plus some unique ones. Web-PackMol is available as a module of the online PDB manipulation suite at https://pdbms.altervista.org.

papers.title: Impact of Methylation on the Nematic Phase of Phenyl Benzoate Mesogens and Dimers
papers.abstract: Liquid crystals (LCs) possess anisotropic mechanical and optical properties with applications ranging from soft robotics to display technology. Despite advances in the precise synthesis of liquid crystalline materials, the microscopic origins of substituent effects, which impact functional performance, are not always well understood. Here, we use molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate how methyl substitution affects the nematic-phase behavior of liquid crystal monomers and dimers composed of phenyl benzoate cores flanked by aliphatic tails. Methylation induces a decrease in the nematic-isotropic transition temperature. Using data-driven analysis, we find that for monomers this decrease is associated with an increase in flexibility of core-adjacent aliphatic torsions that influence overall mesogen conformation. For dimers, this manifests as a shift from a continuum of accessible conformations in the isotropic phase to occupying more distinct hairpin and extended states in the nematic phase. The latter exhibits a bend angle consistent with experimental signatures of a modulated nematic phase. Together, these results show how minor changes in chemical structure can impact the conformational ensemble of liquid crystals, trading local conformational entropy for global nematic order, in turn influencing their macroscopic transition temperatures.

papers.title: Next Generation Sulfonyl Fluoride Electrophiles Expand the Scope of Covalent Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Sulfonyl fluorides (SFs) are promising electrophiles for covalent drug discovery, enabling the targeting of diverse amino acids beyond cysteine. However, their widespread application has been hindered by limitations in stability and selectivity, often restricting their utility to early-stage tool development. We introduce heteroaryl sulfonyl fluorides as a next-generation class of tuneable electrophiles designed to overcome these challenges. These electrophiles demonstrate optimized intrinsic reactivity, enhanced solubility and lipophilicity, whilst exhibiting markedly improved stability in whole blood and plasma compared to traditional phenyl-based SFs. Employing a high-throughput chemistry direct-to-biology workflow, we rapidly explored structure-activity relationships, yielding potent covalent inhibitors of carbonic anhydrase II (CAII) with exceptional cellular selectivity. These findings establish heteroaryl SFs as versatile, tuneable electrophiles possessing superior drug-like properties and outstanding target specificity. This platform offers a powerful new avenue for developing highly selective covalent ligands that are suitable for drug discovery.

papers.title: Strategies to predict and design spin defects for quantum technologies
papers.abstract: The design of materials with functionalities optimally suited for quantum information applications is a critical need in the field of quantum science and engineering. This Account focuses on a specific class of systems, spin defects in semiconductors and insulators, and on the manipulation of their electron spins, which can provide controllable qubits with long relaxation and coherence times, and can be coupled to nuclear spins for long-lived quantum memories. Specifically, this Account summarizes recent contributions by the authors to the development of integrated theoretical frameworks and high-performance codes to predict and design spin defects and presents examples of validated predictions and interpretations of experimental results. Starting from a brief description of the structural and charge stability at zero temperature using density functional theory (DFT), we discuss simulations to understand the mechanism of spin defect formation. These simulations are carried out using first-principles molecular dynamics coupled with advanced sampling methods or with machine-learned potentials. We then move to discuss in detail two classes of properties that are essential for the prediction of spin defects' functionalities: electronic and coherence properties. The former are critical to understand optical cycles used for spin initialization, control, and readout. The latter determine how long a quantum state can maintain its characteristics, and hence, the limits of operability of any quantum device. While DFT may be sufficiently accurate for structural properties, the investigation of the electronic properties of spin defects requires more advanced methods to describe many-body interactions. We present our developments of theoretical and computational frameworks based on many-body perturbation theory, (spin-flip) time-dependent DFT, and quantum defect embedding theory. All together these techniques enable the calculation of absorption and photoluminescence spectra, the study of multi-reference, correlated electronic states, the optimization of excited state potential energy surfaces, and the calculation of inter-system crossing rates. Importantly, these methods have been implemented in the same code (WEST), and they can be compared at the same level of numerical accuracy for each system of interest. Further, they have been coupled to stochastic and dynamical methods to study quantum vibronic effects, and to a non-relativistic quantum electrodynamics description of photons in the weak-coupling regime, to study non-resonant energy transfer between interacting defects. The study of coherence properties is carried out with spin Hamiltonians describing the interaction of electronic and nuclear spins, and with cluster correlation expansion (CCE) methods to simulate spin dynamics, including the treatment of open quantum systems. CCE calculations are also instrumental in high-throughput searches of suitable hosts with low magnetic noise for three- and two-dimensional materials, and in guiding the experimental identification of specific nuclei surrounding spin defects. The discussion of computational frameworks is followed by that of results for specific systems illustrating successes and open problems, with examples for heterogeneous solids, inclusive of surfaces and mesoscopic defects, and with a focus on quantum sensing and communication applications.

papers.title: Nikolas: Autonomous Discovery of Novel EGFR Kinase Inhibitors via the PRISM Meta-Cognitive Architecture
papers.abstract: Discovering targeted small-molecule therapeutics requires navigating a chemical space exceeding 10 60 drug-like compounds-a process traditionally demanding years of iterative synthesis and screening. We present Nikolas, a semi-autonomous AI agent powered by PRISM (Persistent Recursive Intelligence with Structured Metacognition)-a domainagnostic 5-layer meta-cognitive architecture that enables emergent chemical intuition through hierarchical memory and recursive self-reflection. Previously validated on inorganic CO 2 reduction catalysis, PRISM is applied here to de novo EGFR kinase inhibitor design for non-small cell lung cancer. The pipeline integrates GPT-5.2 for generative molecular reasoning, RDKit for multi-objective drug-likeness validation, and AutoDock Vina for physics-based docking against PDB: 1M17. In 20 autonomous iterations, Nikolas generated 13 valid drug-like molecules, 12 achieving "Excellent" binding affinities (∆G < −9.0 kcal/mol). The champion (∆G = −9.67 kcal/mol, Drug Score 95/100) surpasses Erlotinib (∆G ≈ −9.5 kcal/mol) with confirmed Met793 hydrogen bonding. Cross-referencing against PubChem (115M+ compounds) and ChEMBL (2.4M+ bioactive molecules) confirmed 4 of 5 top candidates are Novel Chemical Entities. Tanimoto analysis (T c = 0.183-0.474 vs. approved TKIs) confirms structurally distinct scaffolds. All candidates exhibit ideal ADMET profiles: zero Lipinski violations, high GI absorption, and SA scores of 2.2-2.5.

papers.title: CO 2 Hydrogenation to Methanol Catalyzed by Cu Phosphine Complexes Immobilized on Lewis Acidic Supports
papers.abstract: Methanol synthesis from CO2 is key for a sustainable chemical industry. Cu-based heterogeneous catalysts are standard for this reaction but need high temperatures (250-400 °C), resulting in low equilibrium yields. Homogeneous catalysts based on first row transition metals could potentially produce methanol from CO2 and H2 at lower temperatures. However, no molecular Cu catalyst has been previously observed to hydrogenate CO2 to methanol, due to the fact that Cu requires the assistance of Lewis acidic supports such as ZrO2 to produce methanol. Inspired by these cooperative heterogeneous catalysts, we immobilize Cu(I) phosphine complexes on Lewis acidic supports and test them for their reactivity for gas-phase CO2 hydrogenation to methanol in a plug flow reactor. These complexes are activated by close contact to Lewis acid sites in Al2O3 and the Zr-metalorganic framework (MOF) NU-1000 toward MeOH production at as little as 110 °C in the gas phase without additives and are stable for more than 24 h on stream. This is the first observation of methanol production from a molecular Cu catalyst and suggests that immobilization on Lewis acidic supports could be a mechanism to increase the activity of other molecular CO2 hydrogenation catalysts.

papers.title: Constellation Plots in KNIME: An Automated Scaffold-Based Workflow for Interactive Chemical Space Visualization
papers.abstract: Chemical space analysis is extensively used in different chemistry areas, ranging from the study of natural products to drug discovery projects. Its versatility stems from the ability to integrate continuous properties with molecular representations. This data is used to generate visualizations through dimensionality reduction algorithms. Constellation Plots have been proposed as a general approach to the visual representation of chemical space by encoding structural similarity, scaffold contents, frequency, and continuous properties into a single coordinate-based map. Thus, Constellation Plots provide a high-density visual representation of the chemical space of compound datasets with complex relations. Despite the versatility of Constellation Plots, there remains a significant lack of intuitive, user-friendly, or low-code protocols to automate the generation of these plots for non-computational experts. Herein, we present an interactive and automated scaffold-based Constellation Plot workflow developed within the open-source platform KNIME, facilitating chemical space visualization and analysis. To illustrate the application of the workflow, we used a dataset of 5,222 compounds that inhibit Tau protein, a key therapeutic target for Alzheimer's disease. The KNIME workflow is a general resource that can be used to analyze virtually any data set annotated with a property, including biological activity. The workflow is freely available at https://github.com/Daniphantom99/KNIME_Constellation_plots.

papers.title: Coaxial Multi-Material Melt Electrowriting Using the Open-Source MEWron Platform
Combining aqueous and solid-phase analysis to improve the understanding during sulfuric-acid based leaching of LCO
papers.abstract: The leaching of LiCoO₂ particles was investigated combining aqueous analysis (inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectroscopy) with solid-phase analysis methods (X˗ray diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy). The most common industrial leaching mixture H₂SO₄ and H₂O₂ was used to understand the ongoing processes on the material level rather than performing an empirical improvement of a hydrometallurgical process. Instead, the reactions inside the bulk and on the surface of the LiCoO₂ particles during leaching are investigated. LiCoO₂ undergoes different structural phase transitions at the surface as well as in the bulk when leached with sulfuric acid, due to strong lithium loss and the oxidation of cobalt. A stable outer shell with a delithiated core forms during leaching, causing leaching limitations. Adding enhancing agents, e.g. H₂O₂ or S₂O 8 2- , results in higher conversion rates, which is explained by the reduction of the cobalt at the surface forming soluble species. Thus, no stable lithium-depleted phase is formed as passivation layer and completed leaching is possible.

papers.title: When Bonds Resist Rotation: Automated Classification and Representation of Atropisomers in the MolBar Identifier
papers.abstract: Atropisomerism, a form of chirality arising from restricted rotation around single bonds, holds significant pharmacological importance. Yet, the automated identification and representation of atropisomerism in molecular databases and cheminformatics tools remain limited. Identifying bonds that lead to stable atropisomers typically involves labor-intensive experiments or costly quantum chemical scans. In this work, we present an extension of the molecule identifier MolBar that automatically classifies each rotatable bond in a three-dimensional molecular structure as either rapidly convertible or configurationally stable, specifying the absolute configuration for the latter. Our methodology uses two distinct classifiers, a physically motivated classifier for steric hindrance and a message-passing graph neural network for electronic effects. Integrated into MolBar, this module enables unsupervised, largescale annotation of atropisomeric bonds along with their absolute configurations. This advancement facilitates the representation of atropisomerism in databases and supports atropisomerism-aware machine learning in drug discovery. A preliminary version of MolBar 1.2.0 is available on the Python Package Index (PyPI) and can be installed using the pip command: pip install-pre molbar.

papers.title: Efficient Electrocatalytic Interface Based on a Solution-Processable Nickel-Dithiolene Coordination Polymer
Illumination-Driven Multihole OER on Hematite: Unraveling Coexisting Water Oxidation Pathways via Ga2O3 Surface Regulation
papers.abstract: Efficient multihole transfer and selective activation of surface reaction pathways remain critical challenges in photoelectrochemical (PEC) water oxidation on hematite. In this study, we combine variable-intensity illumination (0.25-6.21 Suns) and Ga₂O₃ surface modification to uncover coexisting water oxidation mechanisms on ultrathin (~50 nm) ALD-grown α-Fe₂O₃ photoanodes

papers.title: Tuning Metal-Chalcogen Interactions Unlocks Phototoxicity Pathways
papers.abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a promising minimally invasive treatment for cancer, yet current photosensitizers rely predominantly on oxygen-dependent Type II pathways, rendering them less effective in hypoxic tumor regions. Here we establish a computational design framework for hypoxia-relevant metal–complex photosensitizers by systematically varying the central metal (Ru(II), Os(II), Rh(III), Ir(III), Pt(IV)) and the heteroatom identity in a three-ring conjugated tail (O, S, Se, Te) within a TLD1433-inspired scaffold. Using a unified TDDFT and spin–orbit coupling workflow, we quantify trends in absorption, excited-state character, triplet energetics and intersystem crossing propensity, and evaluate Type I feasibility using vertical ionization potential/electron affinity (VIP/VEA) descriptors for direct superoxide formation and indirect radical pathways via autoionization. Heavier chalcogens produce systematic redshifts of the lowest bright transition, while spin–orbit coupling is strongly influenced by excited state composition, with Os(II) complexes exhibiting the highest calculated SOC. Across the series, triplet energies remain compatible with singlet-oxygen sensitization, supporting Type II accessibility, whereas VIP/VEA trends reveal candidates with thermodynamically favorable Type I reactivity. Together, these results provide actionable design rules to co-optimize long-wavelength excitation, triplet yield, and redox thermodynamics for hypoxia-active PDT.

papers.title: Ligand topology tunes energy and character of emissive triplet states in stannylenes
papers.abstract: In the last decades, phosphorescent or photoactive complexes with earth abundant transition metals have gained huge attention. On the contrary, heavy main group elements with similar properties are rare, in particular group 14 complexes in the oxidation state +II, e.g. tetrylenes. The excited state properties remained mostly undiscussed and general design concepts for excited state properties-as established for transition metal complexes-are lacking. The present study offers a conceptional topological approach for understanding and addressing specific excited state properties of main group complexes, exemplary discussed by the Sn(t-Bu PDP t-Bu) complex 1 with 2 the dianionic pincer-type ligand t-Bu PDP t-Bu2-(H2 t-Bu PDP t-Bu = 2,6-bis(3,5-di-tert-butylpyrrol-2yl)pyridine). 1 shows red triplet ligand-to-metal charge transfer (3 LMCT) phosphorescence in the solid state. Emission intensities of solid 1 vary in an unusual manner with temperature. The obtained experimental results are underpinned and interpreted with detailed (SOC-TD)DFT calculations. The present results are put into context with the few reported studies on the photophysics of stannylenes to achieve a deeper general understanding of the photophysics of main group complexes.

papers.title: Mechanochemical depolymerization of post-consumer aliphatic polyesters and repurposing to tunable disulfide-based dynamic covalent materials
papers.abstract: Aliphatic polyesters such as poly(lactic acid) (PLA) and poly(hydroxyalkanoates) (PHAs) are inherently biodegradable, therefore these materials are typically collected and composted at end of life which results in products that prevent recycling and repurposing into new materials. Chemical recycling presents an orthogonal method for the depolymerization of polyesters and their packaging formats (e.g., multilayer flexible packaging), but this process can produce significant chemical waste in the form of solvents and excess reagents. Using ball mill grinding (BMG) to overcome the limitations of conventional ester aminolysis, we demonstrate an operationally simple mechanochemical depolymerization of PLA, PHAs, and biodegradable multilayer flexible film packaging. Maintaining a focus on sustainable materials, we then demonstrate the synthesis of tunable αlipoic acid (αLA)-based resins for photopolymerization to disulfide covalent adaptable networks (CANs) from the depolymerized polyesters in one-pot. Investigation into structure-property relationships reveals a range of mechanical properties-producing materials with significantly lower elastic moduli (ca. 50 times lower) relative to the initial polyester film packaging material. Additionally, microscopy images of the αLA-based materials after composting studies show evidence of biodegradation. Ultimately, this work further solidifies the utility of BMG mechanochemistry for mild and sustainable depolymerizations and demonstrates effective metamorphosis of the depolymerized monomers into bio-based, reprocessable CANs with unique properties while maintaining biodegradability.

papers.title: Proton donor and outer coordination sphere control of CO2 reduction selectivity by a cobalt electrocatalyst in water
Semi-dry printing process for sustainable lithium-ion battery electrode manufacturing
papers.abstract: Current wet slurry process for lithium-ion battery electrode manufacturing raises significant concerns regarding energy consumption and environment sustainability due to its reliance on large volumes of toxic solvent. Meanwhile, the industrial adoption of emerging dry electrode technologies remains limited by material compatibility and processing constraints. To address these challenges, we present a semi-dry printing approach that bridges wet and dry electrode manufacturing while avoiding their respective limitations. This method involves spreading a layer of premixed feedstock onto a current collector, followed by selective inkjet deposition of pico-litre solvents to locally activate binder via dissolution. This strategy reduces solvent usage by approximately fivefold, corresponding to projected reduction of 32% in processing cost and 44% in energy consumption. Physical and electrochemical analysis reveal that semidry printed LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NMC811) electrodes exhibited enhanced transport kinetics enabled by an optimised microstructure, delivering higher maximum power and energy densities than conventional slurrycast electrodes. These results establish the potential of semi-dry electrode printing as a practical and scalable manufacturing solution for next-generation lithium-ion batteries.

papers.title: Transition-State Damping as a Mechanistic Descriptor of Rate Turnover in Chemical Reactivity
papers.abstract: Chemical rate theory has a well-developed thermodynamic axis but lacks a unified framework for the dynamical axis: the extent to which a reactive coordinate commits productively rather than recrossing. This research shows that dynamical commitment near a transition state is governed by a dimensionless damping ratio, χ = Γ eff /(2Ω TS), which separates oscillatory recrossing from overdamped sluggishness and is maximized at χ ≈ 1. Established theories of barrier crossing in electron transfer, proton-coupled electron transfer, and heterogeneous catalysis reduce locally to this same dynamical structure despite arising from distinct microscopic mechanisms. Three calibrated estimator routes connect χ to spectroscopic and computational observables with defined validity limits. Worked examples illustrate solvent-dependent rate turnover in TEMPO radical electron transfer and K-promoter effects in Fe(111)-catalyzed N 2 activation. Eight falsification tests are specified; the framework is refuted if the rate turnover predicted at χ ≈ 1 is absent when thermodynamic parameters are held fixed. This dynamical descriptor introduces an axis orthogonal to thermodynamic rate theory, enabling quantitative interpretation of recrossing, catalytic outliers, and mechanism transitions from a single dimensionless parameter. Reader's guide. Sections 1 and 2 establish the theoretical framework and estimator routes. Readers primarily interested in applications may proceed directly to Section 4 and consult the tables in earlier sections as needed. The validity boundaries in Section 5 should be reviewed before applying the framework to a new system.

papers.title: CL5D Hybrid Model and the N 12 Nitrogen Cage: A Preliminary Computational Study of a Strained Polynitrogen Structure
