papers.abstract: This paper introduces the CL5D Hybrid Model-a five-agent computational framework that maps chemical bonding states onto eight symbolic operators, which are encoded as dinucleotide pairs in a quaternary DNA scheme for long-term data storage. We apply the bonding-state heuristics embedded in CL5D to the rational design of N 12 , a proposed twelve-atom strained polynitrogen cage with multicenter bonding character. Density Functional Theory calculations (B3LYP/def2-SVP, Psi4) identify N 12 as a local minimum on the potential energy surface, with no imaginary vibrational frequencies at this level of theory. The computed thermodynamic energy release upon decomposition to 6N 2 yields an energy density of 67.3 MJ/kgapproximately 16 times that of TNT. These results are preliminary and contingent upon validation with higher-level quantum chemical methods and experimental verification of kinetic stability. The findings suggest the potential utility of CL5D bonding-state mapping as a design heuristic for polynitrogen high energy-density materials (HEDMs). Revision Note This version incorporates corrections from peer review, including revised terminology (multicenter bonding), hedged language throughout, additional methodological limitations (multi-reference character, 0 K approximation, dispersion), and restructured CL5D presentation.

papers.title: Multireference Wavefunction Methods for Accurate Adsorption Energies on Single-Atom Catalysts
papers.abstract: Density functional theory (DFT) is the dominant electronic structure approach for elucidating reaction mechanisms and predicting reactivity of graphene-based single-atom catalysts (SACs). However, the exchange-correlation approximations made in semi-local DFT suffer from electron self-interaction error, lack of a derivative discontinuity, and a single-reference description of the electronic structure, preventing predictive accuracy for correlated SAC materials. Alternatively, high-level multireference wavefunction methods offer a more reliable description of electron correlation with strong multiconfigurational characters involving transition metal centers, such as in SACs. In this work, we performed multireference wavefunction calculations, i.e., complete active space self-consistent field (CASSCF) coupled with complete active space second-order perturbation theory (CASPT2), to predict a key catalytic property, namely CO adsorption energy,

papers.title: From Oxo to Oxyl to Biradical: Systematic Multireference Calculations of Methane Activation at MOF Nodes
papers.abstract: In catalysis, density functional theory (DFT) is the workhorse electronic structure method, yet its single-reference nature can lead to considerable failures for reactions involving open-shell transition metals and complex transition states with significant static correlation. While multiconfigurational methods like complete active space self-consistent field offer a more robust description, their routine use is hindered by the need for expertise and repeated user intervention to successfully address the active space selection problem and produce meaningful results. Here, we introduce and validate an automated workflow, which centers on constraining the active space selection process to the relevant reactive region and avoiding the inclusion of unimportant orbitals in the active space, to construct consistent and meaningful active spaces to apply multireference methods to catalytic reactions steps. We use it to apply multiconfiguration pair-density functional theory and n-electron valence perturbation theory to the methane C-H activation step in the methane to methanol conversion cycle by metal-organic framework node catalysts with varied active metals. We find this step exhibits substantial multireference character, driving significant underprediction of multireference predicted barriers by standard DFT and qualitative differences in trends. We further explain the activation barrier trends with the bond order and spin density descriptors of the metal-oxo moiety on the catalyst. These results showcase the importance of multireference treatment for accurate modeling of this catalytic step and present an approach for their routine use in catalysis.

papers.title: Engineering Nitrogen Vacancies in Polymeric Carbon Nitride for Efficient Visible-Light Driven Hydrogen Evolution
papers.abstract: Polymeric carbon nitride (g-C 3 N 4 , GCN) is a highly promising metal-free photocatalyst for solar hydrogen production. However, its activity is still constrained by insufficient visible-light absorption and poor interlayer charge transport. Defect engineering of GCN has been widely deployed to promote photocatalytic hydrogen evolution efficiency, but a significant knowledge gap persists in linking specific defect structures to performance outcomes, and underlying mechanisms remain inadequately explored. Herein, we propose a controllable nitrogen-vacancy engineering strategy for GCN that induces interlayer contraction, thereby promoting interfacial charge transport. The tailored nitrogen vacancies broaden optical absorption, enhance interlayer electronic coupling, suppress charge carrier recombination, and lower the out-of-plane charge transfer barrier. Consequently, the optimized photocatalyst exhibits a ~ 23-fold enhancement in the hydrogen evolution rate compared to pristine GCN, while maintaining excellent stability over 50 hours of continuous illumination. This work establishes a viable regulation of nitrogen vacancies strategy for advancing g-C 3 N 4 -based photocatalysts toward large-scale solar hydrogen production.

papers.title: Fabrication of Sub-20 µm Microfluidic Channels Using Low-Cost FDM 3D-Printed Molds -A Lab-on-Cheap Approach
papers.abstract: In surface-based biosensors, an optimal microchannel geometry combines a large surface area in the XY plane with a reduced channel height along the Z-axis. However, fabricating microchannels with heights below 25 µm and/or incorporating micropillars remains challenging using low-cost, accessible methods. Here, we propose a simple and rapid fabrication method that exploits the intrinsic surface topography generated by fused deposition modelling (FDM) 3D printing. This layer-by-layer fabrication process inherently produces surface features that were exploited to form microchannels. The substrates were characterized to determine the dimensions and geometries using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), fluorescence microscopy, confocal microscopy, and 3D reconstructions. The results showed that surface features from the 3D-printed molds were successfully transferred into polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). When pressed to glass, the PDMS replicas form adjacent microchannels as small as 15 µm in height that provide a shallow and extensive sensing area. Flow tests confirmed the integrity of the channels and demonstrated that they could be sealed without plasma bonding. This approach demonstrates a significant advancement in the fabrication of sub-20 µm microchannels and in the development of alternatives to traditional micropillars, with high-resolution results achieved using standard, low-cost FDM printing.

papers.title: Elemental Sulfur Mediated One-Pot Synthesis of Poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) with High Conductivity for Organic Electronics
papers.abstract: Poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) is a benchmark n-type conductive polymer that combines exceptional electrical conductivity with outstanding environmental stability, positioning it as a pivotal material for the future of organic electronics. However, its practical deployment has been severely limited by intrinsic synthetic constraints. All reported routes suffer from unavoidable trade-offs: the original method requires weeks of dialysis in large volumes of DMSO to remove unreacted monomers, while later approaches either depend on toxic catalysts or involve energy-intensive purification processes. Here we report a transformative, metal-free, sulfur-mediated synthetic strategy that overcomes these longstanding bottlenecks and represents a decisive advance in PBFDO fabrication. Elemental sulfur (S8), an abundant and non-toxic oxidant, drives polymerization through a highly efficient cascade mechanism while simultaneously generating reducing species (hydrogen sulfide, H2S, and dimethyl sulfide, DMS) that in situ dope PBFDO into its conductive state. Consequently, the 2 resulting reaction solution can be used directly as a conductive polymer ink, completely eliminating prolonged purification processes-a major barrier to scalable PBFDO synthesis across all existing methods. This approach yields PBFDO with electrical conductivities up to 2059 S cm-1 , matching the highest values reported to date. Crucially, the method exhibits excellent scalability, enabling synthesis at the 500 mL scale while maintaining high conductivity (>1300 S cm-1), effectively resolving the scalability limitations that have hampered previous routes. Devices based on the resulting PBFDO demonstrate outstanding performance in thermoelectric and organic electrochemical transistor applications. Overall, this sulfur-mediated strategy simultaneously eliminates toxic reagents, complex and energy-intensive purification, and poor scalability in PBFDO synthesis, paving the way for the much desired widespread adoption of this highly promising n-type conductive polymers in organic electronics.

papers.title: Physics-Constrained Artificial Intelligence for Accelerated Experimental Discovery of Metal-Organic Frameworks in Gas Separation
papers.abstract: The development of efficient adsorbents is significant but challenging for gas separation. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) show great potentials in cutting separation energy consumption, while suffering from the problems caused by its vast diversity. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers effective solutions, but still faces high data consumption and poor extrapolation. To address this issue, taking C 3 H 6 /C 3 H 8 as an example, we proposed a physics constrained neural network (PCNN) which integrates physical knowledge into the framework and reach a great balance between prediction accuracy and physical rationality. Meanwhile, PCNN can be well trained using much less data (< 10%) than that required by conventional models, significantly cutting the training cost. Moreover, our model can provide accurate assessments of adsorption isotherms across the full pressure range even after being trained on data from only a single pressure point, demonstrating excellent extrapolation. Finally, a series of experiments were carried out to confirm the precision of PCNN in MOF screening. MOF (CCDC ID: CUIMDZ01) with ultrahigh C 3 H 6 /C 3 H 8 selectivity (IAST selectivity of 3.5×10 5) was successfully discovered, which demonstrated the potential of our model in material discovery. This work presents an efficient workflow with broad applicability for material discovery across diverse fields.

papers.title: Aggregation-Free Kinetic Dissection Reveals Energetic Control of Donor-Dependent NIR Exciplex Emission in a Perylene Diimide
papers.abstract: Exciplex formation between molecular donors and acceptors underpins a wide range of charge-transfer photophysical phenomena, yet its intrinsic kinetics and emissive behavior are often obscured by aggregation effects, particularly in perylene diimide (PDI)–based systems. Here we present a spectroscopic aggregation-free, solution-phase kinetic dissection of donor-dependent near-infrared (NIR) exciplex emission in a model PDI acceptor, N , N '-bis(ethylpropyl)perylene-3,4,9,10-tetracarboxylic diimide (EP-PDI). By rigorously establishing a spectroscopic monomeric benchmark for EP-PDI in toluene and restricting donor concentrations to the diffusion-limited regime, we isolate intrinsic exciplex formation and decay processes with pyrene and anthracene donors. Time-resolved measurements reveal diffusion-limited photoinduced electron transfer for both donors, while exciplex emission lifetimes and intensities exhibit pronounced donor dependence. Notably, faster exciplex formation does not translate into higher emissive efficiency. Long-range corrected DFT calculations reproduce the relative exciplex emission energies and oscillator-strength trends and show that the emission energy is primarily governed by donor-dependent stabilization of the EP-PDI-centered LUMO. Because the exciplex HOMO energies remain nearly unchanged, this shift modulates the emissive gap and controls the balance between radiative and nonradiative decay. Because exciplex-based charge-transfer states play central roles in NIR emitters, OLED hosts, and photochemical charge-separation systems, understanding the energetic factors governing their emissive behavior is essential. These results demonstrate that exciplex emission efficiency is governed by a balance between PET driving force and emissive gap, establishing a physically transparent framework for understanding and designing NIR charge-transfer emitters in aggregation-free solution.

papers.title: Programmable chemical sensitivities scale with extent of reaction instead of time
papers.abstract: The programmable oscillation of external energetic stimuli to drive a catalytic surface between distinct regimes of kinetic control has emerged as a strategy to surpass steady-state Sabatier limitations, yet experimental probes of the underlying kinetic origins of rate enhancement remain limited. Here, we demonstrate that chemical sensitivities such as apparent reaction orders, activation energies, and the Gibbs free energy, scale with reaction events (extent of reaction) under oscillatory conditions and not time. Using formic acid electro-oxidation on polycrystalline Pt as a model system, an analytical framework demonstrating that transient kinetic parameters are governed by reaction event weighting was developed, rather than time-weighted averages based on duty cycle. Experimentally-observable charge transfer during potentiodynamic oscillations provided a direct and quantitative measure for the extent of reaction, enabling prediction of dynamic chemical sensitivities across a wide range of oscillation timescales (10 -3 - 10 1 Hz) and reaction conditions (285-305 K, 0.05-2.5 M HCOOH). The extent of reaction formalism accurately reconciled experimentally-observed potentiodynamic reaction orders and activation barriers with steady-state behavior. Considering the overall driving force as an extent of reaction weighted average, programmable oscillations were found to significantly reduce the overpotential required to achieve a rate of catalytic turnover equal to potentiostatic operation. Although developed for electrochemical potential oscillations, the extent of reaction weighting framework is universally applicable to any catalytic system driven by programmable energetic stimuli (e.g. electrical, photonic, mechanical).

papers.title: Quantitative Host Cell Protein Analysis of Antibody-Based Protein Therapeutics using the Orbitrap Astral Mass Spectrometer
papers.abstract: Host cell proteins (HCPs) are endogenous proteins generated in cellular production systems alongside the biotherapeutic of interest. Removal of HCPs is crucial as they can be detrimental to product efficacy and patient safety. Due to its ability to determine individual HCP concentrations, liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry is increasingly utilised as an orthogonal method to ELISA for HCP monitoring. For protein biotherapeutics like monoclonal antibodies, their dynamic range makes detection of low-level HCPs difficult. The Orbitrap Astral MS has the potential to overcome such challenges, offering significant improvements in protein identifications in complex sample matrices while simultaneously reducing analysis times. Here, we utilise the Orbitrap Astral MS to perform HCP analysis on 37 protein biotherapeutics. The use of a short 60 samples-per-day separation method, dramatically reduced analysis time without sacrificing HCP identifications. 544 HCPs were detected across the cohort and 63.60% of those found to be quantifiable in at least one product using Hi3 quantitation. Functional analysis revealed that most detected HCPs had functions related to catalysis or binding, predominately catalytic activity (46%, 97 gene IDs) or protein binding (44%, 91 gene IDs). Over 80% of quantifiable HCPs were detected at concentrations below 10 ng/mg, ~9% below concentrations of 1 ng/mg. These included HCPs considered as “high-risk” by the Biophorum Development Group. This study shows how the Orbitrap Astral MS can improve detection of low-level HCPs while significantly reducing analysis times, allowing for rapid and more informed understanding of a products HCP content.

papers.title: Dose-Dependent and Irreversible Photodarkening of InP/ZnSe/ZnS Quantum Dots
papers.abstract: Indium phosphide-based quantum dots (QDs) are leading Cd-and Pb-free alternatives for photonic applications spanning 400-920 nm. However, their long-term photostability under prolonged illumination remains poorly understood. In this study, we systematically investigate the optical response of colloidal InP/ZnSe/ZnS core/shell/shell QDs exposed to white light under a dynamic inert atmosphere (glove box filled with circulating N 2 with O 2 <0.1 ppm, H 2 O<1.0 ppm). Upon illumination, the QDs exhibit 1 irreversible photodarkening, defined as a reduction in photoluminescence quantum yield with a nearly unchanged absorption spectrum. Photodarkening shows a linear dependence on absorbed photon dose, with photoexcitation deep into the conduction band inducing it more rapidly than resonant photoexcitation. Additionally, prolonged photoexposure leads to an emission redshift and an enhanced delayed-emission component, consistent with the selective photodarkening of individual QDs. Experiments in air and controlled humidity (10% and 90% relative humidity) indicate that photodarkening primarily arises from photooxidation by oxygen, whereas water promotes QD photoetching. This is further corroborated by control experiments in which the QDs are illuminated under dry oxygen (< 3 ppm H 2 O) and in a cuvette sealed by fusion under a N 2 atmosphere with < 0.1 ppm O 2 and < 1 ppm H 2 O. These experiments show that photodarkening does not occur in QDs contained in the fusion-sealed cuvette, while under dry oxygen the photodarkening rates of the QDs are even faster than in dry air. These findings advance understanding of InP-based QD photodegradation and provide a framework for quantifying their stability under light stress.

papers.title: From waste to resource: The untapped value of the separate collection of single-use laboratory plastics to enable recycling
Towards a direct recycling approach for complex Li/Na ion cathode mixtures: a selective leaching approach to separate components
papers.abstract: The large growth in Li/Na ion battery demand and use will ultimately lead to a significant amount of waste cells, when they reach the end-of-life requiring recycling to reclaim valuable resources. Commonly, the first stage of the battery recycling process involves shredding to liberate the materials for further processing. In cells where blended electrodes are a common occurrence, or cross-contamination occurs from the shredding of different cell chemistries, direct recycling-where the framework of the material remains intact-becomes increasing more challenging. Here we report a potential strategy for dealing with such complex mixtures, highlighting a selective leaching approach that can allow the selective separation of a commercial Na-ion cathode material (NFM: NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2) from a mixture with a 2 commercial Ni rich NMC (83% Ni) (NMC: LiNi0.83Mn0.06Co0.11O2) cathode material. A simple ascorbic acid treatment selectively dissolves the NFM leaving the NMC as a solid, allowing the subsequent direct recycling/regeneration of the NMC, along with the short loop recycling/regeneration of the NFM. The directly recycled NMC is of high quality, preserving the morphology of the pristine material and illustrating performances matching it. The NFM sample was also successfully regenerated from the leachate via a short loop approach, although further optimisation is required here to match the performance of the pristine NFM.

papers.title: Rhodanine to Oxorhodanine Switch Switches Switching Mechanism in a Monomethine Photoswitch
papers.abstract: Understanding the excited state dynamics of molecular photoswitches is key for advancing their design and optimizing their applications. Here we characterize the excited state chemistry of a recently reported oxorhodanine photoswitch through ultrafast spectroscopy and multireference quantum chemical calculations. Both Z and E forms undergo excited state isomerization reactions on a sub picosecond timescale to form a hot ground state and the product isomer. The reaction is shown to proceed entirely within the singlet manifold, in sharp contrast to the rhodanine photoswitches, which react through the triplet state. The difference is ascribed to the nπ * state arising from the C=S bond in the rhodanines. The dominance of ultrafast relaxation in the singlet state is confirmed by multireference ab-initio calculations which also show that the reaction coordinate involves torsion and pyramidialization. This reaction coordinate is consistent with the observed viscosity dependence. Calculations also indicate that the observed differences between ultrafast relaxation in the Z and E forms may arise from a shallow minimum on the excited state of the latter.

papers.title: Anti-Kasha emission in DCM-IFC: Computational evaluation of the Type III separated wave function hypothesis
papers.abstract: Kasha's rule, which states that the emitting electronic level of a given multiplicity is the lowest excited level of that multiplicity, is central to the understanding of photochemistry, and the exception due to a large (S1-S2) energy gap, exemplified by azulene, is well understood. Over the last few years, examples of large flexible molecules with modest (S1-S2) energy gaps have been reported to show anti-Kasha (AK) emission, and have been rationalised on the basis of highly spatially separated wavefunctions of the two states. Recently, a fluorophore, having such characteristics, was constructed from dicyanomethylene-4H-pyran (DCM) and integrated fluorescein-chromene (IFC), where a spirolactane open/closed switch was shown to regulate AK behaviour. The open form of the molecule illustrated dual emission which was interpreted as emission from both S1 and S2 states. Here, we investigate theoretically both the FC region and the interpolated pathways towards S2/S1-intersection region using implicit solvation. We calculate excited state energies and oscillator strengths employing both time-dependent density functional theory (with a range of functionals) and high-level wavefunction theories, characterising that the S1 state is the brighter of the valence excited states, dominated by locally excited character, whereas the S2 state is of charge-transfer character and is darker in comparison. Our ab-initio calculations indicate that the spectral absorption profiles for the two states overlap, and that there are barrierless internal conversion pathways from the FC region on the S2 surface towards the S2/S1-intersection region, which suggests that S2 population decay will be ultrafast in this molecule, with no AK emission. Moreover, energy difference between S1 and S2 states at each of the S1 and S2 excited state minima also reduce the possibility of thermal equilibration of population at timescales relevant to emission. Thus another explanation is required for the experimentally observed anomalous emission.

papers.title: Elemental Sulfur Mediated One-Pot Synthesis of Poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) with High Conductivity for Organic Electronics
papers.abstract: Poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) is a benchmark n-type conductive polymer that combines exceptional electrical conductivity with outstanding environmental stability, positioning it as a pivotal material for the future of organic electronics. However, its practical deployment has been severely limited by intrinsic synthetic constraints. All reported routes suffer from unavoidable trade-offs: the original method requires weeks of dialysis in large volumes of DMSO to remove unreacted monomers, while later approaches either depend on toxic catalysts or involve energy-intensive purification processes. Here we report a transformative, metal-free, sulfur-mediated synthetic strategy that overcomes these longstanding bottlenecks and represents a decisive advance in PBFDO fabrication. Elemental sulfur (S8), an abundant and non-toxic oxidant, drives polymerization through a highly efficient cascade mechanism while simultaneously generating reducing species (hydrogen sulfide, H2S, and dimethyl sulfide, DMS) that in situ dope PBFDO into its conductive state. Consequently, the 2 resulting reaction solution can be used directly as a conductive polymer ink, completely eliminating prolonged purification processes-a major barrier to scalable PBFDO synthesis across all existing methods. This approach yields PBFDO with electrical conductivities up to 2059 S cm-1 , matching the highest values reported to date. Crucially, the method exhibits excellent scalability, enabling synthesis at the 500 mL scale while maintaining high conductivity (>1300 S cm-1), effectively resolving the scalability limitations that have hampered previous routes. Devices based on the resulting PBFDO demonstrate outstanding performance in thermoelectric and organic electrochemical transistor applications. Overall, this sulfur-mediated strategy simultaneously eliminates toxic reagents, complex and energy-intensive purification, and poor scalability in PBFDO synthesis, paving the way for the much desired widespread adoption of this highly promising n-type conductive polymers in organic electronics.

papers.title: Bridging decision-making engines and workflow design in self-driving laboratories: A NIMO–IvoryOS integration study
papers.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) have the potential to accelerate scientific discovery, but their development often requires substantial programming effort. To lower this barrier, we present an integrated orchestration framework that combines NIMO and IvoryOS. In this framework, NIMO provides decision-making algorithms for autonomous experimentation, while IvoryOS offers an intuitive web interface automatically generated from Python code. We demonstrate the utility of this integration through an automated study of the coffee ring effect. The proposed framework offers a practical pathway toward more accessible SDLs.

papers.title: Controlling Confinement: Covalent Organic Frameworks induced Confinement of Water probed via EC-SEIRAS
papers.abstract: The study of confinement at the nanoscale in electrochemistry necessitates a well-understood bulk system, a way to induce reproducible confinement, and a method to probe the electrochemical/-catalytic behaviour at the interface. Herein, we utilize electrochemical surface enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (EC-SEIRAS) to characterize the potential-dependent behaviour of water confined in covalent organic framework (COF) films with varying nanopore sizes and chemical pore environments at a gold electrode. Combined with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and solvation shell spectroscopy, we revealed an increased sensitivity of hydrogen-bonded water (H 2 O HB ) as a function of the pore size in an isorecticular COF series as well as a coordinative chemical effect upon confinement. We additionally revealed a decreased sensitivity of H 2 O HB to the applied potential in these confined systems with respect to unmodified electrodes, providing a hitherto missing molecular level insight into the manifold observed effects of COF based confinement on electrochemical reactions in recent literature. These fundamental insights are critical to pave the way toward a knowledge-based design of COFs with specific pore sizes and chemical functionalities to improve reaction pathways and product selectivity in electrocatalytic applications.

papers.title: DNA Condensates Enable Crosstalk-Free Operation of Identical DNA Computing Cascades
papers.abstract: Abstract: DNA strand displacement reactions (SDR) have enabled the development of biosensing devices, molecular machines, and molecular computing. However, the need for high sequence orthogonality poses a major challenge to the modular integration and scaling of DNA SDR networks into more complex systems capable of advanced or parallel functions. Here, we propose the use of liquid-like DNA condensates with addressable barcodes for confining DNA SDR networks for parallel and selective operation of near-identical circuits that would otherwise show undesired crosstalk in homogenous solution. By introducing Transducer modules, specific inputs can be recognized by corresponding condensates and converted to a unified Messenger for triggering downstream DNA processing locally. This allows orthogonal execution of DNA SDRs of the same sequence design in different compartments in parallel without crosstalk and interference. Our strategy contributes a facile approach to enhance modularity and scalability in DNA SDR network design, paving the way for more sophisticated and complex functionalities.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning in Drug Molecular Design
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a powerful framework for drug development, offering a natural way to model the iterative and feedback-driven nature of the discovery process. This chapter provides a systematic overview of recent advances in RL-based methods for drug molecular design. We summarize key developments since 2017 and categorize existing approaches according to their underlying molecular representations, including one-dimensional strings, two-dimensional graphs, and three-dimensional geometries. By connecting these methods to their algorithmic foundations and practical applications, we highlight how RL enables efficient exploration of chemical space and goal-directed molecular design. Finally, we discuss current challenges and future opportunities toward more interpretable, data-efficient, and realistic reinforcement learning systems for drug discovery.

papers.title: What makes a suitable metal-organic framework linker? Discovery from a general chemical database
Room-Temperature Synthesis of Strongly Confined Lead Halide Perovskite Quantum Dots
papers.abstract: Colloidal CsPbBr 3 quantum dots (QDs) are promising for light-emitting applications, but their synthesis under ambient conditions remains challenging. Here we present a rapid, room-temperature (RT) method that produces highly stable CsPbBr 3 QDs within minutes using the zwitterionic ligand 2-ammonioethyl 2-octyl-1-dodecyl phosphate (OD-PEA). The strong binding of OD-PEA enables precise size control and effective passivation, yielding blue-emitting QDs (474 nm) with narrow linewidths (25 nm) and high photoluminescence quantum yields (up to 86 %). The QDs retain their optical quality for months in air and offer tunable emission from blue-cyan through ligand concentration, and from ultraviolet to deep red via halide exchange. A proof-of-concept perovskite light-emitting diode (PeLED) fabricated from these QDs exhibits appreciable electroluminescence (EL) at 480 nm with a low turn-on voltage. This work establishes a simple and scalable strategy for producing stable, strongly confined perovskite QDs, advancing their potential for next-generation optoelectronic and photonic technologies.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Driven Deep Learning Framework Integrating Molecular Descriptors and Multiview Images for Bioactivity Prediction
papers.abstract: Accurately predicting chemical bioactivity across large and structurally diverse chemical spaces remains a central challenge in computational toxicology and molecular design. This work presents a unified framework that systematically benchmarks three complementary modeling strategies for predicting PercentToxCast, an aggregate bioactivity index derived from the U.S. EPA ToxCast program. We integrate twenty seven physicochemical and topological descriptors with standardized three dimensional molecular renderings generated from RDKit conformers and evaluate descriptor based learning, multiview image based deep learning, and multimodal fusion of numerical and image derived features. Across 7,211 compounds, gradient boosted descriptor models deliver the strongest generalization, with CatBoost achieving a hold out R 2 of 0.398 and providing interpretable feature attributions that highlight hydrophobicity, polarity, and electronic structure as dominant contributors to broad assay engagement. A six view convolutional neural network captures geometric and steric information but attains lower external performance (R 2 of 0.217), indicating that image derived structure alone does not fully encode the physicochemical determinants of bioactivity. Multimodal fusion produces extremely strong cross validated performance but yields only modest hold out gains (R 2 of 0.241 to 0.259), revealing overfitting challenges associated with the high dimensional fused representation. This study establishes one of the first rigorously controlled evaluations of descriptor, image, and fused feature spaces for broad bioactivity modeling and demonstrates that descriptors remain the most informative single modality while image based geometry provides complementary but underexploited structural cues. By unifying these approaches within a transparent and reproducible benchmark, this work defines clear performance baselines and identifies key methodological limitations that must be addressed for next generation multimodal architectures. These findings provide a foundation for chemically intelligent models that integrate three dimensional structure with physicochemical properties to advance predictive toxicology, risk assessment, and data driven molecular design.

papers.title: Tautomerism-Governed Two-Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer in the Oxidation of a Molnupiravir by Electrogenerated Superoxide Radical Anion in N,N-dimethylformamide
papers.abstract: Molnupiravir is a nucleoside analog antiviral whose activity originates from the tautomeric flexibility of its N 4-hydroxycytosine moiety, yet its redox reactivity toward reactive oxygen species (ROS) has not been elucidated at the molecular level. In this study, we investigate the interaction between molnupiravir and electrogenerated superoxide radical anion (O2 •−) in aprotic N,N-dimethylformamide using cyclic voltammetry with density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Electrochemical measurements reveal loss of reversibility of the O2/O2 •− redox couple in the presence of molnupiravir and the emergence of a reversible redox couple at more negative potentials. Comparative analyses with N 4-hydroxycytosine, cytosine, and uracil demonstrate that this behavior is unique to the N 4-hydroxycytosine moiety. Thermodynamic and reaction coordinate analyses based on DFT show that the oxidation of molnupiravir by O2 •− proceeds via a concerted two-proton-coupled electron transfer (2PCET) mechanism rather than stepwise transfer. The oxime tautomer forms a hydrogen-bonded prereactive complex with O2 •− , enabling the simultaneous transfer of two protons and one electron in a single kinetic event. No persistent radical intermediates were detected by in situ electrolytic ESR spectroscopy, consistent with rapid tautomerization following PCET. These findings highlight how tautomerism governs PCET-driven redox reactivity in nucleobasemodified drugs, providing a framework linking electrochemistry and antiviral molecular design.

papers.title: AI-guided Autonomous Workflows Accelerate Kinetic Analysis of Polymer Depolymerization
papers.abstract: Deep understanding of polymerization and depolymerization kinetic behavior enables precision synthesis and manufacturing. However, traditional kinetic experiments are bottlenecked by labor-intensive sample collection and analysis practices and suffer reproducibility challenges due to human error and bias. Here, we introduce an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven automated kinetics platform to facilitate kinetic analysis and produce large volumes of high-quality kinetic data with minimal human intervention. Our autonomous workflow, encompassing automated synthesis, analysis, and cloud computing capabilities navigated complex parameter space using an importance-guided Bayesian optimization algorithm, effectively reducing sampling burden while maintaining accuracy in calculating apparent reaction rate constants. Kinetic data from these experiments supported the development of a stochastic simulation model to extract valuable mechanistic information. These capabilities were exploited for “scale-up” synthesis by conducting reactions in parallel, facilitating reproducible access to highly precise polymeric building blocks and showing that depolymerization provides a powerful alternative to polycondensation for the synthesis of telechelics. This work demonstrates how the throughput and accuracy of kinetic experiments can be significantly enhanced by synergizing AI and automation, highlighting the significant potential of these tools to transform the practice of fundamental science.

papers.title: Artificial Glycan Decoys: A Strategy to Inhibit Ebola Virus Infection
papers.abstract: Multivalency is a fundamental principle of lectin-glycan recognition, governing both affinity and specificity of carbohydrate-mediated molecular interactions. The human macrophage galactosetype lectin (MGL), a C-type lectin that selectively binds galactose (Gal) and Nacetylgalactosamine (GalNAc) residues, serves as an attachment factor for several enveloped viruses, including Ebola virus (EBOV). Here, we report the rational design and synthesis of GalNAc-based glycans multiantenna that structurally mimic viral surface glycosylation architectures and act as competitive inhibitors of MGL-mediated viral entry. A library of glycoconjugates bearing two, four, or eight Ser(GalNAc) units was chemically synthesized, and their interactions with the carbohydrate recognition domain of MGL (MGL-CRD) were investigated using 1 H, 15 N-HSQC-based NMR titrations and isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC). These studies revealed a pronounced multivalency-dependent increase in affinity and aviditydriven stabilization of the lectin-glycan complex, consistent with the simultaneous engagement of multiple MGL binding sites. Functional inhibition assays employing pseudotyped EBOV particles demonstrated that these multiantenna constructs efficiently block MGL-mediated viral entry, achieving submicromolar inhibitory potency. Together, these findings establish GalNAc-based multiantenna glycans as effective chemical decoys that disrupt lectin-mediated viral attachment and highlight multivalency as a powerful molecular design strategy for antiviral intervention.

papers.title: Conformer Generation Workflows for COSMO-RS Calculations: Are They All the Same?
papers.abstract: Predicting drug solubility remains a major challenge in the pharmaceutical industry, given its central role in formulation development and bioavailability. In this context, the conductor-like screening model for real solvents (COSMO-RS) is widely employed to estimate solvation and solubility properties, yet the accuracy of these predictions can strongly depend on the molecular conformations provided as input. Although this issue has been addressed in previous studies for specific molecules, no systematic evaluation of the influence of conformer-generation methods on the quality of COSMO-RS solubility predictions has been reported using large and chemically diverse datasets. Here, we assess four representative conformer-generation workflows, ranging from simple RDKit-based approaches to more elaborate semiempirical and density functional theory (DFT)-based pipelines, using a curated dataset comprising 942 experimental solubility values and 416 free energies of solvation. Despite substantial methodological differences and computational cost, all workflows yield comparable accuracy across the full dataset, with mean absolute errors close to one logarithmic unit, and all tend to underperform in the low-solubility regime, which remains a persistent challenge in computational chemistry. We further examine the use of conformer ensembles for representative molecules and compare their performance with solvent-aware single-conformer pipelines. For the cases analyzed, ensemble averaging provides moderate improvements but does not systematically outperform solvent-aware lowest-energy conformer selection. Notably, incorporating solvent information into the lowest-energy conformer identification stage can improve accuracy for molecules capable of establishing intramolecular interactions, such as hydrogen bonds. Overall, our results provide practical guidance for selecting conformer-generation strategies in high-throughput COSMO-RS applications and highlight solvent-aware workflows as a promising direction to improve predictive robustness without compromising computational efficiency.

papers.title: Ion-Conductive Vitrimers Based on Backbone-Type Triazolium Poly(ionic liquid)s: Counterion-Dependent Dynamics and Backbone Flexibility
papers.abstract: To simultaneously achieve high ionic conductivity and recyclability, vitrimers were prepared using backbone-type triazolium poly(ionic liquid)s (TPILs) that integrate ionic transport and dynamic network rearrangement via trans-N-alkylation. TPIL elastomers bearing I⁻, BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻, and TFSI⁻ counteranions were synthesized from “clickable” ionic liquid monomers, and their glass transition temperature (Tg), ionic conductivity, and vitrimeric dynamics were compared. Only the I⁻-based network exhibited stress relaxation at 170 °C, indicating that nucleophilic anions are important for bond exchange. However, a trade-off was observed between ionic transport and dynamic network rearrangement. Furthermore, mixed-anion TPIL elastomers using I⁻+TFSI⁻ exhibited lower Tg and higher ionic conductivity than I⁻-based elastomer, while still maintaining vitrimer-like relaxation. The segmental relaxation was decoupled from Arrhenius-type bond-exchange dynamics. Ionic conduction was dominated by segmental motion, with minimal contribution from cross-link exchange. This design combining flexible polymer backbones and cooperative anion engineering can create recyclable, highly conductive polymer electrolytes.

papers.title: Electrostatic solvation reshapes electrocatalyst nanoparticles under reaction conditions
papers.abstract: Electrocatalysis underpins sustainable energy conversion, yet electrostatic solvation at the electrolyte-catalyst interface has not been resolved as a tunable control parameter. Here we show that minute concentrations of weakly coordinating ions reversibly reshape Pt nanoparticles under operando conditions. Sub-second operando X-ray absorption and surface-enhanced infrared spectroscopy during the hydrogen evolution and ammonia oxidation reactions reveal that electric-field shielding stabilizes distinct morphologies. Weakly coordinating anions and more negative potentials favor compact, spherical particles, whereas weakly coordinating cations and less negative potentials promote flattening. Density functional theory and coordination-based energetic analyses support the thermodynamic plausibility of these electrostatically biased shapes. The kinetic consequences are reaction dependent, reflecting distinct structure sensitivities, as hydrogen evolution tracks interfacial water structure, whereas ammonia oxidation tracks particle geometry. Electrolyte-controlled electrostatic solvation thus provides a reversible, reaction-dependent lever to tune catalytic performance without altering catalyst composition.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn because the content was an unintentional duplication of another ChemRxiv preprint (10.26434/chemrxiv.15000655/v1).

papers.title: Secure and Distributed Cloud Platforms for Large-Scale Genomic Data Processing in Biotechnology
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of high-throughput sequencing technologies has generated unprecedented volumes of genomic data, creating significant computational and security challenges for biotechnology research and industrial applications. Large-scale genomic analysis requires scalable computing infrastructure, efficient data storage architectures, and robust mechanisms to safeguard sensitive biological information. Secure and distributed cloud platforms have emerged as a practical solution by integrating elastic computing resources, parallel processing frameworks, and advanced cryptographic protocols within virtualized environments. This paper examines the architectural foundations, security models, and performance considerations of distributed cloud systems tailored for genomic data processing. It discusses containerized workflows, distributed file systems, and workflow orchestration tools that enable reproducible and high-throughput bioinformatics pipelines. Particular attention is given to data confidentiality, integrity, and access control through encryption standards, federated identity management, and compliance-aware infrastructure. The study also evaluates the trade-offs between public, private, and hybrid cloud deployments in terms of cost efficiency, scalability, regulatory adherence, and latency. By synthesizing recent technological developments and practical deployment strategies, this work highlights how secure cloud-based infrastructures can accelerate genomic research while maintaining ethical and legal standards. The findings underscore the importance of integrating cybersecurity principles with distributed computing design to support precision medicine, agricultural biotechnology, and large-scale population genomics initiatives.

papers.title: QUAD: A Composite Risk Framework Integrating Uncertainty, Applicability Domain, and Model Disagreement for Reliable QSAR Predictions
papers.abstract: Quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) models are widely used to predict molecular bioactivity; however, conventional global performance metrics provide limited insight into the reliability of individual predictions. To address this limitation, we introduce QUAD, a post-hoc framework that integrates three complementary indicators of prediction risk: ensemble-based model uncertainty, applicability domain (AD) risk, and model disagreement. QUAD enables molecule-level reliability assessment without modification of the underlying predictive model. The framework was evaluated on two Alzheimer's disease-relevant targets, β-site amyloid precursor protein cleaving enzyme 1 (BACE1) and glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK3β), using ECFP4 fingerprints and Random Forest regression with fixed external train-test splits. Baseline models demonstrated consistent generalizability, with test-set performance of R² = 0.638 (RMSE = 0.801, MAE = 0.577) for BACE1 (1,514 molecules) and R² = 0.692 (RMSE = 0.777, MAE = 0.564) for GSK3β (4,093 molecules), supported by cross-validated and external Q² metrics. Ensemble-based uncertainty exhibited a moderate association with absolute prediction error for BACE1 (Pearson r = 0.366) and a stronger relationship for GSK3β (r = 0.443), highlighting dataset-dependent reliability behavior. The composite QUAD reliability score reflected these patterns, showing conservative stratification for BACE1 (r = 0.310) and a clearer monotonic relationship with error for GSK3β (r = 0.439). These findings demonstrate that prediction reliability in QSAR modeling is inherently multifactorial and target-specific. Rather than optimizing a single uncertainty measure, QUAD integrates heterogeneous risk signals into a transparent reliability ranking that supports compound prioritization and risk-aware decision-making. Owing to its model-agnostic design and minimal computational overhead, QUAD can be readily incorporated into existing QSAR workflows, providing a practical framework for molecule-level reliability assessment in computational drug discovery.

papers.title: Consequences of Monomer Impurities on Network Characteristics and Dynamic Mechanical Behavior of an Eugenol-based Covalent Adaptable Network
papers.abstract: Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) are an emerging class of polymers exhibiting the potential to introduce recyclability into polymer networks. For industrial applications, robustness of material properties and predictable dynamic behavior are highly desirable. In this study, diepoxides of varying purity were used to prepare hybrid CANs. Hybrid CANs are based on both dynamic vinylogous urethane bonds and permanent bonds formed by the reaction of amines and epoxides. We specifically investigate the robustness of the materials dynamic exchange behavior against impurities that impair or modify the network characteristics. Stress relaxation experiments reveal that the dynamic behavior remains relatively stable up to ca. 23 % monomer impurity. At higher impurity levels we observe pronounced changes of the exchange dynamics. All materials, regardless of purity, exhibit incomplete stress relaxation. Macroscopic manifestations of this fact are visible defects in the nominally purest materials upon reshaping. Thermal and dynamic-mechanical analyses further show that network density and glass transition temperature decrease with increasing impurity, while overall the thermal stability remains largely unaffected. The results demonstrate that hybrid CANs based on vinylogous urethane exchange chemistry can tolerate moderate monomer impurities without losing key dynamic properties, offering insights for industrial-scale processing and material design.

papers.title: Synthesis of a nucleic acid reporter for molecular glue discovery in DNA encoded libraries
papers.abstract: Molecular glues, small molecules that bring two proteins together, are a promising drug modality. By acting as mediators of protein-protein interactions, molecular glues give unprecedented control over protein fate, allowing disease-causing proteins to be degraded, re-localized, inactivated or even reactivated to resume normal function. Despite the widespread interest in molecular glue drug development in both academic and pharmaceutical settings, the rational design of new molecular glues has been slowed by the limited methods for their detection in high-throughput screens. To address this, we conceptualized and developed a beadfree proximity-based screening approach to record molecular glue binding events in DNA encoded libraries (DELs). We describe the synthesis of a nucleic acid reporter of molecular glue binding and demonstrate its implementation with a protein-fragment complementation-based hit selection strategy. Finally, we show that the DNA barcodes of putative molecular glues can be enriched from a pool of non-molecular glue binders by PCR. This proof-of-concept study lays the groundwork for the discovery of novel molecular glue drug candidates and delves into synthetic strategies for tuning DNA-DNA molecular recognition.

papers.title: Tracing proton-lithium exchange and coincident surface contaminant decomposition upon heating of Li + -conductive garnet phase powders
papers.abstract: Garnet-phase Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) is a promising solid-state electrolyte in lithium metal batteries, but suffers from contaminant formation upon exposure to ambient conditions. This work quantifies the impurities present in commercially synthesized and procured LLZO powder and characterizes the removal of these contaminants via heat treatment under argon. We identify 3 unique contaminant removal regimes, one of LiOH at lower temperatures (<350 ˚C) and two of Li2CO3 at intermediate (350-550 ˚C) and high (>550 ˚C) temperatures. Removal of LiOH and the intermediate Li2CO3 proceed through a mechanism involving beneficial H + /Li + exchange with the LLZO lattice, whereas high temperature Li2CO3 removal proceeds through the thermal decomposition mechanism of Li2CO3 to evolve CO2 and deposit solid Li2O. Heating to 800 ˚C allows for the removal of 97% of the Li2CO3 and 85% of the LiOH present in the as-given materials, and we observe that heat treatment in a stagnant atmosphere is less effective than treatment under active gas flow. We show that relithiation of the LLZO lattice improves Li + transport across the LLZO particle interface when immersed in a Li +-bearing organic electrolyte, and that the protonation of LLZO contributes more to slowing interfacial Li + transport than the presence of Li2CO3.

papers.title: Spectroscopic neutron imaging for chemically sensitive in situ electrolyte characterisation
Aromaticity-Driven Regioselective Cyclodehydrogenations in Azahelicenes with High-Performance Circularly Polarized Luminescence
papers.abstract: While increasing helical length n has been proven-theoretically and experimentally-to amplify circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) performance of [n]helicene derivatives, the highly efficient synthetic approaches and the corresponding reaction mechanism investigation remain limited. In this work, the helical lengths of azahelicenes Aza[n] have been successfully extended from Aza[7] to Aza[9] and Aza[11] via a facile two-step approach by different arylamine precursors. The reaction is proposed to proceed via C-N bond-forming cyclization from a cationic intermediate generated by an in situ-formed hypervalent iodine species, thereby favoring α-selectivity to retain aromaticity. All the helical structures are ambiguously confirmed by single-crystal Xray diffraction. Comprehensive photophysical studies and density functional theory calculations reveal that Aza[11] exhibits outstanding chiroptical properties, achieving high absorption dissymmetry factors (|gabs|max = 3.2×10-2) and luminescence dissymmetry factors (|glum|max = 3.0×10-2) ranking among the highest values reported for organic CPL emitters.

papers.title: Three Physically Distinct Modes of Protein Adsorption on Zwitterionic Polymer Brushes
papers.abstract: Zwitterionic polymer brushes are extensively used to fabricate antifouling interfaces. However, the factors governing their protein adsorption behavior remain poorly understood because hydration, chain conformation, and electrostatic interactions occur simultaneously. In this study, we demonstrate that protein adsorption on phosphorylcholine-based zwitterionic brushes does not follow a single hydration-driven pathway. Instead, it proceeds via three distinct adsorption modes, each of which exhibits a characteristic viscoelastic signature. By independently varying the graft density and molecular weight and analyzing the interfacial mechanics using quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation, we identified the conditions that promote substrate-mediated rigid adsorption, hydrated weak adsorption, or brush internal ternary adsorption. These modes exhibit 2 differential dependencies on brush architecture, revealing that minimal adsorption occurs at intermediate chain densities where substrate exposure, hydration repulsion, and polymer-protein dipolar interactions are balanced. Collectively, these findings establish a mechanistic framework for protein adsorption on zwitterionic brushes and provide quantitative guidelines for the rational design of next-generation antifouling materials.

papers.title: Remote Modification-Induced Butterfly Effect on Nonfullerene Acceptor Aggregation for Efficient Organic Solar Cells
Highly Chemoselective Access to Alkyl-Sulfur Compounds via N2 Extrusion of Alkyl Hydrazines
papers.abstract: Sulfur(VI)-containing functional groups, such as sulfonamides, sulfinates, and sulfonyl fluorides, are ubiquitous in pharmaceuticals, conferring unique physicochemical properties that enhance metabolic stability, solubility, and bioactivity across diverse therapeutic areas. Despite their prevalence-appearing in over 300 FDA-approved drugs and rising to 20% of new approvals in 2024-synthetic access to alkyl S(VI) derivatives remains fragmented, often requiring multi-step sequences from scarce precursors or harsh conditions that limit functional-group tolerance and scalability. Here we report a unified platform that enables divergent synthesis of alkyl S(VI) from abundant, unactivated feedstocks including ketones, alcohols, amines, and other structurally complex molecules. Central to this method is the use of alkyl hydrazines (or their sulfonylated derivatives) as practical radical precursors, readily prepared via conventional transformations from these feedstocks. Upon simple thermal activation, these hydrazines undergo efficient homolysis to generate alkyl radicals under exceptionally mild and operationally simple conditions, without the need for photocatalysts, expensive metals or reagents, and elaborate setups. The remarkable chemoselectivity of these transformations is exemplified through the synthesis of over 70 sulfur-containing molecules, including direct functionalization of complex natural products without resorting to protecting group chemistry.

papers.title: Enantioselective synthesis of 1,3-bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes as meta-benzene bioisosteres
papers.abstract: Bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes are rigid bridged scaffolds with well-defined exit vectors that have been proposed as appropriate bioisosteres of phenyl rings. Although many racemic syntheses have recently emerged, access to single enantiomers of these skeletons remains a major challenge. To provide a solution to that, we have developed an enantioselective copper-catalyzed protoborylation to obtain 1,3-disubstituted bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes as suitable mimics of meta-benzenes. The stereocontrolled formation of these bicyclic frameworks, which present an unprecedented substitution pattern, was achieved through a desymmetrization of bicyclo[2.1.1]hex-2-enes. Remarkably, the employment of such strained alkenes had no precedent in catalysis, providing a novel platform for the functionalization of the bicyclo[2.1.1]hexane core. The obtained versatile enantioenriched building blocks have been incorporated into the structure of different drug analogues, leading to an improvement of solubility, metabolic stability and permeability in comparison with the parent drugs. Moreover, the drug analogues showed a retention of biological activity by targeting the same molecular receptors, which unambiguously validated them as suitable meta-benzene bioisosteres.

papers.title: DLP-Based 3D Printing of pH-Responsive Antimicrobial Peptide/GelMA Composite Hydrogels for Advanced Wound Dressing Applications
Systematic Trends in Water Properties Across Jacob's Ladder Density Functionals
papers.abstract: Kohn-Sham density functional theory is the workhorse of computational materials science and chemistry, but the optimal choice of exchange-correlation approximation for a given system is often unclear. Traditional benchmark studies typically compare selected density functional approximations (DFAs) against high-level quantum chemistry results for small structures and static energies, rather than against experimental thermodynamic or response properties. Here, we show how machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) allow for molecular dynamics simulations of these properties at scale, thereby providing a thermodynamic benchmark for DFAs. Focusing on the wellstudied but challenging case of bulk water at ambient conditions, we benchmark 11 DFAs spanning the top four rungs of Jacob's ladder (GGA, meta-GGA, hybrid, and double hybrid) with and without empirical dispersion corrections. Using MLIPs trained on each DFA, we compute infrared spectra, heat capacities, radial distribution functions, and diffusivities. We find a general improvement up Jacob's ladder towards double hybrids, though there is substantial variation between DFAs within the same rung and across different properties. Dispersion corrections yield only a modest influence on the computed properties. We elucidate the similarities and hierarchy among DFAs, both based on correlating the DFA energies and forces for the same training configurations, and based on analyzing the finite-temperature observables. Our work thus demonstrates the power of MLIPs for finite-temperature benchmarking of electronic structure methods.

papers.title: Donor extended blue TADF dendrimer for high performance solution-processed OLEDs
papers.abstract: Achieving highly efficient and stable blue solution-processed OLEDs remains an outstanding challenge in the field. Here, we introduce a rational donor decoration strategy and apply it to the spiroacridine donor of the TADF emitter DOBNA-SpAc (aka. TDBA-SAF), exemplified in the emitter DOBNA-SpAc-DCz. By introducing ter(tert-butylcarbazole) units at the 2 and 7 positions of the acridine moiety, solubility and hole-transport properties are improved without compromising the blue emission endemic to DOBNA-SpAc. This emitter has a high photoluminescence quantum yield, FPL, of 93% in 20 wt% doped films in PPF, a very small singlet-triplet energy gap (ΔEST = 0.01 eV), and thus fast reverse intersystem crossing (kRISC >1 × 10 6 s-1), resulting in a short delayed lifetime of 2 µs. Solution-processed OLEDs with DOBNA-SpAc-DCz reached a maximum external quantum efficiency, EQEmax, of 29.4% at CIE coordinates of (0.145, 0.221). By probing different electron transport materials and comparing to devices using DOBNA-SpAc we found that the introduction of carbazole substituents promotes improved hole transport and a more spatially distributed recombination zone, while the faster kRISC suppresses triplet-related annihilation processes. These results demonstrate that the targeted peripheral donor dendron decoration of spiroacridine-based TADF emitters is an effective strategy to achieve highly efficient emitters suitable for solution-processed OLED applications.

papers.title: Surface Functionalization of ZIF-8 Nanoparticles with Accessible Groups for Covalent Conjugation
papers.abstract: Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-8 (ZIF-8) is a prominent metal-organic framework for biomedical applications, yet its lack of reactive surface groups limits controlled covalent functionalization. Here, we introduce amino (-NH₂), aldehyde (-CHO), and carboxylate (-COOH) functionalities onto nanosized ZIF-8 via solvent-assisted ligand exchange and subsequent post-synthetic modification while preserving crystallinity and morphology. The degree of ligand exchange (4-15%) was tuned by reaction time and quantified by NMR, with surface-selective incorporation supported by the diffusioncontrolled nature of the exchange process. Chemical accessibility of the introduced groups was confirmed through covalent conjugation reactions, including fluorescein labeling and carbodiimidemediated amide formation, combined with competitive washing experiments to verify bond stability. This strategy provides a versatile platform for equipping ZIF-8 nanoparticles with reactive surface functionalities, enabling modular conjugation of imaging agents, targeting ligands, and biomolecules for advanced biomedical applications.

papers.title: Computational Discovery of Selective KRAS G12D Inhibitors Using a Consensus Docking Pipeline A Proof-of-Concept Structure-Based Virtual Screening Study Independent Research Computational Biology / Machine Learning
papers.abstract: KRAS G12D is one of the most prevalent oncogenic mutations in pancreatic, colorectal, and lung cancers, yet it remained historically difficult to target due to the shallow topology of the KRAS binding surface. Recent advances in mutant-selective inhibitors have renewed interest in computational approaches capable of identifying candidate molecules with mutation-specific affinity. In this study, a proof-of-concept consensus docking pipeline was developed to identify potential KRAS G12D inhibitors using structure-based virtual screening. A small filtered chemical library was evaluated using three docking engines (AutoDock Vina, Smina, and Gnina) with weighted consensus scoring. Binding poses were validated using protein-ligand interaction profiling to confirm the presence of a salt bridge with Asp12, a key structural feature of the G12D mutant pocket. Cross-docking against wild-type KRAS was performed to evaluate mutation selectivity. From an initial screen of ten molecules, four candidates demonstrated favorable docking scores and interaction geometry consistent with Asp12 engagement. Three compounds exhibited near-zero predicted affinity for wild-type KRAS while maintaining strong G12D binding, yielding a selectivity gap exceeding −8.3 kcal/mol in the top candidates. Although preliminary, these results suggest that consensus docking combined with structural interaction validation can identify mutation-selective ligands without requiring GPU resources. Experimental validation and larger-scale screening will be required to confirm these computational predictions.

papers.title: Closed-Loop Bayesian Optimization for the Synthesis of Amine-Grafted Resins for Direct Air Capture
papers.abstract: Direct air capture (DAC) of CO 2 remains limited by adsorbent performance. Adsorption kinetics are a particularly underexplored lever to improve adsorbents, despite their significance in realistic processes. Today, the profile of 'the' optimal DAC adsorbent displaying high CO 2 uptake and selectivity as well as fast sorption kinetics remains unknown. Here, we present a closed-loop approach combining high-throughput synthesis and characterisation with Bayesian optimization to understand how the material synthesis space impacts adsorbent properties and how it can ultimately be optimized to enhance adsorption-based DAC performance. To carry out this study, we chose amine-functionalized porous adsorbents as our model system. By jointly optimizing adsorption kinetics and equilibrium CO 2 uptake at 400 ppm, the framework identifies high-performing materials while experimentally mapping a Pareto front. Sorbents with the highest CO 2 uptakes exhibit the slowest kinetics, and vice versa. We link this trade-off to the pore structure of the materials and how the pore geometry imposes diffusion constraints. The optimization study uncovers adsorbents with order-of-magnitude higher adsorption kinetics than benchmark adsorbents at half the uptakes. Beyond this model system, our Bayesian optimization framework is a blueprint for multi-objective materials optimization in fields beyond DAC adsorbents.

papers.title: Conjugated Depolymerizable Organic Excitonic Polymeric Materials: A Platform for Functional and Sustainable Electronics
papers.abstract: Organic excitonic polymeric materials underpin a wide range of optoelectronic, photonic, and biointerfacing technologies, from organic photovoltaics and light-emitting devices to near-infrared imaging and organic bioelectronics. With increased use in biological, wearable, and environmentally transient contexts, the need and interest for chemically degradable and depolymerizable organic excitonic systems is growing more apparent. Traditionally, high excitonic and electronic performance has been associated with uninterrupted π-conjugation along polymer backbones. However, emerging evidence demonstrates that efficient excitonic function can persist, and in some cases be enhanced, in architectures that intentionally break or segment conjugation. In this Perspective, we examine recent advances in degradable organic excitonic conjugated polymers through an architecture-driven lens, spanning fully conjugated backbones, partially conjugated and pseudo-conjugated polymers, and systems incorporating dynamic covalent linkages. By summarizing developments across organic electronics, photonic nanomaterials, and bioelectronics, we highlight common excitonic principles that unify these seemingly disparate approaches. We further discuss how conjugation breaking and dynamic bonding expand the design space for sustainable and transient conjugated polymers. Finally, we outline key challenges and opportunities for future research. This Perspective aims to provide a conceptual framework for designing nextgeneration organic excitonic materials that balance functional performance with controlled degradation and circular lifecycle considerations.

papers.title: Fluidic-enabled formation of EGaIn capsules and droplets with tunable surface chemistry and electromechanics
papers.abstract: The combination of high electrical conductivity and fluidity and biocompatibility exists in liquid metals including eutectic gallium-indium (EGaIn) but their application remains restricted because of spontaneous oxide development and unstable flow behavior. Here we describe a microfluidic method to create EGaIn droplets and capsules with adjustable dimensions and mechanical and surface properties. The acidity level of the suspending fluid, ethanol, determines whether EGaIn will create oxide-covered capsules or non-oxidized liquid droplets. The oxide coating stabilizes aspherical shapes, which deform irreversibly. Droplets readily reform into spheres after applied stress is removed, but are susceptible to coalescence. A thiolated PEG-click complex forms selfassembling structures at metal-liquid interfaces to protect droplets from merging while allowing surface modification. When cast in thin films, the fluidic-generated EGaIn structures exhibit different electromechanical responses: oxide-coated capsules function as field-effect elements while thiol-stabilized droplets operate as ohmic conductors. By integrating microfluidic generation, shape programmability, and chemical stabilization, we open new pathways to multifunctional liquid-metal architectures with controllable electromechanical response. in thin films using four-point probe measurements. 176 In this work, we establish a unified microfluidic plat-177 form for microscale EGaIn formulations that enables si-178 multaneous control over droplet size, shape, mechani-179 cal response, and surface functionalization. By chemi-180 cally modulating pinch-off conditions, we generate tun-181 able droplets or capsules, assess mechanical reversibility 182

papers.title: OT2-CherryPick: A Zero-Install Web Platform for Orchestrating Complex Liquid Handling on the Opentrons OT-2
papers.abstract: Liquid handling automation is fundamental to modern high-throughput research, yet existing tools for the Opentrons OT-2 robot present researchers with a dichotomy: graphical interfaces such as Protocol Designer offer accessibility but lack flexibility for complex workflows, while code-based solutions require programming expertise that excludes many wet-lab scientists. Cherry-picking and sample reformatting operations, common in combinatorial chemistry and screening workflows, remain particularly underserved. Here we present OT2-CherryPick, a web-based platform that bridges this gap by combining zero-install deployment with comprehensive liquid handling customization. The system features a visual deck layout editor, CSV-driven transfer specification, and integration with the official Opentrons application for seamless deployment. Comprehensive liquid handling parameters are configurable through the interface, enabling precise control over aspiration, dispensing, and tip management across diverse experimental scenarios. All configuration compiles into self-contained protocol files requiring no external dependencies at runtime. Built-in simulation ensures protocols are validated before robot operation. The platform architecture exposes all protocol operations through a modular service layer compatible with the Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling AI-assisted workflows. This integration exemplifies a novel approach to laboratory software architecture, making protocol operations natively accessible to AI assistants through structured, validated tool invocations. OT2-CherryPick is open source and freely available at https://github.com/HiteSit/OT2_CherryPick.

papers.title: Understanding the Adsorption and Desorption Dynamics for On-surface Systems
papers.abstract: The adsorption and desorption of gas-phase molecules on solid surfaces are elementary steps in heterogeneous catalysis. However, capturing these dynamics under operando conditions remains challenging due to the limitations of static models. In this study, we investigate the dynamics of CO adsorption on Ru(0001) by combining machine learning potential energy surfaces (ML-PES) with umbrella sampling (US) molecular dynamics. By analyzing the temperature-dependent (300–800 K) potential-of-mean-force (PMF) profiles derived via the Weighted Histogram Analysis Method (WHAM), we reveal that distinct desorption barriers emerge above 400 K. Local PMF and molecular orientation analyses demonstrate that these barriers are entropy-driven, originating from the confined rotational motion of the adsorbate at the desorption bottleneck. Furthermore, a critical comparison between rigid and relaxed surface models reveals a compensation effect: neglecting lattice motion leads to an underestimated activation enthalpy and an overestimated entropy, which cancel out to yield accurate rate constants despite incorrect thermodynamic descriptions. Finally, unbiased MD simulations provide direct evidence of adsorbate-induced surface reconstruction, supporting a dynamic picture in which active sites are continuously created and annihilated. Our work highlights the indispensable role of surface lattice degrees of freedom and offers a robust framework for understanding complex gas-surface interactions.

papers.title: From Kinetic Gateways to Thermodynamic Locking: Unveiling the Dynamic Adsorption Landscape of CO on Pt(111)
papers.abstract: The adsorption of CO on Pt(111) serves as a benchmark system in surface science, yet resolving the discrepancies between theoretical predictions and experimental observations regarding site preference and structural evolution remains a challenge. Here, we present a comprehensive coverage-temperature study that combines generalized simulated annealing on a high-precision potential energy surface (PES) with molecular dynamics-based free energy calculations. Our statistical analysis reveals that surface relaxation plays a decisive role. It enhances the stability of top sites at low coverage and eliminates metastable bridge sites at saturation (0.750 ML), driving the formation of a perfect "top + hollow" hexagonal pattern. Crucially, free energy landscapes reveal a non-monotonic evolution of surface mobility. A critical "kinetic gateway" at ∼0.611 ML was identified, where migration barriers between top, bridge, and hollow sites nearly vanish, creating a highly fluid phase that facilitates complex structural rearrangements. In contrast, at the saturation limit, the CO adlayer becomes thermodynamically locked into deep potential wells with high diffusion barriers, indicative of a rigid "catalyst poisoning" state. These findings bridge the gap between zero-temperature static models and finite-temperature experimental realities, offering a unified theoretical framework for understanding the dynamic interplay between thermodynamic site competition and kinetic accessibility.

papers.title: SO2 Transfer Enabled by an Easy-to-Handle Ionic Liquid
papers.abstract: Herein, the ionic liquid [NEt3Me][Cl(SO2)n] is reported as a reversible sulfur dioxide storage medium and transfer reagent for organic synthesis. Vapor pressure measurements revealed that the ionic liquid can store up to 3.66 equivalents of SO2 at room temperature, which can be released in a controlled manner upon heating or depressurization. The physicochemical properties were investigated, and long-term stability was demonstrated, as no decomposition was observed for more than six months. Based on its solid-state structure, the bonding analysis indicated a covalent sulfur-chlorine interaction, which is consistent with conducted Raman studies and quantum chemical calculations. Atom economy and cost estimates are compared with those of commonly used SO2 surrogates, highlighting the developed transfer reagent as an inexpensive and (atom-)economic alternative for laboratory-scale applications. The synthetic utility of [NEt3Me][Cl(SO2)n] is further demonstrated, enabling the synthesis of valuable organosulfur compounds such as 3-sulfolenes, sulfonamides, sulfones, and sulfonyl fluorides in good to excellent yields. Importantly, the incorporation of SO2 is scalable, rendering [NEt3Me][Cl(SO2)n] as a safe and user-friendly SO2 transfer reagent for synthetic applications.

papers.title: Endogenous and Phytochemical Acyl-Tryptamine Conjugates: Six Structural Classes of Novel Multi-Target Prodrug Candidates for Neuroinflammation, Metal Dysregulation, and Serotonergic Modulation
papers.abstract: A novel series of eighteen N-acyl tryptamine conjugates is presented, organised into six structural classes: indol-3-oyl, thiazol-2-oyl, imidazol-4-oyl, feruloyl, coumaroyl, and salicyloyl. All compounds share a secondary amide bond linking the acyl moiety to substituted tryptamine scaffolds bearing 4-hydroxy, 5-methoxy, or 4-acetoxy substitution, with enzymatic hydrolysis proposed to simultaneously release a pharmacologically active tryptamine and a bioactive acyl fragment. The six classes introduce distinct secondary mechanisms: AhR activation, endogenous Zn²⁺/Cu²⁺ chelation, NF-κB inhibition, MAO-B inhibition, enhanced CNS penetration, and serotonergic-COX dual activity. All eighteen compounds are new chemical entities; no synthesis or biological testing has been performed. SMILES strings, predicted physicochemical properties, and hypothetical pharmacological profiles are provided to stimulate further investigation.

papers.title: Can LLMs Reason About Solubility? The SoluBench Benchmark for Pure and Mixed Solvent Systems
papers.abstract: Solubility prediction is a fundamental task in chemistry and drug discovery, yet the capability of large language models (LLMs) to solve solubility-related problems remains underexplored. Here we present SoluBench, a benchmark comprising 9806 questions across four tasks of increasing complexity, designed to evaluate LLMs’ performance on solubility reasoning in both pure and mixed solvent systems. The tasks include pairwise solvent comparison (Task 1), single-best solvent selection (Task 2), co-solvent effect prediction (Task 3), and pairwise compound comparison (Task 4). The benchmark is grounded in experimental data from BigSolDB 2.0 and MixtureSolDB datasets. Systematic evaluation of over 20 proprietary and open-source LLMs reveals that frontier proprietary models achieve strong performance on solvent-oriented tasks, with Gemini 3 Flash reaching 90.6%, 66.2%, and 86.4% accuracy on Tasks 1, 2, and 3, respectively. Open-source models consistently underperform their proprietary counterparts. The solute-focused Task 4 is exceptionally challenging in standard settings, requiring explicit reasoning to achieve functional accuracy, particularly for polar aprotic solvents such as DMSO and DMF. Across all tasks, a universal performance bottleneck is identified for large solutes (MolWt > 500 Da). These findings demonstrate that while LLMs possess intrinsic chemical reasoning capabilities sufficient for qualitative solubility assessment in technological practice, significant limitations in molecular structure understanding persist.
