papers.title: Assessing Thermodynamic Equilibrium and Corrective approach for VOCs Adsorption on Microporous Activated Carbon
papers.abstract: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are ubiquitous air pollutants arising from industrial, vehicular, and household sources, which present significant risks to both environmental quality and human health. Advances in air purification increasingly rely on high-performing adsorbents for VOC removal, with material innovations in microporous and mesoporous frameworks driving the field toward more efficient and selective remediation methods. However, accurately characterizing adsorbent affinity for VOCs at trace levels remains challenging due to extremely slow adsorption kinetics in highly confining ultramicroporous solids. In this context, accurately determining the Henry constant K H for VOC adsorption in microporous solids at low pressures is limited by difficulties in reaching thermodynamic equilibrium in standard experimental methods. Here, a thermodynamically grounded three-step methodology is introduced for reliable estimation of the Henry constant in such diffusion-limited systems. In practice, this strategy is illustrated by considering cyclohexane adsorption on commercial activated carbon. The approach involves (1) measuring adsorption isotherms at elevated temperatures (which ensure that thermodynamic equilibrium is reached), (2) extrapolating to the target temperature via Polanyi’s adsorption potential theory, and (3) finally deriving K H from the recalculated low-pressure region. Compared to conventional single-temperature volumetric measurements — where equilibrium is hardly attained at low pressure — this method allows reconstructing the adsorption isotherm. This strategy, which is validated by showing that the adsorption isotherms match those obtained from independent breakthrough experiments, reveals systematic underestimation of adsorption at low pressure with standard protocols (up to a 15-fold difference in K H ). This study demonstrates how corrections based on Polanyi’s adsorption potential theory allow overcoming equilibrium limitations, outperforming both measurements and kinetic-based protocols alone. In contrast to previous assumptions that improved measurement criteria or longer equilibration times suffice, our findings emphasize that thermodynamic equilibrium can only be ensured by relying on high-temperature master curves for systematic recalculation. By providing accurate K H values, which are critical for materials screening and process upscaling, this framework enables more robust engineering of sorbent-based air purification technologies. This methodological advance has broad implications for experimental practice in nanostructured adsorbent evaluation and supports safer, more efficient approaches to air pollution control.

papers.title: Benchmarking B3LYP, PBE0 and M06L for nuclear spin-spin couplings against CC3: influence of geometry optimization
papers.abstract: We benchmark the DFT functionals B3LYP, PBE0, and M06L for calculating 45 indirect nuclear spin-spin coupling constants (SSCCs) in 13 electron correlation-rich small molecules, using high-level CC3 reference values from a previous study. The dataset spans a wide variety of one-, two-, and three-bond couplings, enabling a systematic assessment of functional performance and the impact of geometry optimization on SSCC calculations. Overall, PBE0 combined with PBE0-optimized geometries provides the closest match to CC3 results, followed by M06L at B3LYP or M06L geometries. A strong functional dependence is observed for fluorine-containing couplings: M06L markedly outperforms PBE0 and B3LYP for these, especially for one-bond C-F couplings, whereas PBE0 is clearly superior for couplings not involving fluorine. Across all molecules, the geometry-optimization method has a significant influence on the resulting SSCCs, and the best performance is consistently achieved when the same method is used for both geometry optimization and SSCC computation. In contrast, CCSD(T) geometries systematically yield the poorest agreement with CC3 SSCCs when combined with any of the three DFT functionals.

papers.title: Translating Silk Protein Hierarchical Structure into Graphitic Order by FIB-Induced Pyrolysis
papers.abstract: Silk fibers are protein-based materials with a highly ordered hierarchical architecture extending from β-sheet-rich molecular domains and aligned polypeptide chains to nanofibrillar bundles and microscopic fibers, collectively giving rise to their exceptional mechanical performance. This intrinsic multiscale organization also offers a powerful, yet largely unexplored, platform for templating ordered carbon materials with programmable nanoscale anisotropy. During our nanoscale structural analysis, Bombyx mori (B.mori) silk fibers were unintentionally carbonized while being sectioned into thin lamellae using focused ion beam (FIB) milling. Subsequent scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) revealed the formation of distinct graphiticlike nanostructures whose spatial orientation and domain alignment were dictated by the preexisting hierarchical organization of the native silk fiber. The observed graphitic ordering followed the directionality of silk molecular packing and fibrillar alignment, indicating that β-sheet stacking and chain orientation serve as structural templates guiding carbon nucleation and lattice organization during localized pyrolysis. Beyond advancing understanding of beam-induced protein carbonization, the results establish a new paradigm for using self-assembled protein fibers as bottom-up templates for structured carbon materials. Translating molecular organization into functional nanoscale carbon networks opens opportunities to engineer patterned, anisotropic graphitic materials for potential applications in nanoelectronics, sensing, energy storage, and advanced composite systems.

papers.title: Entropy-enthalpy compensation in electrocatalytic rates
papers.abstract: Measuring the temperature dependence of electrocatalytic reaction rates is a powerful, yet underexplored, way of investigating the underlying kinetics. In this analysis, we develop the understanding behind such kinetic measurements. Through a very simple model of the surface kinetics for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), we explore how extracted Arrhenius parameters depend on potential and rationalize a series of entropy-enthalpy correlations in experimental HER rates. We find that the entropy-dependent prefactor can change alongside the apparent activation energy, thus signaling deviations from the established Butler-Volmer kinetics that have so far mostly been attributed to potential-driven solvent dynamics. Distinct kinetic fingerprints emerge for different groups of metal catalysts that are in remarkable qualitative agreement with recent experiments. We elucidate these characteristic fingerprints in terms of shifting kinetic regimes and generalize our findings to other electrocatalytic reactions and setups.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Approaches for Ozone Concentration Prediction: A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: Ozone is an important secondary pollutant, affects numerous processes in the Earth's atmosphere and significantly contributes to air pollution, climate, and environmental change, while its presence at higher altitudes is essential for protecting life on Earth. Tropospheric ozone is a crucial component in the formation of photochemical smog, and its changes are linked to human activity. Recent advancements in tropospheric ozone monitoring help to perform quantitative analysis on global and regional spatiotemporal appearances, and also enable investigation of ozone formation mechanisms involved in the troposphere. Based on the literature, there remains substantial scope for the development of regional and global datasets as well as new predictors for ozone pollution tasks. Moreover, such analyses are needed across individual regions, which highlights an

papers.title: A Y-Shaped Al4 Dianion Featuring a Doubly Negative-Charged Central Aluminum Atom
papers.abstract: Aluminum chemistry has historically been dominated by the thermodynamically stable Al(III) oxidation state, although the development of low-oxidation-state Al(I) species in recent decades has revealed their unique reactivity. In contrast, molecular aluminum species with a formally negative oxidation state remain extremely rare, and experimental evidence for a genuinely negatively charged aluminum center is even more limited. Here, we report the synthesis and characterization of a Y-shaped tetranuclear aluminum dianion. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction, UV-visible spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and density functional theory calculations consistently indicate that the central Al atom carries a charge close to −2. This highly reduced aluminum center provides an unprecedented molecular model for negatively charged Al atoms and offers new insight into the electronic boundary between molecular and metallic aluminum compounds.

papers.title: Anomalous Solubility-Inverted Behavior of LiPF6 in Glyme Ether Solvents for High-Voltage Electrochemistry
papers.abstract: Advanced electrolyte configurations are essential for next-generation lithium batteries. Glyme ether electrolytes are attractive due to their low reactivity with lithium metal. However, the commonly used lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) salt exhibits poor anodic stability due to severe aluminum corrosion. In contrast, lithium hexafluorophosphate (LiPF 6 ) offers excellent aluminum compatibility at high voltages but exhibits abnormally low solubility in glyme ether solvents, limiting its application in lithium batteries. The underlying mechanism for this behavior remains unclear. Herein, we show that the low solubility of LiPF 6 in glyme ether solvents originates from a “dissociation-solvation-reprecipitation” mechanism. Taking LiPF 6 in dimethoxyethane (DME) as an example, weak dielectric screening and high molecular symmetry of glyme ethers promote the association of DME-solvated Li⁺ and PF 6 ⁻, leading to the formation of an insoluble solvate crystal Li(DME) 2 PF 6 . Based on this mechanism, we further predict and experimentally verify a solubility-inverted region (SIR), in which LiPF 6 and glyme ethers reform a homogeneous solution once the LiPF 6 concentration exceeds a critical threshold. This interesting behavior can be rationalized by the eutectic interaction between Li(ether) x PF 6 and LiPF 6 , which lowers the melting point of the mixed phase to below room temperature. Consequently, an electrolyte consisting of 5.0 M LiPF 6 in DME/DEE (1:1 vol%) exhibits anodic stability up to 7.0 V vs. Li⁺/Li. A Li||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 cell with a cutoff voltage of 4.5 V further confirms the feasibility of high voltage electrochemistry in LiPF 6 -glyme ether electrolytes. These results clarify LiPF 6 -glyme ether interactions and offer new opportunities for designing advanced electrolytes for high-voltage LMBs.

papers.title: Reductive and Oxidative Transformations of Nitrite at Nickel(II): Insights into the Generation, Electronic Structure, and Reactivity of {NiNO} 10
papers.abstract: The diverse redox transformations of nitrite (NO 2 - ) link key signaling molecules like nitric oxide (NO) and enable precise regulation of NO flux in physiology. This report employs structurally-characterized mononuclear [Ni]-NO x complexes to illustrate nitrogen-oxide redox chemistry, including conversions between nitrite, NO, and nitrate. Reduction of [( Me 2 PzQu ) 2 Ni II (nitrite)](ClO 4 ) 1-Qu by p-methylthiophenol ( Me ArSH) leads to a {NiNO} 10 species [( Me 2 PzQu )Ni(NO)(ClO 4 )] 3-Qu through the intermediacy of HNO 2 and Me ArSNO. Interestingly, subtle modifications in the ligand properties distinctly influence the thiol-nitrite reactivity and the stability of the resulting {NiNO} 10 species. Importantly, the crosstalk between H 2 S and nitrite at nickel(II) site results in reductive nitrosylation to afford the {NiNO} 10 species. This study uniquely employs a phosphine-mediated deoxygenation strategy to demonstrate intermediacy of HNO 2 during thiol reactions of [( Me 2 PzQu ) 2 M II (nitrite)] + (M = Ni/Zn). In addition, NO and NOligand transfer reactivity of the {NiNO} 10 core in 3-Qu have been evaluated. Using iodosylbenzene (PhIO) as a sacrificial O-atom donor, both 1-Qu and 3-Qu complexes yield [Ni II ]-nitrate 2-Qu , thereby outlining a stepwise O-atom transfers (OAT) pathway for nitrosyl nitrite ® nitrate transformations. Taken together, these findings reveal reductive nitrosylation via nitrite-thiol/H2S crosstalk and demonstrate a stepwise OAT-dependent route for NO/nitrite oxidation relevant to the terminal steps of nitrification.

papers.title: Assessing the Gap Between Actual and Permitted Air Emissions from U.S. Semiconductor Manufacturers: Implications and Future Outlook Under the CHIPS Act
papers.abstract: Legislation like the CHIPS Act of 2022 is encouraging an increase in US semiconductor production. While an uptick in domestic manufacturing enhances technology security, air pollutant emissions will increase. In order to understand the gap between the actual and permitted emission levels, this study compares the actual quantity of various air pollutants to their permitted cap limits. We obtain reported data from the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP) and the National Emissions Inventory (NEI) and permit caps from state departments of environmental quality to calculate ratio coefficients that can be used to project emissions from new semiconductor fabrication plants before GHGRP and NEI data is collected and released. The study reveals that most manufacturers analyzed are emitting pollutants well below their permitted caps, with approximately 80% of the gases examined having median emissions at less than 25% of their allowed limit. This suggests that updating emission permit policies could enhance the effectiveness of the U.S. permitting system.

papers.title: Synthesis of Boranils via Iodide-Mediated Demethylative Borylation and Their Properties
papers.abstract: Boranils, difluoroboron complexes with imine and phenoxy moieties, were synthesized by iodide-promoted demethylative borylation. The use of appropriate amounts of BF3•OEt2, Bu4NI, and Et3N enabled the highly efficient synthesis of boranils. Boranils containing heteroaromatics and highly π-extended boranils were also readily obtained by this method. Their physical properties were studied and the properties were consistent with those calculated by DFT calculations.

papers.title: PipMet: Pipeline for processing GC-MS Metabolomics data and statistical graphics visualization
papers.abstract: Introduction: Metabolomics analysis, a key tool in life sciences, generates large amounts of multidimensional data that require robust computational pipelines. However, many existing data processing tools are costly, depending on online resources, or lack of user-friendly interfaces. This creates a significant barrier to entry, limiting the wider application of metabolomics. Objectives: To address these challenges, we developed PipMet, a cost-free, open-source, and user-friendly R package designed to provide a semi-automated, offline solution for untargeted GC-MS metabolomics data processing. Methods: The PipMet pipeline is built on a modular framework of open-source R packages and consists of four main steps: data reading, preprocessing, compound identification and/or annotation, and quantification. It supports standard '.mzML' and '.mzXML' formats. The pipeline's performance was validated through a comprehensive set of tests, including the analysis of standard mixtures, a standard curve for absolute quantification, and a complex sugarcane metabolomics dataset. Results and Discussion: Our validation demonstrates PipMet's outstanding performance in compound identification, with high scores and consistent results compared to other methods. The pipeline also showed excellent reproducibility, linearity, accuracy, and precision in both absolute and relative quantification analyses. Results from the complex dataset proved its efficacy in real-world applications. Conclusion: PipMet provides a flexible and accessible alternative to commercial software and online platforms. Its robust performance and user-friendly design make metabolomics data analysis more attainable for the scientific community, particularly for labs with limited budgets, thereby expanding the reach of this powerful analytical technique. Data availability: The PipMet pipeline is available on GitHub at https://github.com/PipMet/PipMet

papers.title: Shannon and Rényi entropies of molecular densities under atomic partition: insights into extensivity and an incomplete description of correlation
Late-Stage Aryl NCF₃ and SCF₃ Installation Enabled by Coupling Flow-Generated Anions with Aryl Thianthrenium Salts
papers.abstract: The incorporation of heteroatom-linked trifluoromethyl groups, such as N-trifluoromethyl (NCF₃) and trifluoromethylthio (SCF₃) motifs, remains challenging, particularly in the context of late-stage aryl functionalization. Herein, we report a flow-enabled platform that allows for the late-stage installation of NCF₃ and SCF₃ groups onto aryl frameworks through the coupling of flow-generated nucleophilic heteroatom-CF₃ anions with aryl thianthrenium salts. In this strategy, readily available organic precursors are converted on demand into NCF₃ and SCF₃ anions using a CsF-packed bed reactor, allowing safe handling of highly reactive fluorinated intermediates while minimizing fluorinated waste. The resulting anions are subsequently engaged in a copper-mediated, photocatalytic cross-coupling, enabling efficient formation of aryl-NCF₃ and aryl-SCF₃ bonds under mild conditions. The method exhibits broad substrate scope and functional group tolerance, and is applicable to the late-stage diversification of medicinally and agrochemically relevant molecules. Overall, this work expands the scope of nucleophilic CF₃X anions as viable partners in late-stage aryl functionalization and provides a modular platform for the discovery-oriented synthesis of fluorinated molecules.

papers.title: Isohypsic Pd(II)-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling Enables C2-Selective Amination of 2,4-Dihalopyrimidines
papers.abstract: 4-Substituted-2-(arylamino)pyrimidines are a privileged motif found in protein kinase inhibitors, but synthetic routes to these compounds are limited by the reactivity of 2,4-dihalopyrimidine precursors. 2,4-Dihalopyrimidines typically react preferentially at C4 during cross-couplings and nucleophilic aromatic substitutions, which is problematic when late-stage installation of the 4-substituent is desirable. In Pd(0)-catalyzed cross-couplings, selectivity usually arises during oxidative addition, which is heavily biased toward the C4-halide site. We report a Pd(II)-catalyzed cross-coupling that enables the first C2-selective amination of 2,4-dichloropyrimidine. The unusual selectivity arises from a novel isohypsic mechanism in which there is no oxidative addition step. Diverse 4-chloro-2-(arylamino)pyrimidines can be synthesized by this method. The work reveals that redox steps do not have to be a part of cross-coupling catalytic cycles using Pd.

papers.title: Accelerating Lead Optimization away from Anti-Targets: Navigating the Structural Complexity of Promiscuous ADMET Proteins
papers.abstract: The development of a small-molecule suitable for clinical use involves optimization of ligand binding to an identified target protein but also frequently the reduction of binding to a variety of anti-target proteins known to pose translational risk. These anti-targets, often referred to as ADMET proteins, often contain large, highly flexible binding sites leading to promiscuous binding of small molecules. This property often frustrates efforts to execute structure-based design against these anti-targets. Here we demonstrate the application of a combination of induced fit docking and free energy perturbation to structurally enable several of the most common anti-targets: cytochrome P450 isoforms 3A4 and 2D6, the hERG ion channel, and PXR. Crucially, the enforcement of a consensus binding mode across a congeneric series allowed for the efficient exploration of a wide range of receptor conformation space. Results are presented for both public retrospective datasets and prospective application in active drug discovery programs.

papers.title: Grand Banquet: A next-generation chemometrics framework for classification analysis on data matrix
papers.abstract: The advancement of high-throughput analytical instrumentation has placed analytical science into the "Fourth Paradigm" of data-intensive discovery. In this new era, the limitation of scientific insight is not merely data acquisition but the objective, reproducible interpretation of high-dimensional data matrices. Conventional chemometric workflows remain fundamentally reliant on "try-and-trust" methodologies. These expert-assisted paradigms require analysts to manually select preprocessing filters, feature selection methods, and classification models based on intuition or limited resources. Such subjectivity introduces analyst bias, raising concerns about reproducibility when applied to biological or chemical signals. Inspired by the concept “there is no one silver bullet”, a next-generation chemometrics framework, named Grand Banquet (GB) , is designed to standardise the analytical pipeline in this paper. GB replaces manual selection with a near-exhaustive approach, evaluating 990 pipelines (combinations of 15 preprocessing, 6 feature selection, and 11 classification methods) using various performance indices. Beyond this automatic pipeline, Qwen series Large Language Models (LLMs) have been integrated to generate natural-language narratives of these results, bridging the gap between complex computational outputs and human interpretation. GB offers a near-standard baseline (“Glass-box”) for data analysis and a practical step toward method governance and reproducibility. The operation of GB has been tested on four public datasets from the Chemometrics Group at Copenhagen University. GB generates near-exhaustive pipelines for each dataset, with validation accuracies ranging from 40% to 100%, highlighting its ability to systematically explore the data matrix rather than providing only best-performing results. To pay tribute to experts in this field and to promote the standardisation of data analysis practices, related Python files and manuals have been published on GitHub under the Apache License 2.0 licence (GitHub link: https://github.com/Omicsforever867/Grand-Banquet).

papers.title: Second-Generation Crystalline Sponges Enabling Consistent Structure Analysis under Standardized Conditions for Diverse Molecules
papers.abstract: Crystallization is typically highly sensitive to even minor structural differences in target molecules. As a result, obtaining crystals of complex compounds often requires extensive trial-and-error experiments for each target molecule. We recently reported a second-generation crystalline sponge (2G-CS), in which a coordination cage is fixed within a crystal lattice. In the 2G-CS, target molecules are first encapsulated within the cage in solution, followed by salt formation with a symmetry-mismatched polyanion, leading to the formation of single crystals suitable for structure analysis. However, practical implementation still requires case-by-case optimization of crystallization conditions. In this study, we demonstrate that combining the cage with a specific polyanion enables crystallization of a wide range of structurally distinct guest molecules under a single set of standardized conditions. In a test set comprising 39 guest molecules, 31 cases (80%) were successfully crystallized using the same conditions. These examples include polar, medium-sized, and structurally complex molecules, most of which are of pharmaceutical interest. Crystal structures showed that the polyanion induced a predominant packing type for cages and anions in crystals. We suggest that this recurrent packing type may contribute to the ability to obtain crystals under standardized conditions despite variations in guest structures.

papers.title: Fundamental Electrostatics Explains Why Ferredoxin-and HiPIP-type Proteins Favor Different Redox Transitions in [4Fe-4S]-Cys4 Clusters
papers.abstract: [4Fe–4S] clusters in proteins typically occur in three distinct redox states: the oxidized state ([4Fe–4S]3+ ), the semi-reduced state ([4Fe–4S]2+), and the reduced state ([4Fe–4S]1+ ). Consequently proteins containing these clusters could exhibit two distinct redox transitions - the low-potential transition (LPT: [4Fe–4S]1+/[4Fe–4S]2+) and the high-potential transition (HPT: [4Fe–4S]2+ /[4Fe–4S]3+ ). Yet, individual proteins employ only one of them for their biological function. Despite of sharing an identical inorganic cofactor, ferredoxins (Fds) consistently operate via the LPT, whereas high-potential iron-sulfur proteins (HiPIPs) exclusively use the HPT. In this study, we analyze the physical basis for the different behavior of the two protein classes. Using continuum electrostatics, we calculate the redox potentials for both transitions across a representative selection of high-resolution protein structures from both classes. We find that transferring the cluster from water into the protein interior shifts both transitions to lower redox potentials, with the LPT experiencing a larger shift than the HPT. This larger shift is caused by the larger desolvation penalty due to the higher charge of the redox states involved in the LPT. As a result, the separation between the two transitions increases to about 1 V, matching values observed for model clusters in organic solvents. Protein background charges including peptide bond dipoles shift the redox potential of both transitions by nearly the same amount, tuning only one transition into the physiological redox window while pushing the other transition outside of this window. These background charges stabilize the reduced state in both transitions, but the magnitude of this stabilization is substantially larger in Fds than in HiPIPs. Together, these effects position the native redox transition of each protein class at its physiological value, while shifting the non-native transition outside of the biologically accessible range.

papers.title: Detection of 1-Hydroxypyrene as biomarker for polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons via cyclodextrin-based systems
papers.abstract: 1-Hydroxypyrene (1HOPy) is the major urinary metabolite of pyrene and one of the most widely used biomarkers for assessing human exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). Despite its analytical relevance, the molecular determinants governing the interaction of 1HOPy with supramolecular hosts in aqueous solution remain poorly understood. In this work, we present a combined spectroscopic and computational investigation of the binding of 1HOPy to β-cyclodextrin (βCD), γCD (γCD), hydroxypropyl-βCD (HPβCD), dimers of βCD and two polymers with the aim of elucidating the structural and thermodynamic factors underlying complex formation. Steady-state absorption and fluorescence spectroscopy, and time-resolved fluorescence measurements reveal distinct binding behaviours depending on the host architecture. While βCD, HPβCD and the dimers predominantly form 1:1 complexes with 1HOPy, γCD displays cooperative binding, giving rise to both 1:1 and 2:2 host–guest assemblies. In the polymers 2 CDs tend to encapsulate the 1HOPy guest. Spectroscopic signatures further indicate that, under buffered conditions, partial formation of the enolate form of 1HOPy may contribute to enhanced stabilization in one dimer. Binding constants differ even by 2 orders of magnitude with HPβCD displaying the highest affinity followed by one dimer. To rationalize these observations at the molecular level, extensive molecular dynamics simulations combined with thermodynamic integration (TI) were performed. Computational models were designed to reflect the experimentally relevant stoichiometries while also probing alternative binding scenarios to explain deviations from experimental fits. Structural analyses based on RMSD, minimum host–guest distances, hydrogen-bond patterns, and clustering reveal that βCD dimers remain relatively flexible and poorly compacted upon guest binding, whereas γCD undergoes pronounced guest-induced dimer stabilization. In particular, inclusion of two 1HOPy molecules drives the compaction of the otherwise labile γCD dimer, leading to a rigid and cooperative supramolecular assembly. Binding free energies computed by TI reproduce the experimental hierarchy of affinities and highlight that interaction energies alone do not predict thermodynamic stability. For βCD systems, strong local host–guest interactions translate only into moderate binding free energies, whereas γCD exhibits a marked amplification of affinity arising from cooperative host–host reorganization. Comparison between calculated and experimental free energies shows overall agreement, while also delineating specific deviations attributable to chemical effects not explicitly captured by the classical force-field description. Overall, this study demonstrates that 1HOPy not only acts as a passive guest but can actively stabilize supramolecular architectures, particularly in γCD systems. These findings provide molecular-level insight into cyclodextrin–PAH metabolite recognition and support the rational design of cyclodextrin-based platforms for the detection and sensing of environmental biomarkers.

papers.title: Advancing Computational Enzymology with Multiscale Machine Learning/Molecular Mechanics: Catalytic Mechanism and Stereoselectivity in Diels–Alderases
papers.abstract: Enzymes catalyze complex chemical transformations with remarkable efficiency and selectivity, yet their atomistic mechanisms remain challenging to capture because conventional simulations trade accuracy for efficiency. Here we introduce a reactive machine learning/molecular mechanics (ML/MM) framework that bridges quantum chemistry with long-timescale sampling, enabling direct exploration of enzymatic transition states and free-energy landscapes. Coupled with metadynamics, this approach achieves nanosecond sampling of bond-forming reactions and quantitatively predicts activation barriers, mutational effects, and stereoselectivity. Applied to Diels–Alderases, the framework not only reproduces experimental activity andendo/exo preferences with sub-kcal/mol accuracy but also uncovers how pathway dynamics and local electrostatics preorganize substrates for selective outcomes. By uniting reactivity, conformational dynamics, and predictive power, this work establishes reactive ML/MM as a broadly applicable strategy for mechanistic enzymology and a foundation for the rational design of new biocatalysts.

papers.title: From Microcurrents to Macrodynamics: Harnessing Mixed Potentials for Large, Tunable Acceleration of Belousov–Zhabotinsky Oscillations
papers.abstract: Chemical oscillators such as the Belousov-Zhabotinsky (BZ) reaction offer a promising foundation for energy-efficient, biologically inspired chemical information processing. While optical and mechanical manipulation of BZ has been extensively studied, electrochemical control has remained largely elusive and lacks fundamental understanding, in spite of its superior energy efficiency. Here, we investigate how a platinum electrode influences the dynamics of a ruthenium-catalyzed BZ reaction. We observe a pronounced acceleration of the oscillation frequency that scales with the electrode’s surface to solution-volume ratio. In addition, we demonstrate that small DC currents (<0.4 mA) further modulate the effect up to a full recovery of the natural period. To explain these findings, we develop a quantitative model based on mixed-potential theory, which accurately captures the observed behavior. This framework reveals how the low-volume electrochemical conversion of molecules at the electrode's surface gets amplified by the chemistry and finally causes a pronounced impact on the entire system. This surprising effect, controllable through small applied currents, offers new strategies for designing programmable chemical systems for sensing and computing applications.

papers.title: Assessment of Protein Conformation via Diazirine-Promoted Oxidation
papers.abstract: Photo-affinity labeling (PAL) utilizes photoreactive molecules to derivatize proteins in a solvent-accessible depend-ent manner. The site and frequency of the products of this reaction can be used to garner insights into the confor-mation of the protein. In this work, we document and characterize a novel oxidation process instigated by UV irradia-tion of aromatic diazirines. Diazirine is an increasingly utilized reagent for probing protein conformations, and this product has yet to be documented. We initially assess the selectivity of the chemical reaction and find that it is highly selective to methionine (Met) and tryptophan (Trp) residues. We next examine whether this oxidative labeling can be utilized to evaluate protein conformation. We assess native and urea-denatured ubiquitin and cytochrome c, holo- and apo-myoglobin, and native and copper-bound B-2-microglobulin. In all surveyed protein systems but ubiquitin, this diazirine-promoted oxidation readily differentiates between the two protein conformations.

papers.title: Tuning the reactivity of g-C3N4 photocatalysts using liquid phase exfoliation
papers.abstract: To address global water quality issues photocatalysis has emerged as a sustainable advanced oxidation process to degrade aqueous organic pollutants. Layered semi-conductors, such as graphitic carbon nitride and other two-dimensional materials, have shown promise as photocatalysts for water treatment and splitting applications. Despite this, improving the reactivity of these materials typically involves lab-based chemical processing steps that are challenging to scale and can indirectly introduce their own sustainability issues with toxic reagent use. To improve the catalytic performance and drive sustainable real-world deployment, scalable production methods are required. Here we show that rapid liquid phase exfoliation using shear-driven methods can enhance the reactivity of g-C3N4, achieving up to 2.5X increase in the removal of organic dye model pollutants compared to the bulk material. We show that organic-inorganic two dimensional material heterostructures (g-C3N4/MoS2) also outperform bulk catalysts, however, the simple action of shear exfoliation is found to be the primary reason for enhancement. We reveal the mechanisms behind these enhancements and verify the catalysts ability to degrade several model pollutants (Indigo Carmine, Rhodamine B, Acid Red 266), including those containing tough-to-break C–F bonds such as those present in persistent environmental pollutants.

papers.title: Activity of MXene Single Flakes in situ using SECCM
papers.abstract: MXenes are 2D transition metal carbides, which are studied for various applications including electrocatalysis and energy storage. Ti 3 C 2 T x is a MXene, which has shown activity for the hydrogen evolution reaction. We study the activity of Ti 3 C 2 T x singles flakes for this reaction, mixed single layer and multilayer, using SECCM and ex situ AFM. Our SECCM results reveal that multilayer flakes have a larger overpotential, possibly because of more difficult insertion of ions between layers compared to the reaction on the basal plane. We use an in situ method for evaluating electrochemical surface area using the redox chemistry of Ti 3 C 2 T x . Contrary to AFM-derived surface area, it takes into account insertion between layers to properly understand the activity of multilayer flakes.

papers.title: Nature of Surface Sites in Ziegler-Natta Pre-Catalysts from Quantitative Analysis of Ti K-edge X-Ray Absorption Spectra
papers.abstract: Ziegler-Natta catalysts, discovered in 1950s, are still nowadays central to the industrial production of polyethylene and polypropylene. Despite being the workhorse of the polymer industry and despite years of extensive research, the improvement of Ziegler-Natta catalysts has been mostly empirical. In particular, the coordination surrounding of Ti sites in pre-catalysts, key for the formation of active sites upon AlEt3 activation, has been highly debated. Notably, quantification of different Ti sites on the MgCl2 surface has not been possible so far, hindering the development of quantitative structure-activity relationships. In this work, we prepared a series of pre-catalysts with increasing concentration of BCl3 modifier during the catalyst synthesis, known to affect the amount of Cl- and alkoxo-ligands in the Ti local surrounding as well as the activity in ethylene polymerization. We develop a methodology, relying on a library of theoretical XAS spectra for DFT-optimized structural models, benchmarked on a series of well-defined molecular compounds. Quantitative analysis of XAS data allows us to evaluate the relative fractions of Ti sites in fully Cl-surrounding as well as containing alkoxide and O-donor ligands. The analysis shows that the number of Ti-O bonds (initially mostly present in their alkoxo-form) decreases upon treatment with BCl3 up to B/Ti ratio of 2, coherent with earlier proposals, and increases afterwards, due to O-donor ligands, likely related to B-alkoxo species coordinated to Ti. The catalytic activity of these pre-catalysts after activation with AlEt3 in ethylene polymerization passes through a maximum at B/Ti ratio of ~2, pointing to its relation to the detrimental effect of O-based ligands on the activity. This approach allows to address and quantify the metal speciation in the complex Ziegler-Natta pre-catalysts and relate this to their catalytic activity, a first step towards establishing quantitative structure-activity relationships.

papers.title: 1,4-Bromoboration of Nitroalkenes
papers.abstract: The selective bromoboration of nitroalkenes occurs under mild conditions with a bromoborane featuring two 1-methyl- ortho -carborane substituents, BrB Me o Cb 2 . The bromide is introduced on the β-carbon and the boryl moiety on the nitro group is bound to boron in a k 2 manner. Screening a variety of other haloboranes gave either no reaction or indiscernible mixtures indicating the necessity for the BrB Me o Cb 2 reagent. The haloboration reaction tolerates a variety of aryl functional groups as well as a hydrogen or methyl group on the α -carbon that all proceed with excellent regioselectivity and high isolated yields.

papers.title: A Dual−hydride Channel Strategy for Water−mediated Lignin Depolymerization during Reductive Lignocellulose Fractionation
papers.abstract: Reductive catalytic fractionation (RCF) of biomass conventionally employs methanol as a passive solvent primarily for lignin solubilization. Herein, we report a conceptual shift by using water not merely as a green solvent, but as an active catalytic participant. This water-mediated RCF system achieves efficient fractionation of various sawdust feedstocks over conventional catalysts under notably mild conditions (170 °C, 3 MPa H 2 , 5 h), delivering superior efficiency and sustainability compared to methanol-based systems. Combined kinetic and isotopic labeling experiments confirm the essential dissociation of both H 2 O and H 2 , with hydrogen from both sources incorporated into the products. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal a unique dual‑hydride mechanism, wherein water dissociation on the ruthenium catalyst surface generates hydroxyl species that markedly promote H 2 activation, producing additional hydrides. This synergistic dual‑hydride pathway significantly enhances the cleavage of key lignin linkages, enabling efficient depolymerization. Our work fundamentally redefines the role of water in catalytic biorefining and establishes a new paradigm for sustainable RCF, wherein water operates through a concerted catalytic mechanism.

papers.title: Assessing the Gap Between Actual and
papers.abstract: Legislation like the CHIPS Act of 2022 is encouraging an increase in US semiconductor production. While an uptick in domestic manufacturing enhances technology security, air pollutant emissions will increase. In order to understand the gap between the actual and permitted emission levels, this study compares the actual quantity of various air pollutants to their permitted cap limits. We obtain reported data from the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP) and the National Emissions Inventory (NEI) and permit caps from state departments of environmental quality to calculate ratio coefficients that can be used to project emissions from new semiconductor fabrication plants before GHGRP and NEI data is collected and released. The study reveals that most manufacturers analyzed are emitting pollutants well below their permitted caps, with approximately 80% of the gases examined having median emissions at less than 25% of their allowed limit. This suggests that updating emission permit policies could enhance the effectiveness of the U.S. permitting system.

papers.title: Simultaneous CEA and CDH-17 Detection from Cancer Extracellular Vesicles Via Machine Learning Enabled Bio Silent Azide-Infrared Spectroscopy
Uncovering non-hydrogen bonded dormant states of perylene diimide monomer through molecular dynamics simulations and Markov state modeling
papers.abstract: Living supramolecular polymerization often involves manipulating the energy landscape of supramolecular polymerization to slow down thermodynamic processes and enhance kinetic barriers. This control allows for the precise assembly of complex supramolecular polymers. A deep understanding of the structural details and dynamic transitions of kinetically trapped intermediates is crucial for the rational design of supramolecular polymerization processes. Hydrogen bonding within the molecule is highly regarded as the primary contributor to the kinetic stability of monomeric species. The strucrual details of long-lived intermediates that delays the self-assembly are not well-understaood. In this study, we utilized molecular dynamics simulations and Markov state modeling to characterize the metastable states of perylene diimide (PDI) derivatives as a function of alkyl spacers of varying length (ethylene to pentylene chains). Our results demonstrate that these PDI derivatives become trapped in multiple metastable states, each characterized by distinct conformational pathways. All metastable states primarily exhibit intramolecular hydrogen-bonded structures regardless of alkyl spacer length. three states However, we also identied new conformation, lacking intramolecular hydrogen-bond, where the trialkoxybenzamide moiety is either parallel or slanted to the PDI π-plane. While molecules with ethylene, propylene, and pentylene spacers exhibit conformations that shield the π-surface, hindering self-assembly, molecule with butylene spacer adopt conformations that favour selfassembly. Interestingly, structural comparisons reveal similarities between molecules with ethylene and pentylene spacers, as well as between molecules with propylene and butylene spacers. We believe our work provides intruging insights into the dynamics of the kinetic trapped species, contributing to the understanding and advancement of living supramolecular polymerization.

papers.title: Efficient Organocatalyzed ATRP in both Organic and Aqueous Media via AIE photocatalysts
papers.abstract: Organocatalyzed atom transfer radical polymerization (O-ATRP) presents a metal-free alternative to traditional ATRP. As a light-mediated method, it utilizes organic photoredox catalysts (PCs) to produce polymers with well-defined architectures. The development of highly efficient PCs operable in diverse solvents is crucial for advancing O-ATRP. In this work, we firstly demonstrated the application of aggregation-induced emission (AIE) photoredox catalysts in O-ATRP. Due to the aggregation-enhanced intersystem crossing and prolonged excited-state lifetime in aqueous aggregates, AIE-PC exhibited superior catalysis performance for O-ATRP in both organic and aqueous media. With the catalysis of AIE-PC, 95 % methyl methacrylate conversion in DMF (Ð = 1.11, Mn = 32.1 kDa) and 90 % DMAEMA conversion in aqueous media (Ð = 1.22, Mn = 31.6 kDa) at 100 ppm catalyst loading were achieved. Furthermore, well-defined block copolymers (PDMAEMA-b-POEGMA500) were successfully synthesized in aqueous media. Even under sunlight (30 mW cm-2) irradiation for 4 h, the polymerization of MMA was successfully initiated, achieving 66 % conversion. This work demonstrates the promising application of AIE-PC in O-ATRP whether in organic phase or aqueous media.

papers.title: An uncontracted Epstein-Nesbet perturbation theory approximation to SC-NEVPT2 based on spin-pure selected CI wave functions
papers.abstract: Recently, we have developed a spin-adapted selected configuration interaction (SCI) method for capturing static electron correlation effects in large active orbital spaces 1 and the corresponding nuclear gradients for geometry optimizations. 2 This work reports two methods to incorporate dynamical electron correlation effects on top of the SCI wave function. First, we implemented the strongly contracted variant of N-electron valence state perturbation theory (SC-NEVPT2) 3 including the residual terms emerging from the incompleteness of the SCI wave function. 4 Through utilization of prototyping symmetries, efficient selection procedures and specifically designed parallelization/batching schemes the steeply scaling computational costs and memory requirements could be alleviated. Second, we developed an approach where the notoriously problematic V −1 a and V +1 i perturber classes are treated by Epstein-Nesbet (EN) perturbation theory. The resulting hybrid EN-SC-NEVPT2 method is able to tackle active spaces of up to 30 orbitals with significantly lower computational costs than SC-NEVPT2. A set of test calculations illustrate the performance of the implemented methods.

papers.title: Physics-Constrained Artificial Intelligence for Accelerated Experimental Discovery of Metal-Organic Frameworks in Gas Separation
papers.abstract: The development of efficient adsorbents is significant but challenging for gas separation. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) show great potentials in cutting separation energy consumption, while suffering from the problems caused by its vast diversity. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers effective solutions, but still faces high data consumption and poor extrapolation. To address this issue, taking C 3 H 6 /C 3 H 8 as an example, we proposed a physics constrained neural network (PCNN) which integrates physical knowledge into the framework and reach a great balance between prediction accuracy and physical rationality. Meanwhile, PCNN can be well trained using much less data (< 10%) than that required by conventional models, significantly cutting the training cost. Moreover, our model can provide accurate assessments of adsorption isotherms across the full pressure range even after being trained on data from only a single pressure point, demonstrating excellent extrapolation. Finally, a series of experiments were carried out to confirm the precision of PCNN in MOF screening. MOF (CCDC ID: CUIMDZ01) with ultrahigh C 3 H 6 /C 3 H 8 selectivity (IAST selectivity of 3.5×10 5) was successfully discovered, which demonstrated the potential of our model in material discovery. This work presents an efficient workflow with broad applicability for material discovery across diverse fields.

papers.title: Grand Challenges for Predictive Modeling in Small Molecule Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: We present a set of Grand Challenges for predictive modeling in small molecule drug discovery, with the goal of defining, prioritizing, and quantifying the areas where computation can have transformative impact. Rather than offering another broad survey of methods, this paper articulates specific scientific and technical problems that limit progress today and proposes measurable criteria by which advances can be judged. Our objective is to align researchers, investors, and industry leaders around the challenges that matter most for advancing real drug discovery programs. This work seeks to broaden participation in drug discovery by providing a clear roadmap for contributors from the growing areas of artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotics, high-performance computing, and quantum computing, where tools are rapidly advancing but are often disconnected from the practical realities of medicinal chemistry and pharmacology. The insights presented here draw on extensive discussions with experienced drug hunters, computational method developers, and thought leaders across biotech, pharma, software, and venture capital, as well as lessons learned from our own drug discovery efforts. While there is substantial enthusiasm (particularly around AI) for revolutionizing drug discovery, this moment demands sharper problem definition. Without clearly articulated challenges and performance metrics, computational innovation risks optimizing for benchmarks rather than for translational impact. We therefore identify Grand Challenges across four domains: Chemistry, Structure, Energy, and Pharmacology. For each domain, we present a common framework: a well-defined challenge, the underlying physical principles, its relevance to drug discovery decision-making, the current state of the field, and quantitative metrics that define progress. By grounding computational ambition in concrete scientific problems, we aim to catalyze sustained, measurable advances rather than episodic waves of enthusiasm.

papers.title: Comprehensive Kinetic and Mechanistic Analysis of AlkB-Catalyzed Oxidation of Alkyl Modifications
papers.abstract: Despite extensive studies of the 2-oxoglutarate/Fe(II)-dependent dioxygenase AlkB, the determinants of its substrate selectivity and specificity remain incompletely defined. Reported kinetic parameters vary widely across studies due to differences in nucleic acid sequence and context, reaction conditions, analytical approaches, and limited substrate scope, complicating cross-study comparisons and obscuring the enzyme’s catalytic capacity. In particular, AlkB’s ability to process exocyclic dimethyl modifications has not been systematically evaluated within a unified kinetic framework alongside other alkyl substrates. Here, we present a comprehensive kinetic analysis of wild-type E. coli AlkB using a chemically diverse panel of alkyl modifications inserted at a defined position within DNA, all examined under identical conditions. The results provide the most comprehensive and quantitative kinetic study of AlkB on thirteen substrates in both single-stranded and double-stranded DNA. These results reveal that exocyclic dimethyl modifications are demethylated more efficiently than their corresponding monomethyl counterparts and that it proceeds through a stepwise, biphasic mechanism with a kinetically favored first demethylation step. Within this framework, we identify N 4 ,N 4 -dimethylcytidine (m44C) and N 2 , N 2 -dimethylguanine (m22G) as a previously unreported wild-type AlkB substrate together with a known substrate, N 6 , N 6 -dimethyladenine (m66A). We further show that AlkB demethylation is nucleobase position-, substrate-, and strand-context dependent. Molecular dynamics (MD) and hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) studies to investigate AlkB catalysis of m22G and m2G as a representative dimethyl modification and its monomethyl counterpart show structural and dynamical differences depending on the substrate, giving rise to differences in interaction of the substrate and the percentage of catalytically competent structures. The calculated reaction energy profiles show that although hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) kinetics in the slowest step are comparable for both substrates, the m22G is thermodynamically driven, with the intermediate being significantly more stabilized. We also demonstrated that AlkB has activity towards alkyl modification in RNA. Together, this work reconciles discrepancies in the AlkB literature, establishes a unified kinetic and mechanistic framework for exploring the demethylation of analogous AlkB homologs’ diverse substrates, including dimethyl modifications, and refines our understanding of how AlkB and its homologs handle chemically and sterically diverse alkyl modifications.

papers.title: Binder-Free Core-Sheath MOF/COF Aerogels by Reactive Direct Ink Writing for High-Performance Dye Removal from Water
papers.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer remarkable porosity and chemical tunability, yet their integration and shaping into binder-free, mechanically robust, and porosity-retaining architectures remains an issue. Here, we introduce reactive direct ink writing (RDIW), an additive-manufacturing strategy that utilizes the intrinsic thixotropy of high-aspect-ratio MOF nanorods to create printable inks without any polymeric binders. After extrusion of the ink into a bath of COF monomers, rapid imine condensation produces a continuous COF sheath around each filament, forming core-sheath MOF/COF aerogels that preserve the microporosity of both components. We demonstrate that this approach is general across multiple MOFs and four imine-linked COFs and produces wood-pile structured monoliths with tuneable composition and architecture. The 3D-printed aerogels exhibit over 4 times higher initial rate of adsorption h 0 than MOF, COF, or sol–gel-derived MOF/COF analogues, while maintaining structural integrity and recyclability. RDIW establishes a scalable framework for shaping porous crystalline materials into mechanically resilient, high-surface-area monoliths, opening new opportunities in water purification, separations, and catalytic flow systems.

papers.title: A Mechanism for Aromatic Nitration Catalyzed by Cytochrome P450 Enzymes from Rufomycin Biosynthesis
papers.abstract: During the biosynthesis of the peptide antibiotic rufomycin, the cytochrome P450 (P450) RufO catalyzes the aromatic nitration of a tyrosine residue in a ribosomal pentapeptide that serves as a precursor for nonribosomal peptide synthesis. To understand the mechanism of this unusual P450-mediated reaction, a series of pentapeptides were tested as substrates alongside molecular dynamics simulations and quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM, ONIOM approach) calculations. A new substrate bound crystal structure of the homolog NsRufO was also obtained. These experiments revealed the intimate and necessary involvement of a histidine residue within the pentapeptide substrate of RufO in supporting effective nitration, with the protonation state of the intermediate Compound II proposed to influence the production of nitrated tyrosine over unwanted nitrate formation. These findings provide key insights into the mechanism of P450-mediated nitration that explains how sequence differences in RufO and its analogues, along with the structure of the pentapeptide substrate, facilitate aromatic nitration of tyrosine by RufO.

papers.title: Computational and Experimental Testing of Natural Products Against Staphylococcus aureus
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial drug resistance is a global concern driven by diverse bacterial mechanisms, many of which are exacerbated by human activities. Staphylococcus aureus resistant strains pose an immediate threat and a substantial health burden. Natural products (NPs), recognized for their structural diversity and antimicrobial properties, can inhibit enoyl-acyl carrier protein reductase (FabI), a rate-limiting enzyme of the type II fatty acid synthase (FAS-II) system, essential for the biosynthesis of fatty acids that form the bacterial lipid membrane. Herein, we present a general workflow that integrates structure-and ligand-based approaches, specifically, consensus molecular docking with predictions of machine learning models to prioritize NPs candidates for testing as FabI inhibitors of S. aureus. Structural analysis of top-1000 NPs identified 472 scaffolds, with the predominant chemotypes corresponding to chalcones, flavanones, flavones, and phenylpropanoids. Experimental evaluation of selected compounds highlighted taxoquinone as a promising scaffold, exhibiting moderate activity against S. aureus strains tested (pMIC = 3.21). Structure similarity calculations further identified additional promising NPs within the analyzed LANaPDB and NatUV DB collections.

papers.title: Synthesis of Boranils via Iodide-Mediated Demethylative Borylation and Their Properties
papers.abstract: Boranils, difluoroboron complexes with imine and phenoxy moieties, were synthesized by iodide-promoted demethylative borylation. The use of appropriate amounts of BF3•OEt2, Bu4NI, and Et3N enabled the highly efficient synthesis of boranils. Boranils containing heteroaromatics and highly π-extended boranils were also readily obtained by this method. Their physical properties were studied and the properties were consistent with those calculated by DFT calculations.

papers.title: Hydration Free Energies of Alkali and Halide Ions from Data-Driven Many-Body Potentials
Quantifying Hydroxyl Adsorption on Copper with Electrochemical-Aware Random Phase Approximation
papers.abstract: Accurate adsorption thermodynamics of reactive intermediates at electrified metal interfaces are central to predictive surface science, heterogeneous catalysis, and electrochemical modeling, yet remain challenging for standard density functional approximations and difficult to benchmark experimentally. Here we apply electrochemical-aware random phase approximation (RPA) methods that incorporate solvent dielectric screening and grand-canonical constantpotential control to establish a reference-quality description of hydroxyl (*OH) adsorption on Cu(100) in electrocatalytic conditions. At the potential of zero charge (pzc), we quantify the site dependence of *OH binding across terrace sites and representative defective motifs. Under applied potential, electrochemical-aware RPA reproduces the experimentally inferred *OH desorption fingerprint, predicting an *OH desorption potential of-0.54 V vs SHE, in excellent agreement with experimental value-0.56 V vs SHE at pH = 7, whereas widely used GGA functionals (PBE, RPBE) underestimate *OH stability and compress the stability window under reducing conditions. G0W0-RPA electronic structure analysis provides a mechanistic rationale for the discrepancy. Finally, we reassess the Cu(100) surface-state diagram with *OH and *CO co-adsorption under electrochemical conditions, including the stability of metastable CuCO(OH)n motifs, and show that many-body accuracy can qualitatively alter predicted interfacial speciation. Overall, our results establish electrochemical-aware RPA as a broadly applicable, systematically improvable many-body framework for quantitative adsorption thermodynamics at constant potential, enabling predictive surface-state maps for complex electrochemical interfaces.

papers.title: The Scaffold-assisted Diastereoselective Synthesis of small αα Calix[4]pyrrole Building Blocks via Strapped Calix[4]pyrroles & A Robust Analytical Tool for the Notoriously Difficult Separation of "Two Wall" sp3 Calix[4]pyrrole Diastereomers
papers.abstract: The new methodology for the diastereoselective synthesis of αα "two-wall" calix[4]pyrroles with aliphatic walls ("αα sp 3 C[4]Ps") offers a unique access to these elusive building blocks. Their conventional synthesis by acid-condensation of dipyrromethanes with acetone lacks stereocontrol and the formed αα and αβ diastereomers are commonly inseparable by chromatography. In this study, a robust chromatography method for "two-wall" sp 3 C[4]Ps was developed for the analysis of C[4]P diastereomeric mixtures. To circumvent the difficult, labour and material intensive diastereoseparations entirely, we developed a modular "scaffold-assisted" synthesis that utilises a catechol-based dicarboxylic acid tether "Henkel" and different dipyrromethanes for the convergent preparation of strapped C[4]Ps on the g-scale. Cleavage of the strap produces the desired αα C[4]P building blocks diastereoselectively. This approach offers a platform for the diastereoselective synthesis of various αα C[4]Ps due to the simplicity, inexpensiveness and scalability to the multi 100 g scale of the "Henkel" synthesis. Both, αα C[4]Ps with aromatic and aliphatic "walls" are easily obtained by the method in good to excellent yields. The obtained αα C[4]Ps are versatile building blocks for C[4]P-based supramolecular architectures and smart materials. Their structures are discussed based on XRD analysis. The small αα sp 3 C[4]P offers flexible walls and a synthetic handle close to the C[4]P core, while the αα sp 2 C[4]P features electron-poor aromatic walls. To aid future investigations, diverse post-modification methods for the C[4]Ps and their precursor dipyrromethanes were developed.

papers.title: Photoinduced capacitive-to-conductive transition in Cu-doped tungsten oxide hydrates
papers.abstract: A distinct photoinduced capacitive-to-conductive (C2C) transition was identified in Cu-doped tungsten oxide hydrates, demonstrating light-controlled modulation of electronic conductivity and hydrogen evolution activity. This transition occurs during the electrochemical reactions under cathodic potentials and strongly depends on Cu-doping level, illumination, and potential sweep rate. To investigate this phenomenon, WO 3 ·H 2 O (tungstite) and Cu-doped WO 3 ·H 2 O nanoplates were synthesized using the submerged photosynthesis of crystallites (SPsC) method, an environmentally benign, light-driven aqueous approach. Electrochemical and photoelectrochemical analyses, including cyclic voltammetry, Mott–Schottky, and linear sweep voltammetry, reveal that under slow scan and cathodic potentials, proton intercalation leads to H x WO 3 ·H 2 O formation, triggering a C2C transition due to a semiconductor-to-metal conversion accompanied by hydrogen evolution. Illumination induces a rapid and reversible increase in cathodic current, reflecting enhanced carrier density and electronic conductivity. Both carrier density and photocurrent increase linearly with illumination intensity, while the overpotential of hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) decreases correspondingly, exhibiting a clear light-intensity dependence. Cu doping narrows the bandgap and introduces oxygen-vacancy-related sub-band states, thereby improving photoresponse and hydrogen evolution activity. These findings provide fundamental insight into light- and defect-mediated conductivity switching and highlight WO 3 ·H 2 O as a promising photoresponsive material for energy storage and photoelectrocatalysis.

papers.title: Copper catalyzed Reduction coupling of N-tosylhydrazones with Anilines in water
papers.abstract: This study presents a novel and environmentally friendly approach for synthesizing N-(1phenylethyl)aniline derivatives via reductive coupling of N-tosylhydrazones with anilines in aqueous media. The method employs sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) as a surfactant to enhance substrate solubility and facilitate efficient mass transfer during the reaction. Notably, this protocol exhibits broad substrate compatibility, scalability to gram-scale production, and the ability to recycle the catalyst, demonstrating its potential for sustainable and practical synthetic applications.

papers.title: PipMet: Pipeline for processing GC-MS Metabolomics data and statistical graphics visualization Author information
papers.abstract: Introduction: Metabolomics analysis, a key tool in life sciences, generates large amounts of multidimensional data that require robust computational pipelines. However, many existing data processing tools are costly, depending on online resources, or lack of user-friendly interfaces. This creates a significant barrier to entry, limiting the wider application of metabolomics. Objectives: To address these challenges, we developed PipMet, a cost-free, open-source, and user-friendly R package designed to provide a semi-automated, offline solution for untargeted GC-MS metabolomics data processing. Methods: The PipMet pipeline is built on a modular framework of open-source R packages and consists of four main steps: data reading, preprocessing, compound identification and/or annotation, and quantification. It supports standard '.mzML' and '.mzXML' formats. The pipeline's performance was validated through a comprehensive set of tests, including the analysis of standard mixtures, a standard curve for absolute quantification, and a complex sugarcane metabolomics dataset. Results and Discussion: Our validation demonstrates PipMet's outstanding performance in compound identification, with high scores and consistent results compared to other methods. The pipeline also showed excellent reproducibility, linearity, accuracy, and precision in both absolute and relative quantification analyses. Results from the complex dataset proved its efficacy in real-world applications. Conclusion: PipMet provides a flexible and accessible alternative to commercial software and online platforms. Its robust performance and user-friendly design make metabolomics data analysis more attainable for the scientific community, particularly for labs with limited budgets, thereby expanding the reach of this powerful analytical technique. Data availability: The PipMet pipeline is available on GitHub at https://github.com/PipMet/PipMet

papers.title: Reaction Kinetics for Carbon dioxide absorption on improved soda lime beads
papers.abstract: Soda lime beads are commonly used for the capturing of carbon dioxide (𝐶𝑂 2) gas at room temperature due to their high absorption capacity and reusability compared to other absorbers. For the cyclic reuse of the soda-lime beads, it is necessary to provide adequate strength to the beads and to enhance up to the desired level of strength; silicon dioxide is added with soda lime before the fabrication of beads. The fabricated soda-lime beads with added silicon dioxide are named as improved soda lime beads. The process of fabrication of the improved soda-lime beads were discussed in a previous study. The improved soda-lime beds have potential for repeated reuse for the absorption and desorption of carbon-dioxide gas in a confined space viz. submarine, space crafts, mines etc. The kinetic data are essential for the effective deign of a carbon-dioxide capturing system in a confined space and to maintain the carbon-dioxide concentration well below the permissible limit. In the present study, the reaction kinetics of the absorption of carbon dioxide on the improved soda lime beads at room temperature was investigated. Such kinetic studies are not reported in literature. The experimental and results from the study are discussed in this paper.

papers.title: Mechanochemically mediated cascade cyclization of Narylacrylamides with aldehydes
papers.abstract: We established a rapid, versatile mechanochemical method for synthesizing carbonylcontaining oxindoles via TBPB-mediated cascade cyclization of N-arylenamides with aldehydes. Mechanistic studies indicate acyl radical generation through aldehyde hydrogen abstraction by TBPB. This transformation demonstrates broad substrate tolerance, solvent-free conditions, short reaction times (18 min), and operational simplicity.

papers.title: Mechanically induced self-propagating reactions: Fundamentals, overview, in situ monitoring and perspectives
papers.abstract: Mechanically induced self-propagating reaction (MSR) represents a promising but a rather underexplored phenomenon within mechanochemistry, a solvent-free alternative to classical solutionbased chemistry, capable of yielding functional materials within a short timeframe. On the contrary to the gradual mechanochemical reactions, MSRs are sub second combustive-like processes bringing about substantial benefits such as faster product formation, time efficiency, and lower energy consumption. Even though the mechanochemical field is in the research spotlight, MSR investigation remains on the periphery. This review aims for catalyzing a renaissance in MSR fundamentals investigation by reviewing the current state-of-art. This is done via systematically reviewing the reaction systems that were reported to react via a MSR in the past twenty years, such as metal-metalloid ones (carbides, borides, silicides, and carbonitrides), metal chalcogenides, metal oxides, and other specific types of reactions. A couple of case studies are briefly reviewed for each system, and the comprehensive table follows afterward. The review also revisits the factors impacting the MSR course from milling conditions and reagent's properties point of view, showing either a direct or inverse relationship with MSR ignition time. The recent development in the in situ monitoring of mechanochemical reactions allowed to obtain some mechanistic insights into the MSR process, which are summarized in the last chapter.

papers.title: Effects of UVC/H2O2 on dissolved organic matter derived from a cyanobacterial bloom
papers.abstract: Cyanobacterial harmful algae blooms (cyano-HABs) release complex mixtures of metabolites into aquatic ecosystems, including potent toxins. While the degradation of several individual cyanotoxins by reactive species such as the hydroxyl radical (HO •) is well documented, the fate of cyanometabolites in bloom-derived mixtures during water treatment remains poorly understood. This study investigates the degradation of cyanometabolite-rich aqueous extracts from a natural cyanobacterial bloom using UVC/H2O2 to generate HO •. To assess the chemical composition of the samples before and after treatment, we applied an analytical pipeline combining LC-HR-MS/MS with computational metabolomics and statistical analysis. This workflow enabled the identification of nine microcystins (MC), MC-LR, MC-RR, MC-YR, MC-HilR, [D-Asp3]MC-LR, [D-Asp3]MC-RR, MC-WR, MC-Prhcys(O) and MC-(H4)YR, four anabaenopeptins (AP), AP A, AP B, AP F and Oscillamide Y, and seventeen microginins (MG), for which structures of five new congeners and two transformation products (TP) were proposed. UVC/H2O2 accelerated the degradation of cyanopeptides as compared to UVC or H2O2 control treatments. The second-order kinetic models observed were consistent with studies showing the dual role of background dissolved organic matter (DOM) as both a competitive radical scavenger and a photosensitizer. Molecular networking and network annotation propagation (NAP) facilitated the detection of several known TP of MC, and new oxidative cleavage products of MGs and APs. Compositional profiling of treated samples demonstrated molecular restructuring, with nitrogen-rich peptides decreasing, while lipids and fatty acids concurrently increasing. Overall, this study provides valuable insights into • OH-driven transformation pathways in complex cyano-HAB derived mixtures, necessary for developing water treatment strategies.

papers.title: Molecular Design of Biobased, Printable Monomers for Two-Photon Polymerisation
papers.abstract: This study reports the strategic molecular design of a range of novel multi-acrylate monomers derived from the terpenoids nopol and verbenol, and their successful use in twophoton polymerisation (2PP). This design process allowed the identification of structures most appropriate for use in additive manufacturing (AM) resins. This was achieved by deriving new synthesis routes that enabled the fabrication of monomers with bespoke numbers and placements of vinyl groups, which were then shown to dictate the level of success achieved in resin-based AM processing. By identifying the correct molecular design, it was demonstrated via 2PP that structures with uniform composition, smooth surfaces, and finely resolved features could be printed, as confirmed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM). 2PP is a high-precision 3D-printing technique for fabricating complex micro-and nano-scale structures. Despite its potential in functional devices, advanced manufacturing, and biomedical applications, the range of biobased monomers suitable for 2PP remains limited, and they are typically derived from petrochemical sources. This study also demonstrated that terpene and terpenoid reagents, which are abundant and renewable natural compounds, offer a promising platform for developing biobased, multifunctional monomers for AM. 2

papers.title: Aqueous Polymorph and Morphology Control in ZIFs via 1-Methylimidazole for Efficient Lipase Entrapment
papers.abstract: Controlling the phase and morphology of zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (ZIFs) is crucial for optimizing properties relevant to gas separation, adsorption, and, in particular, biocatalysis. In conventional synthesis, the formation of ZIF-8 often relies on organic solvents and a large ligand excess, which undermines sustainability and complicates in situ enzyme incorporation. Although aqueous synthesis is more environmentally friendly, it typically yields the ZIF-L phase, a sheet-like kinetic polymorph that competes with ZIF-8 in water. Here, we demonstrate that 1-methylimidazole (1-mIm) acts as a coordination modulator in water, enabling selective ZIF-8 formation without organic solvent and a large excess of imidazole ligands. By varying the 1-mIm:2-mIm (2-methylimidazole) ratio, we direct the phase selection from the kinetically favoured ZIF-L (1-mIm:2-mIm = 0:1) to the thermodynamically stable ZIF-8 (1-mIm:2-mIm = 2:1), obtaining well-controlled ZIF morphologies. Comprehensive materials characterization (HR-XRPD, SEM, FTIR, BET, and TGA) confirms corresponding phase purity, crystallinity, and tuneable surface properties across morphologies. Applying this control to Thermomyces Lanuginosus Lipase (TLL) entrapment, a lipase@ZIF composite with an intermediate ZIF morphology at 1-mIm:2-mIm = 1:1 was prepared. It delivers the highest enzymatic activity among all ZIF phases, attributed to an increased enzyme loading and improved substrate access to active sites. This water-based, modulator-assisted synthesis route is a sustainable option for green MOF design, enhancing their biocompatibility and their use in the real world.

papers.title: Can cavity prediction algorithms help in docking experiments?
papers.abstract: Blind docking is a method for predicting a binding mode of a ligand with a protein without any prior information about a binding site. Some tools allow this type of docking experiment directly, others, including some established tools , require binding site information being passed as an input. In this latter case, one can use cavity prediction tools and use the results of their prediction as an input in these docking calculations. However, it is still unclear if the results of these predictions can be reliably used in protein-ligand docking and what is the best technical way to pass this information to the docking algorithm. In this study we estimated the applicability of the binding pocket prediction tools in docking experiments to address this gap in knowledge. We exploit four different computational tools for cavity prediction and use the best predicted cavities represented in different ways to run GOLD docking calculations. Analysis of subsequent use in docking highlights that Fpocket and CAVIAR are the best performing cavity prediction tools in this context. Further analysis shows that accurate binding site input does not guarantee accurate binding pose predictions and , even with the predicted cavities, the more restrained the input is, the more reliable the docking results are.

papers.title: Shannon and Rényi entropies of molecular densities under atomic partition: insights into extensivity and an incomplete description of correlation
Design of experiments (DOE) approach for optimizing ZnS nanoparticle morphology via displacement synthesis
papers.abstract: The controlled tailoring of zinc sulfide (ZnS) nanoparticle morphology is essential for achieving predictable optical, electronic, and catalytic performance in semiconductor applications. Displacement synthesis offers a simple and scalable route to ZnS formation; however, morphological outcomes are highly sensitive to the interacting reaction parameters, including precursor concentration, temperature, pH, reaction time, and stirring conditions. This study proposes a structured Design of Experiments (DOE) framework to systematically optimize the morphology of ZnS nanoparticles produced via displacement reactions. A multivariate experimental matrix based on factorial and response surface methodologies was employed to quantify the individual and interaction effects of critical process variables. Morphological characteristics, including particle size, aspect ratio, and agglomeration tendency, were correlated with statistical models to identify optimal synthesis windows. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) confirmed the statistical significance of key factors and their coupled effects, while predictive regression models demonstrated strong agreement with experimental observations. The optimized conditions enabled reproducible synthesis of narrowly distributed ZnS nanoparticles with controlled structural features. The proposed DOE-guided strategy reduces experimental redundancy, enhances process reproducibility, and provides a scalable pathway for morphology-driven functional tuning of ZnS nanomaterials. This methodology can be extended to other metal chalcogenide systems where precise nanostructure control is required.

papers.title: Machine-Learning-Accelerated Particle-Swarm Optimization for New Ground-State Reconstructions on TiO2 (110)
papers.abstract: Determining the atomic structure of reduced rutile TiO 2 (110) remains a long-standing challenge due to the complex rearrangements of Ti and O atoms and the vast configurational space accessible under reducing conditions. Here, we employ an advanced global structuresearch framework that integrates deep-potential energy surfaces with particle-swarm optimization, enabling efficient and unbiased exploration across multiple reduction states. Our search identifies a previously unreported Ti 3 O 2 -(2×1) reconstruction that is thermodynamically more stable than the earlier Ti 3 O 2 -(1×2) model. Simulated STM images of this newly identified structure reproduce the experimentally observed rosette motifs with a high degree of similarity. Electronic-structure analysis shows that its enhanced stability originates from strengthened orbital hybridization between the occupied Ti 3+ 3 d states and the O 2 p states. This work refines the atomic-level understanding of a widely studied TiO 2 (110) reconstruction and highlights the capability of machine-learning-accelerated global search to resolve complex oxide surface structures with direct experimental relevance.

papers.title: Two Reactivity Modes for the Price of One Catalytic Cycle: Sulfonamides as Dual PET/HAT Catalysts
papers.abstract: Cyclic biaryl sulfonamides (BASNs) have emerged as a versatile and synthetically accessible class of reductive organophotocatalysts for photoinduced electron transfer (PET) reactions. Following PET engagement of a reductively labile substrate partner, BASN − transforms into a nitrogen-centered radical.
