The selective electrooxidation of isopropanol (IPA) to acetone has primarily been explored on platinum group metals and their alloys. Given their high cost and relative scarcity, strategies are needed to ensure these catalysts are used efficaciously without sacrificing device performance (e.g., power densities, energy/faradaic efficiencies, and longevity). While 3-electrode experiments provide a means to estimate catalytic activity, metrics obtained from literature-sourced cyclic voltammetry (CV) are concerningly discrepant. To clarify reasons for such a range in observed behavior, we perform CV experiments in quiescent electrolyte and using a rotating disk electrode. We find that small amounts of impurities suppress IPA oxidation, especially under convection. Further, scan rate, convection, electrolyte purity, and IPA concentration individually can substantially influence the reaction rate explaining some of the breadth in the published literature. Because accumulation of impurities and reactive intermediates at the surface over time convolute understanding of CVs, we also perform chronoamperometry (CA) experiments to assess the timescales, extent, and persistence of performance decay. Finally, we show, through modeling and experiments, that potential pulsing offers a way to repeatedly recover catalyst performance and increase average reaction rates. Without a dynamic strategy to continue IPA oxidation, measures of performance from transient means (e.g., CV or CA) are challenging to contextualize.

papers.title: Nicotinoyl and Heteroacyl Tryptamine Conjugates: An Extended Series of Novel Dual-and Multi-Action Prodrug Candidates Targeting NAD⁺ Metabolism, Neuroprotection, and Serotonergic Signalling
papers.abstract: A novel series of twenty-five heteroacyl-tryptamine conjugates is presented, organised into six structural classes based on the acyl moiety: nicotinoyl, kynurenoyl, lipoyl, furoyl, thiophenoyl, and tetrazoloyl. All compounds share a secondary amide bond linking the acyl group to substituted tryptamine scaffolds bearing 4-hydroxy, 5-methoxy, or 4-acetoxy substitution. Enzymatic hydrolysis of the amide bond in vivo is proposed to simultaneously release a pharmacologically active tryptamine and a bioactive acyl fragment with distinct therapeutic properties. Each acyl class introduces a separate mechanistic rationale: NAD⁺ replenishment, kynurenine pathway modulation, mitochondrial redox support, antiinflammatory activity, enhanced CNS penetration, and metal chelation, respectively. No synthesis or biological testing has been performed. This preprint presents the structural framework, in silico physicochemical evaluation, and hypothetical pharmacological profiles to stimulate further investigation.

papers.title: Science to be proud of – A Global Policy Roadmap for Sustainable Science
papers.abstract: The current research model, built for expansion and competition, too often rewards throughput over thoughtfulness. Laboratories discard functional equipment for minor upgrades, researchers fly halfway across the globe to deliver short talks, and procurement systems prioritize short-term costs over lasting value. These practices waste resources, but more critically, they erode the integrity and reproducibility of science itself. A sustainable research enterprise is not a limitation; it is the only way to preserve scientific credibility in a resource-constrained world.

papers.title: A skin-affinitive organic electrochemical transistor based on all-hydrogel design for wearable biocomputing
papers.abstract: Skin-integrated transistors have been explored for wearable sensing, computing and programmable synthetic bioelectronics. However, their high modulus, low sweat permeability, and limited scalability result in multidimensional mismatches with the real skin. Here, we introduce skin-affinitive organic electrochemical transistors (SA-OECTs) based on all-hydrogel, designed to simultaneously overcome these limitations. Our all-hydrogel SA-OECTs incorporates a semiconducting hydrogel channel and thus capable of conducting active sensing and computing functions. This unified all-hydrogel strategy yields the SA-OECTs with skin range softness (10-500 kPa), thickness (500 nm-500 μm), biocompatibility, breathability - a combination of properties unattainable with conventional transistors - while achieving tunable transistor characteristics via ion-electron conversion, achieving an on/off ratio exceeding 10 4 . Additionally, these all-hydrogel SA-OECTs exhibit a substantial enhancement in operational speed over conventional poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) based OECTs of equivalent dimensions. Leveraging these attributes, we constructed a SA biocomputing platform using an all-hydrogel SA-OECTs array, paving the way for biohybrid AI that bridges artificial and biological intelligence.

papers.title: Privacy-Preserving Cloud-Based Genomic Analysis for Precision Medicine and Biotechnological Innovation
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of high-throughput sequencing technologies has generated vast volumes of genomic data, creating unprecedented opportunities for precision medicine and biotechnological innovation. Cloud computing platforms provide scalable storage and computational power to process these datasets efficiently; however, concerns regarding data confidentiality, regulatory compliance, and patient trust remain significant barriers to widespread adoption. This study presents a privacy-preserving framework for cloud-based genomic analysis that integrates cryptographic protection, secure multi-party computation, federated learning, and fine-grained access control mechanisms. The proposed approach enables distributed genomic data processing without exposing identifiable genetic information to unauthorized entities. The framework supports core analytical tasks, including variant calling, genome-wide association studies, and predictive modeling for disease risk stratification, while maintaining compliance with international data protection standards. Performance evaluation demonstrates that the integration of encryption and distributed learning techniques introduces manageable computational overhead while substantially reducing the risk of data leakage. Furthermore, the architecture facilitates collaborative research across institutions by enabling model sharing rather than raw data exchange, thereby accelerating translational applications in personalized therapeutics, drug discovery, and biomarker development. By combining secure cloud infrastructure with advanced privacy-enhancing technologies, this work provides a practical, scalable solution for responsible genomic data utilization. The findings highlight the potential of privacy-aware computational ecosystems to advance precision medicine and foster innovation in biotechnology without compromising ethical and legal obligations.

papers.title: Bridging MS2 Spectra and Chemical Space: Advances in Spectral Similarity, Molecular Retrieval, and De Novo Structure Discovery
papers.abstract: Mass spectrometry-based metabolomics increasingly relies on computational methods to translate information-rich MS/MS fragmentation patterns into chemical insight, yet assigning chemical identities to spectra ("annotation") remains a major bottleneck because reference libraries cover only a small fraction of plausible compounds. In this review, we frame the field through the lens of two interacting representation spaces: spectral space, where MS/MS data reside, and chemical space, where molecules are represented by fingerprints, descriptors, or learned embeddings. We discuss how different design choices induce different geometries, what it means for spectra or molecules to be "close", and survey methods for representing and comparing spectra, representing molecules, and mapping between both spaces. We highlight emerging deep-learning trends for cross-modal alignment and retrieval, and we outline where the analogy to text-image learning breaks due to peak ambiguity, noise, and the one-to-many nature of spectrum-to-structure relationships.

papers.title: Surface Termination Unlocks Photocatalytic Potential: Reshaping Structure and Electronics in Ultrathin MoS2/TiO2 Heterojunctions
papers.abstract: Anatase TiO 2 stands out for its exceptional chemical stability, non-toxicity, and robust photocatalytic capabilities; however, its intrinsically wide band gap (∼ 3.2 eV) severely restricts its activity to the ultraviolet spectrum, thereby limiting practical efficiency under solar illumination. To circumvent this bottleneck, the strategic integration of TiO 2 with transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs)-such as monolayer MoS 2 -has proven highly promising, harnessing interfacial charge transfer dynamics, Schottky barrier formation, and bandgap renormalization to extend light absorption into the visible range while suppressing charge carrier recombination. In this study, by means of a campaign of ab initio calculations, we systematically explore the anatase TiO 2 (001) surface interfaced with MoS 2 , with a particular emphasis on elucidating how distinct surface terminations dictate the structural relaxation, interfacial bonding, and resultant electronic structure of the resulting TiO 2 /MoS 2 van der Waals heterostructure. Starting from the idealized (1×1), bulk-truncated, unreconstructed termination as a reference model, we delineate critical similarities and disparities relative to the experimentally prevalent and thermodynamically more stable (1×4) reconstructed surface, thereby providing atomistic insights into the design principles governing optimal nano-hybrid performance.

papers.title: Trends in Structural and Spectroscopic Signatures of Iron(II) Complexes Supported by Systematically Varied Tetra-NHC Macrocycles
papers.abstract: The structural, spectroscopic and electrochemical properties of a series of sixcoordinate iron(II) complexes of the types [(MTC)Fe(NCMe)2] 2+ , [(MTC)Fe(CO)(NCMe)] 2+ and [(MTC)Fe(CO)2] 2+ , where MTC represents four different macrocyclic tetra(NHC) ligand scaffolds (NHC = N-heterocyclic carbene), are compared to better understand the effects of ligand variations on electronic structures. The set of parameters evaluated includes Fe−C bond lengths, IR stretching frequencies of the axial ligands, zero-field 57 Fe Mössbauer data, 13 C NMR chemical shifts and Fe III /Fe II redox potentials. Several new complexes, as well as some known complexes for which structural information was so far lacking, have been characterized by X-ray crystallography. It is found that for most spectroscopic properties there is a large effect of changing the MTC ring size, 2 but much less of an influence of the peripheral NHC ligand substituents. Additionally, a set of complexes [(MTC)Fe(CO)(L/X)] n+ are included in this study where the ligand trans to the axial CO is either a neutral (L = NCMe, CO) or anionic (X − = Cl − , OCP −) donor. Understanding the trends in molecular and electronic structure for the present series of complexes with ligand variations in both equatorial and axial positions will help to rationalize reactivity trends observed for this versatile MTC/iron(II) platform.

papers.title: Axial Chirality Induction in Ferrocene-Amino Acid Hybrids -Toward Chiral Redox-Active Building Blocks
papers.abstract: In this paper, we report the construction of chiral ferrocene-containing supramolecular platforms with high symmetry and well-defined geometry via dynamic covalent chemistry. Starting from amino-acid trihydrazides and ferrocene dialdehyde precursors, we obtained C₂-symmetric motifs Fc(L-1)₂ with hydrogen-bond-stabilized conformations, that display intense circular dichroism (CD) signals in the visible region associated with ferrocene-centered electronic transitions. CD and UV-Vis spectroscopy, supported by computational analysis, reveal efficient transfer of chirality from the remote stereogenic centers to the Fc unit and a robust correlation between amino acid configuration, Fc helicity, and CD sign (L-amino acid → (P)-Fc → (-)CD at 470 nm). Exploiting the dynamic character of the acylhydrazone linker, L-2 was further assembled into D₃-symmetric doubledecker trigonal platform Fc3(L-2)2 with high synthetic efficiency (>90%). Under these conditions, narcissistic chiral self-sorting occurs via dynamic covalent exchange, which results in the formation of homochiral platforms from racemic precursors. The combination of conformationally locked axial chirality, reversible covalent connectivity, and inherent redox activity establishes new amino acid-based motifs as promising modules for constructing chiral Fc-containing porous architectures such as molecular cages, MOFs, and COFs, with potential for asymmetric electrochemical applications.

papers.title: Exciting role of electronic factors: Substituent driven selective functionalization of Dibromo vinyl-aromatics/hetero-aromatics to give Esters and/or Terminal alkynes
papers.abstract: Interesting room temperature conversions have been developed on aryl/heteroaryl substituted1,1-dibromoalkene molecules for the generation of esters and terminal alkynes by the aid of metal alkoxides and that could trigger by the electronic factors of aryl/hetero aryl ring. The group attached to the aryl ring exhibits a crucial role in the selection of the reaction pathway; in general, electron withdrawing groups (EWG) directs the reaction to the generation of ester through its nature of deactivating the ring. On the other hand, electron donating groups (EDG) on the ring turn the reaction to another direction to produce terminal alkynes.

papers.title: Predicting Aqueous Solubility of Pharmaceutical Cocrystals via Constant Chemical Potential Enhanced Sampling Simulations: The Aspirin-Theophylline System
Comparative Study of Displacement and Hydrothermal Approaches for Tailored ZnS Nanostructure Fabrication
papers.abstract: Zinc sulfide (ZnS) nanostructures have attracted sustained interest due to their tunable optical, electronic, and catalytic characteristics, which are strongly influenced by crystal phase, particle size, and morphology. Among various synthesis routes, displacement reactions and hydrothermal processing remain widely adopted because of their operational simplicity and adaptability. This study presents a systematic comparative investigation of displacement and hydrothermal approaches for the controlled fabrication of ZnS nanostructures. Reaction parameters, including precursor concentration, temperature, pH, reaction time, and solvent environment, were optimized to evaluate their influence on nucleation kinetics, crystal growth, and morphological evolution. Structural and physicochemical characteristics were assessed using X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy, and optical spectroscopy. The displacement method demonstrated rapid nucleation and the formation of relatively smaller crystallites with narrow size distribution under ambient conditions, though with moderate agglomeration tendencies. In contrast, the hydrothermal approach enabled enhanced crystallinity, improved phase purity, and well-defined morphologies such as nanorods and hierarchical assemblies, attributed to controlled supersaturation and high-pressure thermal environments. Optical band gap variations were found to correlate with particle size and defect density, highlighting the role of synthesis conditions in tailoring functional properties. The comparative findings provide practical guidance for selecting appropriate synthesis strategies based on desired structural precision, scalability, and application-specific performance requirements. The study contributes to the rational design of ZnS nanomaterials for optoelectronic, sensing, and catalytic applications.

papers.title: Structural Non-Ideality of Graphene
papers.abstract: In practice, graphene synthesized through mechanical exfoliation, chemical vapor deposition, chemical routes etc. inevitably contain structural, interfacial, and compositional non-idealities imposed by thermodynamic limits, kinetic growth pathways, transfer processes, and environmental stabilization. These features are intrinsic consequences of real synthesis conditions rather than peripheral defects. This perspective indicates the persistent conceptual gap between ideal graphene models and the structural reality of synthesized graphene. The mismatch constrains predictive interpretation across spectroscopic analysis, electronic transport modeling, device physics, and structure-property relationships. Edge configuration, strain localization, corrugation, folding, grain boundaries, substrate coupling, and terminal chemistry redefine the electronic landscape, phonon response, and chemical reactivity at experimentally relevant scales. Current experimental interpretations and computational treatments frequently retain assumptions of structural symmetry and perfection that do not reflect material reality. A structurally contextualized framework, in which non-idealities are treated as defining variables, is essential for achieving predictive understanding and rational design of graphene-based systems. Graphene is the structural progenitor of all graphitic carbon and a foundational platform for two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials research. Although its ideal structure is defined as a defectfree hexagonal honeycomb lattice of sp²-hybridized carbon atoms (1,2), graphene realized in practice is intrinsically non-ideal. Across all known synthesis routes, ranging from mechanical, liquid-phase exfoliation, state-of-the-art low-pressure chemical vapor deposition (LPCVD) etc. structural imperfections emerge as a fundamental consequence of growth kinetics, thermodynamics, and post-synthesis processing (1,2). Though large-scale production now

papers.title: Spin-Adapted Restricted Open-Shell Hartree-Fock and Its Dynamic Correlation Extension
papers.abstract: We report a spin-adapted configuration-state-function restricted open-shell Hartree-Fock implementation in OpenMolcas, hereafter denoted CSF-ROHF. The implementation is based on the Graphical Unitary Group Approach for reduced density matrix evaluation, and on the generalized active space and Super-configuration interaction algorithms for orbital optimization. The method enables orbital optimization of a single spin-pure electronic configuration at mean-field cost. Analysis of CSF-ROHF convergence reveals that the initial orbital ordering is decisive for avoiding and escaping local minima during optimization. The computational efficiency of the method, in terms of both iteration count and wall time, is demonstrated on {[Ni(H 2 O) 4 ] n O n-1 (H2O) 2 } 2+ (n = 1, . .. , 10) model systems. For spin gaps of iron-sulfur clusters, CSF-ROHF exhibits intrinsic limitations yielding qualitatively incorrect gaps and offering minimal-to-no advantages over conventional high-spin ROHF. To address these limitations, we introduce a near-mean-field-cost orbital optimization protocol that incorporates dynamic correlation via a second-order, spin-adapted perturbation strategy relying on the recently developed Stochastic-SplitGAS algorithm. The resulting low-spin references substantially improve post-HF treatments, yielding energies and spin gaps in excellent agreement with the far more expensive complete active space self-consistent field calculations for these systems.

papers.title: ChemSpace Copilot: Agentic AI for Interactive Visualization and Exploration of Chemical Space
papers.abstract: Chemography provides a foundational approach to exploring chemical space by compressing high-dimensional representations of chemical structures into 2D maps, enabling clearer interpretation of similarity, diversity, and activity. Such maps power core chemoinformatics tasksstructure-activity relationship analysis, library design, virtual screening, and de novo design. In practice, effective use of chemography relies on manual application of data analysis tools and expert-driven interpretation of the resulting landscapes for hypothesis generation. To automate chemography-guided discovery, we introduce ChemSpace Copilotan agentic AI application that encapsulates standard chemographic workflows based on the non-linear dimensionality reduction technique Generative Topographic Mapping (GTM). ChemSpace Copilot enables researchers to perform chemographic tasks end-to-end through an intuitive, chatbot-style interface. Its modular toolkit integrates chemical data retrieval from ChEMBL, GTM parameter optimization, chemotype analysis and report generation. We further demonstrate the extensibility of the framework by integrating generative deep learning models with the synthesis planning, enabling effective and illustrative end-to-end molecular discovery from design to synthetic feasibility. We demonstrate its utility across three tasks: exploration of ChEMBL's chemical space, chemography-guided compound generation, and synthesis prediction.

papers.title: A New Class of Acene-Based Polymers: Nanowires Made from Linear-Ladder Hydroxy-Substituted Acene Quinones
papers.abstract: Polyacenes, one-dimensional (1D) linear chains of fused benzene rings, are expected to exhibit interesting optoelectronic properties. Short-chain polyacenes, up to nine rings, have been reported to be unstable in air, oxidizing or dimerizing easily under UV light. We have synthesized highly stable substituted pentacene, nonacene, and polyacenes by the Friedel-Crafts acylation using pyromellitic dianhydride (PMDA) and hydroquinone or quinizarin. TEM images reveal nonacene chains self-assembled into nanocrystalline structures and polymer chains tens of nanometers long, indicating hundreds of benzene rings fused together. The electronic conductivity of the polymers at room temperature is in the range of semiconductors, which is remarkably high for an undoped organic compound. The electronic spectra of the polymers extend into the near-IR region, indicating the presence of intrinsic free carriers. These polymers exhibit exceptional thermal and oxidative stability and produce high char yields.

papers.title: Lanthanum-Promoted Al/Si Catalytic Frameworks for Efficient Carbon Dioxide Utilization under Packed-Bed Reactor Conditions
papers.abstract: The escalating concentration of atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO₂) has intensified global efforts toward sustainable carbon utilization technologies. This research investigates the catalytic conversion of CO₂ into value-added fuels-primarily methanol and methane-using lanthanum-nickel-based catalysts supported on alumina and silica within a custom-designed packed-bed reactor. Catalysts with fixed nickel loading (20 wt%) and varying lanthanum contents were synthesized and comprehensively characterized through FTIR, XPS, XRD, BET, SEM, EDX, and mass spectrometry. FTIR confirmed the formation of La-O and support-linked Al-O/Si-O functional groups, while XPS revealed lanthanum in the La³⁺ oxidation state, exhibiting pronounced charge-transfer satellites indicative of strong La-O bonding and enhanced surface basicity. XRD analysis showed distinct crystalline phases of NiO, La₂O₃, and the supports, with La crystallinity increasing at higher doping levels. BET measurements indicated a decrease in surface area with increasing La content, attributed to pore blocking and partial surface coverage, as supported by SEM and EDX evidence of agglomeration at higher loadings. The packed-bed reactor (600 mm length, 162 mm diameter) was operated at 250 °C with CO₂ flow rates of 7.5-15 ml/s. Methanol conversion of 60 percent nearly obtained via refractometry analysis, with maximum yield at 12.5 ml/s due to optimal residence-time and heat-transfer balance. Methane formation reached ~70%, validated by GC-FID, carbon dioxide sensor based analysis and mass spectrometric detection of CH₄ and CO intermediates. Reaction pathways proceeded through the reverse water-gas shift route followed by CO hydrogenation to methanol, competing with Ni-driven methanation. Overall, the study demonstrates that moderate lanthanum loading (20-25 wt%) provides the best synergy between CO₂ adsorption and hydrogenation activity, offering a scalable and

papers.title: Data-Driven Design of Sustainable Thermoplastic Elastomers through Microbial and Computational Engineering
papers.abstract: The transition toward circular materials has intensified interest in sustainable thermoplastic elastomers (TPEs) that combine mechanical resilience with reduced environmental impact. This study presents a data-driven framework for the rational design of sustainable TPEs through the integration of microbial biosynthesis and computational engineering. Microbial platforms were optimized to produce bio-based monomers and polymer precursors with controlled molecular architectures, while computational modeling and machine learning techniques were employed to predict structure-property relationships and processing behavior. By correlating microbial metabolic parameters with polymer chain characteristics and thermomechanical performance, the proposed approach enables targeted tuning of elasticity, tensile strength, thermal stability, and recyclability. Experimental validation demonstrates that integrating predictive algorithms with bio-manufacturing significantly reduces development time and material waste compared to conventional trial-and-error strategies. The results highlight the potential of combining systems biology, polymer informatics, and sustainable processing routes to accelerate next-generation elastomer development. This work contributes a scalable pathway for designing environmentally responsible TPEs suited for automotive, biomedical, and consumer applications, while supporting global efforts toward low-carbon and resource-efficient manufacturing.

papers.title: HELMify: A Hybrid Rule-and LLM-Based Generator of Peptide Monomer HELM Names
papers.abstract: HELM is a hierarchical notation system for biopolymers that is an increasingly popular choice for representing peptides. In this system, each monomer name must uniquely identify a single monomer, and until now, chemists have named peptide monomers by hand using a limited set of rules. As the chemical space of monomers is practically unlimited, this naming process is too time consuming to be done by chemists, and is prone to inconsistency. To address this bottleneck, we developed two complementary automated naming approaches for HELM name generation: a zone-based namer which relies on hand-curated dictionaries of substructures, and a generative AI namer which relies on a pre-trained Large Language Model (LLM) with chemistry world knowledge. We evaluated both approaches on a set of publicly disclosed alpha amino acids. For a time-split test set, the zone-based namer produced usable names for 84% of cases: 54% matched the human-generated name exactly, and an additional 30% did not match, but were interpretable as the correct structure. The LLM-based namer produced usable names for 42% of cases: 33% of the names matched the human-generated name exactly, and an additional 9% were non-identical but still interpretable as the correct structure. In another 49% of cases, the outputs were considered close matches, and while not directly usable, they can still inform the generation of correct names. The zone-based namer is deterministic, fast, and independent of any previous names, explicitly handling zone order and chirality. The LLM-based namer can generalize from human‑named examples to propose names for novel chemical groups, helping fill library gaps. Together, the approaches offer complementary coverage: rules‑based precision and speed paired with data‑driven flexibility for novel moieties. Combining the strengths of both approaches paves the way for an automated peptide monomer naming process that can accelerate research by: (i) helping the community establish standardized guidelines for the rapidly expanding non-canonical amino acid (ncAA) space; (ii) streamlining integration with synthesis planning, inventory management, and analysis pipelines (iii) enabling more consistent annotation in ELNs, databases, and publications; and (iv) facilitating cross-lab replication and data exchange. Together, these advances can expedite method development, reduce ambiguity in collaboration, and ultimately support the discovery of novel peptides with improved drug-like properties.

papers.title: Biotechnology Meets Polymer Science: AI-Optimized Microbial Pathways for High-Performance Elastomer Production
papers.abstract: The convergence of biotechnology and polymer science is reshaping the landscape of sustainable elastomer production. Conventional elastomers, largely derived from petrochemical feedstocks, present environmental and supply chain challenges that necessitate alternative manufacturing strategies. Recent advances in synthetic biology, metabolic engineering, and artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled the rational design of microbial cell factories capable of producing elastomer precursors with enhanced efficiency and tailored properties. This study explores the integration of AI-driven pathway optimization with microbial biosynthesis to develop high-performance bio-based elastomers. Machine learning models were employed to predict metabolic flux distributions, identify gene targets for overexpression or knockout, and optimize fermentation parameters for maximal yield and material performance. The engineered microbial strains demonstrated improved monomer productivity, reduced by-product formation, and scalable biosynthetic stability. Furthermore, polymerization of the biologically derived monomers yielded elastomers exhibiting competitive tensile strength, elasticity, and thermal resilience compared to conventional counterparts. The findings highlight how AI-guided systems biology can accelerate the transition toward renewable, high-performance polymer materials while reducing environmental impact. This interdisciplinary framework provides a scalable pathway for next-generation elastomer manufacturing that aligns with circular economy principles and industrial sustainability goals.

papers.title: How Do DICER1 Syndrome Mutations Disrupt Catalysis? Unveiling Dicer Metal Binding Architecture and Mechanism of Action using MD Simulations and QM/MM Calculations
papers.abstract: The RNA interference (RNAi) pathway regulates gene expression and viral defense and has been harnessed in therapeutic solutions to inhibit otherwise undruggable proteins by preventing translation. Dicer initiates RNAi by generating cleaved RNA products that bind to a target mRNA to promote gene silencing. Mutations to the Dicer catalytic domain cause DICER1 syndrome, which increases the risk of cancers, including early childhood variants. However, the catalytic mechanism remains poorly defined due to the lack of structural data for Dicer bound to a substrate (or substrate mimic) in the presence of divalent ions known to be critical for nuclease activity. This study uses molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to uncover the first atomic level structure of the wild-type Dicer-RNA complex, including the binding pattern of two catalytically-essential Mg 2+ ions. Subsequently, quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) techniques are used to elucidate the Dicer catalytic mechanism for phosphodiester bond cleavage. Among three fully characterized pathways, our data suggest catalysis is only feasible when both active site Mg 2+ ions are directly coordinated to the RNA substrate and a hydroxide ion nucleophile is bound to an active site Mg 2+ ion. Phosphodiester bond hydrolysis proceeds through a twostep mechanism involving a phosphorane intermediate that is stabilized by direct Mg 2+-substrate coordination and a hydrogen bond with K1806. This newly identified mechanism is consistent with experimental kinetic data, the impact of mutating the corresponding lysine in mouse Dicer, and the active site architectures and proposed mechanisms for several other nucleases. Directed by the enhanced understanding of wild-type Dicer function, MD simulations subsequently show that six known 2 DICER1 syndrome-causing mutants likely impede catalysis by inducing unique active site disruptions that inhibit Mg 2+-ion coordination to the substrate. By furthering our knowledge of the structure and catalytic mechanism of wild-type and mutant Dicer, this work unveils the molecular underpinnings of DICER1 syndrome and opens the door for the development of enhanced RNAi-based therapeutics and biotechnologies.

papers.title: DFT vs ab Initio Wavefunction Methods for Reaction Barrier Heights
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of reaction barrier heights remains a central challenge in computational chemistry because transition states exhibit complex electronic structures characterised by stretched bonds, fractional bond orders and enhanced electron correlation. Since barrier heights enter exponentially into rate constants within transition state theory, even small energetic errors can produce substantial deviations in predicted kinetics. Density functional theory (DFT) has become the dominant framework for mechanistic studies owing to its favourable balance between computational cost and accuracy; however, approximate exchange-correlation functionals suffer from self-interaction and delocalisation errors that are amplified in transition state geometries, leading to systematic underestimation of barrier heights. In contrast, correlated wavefunction-based methods provide a systematically improvable treatment of electron correlation. Coupled-cluster theory with perturbative triple excitations, CCSD(T), remains the de facto reference standard at steep computational cost. This perspective critically compares the theoretical foundations, characteristic error patterns and practical limitations od DFT and wavefunction approaches for reaction barrier calculations, drawing on established benchmark datasets. Emerging reduced-scaling coupled-cluster techniques and data-driven models are discussed as promising strategies for bridging the gap between accuracy and computational feasibility. A clear understanding of methodological strengths and limitations is essential for reliable mechanistic interpretation and for the rational development of next-generation electronic methods.

papers.title: MaterIA: Learnable Tool Injection for Emergent Tool Discrimination in Molecular Transformers
papers.abstract: This work introduces MaterIA, a lightweight transformer (658K parameters) that predicts molecular properties directly from raw atomic data, atomic numbers, 3D coordinates, and pairwise distances without pre-programmed physical rules or domain-specific inductive biases. The key contribution is Learnable Tool Injection, a framework that offers physics-informed tools (spatial, electronegativity, and angular biases) as optional attention biases, each gated by a learnable scale parameter (bias_scale). The model autonomously determines which tools to use for each target property. On the QM9 benchmark (134K molecules), MaterIA exhibits emergent tool discrimination: spatial tools reduce HOMO-LUMO band gap prediction error by 72.3% while degrading internal energy (U0) predictions by 4.2%; conversely, electronegativity and angular tools improve U0 predictions by 29.9% and 30.7%, respectively. This selective behavior emerges without explicit supervision no loss term, reward signal, or architectural constraint guides tool selection. Analysis of learned bias_scale parameters reveals that the model amplifies useful tools (mean bias_scale of 2.35 for band gap+spatial) while moderating less relevant ones, with amplification magnitude correlating with prediction improvement. These results demonstrate that a transformer can learn not only to predict molecular properties but also to identify which physical information is relevant to each property, suggesting a path toward self-organizing molecular models that autonomously build their own physical intuition.

papers.title: Mid-IR ATR-FTIR with Simple ML Framework for PVC Screening and Polyethylene Subclassification with Perfect External Validation
papers.abstract: Reliable and chemistry-specific presorting of waste plastics is a prerequisite for safe and efficient recycling and upcycling. In this study, we show that mid-infrared ATR-FTIR spectra in the fingerprint region are sufficient to perfectly classify seven common plastics including polyvinylchloride (PVC) and to robustly resolve the three PE subclasses when combined with simple machine-learning models. We collected 770 ATR-FTIR spectra (2500-500 cm⁻¹) from LDPE, LLDPE, HDPE, PP, PS, PET and PVC, using commercial pellets together with PET from a post-consumer bottle and PVC from discarded laboratory gloves. Each pellet or cut piece was placed so that a reasonably flat face contacted an ATR crystal and was measured under a fixed clamp setting; spectra were recorded with about 2 cm⁻¹ nominal spacing and normalized before analysis. After truncation to the fingerprint region and normalization, spectra were compressed by principal component analysis (PCA), and the resulting scores were used to train support-vector machine (SVM) and shallow deep neural network (DNN). For the baseline dataset, all four models achieved 100 % accuracy on both internal test splits and a strictly independent external validation set; PVC false-negative and false-positive rates were 0 %, and LDPE, LLDPE and HDPE were perfectly resolved. To assess robustness to reduced spectral quality, we numerically degraded the spectra to effective resolutions of about 8 and 16 cm⁻¹ by convolving with a broadened instrument function and rebinning to coarser wavenumber grids. Even under the most degraded condition (16 cm⁻¹), SVM and the shallow DNN retained 100 % internal and external accuracy for PVC screening, PE-grade subclassification and full seven-class discrimination. These results demonstrate that ATR-FTIR fingerprints combined with straightforward machine-learning classifiers can deliver perfectly reliable PVC detection and PE subclassification across a realistic range of spectral resolutions, and they provide a general framework that can be extended to other grindable solid feeds.

papers.title: Ice-ray pentagonal packing of pseudo-fivefold helices
Quantum Efficiency of Electron Photoinjection from Magnesium into a Non-Aqueous Electrolyte
papers.abstract: Harnessing light energy through its interaction with metals remains a long-standing challenge. While noble metal plasmonics have been studied extensively, their high cost is a limiting factor. This motivates research into abundant and inexpensive metals with low work functions, such as magnesium. We report electron photoinjection from a magnesium electrode into dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO). The electrode was biased (−1.0 to −2.5 V vs. Ag/AgCl), illuminated with light (350-600 nm), and the photocurrent was measured. As a function of increasing photon energy, the quantum efficiency of photoinjection initially increases exponentially. However, beyond a threshold energy of 2.9 eV, it follows a power law with an exponent ~5/2, consistent with above-threshold electron injection into the conduction band of DMSO. Comparison of the observed threshold to the vacuum work function of magnesium suggests that the conduction band of DMSO is ~0.76 eV lower than the vacuum level. The quantum efficiency increases at more negative potentials, reaching ~10 −4 , a quantity comparable to plasmonic noble metal electrodes. This study will open opportunities to exploit magnesium as an inexpensive and versatile material for metal photoelectrochemistry, and potentially magnesium plasmonics.

papers.title: Chemistry-Principle Embedded Generalized Operator Networks for Accurate and Interpretable Organic Reaction Yield Prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of organic reaction yields is paramount for accelerating discovery, yet it presents significant challenges due to complex parameter interplay, vast chemical space, poor out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization, and limited interpretability. We propose ChemReactONet, a novel framework that fundamentally embeds chemical principles into its neural network architecture. Our approach employs a dual Generalized DeepONet structure to disentangle the intrinsic reaction propensity from external condition modulation. Specifically, the model learns a "base reaction yield" from reactant and product structures, and a "condition scaling factor." This factor is influenced by a chemically-informed Normalized Reaction Potential (Ψ *), derived from estimated reaction free energies and steric effects, alongside catalyst, solvent, temperature, and pressure. Trained on a comprehensive dataset with a rigorous OOD-focused partitioning strategy, including numerous unseen catalysts and new reaction types in test sets, ChemReactONet consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. It achieves significantly lower Mean Absolute Relative Deviation on OOD catalysts and entirely new reaction types compared to the next best graph neural network method. This work demonstrates superior generalization capabilities, particularly in challenging OOD chemical spaces, while offering enhanced interpretability to guide rational reaction design.

papers.title: Color-Changing Hydrogels for Visual pH Monitoring of Confined Living Systems
papers.abstract: Maintaining pH homeostasis in living systems is critical for sustaining cell viability and function For example, engineered expression microbes in confinement, like in bioreactors, may directly alter the pH of the media despite a controlled nutrient supply, hindering their own performance. This highlights the importance of methods to reliably monitor pH in situ in a wide range of environments. Here, we present a custom-built chamber (4 mL) designed for real-time visual pH monitoring. We use dual-dye hydrogel sensors spatially separated from active microbial cultures to monitor changes via image recognition and processing to generate numerical pH values. This workflow reproducibly generates quantitative pH measurements within ± 0.1 pH units relative to conventional sensors, highlighting an alternative material strategy for in situ monitoring of confined culture environments and the integration of systemlevel design to enable dynamic tracking in biological systems.

papers.title: Crystal size/strain modulation and balanced electrochemical activity regulate the water oxidation performance of hematite photoanodes
papers.abstract: Hematite (α-Fe 2 O 3) is one of the most promising photoanode materials in solar water splitting owing to its high theoretical performance, low cost and earth abundance. However, it has low practical efficiency due to its mismatching opto-electronic properties. Doping and annealing have been utilized extensively to improve bulk conductivity and surface reactivity. However, the underlying mechanisms for these improvements are still not fully understood. In this study, we investigated the interplay of doping and annealing conditions on crystal size-strain and electrochemical processes. Doping with Ti 4+ greatly enhanced bulk conductivity by not only increasing the n-type character of the material, but also shortening electron hopping distance due to lattice compression. However, this is countered by increased lattice strain and smaller crystallite size. A model was developed to explain the interplay of size-strain effect and electrical conductivity at various dopant levels. Co-doping with Ffurther improved performance without causing additional lattice strain. Although nitrogen annealing is necessary to reduce bulk charge transport resistance, it was found that air annealed hematite has more favorable surface charge transfer properties. A multistep-annealing protocol was then conducted, first in nitrogen, and then at a lower temperature in air, to balance the bulk and surface electrochemical processes. Our work highlights how high performant hematite can be produced by balancing these synthesis parameters.

papers.title: Novel Heteroaromatic Acyl-Tryptamine Conjugates: Four Structural Classes of Potential Dual-Action Prodrug Candidates
papers.abstract: Building on a previously described series of nicotinoyl-tryptamine hybrids, four novel structural classes are proposed in which the nicotinoyl moiety is replaced by alternative heteroaryl-carbonyl groups: picolinoyl (pyridine-2-carbonyl), isonicotinoyl (pyridine-4carbonyl), quinolinoyl (quinoline-carbonyl), and pyrazinoyl (pyrazine-2-carbonyl). These substitutions preserve the amide-bond prodrug concept while introducing distinct electronic and steric properties predicted to modulate receptor binding, metabolic stability, and bioavailability. No synthesis or biological testing has been performed; this preprint presents the structural rationale and hypothetical pharmacological profiles to stimulate further investigation.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights into Anion Intercalation for Nanosheet-Interlaced Bi-Based Catalysts
papers.abstract: The dynamic evolution of bismuth (Bi)-containing compounds represents a viable approach for fabricating nanosheet-interlaced electrocatalysts for electrochemical CO 2 reduction at industrially relevant scales; however, rational design remains challenging owing to substantial compositional and structural reconstruction under electrochemical conditions. Herein, six anions are experimentally and computationally investigated to elucidate their intercalation behavior in [Bi 2 O 2 ] 2+ interlayers. Operando Raman spectroscopy and ex situ SEM imaging reveal that HCO 3 - , CO 3 2- , NO 3 - , and Cl - readily intercalate into [Bi 2 O 2 ] 2+ interlayers, forming Bi 2 O 2 CO 3 , BiONO 3 , and BiOCl, respectively, with the intercalated anion governing the resulting nanosheet dimensions. In contrast, OH - and SO 4 2- fail to yield nanosheet-interlaced architectures owing to either the strong [Bi 2 O 2 ] 2+ -OH - interaction or the geometric incompatibility of SO 4 2- within [Bi 2 O 2 ] 2+ interlayers. DFT calculations further reveal that CO 3 2- intercalation is nearly thermoneutral with negligible interlayer contraction, rendering it the thermodynamically favored intercalant. These findings offer a generalizable strategy for engineering nanosheet-interlaced Bi-based catalysts through selective anion intercalation.

papers.title: Li₂PbO₃ Cluster Simulation: Exploring Local Polarity and Electronic Structure with Implications for Glass-Like Lead-Alkali Oxide Materials

Prebiotic synthesis of nucleotides in atmospheric plasma reactors with toroidal recirculation over Hadean hydrothermal fumaroles: role of the primitive magnetosphere and post-event distribution of organic products
papers.abstract: We present a hypothesis on the prebiotic synthesis of nucleotides in the late Hadean Earth (4.0-3.8 Ga) through atmospheric plasma reactors with internal toroidal recirculation generated over active hydrothermal fumaroles. The proposed mechanism integrates three cooccurring physical elements of the Hadean: (1) the interaction between volcanic electrical discharges and fumarole vapor plumes, which generates plasma volumes with a radial thermal gradient from 1000°C (core) to 200°C (periphery); (2) the resulting internal toroidal convection, which recirculates molecular precursors through specific temperature zones in 45 to 180 cycles per event; and (3) the primitive Hadean magnetosphere, weaker than today's, which modifies the dynamics of charged particles in the plasma, extends its duration, and orients post-event deposition gradients. Upon reactor extinction, the differential sedimentation of micro-droplets by size-a process that may extend from minutes to hours-distributes products in a radial spatial gradient that places complete nucleotides in nearby basalt pores, nucleosides in intermediate catalytic clay zones, and free bases in dispersed aerosol. We estimate a yield of 10¹²-10¹³ nucleotides per event, with efficiency 100-1000 times superior to scenarios without recirculation. The hypothesis generates four falsifiable predictions verifiable through laboratory experiments, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling, and geological analysis of early Archean formations.

papers.title: Stability of SDS Micelles in Reline / Water Mixtures: a Molecular Dynamics Study
papers.abstract: Deep eutectic solvents of type III, like reline, a mixture of choline chloride and urea, are a relatively new class of green solvent that displays physical properties intermediate between conventional salt solutions and ionic liquids. Well-established models used to explain colloidal stability and macromolecules conformation in usual solvents, including the hydrophobic effect and the formation of the electrical double layer, are not applicable to these solvents and their mixtures with water due to the strong non-ideal behavior and the high ionic strength of those solvents. Hence, in this work, molecular dynamics simulations were performed to evaluate the thermodynamic stability of sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) micelles in reline/water mixtures with different compositions by potential of mean force (PMF) calculations and splitting the contributions from the surfactant ionic head and the hydrophobic tail. The presence of reline reduces the favorable contribution of the surfactant alkyl tail to aggregation, indicating a reduction of the hydrophobic effect, which is explained by a smaller amount of water molecules in contact with the surfactant. However, the high adsorption of choline cations over the micelle surface also reduces the repulsion between charged heads. The second effect dominates over the reduction of the hydrophobic effect, resulting in more negative aggregation free energy and improved micelle stability in the presence of reline. The electrostatic potential from the anionic micelle was also computed and does not follow the usual double layer profile, presenting oscillations away from the micelle surface in mixtures with high reline concentration and with the choline cations almost completely replacing the sodium counterions from the micelle surface.

papers.title: Designing Coherence in Perovskite Quantum Dot Assemblies by Choice of Ligand
papers.abstract: Loss of coherence in the quantum subsystem by coupling to environment limits its applications to quantum information technology. Perovskite quantum dots because of their large absorption coefficient and high single-photon emission rates have garnered considerable attention for applications in quantum systems, but they are limited by rapid loss of coherence due to electron-phonon coupling. In this paper, we study the coherence timescales in dimer assemblies of cesium lead bromide quantum dots, bridged by different ligands. Typically, non-conjugated organic ligands give longer coherence in quantum dot dimers compared to monomers. However, if ligand frontier orbitals extend onto perovskite band edges, or if mid-gap ligand states appear, then coherence is short. In dimers with conjugated ligands, coherences can be elongated by selecting ligands whose frontier orbitals do not hybridize with the perovskite band edges. A number of factors guide the improved coherence times, including enhanced delocalization, surface passivation, and suppression of certain phonon modes in dimers compared to monomer. This study explores materialengineering strategy to enhance coherence in perovskite quantum dots for application in quantum information technology.

papers.title: UEPI-R Batteries: A Training-Free Regime-Transition Detector for Lithium-Ion Battery Degradation
papers.abstract: When a lithium-ion cell shifts from linear aging to accelerated capacity fade, operators today discover it too late-after the knee, or not at all without chemistry-specific models. UEPI-R detects this regime transition in real time from discharge-voltage waveforms alone, with zero training data and zero false positives across 803 cells and four chemistries. On Severson LFP (n = 82), the fade rate increases 2.84× after the alert (Cohen's d = 0.84), with the alert preceding the capacity knee in 81% of cells (n = 118; 95% CI: [74%, 88%]) by a median of 311 cycles. On Michigan NMC111 (n = 24), the acceleration is 5.64× (p = 4.2 × 10 −6), confirming that the mechanism generalizes beyond LFP. The algorithm fires at a median 97.6% retained capacity, requires 3.5 KB of memory, runs in O(n) time, and is compatible with embedded BMS hardware. A complementary capacity-fade channel raises coverage to 66.0% of cap-enabled cells (384/803). UEPI-R is a regime-transition detector, not a remaining-useful-life predictor.

papers.title: Drop-to-Drop Transfer of Magnetic Activity and the Formation of Heterogeneous Drops
papers.abstract: While the interactions between nanoparticles (NPs) and liquid drops have been extensively used for manipulating both drops and NPs, it has been a massive challenge to completely separate drop and NPs from each other (for a NP-laden drop system) without affecting their individual states. In a previous study (ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 2024, 16, 64253-64263), we achieved precisely that by extracting magnetic NPs in the form of an aggregate from the interior of a magnetic-NPladen drop. In this paper, we move one step ahead: we develop of technique by the virtue of which this NP aggregate extracted from a liquid drop (denoted as a source drop) is seamlessly transferred in its entirety into the interior of a second drop (denoted as a receiver drop), and in the process there is no permanent deformation of either of the drops. This transfer represents the first example of the seamless drop-to-drop NP transfer (and specifically for this case, the drop-to-drop transfer of the magnetic activity) without any permanent deformation of the drops. Also, this transfer makes the receiver drop heterogenous and one can witness intriguing events, such as the transferred NPs forming either skyscrapers-like solid structures or magnetic liquid layers with these structures/liquid-layers demonstrating distinct dynamics in the presence of magnetic fields of different orientations.

papers.title: TADF Emitters: How a Donor-Acceptor Phenylene Bridge Controls Their Photophysics
papers.abstract: We investigate new DMAC-TRZ analogues having an aza-embedded DMAC derivative donor structure to reduce donor strength, yielding 0.31 eV blue-shifted emission. The presence/absence of a bridging phenylene unit between the donor and acceptor moieties was found to be pivotal in defining the equilibrium conformational geometry of the emitters investigated, controlling the charge-transfer (CT) state energy and balance between radiative decay and reverse intersystem crossing (rISC). With a phenylene bridge, a quasi-equatorial (QE) conformation in both the ground and excited state is stabalised, leading to well-defined CT absorption and fluorescence bands. Without the phenylene bridge, a quasi-axial (QA) conformation ground state is adopted, pushing the CT state to higher energy. CT fluorescence is, however, observed having a large Stokes shift indicative of excited state reorganization to the QE conformation. Computational modelling highlighted that the phenylene bridge introduces conformational disorder, inducing strong D-A communication giving high absorption and fluorescence intensities. Without the bridge, this communication is lost reducing fluorescence quantum yield but gives rISC rates reaching 10 6 s-1. Our findings demonstrate that phenylene bridge mediated conformational control provides a powerful tool to modulate excited-state dynamics. Our new azaDMAC weak donor is a very promising design of high-performance deep blue TADF emitters.

papers.title: Scalable Cloud Architectures for High-Throughput Genomic Sequencing and Bioinformatics Workflows
papers.abstract: The rapid decline in sequencing costs and the widespread adoption of next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies have generated unprecedented volumes of genomic data, challenging the scalability and efficiency of traditional computational infrastructures. High-throughput genomic sequencing projects now demand elastic storage, parallel processing, and secure data sharing mechanisms capable of supporting complex bioinformatics workflows at scale. This study examines scalable cloud architectures designed to address these computational and operational challenges in large-scale genomics. The paper analyzes architectural models based on distributed computing, containerized workflow orchestration, serverless processing, and hybrid cloud integration. Emphasis is placed on dynamic resource allocation, workflow portability, fault tolerance, and cost optimization strategies that enhance throughput while maintaining reproducibility and data integrity. Key enabling technologies, including containerization frameworks, workflow management systems, distributed object storage, and cloud-native security controls, are evaluated in the context of alignment, variant calling, transcriptomic analysis, and multi-omics integration pipelines. Furthermore, the study discusses data governance, compliance considerations, and encryption mechanisms necessary for managing sensitive genomic information across geographically distributed research environments. Performance benchmarks and architectural design principles are synthesized to propose a reference model for scalable, resilient, and interoperable genomic data processing platforms. The findings demonstrate that cloud-native architectures significantly improve computational elasticity, workflow reproducibility, and collaborative research capabilities, while reducing infrastructure overhead and capital expenditure. The proposed framework advances precision medicine research, population-scale genomics initiatives, and real-time bioinformatics analytics by enabling robust, high-throughput processing across distributed cloud ecosystems.

papers.title: Iodine(III) Mediated Synthesis of Isoxazoles from Ynones via Cloke-Wilson-Type Rearrangement
papers.abstract: Herein, we report the first hypervalent iodine-mediated synthesis of isoxazoles from ynones. The reactions proceed via Cloke-Wilson-type rearrangement. A broad range of ynones efficiently converted to the corresponding isoxazoles.

papers.title: A rapid and practical direct α-halogenation of carboxylic acids with N-bromosuccinimide (NBS) or trichloroisocyanuric acid (TCCA) using catalytic p-toluenesulfonic anhydride
papers.abstract: A rapid and practical direct α-halogenation of carboxylic acids was developed using N -bromosuccinimide (NBS) or trichloroisocyanuric acid (TCCA) in the presence of catalytic amounts of p -toluenesulfonic anhydride (Ts 2 O) and H₂SO₄. The protocol proceeds without prior conversion to acyl chlorides and is applicable to bromination and chlorination. Compared with our previous system, the present method significantly shortens reaction times and facilitates product isolation. A broad range of carboxylic acids undergo smooth α-halogenation in good to excellent yields, and the reaction can also be performed under solvent-free conditions. The operational simplicity, scalability, and improved efficiency highlight the synthetic utility of this transformation.

papers.title: Local Solvent Ordering Drives Supramolecular Chirality Inversion
papers.abstract: Solvent composition is widely assumed to influence supramolecular chirality indirectly through bulk properties such as polarity or solvophobicity. Here we show that local solvent organization can directly dictate chiral pathway selection and invert supramolecular helicity. A chiral perylene bisimide bearing L-phenylalanine substituents (L-PhePBI) undergoes a complete reversal of helical sense in water/DMSO mixtures upon a narrow change in solvent composition (Δfwater = 0.2), despite maintaining a nearly identical degree of aggregation. The comparable polarity of the two solvent compositions excludes bulk solvent effects as the origin of this stereomutation. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that solvent-composition-dependent reorganization of the first hydration shell biases molecular twist angles within stacked assemblies, thereby selecting opposite chiral pathways. Variable-temperature spectroscopic studies further identify a kinetically 2 trapped chiral state that irreversibly converts to a thermodynamically stable enantiomorph upon heating. This thermal inversion is associated with a redistribution of hydrogen bonding from nearest-neighbor to nonadjacent molecular pairs, stabilizing a distinct packing motif. Together, these results establish a direct mechanistic link between local solvent ordering, noncovalent interaction reorganization, and supramolecular stereomutation, demonstrating solvent composition as a precise control parameter for programming chiral organization in supramolecular materials.

papers.title: True Closed-Loop Recyclable Hydrogels enabled by Imine Boronic Ester Crosslinking
papers.abstract: The relationship between molecular structure and macroscopic function is a foundational principle in materials science, in which subtle molecular variations produce pronounced differences in strength, stiffness, and elasticity. In hydrogels, replacing static covalent bonds with dynamic covalent bonds (DCBs) creates newfound capabilities, including selfhealing and recyclability. Herein, how substitutional differences in dual DCB imine boronic ester crosslinkers, together with matrix pH, influence hydrogel properties was investigated. A comparison of orthoand para-imine boronic esters showed the formation of 3-amino-benzoxaborole heterocycles in hydrogels derived from 2-formylphenylboronic acid. Tautomerization to the heterocycle significantly enhanced hydrogel elasticity, despite a lower crosslinking density than hydrogels formed with 4formylphenylboronic acid. Two closed-loop end-of-life management pathways were also demonstrated. Reprocessing through self-healing was accomplished, with hydrogels regaining at least 90% of their original rheological properties. A fully circular recycling pathway was also established, recovering all starting materials for reuse, with recycled hydrogels achieving over 100% recovery of rheological properties. Overall, the presence of previously undisclosed 3-amino-benzoxaborole structures was demonstrated, expanding the understanding of formylphenylboronic acids in polymeric materials, and complete closed-loop pathways were designed to inspire researchers in materials circularity to demonstrate and validate the full end-of-life processes for the materials they develop.

papers.title: From Zn to Cd: Extending Halide-First Stabilization Strategies to Dimethylcadmium through Ion Pairs
papers.abstract: Dimethyl cadmium (Cd(CH₃)₂) is an important molecular source for II-VI semiconductor growth; however, its extreme reactivity increases the hazards associated with transport and storage, motivating the development of safer, more stable derivative forms. Here, we computationally evaluate whether a halide-attachment stabilization strategy reported by Falkowski and co-workers (J. Phys. Chem. A, 2025) can be transferred to Cd(CH₃)₂. We examine the formation of ate species (CH₃)₂CdX⁻ (X = F, Cl, I) and quantify how substitution of chloride versus iodide and fluoride modulates structure, bonding, and thermodynamic stability.

papers.title: The growing role of open source software in molecular modeling
papers.abstract: The increasing importance and predictive power of modern molecular modeling, driven by physics- and machine learning-based methods, necessitates a new collaborative architecture to replace the isolated, traditional model of software development. The traditional approach often led to redundant engineering effort, high costs, and opaque systems that limit reproducibility, independent scrutiny, and scientific independence. Additionally, it results in taxpayer-funded research being left siloed in commercial tools where it cannot have as much impact as if it were returned to the general public. This perspective advocates for permissively licensed open source software as a scientific and economic multiplier by reducing the duplication of effort, enabling scientific validation of modeling tools, and frictionless experimentation with new ideas. Coordinated, multi-project consortia, such as Open Force Field, Open Free Energy, OpenFold, and OpenADMET have formed to collaboratively build shared computational infrastructure and release all methods under permissive licenses. The success of these large-scale efforts requires organizational structures that extend beyond code. The Open Molecular Software Foundation (OMSF), a US nonprofit, serves as a domain-specific institutional home and fiscal sponsor. By providing governance, administrative infrastructure, and dedicated research software engineers, OMSF aligns incentives across academic and industrial stakeholders. This framework enables a synergistic ecosystem where projects interoperate to accelerate innovation, eliminate duplication, and ensure long-term software sustainability, thereby creating durable foundations that elevate the entire molecular modeling community.

papers.title: Coupled Cluster Free Energies for Atmospheric Molecular Clusters: Benchmark and Matching Experimental Free Energies
papers.abstract: The initial formation of secondary aerosols, a large cause of uncertainty in modern radiative forcing modeling, can be simulated using quantum chemical methods. When based on quantum chemistry, the simulations have an exponential dependence on the free energy, requiring a high-accuracy description. In this study, we have computed harmonic frequencies and quasi-harmonic free energies for a set of 10 monomers and 29 dimers relevant for atmospheric molecular clusters at the DF-CCSD(F12b)(T*)/cc-pVDZ-F12 level of theory. The set is used to benchmark the M06-2X, PW91, ωB97X-D3BJ functions with the Jensen, Karlsruhe, and Pople style basis sets. The composite methods B97-3c, r2SCAN-3c, and ωB97X- 3c are also tested. We find ωB97X-D3BJ/ma-def2-SVP to be an optimal choice as it has low errors (mean absolute error of 0.13 kcal/mol) and few outliers in the thermal contribution. For calculations on larger clusters, B97-3c stands out. Using the ωB97X-D3BJ/ma-def2-SVP and B97-3c level of theories, we compute anharmonic frequencies using the VPT2 method and determine an anharmonic scaling factor of 0.961 and 0.953 for ωB97X-D3BJ/ma-def2-SVP and B97-3c frequencies, respectively. The scaling factor together with incorporating multi-conformer entropy effects and a high-level single-point correction at the Normal LNO-CCSD(T)/CBS(aug- 3,aug-4) are used to compare to experimental determined free energies of the 11 hydrogen-bonded systems. We find that we obtain sub 1 kcal/mol errors when incorporating the scaling factor, the multi-conformer entropy effects, and the single point correction.

papers.title: On Trapping of Ions Using Low E/N Rotating Electric Fields: Towards All-Pressure Ion Confinement
papers.abstract: Here, we introduce a novel approach that enables ion confinement at atmospheric pressure and extends it across pressure regimes where low to moderate E/N conditions prevail. We show ion trapping at atmospheric pressure by suspending ions within dynamic rotating electric fields. More broadly, we report ion confinement with applied voltages rotating at kHz frequencies, where ions are thermalized and confined by being constantly passed over by a rotating wave that causes them to move angularly forward and roll backward, keeping them confined. We report on theoretical and computational studies of ion trajectories inside a cylindrical volume with a constantly rotating electric field, with selected electrodes supplied with a high voltage and others with a low voltage. This setup created a voltage profile in a constant rotation about the cylinder's center. We also provide theoretical conditions for ion stability inside the cylindrical volume and compare them with simulation and experimental results. We define a parameter, the Lagrange Ion Stability (α LIS ), that expresses the condition for ions of a given mobility to be retained within the trap in dynamic equilibrium. This parameter depends on the applied voltage, the rotational frequency of the voltage, and the size of the cylindrical region. Under a stable trapping condition, the ions exhibited a large circular motion roughly around the center of the trap and small circular micromotions about the larger motion. The micromotion frequency correlated with the rotational frequency of the electric field. The amplitude of the micromotion depended on the mobility of the ion and the applied voltage. Two devices with different inner diameters (5 mm and 10 mm), a wide mobility range, and a range of voltages and rotational frequencies were evaluated to theoretically study the stability conditions. The confinement conditions were then generalized across a wide pressure scale. While lower pressures provided marginally higher E/N conditions for the ions (~30 Td), higher pressures supplied lower E/N conditions for ions under operational parameters favoring ion confinement. At 760 torr, ions predominantly experienced E/N conditions <10 Td while remaining confined. We report computational implementations of confinement using sinusoidal, quadrupolar and bipolar rotating potentials/waveforms to generalize the concept of mobility-dependent ion confinement. Consolidated experimental observations using sinusoidal and bipolar waveforms under atmospheric and lower pressures (up to 8 torr) showed good agreement with theory and computation. Overall, we report a novel device that can provide ion confinement across pressure scales, including atmospheric pressure, where ions are predictably stable. This new concept opens doors for analytical devices through ion trapping under ambient conditions. Keywords : atmospheric pressure, elevated pressure, ion confinement, ion focusing, ion trajectory simulations, mass spectrometry, rotating electric field

papers.title: Size-Extensivity and Connectedness of First-order Exchange Energy in Symmetry-Adapted Perturbation Theory: a Graph-based Approach
papers.abstract: We present a graph-based proof of size-extensivity and connectedness of the first-order exchange energy in symmetry-adapted perturbation theory (SAPT). The connected character of the first-order exchange energy is defined and demonstrated in two special cases: the second-quantized formulation of many-body SAPT and the multiconfigurational SAPT approach based on antisymmetrized product of strongly orthogonal geminals. The connectedness of the exchange-energy expression can be established via derivatives of chromatic polynomials π’(x) , evaluated at x=0. The proof holds to all orders in the overlap expansion.

papers.title: Overcoming cisplatin resistance with AI-driven metallodrug discovery
papers.abstract: Cisplatin resistance poses a significant challenge in cancer treatment, particularly when no alternative broad-spectrum drugs are available. While artificial intelligence has emerged as a powerful tool for drug discovery in organic chemistry, its application to metallodrugs remains largely underdeveloped. We hereby report a deep learning model for the screening and de novo design of platinum anticancer drugs. This model integrates a curated dataset of 3,725 platinum complexes with chemoinformatic representations supporting metal-ligand bonds and charges. After screening a large library of 214,373 known complexes, we selected 19 structurally diverse platinum complexes predicted by the AI model to be either active or inactive in different cancer cell lines. The experimental synthesis and testing of these complexes showed up to 72% agreement with the predictions. Leveraging AI-driven metal-ligand combinatorics for de novo design, we developed the PlatinAI complex, which overcame cisplatin resistance in both in vitro and in vivo experiments through a protein signaling network distinct from DNA damage. Additionally, we integrated our manually curated comprehensive platinum database of 17,732 IC50 values with the metal-supporting deep learning model to create MB Finder (www.mb-finder.org), a free public platform that enables users to search for platinum complexes with reported cytotoxicity and predict the anticancer activity of their desired molecules. This open-access resource provides a foundational tool for next-generation platinum-based drug discovery.

papers.title: Simulating enzyme catalysis with electrostatically embedded machine learning potentials
papers.abstract: To simulate enzyme reactions, multiscale quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) approaches are well established and popular. However, accurately and efficiently estimating enzyme activity is a challenge, because in general, precise methods are too computationally expensive. Here, we demonstrate that enzyme catalysis can be captured by coupling efficient machine-learned potentials (MLPs) for a reaction to the wider enzyme environment using electrostatic machine-learning embedding (EMLE). Our EMLE model is first applied to the natural Diels-Alderase AbyU, showing that it correctly differentiates the catalytic action on different enzyme-substrate conformations. Then, we show that training a reaction-specific EMLE model allows us to accurately capture the enzyme catalytic effects of the conversion of chorismate to prephenate, a reaction with a highly polarizable and charged transition state. In both cases, in contrast to mechanical embedding approaches, EMLE embedding allows accurate and efficient predictions of enzyme activity, agreeing with high-level QM/MM reference calculations. This approach facilitates the use of gas phase-trained MLPs in MLP/molecular mechanics (ML/MM) simulations and should thus be highly beneficial for computational activity screening of enzyme biocatalysts.

papers.title: Active Metasurface Thermal Emitters by Metallic Polymers
papers.abstract: Conducting polymers (CPs) have been a versatile and effective material for dynamically controlling optical properties with applications ranging from electrochromic windows and displays to variable infrared (IR) emittance devices and terahertz modulators. In particular, its biocompatibility, flexibility, reversibility, solution-processability, and non-volatile switching make it suitable for radiative thermoregulation under various application scenarios. However, the current CPs for variable thermal emittance devices largely have low conductivity and are limited to thin film configuration, resulting suboptimal emissivity tunability. Here, we numerically and experimentally demonstrate CPs with extraordinary optical conductivity and properly designed metasurface structure can outperform the conventional counterparts. The IR emissivity tunability is achieved by synthesizing solution-processable polyaniline doped with camphor sulfonic acid (PANI-CSA) and characterizing the complex refractive indices at its conducting and insulating state. A forward-designed broadband wide-angle metasurface emitter based on asymmetric Fabry-Pérot cavity and gap surface plasmon resonance effectively utilizes the lossy dielectric properties at its insulating state for the high-emissivity mode. When switched to the conducting state, the metasurface becomes highly metallic and reflective, resulting in the low-emissivity mode. This study marks a new approach as we perform the co-design of macromolecular and photonic structure to enable solution-processable active metasurfaces.

papers.title: Exploring Conformer Search Workflows using OpenBabel, Hierarchical Clustering and Quantum Chemical Optimizations: A Benchmark Study Including Oligothiophenes and Y6
papers.abstract: Identifying all energetically relevant conformers is crucial for accurate quantum chemical predictions of molecular and material properties, yet assessing the completeness of a conformer ensemble remains a persistent challenge. Among these is the open-source toolkit OpenBabel , which offers multiple conformer generation algorithms and user-adjustable parameters that can significantly affect search outcomes. In this study, we systematically investigate how different methods and parameter choices in OpenBabel influence the conformer search results, a broad set of reference molecules. We demonstrate our workflow for Oligothiophenes with their well-known conformational landscapes. Our workflow involves: (i) generating conformers with OpenBabel , (ii) clustering them based on geometric similarity, and (iii) optimizing the most energetically favorable representatives of each cluster using density functional theory (DFT). We further explore whether additional conformational space can be accessed by reinitiating OpenBabel searches from DFT-relaxed structures, thereby possibly identifying previously overlooked but energetically relevant conformers. We demonstrate the transferability of our workflow by applying it to the more complex and technologically important non-fullerene acceptor molecule Y6. By combining RMSD-based genetic searches with hierarchical clustering and normalized RMSD metrics, we establish a tree-wise, iterative conformer search strategy in which secondary searches are initiated from geometrically distinct conformers identified in preceding generations. We present a thorough benchmark and workflow analysis of a tree-wise genetic conformer search on a benchmark set of small molecules, whose conformers are well-established in literature. This work provides a practical, benchmark-based framework for selecting suitable OpenBabel parameters and developing reliable workflows for conformer identification through hierarchical clustering and DFT-based refinement.

papers.title: Accurate Structure Prediction of Natural Products with NatGen
papers.abstract: Natural products (NPs), as a vital source of pharmaceutical agents, have contributed to the development of 60% of marketed small-molecule drugs. However, NP-based drug discovery faces a major challenge due to the combinatorial expansion of NPs' configurational space and their complex 3D structures, which arise from atomic chirality dictated by stereospecific biosynthetic enzymes. To date, more than 30% of natural products with stereocenters lack complete stereochemical assignments, and only about 1% of known natural products have fully resolved crystal structures. To overcome this bottleneck, we introduce NatGen, an innovative deep learning framework designed to predict both the stereochemical configurations (R/S and E/Z) and the 3D conformations of natural products. NatGen integrates data augmentation strategies with generative modeling techniques and outperforms baseline models in configurational prediction, achieving a full-assignment accuracy of 78.39% (Top-5) on the COCONUT test set. In an external test set comprising 17 recently elucidated plant-derived natural products, NatGen attains a full-assignment accuracy of 88.24% (Top-5). The RMSD of the best matching conformation among the top 15 candidates generated by NatGen is consistently below 1.5 Å. Using NatGen, we successfully predicted the 3D structures of 721,010 NPs from COCONUT - the largest open NP repository to date - and made the full dataset publicly available at https://www.lilab-ecust.cn/natgen/.
