We believe this resource significantly expands the structural landscape of natural products and will empower researchers to cross-validate findings and accelerate progress in diverse fields including natural product chemistry, enzymatic biosynthesis, physical, organic and analytical chemistry, phytochemistry, NP and NP-derived drug discovery.

papers.title: In situ observation of ultra-giant spherulites in perovskite hydrates
Scale-Bridging Solid Adsorbents for Direct Air Capture: Integrating Material Chemistry, Structured Contactors, and Advanced Regeneration Processes
papers.abstract: As the global carbon budget rapidly depletes, the transition to a sustainable, stable climate demands the urgent, gigaton-scale deployment of negative emission technologies. Direct air capture (DAC) has emerged as an essential, emissions source independent pathway toward global net-zero targets. Compared to solvent-based systems, solid adsorbent-based DAC holds distinct advantages due to its broader material versatility, modular scalability, and streamlined equipment architecture. However, transitioning from laboratory-scale material discovery to commercial deployment requires a holistic, system-level engineering approach. Because intrinsic adsorbent properties dictate the design of scalable structured contactors, the selection of energy-efficient regeneration methods, and the ultimate techno-economic and environmental viability of the process, these interdependent components must be synergistically co-optimized. To address this co-optimization challenge, this review provides a critical, integrated evaluation of solid adsorbent DAC. By systematically analyzing recent advancements across adsorbent development, structured contactor engineering, regeneration strategies, and system-level assessments, we outline a strategic roadmap to accelerate the development of commercially viable solid adsorbent DAC technologies.

papers.title: Hybrid dispersion and chemical transport modeling frameworks for characterizing sources of ambient hydrocarbons in the Permian Basin
papers.abstract: Emissions from oil and gas operations contribute to elevated air pollutant concentrations in oil and gas production regions. Attribution of elevated concentrations to specific oil and gas sources is challenging because the sources are extensive and their emissions have highly complex spatial, temporal, and chemical emissions profiles. In this work, detailed emissions modeling is coupled with dispersion- and chemical transport modeling to evaluate the sources of light alkanes (ethane and propane) measured at an air quality monitor in the Permian Basin in west Texas. Local sources (< 50km away) are shown to produce the largest observed concentrations, but concentrations attributed to distant sources ( 50 km away) are, at times, dozens of ppb and contribute, on average, 20% of observed concentrations. At some times, distant sources are predicted to contribute more than 90% of the observed concentrations. Atmospheric chemistry is not predicted to significantly impact ethane and propane concentrations from local sources, but concentrations from distant sources and of higher molecular weight reactive hydrocarbons (e.g., benzene) can be decreased by up to 40% due to reactive losses, depending on the species and the season. These findings suggest modeling approaches for predicting ambient air quality in complex and extensive oil and gas regions like the Permian Basin require detailed treatment of both local and regional sources as well as atmospheric chemistry.

papers.title: Reaching the Physical Limits of Desalination Membrane Selectivity with Vapor-Synthesized Polyamide
papers.abstract: Desalination membranes are essential for global freshwater production, yet the performance of conventionally synthesized membranes is limited by the lack of synthetic control over the selective film. Solvent-based polymerization methods result in inhomogeneous density, nodular morphology, and the presence of nanoscale defects that hinder salt and boron selectivities. By employing a vapor-phase synthesis strategy, we circumvent the reliance on solvent interfaces to create compositionally homogeneous, defect-free thin-film composite polyamide membranes with Angstrom-level control over thickness. With a structure and thickness defined with nanoscale precision, we measure previously inaccessible properties of membrane selective layers, including intrinsic water and salt permeabilities, and explore the limits of thickness on membrane performance. Membranes with a 12 nm, vapor-synthesized, selective layer exhibit a two-order-of-magnitude reduction in both salt ions and uncharged boron molecules permeabilities, and a twofold improvement in NaCl selectivity relative to commercial desalination membranes. Mechanistic analysis, supported by theoretical modeling and molecular dynamics simulations, demonstrates that salt permeability increases sharply for films thinner than the Bjerrum length, revealing a physical lower bound on selective-layer thickness. These results establish a high-precision platform for probing and optimizing molecular transport in thin-film composite membranes.

papers.title: Conformations and Thermodynamics of Mechanically-Linked Polyelectrolyte Rings
papers.abstract: By means of Langevin dynamics simulations and a primitive model of electrolytes, we study the conformations and thermodynamics of the simplest mechanically linked polyelectrolyte: two identical, unknotted rings concatenated by a Hopf-link ([2]catenane). We consider both quenched (strong) and charge-regulating (weak) rings; for the latter, ionization is pHdependent and implemented via a stochastic constant-pH scheme. We find that the link acts as a topological hotspot where screening and correlations become highly nonuniform. In weak chains, ionization is locally suppressed at the tangle, yet the same region remains a preferred site for counterion accumulation. Increasing ionization swells and reorients the complex toward nearly orthogonal ring planes. Importantly, the rings keep a persistent contact at the link, rather than separating into a threaded interpenetrating geometry. We further show that quenched charge patterning provides an additional control knob: homogeneous quenched charge distributions reproduce the charge-regulating behavior at matched ionization, whereas diblock patterns stabilize contact-rich states via neutral-block localization at the link and concomitant counterion depletion from the tangle. For fully ionized chains, added salt induces a marked reorganization of the [2]catenane, with ring separation showing nontrivial trends as ionic conditions vary.

papers.title: Vacancy-Driven Phase Separation Governs Li+ Transport Degradation in Li2−xO2 : A Computational Study Relevant to Li–O2 Batteries
papers.abstract: Ionic transport in electrochemically formed lithium peroxide (Li 2− x O 2 ) is a critical factor determines the charging kinetics of lithium-oxygen batteries (LOBs), yet the atomistic origin of the experimentally observed Li + diffusivity drop during charging remains unknown. Here, we employ molecular dynamics simulations based on machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) trained on first-principles calculations to systematically investigate Li + diffusion in Li 2− x O 2 across a wide range of Li-deficiency levels. The results revealed that, at low Li deficiency, the Föppl-type framework is maintained and high Li + diffusivity is observed, whereas at high Li deficiency, Li vacancies aggregate in a layered manner, leading to the formation of LiO 2 -like phases and a marked reduction in diffusivity. The low interfacial energy between LiO 2 and Li 2 O 2 (0.41-0.59 J m -2 ) is identified as a key thermodynamic factor enabling this phase separation. These findings establish vacancy-driven phase separation as the primary atomistic mechanism underlying Li + transport degradation in Li 2− x O 2 , providing a microscopic explanation for the charging overpotential observed in LOBs and offering design guidelines for enhancing ionic transport through doping and interface engineering.

papers.title: Tuning the Architecture of High-Density Bottlebrush Block Copolymers to Control Their Photonic Properties
papers.abstract: The backbone rigidity of bottlebrush block copolymers (BBCPs) induced by the dense brushes distributed along their polymeric backbone has made them materials of interest for as self-assembled of photonic materials. Today, the rigidity of BBCPs is limited by the maximum number of brushes per backbone repeating unit synthetically accessible (≤ 2). Here, we report a methodology to yield polystyrene- b -poly(lactic acid) BBCP with five PLA brushes per backbone repeating unit (PS- b -PLA 5 ). A graft-through ring opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP) of PS macromonomer followed by the addition of a norbornene-based monomer bearing five hydroxyl groups (M(OH) 5 ) yields a block copolymer with a bottlebrush block and a linear polyol block (PS- b -PM(OH) 5 ). A graft-from ring opening polymerization of lactide initiated by the polyol macroinitiator then affords the desired PS- b -PLA 5 . Monitoring the monomer consumptions for the three polymerizations supports the successful synthesis of the targeted high brush density BBCP. The low solubility of the growing of PS- b -PM(OH) 5 favored a termination of the ROMP via recombination which results in the formation of triblock PS- b -PM(OH) 5 - b -PS (that can subsequently be converted into PS- b -PLA 5 - b -PS). Simple manipulation of the solvent composition for the ROMP provides control over the fraction of triblock BBCPs present in the final material. The self-assembly structure of the polymers containing different ratios of diblock to triblock were compared experimentally by SEM and UV-vis diffusion reflectance spectroscopy. All the material showed similar domain spacing which is consistent with predictions obtained from coarse-grained simulation. Overall, this work showcases the broad application of the GT-GF methodology in the synthesis of high density BBCPs and the control we have over the synthesized product.

papers.title: Phosphorodiamidate Linkages In DNA: Synthesis and Biophysical Studies
papers.abstract: Antisense drug development is an emerging strategy for the treatment of various genetic disorders. To enhance the therapeutic potential of antisense oligonucleotides, numerous chemical modifications and conjugates have been explored in which phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligonucleotides (PMOs) are well known for having therapeutic potential. In this study, we report the development of a DNA oligomer containing a phosphorodiamidate linked backbone. Thermal melting (Tm) studies revealed that duplex stability decreases gradually with the increasing number of diamidate linkages. However, Tm was comparable when the linkages were incorporated at both 5' and 3'-end of T12 sequence and at the same time the modification significantly improves resistance to exonuclease degradation compared to unmodified phosphodiester DNA. The enhanced stability conferred by this backbone suggests strong potential for future applications in therapeutic oligonucleotide design.

papers.title: A Novel Radial-Linear π-Conjugated Polymer by Integrating Poly(para-phenylene vinylene) and Cycloparaphenylene for Enhanced Optoelectronic and Electrochemical Performance
papers.abstract: Herein, we present a new class of hybrid conjugated polymer that integrate [8]cycloparaphenylene ([8]CPP) directly into poly(para-phenylene vinylene) (PPV) frameworks, creating a π-extended poly(cyclo(para-phenylene vinylene)) ([8]CPPV). This architecture represents a polymeric segment of an armchair single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT). Comprehensive characterization confirmed its well-defined alternating structure. Photophysical analyses revealed curvature-driven electronic coupling between the radial CPP and linear PPV π-systems, resulting in broadened absorption, red-shifted emission, and high fluorescence quantum yield. Furthermore, [8]CPPV demonstrates excellent performance as a lithium-ion battery anode, combining high initial capacity with stable cycling enabled by mixed pseudocapacitive and diffusion-controlled Li + storage mechanisms. These results establish [8]CPPV as a versatile all-carbon polymeric framework that bridges molecular nanohoops and extended π-networks, offering a tunable platform for optoelectronic and energy storage applications.

papers.title: Electrochemical Upgradation of Cn to Cn+1 (n = 1, 2, 3, 4…) Alcohol via C-C Coupling on Cobalt Phenanthroline Catalyst Complex
papers.abstract: Carbon-carbon (C-C) coupling reactions are crucial in modern synthetic chemistry due to their central role in construction of complex organic molecules. Herein, DFT calculations were performed to explore the detailed mechanistic pathway for the electrochemical upgradation of C n OH to C n +1 OH ( n = 1, 2, 3, 4…) through the C-C coupling of CO and C n OH on the Co(Phen) 2 catalyst complex. The most favorable pathway as predicted from our DFT calculation is *→*CO→CO*C n H 2 n +1 →*COC n H 2 n +1 →*OCHC n H 2 n +1 →*OCH 2 C n H 2 n +1 →C n H 2 n +1 CH 2 OH ( n = 1, 2, 3, 4...). The *OCHC n H 2 n +1 →*OCH 2 C n H 2 n +1 step is the rate-determining step (RDS) for this electrochemical conversion process. The C-C coupling reaction is enabled by the large open space at the Co active site provided the perpendicularly oriented phenanthroline ligands that facilitates the simultaneous adsorption of CO and alcohol fragment at the active site. Our results indicate that Co(Phen) 2 complex can be employed as an effective electrocatalyst for the upgradation of lower alcohols to higher alcohols with high product selectivity and low overpotential. Such an electrocatalyst will enable the use of CO for production of long-chain hydrocarbons, promoting the development of sustainable air fuels.

papers.title: Comprehensive Evaluation of Cryogenic Processing on Functional and Structural Behaviour of Biomedical Alloy CoCr28Mo6
papers.abstract: Highlights 1. Wrought CoCrMo alloys benefit from deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) 2. DCT increases corrosion resistance and raises microhardness values 3. Micro residual stresses are changed to compressive character 4. DCT demonstrates potential to enhance long-term implant performance

papers.title: A Classical-to-Quantum Selection Workflow for Hydration Microstate Identification in the Nav1.7 Sodium Channel Pore
papers.abstract: Voltage-gated sodium channels such as Nav1.7 control neuronal excitability and pain signaling, yet their narrow pores create heterogeneous Na hydration environments that can challenge fixed-charge molecular dynamics (MD) descriptions. Here we present a classical-to-quantum workflow to identify and prioritize structurally distinct Na hydration-coordination microstates within the Nav1.7 pore for downstream quantum mechanical refinement. Using explicit-solvent MD sampling, we define a protein-centered cylindrical pore region and compute time-resolved descriptors of pore hydration and Na inner-shell coordination using a distance-based criterion (3.2 Å Na-O cutoff). We classify Na configurations into chemically interpretable coordination microstates based on inner-shell ligand identity: water-only (W), mixed protein-water (PW), and protein-only (P). In an analyzed window of 20 frames spanning approximately 2 ns, the pore remains persistently hydrated while Na coordination is dominated by water-dominated states with a resolvable subpopulation of protein-contact configurations. The resulting representative snapshots provide quantum-ready starting structures for subsequent electronic-structure refinement (e.g., DFT or VQE) focused on local ion-ligand effects in confined ion-channel environments. In this manuscript we demonstrate the selection and classification workflow on an analyzed window of 20 frames (~2 ns) and do not report microstate-resolved quantum energies.

papers.title: A rapid and practical direct α-halogenation of carboxylic acids with Nbromosuccinimide (NBS) or trichloroisocyanuric acid (TCCA) using catalytic p-toluenesulfonic anhydride
papers.abstract: A rapid and practical direct α-halogenation of carboxylic acids was developed using N-bromosuccinimide (NBS) or trichloroisocyanuric acid (TCCA) in the presence of catalytic amounts of p-toluenesulfonic anhydride (Ts 2 O) and H₂SO₄. The protocol proceeds without prior conversion to acyl chlorides and is applicable to bromination and chlorination. Compared with our previous system, the present method significantly shortens reaction times and facilitates product isolation. A broad range of carboxylic acids undergo smooth α-halogenation in good to excellent yields, and the reaction can also be performed under solvent-free conditions. The operational simplicity, scalability, and improved efficiency highlight the synthetic utility of this transformation.

papers.title: Miniaturized HOXB13 Mimetics are Sequence-Specific, Methyl-Sensitive DNA Binders
papers.abstract: Homeobox protein Hox-B13 (HOXB13) is an oncogenic transcription factor associated with prostate cancer risk. Unlike most transcription factors, HOXB13 is methyl-sensitive and has been shown to be preferentially recruited to DNA prostate cancer risk loci. Here we miniaturized HOXB13 to create metal-stapled mimetics that can target its cognate primary DNA binding site in a sequence-specific, methyl-sensitive manner. Targeted profiling of 5-methylcytosine (5mC) recognition using V269X mimetic mutants revealed that Leucine can further enhance both methyl-sensitivity and methylspecificity through methyl-methyl contact with 5mC and decreased methyl-pi interactions with cytosine. Collectively, our study revealed novel insights into the molecular interactions of HOXB13 with methylated DNA, and new tools that will provide a structural basis for future development of a new class of sequence-specific methylated DNA binders.

papers.title: Evaluation of AlphaFold-derived Structures for Earlystage Virtual Screening: Utility and Limitations
papers.abstract: Structure-based virtual screening increasingly relies on computationally predicted protein models, particularly those generated by AlphaFold. However, the practical reliability of AlphaFold-derived structures in early-stage drug discovery remains incompletely characterized. In this study, a limited chemical space exploration (~329 compounds) and comparative docking analysis of oseltamivir (Tamiflu) against influenza A neuraminidase were performed using both AlphaFold-predicted and experimentally determined crystal structures. Spatial convergence was evaluated through center-of-mass (COM) distribution and pose clustering analyses. The AlphaFold-derived structure supported spatial convergence within the predicted binding region, enabling identification of binding-competent pockets. However, local geometric differences influenced affinity optimization and pose compactness compared to the co-crystal structure. These findings demonstrate that AlphaFold models are structurally informative for rapid binding region identification but require explicit geometric convergence analysis for reliable interpretation in virtual screening workflows. A two-stage strategy integrating exploratory screening and structural refinement is proposed for time-sensitive drug discovery scenarios.

papers.title: Comparative elimination analysis of lipid nanoparticle-encapsulated erythropoietin mRNA by multi-modal approaches suggests an effective doping control strategy for mRNA-based agents
FragBERTa: Exploring Fragment-based Molecular Representation Learning with SAFE
papers.abstract: Automated exploration of chemical space through machine learning has become a central strategy in modern drug discovery, where the ability to learn transferable molecular representations directly impacts predictive modeling performance. Recent advances in chemical language models have primarily relied on atom-level string encodings such as SMILES or SELFIES, treating molecules as sequences of individual atoms or characters. However, medicinal chemistry reasoning is often fragment-centric, emphasizing scaffolds, functional groups, and modular substructures rather than isolated atoms. In this study, we introduce FragBERTa, a molecular fragment-aware transformer-based representation language model pretrained using masked language modeling on Sequential Attachment-based Fragment Embedding (SAFE) representations. SAFE decomposes molecules into chemically meaningful fragments while preserving attachment information, enabling the model to learn fragment-level structural patterns within a sequence framework. FragBERTa is pretrained on 11 million unique SAFE sequences extracted from multiple public chemical databases and subsequently finetuned on diverse MoleculeNet benchmarks covering both regression (ESOL, FreeSolv, Lipophilicity, PDBBind) and classification (BACE, BBBP, HIV, Tox21, SIDER) tasks under random and scaffold splits. Our evaluation shows that FragBERTa achieves competitive performance across tasks, often matching or surpassing prior transformer-based models. In regression, it demonstrates strong gains in lipophilicity and protein-ligand binding affinity, including the best scaffold-split PDBBind performance within our comparison. In classification, FragBERTa attains the strongest reported random split ROC-AUC results on HIV and Tox21 and delivers robust performance across bioactivity, permeability, and toxicity benchmarks, indicating that fragment-based representations effectively capture biologically driven and interaction-sensitive endpoints. Collectively, these findings suggest that SAFE representations offer advantages over atom-level representations such as SMILES and SELFIES for scaffold-sensitive and interaction-driven tasks, highlighting the value of fragment-level inductive bias for future molecular foundation models in drug discovery.

papers.title: Local Solvent Ordering Drives Supramolecular Chirality Inversion
papers.abstract: Solvent composition is widely assumed to influence supramolecular chirality indirectly through bulk properties such as polarity or solvophobicity. Here we show that local solvent organization can directly dictate chiral pathway selection and invert supramolecular helicity. A chiral perylene bisimide bearing L-phenylalanine substituents (L-PhePBI) undergoes a complete reversal of helical sense in water/DMSO mixtures upon a narrow change in solvent composition (Δfwater = 0.2), despite maintaining a nearly identical degree of aggregation. The comparable polarity of the two solvent compositions excludes bulk solvent effects as the origin of this stereomutation. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that solvent-composition-dependent reorganization of the first hydration shell biases molecular twist angles within stacked assemblies, thereby selecting opposite chiral pathways. Variable-temperature spectroscopic studies further identify a kinetically 2 trapped chiral state that irreversibly converts to a thermodynamically stable enantiomorph upon heating. This thermal inversion is associated with a redistribution of hydrogen bonding from nearest-neighbor to nonadjacent molecular pairs, stabilizing a distinct packing motif. Together, these results establish a direct mechanistic link between local solvent ordering, noncovalent interaction reorganization, and supramolecular stereomutation, demonstrating solvent composition as a precise control parameter for programming chiral organization in supramolecular materials.

papers.title: Scanning Tunnelling Microscope-based Break-Junction Technique -A Tutorial
papers.abstract: Over the past two decades, molecular electronics has made significant progress towards discovering nanoscale analogues of conventional electronic components-including resistive elements, diodes, switches, transistors, and more recently, highly conducting wires. These advances have been largely enabled by the development of the scanning tunnelling-based break-junction (STM-BJ) technique, in which a thin metallic contact between the STM tip and substrate is broken in the presence of target molecules, allowing a single molecule to bridge the resulting gap. The STM-BJ technique enables precise and highly reproducible measurement of the molecule’s electronic transport properties, making it a powerful technique to explore physiochemical and electrochemical phenomena that are otherwise difficult to access.

papers.title: Outer-Sphere Modulation of Zr-based Metal-Organic Frameworks for Nerve Agent Detoxification
papers.abstract: Organophosphorus nerve agents with extreme toxicity have been still used in the past few years. Recent advances in Zr-based metal-organic framework (MOF) catalysts have emerged as promising platforms for efficient nerve agent degradation, based on highly active Zr6 nodes and further enhancement of the activity via ligand functionalization. However, catalytic optimization confined to proximal modulation, where functional groups often interact with substrates, and thus impacts of outer-sphere modulation are still veiled. Here, we present a strong influence of outer-sphere modulation in optimizing the catalytic activity of Zr-based MOFs for nerve agent simulant degradation. A series of Zr-based MOFs with porphyrin ligands was prepared by substituting porphyrin cores with different metal ions (Al, Cu, Co, and Fe). Notably, the Fe-substituted MOF exhibited superior hydrolytic performance against a nerve agent simulant, achieving a half-life of just 5 minutes at 1 mol% catalyst loading. This performance is comparable to the most active Zr-based MOF catalysts reported to date. Our findings highlight a new perspective for optimizing catalytic metal nodes of Zr-based MOF via outer-sphere modulation and provide a new paradigm for engineering high-performance MOFs for chemical defense.

papers.title: Curated Dataset, Structure-Property Relationships and Machine Learning Prediction of Band Gaps for One-Dimensional Bismuth(III) and Antimony(III) Halides
papers.abstract: Vast structural diversity and remarkable optoelectronic properties of organic-inorganic and all-inorganic metal halides continue to stimulate huge research interest. While the outstanding performance of lead halide perovskites has defined the field of perovskite photovoltaics, concerns regarding lead toxicity and long-term stability have driven the search for lead-free alternatives. Low-dimensional bismuth(III) and antimony(III) halides have emerged as promising candidates; however, their rational design remains hindered by the lack of established structure-property relationships and structure predictive possibilities. In an effort to fill this knowledge gap, we report here an open curated dataset of one-dimensional (1D) bismuth(III) and antimony(III) halides featuring edge-sharing {MX4}chain-type anions (M-Bi, Sb; X-Cl, Br, I), including experimentally determined optical band gap values. Leveraging crystallographically accessible structural parameters, we constructed two descriptor spaces for compounds with an α-{MX4}anion-type: a primary space based on M-X bond lengths and X-M-X bond angles (Full Geometric Descriptor Space), and a reduced space comprising average bond lengths and distortion parameters of building units [MX6] (Reduced Distortion Descriptor Space). Both spaces additionally incorporate descriptors capturing the interchain X•••X contacts, anion composition, and crystallographic experiment temperatures. Given the limited data volume, we deliberately employed classical machine learning (ML) algorithms with cross-validation and stability analysis. The resulting models achieve prediction errors of 0.10 and 0.11 eV for the two descriptor spaces, approaching a typical experimental uncertainty of optical band gap determination. The feature importance analysis reveals that geometric descriptors of the inorganic anionic framework dominate over noncovalent interchain interaction descriptors in governing the band gap. To promote reproducibility and further development in the field, we released a complete dataset of group 15 1D-halometallates, trained models, and supporting materials in an open-access repository under the MIT license (Figure S1).

papers.title: True Closed-Loop Recyclable Hydrogels enabled by Imine Boronic Ester Crosslinking
papers.abstract: The relationship between molecular structure and macroscopic function is a foundational principle in materials science, in which subtle molecular variations produce pronounced differences in strength, stiffness, and elasticity. In hydrogels, replacing static covalent bonds with dynamic covalent bonds (DCBs) creates newfound capabilities, including selfhealing and recyclability. Herein, how substitutional differences in dual DCB imine boronic ester crosslinkers, together with matrix pH, influence hydrogel properties was investigated. A comparison of orthoand para-imine boronic esters showed the formation of 3-amino-benzoxaborole heterocycles in hydrogels derived from 2-formylphenylboronic acid. Tautomerization to the heterocycle significantly enhanced hydrogel elasticity, despite a lower crosslinking density than hydrogels formed with 4formylphenylboronic acid. Two closed-loop end-of-life management pathways were also demonstrated. Reprocessing through self-healing was accomplished, with hydrogels regaining at least 90% of their original rheological properties. A fully circular recycling pathway was also established, recovering all starting materials for reuse, with recycled hydrogels achieving over 100% recovery of rheological properties. Overall, the presence of previously undisclosed 3-amino-benzoxaborole structures was demonstrated, expanding the understanding of formylphenylboronic acids in polymeric materials, and complete closed-loop pathways were designed to inspire researchers in materials circularity to demonstrate and validate the full end-of-life processes for the materials they develop.

papers.title: AirNet: A Deep Learning Driven Auto Baseline Correction Algorithm Balancing Global Smoothness and Local Fidelity
A Comparison of the Molecular Orbital (MO) and Orbital Exchange Methods for Calculating the Chemical Bond
papers.abstract: This paper discusses the major differences between the linear combination of atomic orbitals MO and orbital exchange methods for calculating chemical bonds. The MO method employs explicit functions whereas the orbital exchange method performs calculations numerically. The MO method assumes that the overlapping orbitals of the bonding atoms are distinguishable. The combined orbital method postulates that overlapping atomic orbitals are indistinguishable to the extent of overlap/(1.0+overlap). The distinction between orthogonality and distinguishability is discussed. The combined-orbital orbitals are little changed from the atomic orbitals of the bonding atoms. The MO orbitals are significantly changed from the atomic orbitals. The orbital exchange method calculates the bond energy directly; the MO method calculates the total energy of the molecule. The orbital exchange method utilizes no or few variable parameters, to produce more accurate results than the MO method. The MO method optimizes the bond energy in terms of a large number of variable parameters, sometimes a very large number.

papers.title: Artificial Glycan Decoys: A Strategy to Inhibit Ebola Virus Infection
papers.abstract: Multivalency is a fundamental principle of lectin-glycan recognition, governing both affinity and specificity of carbohydrate-mediated molecular interactions. The human macrophage galactosetype lectin (MGL), a C-type lectin that selectively binds galactose (Gal) and Nacetylgalactosamine (GalNAc) residues, serves as an attachment factor for several enveloped viruses, including Ebola virus (EBOV). Here, we report the rational design and synthesis of GalNAc-based glycans multiantenna that structurally mimic viral surface glycosylation architectures and act as competitive inhibitors of MGL-mediated viral entry. A library of glycoconjugates bearing two, four, or eight Ser(GalNAc) units was chemically synthesized, and their interactions with the carbohydrate recognition domain of MGL (MGL-CRD) were investigated using 1 H, 15 N-HSQC-based NMR titrations and isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC). These studies revealed a pronounced multivalency-dependent increase in affinity and aviditydriven stabilization of the lectin-glycan complex, consistent with the simultaneous engagement of multiple MGL binding sites. Functional inhibition assays employing pseudotyped and wild-type EBOV particles demonstrated that these multiantenna constructs efficiently block MGL-mediated viral entry, achieving submicromolar inhibitory potency. Together, these findings establish GalNAc-based multiantenna glycans as effective chemical decoys that disrupt lectin-mediated viral attachment and highlight multivalency as a powerful molecular design strategy for antiviral intervention.

papers.title: Cycloazulenylene
Uncertainty-Aware Mixture Models of First Significant Digit Frequencies Detect Irregularities in Scientific Data
papers.abstract: Big data is the essence of modern research. Therefore, data integrity matters more than ever, motivating scalable tools for detecting anomalies across large collections of datasets. A promising yet underexplored approach is Benford's law, which posits that in naturally occurring datasets across several domains, smaller digits occur more frequently as leading digits. Deviations from this pattern can serve as an anomaly signal, flagging datasets for targeted expert review. However, quantifying the degree of adherence to Benford's law and estimating the associated uncertainty is challenging, especially across datasets of varying sizes. We introduce Simulation-Based Benfordness Estimation (SBBE), a Bayesian framework that models an observed dataset as a mixture of a Benford-conforming ("natural") component and a non-conforming component. SBBE returns uncertainty-aware estimates and enables interpretability and comparisons across datasets of different sample sizes. We validate SBBE on simulations and real-world datasets known to follow Benford's law. Finally, we apply SBBE to a bioactivity data case study, where rich metadata enable targeted follow-up analyses. Using SBBE, we detect irregularities in a highly curated database and trace likely sources of deviation, demonstrating that SBBE can serve as a domain-agnostic proxy for data quality.

papers.title: Dual-SplitNluc: A Spectrally Resolved Bioluminescence Platform Enabling Duplex Homogeneous Immunoassays
papers.abstract: Bioluminescence (BL)-based assays are broadly used for genetic reporter assays, imaging, as well as in vitro biomarker or serological analysis. However, nearly all existing BL assays are operated in a single-channel mode, which limits the detection capacity to one analyte each time. To extend the potential of BL assays, we developed the Dual-SplitNluc platform, a spectrally resolved BL reporter system which enables simultaneous detection of two analytes in homogeneous format based on spectral unmixing. Dual-SplitNluc represents the integration of our previously reported SplitNluc system together with SplitNanoBRET, an orange-emitting complementation-based immunoassay platform derived from SplitNluc. With chemical modification of the SplitNluc reporter by adding a fluorophore acting as a BL resonance energy transfer (BRET) acceptor, red-shifted photon emission can be generated and spectrally separated from the conventional SplitNluc signal. Through mathematical deconvolution of the integrated luminescence readouts, the original BL signals from each individual analyte can be extracted and utilized for ratiometric or quantitative analysis of both analytes. Collectively, Dual-SplitNluc extends BL assays beyond the single-analyte mode and provides a generalizable strategy for duplex and potentially higher-order multiplex homogeneous detection using spectral resolution as an orthogonal analytical dimension.

papers.title: Natural Orbital Correlation Analysis of Cluster Bonding: From Aromatic Clusters to Metallic Superatoms with Quantum Topology Probes
papers.abstract: We present a systematic study of electron correlation across molecular and cluster systems using the number of effectively unpaired electrons ND = P i ni(2 − ni)—the Takatsuka–Head-Gordon index—computed from coupled-cluster natural orbital occupations over the complete correlated orbital space. Computed at the CCSD/def2-SVP level, all systems studied exhibit substantial total electron correlation when the full natural orbital space is retained: aromatic Al4 2 – (ND = 3.84), antiaromatic Al4 4 – (4.03), planar and icosahedral B12 clusters (4.42 and 4.99), heteroatomic B6N6 (5.11), and cesium–aluminum superatoms Cs3Al8 – and Cs3Al12 – (5.58 and 7.10, respectively). We show that ND is an extensive quantity dominated by the dynamic correlation tail over many weakly occupied virtual orbitals, and introduce the per-electron correlation density fe = ND/Ncorr as a complementary intensive measure. This intensive measure reveals a clear separation: small clusters (Al4, B12, B6N6) exhibit fe ≈ 0.07–0.14, while metallic superatoms show fe ≈ 0.04, reflecting the diluted nature of correlation in large delocalized systems. We demonstrate that truncation of the natural orbital space to a small active window dramatically underestimates ND, and that complete occupation data are essential for physically meaningful correlation diagnostics. In a separate study, we explore whether molecular bonding topology generates characteristic entanglement signatures on a neutral-atom quantum processor (Pasqal). Mapping atomic coordinates of nine molecular systems onto Rydberg atom registers, we find that different chemical topology classes—aromatic, antiaromatic, cage, and metallic—produce systematically distinct entanglement patterns, suggesting that molecular graphs encode topological information accessible to analog quantum hardware.

papers.title: Screening ASb2O6 (A = Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba, Cd) for High Performance Transparent Conducting Oxides
papers.abstract: Transparent conducting oxides (TCOs) play an indispensable role in modern optoelectronic technologies. However, industry primarily relies on a limited range of n-type oxides, severely constraining the design flexibility and optimization of optoelectronic device architectures. Expanding the range of known TCOs would significantly broaden the available electron affinities, facilitating precise energetic matching and thereby enhancing device performance. Recently, Sb(V)-based oxides have emerged as promising candidates, introducing a new class of potential TCOs. In this study, we performed a computational screening of the ASb 2 O 6 series (A = Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba, Cd) to identify promising TCO candidates. Our analysis reveals that Ga-doped MgSb 2 O 6 has a moderate carrier concentration of around 10 17 cm −3 , which can be further enhanced with higher annealing temperatures, while Y-doped CdSb 2 O 6 is predicted to be a degenerate TCO. Experimental characterisation of solid-state synthesised Y-doped CdSb 2 O 6 powders corroborates these computational predictions, where Y incorporation leads to a Burstein-Moss widening of the optical band gap and a 0.1 eV shift of XPS core levels to higher binding energies, confirming a Fermi-level rise due to n-type doping. In addition, the resonant nature of Y Cd preserves high mobility and reinforces the material’s strong potential for practical applications in next-generation optoelectronic devices.

papers.title: Intrinsic electrocatalytic activity of nitrogen-doped monolayer graphene observed using a Janus bilayer design
papers.abstract: Nitrogen doping is a widely-used strategy for enhancing the electronic and electrocatalytic properties of graphene. On single-sheet graphene electrodes, substrate-induced charge density effects obscure their intrinsic behavior and limit the efficiency of surface-sensitive electron transfer. Here, we report a Janus bilayer electrode architecture that decouples a nitrogen-doped graphene top layer from the substrate via a pristine graphene bottom layer. This design allows the presentation of catalytically active nitrogen sites while simultaneously suppressing substrate effects, enabling a direct evaluation of the intrinsic effect of nitrogen-doping on the electron transfer (ET) properties of graphene. Using ferricyanide as a redox-probe, we show that the ET kinetics of pristine bilayer graphene are pH-dependent, while nitrogen-doped bilayer graphene displays stable, pH-independent redox behavior. As an application avenue of biological relevance, we demonstrate that nitrogen-doped bilayer graphene exhibits a reduced overpotential for NADH oxidation. These results demonstrate that the synergy between substrate decoupling and controlled nitrogen incorporation yields a robust electrode architecture with enhanced stability and improved electrocatalytic activity.

papers.title: Hardware Software Synergy in Proteomics: Systematic Evaluation Across Mass Spectrometry Platforms, Search Engines, and Rescoring Methods
papers.abstract: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics has advanced through parallel improvements in hardware (instrumentation) and software (data analysis), yet whether these improvements interact synergistically or provide diminishing returns remains unclear. Here, we systematically evaluate hardware-software co-evolution across eight mass spectrometry platforms, three generations of search engines, and multiple rescoring approaches, yielding 72 unique hardware-software combinations spanning from 2004-2024. Our results reveal that hardware and software improvements produce synergistic rather than substitutive benefits. Here, machine learning-based rescoring consistently identifies peptides from low-intensity precursors that produce noisier, more challenging spectra. Crucially, because of increased sensitivity and speed, modern instruments detect more low-intensity precursors, increasing the population of challenging spectra where rescoring provides the greatest benefit. However, this expanded detection depth comes at a cost: recovered low-abundance peptides exhibit inherently higher quantification error, creating a fundamental trade-off between proteome coverage and quantification accuracy. Together, these findings provide a systematic overview of how hardware and software advances have jointly shaped proteomics performance over the past two decades.

papers.title: Unlocking the Potential of Organoaluminum Reagents for Versatile C-C Couplings Using YPhos-Pd Catalysts
papers.abstract: We report a general and efficient protocol for the palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling of aryl chlorides with a broad range of organoaluminum nucleophiles, enabled by strongly donating ylide-functionalized phosphines (YPhos). Unlike other earthabundant organometallic reagents, the protocol demonstrates broad functional group tolerance, even allowing for late-stage functionalizations of complex molecules. In general, high selectivities and yields are achieved, while maintaining the high reactivity characteristics of this class of compounds even at room temperature. The presented protocol highlights the key advantages of this thus far underestimated class of nucleophiles in coupling chemistry and illustrates both the strengths and limitations of in situ generated alkyl-, aryl-, alkenyl-, and alkynylaluminum reagents.

papers.title: Optimize before you Synthesize - Enhancing the Ionic Conductivity of Li7SiPS8 using Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: Tetragonal Li 7 SiPS 8 is a superionic solid electrolyte, yet its Li ion conductivity suffers from the presence of an amorphous side phase. Attempts to optimize the ionic conductivity, however, are incremental and hence time-consuming, because the relationship between synthesis conditions and electrolyte performance is largely unknown. In this work, we employ Bayesian Optimization (BO) as an efficient design-of-experiment approach to increase the ionic conductivity of the Li 7 SiPS 8 system. Our data-driven workflow reproducibly yields Li 7 SiPS 8 with ionic conductivities exceeding 7mScm −1 at room temperature, an increase by up to 350 % compared to previously reported routes. Simultaneously, the optimized solid-state synthesis lowered the synthesis temperature by 100K (20 %) and shortened the reaction time by 76 h (76 %), delivering a more energy-efficient and, hence, sustainable process. To probe the origin of the increased conductivity, we examined six representative samples by quantitative Rietveld refinements, synchrotron X-ray powder diffraction, pair distribution function analysis, solid-state and pulsed-field-gradient NMR, electron microscopy, and Raman spectroscopy. We demonstrate that BO can help navigate the complex synthesis parameter space, thereby accelerating the development of high-performance sulfide electrolytes for next-generation batteries.

papers.title: Bridging between structure-based and data-driven affinity prediction
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand binding affinity prediction is central in computer-aided drug design, and a wide range of physics-based, empirical and machine learning (ML) tools have been developed for this purpose. Scientists are often tasked with choosing an optimal tool for a given discovery problem, which can be difficult. Physical models typically perform best in the absence of target-specific data, but are often outperformed by ML models as the amount of data on a given target grows. Here, we introduce a method to smoothly transition from physics-based to knowledge-based predictions based on the uncertainty of each model. We apply this framework to combine docking scores with predictions from a Gaussian Process model trained on binding affinities from two industrial datasets. We show that combining structure-based and ML models significantly improves the prediction accuracy if training data is limited, whereas the weighting smoothly shifts from docking to ML as more data is acquired. We also show that structure-based methods, being insensitive to the distribution of binders across chemical space, can improve generalizability to new chemistries and increase the hit rate in active learning screens where the binder density varies among scaffolds in a virtual library. Thus, integrating predictions from multiple tools not only optimizes the use of limited experimental data but also ensures more robust performance compared to reliance on a single model.

papers.title: Coupling High-Throughput DFT, Automated Experimentation, and Adaptive Experimental Design to Achieve Selective Rare-Earth Element Separations
papers.abstract: Developing new separation technologies for rare-earth elements is essential for sustaining the critical materials supply chain. Toward this end, we developed a pH-controlled solvent extraction strategy employing an aqueous-phase holdback agent to enable selective lanthanide separations, driven by an integrated computational, machine learning, and automated experimental high-throughput workflow. Database screening combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations identified oxaloacetic acid as a promising holdback agent that enhanced selective extraction of four lanthanides (Nd, Eu, Dy, Ho) when paired with the di-(2-ethylhexyl)phosphoric acid (HDEHP) extractant. Within this framework, the dependence of lanthanide solvent extraction was determined across a multi-dimensional chemical matrix (pH, extractant concentration, holdback agent concentration, and salt concentration) using automated, high-throughput experiments coupled with multi-objective Bayesian Optimization. Through efficient exploration of a large experimental space, we discovered Eu, Dy, and Ho could be selectively extracted over Nd in acidic media at pH~2.0. Surprisingly, Eu could further be separated from Dy and Ho when the pH was decreased slightly to ~0.5. DFT and machine learning with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analyses revealed that oxaloacetic acid protonation was likely responsible for the selectivity change. Overall, this work establishes an adaptive, data-driven framework for rapid separation design in grouped lanthanide separations. Multi-objective Bayesian Optimization eliminated the need to conduct 3,300 of the 3,840 experiments needed compared to a complete grid-based, exhaustive sampling approach. This gain in efficiency accelerates separation discovery, provides a foundation for future development, and moves the field one step closer to achieving a self-driving separation laboratory.

papers.title: Temperature-Dependent N₂ Reduction and Energy Demands of Mo-and V-Nitrogenases
papers.abstract: Nitrogenase catalyzes the ATP-dependent reduction of dinitrogen to ammonia, a key step in the global nitrogen cycle. The Mo-and V-dependent nitrogenase isozymes are expressed under different environmental conditions, including temperature. Yet very little is known about how the product profiles and energy (ATP) requirements for these isozymes change with temperature. Here, we examine the temperature dependence of total electron flux, electron partitioning into the products NH3 and H2, and ATP energy costs per N2 fixed for purified Mo-and V-nitrogenases from Azotobacter vinelandii over a 10-50 ˚C temperature range. Both isozymes exhibit similar temperature-dependent scaling of total electron flux to all products across the temperature range, but with significantly different distributions of electrons to H2 or NH3 formation. As temperature increases, V-nitrogenase diverts an increasing fraction of electron flux into H2 formation, whereas Mo-nitrogenase maintains a nearly constant electron partitioning to N2 reduction. The ATP molecules hydrolyzed per N2 reduced change little for the Mo-nitrogenase across this temperature range, but rises significantly for the V-nitrogenase with increasing temperature, reaching over 200 ATP per N2 fixed at 50 ˚C. These results demonstrate that, in A. vinelandii, the Mo-and V-nitrogenases exhibit significantly different responses of electron partitioning to products and ATP hydrolyzed per N2 reduced across the temperature range. These findings suggest environmental conditions under which each isozyme would be optimal, with V-and Monitrogenase both being favorable at low temperatures and Mo-nitrogenase being the only energetically reasonable enzyme at higher temperatures.

papers.title: A Comparative Study of SMILES, SELFIES, and ECFP4 Representations for Molecular Similarity Search
papers.abstract: We compare SMILES and SELFIES embeddings generated by two transformer models (ChemBERTa, SELFormer) against 1024-bit ECFP4 fingerprints for molecular similarity search. Using thirty chemically diverse query molecules, we retrieve the top-k nearest neighbours k ∈ {5, 8, 10, 15, 20, 25, 35} via cosine similarity for all embedding representations and Tanimoto's coefficient for fingerprints. Hits are evaluated on chemical similarity (Hamming distance), structural similarity (Graph Edit Distance, GED), and functional similarity (Functional Hamming Distance). Statistical significance is assessed with one-way ANOVA and Tukey's HSD. Our results confirm that ECFP4 with Tanimoto yields the lowest mean Hamming distances (mean=12.5 at k=35) as well as the lowest mean GEDs (mean=18.9). SELFIES embeddings consistently outperform SMILES embeddings yet remain inferior to fingerprints.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Mixture Models of First Significant Digit Frequencies Detect Irregularities in Scientific Data
papers.abstract: Big data is the essence of modern research. Therefore, data integrity matters more than ever, motivating scalable tools for detecting anomalies across large collections of datasets. A promising yet underexplored approach is Benford's law, which posits that in naturally occurring datasets across several domains, smaller digits occur more frequently as leading digits. Deviations from this pattern can serve as an anomaly signal, flagging datasets for targeted expert review. However, quantifying the degree of adherence to Benford's law and estimating the associated uncertainty is challenging, especially across datasets of varying sizes. We introduce Simulation-Based Benfordness Estimation (SBBE), a Bayesian framework that models an observed dataset as a mixture of a Benford-conforming ("natural") component and a non-conforming component. SBBE returns uncertainty-aware estimates and enables interpretability and comparisons across datasets of different sample sizes. We validate SBBE on simulations and real-world datasets known to follow Benford's law. Finally, we apply SBBE to a bioactivity data case study, where rich metadata enable targeted follow-up analyses. Using SBBE, we detect irregularities in a highly curated database and trace likely sources of deviation, demonstrating that SBBE can serve as a domain-agnostic proxy for data quality.

papers.title: Modulation of adenosine diphosphate-magnesium ion radical pair spin populations in an external magnetic field
papers.abstract: Life's dependence on adenosine triphosphate (ATP) makes its synthesis one of the most important biochemical processes in nature. During ATP synthesis, the (Mg 2+)-adenosine diphosphate (ADP) complex is formed. It has been posited that magnetic field effects (MFEs) may arise through intermediate access of a radical pair state. Prior studies have invoked radical pair mechanisms to explain MFEs and magnetic isotope effects (MIEs) in enzymes involved in ATP synthesis. However, the microscopic conditions required for such effects to occur-and to be reproducibly measured-have not been clearly established. In this work, we investigate the microscopic conditions required for MFEs in the ADP-Mg dimer and identify the criteria for magnetic field sensitivity. Thermal suppression of singlet pathways was observed in the low-moderate magnetic field regime. Corresponding triplet populations exhibited a robust bimodality, with a dominant orientation-independent maximum near 2.2 mT alongside a secondary orientation-dependent maximum at 50 mT. Modelling of MIEs from Mg revealed minimal differences in the spin statistics, suggesting that MIEs are a secondary factor rather than a governing determinant. Embedding these field-dependent spin populations within a time evolution framework demonstrated that MFEs shift the balance between productive and unproductive radical pair recombination, yielding an up to 5-fold increase in effective ATP yields. These results establish a concrete physical basis for magnetic sensitivity of radical pair dynamics in ATP synthesis, and delineate field regimes in which spin-state populations can, in principle, couple to bioenergetic chemistry, while also elucidating the conditions key to observing MFEs in ATP synthesis.

papers.title: Mechanistic Investigation of [Co2(CO)8] Catalyzed Photoaminocarbonylation
papers.abstract: Recent advances in cobalt photocatalyzed carbonylaLon methods offer an efficient syntheLc route to a range of amides and esters. Although preliminary studies provide important mechanisLc insights, the kineLcs of these reacLons have not been studied in detail. Herein we report an in-depth mechanisLc invesLgaLon into the [Co2(CO)8] catalysed aminocarbonylaLon of aryl halides. Rarely used 59 Co NMR spectroscopy provided evidence for [Co(CO)4]as an on-cycle catalyLc intermediate. Orders in reagents, HammeY analysis, and Eyring analysis gave unique insight into both photon-limited and photon-unlimited regimes. Data strongly suggested that the turnover-limiLng step of catalysis is reacLon of [Co(CO)4]with the aryl bromide. Plausible mechanisms for this step were considered and differenLated by experimental data including quantum yield measurements, radical probes, and compeLLon experiments. It is concluded that this step most likely occurs through a light-promoted nucleophilic aYack of the cobalt anion on the aryl bromide. In turn, this knowledge was used to expand catalysis to more challenging reagents such as aryl chlorides, low nucleophilicity amines, and acyclic vinyl halides. Enhanced catalyst efficiency (TON, TOF improved > 10-fold) was also achieved for established substrates, strengthening the industrial use case of this technology. In 2023, the amide moLf was present in 71 of the top 100 small molecule drugs. 1 In 2018, amide synthesis through catalyLc, atomeconomical and low-waste routes was named the second most important challenge for modern chemistry by industrial leaders. 2 Yet, years later, the challenges surrounding sustainable amide synthesis sLll prevail.
