papers.title: Assessment of Trajectory Surface Hopping Methods in Long-Time Nonadiabatic Dynamics
papers.abstract: We present an assessment of an extensive set of trajectory surface hopping methodologies for modeling long-time population dynamics in a two-level spin-boson model. The considered methodological recipes involve combinations of three surface hopping approaches with five decoherence correction methods, several decoherence time computation schemes, and two initial conditions sampling methods. On top of these combinations, phase correction approach of Shenvy, Subotnik, and Yang (SSY) are considered. By exploring a wide range of metaparameters controlling decoherence and dephasing times, we find the optimal performance of such method and provide a ranking of such best-performing approaches. We find that inclusion of the SSY correction generally over-accelerates the population relaxation dynamics. We also find a strong dependence of the TSH calculations on the type of initial conditions sampling: Wigner sampling leads to overestimated population transfer rates and requires decoherence corrections. Simplified decay of mixing approach is found to perform well in this situation. On the contrary, Boltzmann 2 sampling leads to surprisingly remarkable performance of bare TSH schemes without decoherence, which may be a consequence of error cancellation. We provide a critical discussion of the observed trends in different methods' performance and suggest possible avenues for their further improvements.

papers.title: Confidence intervals on the kinetic parameters of condensed-phase reactions
papers.abstract: This study introduces a novel methodology for deriving the confidence intervals on the kinetic parameters—including the rate constant, conversion function, activation energy, and pre-exponential factor—in condensed-phase reactions. The approach employs multiple linear regression to factorize the reaction rate into a temperature-dependent rate constant and a conversion function. Confidence intervals for the rate constant and conversion function are approximated using the delta method. Activation energy and its interval estimator are obtained by the Friedman method. Additionally, confidence interval for the pre-exponential factor is computed using the distribution of the difference between means of two populations. The methodology accommodates both isothermal and nonisothermal conditions and is versatile for reactions exhibiting single- or multi-peak rate profiles. Validation on two simulated complex reactions demonstrated excellent agreement between estimated and exact parameter values, with true values consistently falling within the calculated 95\% confidence intervals. Application to experimental thermal degradation data of poly(methyl methacrylate) and a blend of poly(methyl methacrylate) with cyclic olefin copolymer further confirmed practical utility. GNU Octave/MATLAB codes and sample datasets have been provided to enable readers to apply the proposed methodology to their own experimental data.

papers.title: Elucidating the Role of Mo Vacancies in a Two-Dimensional Molybdenum Carbide MXene on Fischer-Tropsch Catalysis
papers.abstract: Bulk molybdenum carbides catalyze the Fischer-Tropsch (FT) reaction but display low selectivity to liquid hydrocarbons. Understanding which structural features of Mo carbide-based catalysts correlate with a selectivity to C 5+ products requires detailed structure-performance studies. Here, we investigate the effect of Mo vacancies (V Mo ) on the FT performance of the two-dimensional (2D) i -MXene Mo 4/3 C T x , where T x are surface passivating groups. We show that the initially ordered V Mo sites, constituting ca. one-third of all Mo sites in Mo 4/3 C T x , undergo clustering already at 250 °C under H 2 . Following V Mo clustering, lattice carbon is released as CH 4 and CO, creating carbon vacancies (V C ), which also form in Mo 4/3 C T x under FT conditions at 330 °C. The presence of V C sites is associated with a high selectivity towards methane and C 2 -C 4 alkanes. Mo 4/3 C T x converts CO at a rate of ca. 60-80 mmol CO (g cat h) −1 , which is comparable to that of the T x -free 2D-Mo 2 C and 2D-Mo 2 C 1- x reference catalysts that only contain a Mo +2 (carbidic) electronic state. However, post-FT analysis of Mo 4/3 C T x shows that it contains Mo +2 , Mo +4 , and Mo +5 states, possibly because oxygen atoms populate the V C sites and do not block the Mo +2 active sites at the surface. Mo 4/3 C T x undergoes a phase transition to cubic a-MoC 1− x at 400 °C under H 2 , which leads to a continuous deactivation under FT conditions, suggesting, more generally, that pretreatment protocols for MXenes should be carefully optimized to unlock their potential in thermal catalysis.

papers.title: A dπ-pπ conjugated system integrating both Hückel rule-violating and rule-compliant aromatic frameworks
papers.abstract: Porphyrins have played a time-honored role in chemistry and they continue to attract attention because of their widespread applications. Expanding the range of wavelengths absorbed into the near-infrared (NIR) and increasing the absorption intensity is crucial to improve the photochemical properties of porphyrins. Conventional strategies require dedicated syntheses and are typically characterized by low yields. Additionally, the characteristic energy absorption bands of the resulting porphyrin derivatives exhibit low molar absorption coefficients ( ε ), especially in the NIR-Ⅱ region. Here we show that by introducing an aromatic metallapentalyne that violates Hückel’s rule into a porphyrin system provides a series of porphyrin derivatives exhibiting ultra-strong characteristic absorption bands in the NIR region ( ε > 10 5 M −1 cm −1 ). The approach relies on a reaction between porphyrin alkynyl groups and metal carbynes and enjoys the advantage of facile experimental operation, short synthetic procedures, and broad substrate scope. It also allows the lowest energy absorption band, ascribed to a d π - p π transition, to be tuned to a maximum of 1032 nm with a corresponding narrow optical bandgap of 1.13 eV. The present hybrid materials integrate both Hückel’s rule-violating and rule-compliant aromatic frameworks and display high thermal- and photo- stability, as well as good solubility. Under 1060 nm irradiation a lead system displays a photothermal conversion efficiency (PCE) value of 97%. To our knowledge this represents the highest reported PCE value for a NIR-absorbing dye. It and the other porphyrin metallaaromatic hybrids of this study were found to be promising photothermal therapy agents as inferred from in vivo studies involving tumor-bearing mouse models.

papers.title: Sub-microsecond Delayed Fluorescence Enabled by Molecular Engineering of Triazatruxene Emitters for High-Performance OLEDs with Suppressed Efficiency Rolloff
Configurational entropy suppresses crystallization in multicomponent molecular glasses
papers.abstract: The formation of stable amorphous solids is fundamentally limited by crystallization from the supercooled liquid. An ideal stabilization strategy would be broadly applicable, independent of specific intermolecular interactions, and effective at high molecular loadings. Here we demonstrate that increasing configurational entropy through multicomponent molecular mixing provides a general physical route to suppressing crystallization in molecular glasses. Using equimolar mixtures of small biocompatible molecules, we show that increasing component number markedly reduces liquid fragility without increasing the glass-transition temperature. Above a critical component count, crystallization is arrested, yielding stable amorphous phases upon cooling and reheating. Applying this principle to pharmaceutical systems, we show that drugs crystallizing readily in isolation can be stabilized in the amorphous state at high loadings within multicomponent matrices, forming high-entropy amorphous drugs (HEADs). These results establish configurational entropy as a design parameter for controlling crystallization in molecular glasses suggesting a general stabilization strategy for amorphous molecular solids. Teaser: High-entropy molecular mixtures prevent crystallization, stabilizing amorphous drugs.

papers.title: Photophysical and Structural Characterization of a Ruthenium Complex-Pyrene Coulombic Dyad Photocatalyst
papers.abstract: Coulombic dyads have recently emerged as a novel class of photocatalysts that exploit noncovalent ion-pair interactions to combine the favorable photophysical properties of metal complexes and organic chromophores in solution. A key mechanistic step in these systems is a Dexter-type energy transfer between the ionic components. This study thoroughly investigates the (photo)physical properties and geometry of the first reported Coulombic dyad, composed of dicationic tris(1,10-phenanthroline)ruthenium(II) (Ruphen) and 1,3,6,8-pyrenetetrasulfonate (PTS). This serves as a textbook-like system with mixed dynamic and static quenching behavior, which was investigated by various emission-based time-resolved and steady-state spectroscopic methods, highlighting their differences and the importance of accurate models to determine the association constant. Temperature-dependent measurements revealed a decrease in dynamic and static quenching efficiency at elevated temperatures and provided thermodynamic parameters characterizing ion-pair formation. The time constant for intra-ion-pair energy transfer from the triplet metal complex to the organic chromophore was determined to be ~87 ps using femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy. Structural insights were obtained from single-crystal X-ray crystallography and molecular dynamics simulations. The simulations revealed a high persistence of the ion-pair in the ground-state and a dynamic yet geometrically well-defined association. A structural similarity was found between solution and solid-state arrangements, indicating π-interactions besides Coulombic interactions between the ions. These interactions enable sufficient orbital overlap rationalizing the observed efficient Dexter energy transfer, which is as fast as in many covalently linked systems. These in-depth investigations provide a comprehensive picture of structure-property relationships in Coulombic dyads, offering valuable insights for their future design and applications.

papers.title: MSReportChecker: Real-Time HRMS Report Validation Directly Inside Your Word Processor
papers.abstract: MSReportChecker is a transformative Add-in for Microsoft Word that instantly delivers validation for high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) reports, addressing widespread errors recently identified in the chemical literature. Operating directly within the author's text processor, it verifies stoichiometry and exact masses with sub-ppm precision, highlights syntax deviations, and presents contextual correction advice without demanding technical aptitude from the user. This seamless integration into existing workflows ensures consistent and accurate HRMS data reports with minimal effort.

papers.title: Peptide Bond Formation via Anhydride Exchange Mediated in situ Generation of N-Methylimidazolium Cation
Gradient-Maintaining Water-Water Interfaces Generate Ordered Mineral Architectures with Nanofluidic Functions
papers.abstract: Understanding how ordered structures emerge in chemically complex environments remains a central challenge in chemistry. Although chemical gradients impose directionality in aqueous systems, it remains unclear whether such gradients can drive self-organization in compositionally diverse seawater. Here we show that gradientmaintaining water-water interfaces, designed to reproduce seawater-hydrothermal fluid interactions, convert chemical gradients into ordered mineral architectures through diffusiophoresis. Using a microfluidic platform, we demonstrate that sustained ionic gradients align brucite nanocrystals into vent-like structures with unidirectional, periodic, and radial patterns. These mineral architectures function as nanofluidic systems and enable osmotic energy conversion. Increasing the NaCl gradient further enhances structural alignment and diffusion potentials, directly linking chemical gradients to structural order and function. These results identify the gradient-driven electric fields established at water-water interfaces as essential for translating chemical gradients into structural order and function, redefining seawater not merely as a solvent but as a source of self-organization.

papers.title: Design of fluorinated polymer interphases for anodeless lithium metal batteries
papers.abstract: Increasing the energy density of batteries is critical for accelerating transportation electrification and expanding the use of renewable energy sources. Anodeless lithium metal batteries (ALLMBs), which eliminate the need for excess lithium inventory, are a promising route to higher energy density. However, their practical implementation is hindered by the reversibility of Li plating and stripping on copper current collectors, and both the attainable reversibility and dominant failure modes depend strongly on electrolyte chemistry. Here, we report a norbornene-derived polymer bearing pentafluorophenyl side chains as an interface layer for ALLMBs. In this design, the rigid polynorbornene backbone enables a mechanically robust, continuous coating, while the pentafluorophenyl groups are intended to act as a fluorine source, promoting LiF-rich passivation during initial Li deposition. Through spin coating, we investigated how controlled coating thickness impacts the cycling performance of ALLMBs in carbonate-and ether-based electrolytes. We identify an optimal thickness window that improves Coulombic efficiency and capacity retention in both ether and carbonate-based cells, whereas thinner coatings fail to provide durable protection and thicker coatings increase polarization. These results establish a thickness-governed balance between ion transport and interfacial passivation that is modulated by electrolyte chemistry, offering practical design guidelines for fluorinated polymer interphase layers for high-energy ALLMBs.

papers.title: Investigation of Allometric Scaling Exponents for mAb PK Prediction and Evaluation of Machine Learning as an Alternative Approach
An Interactive Web Application for Composing Nearest-Neighbor Suspect Spectral Libraries
papers.abstract: Untargeted metabolomics produces millions of tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) spectra, yet only a small fraction can be matched to reference spectra in community libraries. The nearest-neighbor suspect spectral library was introduced to narrow this gap by propagating annotations from known to unknown spectra based on spectral similarity and mass differences. This approach produces large collections of "suspect" spectra that are structurally related to known compounds and can guide hypothesis generation about unknown features in metabolomics data. We present a web application that operationalizes this concept and makes the suspect library workflow easier to run. It builds on a precomputed data cache derived from large-scale GNPS living data molecular networking. Users can interactively compose new suspect sets under different filters, optionally enrich them with additional spectrum annotations, and then visualize these suspect sets and export them as MGF files. By separating the heavy data preparation from lightweight, interactive composition and export, the web application makes the nearest-neighbor suspect library more accessible and reproducible for users who do not want to manage large-scale batch workflows themselves.

papers.title: Quantum-inspired Inverse Design of Heterogeneous Catalysts for Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
papers.abstract: Data-driven discovery of stable and functional materials remains a major challenge in chemistry and materials science, both from classical and quantum perspectives. Quantum machine learning provides new opportunities to optimize materials across vast chemical spaces, but hardware limitations restrict its practical application. Classical models can process large datasets, but limitations in their latent representations prevent exploration beyond the training distribution. To address these challenges, we introduce a quantum-inspired generative framework for discovering catalytic materials for hydrogen evolution reactions (HER). Inspired by variational quantum circuits (VQCs), which outperform classical models in certain tasks, we hypothesized that the norm-conserving property of VQCs plays a key role in materials representation and optimization. Thus, we incorporated the orthogonal transformations into the classical generative model to maintain latent space structure and enhance materials discovery. With additional data through transfer learning, the classical model with orthogonal transformations becomes useful. Our results provide practical guidelines for applying quantum machine learning to materials discovery and suggest the potential of quantum-inspired generative models to explore previously inaccessible chemical spaces.

papers.title: Chitosan-lignin cryogel beads for the adsorption of diclofenac in water
A linear-scaling integral-direct explicitly correlated second-order Møller-Plesset approach
papers.abstract: We present an integral-direct, iteration-free, linear-scaling, local explicitly correlated second-order Møller-Plesset (MP2-F12) approach, extending our previous local MP2 method [J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2016, 12, 4897]. The correlation contributions for individual electron pairs are computed within domains defined by the corresponding localized orbitals, while the correlation energies of spatially distant electron pairs are determined via multipole expansions. All the various types of integrals are computed and transformed directly, thereby precluding the need for integral storage and yielding asymptotically constant memory as well as negligible disk I/O demand. Another competitive advantage is the implementation of the 2B MP2-F12 ansatz, the 1 most complete one so far with local approximations, enabling excellent basis set convergence even with double-ζ basis sets. Our validation studies indicate that the approach recovers at least 99.9 % of the canonical MP2-F12 correlation energy and yields reaction energies with a mean error of lower than 1 kJ/mol. With respect to the complete basis set limit of MP2, the error of our local approach is just slightly larger than that of canonical MP2-F12. With the new local MP2-F12 approach, we were able to compute the correlation energy for a small protein containing 644 atoms, which is the largest system ever considered in an explicitly correlated calculation.

papers.title: Tailoring Electron Flow in the Redox Reactions of CoCu2O3 Nanocatalyst with Surface Hydroxyls for Humidity-Enhanced Molecular Sensing
papers.abstract: Oxidation chemistry requires understanding the electron flow within a redox cycle involving reactants, products, and reaction intermediates. In heterogeneous catalysis, the latter are tracked because they precede product formation. In chemoresistive gas sensors, however, adsorbates matter only if they are ionized and electronically coupled to the solid, in which case electrons are injected into (or withdrawn from) the semiconductor. Here we develop a framework for oxidation-driven sensing that separates ionized from dipolar surface populations, focusing on where the transferred electrons are allocated within the oxide. We apply this framework to elucidate the unusual promoter effect of humidity on metastable, nanocrystalline CoCu 2 O 3 chemoresistors. By combining operando work function analysis with in situ vibrational and X-ray spectroscopies, we follow electron redistribution during chemical sensing of different reducing molecules. Despite inhibiting lattice-oxygen chemistry, we find that water vapor improves the oxidative removal of carbonaceous dipoles and tailors electron injection and flow between Co and Cu sublattices, which amplifies conductivity changes and thus sensor performance. To date, humidity has been considered as detrimental to gas sensor performance, but our results outline strategies to turn it into a functional advantage, by tailoring intermediates speciation (ionized vs. dipolar) and electron allocation.

papers.title: Syntheses, Structures and Optoelectronic Properties of Copper(I) Tungstate/Molybdate Solid Solutions
papers.abstract: Solid solutions of semiconducting oxides have recently emerged as effective approaches for the modulation of optoelectronic properties and stabilities. Herein, a Cu(I)containing molybdate, Cu 6 Mo 5 O 18 , and its solid solution with tungsten, Cu 6-x Mo 5-y W y O 18 (y = 0.5, 1, 1.5, and 2.1), have been synthesized via both conventional solid-state reactions and a novel arc-melting approach. While preparation by solid-state reactions requires several days, their preparation by arc-melting takes only seconds. Both methods yield single crystals that were structurally characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Their structures were found to be comprised of distorted (Mo/W)O 6 octahedra that condense via edge-sharing to form zigzag chains along the c-axis. These chains are arranged in layers, capped by additional (Mo/W)O 6 octahedra, and bridged by charge balancing Cu(I) cations within distorted CuO 4 tetrahedra. Despite the similar cationic radii of Mo(VI) and W(VI), the W(VI) cation exhibits a site preference for coordination within the edge-shared chains (moderately C 2 /C 4 -distorted) versus the terminal capping position (strongly C 3 -distorted). Electronic structure calculations confirm an energetic preference for W(VI) cations within the edge-shared chains. Their black-colored powders show small bandgaps, slightly decreasing from 1.25(2) to 1.12(2) eV with increasing tungsten content. Additionally, calculations show optical absorption coefficients greater than 1×10 5 cm -1 at only 1 eV and steeply rising to 5×10 5 cm -1 at 2.4 eV. Their bandgaps were found to stem from conduction and valence band edges comprised of filled Cu 3 d -based and empty Mo 4 d -based states, respectively. The W 5 d -orbitals contribute at higher energies and have negligible impact on the band gap. Hence, these findings demonstrate a rapid and efficient arc-melt synthesis of Cu(I)-molybdates/tungstates and their promising optoelectronic properties as small bandgap semiconductors.

papers.title: Where do we go from here? Current state of drug-target binding kinetics and a roadmap to their establishment in drug discovery campaigns
papers.abstract: Due to the observation that kinetic rates can be better correlated with in vivo drug efficacy than simple affinities, significant efforts have been made to develop experimental and computational methods to predict drug-target residence times over the last years. Here, we summarize the discussions and reflections from an international CECAM workshop which took place in March 2025 with participants from both academia and industry, including experimentalists as well as computational scientists, and was dedicated to computational methods for protein-ligand binding kinetics prediction. As currently standing challenges, we identify the need for standardized benchmark data sets, the need to move from simple to more complex and biomedically relevant targets and the question how academia and industry can work together to move the field of drug-target binding kinetics forward. We also discuss what level of accuracy can be expected from computational methods, and highlight that the field would benefit from blind challenges to enable a fair comparison of different computational methods to predict kinetic rates.

papers.title: Extending the Periodic Transient Kinetics Method by Techniques resolving Surface Reaction Intermediates
papers.abstract: Transient experimentation is broadly applied in heterogeneous catalysis as insights into surface dynamics can be retrieved. However, the nature and activity of the involved surface intermediates remains uncertain impeding clear mechanistic conclusions. Thus, in this work, we extend transient experimentation with microkinetic modelling and spectroscopic techniques. Herein, CO2 methanation experiments were performed on a supported catalyst (Ru/TiO2) using the Periodic Transient Kinetics (PTK) method. Elemental balances based on the transient results showed decoupled hydrogenation pathways and storage behavior for surface carbon and oxygen species. The nature of these species was elucidated by Diffuse Reflectance Infrared Fourier Transform Spectroscopy (DRIFTS) studies providing evidence for support-bound species. Potential lumped mechanisms were formulated discriminating between species adsorbed on the support or active material. On basis of these mechanisms, microkinetic models were set up, fitted to the experimental data and compared by their deviation to the transient experimental data. By comparing the steady-state coverage of the simulated surface to the spectroscopic results, plausibility was checked and inactive species can be quantified. We show that DRIFTS, PTK and microkinetic modelling provide complementary data in a way that quantitative mechanistic information can be obtained. This synergy is only possible using dynamic experimentation.

papers.title: Prediction of hydrazone colorimetric response for Novichok sensing: a combined experimental and TD-DFT study
papers.abstract: Organophosphorus nerve agents, including Novichok agents, are highly toxic chemical warfare compounds regulated under the Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC). Detecting these agents is challenging due to their limited accessibility. This study presents a novel approach using Density Functional Theory (DFT) and Time-Dependent DFT (TD-DFT) to model and predict the colorimetric response of hydrazone-based chemosensors for Novichok detection. UV-visible spectroscopic data were collected for both neutral and anionic forms of hydrazone derivatives, revealing significant shifts in absorption maxima (λ max ) and molar absorption coefficients. A benchmark study comparing five hybrid functionals (B3LYP-D3, PBE0-D3, ωB97X-D, M06-2X, and CAM-B3LYP-D3) revealed that PBE0-D3 was most accurate for neutral species, while B3LYP-D3 performed best for anionic species. Theoretical UV-visible spectra and RGB triplets were generated to predict the visual color renderings. The predicted colors were compared with experimental observations, showing good agreement for neutral species and improved accuracy for anionic species after applying a spectral shift of +27 nm. This methodology enables the accurate prediction of colorimetric responses for hydrazone chemosensors, facilitating the design of new detection methods for Novichok agents without direct manipulation of these hazardous compounds. In conclusion, this study demonstrates the potential of DFT/TD-DFT modeling to enhance the development of colorimetric detection methods for chemical warfare agents, contributing to advancements in chemical safety and security.

papers.title: Fluorine-free Gas Diffusion Layers via Covalent Hydrocarbon Grafting
papers.abstract: Electrochemical energy systems critically rely on hydrophobic porous materials to sustain efficient multiphase liquid-gas transport and ensure stable operation. The prevailing materials paradigm based on dip-coated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), while effective, offers limited coating uniformity, suffers from constrained long-term durability, and faces increasing environmental and regulatory scrutiny. Here, we introduce a grafting-based strategy to form thin, covalently anchored, fluorine-free hydrophobic coatings on carbonaceous gas diffusion layers for polymer electrolyte fuel cells. Chemical and electrochemical grafting routes are employed to attach unbranched hydrocarbon chains, enabling systematic tuning of surface chemistry and hydrophobicity through precise control of chain length. Microscopy, spectroscopy, contact angle measurements, and electrochemical characterization reveal a progressive reduction in solid surface energy with increasing chain length, approaching the liquid repellency of PTFE. An 18-carbon grafted layer exhibits a surface energy of 22.3 mJ m-2 , comparable to that of PTFE (20.4 mJ m-2). Fuel cell testing further reveals a strong link between chain length, water management, and device performance: while shorter chains result in flooding under wet conditions, grafted layers comprising ≥14 carbon atoms outperform commercial PTFE-based benchmarks. Collectively, these results establish covalent hydrocarbon grafting as a viable pathway to engineer durable, fluorine-free gas diffusion layers with competitive hydrophobicity.

papers.abstract: Electrochemical energy systems critically rely on hydrophobic porous materials to sustain efficient multiphase liquid-gas transport and ensure stable operation. The prevailing materials paradigm based on dip-coated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), while effective, offers limited coating uniformity, suffers from constrained long-term durability, and faces increasing environmental and regulatory scrutiny. Here, we introduce a grafting-based strategy to form thin, covalently anchored, fluorine-free hydrophobic coatings on carbonaceous gas diffusion layers for polymer electrolyte fuel cells. papers.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Transport Properties in Amorphous Polymer Electrolytes Using Chemically Informed Structural Descriptors
papers.abstract: Amorphous polymer electrolytes are promising candidates for next-generation lithium batteries due to their improved safety and mechanical stability compared to conventional liquid electrolytes. However, predicting their transport performance remains challenging because ionic conductivity and diffusivity depend on complex, coupled interactions between polymer structure, chemistry, and ion dynamics. In this work, we apply machine learning to predict four key transport properties-ionic conductivity, TFSI diffusivity, Li-ion diffusivity, and polymer diffusivity-using a molecular dynamics dataset of 6,286 polymer electrolyte systems. To enhance predictive capability, chemically and structurally meaningful features were engineered from SMILES representations, including elemental composition, functional group densities, polarity descriptors, and polymer flexibility metrics. Three modeling frameworks, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Neural Networks were trained and evaluated, with Neural Networks achieving the highest overall performance. Feature importance analysis revealed that polymer backbone flexibility, polarity, and ionic environment dominate transport behavior. These results demonstrate that machine learning can effectively predict electrolyte performance while providing mechanistic insight, enabling accelerated screening and design of high-efficiency polymer electrolytes for future energy storage applications.

papers.title: Synthesis of New-Generation of 1,4-Dihydropyridine-Linked Covalent Organic Framework
papers.abstract: We report 1,4-dihydropyridine covalent organic framework (DHP-COF) constructed through 1,4-dihydropyridine linkage via the Hantzsch pyridine synthesis. The synthesis is carried out under mild conditions and produces high yield of porous material. The 1,4-dihydropyridinelinked COF-3 (DHP-COF-3) has a high crystalline hexagonal structure with an ABC stacking pattern in three layers. The 1,4-dihydropyridine linkage introduces both hydrogen-bond acceptor sites and hydrophobic domains within the framework, which provide areas for electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions with per-and poly-fluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). DHP-COF-3 removed PFOS and PFOA from drinking water near quantitatively with a starting concentration of 2.4 μg L-¹, and it can be reused over several absorption cycles efficiently.

papers.title: Virtual Screening Identifies Inhibitors and First-in-Class Activators of 17β-Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase Type 10
Do We Really Need All That Data: From Data to Agency in Automated Microscopy
