When Do Band Gap Calculations Meet with Experiments in Cu14 and Au20 Atomically Precise Nanoclusters? A Detailed and Systematic (TD)-DFT Comparison of HOMO-LUMO, Fundamental, Optical, and Electrochemical Energy Gaps
papers.abstract: In view of the tremendous progress in atomically precise metal nanoclusters where electrochemical and optical energetics are routinely supported by computations to establish structure-function correlations, we explore the relationship between different protocols for measuring and computing band gaps of two distinct organic ligand-protected nanoclusters: [Cu 14 H 10 (MBN) 3 (PPh 3 ) 8 ] + and Au 20 (TBBT) 16 . Through UV/visible spectroscopy and Differential Pulse Voltammetry, we measure optical and electrochemical band gaps in those systems. We then compare these experimentally determined gaps to HOMO-LUMO gaps, fundamental gaps, vertical excitation energies, and E o ox - E o red potentials computed using different density functional theory (DFT) or time-dependent DFT (TD-DFT) methods. Specifically, in both copper and gold nanoclusters, we test the effect of truncating inert ligands from the model and compare density functionals with varying degrees of Hartree-Fock (HF) exchange from 0% to 50%, range-separated hybrids with a varying long-range tuning parameter, different correlation functionals, basis sets, and (equilibrium and non-equilibrium) continuum solvation models. Despite having different frontier orbital characters (the copper nanocluster has a metal-to-ligand charge transfer character while the gold nanocluster has metal-centered frontier orbitals), both nanoclusters display a similar sensitivity of the HOMO-LUMO gap to the HF exchange that is partially mitigated when computing the fundamental, optical, and electrochemical gaps. Other factors, such as the nature of the correlation functional, basis set, and geometry relaxation, have a considerably smaller effect on computed band gaps in these systems. Overall, this work provides guidelines for factors of varied importance for correlating computed and experimental band gap values.

papers.title: CrystalNets: a web app for topology determination of crystalline structures
papers.abstract: Because topology plays a key role in many chemical and physical properties of materials, identification of topology from crystalline structures is a common and important task in materials science. We present here a new web application, CrystalNets, whose user-friendly interface allows scientists to identify and visualize the topology of crystals from their atomic structure in CIF format. The software has a lot of options to customize its features, such as detection of bonding, choice of clustering model, type of materials (inorganic, hybrid, etc). It has a default mode with powerful heuristics, and allows the user to easily visualize and check the topology detected against the full structure. We also improved the underlying CrystalNets.jl Julia library, including a systematic algorithm to handle the complex case of unstable nets.

papers.title: Probabilities of phases. An algebraic approach in determining the exact phases III
papers.abstract: In this paper we give the exact linear equations to solve the phase problem for a point atom structure. The equations are written for P 1, but they are very easily extended to other spacegroups.

papers.title: Metal-Organic Framework Modified Microelectrodes for Electrochemical PFAS Monitoring in River Waters
papers.abstract: Per-and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent, bioaccumulative environmental contaminants that pose significant risks to human health and water quality. Among them, perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) are highly regulated due to their toxicity and widespread occurrence at trace levels in drinking water. The need for rapid, sensitive, and field-deployable detection technologies has motivated the development of alternative sensing strategies beyond conventional laboratory-based methods. A porous metalorganic framework (MOF) incorporating gold nanoparticles is integrated onto microfabricated electrodes, enabling dual-mode detection via electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and voltammetry. It offers high surface area, tunable pore structures, and chemically adaptable metal nodes, enabling selective interactions with PFOA through electrostatic and hydrophobic mechanisms. Structural and electrochemical characterization confirmed the integrity and uniformity of the Au-Cr-MIL-101 nanocomposite and elucidated its molecular interaction with per-and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). The modified electrodes exhibit strong affinity toward long-chain PFAS, producing concentration-dependent changes in charge-transfer resistance and current response. Validation in river water samples confirms robust performance in complex matrices. This work highlights the potential of MOF-based electrochemical sensors as portable tools for rapid PFAS screening and real-time water quality monitoring.

papers.title: Cobalt polyoxometalate-LDH hybrids: pH-switchable molecular catalysts to confined cobalt oxide oxygen evolution layers
papers.abstract: Intercalating Co-POMs into the LDH lamellar space effectively boosts their OER activity at neutral pH. In alkaline media, Co-POMs decompose into tunable layered cobalt oxide species within the LDH gallery, controlled by Co-POM nuclearity. The latter is a novel method for preparing layered oxides using the LDH galleries as nanoreactors.

papers.title: Magnetic water cleaning of estrogens via tight yet dynamic binding to nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Micropollution is an ever-increasing concern to human health and wildlife caused by population growth, industrialization, and intensive agriculture. An example of such emerging micropollutants are natural and synthetic estrogen hormones. They are found everywhere in the aquatic environment at very low but dangerous concentrations. In this article, we demonstrate efficient water cleaning of such low-concentrated estrogens by adsorbing them onto superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs) and removal by simply applying a magnet. We facilitate the adsorption by tuning the SPION surface with a binary self-assembled monolayer (SAM) composed of two phosphonic acid derivatives: one serving as hydrophobic interaction site and the other improving water dispersibility of the system. We conclude the demonstration of our nanomaterials by unveiling the dynamic estrogen-SAM interaction via synergistic combination of state-of-the-art scattering, spectroscopy, and simulation. Thereby, we identify different adsorption motifs at molecular space and time scale. We believe that beyond our materials, these insights on the pollutant-adsorbent interface may accelerate the design of next-generation nano-adsorbents for water remediation.

papers.title: Exploring Acylcarnitine Metabolism Using Reverse Metabolomics
papers.abstract: Untargeted mass spectrometry (MS) is a valuable tool for studying human metabolism and identifying small molecule disease biomarkers. However, annotation of chemical structures and validation of findings across numerous cohorts remains challenging. Reverse metabolomics employs a structure-driven approach to overcome these issues by searching spectra of known structures against an entire repository of untargeted LC-MS/MS data to see where metabolites of interest are found. This work uses reverse metabolomics to study acylcarnitine (AC) metabolism in humans and other animals. Here, a library of 76 ACs was chemically synthesized then searched against public metabolomics data to explore where metabolites of interest are detected. From this analysis, it was determined that acylcarnitines are most frequently observed in human and mouse samples, with about 90% of all searched AC structures present in both blood and fecal samples from these species. This work identified positive associations between certain AC structures and disease, indicating their capacity as health biomarkers. Machine learning was applied, determining that AC presence and absence data can accurately predict healthy versus unhealthy individuals with good precision and recall, albeit the models lack disease specificity. Overall, our findings suggest that AC profiles can serve as valuable biomarkers for disease detection throughout the entire lifespan and should be examined for their potential beyond current clinical screening protocols.

papers.title: Insights into the Redox Landscape of Polyoxovanadate-Alkoxide Species
papers.abstract: Polyoxovanadate-alkoxides are a class of polynuclear earth-abundant transition metal compounds with highly tunable catalytic, redox, and magnetic properties. These species are ideal electroactive molecular agents for environmentally friendly energy storage applications, such as non-aqueous redox flow batteries. As such, it is fundamental to understand structure-redox relationships in the multielectron redox profiles of polyoxovanadate-alkoxides species. Here, we studied the redox properties of monomeric vanadate-alkoxide species that control the formation of two distinct chemical spaces with mix-valent clusters and fully reduced cyclic species. The accuracy of various density functional theory approximations and basis sets choices was benchmarked against domain-based local pair natural orbital coupled cluster, specifically DLPNO-CCSD(T). To further confirm the broader applicability of density functional theory in higher nuclearity species, we studied the redox profile of [(V V 6-n V IV n O 6 )(O)(OCH 3 ) 12 ] 4-n , [(Nb=O)(V V 5-n V IV n O 5 )(O)(OCH 3 ) 12 ] 4-n , [(M-OCH 3 )(V V 5-n V IV n O 5 )(O)(OCH 3 ) 12 ] 4-n (M = Ti, Zr, or Hf), and [(Fe-Cl)(V V 5-n V IV n O 5 )(O)(OCH 3 ) 12 ] 3-n hexanuclear polyoxo vanadate-alkoxiode species. The calculated redox profiles of these species were in good agreement with experimental data with an average absolute error of 0.11 V. The coupling between vanadium centers in the reduced species was determined to be weak via second-order multireference complete active space calculations (CASSCF/CASPT2).

papers.title: Reversing the 3d6 Relaxation Paradigm: Ultrafast Quintet Decay and Triplet Trapping in the Strong-Field [Co(terpy)2]3+ Complex
papers.abstract: The deactivation mechanism of photoexcited [Co(terpy) 2 ] 3+ (terpy = 2,2':6',2"-terpyridine) in acetonitrile is explored using transient absorption spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations. Based on the time-resolved experimental data and its theoretical assignment, we observe a quintet metal-centred ( 5 MC) transient that decays with a time constant of 170 fs via 5 MC → 3 MC intersystem crossing (ISC). We report vibrational cooling within the 3 MC state (characterized by a time constant of 5.7 ps) and a 3.4 ns 3 MC excited-state lifetime. While both Fe(II) and Co(III) polypyridine complexes exhibit excited-state lifetimes on the order of a few nanoseconds, the governing excited-state dynamics are different. For Fe(II), the ns-lived excited state is the 5 MC, and thus the lifetime is controlled by the weak second-order singlet-quintet coupling. On the other hand, for 3 MC character for Co(III) means significantly stronger singlet-triplet coupling and the excited-state lifetime is controlled by unfavorable energetics governing triplet-singlet ISC (from 3 MC to the singlet ground state).

papers.title: Chain Length Dependent Structural Organization of Imidazolium Ionic Liquids for Potassium-Ion Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Understanding how molecular architecture influences the local structure and dynamics in ionic liquid electrolytes is critical for advancing potassium-ion battery technologies. We employed all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to investigate a series of TFSI⁻-based imidazolium ionic liquids with systematically varied alkyl chain lengths, enabling direct assessment of their impact on electrolyte structure and K⁺ dynamics. Radial distribution functions reveal strengthened K⁺-TFSI⁻ correlations and progressive reorganization of cation-cation interactions with increasing nonpolar character. Static structure factor analysis shows enhanced intermediate-range ordering, consistent with the emergence of nanoscale polar-nonpolar segregation. Dynamical analyses, including velocity autocorrelation functions and probe-accessible free-volume distributions, demonstrate that longer alkyl chains induce stronger and longer-lived caging environments, leading to slower structural relaxation and reduced K⁺ mobility. These findings establish a direct link between cation alkyl chain length, mesoscale organization, and ion transport behaviour, providing molecularlevel design insights for developing stable and high-performance ionic liquid electrolytes for potassium-ion batteries.

papers.title: Unravelling the Structure and Adsorption Properties of a Highly Stable Porous Hafnium Phosphonate Framework
papers.abstract: The highly stable hafnium-phosphonate framework based on 2,4,6-tris(4-phosphonophenyl)-1,3,5triazine as the linker (Hf-ttbp) displays exceptional separation performance towards uranium and transuranium elements in acidic environment. Here, we report the crystal structure of Hf-ttbp, solved from powder X-ray diffraction data, revealing that it is not isostructural to the previously reported Zr-btbp, as originally hypothesised. Hf-ttbp features honeycomb-like layers with cavities having diameter of about 10 Å filled with water molecules. The same structural arrangement is displayed by the newly synthesised Zr-ttbp. Different from Zr-btbp, where the inorganic unit is a trinuclear Zr-phosphonate cluster, Hf-ttbp contains isolated Hf atoms. The removal of water from the pores of Hf-ttbp does not induce any structural rearrangement, generating accessible porosity. Multinuclear solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy was employed to shed light on the local structure upon removal of water from the pores, finding evidence of symmetry breaking in the Hf environment, not detectable by X-ray diffraction, following reallocation of acidic protons. The adsorption properties of Hf-ttbp towards Ar, CO 2 , N 2 and H 2 O were also assessed, finding that it displays CO 2 adsorption capacity comparable to other porous metal phosphonates and high affinity for H 2 O, attributed to the highly polar nature of the pores. Highlights-The crystal structure of a porous Hf-phosphonate is determined from powder X-ray diffraction data-The structure is compared with that of a previously reported Zr-phosphonate based on a similar tritopic linker-Insight into fine structural details is gained with multinuclear solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy-The gas and vapour sorption properties are assessed

papers.title: Bending Rigidity of Prebiotically Relevant Fatty Acid Membranes from Atomistic Simulations
Geometric Convergence and Aromatic Anchoring Define Ligand Binding in the Serotonin 5-HT1A Receptor: Insights from Docking and Natural Product Motifs
papers.abstract: Understanding how ligands achieve stable binding within receptor cavities is essential for structure-based drug design. While specific anchor interactions such as hydrogen bonding and π–π stacking are often considered primary determinants of binding stability, the role of geometric constraints within the binding pocket remains less clearly defined. In this study, a docking-based structural analysis of aripiprazole, brexpiprazole, and herdmanine within the receptor cavity was conducted to investigate the relationship between anchor interactions and spatial convergence. This study proposes the concept of a geometry-driven convergence region as a structural determinant of ligand binding. These results suggest that spatial compatibility within receptor cavities may play a more fundamental role than individual anchor interactions, providing an additional perspective for in silico drug discovery and rational ligand design.

papers.title: Elucidating Hydroxide Transport in Anion Exchange Polymer Membranes Via Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Efficient ion transport is fundamental to the performance of electrochemical energy devices such as fuel cells and electrolysers. Understanding the ion transport mechanisms within anion exchange membranes (AEMs) provides valuable insights for membrane design. Computational methods, particularly first-principles approaches, have been extensively employed to study ion transport mechanisms due to their ability to describe proton-transfer events. However, applying first-principles methods to large polymer systems is very computationally demanding. To overcome this limitation, we developed a machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) model tailored to investigate hydroxide diffusion in hydrated AEM polymer systems. Using this MLIP model, we characterised both the local environments and the overall morphology of the hydrated polymer systems. Furthermore, we elucidated the hydroxide transport mechanism by quantifying solvation patterns and proton-transfer dynamics. Our results demonstrate that the MLIP model effectively captures reactive proton-transfer events and accurately differentiates transport dynamics under varying hydration conditions. Additionally, the MLIP model is capable of efficiently simulating large-scale polymer systems containing thousands of atoms with computational resources that remain practical, while still achieving quantum-mechanical level accuracy.

papers.title: Exploring Cobalt Accessibility Limits in a Two-dimensional Porphyrin-based Covalent Organic Framework for the Oxygen Evolution Reaction
papers.abstract: There is a growing need for new technologies in the energy and chemicals sectors to improve global sustainability. Meeting this need requires the development of efficient and robust catalysts and a detailed understanding of the nature, accessibility and stability of their active sites under operando conditions. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are crystalline, porous materials that offer high surface areas and molecular-level design, making them attractive platforms for heterogeneous catalysis. However, while COFs are highly porous systems, the accessibility of active sites in layered COFs remains insufficiently explored. Here, we investigate the activity, stability, and accessibility of metal active sites in the prototypical two-dimensional cobalt porphyrin-based COF (COF-366-Co) for the electrocatalytic oxygen evolution reaction (OER). COF-366-Co exhibits an overpotential of 492 ± 13 mV at 10 mA cm -2 and demonstrates notable cobalt coordination stability in alkaline electrolyte (0.1 M KOH). By selectively blocking surface-accessible cobalt sites using ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid tetrasodium salt (EDTA), corroborated by quantum chemical calculations, we reveal that cobalt centers in the bulk of the COF - despite its large surface area - are largely inaccessible for OER catalysis. Altogether, this work highlights active-site accessibility as a critical design parameter for 2D COF-based catalysts and aims to motivate the development of new strategies to achieve optimal utilization of catalytic sites.

papers.title: Sub-stoichiometric peptide synthesis
papers.abstract: Solid-phase peptide chemistry is more than sixty years old. Its advent revolutionized peptide science. Innovation has increased safety and expanded the range of chemistries available to the practitioner, but the fundamental basis of the technology, the ability to easily wash away the required excess of amino acids needed to obtain quantitative conversion to avoid deletion sequences that complicate purification remains unchanged. It also masks a limitation: we must use super-stoichiometric amounts of amino acids, designing-in waste as part of our process. When using natural amino acids, readily and inexpensively available on large scale with Fmoc and appropriate orthogonal side chain protection, this is not a significant issue. When using a custom-made residue, "wasting" 60-90% of your valuable material becomes a scientific tragedy. This is no longer inevitable; we report that variable bed flow reactors allow for the high-purity synthesis of peptides, exemplified in up to 30mers, using less than one equivalent of amino acid per active amine group on the resin bed. By avoiding wasting amino acid building blocks, this technology likely represents the most significant effort to date in both reducing the environmental footprint and reducing the economic cost of peptide synthesis since Merrifield's innovation in 1963.

papers.title: Novel successive multi-ionic layers for ultra-efficient, diffusion-limited separationof intact proteins by capillary electrophoresis and capillary electrophoresis-mass spectrometry
papers.abstract: Over the last few decades, biopharmaceutical products have seen remarkable growth and have started to outrun top-selling small molecules, attesting to their usefulness for the treatment of many diseases. Moreover, proteins and proteoforms are increasingly used for diagnostic purposes. Such complex protein mixtures require proper characterization tools such as capillary electrophoresis (CE), a highly efficient and versatile technique for the separation of intact proteins. The use of successive multiple ionic-polymer layers (SMILs) as capillary coatings further improves CE performance by limiting interactions between analytes and the capillary wall as well as enabling control of the electroosmotic flow (EOF). In this project, SMIL coatings were initially characterized for the separation of model proteins by CE. Experimental conditions were optimized, reaching separation efficiencies of up to 1 million plates/m. The factors governing separation efficiency were thoroughly studied by plotting plate heights as a function of migration velocity, enabling a quantitative comparison of different coatings and experimental conditions. A previous model describing protein adsorption as a mechanism based on retention was refined, showing that some proteins may be adsorbed onto the capillary surface with slow kinetics of desorption. The main source of peak broadening in optimal conditions was identified to be electroosmotic inhomogeneity caused by coating defects. In order to improve the resolution, the EOF needs to be controlled as well. Here, the frequently used and efficient cationic SMIL coating agent poly(α-L-lysine) (α-PLL) was modified by converting stepwise the ε-amino functions of this polycation into carboxamides. To keep simultaneously the analyte-surface interactions as small as possible, zwitterionic functionality based structurally on a sulfobetaine motif was developed allowing to adjust the degree of functionalization between 8 and 99 %. The obtained set of mixed polycationic/polyzwitterionic polymers were investigated as outermost layers of SMIL coatings, clearly showing that the EOF decreases with a higher degree of functionalization while keeping the high efficiency. The separation of charge variants of monoclonal antibodies was developed based on a new SMIL coating resulting in a relatively low EOF. Moreover, we applied our new highly efficient sulfobetaine-modified α-PLL coating for mass spectrometry-based top-down protein analysis in biological samples with clearly improved resolution for slow migrating proteins. This leads to the identification of 2.5 times more proteoforms by MS/MS experiments in the lower mobility range of a yeast proteome. Thus, the sulfobetaine-modified α-PLL coatings developed here exhibit a toolbox for highly-resolved separation of proteins and proteoforms in targeted or untargeted top-down protein analysis.

papers.title: Shelf-stable Bis-(Perfluoroaryl)nickel(II) Complexes for Organometallic Synthesis and Catalysis
papers.abstract: We describe two bis(perfluoroaryl)nickel(II) complexes, Ni(C6F5)2(NCPh)2 and [NBu4]2[{Ni(C6F5)2(μ-OH)2}2], as bench-stable, broadly soluble, and readily coordinating Ni(II) sources for applications in organometallic synthesis and catalysis. Their catalytic competence is demonstrated across representative transformations including Suzuki-Miyaura coupling, Buchwald-Hartwig amination, Miyaura borylation, and recently developed alkene difunctionalization reactions, with performance comparable to or exceeding that of conventional Ni sources. The presumed activation pathway via reductive elimination of decafluorobiphenyl offers a benign route, minimizing off-cycle species formation.

papers.title: Prism[5]MaxQ: Synthesis and Molecular Recognition Properties
papers.abstract: We report the synthesis of sulfated prism[5]arene (Pr[5]AS) from Pr[5]A by reaction with pyridine•SO 3 . Uncomplexed Pr[5]AS undergoes aggregation in water at NMR concentrations but addition of acetone as guest results in a diagnostic 1 H NMR spectrum indicative of a D 5 -symmetric Pr[5]AS•acetone complex. Fluorescence spectroscopy titrations performed at very low concentrations ([thionin] = 1.5 µM) and at different temperatures allowed a determination of the binding constant for Pr[5]AS•thionin (K a = (2.99 ± 0.36) × 10 7 ); the van't Hoff analysis yielded DH = (-2.60 ± 0.11) kcal mol -1 . Subsequent competitive isothermal titration calorimetry experiments allowed the determination of the thermodynamic parameters for 16 Pr[5]AS•guest complexes with binding constants exceeding 10 12 M -1 in PBS for Pr[5]AS•Me 4 Bipip. Pr[5]AS binds to quaternary diammonium ion guests (e.g. Me 6 C 6 DA) preferentially over the corresponding primary ammonium form (e.g. C6DA) by factors up to 5136fold. Sulfated Pr[5]AS binds more tightly than WPr[5] toward a common guest by factors from 5-to 4300-fold but is a less potent host than P[6]AS by factors up to 88000-fold.

papers.title: Prism[5]MaxQ: Synthesis and Molecular Recognition Properties
papers.abstract: We report the synthesis of sulfated prism[5]arene (Pr[5]AS) from Pr[5]A by reaction with pyridine•SO3. Uncomplexed Pr[5]AS undergoes aggregation in water at NMR concentrations but addition of acetone as guest results in a diagnostic 1 H NMR spectrum indicative of a D5-symmetric Pr[5]AS•acetone complex. Fluorescence spectroscopy titrations performed at very low concentrations ([thionin] = 1.5 µM) and at different temperatures allowed a determination of the binding constant for Pr[5]AS•thionin (Ka = (2.99 ± 0.36) × 10 7); the van't Hoff analysis yielded DH = (-2.60 ± 0.11) kcal mol-1. Subsequent competitive isothermal titration calorimetry experiments allowed the determination of the thermodynamic parameters for 16 Pr[5]AS•guest complexes with binding constants exceeding 10 12 M-1 in PBS for Pr[5]AS•Me4Bipip. Pr[5]AS binds to quaternary diammonium ion guests (e.g. Me6C6DA) preferentially over the corresponding primary ammonium form (e.g. C6DA) by factors up to 5136fold. Sulfated Pr[5]AS binds more tightly than WPr[5] toward a common guest by factors from 5-to 4300-fold but is a less potent host than P[6]AS by factors up to 88000-fold.

papers.title: A Modular Strategy for the Gram-Scale Synthesis of Tetraarylammonium Salts
papers.abstract: Tetraarylammonium salts are a structurally unique yet synthetically challenging subclass of quaternary ammonium salts. Classical Menshutkin reactions are generally ineffective for their syntheses due to the diminished nucleophilicity of triarylamines and the low reactivity of aryl halides toward SN2 processes. Herein, we report a modular and scalable strategy for the synthesis of tetraarylammonium salts. Starting from readily accessible diarylamines, the target structures are obtained through a concise five-step sequence comprising Buchwald-Hartwig amination, halogen-lithium exchange/silylation, rhodium-catalyzed arylation, intramolecular cyclization, and protodesilylation. The optimized protocol enabled gram-scale isolation of tetraphenylammonium salt (1.2 g isolated). This work provides a practical platform for the scalable and flexible synthesis of tetraarylammonium salts, facilitating future studies of their properties and applications.

papers.title: Synthesis and Characterization of Uranyl Metal-Organic Frameworks Containing Selenophene and Tellurophene Linkers
papers.abstract: Herein we describe the synthesis and characterization of uranyl metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) featuring 2,5-selenophene dicarboxylic acid (2,5-SeDC) and 2,5-tellurophene dicarboxylic acid (2,5-TeDC) linkers. All compounds were analyzed structurally using single-crystal and powder X-ray diffraction and spectroscopically characterized via Raman and infrared spectroscopies, thermogravimetric analysis, and scanning electron microscopy. Thermal analysis revealed that uranyl-2,5-SeDC and 2,5-TeDC based MOFs were stable to between 250-350 °C. These measurements also led to the discovery of an unprecedented ligand-induced redox transformation to uraninite (UO2) under inert atmosphere (N2), wherein heating of U(VI) hybrid materials featuring 2,5-SeDC and 2,5-TeDC did not lead to U(VI) oxides after framework degradation, rather U(IV) was formed at ambient pressure in the absence of chemical reductants. This redox transformation does not occur when hybrid materials are prepared with 2,5thiophenedicarboxylic acid (2,5-TDC) or 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (2,5-FDC); however, physical mixing of 2,5-TeDC with uranyl-2,5-TDC or uranyl-2,5-FDC compounds in a 1:1 stoichiometric ratio does lead to the formation of UO2. Pre-and post-TGA SEM/EDS analyses revealed that tellurium content decreases to near-background levels after heating under N2, whereas selenium content is reduced but remains still detectable. PXRD analysis of the post-TGA residues further showed no evidence for crystalline seleniumor tellurium-containing phases, consistent with decomposition pathways involving volatile chalcogencontaining intermediates that facilitate spontaneous in situ U(VI) to U(IV) reduction under mild conditions.

papers.title: σ-Aromatic Stabilization of a Be₄ Core by NH Ligands: DFT Study
papers.abstract: Beryllium-based clusters exhibit diverse bonding motifs, ranging from weak van der Waals interactions in small aggregates to metallic-like delocalization in larger species. This paper presents a detailed investigation of the structural, thermodynamic, and electronic properties of the Be₄N₂H₂ cluster using density functional theory (DFT) at the TPSS/def2-TZVP and M06-2X/def2-TZVP levels of theory, augmented by high-level domain-based local pair natural orbital coupled-cluster (DLPNO-CCSD(T)) local energy decomposition (LED) analysis. Geometry optimization identifies a stable isomer featuring a compact Be₄ core coordinated by two NH units. Energy decomposition analysis combined with natural orbitals for chemical valence (EDA-NOCV) reveals a remarkably strong orbital interaction energy (ΔEorb = −370.62 kcal/mol), dominated by σ-type donation. High-level LED calculations quantify the dispersion contribution at approximately −5.7 kcal/mol. Kinetic stability is supported by a substantial HOMO-LUMO gap and the absence of imaginary vibrational frequencies. The bonding was further elucidated using Natural Bond Orbital (NBO) analysis, Adaptive Natural Density Partitioning (AdNDP), and topological methods including Interaction Region Indicator (IRI), Density Overlap Regions Indicator (DORI), Localized Orbital Locator (LOL), and delocalization indices (SEDI/DI), confirming σaromaticity and multicentre bonding in the Be₄ core.

papers.title: Differential Coats-Redfern Analysis for Thermolysis of Carbon-Relevant Polymers
papers.abstract: Thermolysis of plastic waste is increasingly explored both as an end-of-life route and as a precursor step for producing carbonaceous materials, but most thermogravimetric (TG) data for polymers are collected under single heating rates with limited data resolution and are not optimized for kinetic analysis. In this study, we use the recently developed differential Coats-Redfern (d-CR) framework to extract conversion-resolved kinetic information from opensource TG curves of eight technologically important polymers (PP, PS, PET, PMMA, PC, PA, PUR, PTFE) recorded at 10 °C•min⁻¹. Classical Coats-Redfern (CR) analysis of these singlerate datasets yields curved ln[g(α)/T²] versus 1/T plots and conversion-averaged activatio n parameters that can misrepresent the underlying degradation behavior. In contrast, d-CR converts the same thermogravimetry into conversion-resolved Eₐ(α) and ln A(α), while rateparity and conversion-variant compensation tests for an effective mechanistic model selection. The resulting profiles reveal systematic differences in thermolysis energy demand between commodity and engineering polymers and provide a kinetic baseline for assessing whether catalytic routes genuinely reduce process severity in plastic recycling schemes from future works.

papers.title: Adsorption Layer of Potassium Dodecanoate and Diglycerol Derivative Mixtures at the Air/Water Interface Studied by Neutron Reflectivity and Small-angle Neutron Scattering
papers.abstract: The behavior of the air/water interface in a one-component surfactant system has been studied by performing surface tension measurements and analysis based on Gibbs adsorption isotherms. However, this method is inefficient for evaluating surface compositions of mixed solutions, which is important for optimizing the compositions of industrial products according to their practical applications. In this study, the diglycerol derivative 2GlyPO 9 with polyoxypropylene chains developed for industrial applications was investigated to understand how its mixing with potassium dodecanoate (C 11 COOK) improved the foam stability. The adsorption properties at the air/water interface were examined by conducting surface tension and neutron reflectivity measurements, and the aggregation structure was studied via small-angle neutron scattering. With increasing C 11 COOK concentration, the surface tension decreased through the following processes: (1) 2GlyPO 9 was replaced with C 11 COOK at the interface, (2) 2GlyPO 9 -based aggregates were formed in solution, and (3) mixed micelles were formed with C 11 COOK. This process changed slightly depending on the utilized solution. At excessive 2GlyPO 9 concentrations, process (1) was less likely to occur than at lower concentrations because 2GlyPO 9 formed aggregates even in the absence of C 11 COOK. When another diglycerol derivative, 2GlyEO 9 , in which the hydrophobic polyoxypropylene chains of 2GlyPO 9 were replaced with hydrophilic polyoxyethylene chains, was mixed with C 11 COOK, process (2) was skipped because no aggregates of 2GlyEO 9 were formed. Compared with the C 11 COOK solutions without diglycerol derivatives, the addition of 2GlyPO 9 lowered the surface tension above the critical micelle concentration, whereas 2GlyEO 9 did not produce this effect, although the surface excess concentration of C 11 COOK decreased in both cases. This detailed structural analysis conducted at the interface and in solution using neutrons provided useful insights into the mechanism of adsorption at the air/water interface, especially in mixed solutions.

papers.title: Enantioselective B-H insertion of branched α-alkyl carbenes
papers.abstract: The intermolecular carbene transfer reaction of branched α-alkyl Fischer carbenes remains inaccessible due to their high susceptibility to rearrangement side reactions. This study overcomes these limitations by achieving copper-catalyzed, highly enantioselective insertion reactions of branched α-alkyl carbenes into B-H bonds. A variety of important chiral pharmaceuticals starting from readily available ketones has been effectively achieved based on this reaction platform. The precise modulation of carbene electronic properties and transfer reaction kinetics makes sterically demanding and unstable branched α-alkyl carbenes unprecedently undergoing intermolecular transfer reactions with high efficiency and selectivity. The unlock of transformations of structurally diverse branched α-alkyl carbenes undoubtedly significantly advances carbene chemistry from both experimental as well as theoretical aspects.

papers.title: Beryllium-Trapped Electride Electrons: A Stable Non-Nuclear Bridge in Triazole Dimers
papers.abstract: We report a comprehensive computational investigation into a novel organometallic dimer featuring a beryllium-bridged phenyl-triazole framework. High-level DLPNO-CCSD(T) calculations reveal an exceptionally high binding energy of-1151.5 kcal/mol. Topological analyses via QTAIM, ELF, and LOL reveal the presence of two non-nuclear attractors (NNAs) trapping approximately 1.94 electrons between the cationic beryllium centres. This finding characterizes the complex as a rare stable molecular electride, where interstitial electron density serves as the primary "glue" for dimerization. The system exhibits massive static polarizability components reaching 858.6 a.u., identifying it as a potent candidate for non-linear optical (NLO) applications.

papers.title: Resolving Charge and Glycosylation Variants of Cetuximab Combining Ion-Exchange and Hydrophilic Interaction Chromatography -HRMS
authors: Annika A M Van Der Zon
papers.abstract: Biopharmaceuticals, such as monoclonal antibodies (mAb), are complex molecules that require thorough analysis due to post-translational modifications, including charge variants and glycoform patterns. When analyzing intact mAbs, single liquid chromatography (LC) mass spectrometry (MS) methods often lack the resolution to distinguish this heterogeneity because they offer limited separation in both chromatographic and mass dimensions. Consequently, these methods struggle to detect low-abundance species, highlighting the importance of 2DLC-MS workflows. Here, we demonstrate the potential of the offline IEC–HILIC–MS method to effectively separate charge and glycoform variants of complex mAbs. Cetuximab served as the model antibody due to its multiple charge variants (arising from sialylation and C-terminal lysine clipping) and four glycosylation sites (in both Fab and Fc regions). Charge variants were first separated using non-volatile IEC and collected as individual fractions. These fractions were then analyzed using a low-flow HILIC-MS setup to increase sensitivity for low-abundance species. A RPLC trap placed before the HILIC column enabled efficient desalting. The IEC-HILIC results showed that both Fc- and Fab-associated glycoforms of cetuximab were resolved to a level not achievable with HILIC-MS alone, allowing deeper insights into charge heterogeneity and glycosylation. In addition to resolving combined Fab/Fc glycoforms, the method also distinguished Fc-only glycoforms from the main isoform. This orthogonal IEC-HILIC method provides additional insights into charge and glycosylation heterogeneity, enabling a more comprehensive analysis of cetuximab. It provides an effective approach for detailed characterization of charge variations and glycoform diversity in next-generation protein therapeutics.

papers.title: Newfound source of atmospheric gas-phase PFAS from sea spray aerosol
papers.abstract: Per-and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), known as "forever chemicals", are toxic compounds that persist in the environment. Studies have shown that sea spray aerosol (SSA) is enriched in PFAS and provides a means for their particle-phase transport from the oceans to the atmosphere. Atmospheric particulate transport is considered a main pathway for the distribution of PFAS to even remote locations, impacting human and ecosystem health far away from sources. Here we present novel evidence that SSA also serves as a source of atmospheric gasphase PFAS, suggesting that their transport from the oceans to the atmosphere is much larger than currently assumed. Our field observations and laboratory studies reveal that the amount of gaseous PFAS released may exceed particle-phase concentrations and depends primarily on the low pH of SSA particles, a result of the concentration of ocean water components in SSA particles upon formation and drying. To date, this mechanism has not been considered in estimates of oceanic PFAS emissions, indicating an underestimation of this source for PFAS deposition also in remote locations.

papers.title: Statistical Benchmarking of MnOx Thin-Film Catalysts for Alkaline OER: A Medium-Throughput Approach
papers.abstract: The lack of statistical rigor in electrocatalytic measurements, where catalyst performance is traditionally determined based on a few representative measurements of thin catalyst films, limits the reliability of benchmarking reactions such as the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). This study reports a medium-throughput, statistically rigorous benchmarking framework that converts anecdotal claims of catalytic activity into quantitatively validated evidence. Two MnOₓ-based OER catalysts synthesized via different hydrothermal routes were evaluated across 144 identically prepared thin-film electrodes to explicitly resolve film-to-film variability. The data distribution, intrinsic dispersion, and required sampling size for robust benchmarking were quantified statistically. The HCl-derived catalyst, MnOₓ(H), exhibits narrow, near-Gaussian activity distributions with low relative standard error of the mean (RSEM < 8%) and tight confidence intervals, indicating statistically converged performance at moderate sample sizes. In contrast, the H₂SO₄-derived catalyst, MnOₓ(S), displays broad, right-skewed, non-Gaussian distributions with persistent high-activity outliers and wide confidence intervals (±25-50%), reflecting intrinsic catalyst-film heterogeneity. Importantly, population-level statistics demonstrated that reliance on a small number of selected measurements can substantially overestimate apparent activity and obscure statistically relevant variability. The findings demonstrate that statistical robustness is as essential as electrochemical metrics for meaningful comparison of OER activity data and that variability can arise from both intrinsic material heterogeneity and measurement artefacts. Taken together, this study highlights the limitations of conventional representative-curve reporting and provides a generalizable framework for statistically robust benchmarking of electrocatalysts.

papers.title: A structured dataset of polymers in molecular dynamics simulations extracted by LLM-assisted text mining
papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are widely used to study polymer behavior, yet the resulting simulation data remain scattered across the literature and are rarely available in standardized, machine-readable formats. To address this gap, we present a curated dataset of polymer MD simulations reported in peer-reviewed publications from 1995-2025 using largelanguage-model (LLM)-assisted extraction followed by expert curation. Starting from an initial set of 48,206 abstracts retrieved through keyword-based bibliographic searches, automated screening narrowed the corpus to 755 polymer-MD-relevant publications. Among these, 198 papers reported simulation-derived values for one or more of the six target properties: density, glass transition temperature, radius of gyration, Young's modulus, diffusion coefficient, and viscosity, resulting in 1,095 unique records. Each record captures the polymer system, force field, and available physical properties. By aggregating dispersed literature into a centralized, standardized database, this work supports data-driven analysis, enhances reproducibility in molecular modeling of polymeric systems, and facilitates the development of automated and machine-learning-assisted simulation workflows.

papers.title: Nickel-Photocatalytic Deoxygenative Arylation toward β-Methyl-branched α-Amino Acids
papers.abstract: β-Me-branched α-amino acids are important motifs in peptide therapeutics. However, only few methods on their synthesis have been reported to date. Herein we report an efficient, one-step synthesis of these β-Me-branched α-amino acids through the deoxygenative arylation of threonine, yielding a diverse scope of non-canonical α-amino acids with good functional group tolerance. Our method could also be extended to the deoxygenative arylation of 3-hydroxyproline, giving access to various therapeutically relevant arylated amino acids.

papers.title: Nickel-catalyzed construction of seven-membered rings via [3+2+2] cycloaddition of cis-2,3bis(trimethylsilyl)cyclopropanone and diynes
papers.abstract: Catalytic molecular transformation of cis-2,3-bis(trimethylsilyl)cyclopropanone was accomplished for the first time. In the presence of a nickel catalyst, this reaction yields a bicyclic compound containing a seven-membered carbocycle that is otherwise difficult to construct, via a [3+2+2] cycloaddition of a diyne with a cyclopropanone as a threecarbon unit. Additionally, we illustrated that the molecular transformation of the bicyclic compound occurs through the elimination of the silyl group. This study not only highlights cis-2,3-bis(trimethylsilyl)cyclopropanone as a valuable building block in synthetic organic chemistry but also enhances the comprehension of cyclopropanone chemistry.

papers.title: Insights on the Action and Selectivity of Designed Antimicrobial Lipopeptoids
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial peptoids show promise as host defense peptide mimics, but designing sequences with broad-spectrum activity and low mammalian cell toxicity is challenging. Instead of focusing solely on sequence design, we have explored lipid-based modifications to the C-and N-termini of a helical peptoid motif (Nk-Nfes-Nfes) to achieve a balance between antimicrobial activity and cytotoxicity. Solid-state NMR measurements reveal that these lipopeptoids show interfacial surface activity on both bacterial (POPE/POPG) and mammalian (POPC/Cholesterol) model membrane systems. Their membrane activity correlates with antimicrobial and cytotoxicity results from bacterial cultures (E. coli, P. aeruginosa, S. aureus), hemolysis, and in vitro cell culture assays (HepG2 hepatoblastoma cells). Circular dichroism spectroscopy shows the peptoid and lipopeptoids secondary structures are not the only determinant to deduce activity/cytotoxicity relationships. In summary, our biophysical characterization results closely support the biological observations, suggesting that our peptoids can be rationally designed and hence, offer new dimensions to explore druggable space.

papers.title: Microstructure inference of organic thin films via light modulated photocurrent characterization
papers.abstract: The performance of organic electronic devices is closely tied to their nanoscale donor-acceptor microstructure, yet quantifying these features remains challenging using conventional characterization tools. X-ray scattering and electron microscopy techniques provide high-fidelity structural information, but they are slow, expensive, and challenging to deploy in high-throughput or autonomous processing environments. Here, we propose a complementary, proxy-based route to microstructure inference that leverages the device's transient short-circuit current response under modulated illumination. Using a microstructure-aware excitonic drift-diffusion (EDD) framework that incorporates arbitrary time-dependent generation profiles, we compute current (J(t)) responses for 500 computationally generated donor-acceptor morphologies subjected to full-wave-rectified sinusoidal excitation. From each response, we extract a suite of physically motivated timeand frequency-domain features and pair them with key microstructural descriptors, specifically interfacial area, characteristic domain size, and connectivity. SHAP-based feature selection reveals that a compact subset of transient-response features captures most of the microstructure dependence. Linear surrogate models trained on these subsets achieve good test R 2 across all descriptors, with interfacial area and domain-size predictions exceeding R 2 = 0.9, using fewer than 10% of the simulated morphologies for training. These results demonstrate that high-frequency, amplitude-modulated electrical measurements can recover essential microstructural fingerprints, suggesting a pathway toward compact, non-destructive, and automation-ready characterization tools for high-throughput research in organic electronics.

papers.title: Deoxychlorination of Aliphatic Alcohols via Sulfide-Mediated Electrosynthesis
papers.abstract: This work describes the first example of sulfide-mediated deoxychlorination of aliphatic alcohols under electrochemically triggered conditions. The reaction tolerates a wide range of functional groups, including amines, carbamates, heteroaromatic rings, sulfones and free carboxylic acids and is feasible for primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols. Mechanistic studies indicate that the reaction proceeds via nucleophilic substitution of an electrochemically formed alkoxysulfonium intermediate and represents a new avenue for direct substitution of aliphatic alcohols.

papers.title: Maxwell-Wagner Relaxation in Composite Electrolytes for Solid-State Batteries: Reevaluating Impedance Spectra and Charge Transport of Ceramic-Polymer Hybrids
papers.abstract: Composite electrolytes attract significant attention in solid-state battery research due to their potential to combine the advantages of both inorganic and polymer electrolytes. Ion transport in these electrolytes is frequently investigated using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, where each impedance contribution is typically assigned to a charge migration and polarization process related to a specific phase or interface present within the composite. Here, we provide fundamental insights into the interrelation between impedance spectra and charge transport using electric network simulations. We demonstrate that for 3D composite electrolytes, the assignment of impedance contributions to individual phases or interfaces is often physically not justified. The spatial distribution of the alternating current in these materials depends on excitation frequency, mesostructure, and the electric and dielectric properties of all constituents and their interfaces. This leads to Maxwell-Wagner-type impedance contributions that have no simple correspondence to direct current conduction mechanisms, i.e., leads to impedance contributions that depend on the electric and dielectric properties of multiple phases. We discuss interrelations with classical equations of effective medium theory, e.g., the Maxwell-Wagner model, the impact of particle size, and practical implications for the impedance analysis of ceramic/polymer-based composite electrolytes as one important model case. Among others, the widely studied LLZO-PEO system is considered as a specific example. The conclusions drawn are general and extend to other heterogeneous systems like composite cathodes.

papers.title: An automated platform for tailored late-stage halogenation of pharmaceuticals
papers.abstract: The diversification of lead compounds remains a crucial step in drug development, with bioactive molecules often requiring fine tuning of a range of important pharmaceutical properties. This is achieved through the synthesis of libraries of analogues with subtle modifications in functionality or structure. The complexity of many bioactive molecules, however, does not make this a trivial endeavour. Indeed, many transformations using established chemistry are not suitable due to functional group sensitivity or regiochemical challenges and can require large amounts of time and resources to be spent on multistep syntheses. The development of functional group tolerant transformations can allow the curation of a library of analogues directly from a common, complex precursors through late-stage modification. Harnessing the reactivity of C–H bonds on arenes, which are extremely prevalent in drug like compounds, allows for the addition of functionality to tune electronic and steric properties without the modification of existing functional groups that may be integral to binding properties. Particularly attractive is the installation of a halogen atom to a lead compound to provide opportunities for further diversification through emerging and established cross-coupling techniques as well as the modulation of pharmaceutical properties. Numerous conditions are available to perform C–H halogenation reactions on aromatic compounds. However, “one-size-fits-all” conditions are not reflective of the structural diversity across pharmaceutically relevant molecules and cannot accommodate the density and breadth of functionality. High-throughput screening has been used to optimise C–H functionalisation reactions. However, no such approach exists for the halogenation of pharmaceutical compounds. Here, we develop an automated, machine-learning aided, high-throughput workflow to investigate how varying acidity affects the C(sp 2 )–H chlorination, bromination, and iodination of 32 complex pharmaceutical substrates. Different compounds are shown to require significantly different acidities and yields are improved by optimisation of TFA equivalents. 56 halogenated analogues of 22 pharmaceuticals were prepared using conditions determined by the high-throughput workflow with significant benefit to yield. xTB atomic descriptors were used to predict regiochemical outcomes in a computationally inexpensive way. We envision that the workflow could be used for future similar investigations.

papers.title: Accessing Stable Pyridinium Nanohoops with Low-Lying LUMOs by Pyridine-Directed C-H Activation
papers.abstract: Designing stable organic molecules with tailored electronic properties is key to advancing next-generation electronic materials. Cycloparaphenylenes (CPPs) and related nanohoops have emerged as promising p-type semiconductors, yet their use as n-type materials remains limited due to inherently high-lying LUMO levels. While pyridine-containing CPPs can be alkylated to lower the LUMO, the resulting pyridinium species are often unstable and unsuitable for practical applications. In this study, we report two complementary synthetic strategies to access bridged-pyridinium[n]CPPs as stable, n-type organic materials. A bottom-up approach enables intramolecular cyclization to form the bridged architecture, confirming the stability of this new motif. To streamline access and facilitate structural diversification, we developed a second strategy employing pyridine-directed C-H activation-marking the first example of pyridine-directed C-H functionalization directly on the CPP backbone. The resulting pyridinium-functionalized nanohoops were thoroughly characterized. Electrochemical and spectroscopic studies revealed low reduction potentials (as low as-0.84 V) and red-shifted optical absorption edges (up to 770 nm) for the doubly functionalized di(bridged-pyridinium)[10]CPP 5. Density functional theory calculations corroborate the observed trends in LUMO energies and support the utility of these molecules as n-type building blocks. Together, these results establish bridged-pyridinium[n]CPPs as a new class of stable, tunable materials with potential for organic electronic applications.

papers.title: Predicting Long-Time Quantum Dynamics with Transfer Tensor Method Built from Stochastic Schrödinger Equations †
papers.abstract: The non-Markovian tensor transfer method (TTM) provides a powerful framework for predicting long-time quantum dynamics from short-time evolution data. However, its conventional implementation requires dynamical maps constructed from an information-complete set of N 2 initial states-where N is the system dimension-limiting its use to small-scale problems. Here, we demonstrate that the stochastic Schrödinger equation (SSE) naturally provides an over-complete set of Kraus operators, capturing the essential information needed to build dynamical maps for TTM. This connection enables the extension of TTM to high-dimensional systems by using the dynamical calculation from only one initial state. We demonstrate its performance using two representative SSE methods applied to a symmetric spin-boson model and a 24-site Fenna-Matthews-Olson (FMO) complex. The results confirm that our SSE-TTM can offer an accurate and much more computationally efficient strategy for simulating long-time quantum dynamics in relatively large-scale systems.

papers.title: Preregistered geometry and robustness filters for epitope triage and resistance risk in antibody discovery
papers.abstract: Antibody and ADC programs often commit to expensive epitope mapping before checking whether an epitope is structurally robust to interface substitutions. I extend a previously locked, auditable MD-based epitope triage workflow by adding a resistance robustness layer that quantifies whether core interface contacts remain engaged under matched simulation windows and fixed contact definitions. Applied to EGFR-cetuximab, the K465R substitution produces a localized anchor persistence failure at residue 465 with additional weakening near residue 470, while most interface residues remain highly engaged. This approach is intended as an early, rerunnable screening filter for prioritizing epitope regions and identifying mutation-sensitive anchors, not as a clinical resistance predictor. This work introduces preregistered geometry and robustness filters for early epitope triage and resistance risk screening in antibody discovery by extending a previously locked, auditable MD-based triage engine with a single additional layer: resistance robustness. The fixed core workflow retains matched simulation intervals and sampling, residue-consistent mapping, strict directionality logic for protection-like readouts, and interface filtering based on complex geometry, producing rerunnable audit tables rather than qualitative narratives. On top of this frozen engine, we quantify whether interface anchors remain persistently engaged under a interface substitution using a fixed physical definition of contact and a matched-window comparison. As a case study, we analyze EGFR domain III bound to cetuximab under matched a matched simulation interval simulations (dt a fixed sampling rate) and compute per-residue EGFR-antibody heavy-atom contact occupancy using a locked a preregistered heavy-atom distance cutoff cutoff, complemented by a 0-35 vs the second half of the interval robustness split and no-contact dwell segmentation. The EGFR K465R substitution produces a localized anchor persistence failure rather than a global interface collapse: contact occupancy at residue 465 drops from 0.997 in WT to 0.751 in K465R (Δ = −0.246), driven by an increase in no-contact time from 0.18 ns to 17.4 ns and a clear late-time regime shift, and a neighboring contact at residue 470 is also weakened (0.542 to 0.264; Δ = −0.277). Across the remaining interface, many residues remain near-saturated in both systems, supporting a mutation-localized destabilization of anchor engagement rather than wholesale loss of binding. These results motivate a practical interpretation of "resistance" in this setting as a structural robustness problem under locked rules: identify which interface cores are stable across variants and which anchor contacts become metastable and therefore represent higher risk choices for epitope and ADC pairing decisions. The framework is intended as an auditable screening filter for prioritizing epitope regions and flagging mutation-sensitive anchors, not as a predictor of clinical resistance.

papers.title: A ChemTwin System Enabling Collective Intelligence for Materials Discovery
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven autonomous laboratories are transforming research paradigms and accelerating materials discovery 1-6. However, they still face several critical challenges, including the geographical distribution of experimental platforms with limited resource sharing, a lack of robust data privacy frameworks, and barriers to effective global collaboration for training and prediction. Here, we present ChemTwin, a system that coordinates geographically separated autonomous laboratories for collaborative materials discovery. We demonstrate its performance through three representative experiments that assess data consistency, timeliness, and multi-laboratory collaboration. By integrating a federated learning (FL) module, ChemTwin allocates experimental tasks across laboratories to increase platform utilization while preserving data privacy without any raw data exchange. Furthermore, federated learning-enhanced Bayesian optimization (FBO) achieves more than a twofold reduction in the number of experimental iterations compared with single-node Bayesian optimization (SBO), as illustrated by the optimization of a bismuth-based metal-organic framework (MOF) formulation for peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation in organic pollutant degradation. This study builds a data privacy-preserving framework to share experimental resources across autonomous laboratories for scalable AI-driven materials research.

papers.title: Enhancing the kcat of IsMHETase through a single active site mutation
papers.abstract: Enzymatic PET-recycling offers an environmentally friendly method for regenerating high quality PET from waste PET. This method relies on PET hydrolases to cleave PET into the final monomers terephtalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG) for subsequent re-synthesis. Although PET hydrolases have been significantly improved through engineering, the final breakdown of the intermediate mono(2-hydroxyethyl) terephtalate (MHET) to TPA and EG is slow. Therefore, a dual enzyme process may be beneficial, in which PET hydrolases are accompanied by an efficient MHET hydrolysing enzyme, such as the bacterial IsMHETase from Ideonella sakaiensis. In this study we aimed to improve the catalytic efficiency of IsMHETase by altering the electrostatics in the active site. Guided by prior research we made a series of 36 variants of which ten were purified and tested for MHET hydrolysis. One variant, F495H, showed a 3.4 fold increased kcat and was further characterized both experimentally and computationally. pH and salt profiles showed that the enhanced turnover by F495H depends strongly on the protonation state of the introduced histidine. Computational studies indicate that F495H leaves the binding pose largely unaltered but instead modulates the local electrostatic environment of the catalytic residue Asp492. This leads to higher polarization of the Asp492-His528 dyad and stronger electrostatic stabilization of the transition state. The discovery of this mutation provides a promising route toward faster IsMHETase variants for dual-enzyme systems with an efficient PET-hydrolase. Furthermore, this study provides insight into the structure and mechanistic features of active-site mutations that confer beneficial effects on catalysis.

papers.title: Cosolutes modulate Polyubiquitin Fibrillation
papers.abstract: Ubiquitin, a 76-residue polypeptide, functions as a post-translational modifier and forms polyubiquitin (polyUb) chains on substrate proteins to activate diverse cellular functions. Ubiquitin is often found in the lesions associated with neurodegenerative disorders like Alzheimer's and Huntington's disease. It was recently observed that polyubiquitin chains, under in vitro conditions, often form β-sheet-rich fibrillar amyloid aggregates. However, the exact mechanism of conversion from monomer polyUb to amyloid-like fibrils is poorly understood. We report that polyubiquitin forms higher-order oligomeric fibrils under in vitro conditions. Temperature, pH, and ionic strength modulate polyubiquitin (polyUb) fibrillation. Co-solutes such as ionic liquids and macromolecular crowding agents also enhance the aggregation rate. These findings uncover that temperature/cosolutes lower the energy barrier to populate a partially unfolded form (M*), which drives amyloid-like fibril formation. Other factors increase the effective protein concentration of these partially unfolded forms, accelerating aggregation. These insights provide the fundamental basis for ubiquitin chain aggregation, which is necessary to guide the development of therapies and diagnostics.

papers.title: Thermodynamics without Entropy: Reframing Available Energy as a Thermodynamic Primitive
papers.abstract: Since the inception of thermodynamics, a tension has existed between two frameworks for expressing the second law: Gibbs’ entropy-based formalism, and Kelvin’s conception of the inevitable dissipation of mechanical work. Gibbs' formalism, built upon the fundamental relation, S(U, V, n) , reveals the geometric structure of thermodynamics, from which unexpected physical relationships such as the Maxwell relations and the Gibbs-Duhem equation naturally fall out. Kelvin’s conception, by contrast, is generally treated as a derived construct, and in engineering contexts has developed into availability or exergy analyses. Here, we demonstrate that a complete Gibbsian formalism may be constructed on the basis of a system’s available energy, with no need to invoke entropy. This formalism has its own fundamental relation, Legendre transforms, Maxwell relations, and convex contact-geometric structure, all equivalent to those of the traditional entropy-based framework. We derive several classical results, including the Clausius equation and the expression for the Joule-Thomson coefficient, within this entropy-free formalism, and show how expressions in classical statistical mechanics may be reinterpreted as Legendre transforms of a system’s available energy. Finally, we reflect on the conceptual, pedagogical and historical ramifications of Gibbs' decision to embed entropy, rather than available energy, at the heart of his thermodynamic formalism.

papers.title: Pyrroloquinoline quinone and imidazopyrroloquinoline intake extend healthy lifespan and improve physical dysfunctions with age in mice
papers.abstract: Pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ) and its derivative imidazopyrroloquinoline (IPQ) are nutritionally important, vitamin-like compounds that exert various physiological effects, including cell-growth promotion, neuroprotection, and stimulations of mitochondriogensis. In this study, we investigated whether PQQ and IPQ act as potential geroprotectors that promote healthy longevity as no lifespan aging intervention experiments have been conducted in mammals to date. We conducted lifelong and midlife 0.02% (w/w) PQQ and 0.02% (w/w) IPQ supplementation experiments using senescenceaccelerated mice P8 strain that have a short lifespan. In lifelong supplementation experiments, the day of 75% survival was prolonged by approximately 60% and 30% in the PQQ and IPQ groups, respectively, compared with that in control. In addition, significant delays in the appearance of aging and age-related neuromuscular dysfunction were observed. Furthermore, intake of PQQ and IPQ diets from midlife improved neuromuscular function that had declined with age. We also found that IPQ intake reduced lipid accumulation in adipose tissue and the liver. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to demonstrate that PQQ and IPQ supplementation, whether initiated early or in middle age, is effective in ameliorating age-related alterations, such as neuromuscular function, and extending healthy lifespan in mammals.

papers.title: Natural Orbital Correlation Analysis of Cluster Bonding: From Aromatic Clusters to Metallic Superatoms with Quantum Topology Probes
papers.abstract: We present a systematic study of electron correlation across molecular and cluster systems using the number of effectively unpaired electrons ND = P i ni(2 − ni)—the Takatsuka–Head-Gordon index—computed from coupled-cluster natural orbital occupations over the complete correlated orbital space. Computed at the CCSD/def2-SVP level, all systems studied exhibit substantial total electron correlation when the full natural orbital space is retained: aromatic Al4 2 – (ND = 3.84), antiaromatic Al4 4 – (4.03), planar and icosahedral B12 clusters (4.42 and 4.99), heteroatomic B6N6 (5.11), and cesium–aluminum superatoms Cs3Al8 – and Cs3Al12 – (5.58 and 7.10, respectively). We show that ND is an extensive quantity dominated by the dynamic correlation tail over many weakly occupied virtual orbitals, and introduce the per-electron correlation density fe = ND/Ncorr as a complementary intensive measure. This intensive measure reveals a clear separation: small clusters (Al4, B12, B6N6) exhibit fe ≈ 0.07–0.14, while metallic superatoms show fe ≈ 0.04, reflecting the diluted nature of correlation in large delocalized systems. We demonstrate that truncation of the natural orbital space to a small active window dramatically underestimates ND, and that complete occupation data are essential for physically meaningful correlation diagnostics. In a separate study, we explore whether molecular bonding topology generates characteristic entanglement signatures on a neutral-atom quantum processor (Pasqal). Mapping atomic coordinates of nine molecular systems onto Rydberg atom registers, we find that different chemical topology classes—aromatic, antiaromatic, cage, and metallic—produce systematically distinct entanglement patterns, suggesting that molecular graphs encode topological information accessible to analog quantum hardware.

papers.title: Azopyrazole-based Photochromic Dimerizer Enables Optical Control of Cellular Signaling with Minimal Basal Activation
papers.abstract: Photochromic chemically induced dimerization (CID) system enables reversible optical control of protein–protein interactions in living cells, offering a powerful alternative to conventional optogenetic tools. We previously developed a photochromic CID system using an Escherischia coli dihydrofolate reductase (eDHFR)/HaloTag pair and an azobenzene-based photochromic dimerizer, pcDH, which achieved rapid and reversible protein translocation. However, undesirable background binding resulting from the high affinity of the E -isomer for eDHFR limited its precision. Here, we report an improved system employing an azopyrazole-based dimerizer, pcDH2b, and an engineered eDHFR mutant to reduce background binding. Molecular docking identified F31 as a key residue, prompting cell-based screening of F31 mutants. The eDHFR(F31I) showed minimal background binding while preserving efficient photoreversible dimerization. Fluorescence polarization assays confirmed reduced binding affinity in both dark and violet light-induced photostationary states. The optimized eDHFR(F31I)/Halo–pcDH2b pair exhibited rapid association and dissociation kinetics and enabled precise, lowbackground optical regulation of mitophagy in HeLa cells. Molecular dynamics simulations provided insights into the energetic and structural basis of E/Z selectivity. These results demonstrate that tuning ligand–protein affinity through protein mutation effectively minimizes background binding while maintaining fast photo-responses, providing a practical platform for reversible optical control of cellular signaling with minimal basal activation.

papers.title: Multireference Perturbation Theory Reveals the Intricate Excited-State Electronic Structure of the 2-Phenylpyridine Ligand
papers.abstract: 2-Phenylpyridine (2-ppy) is a widely used cyclometalating ligand in transition-metal complexes (TMCs), yet its intrinsic excited-state electronic structure remains poorly characterized. Here, we investigate its singlet excited states of ππ* nature accessible in the ultraviolet spectral window, both as an isolated molecule and when coordinated in the TMC Ir(2-ppy) 3 , using extended multi-state restricted active-space second-order perturbation theory (XMS-RASPT2). Our study reveals multiple low-lying excited states, whose relative energy ordering and oscillator strengths are strongly dependent on the choice of the orbital active space. The XMS-RASPT2 calculations accurately reproduce the experimental absorption spectrum of the isolated 2-ppy and show that the characteristic two-band profile arises from mixing between the same bright configuration and dark transitions. Coordination to the iridium in Ir(2-ppy) 3 induces an overall red-shift of the ligand-centered transitions accompanied by a change in their energy ordering. In contrast, inter-ligand couplings, evaluated using a Frenkel exciton model, are found to have an almost negligible impact on the electronic structure of the 2-ppy manifold.

papers.title: Towards Utility-Scale Electronic Structure with Sample-Based Quantum Bootstrap Embedding
papers.abstract: One of the main applications for which quantum computers are hoped to find utility is in simulating ground state energies and other observables of molecular chemical systems. The recently proposed sample-based diagonalization method is a readily implementable method for this task on current-day hardware using short circuit depths and has been demonstrated on as many as 85 qubits in recent works. In this work, we combine the recently proposed quantum bootstrap embedding (QBE) method with sampled-based diagonalization (QBE-SQD) and present the first benchmarking study of the QBE method on real quantum hardware, ibm_pittsburgh, a heron r3 processor with 156 qubits. Our test system is a hydrogen ring with 8 hydrogen atoms in the cc-pVDZ basis. We show that for this system, QBE-SQD using an active space of (8e, 19o) per fragment with a 43 qubit footprint produces a ground state energy accuracy which exceeds that of an SQD calculation with a (8e, 30o) active space with a 67 qubit footprint when using a comparable number of Slater determinants. This demonstrates that the use of quantum bootstrap embedding techniques are a promising path towards extending the capabilities of state-of-the-art quantum eigensolvers on near-term devices.

papers.title: Enhancing superexchange through frontier orbital engineering in a van der Waals metal-organic magnet
papers.abstract: Van der Waals metal-organic magnets (vdW MOMs) offer the possibility of realising a wide range of magnetic functionalities not possible in inorganic vdW magnets. In particular, their modularity allows for specific control over ligand-mediated superex- change and hence their ground states. We report a new vdW MOM, CrCl2(btd) (btd = 2,1,3-benzothiadiazole), assembled from a high-energy early transition metal and a redox-active ligand, which leads to a small charge-transfer gap. We solve the structure using a combination of powder neutron diffraction and single crystal electron diffrac- tion, showing that this material contains Cr2+btd0. Magnetometry, neutron diffraction and inelastic neutron scattering measurements allow us to quantitatively determine the magnetic properties of this vdW magnet, showing it is a collinear rectangular antifer- romagnet with small easy-axis anisotropy (JCl = −15.31(5) K, Jbtd = −6.96(10) K, D = −2.0(2) K). Critically, we find that the superexchange through btd, with a low lying LUMO, is significantly stronger than in the CrCl2(pym) (pym = pyrimidine) analogue (Jpym = 1.2(2) K), demonstrating that exchange can be enhanced by potentially redox-active ligands without actual electron-transfer onto ligands. This work provides a route towards vdW antiferromagnetic MOMs with strong magnetic superexchange.

papers.title: Neural Network-based Simulations of Solid Electrolyte Interfaces
papers.abstract: The solid-electrolyte interface (SEI) is a crucial component of electrochemical devices, but its computational description remains challenging due to the many chemical reactions that lead up to its formation. In this paper, we use a neural network forcefield, NeuralIL, to carry out molecular dynamics simulations of the organic layers of a model SEI based on ethylcarbonate and different metal cations, namely lithium, sodium and potassium. The need for an explicit interface is bypassed by introducing reduced electrolyte molecules into the system, whose presence starts a subsequent reaction chain. A series of reaction pathways are identified, leading to a predicted composition of the SEI that is in very good agreement with experimental data from the literature. Moreover, analysis of the structural and dynamic properties reveals key differences between the different metals, such as the presence of additional reactions and chemical species, shifts in the charge distribution of the different molecules, changes in the solvation shells of the metal cations and their impact on the diffusion coefficients.

papers.title: In situ observation of ultra-giant spherulites in perovskite hydrates
Impact of catalyst functionalization, framework defects, and guest loading on nitrobenzene diffusivity in Zr-based metal-organic framework UiO-67 investigated by molecular dynamics and PFG-NMR
papers.abstract: Molecular diffusion in metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) is a key factor controlling their performance in catalysis, gas storage and separation, sensing, and drug delivery applications, where the rate and selectivity of molecular transport directly influence efficiency, selectivity, and the kinetics of molecular recognition. To elucidate critical features of existing MOFs and unravel design principles of novel MOFs, we combine all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with pulsed field gradient NMR (PFG-NMR) measurements to systematically investigate how linker functionalization by proline-derived catalyst, framework defects, and guest loading influence the diffusion of nitrobenzene in the Zr-based MOF UiO-67. We reveal that increasing the fraction of catalystfunctionalized linkers in a mixed-linker MOF reduces nitrobenzene mobility due to steric hindrance in the pore windows and increased surface to volume ratio. Notably, also the position of the functional group on the linker modulates diffusion. Molecular insight provided by MD simulations reveals, that missing linker defects enhance guest diffusivity by enlarging the pore windows of the framework. We furthermore show that an intermediate guest loading maximizes diffusivity, while both lower and higher loadings drastically reduce it. Our combined approach, utilizing MD simulations and PFG-NMR, demonstrates how subtle changes in the framework architecture govern molecular diffusion processes and how a mixed-linker strategy can be employed to mitigate some of these drawbacks.
