papers.title: ChemLint: Conversational Cheminformaticswith Large Language Models
papers.abstract: We introduce ChemLint, an open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that connects any MCP-compatible large language model to a curated suite of local cheminformatics and machine learning tools, enabling rigorous molecular data handling through a conversational interface. Molecular machine learning studies are frequently undermined by inconsistent data preprocessing, including invalid SMILES, unresolved duplicates, and train-test leakage, yet existing LLM-based chemistry tools do not address these data-centric challenges. ChemLint provides tools for data exploration and diagnostics, molecule standardization, and machine learning modeling. All operations are executed deterministically by established libraries and recorded in a project manifest that traces every action, supporting reproducibility and making curation choices explicit. We demonstrate through several examples how ChemLint can be used to identify common data quality issues, evaluate splitting strategies, and execute complete modeling pipelines from raw data to evaluation. ChemLint is freely available at https://github.com/derekvantilborg/ChemLint .

papers.title: Alkali-Metal Base Catalysed Electrocyclisation of Isoprene Derivatives
papers.abstract: The catalytic electrocyclisation of heptatrienes represents an attractive strategy to access seven-membered carbocycles from acyclic precursors, whose medium-size cyclic saturated hydrocarbon counterparts display physicochemical properties of interest for jet-fuel applications. Here we uncover the potential of alkali-metal amides to enable an efficient, high-yielding and multigram-scale electrocyclisation of biobased ocimene and related trienes derived from isoprene. Experimental results shows that both the nature of alkali metal (Li vs Na) and coordination by PMDETA (N,N,N',N",N"pentamethyldiethylenetriamine) play a decisive role in enabling efficient and selective turnover. X-ray diffraction of key metalated intermediates, together with DFT calculations, provides insight into the cyclisation pathway and the factors governing reactivity. The transformation can proceed catalytically at relatively low loadings, with lithium-based catalysis providing full selectivity albeit at higher catalyst loadings, whereas sodium-based systems operate at lower loadings with higher reactivity but decreased selectivity.

papers.title: Operando spectroscopic analysis of photovoltage generation in hematite photoanodes
papers.abstract: Solar-driven water splitting requires sufficient photovoltage to drive both water oxidation and proton reduction. Understanding the factors driving and limiting photovoltage generation is therefore crucial to optimising photoelectrode design but has proven challenging to determine under operando conditions for photoanodes driving slow multi-redox reactions such as water oxidation. In this work, operando optical spectroscopy is employed to measure the hole quasi-Fermi level (E F,p ) position in model hematite photoanodes as a function of applied bias and light intensity. The quasi-Fermi level splitting determined from these data are shown be in excellent agreement with the directly measured photovoltages, demonstrating the electrochemical rather electrostatic origin of photovoltage in these photoelectrodes. E F, p pinning is observed at low light intensities and biases, indicative of hole trap states lying ~ 0.2 eV above the valence band edge with a density of 1 nm -2 . Hole accumulation in these trap states is correlated with first order water oxidation. At higher light intensities and/or more anodic bias, E F,p becomes unpinned, assigned to saturation of these trap states, and correlated with the onset of third order water oxidation to molecular oxygen. Comparison with rate law analyses for other photoanodes indicates that such hole trap states may be a ubiquitous feature of metal oxides and suggests that materials processing strategies to suppress the density of such states would be a promising strategy to enhance photoanode performance.

papers.title: Why Activation Free Energies Converge More Slowly Than Electronic Barriers: Basis set Sensitivity of Vibrational Thermochemistry at Transition States
papers.abstract: Activation free energies are widely assumed to converge in parallel with their underlying electronic barriers. We show that this assumption is not generally valid. Across a diverse set of reactions, electronic activation barriers converge smoothly with increasing basis set, whereas the corresponding free energy barriers exhibit slower and reaction-dependent convergence. Decomposition of ΔG ‡ into electronic, enthalpic, and entropic components reveals that convergence of ΔE ‡ is not sufficient to ensure convergence of ΔG ‡. In most reactions examined, basis set sensitivity of ΔG ‡ is dominated by incomplete cancellation of the entropic contribution (−TΔS ‡) between reactant and transition state, even when the electronic barrier is well behaved. A smaller subset displays mixed enthalpy-entropy sensitivity, reflecting broader changes in vibrational curvature. These behaviors define distinct thermochemical response archetypes that are independent of electronic barrier quality. Activation free energies therefore probe differential vibrational curvature that responds independently to basis set refinement, implying that electronic and thermochemical convergence represent separate dimensions of uncertainty in computational kinetics.

papers.title: Chromatography-free triple quadrupole mass spectrometry for illicit drug identification and quantification
papers.abstract: Drug mixture composition and compound identifications provide public health, first responder, and law enforcement communities with critical and actionable data, guiding emergency response and interdiction, informing the public, and targeting overdose prevention. The advent of novel synthetic opioids, nitazenes, and benzodiazepines, along with the spread of strong veterinary tranquilizer adulterants (e.g., xylazine and medetomidine), have created an ever-changing drug landscape. The Testing, Rapid Analysis, and Narcotic Quality (TRANQ) Research Act of 2023 directs research, method development, measurement science, and standards to address these hurdles. In conjunction with the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Rapid Drug 2 Analysis and Research (RaDAR) program, aimed at monitoring the chemical makeup of the drug landscape, we are investigating analytical instrumentation to enable drug screening to move from the laboratory to an agile point-of-need setting. We explored compound identification with a transportable chromatography-free direct analysis in real time triple quadrupole mass spectrometer (DART-TQ-MS) and the NIST/NIJ DART-MS Data Interpretation Tool with Forensics Database. Full scan analysis of single-component standards demonstrated limits of detection generally in the tens to hundreds of picograms with a few in the single nanogram range (i.e., compounds with extremes in volatility). Single-component, mixtures, and real-world street drug samples were investigated with potential identifications made matching against the highresolution mass spectral library, using both full scan and product ion scan spectra. The development of a compact, chromatography-free TQ-MS system enables rapid on-site analysis, supporting public health, law enforcement, and forensic applications. This innovation paves the way for mobile, point-of-need drug testing and identification, enhancing our ability to respond to emerging drug threats.

papers.title: Stimulated Geological Fuels: Enabling Sustainable Civilization On Earth and Space
papers.abstract: Building civilizations on extraterrestrial planets such as the Moon and Mars will require reliable in situ production of energy and fuels to reduce reliance on Earth-based transport and enable large-scale off-world industry. Existing In Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) strategies focus on atmospheric processing, water extraction, or regolith-based methods, which often require high electrical power and provide limited chemical diversity. Serpentinization has been proposed as a natural source of hydrogen and other value-added chemicals, but naturally occurring processes are slow, spatially constrained, and not readily engineerable. Here, we present a new ISRU paradigm based on "stimulated geofuel production", building on recent experimental demonstrations that serpentinization can be intentionally accelerated and controlled. By activating the redox reactivity of iron-rich ultramafic rocks under subsurface temperature and pressure conditions, this approach converts water, carbon dioxide, and nitrogen species into hydrogen, ammonia, methane, and other reduced products without electricity or direct carbon emissions. The planetary subsurface functions as a self-powered chemical reactor, enabling controlled geochemical synthesis. We also highlight how advances in geoscience, materials science, and artificial intelligence on Earth can accelerate the discovery and optimization of such ISRU pathways where geological fuels can directly be imported back to Earth for sustainable economy.

papers.title: An affordable and low-waste protocol for rapid and robust solid-phase peptide synthesis at elevated temperatures
Development and Evaluation of Rice Husk-Based Cardboard for Sustainable Packaging
papers.abstract: The global e-commerce surge has intensified the demand for cardboard and paper packaging, exacerbating deforestation and ecological degradation due to reliance on wood pulp. This study explores rice husk, an agricultural by-product with an annual global yield exceeding 120 million tons, as a sustainable raw material for packaging applications. A novel manufacturing process was developed combining rice husk with starch, Elmer's glue, and a polylactic acid coating, following sodium hydroxide pretreatment. Comparative mechanical evaluations revealed that PLA-coated rice husk boards demonstrated strong performance, achieving an edge crush resistance of 8.14kN/m and a burst strength of 663kPa. These boards also exhibited enhanced humidity and water resistance. The widespread availability, and robust mechanical properties of these boards position them as an eco-friendly substitute for wood-based packaging. By mitigating solid waste and reducing dependence on virgin wood resources, rice husk-based packaging presents a scalable solution to support sustainable material innovation and environmental conservation.

papers.title: Electronic Shannon Entropy as an Effective Descriptor of Nonradiative Dynamics in Dense Manifolds of Excited States: Case Study of C 20 , C 60 , C 70 , C 76 , C 84 , C 86 and C 90 Fullerenes
Integrating Charge Equilibration with Equivariant Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
Rational Design and Synthesis of Zwitterionic Polysiloxanes with Extreme Dielectric Permittivity
papers.abstract: The design and synthesis of high permittivity polymers face a key challenge; namely, strong polarization requires concentrated dipoles that give rise to high thermal transition temperatures. The inverse relationship between permittivity and mobility limits the dielectric constant of all dipolar materials. Consequently, for pure polymers, the largest known dielectric constants are roughly 100 for vinylidene fluoride copolymers at the Curie temperature and 35 for room-temperature polymer melts. Here, we report the rational design and synthesis of a zwitterionic polysiloxane with a static dielectric constant of 420 at room temperature, the largest value achieved to date. This specific polysiloxane contains pendent zwitterionic dipoles with long, flexible spacers that simultaneously amplify dipole moment and dilute strong coulombic interactions, yielding a glass transition temperature Tg of-14 °C. This novel high-κ dielectric polymer overcomes the permittivity-mobility limitation thereby challenging the existing paradigm for dipolar polymer dielectrics.

papers.title: Data-Driven Design of Metal-Organic Frameworks for Photoelectrochemical Reactions
papers.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are modular materials that are chemical versatile, offering vast design possibilities through the combination of metal clusters, organic ligands, and framework topologies. Traditionally utilized in gas storage and separation, the high porosity and tunable properties of MOFs position them as attractive candidates for (photo)electrochemical applications, including batteries, fuel cells, and solar-driven fuel conversion. We present a data-driven workflow integrating hybrid quantum chemical calculations with a multimodal AI model (MOFTransformer) to efficiently predict oxidation and reduction potentials for over 270,000 known and hypothetical MOFs. Through high-throughput screening, we identify optimal candidates tailored for coupled solar-driven CO 2 -to-CO reduction and water splitting, highlighting promising structural motifs and properties for targeted energy conversion reactions with significantly reduced computational effort compared to traditional approaches.

papers.title: Hydrothermal Synthesis and Structural Characterization of Lanthanum Oxide (La₂O₃) Nanorods
papers.abstract: Lanthanum-based nanostructures have attracted increasing attention due to their unique physicochemical characteristics and relevance in catalysis, energy storage, and electronic applications. This study presents a comparative investigation of lanthanum nanorods and lanthanum nanoparticles with emphasis on their structural, thermal, and electronic properties. Both morphologies were synthesized under controlled conditions to ensure comparable composition while varying dimensional anisotropy. Structural characterization revealed distinct crystallographic orientation and aspect ratio-dependent lattice strain in nanorods, whereas nanoparticles exhibited more isotropic grain distribution and reduced directional growth. Thermal analysis demonstrated enhanced thermal stability and slower mass-loss kinetics in nanorods, attributed to their lower surface defect density along the longitudinal axis. In contrast, nanoparticles showed higher surface reactivity and earlier onset of thermal transformations due to their increased surface-to-volume ratio. Electronic property evaluation indicated morphology-dependent band structure variations, with nanorods displaying improved charge transport pathways and reduced recombination probability compared to nanoparticles. These findings highlight the significant role of shape anisotropy in tailoring the physicochemical performance of lanthanum nanostructures. The results provide insights for optimizing lanthanum-based materials in advanced functional applications where structural stability and electronic efficiency are critical.

papers.title: Morphology-Controlled Fabrication of Lanthanum-Based Nanostructures for Advanced Catalytic Applications
papers.abstract: Precise control over nanostructure morphology has emerged as a decisive factor in optimizing catalytic efficiency, surface reactivity, and structural stability. Lanthanum-based nanomaterials, particularly oxides and composite structures derived from rare-earth elements, exhibit promising physicochemical properties such as high oxygen mobility, tunable electronic configurations, and thermal robustness. This study investigates the controlled fabrication of lanthanum-based nanostructures through solution-assisted and thermal synthesis strategies, emphasizing the influence of reaction parameters on shape evolution, crystallinity, and surface area. Distinct morphologies, including nanorods, nanosheets, and hierarchical porous assemblies, were obtained by systematically varying precursor concentration, pH, temperature, and calcination conditions. Structural characterization confirmed phase purity and uniform particle distribution, while surface analysis revealed enhanced active-site exposure in anisotropic configurations. Catalytic performance was evaluated in representative redox and environmental reactions, demonstrating that morphology-driven surface engineering significantly improves reaction kinetics and long-term stability. Nanorod and porous architectures exhibited superior activity due to improved charge transport pathways and higher accessible surface-to-volume ratios. The findings highlight the critical role of morphology control in tailoring lanthanum-based nanomaterials for advanced catalytic systems. The study provides a scalable synthesis framework and establishes structure-property correlations that can guide the rational design of next-generation catalysts for environmental remediation and energy conversion technologies.

papers.title: Ion Mobility-mass spectrometry Dashboard (IMDash): an automated, multi-platform computational pipeline to support production of robust and large-scale experimental collision cross-section libraries Authors
papers.abstract: Experimental collision cross-section (CCS) libraries are emerging as critical resources for enabling high-confidence molecular annotation in metabolomics studies and providing ground truth for training models to predict CCS. Multifield drift tube ion mobility spectrometry (DTIMS) is the only accepted method for primary CCS determination, yet large-scale CCS library construction has been impractical due to labor-intensive data processing workflows. To address this, we developed the Ion Mobility Mass Spectrometry Dashboard (IMDash), a flexible and containerized pipeline integrating community-developed tools and that performs data preprocessing, CCS determination, and database generation. IMDash can process data from a variety of IMS-MS platforms and methods including both multifield and calibrated single-field DTIMS and traveling wave IMS (TWIMS) methods like structures for lossless ion manipulations (SLIM). Benchmarking results demonstrate both the flexibility of IMDash across computing platforms, from personal computers to cloud and high-performance computing clusters, and the substantial speedups that are possible on more capable systems. We further demonstrate the real-world functionality of IMDash by building CCS libraries for three commercial compound collections using both multifield and calibrated single field DTIMS methods, producing reference CCS values for thousands of compounds and adducts with high reproducibility and agreement between methods. By supporting edicient processing of large experimental datasets, IMDash provides a scalable solution for building high-quality reference CCS libraries, advancing metabolomics research and empowering the development of machine learning models for chemical property prediction.

papers.title: Group 9 Transition-Metal Silyl-and Germylphosphines: From Structure to Cobalt-Catalyzed Carbonyl Hydrosilylation
Rapid Photocrosslinking of Surface-Modified Boehmite Nanofibers for Monolithic Aerogels
papers.abstract: Aerogels derived from hydrolysis-condensation processes typically undergo time-dependent gelation governed by intrinsic reaction kinetics, which restricts external control over network fixation and macroscopic shape formation. Once initiated, structural consolidation proceeds spontaneously, making rapid and programmable immobilization of a percolated framework difficult. Consequently, in most conventional sol-gel systems, independent control of long-term dispersion stability and externally triggered network fixation remains challenging. In this study, a photoresponsive gelation strategy for boehmite nanofiber (BNF)-based monolithic aerogels is reported. This strategy entails the incorporation of photopolymerizable functional groups onto the nanofiber surface through the use of 3-(methacryloyloxy)propyltrimethoxysilane (MPTMS), followed by the induction of crosslinking through photoinduced radical polymerization. The modified BNF dispersion has been shown to exhibit stability over extended periods in the presence of a photoinitiator. However, ultraviolet irradiation under ambient conditions has been shown to trigger gelation and network fixation within several tens of seconds. This externally activated process enables rapid immobilization of a percolated inorganic nanofiber framework. The resulting aerogels had bulk densities ranging from 0.093 to 0.37 g cm −3 and specific surface areas ranging from 328 to 429 m 2 g −1 . Their compressive modulus increased proportionally with MPTMS content. At the optimal composition, the thermal conductivity was 0.0228 W m −1 K −1 at 20 °C, lower than that of air at room temperature. Even after 6 h of heat treatment at 150 °C, this material showed no structural or physical property degradation. The photocrosslinking process enables rapid, externally triggered network formation. This approach is effective for controlling gelation in inorganic nanofiber-based aerogels. It also supports the fabrication of thermally insulating monoliths that require shape control.

papers.title: Europium Doped Atomically Precise Bismuth Oxido Nanoclusters as Molecular Building Blocks for Photoluminescent Hybrid Materials
papers.abstract: Structural and optical characterization of Eu 3+ doped atomically precise bismuth oxido nanoclusters (BiO-NCs) of about 2 nm in size is reported. The BiO-NC [Bi 38 O 45 (NO 3 ) 24 (dmso) 28 ]:Eu ( C-1:Eu ) is transformed into soluble [Bi 38 O 45 (OMc) 24 (dmso) 4 ]:Eu•4dmso•4H 2 O ( C-2:Eu ) and [Bi 38 O 45 (OMc) 24 (EtOH) 10 ]:Eu•4EtOH ( C-2 E :Eu ) by ligand exchange and without changing the amount of Eu 3+ doping (ω ≈ 1 %). SC XRD analysis revealed partial substitution of the bismuth atoms with preference in the inner {Bi 6 O 9 } core unit of the {Bi 38 O 45 } cluster. Temperature dependent photoluminescence studies show bismuth-and europium-based dual emission at low temperatures, whereas only the latter is preserved at room temperature. As a result of the low-symmetry environment of Eu 3+ a remarkable intensity of the 5 D 0 → 7 F 0 (electric dipole) transition is observed, accompanied by lifetimes of about 2 ms and quantum yields ranging from 53 % ( C-2:Eu ) to 65 % ( C-1:Eu ). The solubility of C-2 E :Eu enables its use for the synthesis of organic-inorganic hybrid materials. Thus, transparent hybrid materials were prepared by radical copolymerization of methyl methacrylate, 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate and C-2 E :Eu , showing distinct photoluminescence characteristics even with a low Eu 3+ content of 2.7•10 -5 mol-%.

papers.title: Real-space emergence of statistical unimolecular kinetics in a photoacid generator
papers.abstract: The transition from excitation-specific photochemical dynamics to statistical unimolecular kinetics has not been directly observed at the structural level in complex polyatomic molecules. Using ultrafast X-ray scattering, we track this emergence in gas-phase phenyl triflate (C 6 H 5 OSO 2 CF 3), a model compound for photoacid generators used in photolithography. Following UV excitation, we track the reaction in real-space from femtoseconds to nanoseconds, identifying an early-time dissociation that produces SO 2 CF 3 • before complete intramolecular energy redistribution. We probe this dissociation's crossover into statistical behavior, which is accompanied by secondary dissociation into SO 2 and CF 3 • over a broad distribution of decay times. From the scattering signal we extract pathway-resolved population dynamics, which together with nonadiabatic dynamics simulations, quantify the vibrational energy distributions of the parent and radical intermediates that govern the observed kinetics. Spanning five orders of magnitude in time, these measurements establish direct structural access to the emergence of statistical unimolecular behavior in a complex photoexcited molecule.

papers.title: Advancing the Characterization of Modified Oligonucleotides through an Integrated Infrared Action Spectroscopy-Mass Spectrometry Approach
papers.abstract: Therapeutic oligonucleotides (ONs) incorporate subtle chemical modifications to enhance performance, but these small structural differences and related impurities are difficult to identify and characterize with traditional analytical approaches. To address this challenge, we combined infrared (IR) action spectroscopy with mass spectrometry (MS) to characterize a series of modified ONs. To establish the method, we first examined short 6-mer ON model systems, revealing spectral differences arising from variations in nucleobase composition and intramolecular interactions. These effects were further resolved using hydrogen-deuterium exchange (HDX), which enabled distinction between the N-H and O-H stretching modes, allowing for complete vibrational assignment. Building on these insights, we next applied the IR-MS method to therapeutically relevant 16-mer antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs). The broad spectral features of these larger oligonucleotides, caused by conformational diversity and intramolecular interactions, were narrowed by fragmenting them prior to IR irradiation, yielding spectra of the w7 and w5 ions instead. This tandem-MS workflow, together with the 6-mer assignments, enabled characterization of the ASOs. The method further revealed characteristic behavior of locked nucleic acid (LNA) groups, where LNA-induced stabilization decreases fragmentation efficiency and results in lower yield values in the IR action spectra. Interestingly, the LNA-to-DNA ratio indicated that LNA groups cause redshifts, with the magnitude of redshift increasing at higher LNA content. Adenine-specific spectral features were observed upon addition of a second adenine group, demonstrating the specificity of this method. Overall, these methods advance structural characterization of ONs and overcome previous analytical limitations, highlighting their potential for identifying modified ONs.

papers.title: Modular Design and Dynamic Adjustment Strategy for Enhanced Economic Robustness in Continuous Pharmaceutical Manufacturing
papers.abstract: Continuous pharmaceutical manufacturing plants are conventionally built with customized, fixedcapacity equipment, leading to high capital risk and suboptimal operational performance when adjusting production throughput to match fluctuating market demands. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a modular design and dynamic adjustment strategy that adapts to demand uncertainty. The aim is to ensure long-term economic performance and flexibility. Demand uncertainty is represented using two stochastic models: a fixed-rate compound annual growth rate (CAGR) scenario capturing uncertainty under long-term market growth trends, and a time-dependent CAGR scenario accounting for annual growth rate fluctuations within those longterm trends. As a case study, we evaluate the continuous ibuprofen manufacturing process by comparing the conventional plant consisting of customized reactors with the modular plant including standardized reactor modules. The dynamic adjustment strategy selects active reactor modules based on a kinetically informed switching strategy to maintain optimal performance. Long-term economic performance is evaluated using the levelized cost of production (LCOP) across 100 independent stochastic demand trajectories for each CAGR scenario. Results indicate that conventional design is highly sensitive to demand uncertainty, whereas the modular design demonstrates greater economic robustness, achieving a lower mean LCOP with reduced cost variability, and eliminates the risk of unprofitability.

papers.title: Systematic Computational Identification of Active Drug Metabolites Across the Human Proteome
papers.abstract: Understanding drug metabolism helps mitigate toxicity risks and anticipate pharmacological effects beyond the parent compound. Here, we explore high-confidence in vitro human bioactivity annotations from the public domain associated with a curated dataset of drug-metabolite pairs. Our findings show that 26% of all drug-metabolite-target combinations contain metabolites with retained or increased bioactivity relative to their parent drugs, showing a high proportion of active metabolites with potencies below 100 nM. Moreover, these active metabolites display similar predicted physicochemical and ADME properties to their parent drugs, indicating that their biological activity may be preserved in vivo. Two key features of the identified active metabolites are noted: 1) the metabolite is more likely to be formed via an O-demethylation or an N-demethylation at a tertiary nitrogen, and 2) these drug-metabolite pairs are frequently active against the membrane receptor target class. To support further research in this area, we make our data compilation, including pairs with identified active metabolites and recorded bioactivity data, openly available.

papers.title: Visible light induced photoactive bifunctional nickel catalyst enabled C(sp 2 )−C(sp 2 ) cross electrophile coupling
papers.abstract: The construction of biaryls underpins countless applications in pharmaceuticals and materials science, yet conventional transitionmetal-catalyzed cross-coupling typically requires expensive palladium catalysts, stoichiometric organometallic reagents, and substratespecific conditions, limiting sustainability and scope. Crosselectrophile coupling (XEC) offers an attractive alternative, though the development of a general, selective strategy for uniting diverse (hetero)aryl fragments has remained an enduring challenge. Here we present a general photoinduced nickel catalytic platform that enables modular C(sp²)-C(sp²) XEC under mild conditions. Direct excitation of a Ni(II)-ligand complex and a trialkyl amine with visible light generates α-aminoalkyl radical without the need for an external photocatalyst or photosensitizer. This radical governs selective halogen-atom transfer between electrophiles guided by bond dissociation enthalpies, enabling cross-selective (hetero)aryl-(hetero)aryl coupling. Newly designed donor-acceptor bipyridine ligands facilitate this process, allowing cross-selectivity to be optimized by adjusting (hetero)aryl radical formation and oxidative addition, while the Ni(II) complex serves dually as photoactive and coupling catalyst. Utilizing an earthabundant Ni(II) catalyst, this scalable, metallic-reductant-free protocol delivers diverse unsymmetrical (hetero)biaryls in high yield and crossselectivity, offering a sustainable and economical route to complex molecular architectures.

papers.title: Solar-driven strategies in carbon capture technologies
papers.abstract: The escalating atmospheric concentration of carbon dioxide (CO2), a major greenhouse gas, has intensified the global pursuit of sustainable carbon management technologies. Carbon capture has been identified as a major technology for decarbonising hard-to-abate sectors, but pilot plant trials have been underwhelming due to the high energy requirements of existing processes. Among emerging strategies, solar-driven carbon capture and release (CCR) is promising for its ability to directly harness the abundant solar energy for CO2 abatement and removal. However, major challenges pertaining to fundamental chemical and material discovery and process integration must be overcome before it can be practically implemented. Our review provides an overview of emerging strategies in solar CCR systems, including photothermal, photomorphic, photoelectrochemical, and photochemical approaches, while emphasising the fundamental principles, chemistries, classifications, performance metrics, compatibility, and underlying mechanisms of these diverse strategies. We also discuss the challenges and limitations of current solar CCR technologies, along with process integration considerations for industrial settings, to assist in the practical incorporation of solar energy into carbon capture facilities.

papers.title: Towards a physically interpretable symbolic language of molecular recognition
papers.abstract: Despite decades of structural biology and molecular modelling, molecular recognition remains predominantly interpreted through static structural representations, although it is inherently dynamic. Here we represent protein-ligand recognition as a language-like statistical process arising from sequential interaction dependencies over time. This is achieved through STRIPES (Spatio-Temporal Representation of Interactions in Protein-ligand Engagement Strings), a conceptual framework that encodes molecular interaction dynamics as symbolic sequences. By discarding explicit coordinates while preserving interaction semantics, STRIPES captures recognition-relevant temporal information inaccessible to conventional structural representations. Across ~15,000 molecular dynamics trajectories, STRIPES reveals non-random sequential organization and conserved interaction motifs that transcend protein families and molecular scaffolds. This abstraction compresses highdimensional trajectories into compact symbolic sequences while preserving mechanistic information, enabling interaction-driven similarity analysis and generative molecular design. Leveraging sequence-to-sequence deep learning, we demonstrate that interaction patterns can be translated into chemically valid and bioactive ligands, including compounds with experimentally observed bioactivity. By recasting molecular recognition as an emergent symbolic process, STRIPES establishes a generalizable conceptual framework for comparing, learning, and engineering biomolecular interactions beyond static structural information.

papers.title: Simple and Economical Carbonization of Yerba Mate Stems Using a Self-Built Oven
papers.abstract: The conversion of plant biomass into charcoal is an effective strategy for adding value to agricultural by-products. However, carbonization processes carried out in low-cost, self-built kilns have been rarely studied with scientific rigor. This study demonstrates that an economical oven, designed and built with readily available materials, can efficiently carbonize yerba mate (Ilex paraguariensis) stems. Experimental evidence is presented on the simplicity of the oven's construction and the carbonization process, the charcoal obtained is characterized, and quantitative data confirming the low cost of the procedure are provided. The results support the technical and economic viability of transforming plant biomass into a higher-value product through a simple, accessible, and low-cost process.

papers.title: Data-driven landscape scenicness mapping for continental-scale onshore wind resource assessment
papers.abstract: Visual impacts on scenic landscapes dominate public opposition to onshore wind turbines. Yet wind resource assessments often overlook landscape scenicness due to limited data availability. This study introduces a scalable machine learning framework for generating continental scenicness layers, trained on crowdsourced scenicness ratings from Great Britain and achieving high predictive performance. The resulting scenicness maps are integrated into an onshore wind resource assessment under three landscape preservation scenarios across 29 European countries. We show that prioritizing scenic landscapes in planning can reduce wind generation potential in certain countries by over 60%. However, it only modestly affects the continental median levelized costs of electricity (57 €/MWh and 54 €/MWh under low and high preservation scenarios), while substantially increasing regional costs in scenic mountainous regions such as the Alps and Norway. These findings demonstrate how data-driven approaches can enable socially aware and large-scale energy system planning.

papers.title: Agentic Retrieval for Bio-Based Recovery of Critical and Near-Critical Minerals
papers.abstract: Biological extraction routes are promising for critical-minerals recovery. We present a Large Language Model (LLM)-assisted autonomous literature mining agent that converts a large local PDF corpus into a schema-validated evidence dataset. The agent maintains persistent state in SQLite, applies staged gating, and invokes Claude LLM only on a small shortlist for figure/table-aware extraction. In one run, the pipeline produced 56 validated records. The dataset is dominated by bioleaching and biosorption, frequently targeting Cu, Ni, Zn, Co, and Fe. In the bioleaching of Cu subset (N=16), an analysis shows a dominant ore/tailing-bacterial Fe/S oxidizers-inorganic acid/ferric pathway plus smaller waste-context pathways with organic-acid signatures. This work demonstrates a cost-efficient pathway from unstructured PDFs to a machine-readable knowledge base that can accelerate evidence synthesis and experiment design for biobased critical materials recovery.

papers.title: Dimethyl Isosorbide: A Renewable Solvent for Sustainable Drug Discovery Chemistry
papers.abstract: As regulatory and environmental pressures intensify, the search for greener solvents in drug discovery is paramount. Dimethyl isosorbide (DMIso), derived from biomass, has emerged as a sustainable dipolar aprotic solvent alternative to traditional CMR solvents like DMF, DMAc and NMP. This work presents a comprehensive assessment of DMIso in key synthetic transformations relevant to medicinal chemistry like amide and ester couplings, nucleophilic aromatic substitutions, alkylations, and protection group chemistry. Our findings demonstrate that DMIso supports efficient reactions, tolerates strong bases such as NaH, and facilitates straightforward isolation of products. By sharing this work, we hope to contribute to a wider use of DMIso as a safe and versatile solvent for organic synthesis.

papers.title: Multi-Cation Engineering in Stable Thiocyanate-Templated Layered Double Perovskite Halides
papers.abstract: Hybrid organic-inorganic perovskite halides offer a versatile structural platform owing to their flexible bonding nature. In particular, a remarkable number of novel layered perovskites have been realized by incorporating bulky organic cations. Not only organic cation engineering but also halide engineering using molecular anions has recently emerged as an effective approach to drastically alter the perovskite bonding network, yet the accessible compositional and structural diversity remains very limited. Here, we report, for the first time, hybrid layered Ag-Bi double perovskites, MA 4 AgBiX 4 (SCN) 4 (X = Br, I), in which incorporation of thiocyanate (SCN⁻) at the halide site reduces the dimensionality of the perovskite framework. While the previously reported single metal cation compound, MA 2 PbI 2 (SCN) 2 , offers a unique van der Waals-coupled structural platform, its rapid decomposition under ambient conditions and limited compositional space have hindered further development. First-principles calculations reveal that the structural instability of the lead-based bromide analogue arises from a bromide-induced lifting of the axial SCN ligand and resultant increased interlayer hydrogen-bond distance. By transitioning to an Ag-Bi architecture, we demonstrate that the incorporating Ag + (4d 10 5d 0 ) with isotropic s-orbital character and thus enhanced angular flexibility, compared to Pb 2+ (6s 2 6p 0 ) having orientational preference, effectively mitigate this destabilizing effect. This strategy enables the synthesis of a full range of solid solutions with band gaps tunable from 1.95 to 2.30 eV. The resulting materials, particularly the bromide-rich phases, exhibit a marked increase in environmental robustness. These results establish multi-cation design as a versatile and stable platform for expanding the structural space of pseudohalide-based hybrid perovskites.

papers.title: Benchmarking Steady-State Density Functional Theory for Modeling Electrocatalytic Reactions
papers.abstract: Properly capturing the intricate effects induced by electrochemical potentials is essential for reliably modeling electrocatalytic reactions and guiding the rational design of electrocatalysts. In particular, potential-driven nonequilibrium effects, often inaccessible to conventional equilibrium-based approaches, play a pivotal role in elucidating the underlying reaction mechanisms. In this work, we benchmark a recently developed nonequilibrium ab initio approach based on steady-state density functional theory (SS-DFT) by performing calculations on four prototypical electrocatalytic reactions: the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR), oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO 2 RR). We systematically compare SS-DFT with conventional DFT-based methods, including constant charge (DFT-CC) and constant potential (DFT-CP) approaches. When the system 1 remains near equilibrium with only minor nonequilibrium effects, SS-DFT accurately reproduces conventional DFT results. However, under potentials that induce profound nonequilibrium effects, SS-DFT predicts significant changes in free energies compared to DFT-based methods, which facilitate adsorptions and reaction pathways. These findings demonstrate that SS-DFT provides a powerful framework for modeling electrocatalytic reactions and highlight the importance of incorporating nonequilibrium effects for the fundamental understanding of electrocatalytic mechanisms.

papers.title: High-resolution Photoelectron Spectroscopy of Cryogenically Cooled VO 3 H 2 −
papers.abstract: High-resolution photoelectron spectra of cryogenically cooled VO3H2 − anions obtained with slow electron velocity-map imaging (cryo-SEVI) are reported. Comparison with DFT calculations shows that the spectra are from the cis-VO(OH)2 − dissociative adduct. The same complex is formed through either the VO2ˉ + H2O or VO3ˉ + H2 pathways, with the latter yielding significantly more ions. The experiment yields an electron affinity of 1.857(1) eV and several vibrational frequencies for the neutral species. Comparisons to Franck-Condon (FC) simulations show good agreement with the experimental features, but there are several transitions that do not appear in the simulations. These features are assigned to FC-forbidden transitions involving nontotally symmetric vibrational modes and are attributed to Herzberg-Teller (HT) coupling with the excited 𝐶𝐶 ̃1𝐵𝐵 2 anion state. The results are compared to the previous (cryo-SEVI) study of the titania water-split adduct, TiO3H2 − to explore the role of the additional vanadium valence electron in the spectroscopy and chemistry of these adducts.

papers.title: Unveiling Carbon-Based Highly Exposed Active Sites for Efficient Urea Electrosynthesis via a Descriptor-Based Machine Learning Strategy
papers.abstract: While the synergistic interactions between adjacent active sites and their tunable electronic structures of metal-loaded carbon-based materials (MCMs) are beneficial for urea synthesis, the development of efficient catalysts is significantly impeded by low selectivity and insufficient active site exposure. Herein, we report a data-driven strategy combining high-throughput Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations and Machine Learning (ML) to screen MCMs with highly exposed active sites for efficient urea synthesis. By analyzing the reaction networks of 90 metal pairs, we identify the co-adsorption energy of reactants (E ads (* CO_NO)) as a critical descriptor that governs both the thermodynamic activity and selectivity of the C-N coupling pathway. An XGBoost regression model is subsequently established to map intrinsic atomic features to this descriptor, enabling the rapid screening of 1458 candidates. This workflow efficiently narrowed the candidates pool, from which Zr_Pd@A and Zn_Pd@Z were ultimately identified as the most promising candidates with optimal activity and selectivity. Electronic structure analysis reveals that the delectron density of the Pd site near the Fermi level plays a pivotal role in balancing the activation of NO and facilitating C-N coupling. This work not only proposes high-performance catalyst candidates but also demonstrates a universal ML-assisted paradigm for decoupling complex reaction networks in electrocatalysis.

papers.title: Cosolutes modulate Polyubiquitin Fibrillation
papers.abstract: Ubiquitin, a 76-residue polypeptide, functions as a post-translational modifier and forms polyubiquitin (polyUb) chains on substrate proteins to activate diverse cellular functions. Ubiquitin is often found in the lesions associated with neurodegenerative disorders like Alzheimer's and Huntington's disease. It was recently observed that polyubiquitin chains, under in vitro conditions, often form β-sheet-rich fibrillar amyloid aggregates. However, the exact mechanism of conversion from monomer polyUb to amyloid-like fibrils is poorly understood. We report that polyubiquitin forms higher-order oligomeric fibrils under in vitro conditions. Temperature, pH, and ionic strength modulate polyubiquitin (polyUb) fibrillation. Co-solutes such as ionic liquids and macromolecular crowding agents also enhance the aggregation rate. These findings uncover that temperature/cosolutes lower the energy barrier to populate a partially unfolded form (M*), which drives amyloid-like fibril formation. Other factors increase the effective protein concentration of these partially unfolded forms, accelerating aggregation. These insights provide the fundamental basis for ubiquitin chain aggregation, which is necessary to guide the development of therapies and diagnostics.

papers.title: Vibrational Scaling Factors Follow a Power Law
papers.abstract: Harmonic vibrational scaling factors are shown to follow an empirical power law decay curve for molecular systems. Scaling factors have been tested with constant, linear, polynomial, logarithmic, and power law scaling functions used to scale harmonic frequencies calculated using B3LYP and B97-1 density functional theory. These scaling factors follow non-linear monotonically decreasing trends that approximate to logarithmic and power law decay functions rather than the conventional constant or linear scaling functions. The proposed power law scaling method is found to improve on existing constant scaling factors and wavenumber linear scaling factors by up to ca. 35 % and 19 %, respectively, while treating vibrations more consistently across the spectral range. Triple bond bending vibrations are also shown to deviate significantly and are indicated as pathological.

papers.title: Gas-Phase Investigation of P/N Synergism in Phosphonate-Amine Flame Retardant Systems: The Role of Oxygen in Thermal Decomposition
papers.abstract: Phosphorus-nitrogen flame retardant (PN-FR) systems are discussed for their synergistic effects, yet most studies attributed synergism to condensed-phase activity, leaving the influence of nitrogen on phosphorus gas-phase species poorly understood. This knowledge gap mainly arises from experimental challenges in capturing transient gas-phase species under realistic conditions. To address this, a novel setup was developed that enables steady-state investigations of flame retardant decomposition on textile substrates, with in situ mass spectrometric analysis of the evolved gases. Complementary experiments on the pure flame retardant were conducted to clarify its intrinsic decomposition pathway and how it is modified by the presence of nitrogen or the substrate. The pure phosphonate primarily released larger phosphorus-containing species together with highly flammable hydrocarbons. When an amine was introduced, the mechanism shifted toward the formation of smaller phosphorus species known to act as key intermediates in gas-phase flame inhibition. Similar trends were observed on the cotton textile, alongside additional nitrogen-phosphorus interactions forming phosphoramidates. These findings demonstrate that nitrogen substantially alters the gas-phase chemistry of phosphonate-based flame retardants and underline the necessity of studying complete FR-substrate systems to fully understand their flame-retardant behavior.

papers.title: Gaussian Process Modeling of Bioorthogonal Cycloaddition Reactivity from Sparse Data
Unveiling the Adsorption of N-PHA on Graphene-Supported Single-Atom Catalysts: A DFT and Machine Learning Study
papers.abstract: Highly selective catalytic synthesis of N-phenylhydroxylamine (N-PHA) is of great significance. However, undesired side reactions readily occur under reaction conditions. Understanding its adsorption on catalyst surfaces is essential for controlling reactivity and selectivity. Herein, density functional theory (DFT) is employed to investigate the adsorption of N-PHA on graphene-supported M1-N3X/C single-atom catalysts (M: transition metal; X: a non-metal dopant). Two primary coordination modes, N-and O-coordination, are compared by analyzing adsorption Gibbs free energies, Bader charges, d-band centers, and ICOHP. In addition, high-throughput screening of 108 configurations via the SISSO machine learning algorithm identifies key physical descriptors governing adsorption energy, enabling the construction of predictive regression and classification models. This work reveals the synergistic roles of metal center and non-metal dopant in regulating adsorption strength and selectivity, offering both fundamental insights and a data-driven framework for designing highperformance single-atom catalysts in green synthesis.

papers.title: Composition-Dependent Antiferromagnetism in Low-Dimensional Hybrid Organic Cobalt-Halide Semiconductors
Reactivity of CO2 with isopropanol in gas phase under mild temperature conditions using Ni/CeO2 catalysts
Interplay of Catalyst and Electrode Design Governs C–C Coupling in Ag-Doped Cu Loaded Gas Diffusion Electrodes
papers.abstract: Electrochemical carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) reduction has been intensively studied as a promising route for converting CO 2 into value-added multi-carbon products such as ethylene (C 2 H 4 ). To date, most efforts have focused on the development of highly active electrocatalysts, particularly through alloying and heteroatom doping of Cu, to enhance C–C coupling and C 2 H 4 formation. However, in gas diffusion electrode (GDE) systems operated at industrially relevant current densities, CO 2 reduction proceeds at complex gas–liquid–solid triple-phase interfaces, where the structure of the catalyst layer critically governs the reaction microenvironment and product selectivity. However, how this interfacial structure affect the performance of alloyed catalysts and whether such effects can be generalized across different catalyst compositions remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that CO 2 reduction selectivity in Ag-doped Cu catalyst-loaded GDEs is governed by the cooperative interplay between catalyst and electrode design. Using Ag-doped Cu nanoparticles as a model system, we systematically investigate how Ag doping and catalyst loading collaboratively define the reaction microenvironment and CO 2 reduction selectivity. We demonstrated that moderate catalyst loadings maximize C 2 H 4 selectivity by establishing a balanced reaction environment with appropriate CO accumulation and efficient CO 2 transport, whereas excessively low or high catalyst loadings result in suppressed C 2 H 4 formation also in the alloyed catalysts. These results reveal that alloy catalyst performance is determined not only by inherent electronic and atomic properties but also by the catalyst layer configuration at the triple-phase interface. In GDE systems, optimizing this local environment is essential to fully unlock the catalysts' intrinsic activity.

papers.title: Silicon-Tether Strategy for the Synthesis of Tetraphenylammonium
Structurally Enabling ADMET Anti-Targets via Induced Fit Docking and Free Energy Perturbation
papers.abstract: The development of a small-molecule suitable for clinical use involves optimization of ligand binding to an identified target protein but also frequently the reduction of binding to a variety of anti-target proteins known to pose translational risk. These anti-targets, often referred to as ADMET proteins, often contain large, highly flexible binding sites leading to promiscuous binding of small molecules. This property often frustrates efforts to execute structure-based design against these anti-targets. Here we demonstrate the application of a combination of induced fit docking and free energy perturbation to structurally enable several of the most common anti-targets: cytochrome P450 isoforms 3A4 and 2D6, the hERG ion channel, and PXR. Crucially, the enforcement of a consensus binding mode across a congeneric series allowed for the efficient exploration of a wide range of receptor conformation space. Results are presented for both public retrospective datasets and prospective application in active drug discovery programs.

papers.title: In‑Situ Visualization of ZIF‑L‑to‑Nanocarbon Transformation and Nanoscale Origins of ORR Activity
papers.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks are versatile precursors for nanostructured, heteroatom‑doped carbons, yet the nanoscale processes that couple crystalline collapse, short‑range reorganization, and electrocatalytic function remain obscure. Here, we elucidate the spatiotemporal transformation of 2D leaf‑shaped ZIF‑L into N‑doped carbons by integrating in‑situ TEM and in‑situ XRD with synchrotron X‑ray pair distribution function analysis and electron energy‑loss spectroscopy. Controlled heating to 650 °C visualizes layer‑selective framework collapse decoupled from electron‑beam artifacts, while ex‑situ pyrolysis (700-1100 °C) maps the emergence of amorphous nanodomains, temperature‑dependent ligand scission, migration of Zn-N species, and progressive Zn removal. The resulting carbons exhibit tunable nanoscale porosity and nitrogen speciation that govern oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance, with materials formed at 1000 °C delivering the highest activity in our temperature series. Correlating thermal protocol, local structure/chemistry, and electrochemical metrics establishes a temperature-structure-activity relationship that rationalizes the formation of ORR‑active sites and mass‑transport‑favorable architectures. Beyond ZIF‑L, the mechanistic framework-real‑time imaging of collapse, tracking of short‑range order, and chemistries of mobile Zn-N motifs-provides general guidance for the bottom‑up design of MOF‑derived nanocarbons. This work highlights how in‑situ nanoscale probes deconvolute beam and thermal effects, reveal diffusion‑mediated reorganization within amorphous intermediates, and enable the rational thermal engineering of carbon electrocatalysts with predictable active‑site chemistry and hierarchical porosity.

papers.title: Computational Prediction and Experimental Validation Framework for Nitrogen-Enriched Metal-Decorated Porous Framework Composites: Enhanced Reversible Hydrogen Physisorption at Ambient Temperature
papers.abstract: Version 3 note: Metadata correction only. One abstract term corrected from Li-decorated MOF to Na-decorated porous framework for consistency with Version 2 Supporting Information. Scientific content unchanged. We present a comprehensive computational framework for predicting synergistic hydrogen storage performance in nitrogen-enriched porous framework composites through hierarchical integration of three distinct architectural components. The material design combines: (1) crystalline nitrogen-rich covalent organic frameworks (COFs) synthesized via imine or triazine condensation reactions (nitrogen content 15-35 atomic %, BET surface area 1500-4000 m 2 /g, optimal pore diameter 6-15 Å matching H 2 kinetic diameter 2.89 Å), (2) controlled metal decoration (lithium, sodium, potassium, magnesium, or calcium) coordinated to framework nitrogen Lewis base sites at 4-18 wt% loading creating enhanced hydrogen binding sites (15-25 kJ/mol) through induced dipole polarization mechanisms, and (3) conductive carbon scaffold (graphene aerogel, carbon nanotubes, or activated carbon fibers) at 15-40 wt% providing mechanical support, preventing framework aggregation, and enabling thermal management (>500 W/m•K conductivity). Employing density functional theory calculations (DFT-D3 dispersion corrections) for binding energy prediction and grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations for capacity prediction, we establish predicted hydrogen storage capacity of 3.5-4.5 wt% at 298 K and 50 bar pressure-representing 25-60% improvement over best experimental literature (Li-activated carbon: 2.8 wt% at 298 K/100 bar). The synergistic enhancement factor of 2.0-2.8× (measured versus interference-corrected additive prediction) demonstrates non-additive performance characteristic of multi-component hierarchical architectures. Computational predictions are rigorously validated against 18 peer-reviewed experimental studies establishing binding energies (pristine COF: 5-10 kJ/mol, Na-decorated porous framework: 17-24 kJ/mol), surface areas (COF: 1500-4200 m 2 /g), and capacity benchmarks (Li-carbon systems: 2.1-2.8 wt% at 298 K). Complete experimental validation methodology is disclosed including synthesis protocols (solvothermal COF synthesis 120-180°C, organometallic Li decoration under inert atmosphere, scaffold integration), structural characterization (XRD, BET, XPS for Li-N coordination), and performance testing (Sieverts apparatus isotherms 273-323 K, Clausius-Clapeyron binding energy determination, 500-cycle durability). This work establishes a validated computational-to-experimental framework for rational design of ambient-temperature hydrogen storage materials addressing the global energy transition challenge requiring economical, safe, and reversible storage systems for fuel cell vehicles and renewable energy infrastructure.
