For optimization under data constraints, we compare Bayesian optimization (BO) and reinforcement learning, highlighting BO as a broadly applicable strategy across composition, manufacturing, and device operation optimization. We further describe data fusion and transfer learning strategies that combine multi-fidelity and multi-laboratory datasets and transfer knowledge across chemistries to mitigate data scarcity. Finally, we outline open challenges and research gaps in data, modeling, and hardware/software integration, aiming to motivate continued progress toward data-driven solutions for degradation challenges in energy device development.

papers.title: 77PD-Quinone: Synthesis, Coho Salmon Toxicity Assessment, and Comparison with the Commercial Antidegradant 77PD
papers.abstract: Since the emergence of reports demonstrating the toxicity of 6PPD-quinone towards coho salmon ( Oncorhynchus kisutch ), there has been a growing interest in assessing the toxicity of other para-phenylenediamine-based rubber additives, and their quinone transformation products. A technique for the multi-gram scale synthesis of 2,5-diaminoquinones was developed to prepare 2,5-bis((5-methylhexan-2-yl)amino)cyclohexa-2,5-diene-1,4-dione (77PD-quinone) for toxicity assessment. The toxicities of N,N'-bis(5-methyl-2-hexanyl)-1,4-benzenediamine (77PD) and 77PD-quinone were evaluated in coho salmon. Juvenile coho salmon were exposed to a geometric series of five test concentrations of 77PD or 77PD-quinone, a negative control (dilution water), and a solvent control (100 µL/L dimethylformamide) for 96 hours under flow-through conditions. 77PD was found to be toxic to coho salmon with a 96‑hour LC 50 value of 24 µg/L active ingredient (a.i.), and the NOEC was 13 µg a.i./L. No mortality was observed for 77PD-quinone at the highest attainable dose level, 226 µg a.i./L, at which signs of test water saturation were observed.

papers.title: Discovery Science with Autonomous ML-Driven Continuous Flow Chemistry
papers.abstract: In the context of discovery science, particularly in autonomous ML-driven continuous-flow chemistry, AI and ML play pivotal roles in general data analytics by transforming raw experimental data into actionable insights for experimental design. AI encompasses broader systems like autonomous agents and large language models (LLMs), while ML focuses on algorithms that learn from data to predict, optimize, and classify outcomes. In continuous flow setups, where reactions occur in real-time streams, data analytics involves handling multimodal data (e.g., spectroscopic, geometric, kinetic) from sensors and in-line monitors. This enables closed-loop systems in self-driving labs (SDLs), where AI/ML analyzes trends, reduces noise, and guides iterative experiments to efficiently explore chemical spaces, minimizing human intervention and accelerating discoveries in materials, catalysis, and pharmaceuticals.

papers.title: Silicon-Tether Strategy for the Synthesis of Tetraphenylammonium
Prebiotic Organic Chemistry of Diketopiperazines, Cyclic Dipeptides
papers.abstract: Even though the significance of amino acids and polypeptides is well recognized in broad prebiotic chemistry fields, 2,5-diketopiperazines (DKPs) or cyclic dipeptides remains a mysterious species without clear relevance to the origin of complex biomolecular systems. The aim of this review article is to demonstrate the various roles and functions of DKPs in simulated prebiotic reactions reported over the past few decades. By highlighting both experimental and computational simulations, the formation and reaction of DKP derivatives in a range of prebiotically plausible conditions were discussed from the organic chemistry viewpoint, as the manuscript organization is predicated on fundamental reaction patterns such as photochemical synthesis, aminonitrile chemistry, and amino acid condensation. Analytical challenges of DKPs were identified through the literature review too, as the product detection and characterization are critical not only in prebiotic chemistry but also in synthetic organic chemistry fields. The collection and critical analysis of reports about prebiotically plausible processes of DKPs may imply the breadth of its chemical diversity including the potential relevance to nucleotides, value as a building block to more intricate biomacromolecules, and symmetry breaking.

papers.title: ChemPFN: Unified Bayesian Modelling of Bioactivities Across ChEMBL
Photocatalytic Radical Functionalization of Alkenylammonium Salts
papers.abstract: Alkenylammonium salts are introduced as an underdeveloped class of electron-deficient radical acceptors. Under visible-light photoredox catalysis combined with halogen-atom transfer (XAT) or hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT) activation modes, these cationic alkenes react with a broad range of alkyl radical precursors. The transformation enables modular construction of structurally diverse quaternary ammonium compounds under mild conditions. The synthetic utility of the protocol is demonstrated through cyclopropanation, late-stage functionalization, and one-pot demethylation to access tertiary amines. This work establishes alkenylammonium salts as versatile building blocks in catalytic radical chemistry and expands the reactivity landscape of quaternary ammonium salts.

papers.title: Engineered Cascade for Arene Functionalization: Integrating Unspecific Peroxygenase and Halohydrin Dehalogenase for Continuous Flow Systems
Cyclic Peptide Inhibitors of the MLH1-MSH3 Interaction as a Potential Therapeutic Strategy for Huntington's Disease
papers.abstract: Components of the DNA mismatch repair (MMR) pathway modulate somatic CAG-repeat expansion at the huntingtin (HTT) locus and alter the age of clinical motor diagnosis and progression of Huntington's disease (HD). MSH3, which encodes a subunit of MutSβ (MSH2-MSH3), has been identified as a genetic modifier of age at onset of multiple clinical phenotypes in people with HD (PwHD). MutSβ interacts with MutL endonucleases (MutLα, MLH1-PMS2 and MutLγ MLH1-MLH3) in a ternary complex with DNA to initiate MMR. Disruption of the MLH1-MSH3 protein-protein interaction (PPI) represents a potential therapeutic strategy to inhibit MMR and limit somatic CAG-repeat expansion. Leveraging the MLH1 Interaction Protein (MIP) Box sequence and the structural information of the hMLH1 C-terminal domain (CTD) bound to an MSH3-derived peptide (21 QAVLSRFFQ 29), we designed and optimized potent linear and cyclic peptides targeting the MLH1-MSH3 interface. Dimerization of the optimized cyclic peptide (compound 52) enhanced binding affinity, achieving double-digit nanomolar potency in a MutSβ:MutLα:DNA (MLH1-MSH3-DNA) ternary complex assay in the presence of 100 μM of ATP (compound 52 IC50 = 87 nM, compound 56 IC50 = 32 nM). Evaluation in an in vitro MMR DNA repair assay using cellular nuclear extracts from MMR-proficient and-deficient cell lines demonstrated that our lead compound (56) effectively inhibits MutSβ/MutLα-dependent DNA repair in human cells. These results highlight cyclic peptide-mediated disruption of MLH1-MSH3 as a promising approach to modulate MMR activity and possibly mitigate somatic CAG-repeat expansion in HD.

papers.title: Sampling a GDB-20 Database of 32 Trillion Drug-Like Molecules by Generative Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Identifying new chemical entities for small molecule drug discovery requires the continued exploration of its vast chemical space, which has been speculated to contain 10 60 or more molecules. Here we used generative artificial intelligence to sample a GDB-20 database estimated to contain 32 trillion organic molecules corresponding to 26.9 million molecular graphs up to 20 nodes selected for their limited topological complexity. We show that GDB-20 populates a distinct chemical space of sp 3-rich, 3D-shaped and natural product-like molecules with favorable synthetic accessibility score. The relevance for drug discovery of our 12 billion sample, named GDB-20s and representing 0.04% of the full database, is evidenced by high compliance with drug-likeness and toxicity filters, and the coverage of thousands of scaffolds occurring in bioactive molecules recorded in the ChEMBL database. The generative models for GDB-20 and the 12 billion sample are available for download at https://gdb.unibe.ch.

papers.title: Metal-dependent Adsorption Mechanism in Perfluorinated MIL-140A Metal-Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: Perfluorinated metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) with MIL-140A topology display metal-dependent adsorption behavior: while the Ce IV analogue [F4_MIL-140A(Ce)] exhibits step-shaped CO 2 adsorption isotherms and strong affinity for H 2 O, both associated to a concerted structural rearrangement of the linkers, the Zr IV counterpart [F4_MIL-140A(Zr)] shows a classical type I CO 2 isotherm with a lower adsorption capacity and only weak affinity for H 2 O. A multitechnique approach, including solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, in situ infrared spectroscopy, and variable temperature powder X-ray diffraction, provided clear evidence that this contrasting behavior arises from the absence of an open metal site on Zr IV and the inability of Zr IV to adopt an octacoordinated geometry, which prevent the establishment of strong metal-guest interactions.

papers.title: Far-and mid-infrared spectroscopy of transiently chiral twistacenes: triphenylanthracene and hexaphenylanthracene
papers.abstract: We present experimental gas-phase infrared spectra of two transiently chiral polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, triphenylanthracene and hexaphenylanthracene, in a wide spectral range, to characterize the substitution- and strain-induced changes in vibrational modes of anthracene. The spectra were collected using ion-dip spectroscopy at the free-electron laser FELIX. Analysis of the spectral features, supported by density functional theory computations in the harmonic approximation and by ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, allowed us to identify the specific bands that arise from the perturbations of the phenyl groups of the anthracene backbone.

papers.title: Reproducible Genomic Medicine Stack for Population Structure, Statistical Genetics, Tumour Signatures, Clonality, and AI Variant Prioritisation
papers.abstract: Background: Genomic medicine increasingly depends on integrated analytical pipelines that connect cohort-level genotype quality control, population structure adjustment, statistical genetics, tumour genome interpretation, and clinically credible artificial intelligence (AI). A persistent barrier to translation is that many pipelines are presented as isolated components, with limited reproducibility and incomplete governance reporting for calibration, interpretability, and subgroup performance. Methods: We present a single, end-to-end, deterministic computational framework that regenerates all datasets, figures, and tables under fixed random seeds. The framework unifies, (i) genotype cohort quality control (QC) with ancestry-stratified missingness diagnostics and allele-frequency profiling, (ii) population structure inference using principal components analysis (PCA) and nonlinear embeddings, plus quantitative ancestry differentiation via an FST-like proxy to quantify genetic differentiation between populations, (iii) genome-wide association study (GWAS) testing with PC adjustment and calibration checks, followed by a fine-mapping proxy using approximate Bayes factors (ABF) to produce 95% credible sets, (iv) polygenic risk score (PRS) construction and evaluation with explicit calibration and ancestry-stratified transferability audits, (v) tumour mutational signature extraction from 96-channel catalogues using non-negative matrix factorisation (NMF) with model-selection diagnostics, coupled to tumour mutational burden (TMB) summarisation and exposure profiling, (vi) clonal architecture inference from variant allele frequency (VAF) mixtures using mixture modelling, and (vii) AI-assisted variant prioritisation with discrimination, precision-recall behaviour, calibration, interpretability (permutation importance and partial dependence), and subgroup robustness reporting. Results: The integrated workflow produces reporting-ready outputs that demonstrate how QC and population structure diagnostics propagate into calibrated association testing and locus prioritisation. Credible-set fine mapping narrows causal hypotheses into compact variant sets. PRS analyses show that discrimination can diverge from calibration and that subgroup performance differences arise even under controlled simulations, motivating governance before deployment. Tumour modules recover distinct mutational processes, quantify right-skewed TMB with highburden outliers, and resolve heterogeneous tumour-specific signature exposures. VAF mixture structure separates tumours with simpler versus more complex clonal patterns. The variant prioritisation model achieves strong precision-recall enrichment with low calibration error, yields mechanistically plausible feature effects, and provides ancestry-stratified performance summaries suitable for governance review. Conclusions: This work contributes a reproducible, end-to-end blueprint that integrates population genomics, statistical genetics, tumour mutational processes, heterogeneity proxies, and trustworthy AI evaluation into a single executable pipeline. By making calibration, interpretability, and subgroup auditing explicit outputs, the framework supports training, auditability, and adaptation to local cohorts under appropriate ethics and infrastructure.

papers.title: A Luciferin-Gold Nanorod Bioconjugate Confirms Cellular Uptake of Gold Nanorods by Combined Photoacoustic and Bioluminescence Imaging
Generative Multi-Property Refinement of Polymer Chemistries
papers.abstract: We present a generative, multi-objective optimization method for polymer chemistry. By leveraging monomer-level properties that are directly correlated with polymer properties, we design targeted step-growth polymers with desired glass transition temperatures (T g), band gaps (E g), and Flory-Huggins interaction parameters with water (χ water) across a broad chemical space. Generative design is accomplished using a variational autoencoder integrated with linear property prediction heads. Linear organization of the latent space enables the identification of a single latent vector to steer 1 the simultaneous optimization of multiple polymer property objectives. Subsequent Bayesian optimization within the latent space allows further enhancement of T g , E g , and χ water relative to a reference polymer chemistry. We subsequently applied the generative model to design per-and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)-based polymers with reduced fluorine content but comparable physical properties. Overall, this work establishes a generative, multi-objective approach for navigating early-stage polymer design, prior to experimental validation or computationally expensive simulations.

papers.title: Photochemical para-selective C-H amination of azines via N-shift of heteroaryl azides
papers.abstract: Access to 3,4-diaminoazines is limited by regioselectivity challenges in azine functionalization. We report a photochemical strategy enabling the direct synthesis of 3,4-diaminoazines through a meta -to- para nitrogen migration ( N -shift). Blue LED irradiation of 3-azidoquinolines at room temperature allows para -selective C–H amination while concurrently installing diverse amines at the meta -position. In contrast, N- shifts in 3-azidopyridines preferentially form valuable diazepines, reflecting divergent reactivity governed by N -heterocycle electronics, as supported by computational analysis.

papers.title: Experimental design, machine learning, and genetic algorithm to support the production of conductive polymer nanocomposites
papers.abstract: The development of conductive polymer nanocomposites presents a complex challenge due to the nonlinear interactions between polymer matrices, carbon-based fillers, and processing conditions. In this study, we combine experimental design, machine learning (ML), and genetic algorithms (GA) to optimize the formulation of conductive filaments for additive manufacturing applications. A full factorial experimental design was employed to evaluate different polymer types, carbonaceous fillers, and processing parameters. The electrical conductivity of the resulting composites was measured and used to train predictive models-namely, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) and a random forest (RF)-whose hyperparameters were optimized using Optuna. Both models achieved satisfactory performance metrics, with Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) values of 0.47 for MLP and 0.43 for RF on the test set. The trained models were then integrated into a genetic algorithm to explore optimal formulations, which identified PA66 as the most promising matrix and single-walled carbon nanotubes as the most effective conductive filler. Model interpretability was assessed via SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), which corroborated GA results, particularly highlighting the models' preference for longer processing times and lower/medium rotation speeds-conditions that align with known percolation and dispersion requirements in conductive nanocomposites. This integrated approach illustrates the potential of materials informatics to support the design and discovery of advanced functional materials.

papers.title: Synthesis of Chiral Aromatic Heterocycles: Rhodium-Catalyzed Cyclization of Sulfonimidamides and Sulfondiimidamides
papers.abstract: Although cyclic SIAs have demonstrated promising medicinal potential, methodologies for their construction remain relatively scarce. SIAs have proven to be suitable nitrene precursors for aziridination and C-H amination, when mixed with hypervalent iodine and a metal catalyst. Herein, we report the intramolecular cyclization of SIAs featuring N-acyl type substitution via a dirhodium nitrene intermediate, forming a new N-heteroatom bond. The reaction leads to a diverse array of aromatic heterocyclic products featuring stereogenic sulfur centers. A combination of computational and spectroscopic techniques were utilized to investigate the complex relationship between stereochemistry and aromaticity as well as to explore their unique electronic and geometric features. Finally, the potential for these heterocyclic motifs to be utilized for medicinal chemistry was evaluated by synthesizing an analogue of enzalutamide featuring the heterocyclic core and determining its resulting pharmacokinetic properties and bioactivity.

papers.title: Stereoelectronic-aware catalyst embeddings from 2D graphs via 2D-3D multi-view alignment
papers.abstract: In catalyst discovery, data-driven design and screening are playing an increasingly central role. However, molecular descriptors that encode the decisive steric and electronic properties often lack automation and unification. We present CatEmb, a stereoelectronic-aware catalyst embedding learned through contrastive alignment of 2D and 3D molecular graph representations. Trained on the curated CatCompDB dataset, CatEmb encodes implicit 3D structural and energetic information directly from a 2D molecular graph. We demonstrate its efficacy in clustering chemically diverse ligand classes and enhancing reaction performance prediction in quantitative structure-performance relationship models. Furthermore, we develop a novel, similarity-based iterative strategy using CatEmb. For high-throughput experimental campaigns aimed at exhaustively mapping a large condition space, this strategy efficiently identifies high-performing, substrate-general catalysts, significantly outperforming random and model-based approaches. When applied to large-scale virtual libraries with limited experimental validation, it successfully prioritizes high-performance catalysts tailored for specific reactions. CatEmb provides a versatile and efficient foundation for data-driven catalyst discovery.

papers.title: HHT: A Polymer Property Prediction Framework Leveraging Natural Language
papers.abstract: Predicting the macroscopic properties of polymers solely from 1D chemical sequences (e.g., SMILES) is inherently an ill-posed problem, as it neglects critical higher-order factors such as chain topology, condensed-state morphology, and processing history. To bridge this "semantic gap" between low-level structural representations and high-level physical functionalities, we propose HHT (Highly Hybrid Text), a novel framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) into polymer property prediction. HHT employs a dual-stream architecture that synergizes implicit topological features extracted by a pre-trained chemical language model (PolyBERT) with explicit mechanistic reasoning generated by a scientific LLM. A dynamic Adaptive Gating Mechanism is introduced to weigh the contribution of structural versus semantic features based on task-specific dependencies. Extensive evaluations on seven benchmark datasets demonstrate that HHT outperforms many baseline models. Crucially, HHT transforms the traditional "black-box" fitting paradigm into a "whitebox" interpretable system. We first validate the model's focus on mechanistic logic via semantic attention visualization, confirming its ability to prioritize physical descriptors over statistical noise. Furthermore, through counterfactual sensitivity analysis, we demonstrate that the model correctly infers property shifts induced by textual morphological perturbations, demonstrating that natural language can serve as a high-dimensional, physically consistent feature modality for materials science.

papers.title: How Tetrodotoxin Blocks Sodium Channels: A Docking and Geometric Perspective
papers.abstract: Voltage-gated sodium channels (VGSCs) are essential membrane proteins responsible for electrical signaling in excitable cells. Guanidinium toxins such as tetrodotoxin (TTX) and saxitoxin (STX) block these channels by binding to the extracellular pore region and have traditionally been understood to stabilize binding through multipoint electrostatic and hydrogen-bond interactions. However, the role of geometric constraints imposed by pore architecture in determining binding stability remains insufficiently characterized. Molecular docking of TTX and STX was performed under multiple grid displacement conditions, and the resulting pose ensembles were analyzed using spatial and geometric metrics. Center-of-mass clustering and distance-dependent affinity analysis revealed two distinct regimes: a deep pore region with convergent, stable poses, and an entrance region with dispersed, variable poses. Notably, the number of contact residues did not directly correlate with docking affinity, indicating that binding stability is not determined solely by anchor interactions. These results suggest that geometric convergence within sterically constrained pore regions plays a key role in stabilizing toxin binding. The rigid cage-like structures of TTX and STX appear to promote selective alignment with pore geometry, supporting a geometric constraint model of VGSC blockade.

papers.title: Property-Dependent Scoring Bias in Virtual Screening Validation: Evidence from Dual Scoring Function Cross-Validation of BCL-2 G-Quadruplex Ensemble Docking
papers.abstract: Physics-based docking scores correlate with molecular size, yet virtual screening validation rarely controls for physicochemical property differences between actives and controls, risking inflated discrimination metrics. Here we address this problem through ensemble docking of the BCL-2 promoter G-quadruplex (PDB: 2F8U, 10 NMR models), cross-validated with AutoDock Vina (7,469 compounds, 114 ensemble-validated) and rDock (7,296 compounds, 113 validated), classifying each finding as scoring-function-agnostic or scoring-function-dependent. Agnostic results include the analytical framework, discrimination direction, the Kendall’s W category hierarchy, and G4-specific cross-scoring correlation (rho = 0.632). Dependent results include discrimination magnitude (Vina AUROC = 0.748 vs. rDock 0.602), compound rankings (rho = 0.263, n = 38), and model concordance patterns. Retrospective validation against 111 experimentally confirmed BCL-2 G4 binders (ROBIN dataset) yielded AUROC near 0.5 for both scoring functions (Vina: 0.466; rDock: 0.493), establishing that discrimination observed with size-diverse controls reflects property-dependent scoring bias, not target-specific recognition. Hydrogen bond donor count (rho = 0.647) and topological polar surface area (rho = 0.525) predict rank divergence between scoring functions, whereas rotatable bond count does not, implicating polar interaction parametrization—not conformational sampling—as the source of disagreement. Single-model screening recovered only 45–85% of ensemble top-20 compounds (Jaccard overlap 0.29–0.74). The ensemble docking methodology generalizes across scoring functions; compound prioritization, however, requires multi-scoring-function consensus.

papers.title: Fast and Scalable Sample Preparation for Integrated Metabolome and Exposome-Wide Association Studies (MWAS/ExWAS)
Effect of doping graphene quantum dots with metalloid dopants in the presence of zigzag and armchair edge configuration.
papers.abstract: Graphene quantum dots (GQDs) are known as promising zero-dimensional nanomaterials due to their tunable electronic and optical properties arising from quantum confinement and edge effects. In this work, a comprehensive density functional theory investigation is carried out to explore the influence of semi-metal doping and edge configuration on the structural, electronic, chemical reactivity, and optical properties of hexagonal graphene quantum dots. Two edge types, zigzag and armchair, are considered for pristine GQDs and GQDs doped with fourth group (Si, Ge) and fifth group elements (As, Sb). All geometries are fully optimized using the CAM-B3LYP and ωB97XD functionals via DFT, and the electronic excitations are analyzed via time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT). The results exhibit that heteroatom doping induces significant structural distortion due to the larger covalent radii of dopants and their specific valence shell electron configuration compared to carbon. Electronic structure analysis shows that both dopant type and edge configuration strongly modulate the HOMO–LUMO gap and density of states. In particular, doping the GQDs with fourth group elements —especially with zigzag edges—exhibit a pronounced reduction in bandgap, chemical hardness, and an enhancement in dipole moment and electrophilicity index, indicating improved charge-transfer capability and electronic reactivity. In contrast, arsenic- and antimony-doped systems introduce more localized electronic states, higher electrophilicity, and increased structural strain, because of their different valence shell electron configuration compared with carbon, suggesting carrier trapping tendencies that are less favorable for electronic transport applications.

papers.title: Reductive coupling of aryl (pseudo)halides towards symmetrical biaryls via a dual Ni/photoredox catalysis
papers.abstract: A novel reductive approach towards symmetric biaryls employing dual Ni/photoredox catalysis was developed based on previously conducted mechanistic considerations including DFT calculations. Employing NEt 3 as a cheap and energetically favorable, weak reducing agent for the homo-coupling of conveniently accessible (pseudo)halides, highly functionalized symmetrical biaryls were obtained in generally high yields. To highlight the synthetic value of our herein reported method, different potentially interesting compounds and the hepatitis C drug daclatasvir were synthesized.

papers.title: Stability of Information-Carrying DNA Origami Nanostructures During Repeated Freeze–Thaw Cycles
papers.abstract: Encoding information in molecular arrangements on DNA origami nanostructures (DONs) provides the basis for novel concepts in molecular data storage and computing. To preserve their integrity over long timescales, the information-carrying DONs are often stored in a frozen state. Here, we investigate the effect of repeated freeze–thaw (F/T) cycles on the structural and functional integrity of DONs carrying biotin (Bt) modifications. Streptavidin (SAv) binding is used to visualize the stored information by atomic force microscopy (AFM) before and after 40 F/T cycles. Two strategies are compared by F/T cycling of (I) SAv-bound DONs and (II) SAv-free DONs that are exposed to SAv directly before AFM imaging. Our results reveal that while the DONs retain their overall shape, F/T cycling induces a small amount of damage, leading to slightly reduced SAv binding. Adding glycerol at mM concentrations efficiently protects the DONs and restores the original SAv binding yields. Nevertheless, SAv exposure after F/T cycling leads to slightly higher and more consistent SAv binding yields and a lower background of non-specifically adsorbed SAv compared to strategy I. This makes information readout by AFM more efficient and renders strategy II more convenient for long-term storage of information-carrying DONs with repeated information readout.

papers.title: Dual-Polarity, Highly Responsive Broadband Photoelectrochemical Photodetectors Enabled by Ti3CNTx MXene/GO Heterostructure
papers.abstract: Dual polarity photodetection devices are an important building block for multifunctional devices. In particular, photoelectrochemical photodetectors (PEC PDs) show great promise due to their ability to control photocurrent polarity by varying the incident light wavelength and the choice of electrolyte. However, achieving broadband dual-polarity PEC PDs that deliver high responsivity and bias switchable operation remains a significant challenge. 2D transition carbides, nitrides, and carbonitrides (MXenes) are emerging materials that combine high electrical conductivity, excellent electrochemical properties, and ease of solution processing, making them suitable for constructing multifunctional PEC PDs. Herein, we report the broadband dual-polarity photoelectrochemical photocurrent switching (PEPS) in Ti 3 CNT x MXene/GO operating under a small external bias. We employ a solid-solution Ti 3 CNT x MXene, which exhibits featureless optical absorption and high electrical conductivity, and hybridize it with semiconducting GO, which possesses abundant surface states and a tunable bandgap, to construct PEC PDs that exhibit the PEPS effect. Notably, Ti 3 CNT x /GO heterostructures show excellent bidirectional photoresponse under UV-to-visible light, with the direction of the and responsivity tuned by the Ti 3 CNT x -to-GO ratio. The optimized heterostructure achieves high photoresponsivity values of 0.16 mA/W (cathodic) and 0.45 mA/W (anodic), corresponding to 360-fold and 4-fold enhancements compared to pristine GO and Ti 3 CNT x , respectively. We untangle that the strong PEPS effect is observed due to the role of Ti 3 CNTₓ facilitating efficient charge carrier transfer and interfacial charge separation at the metal/semiconductor interfaces. These intriguing results highlight the potential of MXenes as building blocks for designing highly sensitive optoelectronic devices with the PEPS effect.

papers.title: Patentability of Markush formulae
papers.abstract: Markush formulae play a pivotal role in the field of chemical patent drafting, as they empower applicants to articulate claim families of related compounds that are centered around a shared core structure, accompanied by alternative substituents. However, the breadth of these claims frequently gives rise to patentability challenges before the European Patent Office (EPO), including unity objections during the search process, clarity issues arising from nested definitions, novelty attacks based on overlapping generic disclosures, and challenges under the disclosure-based standards that govern amendments and priority. Utilizing a doctrinal approach that is firmly rooted in the EPO Guidelines and the case law of the Boards of Appeal, this article posits that these doctrines are unified by a singular interpretative anchor point: that which the skilled person derives directly and unambiguously from the patent application as filed. The analysis demonstrates the manner in which this anchor functions as a foundational element in the assessment of unity, the evaluation of novelty within the context of Markush claims, and the analysis of species-focused novelty, encompassing the utilization of multiple-selection "two-list" reasoning. Additionally, it elucidates the rigorous approach to added matter and priority, particularly in the context of diminishing lists and selection inventions. The practical implications for drafting and prosecution are discussed

papers.title: Mapping out the Metabolome: Metabolite Annotation Propagation and Synthesis (MAPS)
papers.abstract: Identification and annotation of unknown metabolites remain a significant challenge in untargeted metabolomics due to the vast chemical diversity and limitations of individual annotation tools. The putative identification of metabolites frequently yields multiple candidate matches, and systematically reviewing annotations from databases such as GNPS and HMDB to determine the most accurate assignment can be a labor-intensive process. Here, we present MAPS (Metabolite Annotation Propagation and Synthesis), an automated annotation workflow that integrates, refines, and extrapolates metabolite annotations from multiple sources within a user-friendly R Shiny application. MAPS leverages the strengths of various data processing and annotation tools used in metabolomics, including MZmine, GNPS2, SIRIUS, and MS2Query, and employs an annotation propagation strategy to enhance coverage, as well as synthesizing annotations across spectral matching and cheminformatic tools to increase annotation confidence, and provide the most exhaustive list of high-confidence metabolites present. One significant advantage to MAPS is its ability to perform compound name standardization, which is not present in any other tool of its kind. To demonstrate its utility, we apply MAPS towards the curation of metabolites from the human gut metabolome; a complex metabolic system for which knowledge-based metabolome annotations tools are currently incapable of interrogating. Such a tool empowers deep metabolome mining in a more accessible, reliable and reproducible manner.

papers.title: Highly Potent Aromatic Isocyanides as Soft Drugs against Methicillin and Vancomycin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Topical Infections
papers.abstract: The increasing spread of multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus calls for new classes of antibacterials with unconventional scaffolds and underexplored functional groups. In this work, we describe a family of highly functionalized synthetic aromatic isocyanides rapidly accessed via multicomponent reactions (Passerini/Ugi) and related modular strategies, enabling efficient exploration of structure–activity relationships. Microbiological screening revealed exceptional potency against S. aureus , with numerous compounds active at low nanomolar concentrations (MICs = 0.03–0.06 μM), maintaining activity against MRSA and VISA/VRSA strains and surpassing the potency of several reference antibacterials. Studies with control compounds demonstrated that the aromatic isocyanide is essential for activity and that potency derives from the overall molecular architecture, consistent with a non-promiscuous SAR profile. The selected lead compounds are predominantly bacteriostatic, inhibit biofilm formation, and display marked selectivity, with low cytotoxicity toward human keratinocytes and fibroblasts (viability >70% up to 64 μM). The presence of an ester functionality enables modulation of metabolic stability, making these compounds suitable as soft drugs for topical use, as evidenced by their rapid plasma hydrolysis to inactive metabolites. Moreover, preliminary in vivo evaluation in Caenorhabditis elegans demonstrated antibacterial activity in the absence of observable cytotoxicity. Finally, in an in vivo murine model of MRSA skin infection, soft-drug candidate 27 significantly reduced bacterial load, showing efficacy comparable to the standard-of-care fusidic acid. Overall, these highly potent aromatic isocyanides define a new class of promising antibacterial agents for topical infections, including those caused by fusidic acid-resistant strains.

papers.title: EXAFS-Resolved Node Asymmetry Links Local Distortions to Lattice Structure in High-Entropy MOFs
papers.abstract: High-entropy materials derive their functionality from chemical complexity, yet this same complexity obscures quantitative understanding of local structure, even when long-range crystallographic order is entropically stabilized. In high-entropy frameworks, local coordination environments are intrinsically heterogeneous, and existing structural descriptions rely largely on ensemble-averaged probes that mask element-specific distortions. Although extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectroscopy provides direct sensitivity to local coordination geometry, its application to chemically complex materials is constrained by overlapping scattering pathways, strong parameter correlations, and limited atomic number contrast. Here, we establish a compositionally resolved and internally calibrated XRD–EXAFS–DFT framework using a model high-entropy metal–organic framework (HE-MOF) platform. A porphyrinic linker is used to construct a three-dimensional hexagonal MOF featuring trinuclear bipyramidal M₃O secondary building units, enabling precise stoichiometric control across mono-, bi-, tri-, and five-metal frameworks incorporating Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, and Zn. Nearly twenty compositions—corresponding to ~50 metal K-edge EXAFS measurements—are systematically interrogated to generate an element-specific description of local coordination environments. This controlled dataset establishes absolute bond-distance baselines, enables quantitative deconvolution of metal–oxygen and metal–metal scattering contributions, and reveals heterometal-induced node-level asymmetry inaccessible by diffraction alone. Density functional theory–optimized SBU geometries provide physically grounded constraints for EXAFS fitting and independently validate the experimentally resolved distortions. High-resolution synchrotron XRD reveals reproducible, composition-dependent lattice-parameter shifts despite conservation of framework topology, demonstrating that local coordination asymmetry propagates coherently to the lattice scale. Stoichiometrically constrained bimetallic nodes define the structural extremes of distortion and bound the heterogeneous local environments observed in tri-metallic and five-metal HE-MOFs. Time-resolved XRD and ICP-MS further reveal that node composition evolves dynamically during synthesis through sequential metal uptake and exchange, a behavior rationalized by molecular dynamics simulations of metal–nitrate precursor coordination. Collectively, this work establishes a quantitative link between node-level asymmetry and lattice-scale response in high-entropy MOFs.

papers.title: Polymer-Encoded Spatial Organization of Antibodies in Complex Coacervates
papers.abstract: Biomolecular condensates organize cellular chemistry without membranes, yet how structurally rigid, multidomain proteins such as antibodies interact with these phases remain poorly understood. In particular, it is unclear whether antibody positioning in synthetic coacervates is governed primarily by bulk electrostatics or by local polymer chemistry. Here we show that subtle differences in polymer functional groups dictate antibody localization in ATP-driven complex coacervates. Immunoglobulin G (IgG) and anti-dinitrophenyl (Anti-DNP) antibodies strongly partitioned into poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDDA)–ATP coacervates, exhibiting homogeneous internal distributions with high partition coefficients (K ≈ 250–450) and rapid fluorescence recovery. In contrast, antibodies were excluded from the interior of poly-L-lysine (PLL)–ATP coacervates and instead accumulated at the interface, forming a kinetically immobilized shell with negligible recovery, despite comparable mesh size and guest permeability. Modulating surface charge, polymer length and solvent conditions did not restore encapsulation, indicating that net electrostatics alone do not determine partitioning. Functionalization of PLL with dinitrophenyl enhanced phase stability but did not promote selective antibody recruitment, as ligands were sequestered within the condensate interior. Together, these findings establish local, multivalent polymer–protein interactions as a dominant determinant of antibody organization in coacervates and provide a design principle for spatially programming complex biomacromolecules in synthetic condensates for diagnostic and therapeutic applications.

papers.title: Evaluating the Validity of In Situ Reference Electrode Measurements in PEM and AEM Water Electrolysers
papers.abstract: Three-electrode cells using in situ reference electrodes enable the deconvolution of the anode and cathode contributions to performance loss in water electrolysers, however, the validity of half-cell potential and impedance measurements is debated. In this work, a reference electrode in contact with the membrane at the edge of the active area was used for reliably testing both proton and anion exchange membrane based cells. The validity of the edge-type configuration was evaluated using a two-dimensional model in conjunction with a series of tests on nominally identical proton exchange membrane cells. Reliable comparison and interpretation of half-cell potential measurements up to 1 A cm -2 was only possible after correcting for ohmic losses using impedance spectroscopy at the same current density to ensure the position of the reference electrode due to anode-cathode misalignment was accounted for. Using this technique, the impact of platinum loading on cathode kinetic and mass transport losses was measured. Reliable impedance up to 0.1 A cm -2 was demonstrated for an anion exchange membrane electrolyser. This three-electrode cell technique presents a robust platform for studying performance losses in both proton and anion exchange membrane water electrolysers

papers.title: Analyzing and Simulating Transient Breakthroughs in Fixed-Bed Adsorbers
papers.abstract: The focus of this article is on the analysis of transient breakthrough experiments measured in laboratory scale units. The scale up of such breakthrough data to industrial scale Pressure Swing Adsorption (PSA) units requires simulations of the adsorption/desorption cycles in a sequence of multiple beds. This article provides a description of the simulation methodology that is essential for interpretation of laboratory scale data, and scaling up. A number of important conclusions are drawn from detailed analysis of large number of experimental breakthrough experiments, along with corresponding simulations. In the event that experimental breakthroughs are "sharp", this is a strong indication of the absence of intra-crystalline diffusion influences. A consequence of intra-crystalline diffusion influences is that breakthrough characteristics attain distended characteristics. Commonly, but not always, distended breakthroughs result in diminished produtivities of the desired product in mixture separation. In exceptional cases, intra-crystalline diffusion serves to complement and enhance the separations dictated by mixture equilibrium thermodynamics; such synergy manifests, for example, for 2MP/22DMB separations in MFI zeolite. For kinetically driven separations of C3H6/C3H8 mixtures using ZIF-8, and KAUST-7, both particle sizes and gas-particle contact times influence separations to a significant extent. The modelling of kinetically driven separations, requires thermodynamic coupling effects to be duly accounted for by use of the Maxwell-Stefan formulation for intra-crystalline diffusion.

papers.title: Decarboxylative Trifluoromethylation of Aliphatic Redox-Active Esters with 2-CF 3 -Benzimidazolium Salt via Copper/Photoredox Catalysis
papers.abstract: The development of methods for constructing C(sp 3)-CF3 bonds from simple, abundant alkyl substrates is of significance but remains less developed. Aliphatic redox-active esters (RAEs), readily derived from aliphatic carboxylic acids, have emerged as versatile platform for bond formation. Their catalytic decarboxylative trifluoromethylation has remained elusive although monofluoromethylation and difluoromethylation were achieved. This is largely due to the lability and low reactivity of conventional nucleophilic trifluoromethylating reagents. Herein, a copper-catalyzed trifluoromethylation of aliphatic N-hydroxyphthalimide (NHPI) esters using a

papers.title: High-Throughput Experimentation on Oxide Photocatalyst: From Large-Scale Screening to Kinetic Insights
Boosting Formic Acid Production in Methane Oxidation by Zeolite Confined Single-site Rh Catalyst
papers.abstract: The selective oxidation of methane to value-added oxygenates remains a long-standing challenge in catalysis, often constrained by poor reactivity (and single-pass methane conversion) and limited product selectivity. Here, we report a Rh-Beta catalyst featuring atomically dispersed Rh δ+ species embedded in the aluminosilicate *BEA zeolite matrix that enables highly selective methane oxidation in a CH4-O2-CO-H2O system. This catalyst achieves a remarkable formic acid space-time yield of 210 mol/molRh/h at 7.84% methane conversion, with formic acid selectivity of 96%-surpassing all previously reported catalyst systems. Mechanistic investigations combining spectroscopy and theory reveal that hydroxyl radicals, generated via acid-promoted water-gas shift and in situ H2-O2 reactions, are responsible for methane activation, while the zeolite backbone plays a vital role in stabilizing formaldehyde intermediate and promoting its further oxidation to formic acid product. This work offers a new approach to overcoming the conversion-selectivity trade-off in methane oxidation and provides a promising route toward industrially viable direct methane upgrading.

papers.title: Engineering thermoresponsive biointerfaces using graft-to strategies: connecting polymer architecture to temperature-dependent surface wettability
papers.abstract: Temperature-responsive substrates provide a promising strategy for addressing issues in biomaterials design, but their utility hinges on achieving predictable, tunable surface response through deliberate thermoresponsive polymer design. Here, we investigate how varying polymer architecture, namely, surface attachment point density and chain length, influence wettability above and below the lower critical solution temperature (LCST) and magnitude of temperature-driven contact angle change of polymer-grafted glass surfaces. Using random copolymers of thermoresponsive di(ethylene glycol) methyl ether methacrylate (DEGMA) units and surface attachment point aminoethyl methacrylate (AEMA) units, we show that increasing polymer attachment point density from 2 to 30 mol% while holding degree of polymerization constant decreases the magnitude of the temperature-driven contact angle change from 15.2 ± 0.5 to 5.7 ± 0.03º. This suggests higher attachment point densities produce compact polymer loop structures on the surface that constrain thermoresponsive units and hinder hydration below the LCST. In contrast, increasing the degree of polymerization from 49 to 350 at a constant attachment point density increases the magnitude of contact angle shift from 7.4 ± 4.4 to 22 ± 2.2º, likely attributed to enhanced chain mobility with increasing chain length. Notably, all surfaces converge to approximately the same contact angle above the LCST, regardless of polymer architecture, likely owing to the formation of similarly collapsed, dehydrated polymer layers that present comparable surface compositions to the interface. This work demonstrates polymer architectures that allow greater chain mobility, achieved through lower attachment point density or longer chain length, produce larger thermal surface responses below the LCST, driven by enhanced hydration. By linking polymer loop structure and chain mobility to surface behavior, these insights provide a framework for designing biointerfaces with predictable and tunable properties.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights into Magnetic Field-Induced OER Enhancement via Magnetization Cycle Analysis
papers.abstract: Disentangling non-spin-dependent and spin-dependent contributions to magnetic field-induced oxygen evolution reaction (OER) enhancement remains challenging due to the difficulty in quantifying magnetic flux density near catalytic surfaces, which depends on both the applied field and the intrinsic magnetic properties of the catalyst. Herein, 2:17-type samarium-cobalt magnets (Sm 2 Co 17 ) with different initial magnetization states were evaluated in an electromagnet-integrated flow cell, employing magnetization cycle analysis to elucidate how intrinsic magnetic properties and magnetization state influence OER enhancement. Analysis of the potential shift (ΔE) throughout a complete magnetization cycle reveals butterfly-shaped hysteresis, with characteristic loop features providing mechanistic insights. Bulk magnetic properties influence the loop contour via spin-pinning effects, whereas surface composition and magnetization state govern the linear ΔE shifts. The slope (κ) of the linear ΔE shifts serves as a descriptor of the catalytic surface response to magnetic field, enabling ΔE determination at a given field strength. Together, κ and the butterfly-shaped loop characteristics provide a potential analytical framework for quantifying magnetic field-induced OER enhancement and may offer insights into the magnetic properties of catalytic surfaces that emerge exclusively under OER conditions.

papers.title: Deciphering the effect of electrostatic interactions on a Polyelectrolyte star: A theoretical approach
papers.abstract: In this article, I tackle the long-standing problem of the Polyelectrolyte stars in thermal equilibrium. By combining the DFT and the PET methods I calculate the density profile, electric potential and charge distribution of the star and its counterions in the regions inside and outside the star. My calculations strongly suggests that upon variation of the Bjerrum length or the strength of the electrostatic interactions, the Manning condensation takes place in the Polyelectrolyte stars. However, this transition is not discontinuous as it is seen in the Polyelectrolyte brushes. This finding proves that the nature of the phase transitions is completely linked to the geometry and symmetry of the system. My results show that spherically symmetric structures like stars undergo a continuous Manning condensation which might have some potential applications in medicine, technology and industry.

papers.title: Vibrationally Mediated Coherent Energy Exchange in Plexcitonic Nanomaterials
papers.abstract: Harnessing strong light-matter coupling to manipulate molecular dynamics is a central goal in modern photonics. Hybrid light-matter states—plexcitons—arising from the interaction between plasmonic and excitonic modes provide a powerful route toward this goal, yet how molecular vibrations influence their coherent dynamics remains elusive. Here, we use femtosecond two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy to directly resolve vibronic interactions in plexcitonic nanostructures formed by cyanine molecular aggregates coupled to gold nanorods. We observe long-lived quantum beatings that evolve from vibronic plexcitonic coherences into vibrational coherences of predominantly excitonic nature following plasmonic relaxation. This behavior reveals that molecular vibrational modes are not quenched under strong coupling but actively sustain coherent energy exchange across the disordered plexcitonic manifoldparticularly between lower plexciton and the exciton reservoir region. The excitonic component supports vibronic coherence formation, while the plasmonic admixture facilitates their generation and delocalization. Our findings identify vibronic coupling as a central mechanism governing light-matter interactions at the nanoscale, unveiling new routes to control coherence, Raman activity, and energy transport in strongly coupled plexcitonic nanostructures.

papers.title: Revisiting the Crystal Structure of Metal-Organic Framework UTSA-16 for Chemical Consistency
papers.abstract: The metal-organic framework UTSA-16, based on K + , Co 2+ and citrate as the organic linker and first reported in 2005, is one of the most attractive candidates as a solid adsorbent for post-combustion CO 2 capture. Here, we revisit the crystal structure of UTSA-16 on the basis of clear evidence that the amount of potassium has been systematically underestimated in previous literature reports dealing with crystallographic characterization. By combining CHN elemental analysis, inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy and thermogravimetric analysis, we find that the actual chemical formula for UTSA-16 is K 2 Co 3 (cit) 2 ꞏ8H 2 O, with a K/Co ratio twice as large as the one assumed in previous literature. Single crystal X-ray diffraction analysis leads to identifying two extraframework positions occupied by previously overlooked K + ions, which are likely to play a key role in the adsorption behavior of UTSA-16.

papers.title: Concentration without complexity: enhancing stationary photoelectrochemical reactor performance with diffuse light concentrating optics
papers.abstract: Integrating concentrating solar optics with photoelectrochemical (PEC) reactors can increase reaction rates without relying on large-area photoelectrodes, which typically exhibit lower efficiencies due to resistive losses. However, concentrating optics can increase balance-of-system complexity because optical efficiency is sensitive to incidence angle, with imaging optics, such as convex lenses, requiring precise solar tracking to avoid rapid misalignment. Herein, we integrated a low concentration (2.9×) non-imaging crossed-compound parabolic concentrator (CCPC) with a PEC reactor. First, we evaluated irradiance and incidence angle dependence in the laboratory, then coupled the reactor with c-Si PVs and validated in dynamic outdoor conditions. Finally, the results were translated into annual H 2 yield predictions and life cycle assessment (LCA). The CCPC (± 30° half-angle acceptance), was resilient to wide incidence angles, enabling higher photocurrent densities than the non-concentrated baseline up to ≈50°. At 1000 W m -2 and normal incidence the CCPC-integrated PEC reactor delivered a water oxidation photocurrent density at 1.23 V RHE of 3.95 mA cm -2 compared to 1.40 mA cm -2 without the optic (2.82× increase). Alongside wide-angle resilience, the CCPC-integrated reactor had a near-linear relationship between irradiance and photocurrent, supporting operation at variable irradiances. The CCPC-integrated reactor consistently delivered higher photocurrents than the non-concentrated system. Compared with convex lens integration, the CCPC showed increased resilience to changeable weather conditions, concentrating diffuse sunlight to a greater extent. Translating laboratory behaviours into a seasonal performance model of a 20 m 2 PEC demonstration further supported CCPC integration, predicting a 70% higher hydrogen production yield for a stationary CCPC-integrated reactor than a non-concentrated reactor with azimuth tracking. LCA showed CCPC integration reduced key midpoint impacts, including global warming potential, terrestrial ecotoxicity and fossil resource scarcity, by 20-70%, compared with a non-concentrated baseline. Overall, this work provides a proof-of-concept for CCPC-integrated PEC reactors, enabling a pathway to PEC scale-up using non-imaging optics to enhance performance without a complex balance-of-system.

papers.title: A reproducible integrating sphere method for standardised diffuse light characterisation of photoelectrochemical and photovoltaic devices
papers.abstract: Testing photoelectrochemical and photovoltaic devices under realistic operating conditions is a critical phase of system development. However, most studies still focus on standard AM 1.5G tests at one sun (1000 W m -2 ) irradiance with direct collimated light beams, which does not capture outdoor operation under broad angular illumination from diffuse skies and low solar elevation. Outdoor field trials are difficult to benchmark reproducibly due to the unpredictable nature of outdoor environments. Herein, we demonstrate a simple, laboratory-based method for generating reproducible, angularly broad “quasi-diffuse” illumination by coupling a continuous solar simulator to an integrating sphere. By positioning a photoelectrochemical device at the integrating sphere exit aperture, we produce a controlled quasi-diffuse illumination geometry and demonstrate its use in two case studies involving WO 3 |BiVO 4 |NiFeOOH photoanodes: one with a planar architecture and another coupled with a crossed-compound parabolic concentrator (CCPC) with wide-angle acceptance, designed to harvest diffuse and off-normal light. After normalisation to one-sun equivalent irradiance, the non-concentrating (planar) configuration performed similarly under direct and quasi-diffuse irradiance, whereas the CCPC-coupled configuration retained ≈ 30% of the direct-illumination photocurrent under quasi-diffuse conditions, consistent with acceptance-angle limited concentration. This method can be extended to any photoelectrode, photovoltaic or other photo-absorber, provided that its dimensions are compatible with the exit aperture of the integrating sphere. This work provides a practical, controllable and transferable framework for quasi-diffuse light characterisation that can be easily benchmarked across different research teams and will complement existing AM 1.5G measurements. This also offers a simple way to assess diffuse light tolerance, wide-angle acceptance and to validate ray tracing models using readily available laboratory equipment. This enables a straightforward test to assess the viability of device architectures in the laboratory before embarking on more challenging field trials.

papers.title: Cyclic Sulfamates through [5+1] Cyclization of Sulfuryl Fluoride and Salicylic Amides: Synthesis and Chemical Transformations
papers.abstract: An efficient sulfuryl fluoride-enabled synthesis of benzo[e][1,2,3]oxathiazine-4(3H)-one-2,2-dioxides from salicylic amides is described. Salicylamides were prepared on a multigram scale, and the corresponding cyclic sulfamates were synthesized via operationally simple one-pot Et3N-promoted [5+1] cyclization. In some cases, intermediate products of O-sulfonylation (fluorosulfates) were isolated. The method was suitable for both primary and secondary salicylic amides, albeit the use of a stronger base was necessary for sterically hindered substrates. The synthetic utility of the obtained heterocycles were demonstrated by their further chemical transformations. In particular, 4-chloro derivatives were obtained by deoxochlorination and converted into various cyclic aminosulfamates on a multigram scale. Derivatives bearing a bromine atom in the benzene ring were subjected to Pd-catalyzed couplings without affecting the sulfamate ring. Physicochemical properties of a representative virtual library derived from the synthesized scaffolds met the criteria of lead-likeness guidelines.

papers.title: Aggregation-Free Solution-Phase Kinetic Dissection of Donor-Dependent NIR Exciplex Emission in a Perylene Diimide
papers.abstract: Exciplex formation between molecular donors and acceptors underpins a wide range of charge-transfer photophysical phenomena, yet its intrinsic kinetics and emissive behavior are often obscured by aggregation effects, particularly in perylene diimide (PDI)-based systems. Here we present a spectroscopic aggregation-free, solution-phase kinetic dissection of donor-dependent near-infrared (NIR) exciplex emission in a model PDI acceptor, N,N'-bis(ethylpropyl)perylene-3,4,9,10-tetracarboxylic diimide (EP-PDI). By rigorously establishing a spectroscopic monomeric benchmark for EP-PDI in toluene and restricting donor concentrations to the diffusion-limited regime, we isolate intrinsic exciplex formation and decay processes with pyrene and anthracene donors. Time-resolved measurements reveal diffusion-limited photoinduced electron transfer for both donors, while exciplex emission lifetimes and intensities exhibit pronounced donor dependence. Notably, faster exciplex formation does not translate into higher emissive efficiency. Long-range corrected DFT calculations reproduce the relative exciplex emission energies and oscillator-strength trends, providing a consistent electronic-structure framework in which the donor-dependent emissive gap (EP-PDI LUMO versus exciplex HOMO) governs the exciplex emission energy. A reduced emissive gap correlates with enhanced nonradiative deactivation, explaining the diminished emissive efficiency. These results demonstrate that exciplex emissive performance is controlled by a balance between formation kinetics and excited-state decay pathways, establishing a robust spectroscopic reference for understanding donordependent NIR exciplex emission in solution.

papers.title: An artificial intelligence approach for prediction of hole taper in Nd: YAG laser drilling on thermoplastic material reinforced by glass fiber
papers.abstract: Laser drilling is an efficient technique for producing intrinsic holes with a diameter of less than 1mm. The critical parameters affecting laser power in a pulse mode of Nd: YAG laser drilling are pulse current, pulse duration, assist gas pressure and workpiece thickness. This study explores an artificial intelligence (AI) technique to forecast the hole taper of Nd: YAG laser drilling. The data acquired from Taguchi's L27 orthogonal array experiment were employed to construct an artificial neural network (ANN) model. The hole taper was represented mathematically as an explicit nonlinear function of the chosen input parameters. Studies have shown that ANNs can be successfully used to analyze the influence of laser drilling parameters on the hole taper produced by Nd: YAG laser drilling on GFRP material. Compared to the experimental outcome data set, the predictive ANN model based on 4-6-1 architecture had the lowest error (MSE=0.001) and an absolute average percentage error of less than 8.94%.

papers.title: Tunable exciton-polariton modes in WS₂ nanotubes: nearfield insights and nanocomposite photonic applications
papers.abstract: Over the last decade, nanostructures that support exciton–polaritons (EPs) have attracted considerable attention due to their distinctive optical properties and technological promise. WS₂ nanotubes (NTs) sustain strong EP coupling under ambient conditions without external cavities. Quasi-one-dimensional systems enable radius-dependent tuning of light–matter interactions, which evolve from excitonic to polaritonic regimes. Scattering scanning near-field optical microscopy (s-SNOM) imaging of an individual NT reveals intricate coupling among surface-bound waves and the evanescent field at the structure–substrate interface. To disentangle these contributions and assess waveguiding characteristics, s-SNOM observations are combined with finite-difference time-domain simulations of nanowires with varied refractive indices (RIs). Geometric resonances emerge at RI = 2, optical cavity dominates at RI = 4, whereas the dielectric response of WS 2 induces EP modes. Radius-dependent simulations show a transition from a geometric mode at small diameters to a two-mode regime governed by a strong EP contribution. Polarization-resolved analysis demonstrates enhanced coupling when incident radiation aligns with the NT axis. Surface-bound waves radiate efficiently into the surrounding medium, evidenced by long-range propagation of the evanescent waves and pronounced interference features on their crests. Embedding WS 2 NTs within polydimethylsiloxane produces flexible nanocomposite fibers exhibiting high quality factors, supporting tunable nanolaser platforms.

papers.title: Creep-Resistant, Extrudable, and Recyclable Polyolefin Covalent Adaptable Networks Incorporating Azine Cross-Links via Reactive Processing
papers.abstract: Polyolefins, encompassing polymers such as polyethylene (PE) and ethylene-based copolymers, are the world's most widely produced class of plastics due to their versatility and facile property tunability. Although these materials are recyclable, in practice their recycling rates are low due to a range of issues, including thermomechanical degradation. Furthermore, converting

papers.title: Synthesis of multisubstituted thiosulfonates from o-silylaryl triflates via halothiolation of aryne intermediates followed by oxidative S-sulfonylation
papers.abstract: An efficient method for preparing aryl thiosulfonates through aryne intermediates is disclosed. Following aryne halothiolation with potassium xanthate, the resulting aryl xanthates were transformed into thiosulfonates using iodine and sodium sulfinates. The versatility of thiosulfonates together with divergent aryne precursors enabled the access to a wide range of highly functionalized organosulfur compounds.

papers.title: Research Progress on Smo Inhibitors of the Hedgehog Signaling Pathway
papers.abstract: The Hedgehog (Hh) signaling pathway plays a pivotal role in embryonic development, tissue homeostasis, and the initiation and progression of various malignancies. Aberrant activation of the Hh signaling pathway serves as a crucial driver in numerous cancers, including basal cell carcinoma, medulloblastoma, and pancreatic cancer. Smoothened (Smo), a core transmembrane receptor within the Hh signaling cascade, acts as a key node for pathway activation and thus represents an important target for the development of Hh pathway inhibitors. Since the approval of the first Smo inhibitor vismodegib in 2012, remarkable progress has been achieved in the research and development of Smo-targeting agents. This review comprehensively summarizes the research advances of Smo inhibitors in the Hh signaling pathway, covering the latest applications of approved drugs, emerging trends of clinical-stage investigational agents (notably the breakthrough of taladegib in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis), mechanisms of drug resistance and corresponding countermeasures, as well as the potential applications of Smo inhibitors in non-neoplastic diseases. Through in-depth analysis of these advances, this review aims to provide novel perspectives and insights for the treatment of Hh signaling pathway-related disorders.

papers.title: Fast computation of exact symmetry-corrected RMSD of conformers
Li-ion Battery Recycling by Energy-Efficient, High Throughput Li2SO4 Salt Splitting in a Diaphragm Flow Cell
papers.abstract: Rapidly growing demand for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) necessitates a significant expansion of LIB recycling to ensure adequate supply and avoid waste buildup. Traditional hydrometallurgical LIB recycling processes use super-stoichiometric quantities of acid and base and generate large volumes of salt waste which pose an environmental burden. Electrochemical regeneration of acid and base from salt offers a zero-waste alternative but faces challenges with respect to throughput and energy consumption, with current densities typically limited to ≤ 100 mA/cm 2 and energy demands > 0.10 kWh/mol. These limitations stem from a reliance on ion exchange membranes (IEMs), which lead to high cell resistance. This study reports a hydrometallurgical process to recycle lithium cobalt oxide (LCO) and lithium nickel manganese cobalt oxide (NMC) cathodes using acid and base electrochemically generated from a Li 2 SO 4 electrolyte. The electrochemical cell used contains no IEMs, enabling excellent energy efficiency between 0.033 - 0.097 kWh/mol at current densities up to 500 mA/cm 2 and imparting a robust tolerance for impurities that typically foul IEMs. The produced acid and base are found to be competent for etching and recovering > 90% of the valuable metals from LIBs at industrially relevant pulp densities up to 66 g/L, and are readily regenerated from the salt solution left at the end of the metal recovery process.

papers.title: Engineering Highly Active PtMo Bimetallic Catalyst for Low-temperature Reverse Water Gas Shift
papers.abstract: Reverse water gas shift (RWGS) reaction is a promising route for CO 2 utilization, providing a versatile syngas component for downstream process such as methanol synthesis and Fischer-Tropsch chemistry. Low-temperature (< 400 o C) RWGS offers reduced energy demand and enables process intensification, yet remains highly challenging. Herein, we report a PtMo@SiO₂ catalyst, synthesized via Surface Organometallic Chemistry (SOMC), that achieves near-equilibrium CO₂ conversion at 300 °C (GHSV = 60000 mL/g cat /h, 1 bar). The catalyst exhibits CO formation rates over two orders of magnitude higher than Pt@SiO₂ at 200 °C and ca. 30-fold higher at 300 °C. Spectroscopic studies, including CO/CO₂-IR, in situ XAS, gas switching and CO-TPD DRIFTS, reveal that partially reduced Mo(IV) interfacial sites on silica promote CO₂ adsorption, while Mo(0) in PtMo alloys facilitate the activation of CO 2 and CO desorption, jointly enhancing Low-temperature RWGS performance.

papers.title: HHT: A Polymer Property Prediction Framework Leveraging Natural Language
papers.abstract: Predicting the macroscopic properties of polymers solely from 1D chemical sequences (e.g., SMILES) is inherently an ill-posed problem, as it neglects critical higher-order factors such as chain topology, condensed-state morphology, and processing history. To bridge this "semantic gap" between low-level structural representations and high-level physical functionalities, we propose HHT (Highly Hybrid Text), a novel framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) into polymer property prediction. HHT employs a dual-stream architecture that synergizes implicit topological features extracted by a pre-trained chemical language model (PolyBERT) with explicit mechanistic reasoning generated by a scientific LLM. A dynamic Adaptive Gating Mechanism is introduced to weigh the contribution of structural versus semantic features based on task-specific dependencies. Extensive evaluations on seven benchmark datasets demonstrate that HHT outperforms many baseline models. Crucially, HHT transforms the traditional "black-box" fitting paradigm into a "whitebox" interpretable system. We first validate the model's focus on mechanistic logic via semantic attention visualization, confirming its ability to prioritize physical descriptors over statistical noise. Furthermore, through counterfactual sensitivity analysis, we demonstrate that the model correctly infers property shifts induced by textual morphological perturbations, demonstrating that natural language can serve as a high-dimensional, physically consistent feature modality for materials science.

papers.title: Tracing Emissions and Impacts of Legacy and Emerging PFAS on Aquatic and Terrestrial Ecosystems from the Fluoropolymer Production Plant at Spinetta Marengo (Italy)
papers.abstract: Perfluoropolymer manufacturing is a major source of non-polymeric PFAS to the ecosystems. The environmental release, transport, and fate of both legacy and emerging PFAS emitted by the fluoropolymer plant in Spinetta Marengo (Northern Italy), one of the main fluoropolymer production facilities in Europe, have been investigated by using a systematic and spatially resolved multimedia approach. Legacy PFAS (e.g., PFOA) and emerging substitutes, including C6O4 and the Cl-PFPECA mixture were measured in wastewaters, river waters, atmospheric depositions, sediments, soils, vegetation, earthworm, fish, and bird eggs, enabling a coherent reconstruction of emission pathways, impact on the vicinity of the plant, long-range transport, deposition mechanisms, and trophic transfer both in aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems. In particular, the significantly different concentrations of legacy and emerging PFAS in eggs of two species (Great tit, Starling) were correlated with the different feeding behavior of the wild bird and demonstrated that PFOA, even though it has been replaced since 2013. is still present in the terrestrial trophic chain. Integrated multi-media analyses demonstrate that emerging PFAS exhibit environmental persistence, mobility, and bioaccumulation patterns broadly analogous to those of regulated legacy compounds, providing critical evidence relevant to current regulatory discussions on regrettable substitution and essential-use frameworks.

papers.title: Intramolecular oxygen coupling mediates water oxidation on an oxide electrocatalyst
papers.abstract: Understanding the mechanistic pathways of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is essential for guiding the design of catalytic materials and advancing sustainable energy technologies, as sluggish OER kinetics remain a major limitation. Here, using 18 O isotope labeling experiments, we provide kinetic evidence for oxygen coupling occurring within the lattice of a Bi 0.2 Sr 0.8 CoO 3-δ perovskite catalyst, unveiling an OER pathway distinct from conventional mechanisms and closely analogous to that of Photosystem II. We demonstrate that oxygen-to-metal charge transfer drives the spontaneous formation of oxidized lattice oxygen species, including molecular O 2 -like dimers confined within the crystal lattice, which represent the key catalytic intermediate during oxygen evolution on a highly active cobalt-containing oxide catalyst.

papers.title: Synthesis of α-Chiral Ketones by Ni-Catalyzed Regio- and Enantioselective Hydroacylation of Alkenes with Acid Chlorides
Synthesis-aware design rules for ammonia decomposition on Co-Ir-Ni-Rh-Ru alloys via segregation and surface-entropy retention
papers.abstract: Finite-temperature segregation can decouple bulk and surface entropy in multicomponent alloys, reshaping the active-site ensemble and complicating catalyst design. Using ammonia decomposition (ADR) as a mechanistically grounded case, we establish a synthesis-aware CE-MMC-microkinetic framework that maps annealingtemperature surface statistics to surface-averaged rates across Ru-based multicomponent catalysts. A single-descriptor volcano based on *N-hcp adsorption (ΔE(*N)) links temperature-dependent step statistics to activity, while a strain correction enables consistent screening across compositions. MMC simulations predict Ni/Rh surface enrichment and Ru subsurface partitioning, depressing the activity of equimolar alloys after annealing despite high rates in the randomly mixed limit. Highthroughput composition-activity maps at 1500 K reveal Ru-rich activity belts with maxima up to ~1.4-1.5× the Ru benchmark, and we quantify the surface configurational entropy (ΔSconf) of the annealed surface to assess synthesis-temperature disorder retention. Notably, the high-⟨TOF⟩ belts overlap elevated-ΔSconf windows, enabling a two-objective compositional filter that jointly prioritizes ADR activity and surface disorder retention. Local-environment statistics show that moderate-Ru step sites most frequently realize near-optimal ΔE(*N). The maps suggest that minimal Rh/Ir doping (~5-10%) maximizes activity and 40-60% Co/Ni substitution reduces noble-metal loading without sacrificing performance. Disorder-preserving syntheses (e.g., short high-temperature exposure followed by rapid quenching) shift the high-activity belts toward lower noble-metal contents, yielding an actionable, cost-aware blueprint for ADR catalyst design.

papers.title: Red-to-NIR luminescent trinuclear gold(I) complexes with exceptionally wide liquid crystalline temperature range
papers.abstract: Luminescent trinuclear Au(I) complexes integrated into liquid crystalline (LC) frameworks provide a promising platform for developing anisotropic and stimuli-responsive soft materials. However, simultaneously achieving LC phase stability over a wide temperature range and phosphorescence under ambient conditions remains a challenge. Herein, we employed a combined linker and side-chain engineering strategy to tune the LC behaviour and photophysical properties of pyrazole-based cyclic trinuclear Au(I) complexes. Structural modulation was achieved by introducing flexible alkyl side chains of varying length and branching through ester linkages. The structure-property relationships of the Au(I) complexes were systematically investigated in the context of functional soft material design. The alkyl substituents exerted a pronounced influence on thermal behaviour: alkyl chain branching effectively lowered the melting temperature, while incorporation of ester linkages raised the LC-to-isotropic transition temperature. As a result of this synergistic effect, the complex bearing the longest branched alkyl side chain exhibited an exceptionally wide LC temperature window spanning more than 300 °C. In the LC state, all complexes selfassembled into a hexagonal columnar mesophase and displayed aggregation-induced emission behaviour. Alkyl chain substitution did not significantly affect the emission wavelength and excited-state lifetime but markedly enhanced the thermodynamic stability of the complexes. Thus, thermal and LC properties are governed primarily by molecular design, whereas photoluminescence characteristics are dictated by the aggregate structure. These findings highlight linker and side-chain engineering as an effective strategy for independently modulating the liquid crystallinity, thermal stability, and luminescence of Au(I)-based soft luminescent materials.

papers.title: Mechanochemical and aging-based amidation of bulk and nanowhisker chitosan via water-catalyzed carbodiimide coupling
papers.abstract: SYNOPSIS. Liquid-assisted grinding with water enables catalytic coupling of carboxylic acids to chitosan amines via solid-state carbodiimide mechanochemistry.

papers.title: Photosynthetic room-temperature reducton of nitrogen to ammonia using natural seawater
papers.abstract: We report that the use of inexpensive iron(II) salts to produce solvated electrons upon irradiation with UV light can be coupled to the Mo-catalyzed nitrogen reduction process to afford ammonia from the oxidation of water with a quantum yield of 5.2 % at rt, pH 4, and 1 bar of nitrogen. The aqueous Fe(III) ions produced during the course of the reaction also absorb UV light and undergo reduction back to Fe(II) with the release of hydroxyl radicals which eventually form water and oxygen, thus coupling water oxidation with nitrogen reduction. The overall process is shown to be insensitive to the presence of oxygen or high concentrations of salt and can be run in unpurified seawater or in ambient air to reduce atmospheric nitrogen. At room temperature, the rate-determining step was found to express [N 2 ] 1/2 , consistent with a rate-limiting process involving the dimerization of the intermediate [Mo]-NH 3 species.
