The efficiency is thus limited by the solubility of nitrogen in water, which can be circumvented by the use of medium to high pressures of dinitrogen (100 – 200 bar) to reach photochemical quantum yields of 10.8 % (i.e. with a reduction efficiency > 80% considering that three electrons are needed per ammonia molecule and a further three for regenerating the Fe(II) salt through water oxidation). The net reaction, supported by H 2 18 O and 15 N 2 isotope labelling, is that water is oxidized to H + and O 2 while N 2 is reduced to NH 3 . The unexpectedly high selectivity of N 2 vs. H + reduction is interpreted on the basis of transient absorption spectroscopy evidencing diffusion-controlled quenching of the solvated electrons by the Mo catalyst. Coupling nitrogen reduction with water oxidation is calculated to be endoergonic by ∆ G 0 = +329.2 kJ/mol, which is offset by the energy of the photons absorbed in agreement with a photosynthetic process possessing an experimentally-determined efficiency of light-to-chemical energy conversion reaching 7.6%.

papers.title: An Iron Complex Bound to Bent Pyrazine Ring
papers.abstract: N-heteroarenes predominantly bind transition-metals as σ-donors via nitrogen lone pair, while their capacity as π-ligating, redox non-innocent ligands remains underexplored, particularly toward earth-abundant metals. Herein, by anchoring pyrazine and triazine in polyphosphine scaffolds, we unveil the ability of those polyazines to stabilize low-valent iron as π-ligand, leading to the discovery of previously unknown coordination modes and metal-ligand redox chemistry. Reaction of pyrazine-anchored diphosphine 1 with Fe(PMe3)4 affords diamagnetic (1)Fe(PMe3) (3, S = 0), as a result of oxidative cyclometallation of Fe(0) and the azadiene moiety of pyrazine. Crystallographic, 57 Fe Mössbauer spectroscopic and computational analyses reveal a low-spin Fe(II) center in distorted octahedral geometry bound to a formal two-electron reduced pyrazine in an unprecedented η 4-binding mode. In contrast, the reaction of triazine-anchored triphosphine 2 with Fe(PMe3)4 yields paramagnetic (2)Fe(PMe3) (4, S = 1), featuring tetrahedral geometry and a rare η 2-triazine as π-ligand. These divergent outcomes underscore the geometric constraints imposed by the phosphine donors dictate the hapticity and redox participation of the N-heteroarene core. Preliminary studies reveal that both 3 and 4 serve as competent precatalysts for dehydrogenative borylation of alkene.

papers.title: Transition Mechanism of the Human Dopamine Transporter via Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.abstract: Dopamine reuptake by the human dopamine transporter (hDAT) is driven by Na⁺/Cl⁻ coupled alternating access, yet the detailed transition mechanism between outwardfacing, occluded, and inward-facing states has remained elusive. Leveraging recently resolved hDAT structures and extensive molecular dynamics simulations, we construct the complete Markov State Model of the hDAT transport cycle. This analysis resolves three novel key intermediates states: Macrostate 5, an extracellular (EC) gate-closure intermediate; Macrostate 4, the kinetic bottleneck corresponding to the ion-release and dopamine-reorientation state; and Macrostate 1, the earliest outward-facing reset state that reopens the EC gate. Together, these intermediates define a sequential transport mechanism: Na2 release → Transmembrane1a helix (TM1a) tilt → intracellular gate opening → Na1 release → dopamine rotation → water influx → dopamine release → Cl release → outward-facing reset. This unified pathway integrates all known transporter conformations into a single continuous mechanism. The structural logic of these intermediates rationalizes longstanding mutational phenotypes and reveals new targets for probing gating kinetics and therapeutic modulation. Together, our results provide the first complete molecular blueprint of Na⁺/Cl⁻-coupled dopamine transport.

papers.title: Tackling Real-World Crystal Structure Prediction from Powder X-ray Diffraction Data
papers.abstract: Crystal structure prediction (CSP) from powder diffraction data is a central challenge in materials chemistry. Machine learning (ML) models show promise, but most are trained on idealized simulated data, limiting reliability on real experiments. Here, we assess real-world behaviour using deCIFer as a representative case. deCIFer is an autoregressive transformer that conditions each step of structure generation on encoded PXRD data, guiding token-wise predictions of space group, lattice parameters, and atomic positions. Using controlled robustness tests, we quantify performance under realistic artefacts (noise, background, peak asymmetry, and Scherrer broadening) and introduce metrics for accuracy and predictive uncertainty. deCIFer adapts smoothly to signal distortions and improves over unconditioned baselines when diffraction features remain informative, while expressing appropriate uncertainty as the PXRD pattern becomes underdetermined. Tests on experimental PXRD show recovery of known structures but also highlight limitations for lower-symmetry and nanocrystalline samples. Overall, ML-based CSP is fundamentally limited by the information content of PXRD, but can accelerate expert workflows by rapidly generating chemically plausible candidates and quantifying uncertainty, making such models valuable human-in-the-loop tools for real-world structure determination.

papers.title: A Planar N,P-Heteroindeno[1,2-b]fluorene as Phosphine-stabilized Pyrazine Dication
papers.abstract: Stabilizing oxidized pyrazine motifs in a cationic state within a conjugated scaffold is rare but attractive for redox-responsive molecular materials. We report a planar N,P-heteroindeno[1,2-b]fluorene dication 2 formed by two-electron oxidative cyclization of pyrazine-anchored diphosphine 1. X-ray diffraction analysis shows a centrosymmetric, planar fused pentacyclic framework containing two annulated P-N five-membered rings and a formally "pyrazine dication" unit ligated by two phosphorus centers. Bond metrics and atomic dipole moment-corrected Hirshfeld (ADCH) charges indicate phosphoruscentered oxidation coupled to increased dihydropyrazine-like character within the pyrazine ring. Dication 2 exhibits a near-UV absorption band at 367 nm consistent with TD-DFT-assigned π→π* excitation and a calculated HOMO-LUMO gap of 3.27 eV. Cyclic voltammetry of 2 shows an irreversible reduction wave at-1.92 V vs. Fc +/0 ; nevertheless, chemical reduction using two equivalents of potassium graphite cleanly regenerates 1, consistent with an E-C-(E) sequence.

papers.title: Quantifying Basis-Dependent Force Errors in KS-DFT Transition-State Modeling
papers.abstract: Transition-state geometries optimized with modest basis sets are routinely combined with higher-level single-point energy calculations to estimate reaction barriers. This approach assumes that the optimized structure remains a stationary point on the higher-level potential energy surface. Here, we show that this assumption can fail in a reaction-dependent manner: basis-set changes induce systematic residual gradients at nominal transition-states, even when electronic barriers appear numerically well converged. By analyzing the magnitude and direction of these gradients, including their projection onto the imaginary mode, we demonstrate that basis-set effects can shift the transition-state location and persist even when electronic energies appear well converged. These results reveal a hidden source of uncertainty in common opt-small/single-point-big workflows and motivate gradient-based diagnostics alongside energy benchmarks.

papers.title: Leveraging Mechanism-Based Inhibition to Enable the Engineering of Enzymatic Activity towards Polyurethane
papers.abstract: Polyurethane (PU) is widely used due to its low-cost production, stability and structural versatility. However, due to inadequate waste management, the widespread use of this material has raised environmental concerns. Recently, academic and industrial efforts have been made to discover enzymes capable of depolymerizing PU. Nevertheless, the enzymes discovered to date lack sufficient efficiency and stability for industrial implementation, requiring further engineering. In

papers.title: Spin Crossover in a Fe(II) Complex with a Radical Iminosemiquinonate Ligand
papers.abstract: Metal complexes that exhibit spin crossover (SCO)-a reversible interconversion between lowspin (LS) and high-spin (HS) states-or valence tautomerism (VT)-an intramolecular electron transfer between a metal center and a redox-active ligand-are promising candidates for molecular materials for sensing, display, and spintronic applications. In an exploration of the

papers.title: Deprotonative Single Electron Oxidation as a General and Controllably Selective Platform for Benzylic C-H Functionalization
papers.abstract: We propose a new strategy for benzyl radical generation through a consecutive deprotonation and single electron oxidation mechanism. The use of HMDS bases generates low concentrations of benzyl carbanionic intermediates that are oxidized and subsequently captured using two equivalents of the persistent aminoxyl radical reagent TEMPO. Compared to traditional oxidation reactions of stoichiometrically prepared carbanionic species, transient carbanion generation ensures selective radical coupling over dimerization and enables a major improvement in functional group tolerance and site-selectivity control. This approach is guided by C-H acidity and carbanion oxidation trends and therefore exhibits fundamentally distinct scope and selectivity trends over hydrogen atom abstraction and single electron oxidation-based radical protocols that are instead guided by alkylarene C-H bond strengths or oxidation potentials, respectively. As such, this method is applicable to alkylarenes with high oxidation potentials and tolerates the presence of traditionally reactive weak C-H bonds and oxidatively-sensitive functional groups. These features enable TEMPO installation on densely functionalized compounds, including a wide array of pharmaceutical and N-heteroaryl substrates. This approach also introduces the opportunity to exploit the inverse correlation between C-H acidity and carbanion oxidation potential such that either property can interchangeably dictate site-selectivity for arenes with multiple benzylic positions. Thus, simple adjustments to the base strength are proposed to initiate a Curtin-Hammett-regulated oxidation pathway that enables a switch in selectivity from the most to least acidic benzylic position. We anticipate that these collective features will enhance benzylic C-H diversification efforts given the downstream synthetic versatility of benzyl-OTMP units.

papers.title: Structurally Enabling ADMET Anti-Targets via Induced Fit Docking and Free Energy Perturbation
papers.abstract: The development of a small-molecule suitable for clinical use involves optimization of ligand binding to an identified target protein but also frequently the reduction of binding to a variety of anti-target proteins known to pose translational risk. These anti-targets, often referred to as ADMET proteins, often contain large, highly flexible binding sites leading to promiscuous binding of small molecules. This property often frustrates efforts to execute structure-based design against these anti-targets. Here we demonstrate the application of a combination of induced fit docking and free energy perturbation to structurally enable several of the most common anti-targets: cytochrome P450 isoforms 3A4 and 2D6, the hERG ion channel, and PXR. Crucially, the enforcement of a consensus binding mode across a congeneric series allowed for the efficient exploration of a wide range of receptor conformation space. Results are presented for both public retrospective datasets and prospective application in active drug discovery programs.

papers.title: Nikolas: AI Agent for Semi-Autonomous Catalyst Discovery Using the PRISM Meta-Cognitive Architecture
papers.abstract: The discovery of efficient catalysts for CO 2 reduction is critical for addressing climate change, yet traditional approaches rely on expensive noble metals and time consuming trial-and-error experimentation. We present Nikolas, a semi-autonomous AI agent for scientific discovery, powered by PRISM (Persistent Recursive Intelligence with Structured Metacognition)-a novel 5-layer meta-cognitive architecture that enables emergent domain intuition from the interplay of large language models (LLMs), computational tools, and hierarchical memory. In its first application, Nikolas autonomously generates and screens catalyst candidates: it proposes structures using Gemini 2.5 Flash, validates them with RDKit, calculates CO 2 binding energies using xTB (GFN2-xTB), and filters candidates using the Sabatier principle (optimal binding: −10 to −20 kcal/mol). The agent's automated screening loop identified a champion catalyst, Fe(2-pyridine) 2 (PPh 3) 2 , with −15.45 kcal/mol CO 2 binding energy (Sabatier optimal). The researchers then independently validated this candidate through reaction pathway analysis, 50 ps molecular dynamics simulation (zero ligand detachment), and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) selectivity testing (11.64 kcal/mol thermodynamic advantage over H 2 binding). While this paper demonstrates Nikolas in the domain of computational chemistry, the PRISM architecture is domain-agnostic-designed to accelerate scientific discovery across disciplines from drug design to materials science.

papers.title: Nikolas: Agent for Autonomous Catalyst Discovery Using the PRISM Meta-Cognitive Architecture
papers.abstract: The discovery of efficient catalysts for CO 2 reduction is critical for addressing climate change, yet traditional approaches rely on expensive noble metals and timeconsuming trial-and-error experimentation. We present Nikolas, a semi-autonomous AI agent for scientific discovery, powered by PRISM (Persistent Recursive Intelligence with Structured Metacognition)-a novel 5-layer meta-cognitive architecture that enables emergent domain intuition from the interplay of large language models (LLMs), computational tools, and hierarchical memory. In its first application, Nikolas autonomously generates and screens catalyst candidates: it proposes structures using Gemini 2.5 Flash, validates them with RDKit, calculates CO 2 binding energies using xTB (GFN2-xTB), and filters candidates using the Sabatier principle (optimal binding: −10 to −20 kcal/mol). The agent's automated screening loop identified a champion catalyst, Fe(2-pyridine) 2 (PPh 3) 2 , with −15.45 kcal/mol CO 2 binding energy (Sabatier optimal). The researchers then independently validated this candidate through reaction pathway analysis, 50 ps molecular dynamics simulation (zero ligand detachment), and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) selectivity testing (11.64 kcal/mol thermodynamic advantage over H 2 binding). While this paper demonstrates Nikolas in the domain of computational chemistry, the PRISM architecture is domain-agnostic-designed to accelerate scientific discovery across disciplines from drug design to materials science.

papers.title: Backbone Double-Mutant Cycle Analysis Quantifies Hydrogen-Bond Energies in Proteins
papers.abstract: Protein structure is stabilized by a variety of noncovalent interactions, but many remain incompletely understood. For example, several potentially ubiquitous interactions involving the protein backbone have been identified, but challenges in determining reliable experimental energies have prevented their integration into structural models. To address this challenge, we adapted a popular protein engineering approach, double-mutant cycle analysis, for the quantification of backbone interactions. By combining this analytical paradigm with chemical peptide synthesis, we selectively probe backbone interactions while avoiding many confounding factors that have complicated previous efforts. We first validate this approach by quantifying the energy of canonical, cross-strand hydrogen bonds in model β-sheet proteins and find excellent agreement with previous results. We then extend this approach to quantify weak, intra-strand hydrogen bonds that have recently been implicated in protein folding and misfolding. Our results provide the first experimental quantification of these interactions, corroborating previous computational predictions that individual intra-strand hydrogen bonds contribute approx. 0.2 kcal/mol each, which is significant given the frequency of these interactions. More broadly, our results illustrate a useful approach to probing backbone interactions in proteins, which can be readily applied to a variety of other systems.

papers.title: High Molar Mass [n]Cycloparaphenylene Conjugated Polymers and Copolymers with Improved Electron Delocalization
papers.abstract: This work reports the synthesis of [ n ]cycloparaphenylene ([ n ]CPP) conjugated polymers and copolymers based on poly( p -phenylene vinylene) (PPV). We utilize the Gilch polymerization to generate high molar mass [ n ]CPP conjugated polymers for the first time, demonstrating that a 2,5bis(chloromethyl)[8]CPP monomer is compatible with the polymerization method by observing the highly reactive p -biquinodimethane intermediate via in-situ NMR spectroscopy. Hindered by their complex synthesis and limited solubility at high [ n ]CPP content, we then synthesize a series of solution-processable [8]CPP-PPV-co-MEH-PPV copolymers. Photophysical experiments in both solution and as drop-cast thin films, in conjunction with computational analysis, allow for the evaluation of both the radial [ n ]CPP and linear PPV component as [n]CPP content is modulated. These findings introduce a new strategy for integrating the radially conjugated [ n ]CPP macrocycle into processable, high molar mass π-conjugated polymeric systems, towards enabling expanded molecular design in organic electronic materials.

papers.title: Measurement of the Critical Ionization Level for Resist Polymer Using a Polypeptoid Platform
papers.abstract: The dissolution of a resist polymer in aqueous base, forming a processable image, is an important step in building nanoscale patterns on semiconductor chips. The most successful resist dissolution theory, critical ionization (CI) theory, states that a specific minimum fraction of the moieties in the acidic polymer, the CI level, is required to be ionized to become soluble in the aqueous base solution. The value of this fraction, which is critical to successful resist polymer designs, has only been estimated in prior studies. In this work, a family of polypeptoids synthesized with controlled chain length and ionizable monomer content is used as a platform for measuring the CI level of a resist polymer. Quartz crystal microbalance (QCM) experiments are combined with reaction diffusion chemical kinetics models to examine the applicability of the CI model to polypeptoid dissolution. The results show that the CI level of the polypeptoid was found to be 20%, and polymers at the CI level exhibited dissolution behavior distinct from those above the CI level. Above the CI level, the dissolution rate increases linearly with the ionizable content, and the CI model is applicable.

papers.title: Mapping Aluminum Flows in the United States using Bayesian Material Flow Analysis
papers.abstract: This paper presents a Bayesian material flow analysis (MFA) of aluminum in the U.S. economy, reconciling a 2017 baseline and updating the system to 2022. We introduce ARCADE (Abiotic Resource Cycles, Allocations, and Dynamics in the Economy), a unified Bayesian MFA framework that integrates system definition, data pedigree, and probabilistic reconciliation under physical constraints. ARCADE combines government statistics, trade records, and industry reports into a physically consistent network and reports uncertainty-aware metrics, including recycled content, end-of-life (EOL) recycling, scrap collection, domestic retention, and stock change. Results show the U.S. (1) remains highly reliant on imports of unwrought and finished aluminum products; (2) had a slightly higher EOL scrap collection rate in 2022 (64%) than in 2017 (63%), but lower domestic retention of collected EOL scrap (52% vs. 58%), indicating a widening gap between collection and domestic use; and (3) could increase wrought-grade recycling by targeting key nodes in EOL scrap collection, domestic processing, and product allocation. Overall, improved collection does not necessarily raise domestic retention given processing constraints and continued scrap exports.

papers.title: Quantum Entanglement and Dissociation Behavior in Hydrogen Fluoride
papers.abstract: By using quantum information theory metrics, we have studied the relationship between quantum correlation and bond dissociation in hydrogen fluoride. Von Neumann entropy, concurrence and quantum discord are calculated as the bond length of H-F is stretched. These are analyzed in comparison with classical descriptor like dipole moment of H-F and Mulliken charge fluorine. Laplacian contour maps also visualize electron concentration and depletion during bond stretching. At equilibrium bond length, quantum correlations and bond polarization both are optimally balanced. As the bond length increases, charge localize on Fluorine but entanglement reduces leading to bond dissociation. At large separations, quantum correlation which are still residual persist near dissociation. These findings provides a critical role of quantum correlations that are involve in stabilizing strongly polar bond. It gives quantitative insights into interplay electronic structure and quantum information theory properties during bond dissociation.

papers.title: Gibbs Energy Minimization Thermodynamics for CO 2
papers.abstract: Gibbs-energy-minimization thermodynamic models (GEM-TMs) provide a rigorous framework for computing chemical equilibrium in aqueous-amine CO 2 capture systems, but published implementations and fitting practices are often inconsistent. This work shows that many reported discrepancies in fitted equilibrium constants, activity coefficients, and predicted speciation arise from (i) incomplete or rank-deficient mass/moiety conservation constraints, (ii) inconsistent use of concentration variables and standard states, and (iii) ill-posed strategies that co-fit equilibrium constants (or standard-state properties) and activity-coefficient parameters to the same solubility data. We give a transparent treatment of the nonstoichiometric and stoichiometric GEM-TM formulations, clarify their distinction from numerical solution algorithms, and derive exact conversions of equilibrium constants and standard chemical potentials across molality, mole-fraction, and molarity conventions for chemical potential models based on the infinite-dilution reference state. Using aqueous MDEA and MEA as representative systems, we demonstrate that distinct formulations and parameterizations can reproduce P CO 2-loading data while implying substantially different equilibrium constants, activity coefficients, and speciation, thereby exposing non-unique parameter fits and compensation effects. All case studies are implemented in Reaktoro, a free opensource Gibbs-energy minimization framework that enables fully transparent model construction, constraint enforcement, and reproducible calculations. Implications for machine-learning surrogates are discussed in the context of thermodynamically consistent equilibrium baselines.

papers.title: From Zn to Cd: Extending Halide-First Stabilization Strategies to Dimethylcadmium through Ion Pairs
papers.abstract: Dimethyl cadmium (Cd(CH₃)₂) is an important molecular source for II-VI semiconductor growth; however, its extreme reactivity increases the hazards associated with transport and storage, motivating the development of safer, more stable derivative forms. Here, we computationally evaluate whether a halide-attachment stabilization strategy reported by Falkowski and co-workers (J. Phys. Chem. A, 2025) can be transferred to Cd(CH₃)₂. We examine the formation of ate species (CH₃)₂CdX⁻ (X = F, Cl, I) and quantify how substitution of chloride versus iodide and fluoride modulates structure, bonding, and thermodynamic stability.

papers.title: Blood-Brain Barrier Exclusion (BBBX) Score: Designing Drugs Not to Enter the Brain
papers.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) is an important physiological barrier that protects the brain by preventing entry of harmful substances into the central nervous system (CNS). While this barrier is effective at blocking most drugs from disrupting the tightly controlled environment of the CNS, certain classes of non-neurologic drugs can cross the BBB, potentially causing neurological side effects. Developing safer alternatives to these drugs requires a reliable method for predicting the BBB non-penetrance, whilst maintaining a high level of drug-like properties to the molecules. Existing regression methods for BBB penetration are inaccurate for this task, tending to overestimate logBB values due to imbalances in available datasets. To address this, we have developed a LightGBM-based model with a custom multi-task loss function that learns from both regression and classification data. Improving performance across classification and regression metrics, our model outperforms existing models in identifying non-penetrant molecules and achieves regression accuracy approximately equal to experimental uncertainty. Based on this, we introduce the BBB Exclusion (BBBX) Score, a scoring method which stratifies compounds by predicted BBB penetrance and confidence. To interpret model outputs, SHAP analysis was used to identify features contributing most to model outputs. We use these features to define threshold values associated with increased likelihood of BBB Exclusion whilst maintaining high oral bioavailability and drug-like properties required for developing a safe, non-CNS drug.

papers.title: The tortuous path to energy density: Microstructure-based cell models for graded electrode design
papers.abstract: Microstructure design of battery electrodes is key to enable fast charge and higher capacity in next-generation lithium-ion batteries but exploring the possible design space traditionally relies on slow trial-and-error. Here we introduce microstructure-aware cell models based on a novel electrode microstructure descriptor, the spatial tortuosity τ(x), which is directly extracted from 3D image-based simulations. The study shows that state-of-the-art approaches for cell characterisation and simulation are only valid for homogeneous battery electrodes while this new approach naturally generalizes to graded and multi-layer electrode designs. By preserving the computational efficiency of porous electrode models while embedding microstructure information, our workflow runs in minutes per design and provides physically interpretable levers for architecture optimisation under fast (dis)charge. Combined with conditionalised generative AI methods, this pipeline enables high-throughput exploration of the electrode microstructure space accelerating the design of electrodes that simultaneously improve transport, reaction uniformity, and accessible capacity.

papers.title: A DFT Study of LiCs molecule and application to prediction of adjusting super atomic molecular orbitals (SAMOs)
papers.abstract: Polar heteronuclear alkali-metal dimers, which can exhibit pronounced charge separation, have been studied experimentally and theoretically because of their unusual bonding and electronic properties. Recent advances in synthetic methodology have increased the feasibility of employing these species as functional components; however, their potential applications remain largely unexplored. A key bottleneck is the computational cost required to predict reliable structural and electronic properties for systems containing heavy alkali elements: high-level wave-function methods such as CCSD(T)-SF are often prohibitively expensive for screening complexes and materials. Herein, we use LiCs as a prototypical system to assess practical computational protocols by benchmarking density functional theory (DFT) calculations against ab initio references and available experimental observables. We find that the CAM-B3LYP, combined with relativistic corrections, reproduces both the equilibrium bond length within 2% error and within 5% error for dipole moment at a substantially reduced computational cost. Using this validated protocol, we investigate the LiCs–benzene complex and show that LiCs can spatially polarize benzene’s Superatom Molecular Orbitals (SAMOs) from the ring toward LiCs while avoiding significant destabilization. This behavior contrasts with that induced by a monovalent cation and by representative alkali–halide ion pairs. These results demonstrate a low-cost route to model alkali-metal dimers and suggest a strategy to regulate SAMOs using polar diatomic alkali species, opening new opportunities in molecular and materials design.

papers.title: Quantum Network Theory of Catalysis: Unifying Zeolites, Enzymes, and MOFs
The Tsetlin Machine: A “Third Way” in QSAR Modelling
Topological engineering of chiral anomalies in Janus nanoribbons
papers.abstract: Topological band theory based on the variety of reciprocal space invariants provides an insightful framework for quantum material characterization in condensed matter physics. Its bulk-boundary correspondence principle has become a reliable tool for predicting Fermi level properties. Here, we investigate a recently proposed bottom-up topological engineering based on reciprocal space invariants and show its connection to a real space in situ topology of Kekule structure originating in organic chemistry. We show that these approaches can be effectively used to engineer magnetic-field-free tunable chiral anomalies that are promising for energy-efficient electronic transport.

papers.title: Indole as a Directing Group for Nonaromatic C-H Activation in Palladium-Catalyzed Cross-Dehydrogenative Coupling with β-Ketoesters
papers.abstract: The selective activation of aliphatic C-H bonds remains a fundamental challenge in synthetic chemistry. Here we disclose a palladium-catalyzed cross-dehydrogenative coupling (CDC) that joins the α-carbon of β-ketoesters with the C3-benzylic position of indoles, forging C(sp 3 )-C(sp 3 ) bonds under mild oxidative conditions. This transformation uncovers an unprecedented directing effect of indolic π-system, which engages in coordination with palladium to guide site-selective C(sp 3 )-H activation via an agostic interaction. The developed protocol exhibits high tunability, a broad substrate scope, and high yields under mild conditions, underscoring its potential for late-stage functionalization in pharmaceutical and materials science applications. The transformation integrates well into one-pot and multicomponent processes as well as enables stereoselective functionalization of the steroid core. Mechanistic investigations, supported by kinetic analysis and DFT calculations, indicate that the transformation proceeds with the involvement of Pd(IV) intermediates, with product decomplexation identified as the rate-determining step.

papers.title: Native Top-Down Mass Spectrometry combined with High-Resolution Charge Variant Analysis of Trastuzumab Originator and Biosimilars
papers.abstract: Comprehensive characterisation of monoclonal antibody (mAb) charge heterogeneity is essential for ensuring product quality, maintaining batch consistency, and supporting biosimilar development. Charge variant analysis (CVA) is widely used to separate acidic and basic proteoforms from the main species. However, cation-exchange chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry provides limited information and cannot localise the post-translational modifications (PTMs) responsible for mAb heterogeneity. Here, we present the coupling of pH-gradient CVA with native top-down mass spectrometry (TD-MS) for proteoform-specific analysis of trastuzumab. Individual charge variants were chromatographically separated under native conditions and directly fragmented on the chromatographic timescale using higher-energy collision dissociation (HCD), electron-transfer dissociation (ETD), and ultraviolet photodissociation (UVPD). The addition of proton-transfer charge reduction (PTCR) helped to reduce spectral congestion and enhanced the detection of high-mass fragment ions, resulting in improved sequence coverage. This workflow enabled the complete sequencing of complementarity-determining region (CDR) 3 and the direct identification and insights on the location of key PTMs at the intact-protein level, including deamidation, succinimide, and N-terminal pyroGlu, on individual proteoforms. Comparison of five trastuzumab samples (originator and biosimilars) demonstrated high reproducibility in fragmentation patterns, sequence coverage, and variant assignment, highlighting the robustness of the method. Although limitations remain due to the challenges of fragmentating intact mAbs under native conditions, this work establishes a proof of concept for CVA native TD-MS characterisation of mAbs to complement bottom-up and middle-down analyses and has potential for broad applicability on antibody-based biopharmaceuticals, from characterisation to biosimilarity evaluation.

papers.title: In situ observation of ultra-giant spherulites in perovskite hydrates
Collective Effect of Color-Centers on Chiroptical Response of Carbon Nanotubes
papers.abstract: The incorporation of color centers or chemical dopants into carbon nanotubes (CNTs) offers a promising strategy to modulate their optical activity, particularly to improve their emission. Here, our computational study aims to investigate the effects of covalent defect ensembles on the chiroptical response of CNTs. Our results suggest that their collective behavior leads to emergent chiroptical effects that go beyond simple additive contributions. The spatial distribution, helicity, density, and symmetry-breaking characteristics of the defect configurations can cooperatively amplify (or in some cases suppress) circular dichroism and optical rotation. These trends may be rationalized by analyzing interactions between multiple color centers that may induce specific delocalized chiral exciton states or modify selection rules, resulting in tunable chiroptical signals. Understanding these collective effects is essential for designing CNT-based chiral optoelectronic and quantum devices and for spectroscopically probing symmetry-breaking phenomena at the nanoscale.

papers.title: Hybridization Kinetics Reveal Backbone-Dependent Binding of Peptide Nucleic Acid Analogs
papers.abstract: Antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), short single-stranded nucleic acids, have emerged as an important class of RNA-targeting agents by binding through sequence-specific base pairing, resulting in alteration or blockage of RNA function. However, unmodified DNA-and RNA-based ASOs are prone to instability and enzymatic degradation. Peptide nucleic acids (PNAs) provide enhanced stability, affinity and sequence selectivity due to their N-(2aminoethyl)glycine backbone, but their limited aqueous solubility can restrict broader application. This limitation can be addressed by the incorporation of γ-miniPEG side chains improving the solubility while retaining favorable binding characteristics. As antisense efficacy strongly depends on target residence time, a quantitative understanding of hybridization kinetics is critical for candidate selection. Yet direct comparisons of γ-miniPEG-modified PNAs with RNA remain scarce. Here, we systematically compare the hybridization of RNA, PNA and γ-miniPEG-PNA toward complementary RNA strand using surface plasmon resonance (SPR) spectroscopy, which enables real-time analysis of association and dissociation kinetics beyond equilibrium duplex stability derived from melting temperature measurements. Our results shows that duplex dissociation slows with increasing strand length, whereas association behavior is largely governed by backbone chemistry. PNA exhibits particularly rapid target binding while maintaining strong affinity. Together, these findings elucidate how backbone structure governs hybridization dynamics and guide the rational design of PNA-based ASOs for RNA-targeting.

papers.title: The Aggregicyclins Shed Light on Type II Polyketide Biosynthesis in Myxococcota
papers.abstract: Polycyclic bacterial specialized metabolites such as anthraquinones, angucyclines, and tetracyclines are predominantly produced by type II polyketide synthase (PKS) systems and represent an important source of antibiotics and anticancer agents. While type II PKS pathways are well characterized in Gram-positive bacteria, their biosynthetic potential in Gram-negative bacteria remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the discovery and activation of a cryptic type II PKS biosynthetic gene cluster from the myxobacterium Aggregicoccus edonensis MCy10622. Using a rapid PCR-based cloning and promoter-exchange strategy, the compact gene cluster was heterologously expressed in Myxococcus xanthus DK1622, leading to the production of two previously unknown specialized metabolites, aggregicyclin and oxyaggregicyclin. Structural analysis revealed an unusual polycyclic scaffold featuring a wide-spanning biaryl ether linkage. Biosynthetic analysis supports an early diversification event during first-ring cyclization as the basis for product divergence. Aggregicyclin exhibited antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and cytotoxicity against human cancer cells. Together, these findings expand the current knowledge of type II polyketide biosynthesis in Gram-negative bacteria.

papers.title: Self-monitoring of Metabolic Status with a Smartphone-assisted Breath Sensing Device
papers.abstract: Human metabolism can be monitored through exhaled breath analysis, which is well suited for home-use due to its non-invasive nature. Despite strong research efforts, its potential outside research laboratories has hardly been exploited due to the lack of accurate and user-friendly sensing devices. Here, we present a fully integrated handheld breath acetone detector designed for smartphone-guided metabolic self-monitoring at home. The device enables volumecontrolled, end-tidal breath sampling through visual guidance, ensuring reproducible and accurate quantification of breath acetone. Small inter-device variability was identified (±5.6% for 3 devices at 1 parts-per-million; ppm), with high humidity robustness (≤4.2% bias across 0-90% relative humidity) and stable performance over 8 months (6.1% inter-day variability). We tested the detector for metabolic tracking during exercise and dietary interventions in 12 volunteers, capturing rapid subject-specific changes in breath acetone levels, in agreement with blood ketone and interstitial glucose assessment. Validation against proton transfer reaction time-of-flight mass spectrometry demonstrated excellent agreement across a physiologically relevant range of 0.2-45 ppm (e.g. 7.5% bias at 2 ppm) in 312 breath samples. This work establishes a comprehensive validation framework for translating breath detectors from laboratory prototypes into healthcare, for instance, for weight management, ketogenic diet guidance or preventive health monitoring.

papers.title: Local Energy Decomposition of Intramolecular Interactions: The CovaLED Approach and its Application to Molecular Recognition in Biomolecular Assemblies
Spectral identification of bacteria and its traces in sol-gel based biosensors
papers.abstract: For many, years scientists around the world are developing spectroscopic methods for pathogenic bacterial identification. One of the main challenges to optically differentiate between bacterial species originates from their high spectral similarity which derives from the similar biological components that exist in all species. For this reason, many of the spectroscopic identification methods are based on different quantities of biomaterials in bacteria. Yet, such quantitative measurements may not always be sufficient as different species may consist of similar quantities which can vary by different environmental or developmental influence. A selective method for selective bacterial capture is polymer imprinting. In this method, the target bacteria are co-polymerized to from polymer surfaces with the bacteria trapped inside. Upon release of the bacteria from the polymer's surface, spatial cavities with the size and shape of the bacteria are formed, enabling to use the polymer as a selective biosensor to recapture the species that was once trapped inside. In this work, we fabricate sol-gel based biosensors for targeting various pathogenic bacteria and show that their intrinsic signal can be detected by synchronous fluorescence spectroscopy. Furthermore, we label the cells with the fluorescent dye 4',6-diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI) and conduct single cell identification by Fourier transform spectroscopic imaging microscopy. In addition to the detection of the bacterial cells, we show that residues of the target bacteria remain in the cavities during the fabrication of the biosensors.

papers.title: Synthesis of multisubstituted thiosulfonates from o-silylaryl triflates via halothiolation of aryne intermediates followed by oxidative S-sulfonylation
papers.abstract: An efficient method for preparing aryl thiosulfonates through aryne intermediates is disclosed. Following aryne halothiolation with potassium xanthate, the resulting aryl xanthates were transformed into thiosulfonates using iodine and sodium sulfinates. The versatility of thiosulfonates together with divergent aryne precursors enabled the access to a wide range of highly functionalized organosulfur compounds.

papers.title: Selective Degradation of Polyurethanes in Mixed Plastic Wastes via Ir-Catalyzed Hydrogenolysis
papers.abstract: Chemical recycling of plastic waste has been widely undertaken to address a circular carbon economy. However, the presence of different polymers or composites in plastic waste complicates its chemical degradation into reusable chemical feedstocks. Here, we report the selective degradation of polyurethanes in mixed plastics with polyesters and polyamides using H2 as a reactant, contrarily to the implicitly low reactivity of urethanes against esters and amides. This chemoselectivity enables selective chemical recycling of urethanes in mixed textiles and end-of-life car seats, while thermoplastic polyesters and polyamides can be separated for mechanical recycling. This innovative recycling approach facilitates composite separation and resource circulation in mixed plastic waste, addressing a pressing global concern.

papers.title: Light-Actuated Shapeshifting Vesicles Without Photoswitches
papers.abstract: The ability to externally control membrane morphology is central to engineering responsive artificial cells and to understanding how primitive protocells might have behaved in fluctuating environments. Here we show that illumination of vesicles containing aqueous dyes produces rapid, reversible, and dye-dependent remodeling of membrane curvature. Giant unilamellar vesicles undergo inward and outward budding, reversible adhesion, and fusion under sustained illumination, relaxing to a new steady-state shape while light is applied. The direction of curvature switching depends sensitively on the identity of the encapsulated dye and buffer, indicating that light perturbs the solute-membrane interactions and thus the spontaneous curvature. Together, these results establish a chemically mediated, dissipative mechanism for light-controlled curvature switching that operates in both phospholipid and fatty acid membranes. This provides a simple, generalizable strategy for actuating shape in synthetic cells and suggests how environmental light cues could have driven dynamic behaviors in early protocellular systems. Harnessing light to induce reversible shape changes could potentially unlock new avenues in synthetic biology, the design and manipulation of microscopic 'swimmers', tissue engineering, and responsive materials.

papers.title: From Zn to Cd: Extending Halide-First Stabilization Strategies to Dimethylcadmium through Ion Pairs
papers.abstract: Dimethyl cadmium (Cd(CH₃)₂) is an important molecular source for II-VI semiconductor growth; however, its extreme reactivity increases the hazards associated with transport and storage, motivating the development of safer, more stable derivative forms. Here, we computationally evaluate whether a halide-attachment stabilization strategy reported by Falkowski and co-workers (J. Phys. Chem. A, 2025) can be transferred to Cd(CH₃)₂. We examine the formation of ate species (CH₃)₂CdX⁻ (X = F, Cl, I) and quantify how substitution of chloride versus iodide and fluoride modulates structure, bonding, and thermodynamic stability.

papers.title: Data-driven pipeline enables discovery of plant protein surfactants
papers.abstract: Designing amphiphilic block copolymers from fossil fuel-derived hydrocarbons is a cornerstone of colloid chemistry, enabling the creation of advanced polymeric surfactants. Despite the high attractiveness of low carbon-emitting plant proteins to defossilise surfactant processing, attempts in identifying plant proteins that will act as appropriate surfactants are somewhat hit and miss. Here, we present a data-driven pipeline to fingerprint plant protein surfactants by harnessing the diblock-like signature of a classic surfactant, integrating protein sequence data with statistical thermodynamics-based calculations, finetuned by machine learning. We demonstrate that protein sequence-level features do not in themselves allow for the prediction of adsorbed configuration. Instead, segmenting adsorbed proteins into blocks enabled identification of hundreds of plant proteins possessing a diblock-like signature, validated experimentally for optimal surface properties. Thus, by embedding adsorption configuration information into the classification process, we streamline the discovery of plant protein surfactants at scale, unlikely to be realised by purely empirical screening.

papers.title: A Theory of Electronic Structure for Coarse-Grained Resolutions
papers.abstract: We present a stochastic diabatic projection method for constructing electronic structure models that operate at coarse-grained (CG) molecular resolutions. By minimizing the relative entropy of joint electronic-nuclear distributions between the fine-grained and CG resolutions, we derive a stochastic effective Hamiltonian that decomposes CG configuration dependent interactions into deterministic means and residual fluctuations. This framework bridges downfolding theory with data-driven CG modeling, enabling the accurate reproduction of electronic properties renormalized over eliminated nuclear and electronic degrees of freedom.

papers.title: Thermodynamics without Entropy: Reframing Available Energy as a Thermodynamic Primitive
papers.abstract: Since the inception of thermodynamics, a tension has existed between two frameworks for expressing the second law: Gibbs’ entropy-based formalism, and Kelvin’s conception of the inevitable dissipation of mechanical work. Gibbs' formalism, built upon the fundamental relation, S(U, V, n) , reveals the geometric structure of thermodynamics, from which unexpected physical relationships such as the Maxwell relations and the Gibbs-Duhem equation naturally fall out. Kelvin’s conception, by contrast, is generally treated as a derived construct, and in engineering contexts has developed into availability or exergy analyses. Here, we demonstrate that a complete Gibbsian formalism may be constructed on the basis of a system’s available energy, with no need to invoke entropy. This formalism has its own fundamental relation, Legendre transforms, Maxwell relations, and convex contact-geometric structure, all equivalent to those of the traditional entropy-based framework. We derive several classical results, including the Clausius equation and the expression for the Joule-Thomson coefficient, within this entropy-free formalism, and show how expressions in classical statistical mechanics may be reinterpreted as Legendre transforms of a system’s available energy. Finally, we reflect on the conceptual, pedagogical and historical ramifications of Gibbs' decision to embed entropy, rather than available energy, at the heart of his thermodynamic formalism.

papers.title: Kilogram-scale Stereoselective Synthesis of an N-methylprolinol Derivative by Enzymatic Transformation
papers.abstract: A scalable method for the manufacture of (S)-1-((2S,4R)-4-methoxy-1-methylpyrrolidin-2-yl)ethan-1-ol, a key intermediate for KRAS inhibitor candidates, was established. This method simplifies the process by performing the decarboxylation of the β-keto ester and the stereoselective reduction of the resulting ketone in a one-pot enzymatic reaction. Furthermore, the direct methylation via Boc group reduction using lithium aluminum hydride was replaced with the safer Eschweiler-Clarke reaction. The resulting prolinol derivative was isolated as its tartrate salt, yielding a high-quality target compound.

papers.title: Benchmarking Universal Machine-learned Interatomic Potentials for Intermolecular and Noncovalent Interactions
papers.abstract: Accurate benchmarking of intermolecular interaction energies is central to evaluating quantum chemical methods and guiding the development of reliable machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for chemical and biological applications. In this work, we benchmark five MLIPs, namely AIMNet2(2023), AIMNet2(2025), MACE-OFF23(M), MACE-OMol, and UMA-S-OMol, across twenty-one datasets spanning hydrogen-bonded, dispersion- and π-dominated, sigma-hole, ionic and charge transfer, and repulsive nonequilibrium interactions, with reference values at or near CCSD(T)/CBS accuracy. AIMNet2(2025) is a continually pretrained variant of AIMNet2(2023) that retains the original architecture but incorporates an additional 3.8 million structures specifically curated to improve the description of noncovalent interactions (NCIs). Across these chemically diverse test sets, AIMNet2(2025) delivers consistent and systematic improvements over its predecessor, with the most pronounced gains observed in the hydrogen-bonded, sigma-hole, and repulsive regimes, while remaining broadly competitive with the substantially larger MACE-OMol and UMA-S-OMol models. Nevertheless, the supramolecular S12L and L7 benchmarks show only marginal improvement, with all evaluated MLIPs exhibiting large errors driven by a small number of pathological complexes. Two factors beyond intrinsic model quality significantly influence the reported performance. First, partial overlap between training and benchmark data, quantified here through systematic overlap detection, inflates apparent accuracy for all models, most strongly for those trained on the OMol25 data. Second, differences in the DFT reference level used for MLIP training establish distinct and irreducible error floors relative to the CCSD(T)/CBS targets, meaning that superior benchmark performance may in part reflect closer proximity of the training functional to the reference method rather than stronger modeling capability. Sigma-hole interactions emerge as the interaction category with the lowest training-benchmark overlap across all models and therefore provide the most discriminating test of genuine generalization. Together, these findings demonstrate that meaningful MLIP evaluation must carefully account for data provenance, reference theory consistency, and the distinction between interpolation and true out-of-distribution generalization, particularly as standard NCI benchmark sets become increasingly absorbed into large-scale training datasets.

papers.title: Experimental Evaluation of Methane Biofiltration under Low-Concentrations Conditions Using Replicated Lab-Scale Systems
papers.abstract: Biofiltration is a promising strategy for mitigating low-concentration methane (CH 4 ) emissions, yet performance remains variable and sensitive to operating conditions. This study experimentally evaluated a lab-scale biofiltration system consisting of nine identical packed-bed biofilter columns operated in parallel to quantify how gas flow rate and inlet CH 4 concentration affect performance. Two flow rates (1 and 2 L min −1 ) and three inlet concentrations (5000, 10000, and 25000 ppmv) were tested, and methane removal efficiency (RE), elimination capacity (EC), and CO 2 production (P CO 2 ) were monitored over extended operation. At 1 L min −1 , the maximum RE reached 89% at 0.5% v/v, while RE decreased with increasing inlet concentration; at 2 L min −1 , the maximum RE values were lower (11-40%), consistent with reduced residence time. Conversely, EC increased with inlet concentration and ranged from approximately 3 to 20 g m −3 h −1 . Across conditions, peak performance occurred early and declined to lower final values, indicating limited long-term stability under the tested regimes. Two-way ANOVA confirmed significant effects of flow rate and inlet concentration on 1 RE and significant effects of inlet concentration on EC. Overall, the results highlight a practical efficiency-capacity trade-off and emphasize residence time as a key operational parameter for managing methane biofilter performance.

papers.title: Automated Parallel Synthesis Accelerates Virtual Screening Hit Discovery
papers.abstract: Virtual screening (VS) is a powerful approach to explore vast chemical space, encompassing libraries of millions to billions of compounds. However, the low hit rates of VS require testing numerous candidates to validate true binders, followed by iterative optimization cycles, making experimental validation costly and time-consuming. Here, we report COMBINAUT, an automated parallel synthesis platform that generates diverse chemical scaffolds to accelerate hit validation and refinement. Using a faculty-wide collection of in-house building blocks, the system enables enumeration of over 22.9 million compounds, each designed for parallelized synthesis within 1-32 hours using repurposed solid-phase peptide synthesis equipment. Using this platform, we performed large-scale virtual screening targeting the allosteric pocket of the immuno-oncology target, C-C chemokine receptor 2 (CCR2). Our approach facilitated the rapid synthesis and testing of 100 virtual screening hits, spanning diverse molecular architectures. In radioligand binding assays, we successfully validated nine hits with distinct scaffolds, including completely novel CCR2 ligand chemotypes. Iterative hit-to-lead optimization using the automated workflow produced cell-active CCR2 antagonists. This work demonstrates the synergy of automated synthesis and VS, enabling efficient exploration of chemical space and rapid discovery of novel ligands.

papers.title: Pyrroloquinoline quinone and imidazopyrroloquinoline intake extend healthy lifespan and improve physical dysfunctions with age in mice
papers.abstract: Pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ) and its derivative imidazopyrroloquinoline (IPQ) are nutritionally important, vitamin-like compounds that exert various physiological effects, including cell-growth promotion, neuroprotection, and stimulations of mitochondriogensis. In this study, we investigated whether PQQ and IPQ act as potential geroprotectors that promote healthy longevity as no lifespan aging intervention experiments have been conducted in mammals to date. We conducted lifelong and midlife 0.02% (w/w) PQQ and 0.02% (w/w) IPQ supplementation experiments using senescenceaccelerated mice P8 strain that have a short lifespan. In lifelong supplementation experiments, the day of 75% survival was prolonged by approximately 60% and 30% in the PQQ and IPQ groups, respectively, compared with that in control. In addition, significant delays in the appearance of aging and age-related neuromuscular dysfunction were observed. Furthermore, intake of PQQ and IPQ diets from midlife improved neuromuscular function that had declined with age. We also found that IPQ intake reduced lipid accumulation in adipose tissue and the liver. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to demonstrate that PQQ and IPQ supplementation, whether initiated early or in middle age, is effective in ameliorating age-related alterations, such as neuromuscular function, and extending healthy lifespan in mammals.

papers.title: A Pd(0)-Catalyzed [3,3]-[4+2] Tandem Pericyclic Sequence Featuring Ring Deletion and Orthogonal Esterification
papers.abstract: We report a Pd(0)-catalyzed tandem [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement/[4+2]-cycloaddition cascade that enables the stereoselective synthesis of cis-1,2-dihydronaphthalenes via a sequence involving regioselective acetate migration, intramolecular cycloaddition, and acid-promoted ring deletion followed by orthogonal esterification. This transformation proceeds through a vinylogous πallyl-Pd(II) intermediate and leverages the dual role of carboxylic acid media in effecting ring deletion and site-selective ester installation. The method exhibits broad functional group tolerance and accommodates structurally diverse substrates, including aryl, alkyl, acetal, halogenated, and drug-like carboxylic acid derivatives. Mechanistic studies, including DFT analysis and intermediate trapping, support a cascade pericyclic/catalytic sequence and underscore the necessity of Pd-catalyzed activation for the cascade to proceed. The resulting cis-dihydronaphthalene frameworks serve as versatile intermediates for late-stage diversification, demonstrating the synthetic power and modularity of this methodology. This work offers a rare example of O-C to O-C [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement and provides a unified platform for constructing stereochemically rich and functionally dense small molecules relevant to natural product synthesis and drug discovery.

papers.title: Stereodivergent Truce-Smiles Rearrangement Enables Enantioselective Access to α-Heteroaryl Quaternary Amino Acid Derivatives
papers.abstract: Increasing molecular three-dimensionality is a key strategy in drug discovery, yet α-heteroaryl α,α-disubstituted amino acids (HAAs) remain largely unexplored despite their potential to modulate peptide conformation and recognition. Here we report a stereodivergent Truce-Smiles rearrangement that converts enantioenriched heteroaryl sulfonamides into HAA derivatives with predictable control over configuration at Cα. The method exploits memory-of-chirality and cation-dependent conformational bias to deliver either inversion or retention of configuration under complementary conditions (Method A: NaHMDS/18-crown-6/LiCl; Method B: KHMDS/Cu(I)OTf). Both protocols operate under mild conditions (THF, −78 °C) and accommodate diverse heteroaryl motifs, N-substituents, and amino acid backbones, achieving high enantiomeric ratios and good yields. Downstream functionalization demonstrates compatibility with peptide coupling and reveals intrinsic limitations such as decarboxylation of free acids. This stereodivergent approach expands the toolbox for constructing quaternary stereocenters adjacent to nitrogen and provides practical access to conformationally defined scaffolds for peptide engineering and 3D chemical-space exploration.

papers.title: DRUGLENS-DL: AN INTEGRATED RULE-BASED AND AI-ASSISTED FRAMEWORK FOR ASSESSING DRUG-LIKENESS
papers.abstract: Drug-likeness prediction represents an important early stage filter in modern drug discovery. This prediction reduces preliminary costs prior to experimental screening. Although, the drug-likeness prediction rules such as Lipinski and Veber filters provide rapid and interpretable screening, but they tend to be deliberately conservative and might not completely represent the current chemical diversity. In this study, we present DrugLens-DL, an open, interpretable, and freely accessible artificial-intelligence-based (AI) web platform for drug-likeness prediction. It integrates classical rule-based filters with a machine-learning-derived probability score obtained from physicochemical descriptors and molecular fingerprints. More importantly, the platform is not designed as a definitive classifier, but as a complementary decision-support tool that augments conventional druglikeness criteria. Model interpretability is obtained through SHAP-based explanations, allowing users to visualize how individual molecular features influence the AI advisory score. DrugLens-DL was organized through a REST-based FastAPI backend and an interactive Streamlit web interface, with real-time predictions from SMILES input. A hybrid output combining AI probability and classical Lipinski rules further improves interpretability and practical relevance. We hope that DrugLens-DL will serve as a 2 practical and reproducible standard advisory checkpoint, along with Lipinski and Veber rules, in modern drug discovery workflows.

papers.title: Configurational Reassignment of (+)-Polycitorol A and (−)-Polycitorol B by NMR Spectroscopic Analysis, Theoretical Calculation, and Total Synthesis
papers.abstract: The proposed structures of (+)-polycitorol A and (−)-polycitorol B, marine tricyclic alkaloids, have been questioned by Kim et al. through total synthesis. In this study, the structure of polycitorol A, a perhydropyrrolo[2,1-j]quinoline derivative, was scrutinized by NMR spectroscopic analysis and theoretical calculation. DP4+ analysis of the DFT calculated NMR chemical shifts showed that the proposed structure most likely required configurational reassignment at the C2 and C5 positions. The reassigned structure of (+)-polycitorol A was finally established through total synthesis. Inspired by known interconversion between cylindricine A and B through an aziridinium ion, a ring-expansion reaction of (+)-polycitorol A under Cossy conditions yielded synthetic (−)-polycitorol B, which was in accordance with natural material with respect to the NMR spectroscopic data and specific rotation. The stereochemistry of (+)-polycitorol A and (−)-polycitrol B corresponded to that of (−)-fasicularin.

papers.title: Rapid and General Machine Learning for Coupling Reactions via a Structure-Based Regression (SBR) Strategy
papers.abstract: Practical adoption of machine learning (ML) in synthetic chemistry is often limited by the need for large datasets and complex feature engineering. A rapid and practical ML strategy termed Structure-Based Regression (SBR) enables predictive modeling of coupling reactions using solely structural information of the substrates. The SBR framework employs uniform bit-length molecular fingerprints to represent diverse reaction archetypes without reaction-specific descriptors, allowing an accurate model construction even from small datasets (<100 data points). The generality of SBR was demonstrated across multiple coupling reactions, including reductive amination, Ni-catalyzed electrochemical etherification, metal-free deaminative coupling, and oxidative amidation. Despite this simplicity, the resulting regression models achieved mean absolute errors (MAE) of 4-12% over ten random train-test divisions. External validation using independent literature datasets revealed that systematic prediction deviations can indicate condition-dependent reactivity trends and highlight substrate classes where conventional conditions remain advantageous.

papers.title: Microbial metabolite L-rhamnose glycates intracellular mammalian proteins
papers.abstract: Host organisms surveil their resident microbiota through the detection of specific microbial metabolites. These molecular patterns are often sensed through noncovalent interactions with pattern recognition receptors. Here, we demonstrate that the non-mammalian monosaccharide L-rhamnose (L-Rha) interacts with host proteins covalently through protein glycation. Through in vitro models of glycation, we find that L-Rha reacts with protein residues and forms advanced glycation end products that can be sensed by host receptors. Using a nonnatural L-Rha analog along with flow cytometry, we show widespread modification of the mammalian proteome across multiple cell lines that mimic the composition of the intestinal wall. Chemoproteomic identification of L-Rha glycation targets reveals that L-Rha enters cells and forms covalent adducts with intracellular proteins enriched within the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondrion. Together, our work uncovers a potential new mechanism for microbiota-mediated host modification via the innate reactivity of microbially generated reducing sugars.

papers.title: Greener, Waste-Minimized Route for Upcycling of Polyethylene Terephthalate Plastic to Antifungal Metal-Organic Framework
papers.abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have drawn broad interest because of their structural versatility and tunable properties. However, sustainable routes to MOF synthesis from low-cost feedstocks, particularly plastic waste, remain largely underexplored. In this report, we present a greener and economical strategy for Cu-based MOF synthesis using terephthalic acid (TPA) obtained from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) under mild, environmentally benign conditions. PET is first directly converted into crystalline TPA (= pTPA ) and ethylene gas via a solvent-free catalytic process, employing a recoverable carbon-supported single-site molybdenum-dioxo catalyst (AC/MoO₂). Compared with conventional alkaline depolymerization, this approach provides a simpler and more sustainable route to TPA feedstocks by eliminating post-depolymerization acidification, solvent-intensive ethylene glycol recovery and salt-waste generation. Next, quantitative room-temperature electrosynthesis of the pTPA –Cu MOF was achieved within 90 min, by using copper foil as sacrificial electrodes, enabling controlled Cu 2+ generation and rapid framework formation under mild conditions. In contrast to conventional solvothermal synthesis, our approach enables waste-minimized and environmentally benign MOF production. Remarkably, electrochemical synthesis of pTPA –Cu MOF remains efficient with recovered electrolyte, enabling continuous, controllable production that minimizes solvent and metal waste. The pTPA –Cu MOF exhibited dose-dependent inhibition of fungal growth, pigmentation and sporulation in A. flavipes and A. fumigatus , highlighting plastic waste upcycling as a sustainable platform for the generation of functional antifungal materials.

papers.title: A General Photoredox C-H Arene Functionalization Towards Substituted Methyls
papers.abstract: The ability to introduce modular C1 units directly into arene C-H bonds remains a fundamental challenge in synthetic design, limiting access to highly diversified molecular architectures from simple feedstocks. We disclose a photoredox-neutral platform that enables direct transfer of a methylenepyridinium linchpin to unactivated arenes, transforming inert C-H sites into versatile synthetic handles. The resulting benzylpyridinium products function as broadly addressable intermediates, supporting a wide range of CC and C-heteroatom bond formation and granting streamlined access to medicinally privileged substituted methyls.

papers.title: Hydrogenation catalysis at aluminium metal
papers.abstract: Activation of molecular hydrogen is the key to many industrial bulk processes that stand at the cradle of modern synthetic chemistry. Hydrogenation traditionally relies on transition metal catalysis by scarce noble d-block metals. However, the transition to a sustainable society provokes the use of more benign abundant metals. We demonstrate hydrogenation catalysis at metallic aluminium, the most abundant metal in the earth's crust. Using a high-surface form of Al 0 , mono-and di-substituted alkenes could be fully converted (150 °C, 50 bar) and, albeit slow, even tri-substituted alkenes and benzene were reduced. Experimental observation combined with a computational study suggest a heterogeneous mechanism. Hydrogenation catalysis at the surface of an abundant main group metal is unanticipated and challenges the monopoly of noble transition metals.

papers.title: Evaluation of Custom REINVENT Priors Trained on Synthetically Accessible Chemical Spaces for Generative Molecular Design
papers.abstract: Generative molecular design is increasingly popular as a promising way to create novel drug candidates with desired properties. The REINVENT approach, originally proposed by AstraZeneca, is a widely used framework for such generative design. However, the synthetic accessibility of generated molecules often remains uncertain. Combinatorial spaces provide access to hundreds of billions of molecules with guaranteed synthetic feasibility and a flat pricing model, making them attractive for planning and executing drug-discovery projects. This study addresses how generative molecular design can be used to ensure that generated molecules remain within a desired chemical space. To achieve this, we developed a new approach and demonstrated the feasibility of training REINVENT Priors on samples from Freedom Space 4.0 and REAL Space. We evaluated the performance of finetuned REINVENT Agent models derived from these Priors using both structure-based and ligand-based computational objectives. Our approach allows the generation of molecules that exhibit the desired activity and remain within the combinatorial space, ensuring synthetic accessibility. The Priors developed in this work are freely released to the community. We hope that the outcomes of this research will boost the practical applications of generative molecular design in academia and industry all over the world.

papers.title: A Flexible and Generalized Constant-Potential Framework in i-PI
papers.abstract: Constant-potential molecular dynamics is essential for realistic simulations of electrochemical interfaces under Operando conditions. Although various constant-potential frameworks exist, most are tightly coupled to specific electronic-structure codes or numerical architectures, limiting portability and extensibility-especially for codes constrained to integer electron numbers. Here we present a flexible constant-potential framework implemented in the i-PI driver, interfacing with multiple density functional theory (DFT) engines and, in principle, extensible to constant-potential machinelearning potentials. The method regulates and samples the electronic chemical po

papers.title: Vector Model of Chiral-Induced Spin Selectivity in Photoinduced Charge-Separations of Cryptochrome for Magnetoreception
papers.abstract: On the "radical-pair-based magnetic compass", mechanisms of the Earth magnetic field sensing are actively debated at molecular levels based upon spin multiplicity-induced reaction selectivity. On this, much remains unknown about how chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) alters the magnetic compass effect. We observed electron spin polarization of the long-range chargeseparated states in cryptochrome using time-resolved electron paramagnetic resonance. Minor effects of CISS on the spin polarization have been clarified. We herein propose that these CISS contributions originate from conformation rearrangements in oxidized tryptophane residues, attributable to reported structural variations between the active and inactive states of the flavoproteins by blue light irradiations. It has also been predicted that even the minor CISS can create a large yield anisotropy and specific directionality of the signaling state due to a violation of the field-inversion symmetry, which would thus serve as a potential contribution to the chemical compass sensory mechanism.

papers.title: Vector Model of Chiral-Induced Spin Selectivity in Photoinduced Charge-Separations of Cryptochrome for Magnetoreception

On this, much remains unknown about how chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) alters the magnetic compass effect.
