papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-driven inverse design of singlet fission candidates in the acene family
papers.abstract: In this work, we describe the successful application of an AI-driven inverse design protocol to identify singlet fission (SF) candidates within the acene family, exploring a chemical space of ~10 19 molecules. Substituent effects are encoded via Hammett σ constants, providing a chemically interpretable and generalizable descriptor for unseen functional groups. A Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU)-based Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) model is used to accurately predict excited singlet (S1) and triplet (T1) states energies. The model is coupled with optimization algorithms, including Genetic Algorithms (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), to efficiently navigate chemical space, optimize S1 and T1 energies, and reveal recurring substituent patterns. This approach not only identifies well-known tetracene and pentacene candidates but also uncovers viable benzene, naphthalene, and anthracene derivatives that satisfy SF criteria, which are typically inaccessible via intuition. The methodology, accessible at https://acene.pythonanywhere.com, establishes a versatile and interpretable platform for rational molecular design, enabling the exploration of large chemical spaces and the discovery of compounds with tailored excited-state properties.

papers.title: Blood-Brain Barrier Exclusion (BBBX) Score: Designing Drugs Not to Enter the Brain
papers.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) is an important physiological barrier that protects the brain by preventing entry of harmful substances into the central nervous system (CNS). While this barrier is effective at blocking most drugs from disrupting the tightly controlled environment of 2 the CNS, certain classes of non-neurologic drugs can cross the BBB, potentially causing neurological side effects. Developing safer alternatives to these drugs requires a reliable method for predicting the BBB non-penetrance, whilst maintaining a high level of drug-like properties to the molecules. Existing regression methods for BBB penetration are inaccurate for this task, tending to overestimate logBB values due to imbalances in available datasets. To address this, we have developed a LightGBM-based model with a custom multi-task loss function that learns from both regression and classification data. Improving performance across classification and regression metrics, our model outperforms existing models in identifying non-penetrant molecules and achieves regression accuracy approximately equal to experimental uncertainty. Based on this, we introduce the BBB Exclusion (BBBX) Score, a scoring method which stratifies compounds by predicted BBB penetrance and confidence. To interpret model outputs, SHAP analysis was used to identify features contributing most to model outputs. We use these features to define threshold values associated with increased likelihood of BBB Exclusion whilst maintaining high oral bioavailability and drug-like properties required for developing a safe, non-CNS drug.

papers.title: How Tetrodotoxin Blocks Sodium Channels: A Docking and Geometric Perspective
papers.abstract: Voltage-gated sodium channels (VGSCs) are essential membrane proteins responsible for electrical signaling in excitable cells. Guanidinium toxins such as tetrodotoxin (TTX) and saxitoxin (STX) block these channels by binding to the extracellular pore region and have traditionally been understood to stabilize binding through multipoint electrostatic and hydrogen-bond interactions. However, the role of geometric constraints imposed by pore architecture in determining binding stability remains insufficiently characterized. Molecular docking of TTX and STX was performed under multiple grid displacement conditions, and the resulting pose ensembles were analyzed using spatial and geometric metrics. Center-of-mass clustering and distance-dependent affinity analysis revealed two distinct regimes: a deep pore region with convergent, stable poses, and an entrance region with dispersed, variable poses. Notably, the number of contact residues did not directly correlate with docking affinity, indicating that binding stability is not determined solely by anchor interactions. These results suggest that geometric convergence within sterically constrained pore regions plays a key role in stabilizing toxin binding. The rigid cage-like structures of TTX and STX appear to promote selective alignment with pore geometry, supporting a geometric constraint model of VGSC blockade.

papers.title: QFlux: Quantum Circuit Implementations of Molecular Dynamics. Part II - Closed Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Quantum computers offer a powerful platform for simulating real-time molecular and materials dynamics, where coherence, entanglement, and many-body correlations govern processes such as charge transport, tunneling, and spin exchange. Building on the foundations introduced in Part I, this tutorial presents practical algorithms for quantum dynamical simulation on qubit-based hardware using the open-source QFlux framework. We formulate molecular and spin Hamiltonians in the Pauli basis and map their propagators to quantum circuits using parity-based phase constructions and local basis rotations. Expectation values and state overlaps are obtained with the Hadamard test, or by direct measurement of Pauli strings, providing a unified protocol for extracting complex observables and variational quantities. We introduce the Quantum Split-Operator Fourier Transform ( Q-SOFT ), the quantum analog of the classical SOFT method for quantum dynamics simulations, which applies kinetic and potential phase operators in conjugate bases connected by the Quantum Fourier Transform to implement second-order Trotterized evolution. A simulation of proton transfer in an asymmetric double-well potential modeling a DNA base pair reproduces benchmark simulations. We also present a variational time-evolution scheme based on the McLachlan principle, implemented in QFlux’s VarQRTE driver. Applied to a two-spin Heisenberg model, it captures coherent spin exchange with shallow, noise-resilient circuits. Together, these methods establish a reproducible workflow—from Hamiltonian encoding to circuit execution and measurement—bridging classical and quantum simulation and providing a practical toolkit for real-time quantum dynamics on near-term hardware.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Identification and Validation of Non-Covalent Inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 Main Protease (Mpro) via Generative Design and Physics-Based Simulations
papers.abstract: The emergence of Coronavirus 2 from serious acute respiratory syndrome (SARS-CoV-2) underscored the urgent need for effective antiviral therapies. The SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro) remains a critical target due to its essential role in cleaving replicase polyproteins into functional nonstructural proteins required for viral replication. Its unique substrate specificity, evolutionary conservation among coronaviruses, and evolutionary divergence from human cysteine proteases make it a high-priority antiviral target. Here, we describe an integrated in silico platform, MedGraph™, which combines AI-based generative modeling, structure-guided docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations to identify potential non-covalent Mpro inhibitors. Five de novo ligands were prioritized using a GPU-accelerated docking protocol into the substrate-binding cleft of Mpro (PDB: 7RFW), focusing on engagement with the catalytic dyad (Cys145-His41), followed by machine learning–aided multiparameter optimization and 100 ns MD simulations for dynamic assessment. To evaluate chemical novelty, the CHEESE tool was used for Morgan fingerprint-based and electrostatic-based similarity analyzes against Enamine and ZINC15 libraries, confirming the uniqueness of the prioritized scaffolds. Benchmarking against the COVID Moonshot dataset further confirmed low scaffold overlap, with maximum Tanimoto similarity values ≤0.35, high lighting exploration of underrepresented regions of chemical space. The resulting candidates therefore combine pharmacophoric anchoring with scaffold novelty, providing both therapeutic promise and intellectual property differentiation. Independently, identified hits demonstrated strong and stable binding, favorable thermodynamic profiles, and complementarity with conserved Mpro residues. The distinct chemotypes observed suggest synthetic novelty and potential tractability. This study demonstrates the utility of MedGraph™ in coupling AI-based generative modeling with physics-driven simulations to accelerate antiviral discovery and providing a generalizable framework for the iterative optimization of structurally diverse and pharmacologically tractable inhibitors.

papers.title: Identifying Electrolyte Reduction Intermediates in Lithium Metal Batteries with Spin Trapping
papers.abstract: Despite promising developments in liquid electrolyte engineering for lithium metal batteries, solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation mechanisms from electrolyte components remain challenging to study. Here we establish an approach employing spin trapping to identify radical intermediates formed during electrolyte reduction. We use electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy to identify three distinct radical intermediates formed during fluoroethylene carbonate reduction that confirm a ring-opening mechanism. Our spin trapping approach further enables confirmation of radical identity with liquid-chromatography mass spectrometry and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy. The resulting SEI formed in the spin trapped system is investigated with titration and spectroscopic techniques to observe how stunting organic SEI formation reduces SEI stability and increases anion decomposition. Overall, this is the first time radical intermediates in battery interphase formation reactions have been directly characterized, affording insight into the complex mechanisms of electrolyte reduction and establishing a new approach for studying SEI formation and function.

papers.title: Solar Thermoelectric Cells
papers.abstract: To meet future energy demands while mitigating environmental impact, the advancement of renewable energy conversion technologies is essential. Solar cells represent the dominant technology for converting sunlight into electricity but have inherent limitations – including sensitivity to radiation damage, performance degradation at elevated temperatures, and intermittency. In this work, the potential of solar thermoelectric cells (STECs) as a complementary or alternative solar energy conversion technology is investigated. By testing STECs coated with organic photothermal materials ATT in indoor and outdoor settings, the performance of ATT-STEC was measured under various conditions, including intense sun irradiation and high temperatures. ATT-STECs saw voltage increase 120% with greater intensities from 1 to 4 suns and 170% with enhanced operating temperatures from room-temperature to 90 o C – while the commercial solar cell of the same size saw no change with increased solar irradiation and a decline in performance at high temperatures. Furthermore, under the same conditions, ATT-STEC was able to drive hydrogen production, which was not achievable by the commercial solar cell. These results indicate the unique advantages of STECs that are also the limitations of solar cells, suggesting broader potential of STECs as a complementary or alternative solar energy conversion approach in natural environments with intense sun exposure, high temperatures, and/or sizable temperature differences.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights into Nanobody-Based Quenchbody Sensing via Structural Modeling and Molecular Simulations
papers.abstract: Nanobody-based quenchbodies are emerging as powerful tools for the sensitive and specific detection of biomolecular targets. These fluorescent sensors contain tryptophan residues in the antigen-binding site that can quench (darken) a fluorophore attached via a flexible linker. Upon antigen binding the fluorophore is displaced, resulting in an increase in intensity. Recent quenchbodies developed against the inflammatory cytokine interleukin-6 (IL-6) exhibit variable fluorescence responses despite comparable antigen binding. To investigate the molecular basis of this discrepancy, we combined data-driven structural prediction with physics-based molecular dynamics simulations. Using a benchmark dataset of nanobody–lysozyme complexes, we first established that HelixFold3 provides more accurate structural predictions than AlphaFold3. Leveraging this finding, we used HelixFold3 to model the structures of the IL6-binding quenchbodies. Our analyses revealed that low and non-responders exhibit solvent-exposed tryptophan residues upon antigen binding, notably tryptophan 110, allowing fluorophore quenching and reduced fluorescence. In contrast, good responders adopt conformations in which these tryptophan residues are largely buried, resulting in a more pronounced fluorescence increase upon antigen binding. Together, these results illustrate that integrating structural predictions with molecular dynamics simulations offer a powerful framework for decoding quenchbody mechanisms and advancing the rational development of highly responsive fluorescent sensors.

papers.title: Plasma-Enabled Active Site Regeneration for Selective Liquid Fuel Production across Catalyst Binding Regimes in CH4-CO2 Conversion
papers.abstract: The selective conversion of CH4 and CO2 to liquid fuels is constrained in thermal catalysis by linear scaling relationships, overoxidation of oxygenate intermediates, and irreversible surface poisoning. Nonthermal plasma-enabled catalysis circumvents some of these limitations by introducing non-equilibrium excitation (e.g., vibrational, electronic, and dissociative) of molecular reactants. However, performance remains hindered by catalyst deactivation due to carbon and oxygen accumulation on active sites, driven by distinct mechanisms tied to metal-adsorbate interactions. Here, we show how continuous active-site regeneration during plasma-catalysis can be achieved by coupling plasma-driven dissociative chemisorption with targeted co-reactant activation. This strategy enables selective removal of surface poisons and is applicable across distinct catalyst regimes. On weakly binding catalysts like Cu, plasma-generated species remove adsorbed oxygen atoms, restore CH3O* intermediates and triple methanol selectivity. On strongly binding catalysts like Ni, accumulated CHx* fragments are selectively removed, doubling C2 hydrocarbon yields by reactivating C-C coupling. Unlike thermal systems, plasma excitation decouples regeneration from equilibrium constraints that correlate adsorption and desorption kinetics to a single gas temperature, enabling continuous, in situ removal of poisons without cycling and disrupting steady-state conversion. Using a combination of surface characterization methods and density functional theory calculations, we identify the mechanism by which plasma-co-reactant synergy tunes surface intermediates and redefines the design space of heterogeneous catalysis under mild conditions (Tsur = 473 K, Tvib = 4200 K, p = 1 atm).

papers.title: Global cost drivers and regional trade-offs for low-carbon fuels: a prospective techno-economic assessment
papers.abstract: Low-carbon fuels (LCFs) such as green hydrogen, synthetic hydrocarbons, and biofuels are critical for decarbonizing sectors that are difficult to electrify. In this study, we present a globally harmonized techno-economic assessment of 21 LCF production pathways, including power-to-X, biomass- and sun-to-liquids, and multiple hydrogen routes, evaluated across all countries and three future scenarios for 2024, 2030, and 2050. The model integrates spatially explicit resource data, learning-driven capital cost trajectories, and a dynamic, country- and technology-specific cost of capital, supported by robust scenario and uncertainty analysis. By 2050, median levelized costs are projected at 0.07 to 0.10 EUR 2024 per kWh for green hydrogen, 0.15 to 0.18 EUR 2024 per kWh for power-to-liquid kerosene, and 0.14 to 0.20 EUR 2024 per kWh for most bio-based aviation fuels, reflecting both substantial progress and persistent regional disparities. Our results show that while innovation, technology learning, and deep power sector decarbonization can unlock cost-competitive electrofuels in countries with abundant renewables, bio-based routes are frequently cost competitive for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) production in near-term scenarios, and solar-to-liquid fuels remain constrained by feedstock and capital barriers. The emergence of nuclear- and methane-based hydrogen as primary options in many regions, as well as the dominance of turquoise hydrogen in Russia, the Middle East, and Central Asia where carbon management is viable, highlights the context-specific nature of future low-carbon fuel systems. We also find that the least-cost logistics for global hydrogen trade will shift from ammonia shipping to pipeline and methanol delivery, with North Africa and Iberia emerging as leading suppliers to Europe. These findings underscore the need for integrated innovation, policy coordination, and investment strategies that address both resource and financial barriers, in order to achieve scalable, resilient, and cost-effective low-carbon fuel supply chains worldwide.

papers.title: Very Weak but Strongly Directional N-H∙∙∙π Hydrogen Bonds in Benzene Ammonia/Methylamine Solutions
papers.abstract: N-H∙∙∙π hydrogen bonding plays an important role in chemistry and biochemistry, from molecular recognition to protein folding and drug-receptor binding. Much of our understanding of such interactions is derived from X-ray crystallographic structures and experimental or theoretical studies of gas phase clusters. However, N-H∙∙∙π interactions have seldom been observed directly in their native liquid state. In this context, solutions of benzene, the archetypal π-system, with ammonia or methylamine, the simplest N-H donors, are an excellent model system. Total neutron scattering and simulation-based data refinement reveal that benzene solvation in ammonia and methylamine comprises ~17 and ~14 molecules respectively, with recurrent N-H∙∙∙π interactions. These hydrogen bonds show strong directionality in spite of a relatively long bonding distance of 2.55 Å and 2.75 Å in methylamine and ammonia, respectively. Methylamine makes a closer N-H∙∙∙π approach than ammonia, the latter being held away from the aromatic ring by the network of N-H•••N hydrogen bonds to the surrounding ammonia molecules, that is naturally disrupted in methylamine by the presence of the methyl group. Near the plane of the benzene ring, the solvation has six-fold symmetry and is dominated by bifurcated C-H∙∙∙N hydrogen bonds: the methyl group of methylamine enhances dispersion interactions around the ring that compete with the C-H∙∙∙N hydrogen bonds to structure the benzene's coordination sphere. These findings have profound implications for our understanding of this important class of weak interactions in solution, where the remarkable directionality at such distances is a structural driver in biological complexes.

papers.title: B(C6F5)3-catalyzed bisthiolation of terminal alkynes: regioselective metal-free synthesis of 2-methyl-1,3-dithiolanes
papers.abstract: We report a metal-free protocol for the bisthiolation of terminal alkynes with 1,2-ethanedithiol catalyzed by commercially available tris(pentafluorophenyl)borane B(C 6 F 5 ) 3 . This readily implementable, scalable reaction operates under mild conditions, showing broad substrate compatibility. Developed method demonstrates excellent yields and Markovnikov regioselectivity across a range of substrates. A plausible reaction mechanism proceeding via alkyne-catalyst zwitterionic intermediates was also proposed. Efficient derivatization of model dithiolane product highlighted its suitability for subsequent functionalization.

papers.title: Transient Reactive Grain Model with Uncertainty Quantifications and SensiTivity (TRUST) for Hydrogen Direct Reduction of Iron Ore
papers.abstract: Global direct reduction of iron (DRI) for steelmaking has marked production increase of over 25% over the past five years. As production increases, the need for robust computational models predicting the DRI process becomes critical. However, existing modeling approaches are deterministic, which do not account for the probability distribution of parameters. So, when these models are calibrated to specific experimental data under fixed conditions, they need extrapolations for other operating conditions. Here we present a Transient Reactive Grain Model (TRGM) with Uncertainty Quantifications and Sensitivity (TRUST) by integrating probabilistic uncertainty quantification, surrogate-based Monte Carlo propagation, and global sensitivity analysis with the TRGM. Gaussian process regression (GPR) proved effective in capturing the nonlinear model dependencies and enabling uncertainty-aware predictions. Monte Carlo simulations show that activation energies of conversion chemical kinetics in iron ore reduction dominate conversion uncertainty through the entire conversion transient, while operational variables have secondary influence, and temperature effects are mostly local. Early-stage conversion exhibits high variability, whereas later stages converge predictably, suggesting streamlined monitoring strategies. Correlation analysis further indicates redundancy in late-stage measurements, and global sensitivity analysis identifies activation energies as critical targets for calibration. TRUST provides a validated, probabilistic framework for risk-informed process optimization and experimental design, and can be generalizable to other high-temperature metallurgical and chemical systems, supporting uncertainty-aware decision-making in hydrogenbased steelmaking.

papers.title: EZGA: An evolutionary structure exploration framework
papers.abstract: Evolutionary algorithms provide a powerful route to exploring the structural complexity of molecules and materials, enabling most efficient searches of the system’s energy landscape to identify the minima related to stable and metastable configurations. Yet, existing frameworks often trade flexibility for chemical fidelity or scalability, leading to unphysical structures or overly restricted search spaces. The here presented framework EZGA is designed to overcome such limitations through a modular evolutionary framework that preserves chemical consistency while enabling scalable exploration. EZGA combines an interchangeable evolutionary pipeline with chemically grounded molecular and crystalline encodings, ensuring physically meaningful sampling without system-specific heuristics. A hierarchical Supercell Escalation (HiSE) protocol propagates low-energy motifs from minimal cells to larger supercells, improving sampling efficiency in extended systems. The execution model integrates synchronous parallelism for physical evaluations with an asynchronous multi-agent island strategy, while a hybrid SQL–HDF5 archive ensures efficient, reproducible, and fault-tolerant data management. Across benchmarks spanning peptide conformations, Lennard–Jones nanoclusters, binary-oxide convex-hull reconstruction, and CuO/Cu2O surface phase diagrams, EZGA consistently identifies low-energy basins, resolves complex phase boundaries, and achieves near-linear strong scaling. High-level YAML workflows enable autonomous discovery campaigns without manual steering, reducing human bias and establishing EZGA as a general platform for scalable, chemically consistent atomistic exploration.

papers.title: Life Cycle Assessment of CVD and ALD of Gallium Nitride
papers.abstract: Gallium nitride (GaN) is a wide-bandgap semiconductor that forms a cornerstone in several electronic devices in modern society, such as light-emitting diodes and chargers for computers and phones. Gallium production is increasing rapidly in response to rising demand, with direct implications for raw material extraction and energy consumption. Yet the environmental footprint of producing devices of GaN remains largely unexplored. A key step in making a GaN-based device is to deposit a thin film of GaN on a substrate. We present a cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA) of GaN deposition via atomic layer deposition (ALD) and chemical vapor deposition (CVD), incorporating process-level inputs and outputs. The analysis compares scenarios that include or exclude the silicon substrate and use alternative geographic electricity mixes. Our study shows that the electricity consumption and use of metal organic precursors for Ga are the environmental hotspots in both ALD and CVD of GaN. This makes the sustainability of production highly dependent on electricity generation. Depositions using ALD exhibit higher sustainability burdens than CVD across most impact categories, despite the much lower process temperature in ALD. This is driven by upstream precursor production and process energy demands. By including the silicon wafer in the LCA, impact dominance shifted to upstream substrate manufacturing. These results clarify the key environmental hotspots in GaN deposition and provide a basis for targeted mitigation strategies in semiconductor process design.

papers.title: Designing π-stacking aurones via metalation to square-planar Pd(II)
papers.abstract: Square-planar transition metal complexes supported with appropriate ligands can selfassemble via interfacing ligation planes. Here, we present solid-phase (x-ray crystallography) and solution-phase (1 H NMR) data that suggests the monomeric (L1)PdCl units π-stack, e.g. manifesting in dimeric adducts, while corresponding free ligand L1 does not. The x-ray structure of (L1)PdCl suggests that the native π-accepting character of the benzofuranone unit have been amplified by coordination to the Lewis acidic "PdCl." These aggregates also form in solution, with apparent Kdimer ~ 58 M. Main Text: Unique modes of self-assembly will be accessible to square-planar transition metal complexes because they lack apical ligands. Two square-planar coordination planes could πstack with one another if supported with an appropriate ligand, for example. 1-5 However, πstacking refers to a combination of attractive-e.g. electrostatic, dispersion, and donor-acceptor interactions-and repulsive forces-e.g. sterics and Pauli repulsion-for aromatic π-systems; 6-13

papers.title: Simulation of unimolecular fluoromethane dissociation on a quantum computer using the cascaded variational quantum eigensolver algorithm
papers.abstract: Simulating chemical reactions on quantum computers has the potential to offer insight that cannot be gained practically from conventional quantum-chemical approaches on classical computers. This is because quantum computing provides a platform for efficient, high-level electronic structure calculations that approach the full configuration interaction (FCI) limit. Herein we apply the cascaded variational eigensolver (CVQE) algorithm to simulate the unimolecular dissociation of fluoromethane (CH 3 F) by two pathways: (1) CH 3 F → CH 2 + HF and (2) CH 3 F → CHF + H 2 . We compare the results of CVQE calculations on the ibm_torino quantum computer to Hartree-Fock and FCI calculations on a classical computer. Our results suggest that quantum computing with CVQE can provide high-level electronic structure information for chemical reactions and other cases that require the simulation of multiple geometries.

papers.title: Electronic and Atomic Structures of a New Cu14H Nanocluster: Case Studies with SpectroElectrochemistry and First-Principles Calculations
papers.abstract: Copper-based atomically precise nanoclusters with discrete and tunable electronic structures can be synthetically tailored to enable applications in heterogeneous catalysis, sensing, and energy conversion. Unlike the better-known gold or silver counterparts, Cu nanoclusters often exhibit subtle optical and complicated electrochemical properties, making it challenging to determine their intrinsic electronic structures. Here we combine voltammetry, spectroscopy and spectroelectrochemistry to probe a new [Cu14H(BzT)12(TPP)6]BF4 nanocluster, with experimental observations supported by density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT (TD-DFT) calculations. Structure-wise, Benzenethiol (BzT) and triphenylphosphine (TPP) ligands form six S2-CuP units bound on a distorted Cu8 cage, within which four Cu atoms coordinate in a near square planar geometry with a single deuteride(hydride) located exactly at the Wycko position as an inversion center. The high uniformity of nanoclusters redissolved from single crystals allows for rigorous correlation between ensemble-based experiments and DFT calculations. The Cu14H features an electrochemical band gap of 2.3 eV, with oxidation of the HOMO quasi-reversible and reduction to LUMO chemically irreversible. The signature of quantized one-electron charging, featuring relatively uniform peak spacing in voltammograms, is obscured by the less reversible electron transfers and the interferences from intermediate species associated with electron transfer reactions. A general strategy for deconvoluting these complex redox features is demonstrated by varying the potential range, scan rate, and solvent in cyclic voltammetry, in comparison with those of precursor Cu complexes. Spectroelectrochemistry experiments resolve rich yet subtle features otherwise inaccessible. Through the comparisons of original and further oxidized nanoclusters, TD-DFT successfully reproduce the experimental trends which are explained by orbital reorganization and shifts in charge distribution. These findings demonstrate the e icacy and generalizability of combining electrochemical-spectroscopic and computational approach to understand the redox properties and electronic structures of material systems that lack or display weak classical diagnostic features.

papers.title: 9-Bismatriptycene (BisTrip) Enables Single-Aryl Transfer for Regiospecific α-Arylation of Carbonyl Compounds
papers.abstract: The α-arylation of carbonyl compounds is a cornerstone transformation in the synthesis of pharmaceuticals and natural products. Despite decades of effort using transition metal, main-group, and photoredox strategies, a general and practical α-arylation method with broad substrate scope has remained elusive. Here we show that 9-bismatriptycene (BisTrip), a rigid shackled form of triphenylbismuth, functions as a universal aryl group transporter, enabling controlled and regiospecific α-arylation across a wide range of ketones, including the construction of sterically demanding quaternary carbon centers as well as iodoarylation. BisTrip can be readily loaded with aryl groups from simple arylboronic acids in a one-pot procedure to give Aryl-BisTrip and is recovered in quantitative yield after aryl transfer to the carbonyl substrate. Significantly, the arylation of basic enolates proceeds at “warp speed”, reaching completion within seconds even at –78 °C, delivering record selectivity in a memory-of-chirality experiment. Computations support a low activation energy for the C–C bond-forming pathway that explains the preferential axial α-arylation observed in six-membered ring ketones. Collectively, these findings establish BisTrip as a powerful and broadly applicable platform with clear potential for complex molecule synthesis.

papers.title: A synthetic molybdenum hydroxylase compound that cleaves C-H bonds by hydride abstraction
papers.abstract: Molybdenum-dependent hydroxylases catalyze site-selective C-H hydroxylation reactions involving hydride abstraction pathways, yet no synthetic system has previously reproduced this reactivity. Here we report a synthetic molybdenum hydroxylase that achieves C-H bond cleavage and hydroxylation through a bio-inspired H⁻ abstraction pathway. A cis -dioxomolybdenum(VI) complex supported by a tetradentate [N 2 S 2 ] 2- ligand reacts with hydridic benzimidazoline substrates to effect net C-H hydroxylation, yielding the corresponding alcohol products (observed as tautomeric amides) and a Mo IV =O species. Mechanistic experiments and density functional theory calculations support a pathway involving hydride transfer to cis -O=Mo VI =O to generate a O=Mo IV -OH intermediate capable of carbocation/hydroxide rebound. The transformation is reversible and dependent on a sulfur-rich ligand environment, with a [N 2 O 2 ] 2- analogue showing no reactivity. Notably, the reduced Mo IV =O product undergoes biomimetic re-oxidation to cis -O=Mo VI =O using H₂O as the oxygen-atom source in the presence of a PCET acceptor (O 2 or 1,4-benzoquinone). Overall, this system establishes a bio-inspired H⁻ abstraction paradigm for C–H activation and charts the reaction pathways needed for catalytic turnover.

papers.title: Hydrogen Bonding Networks Formed by Hydroxyl-Functionalized N-Heterocyclic Carbenes on Ag(111)
papers.abstract: N-Heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) have emerged as robust alternatives to thiols for metal-surface functionalization, offering strong σ-donor character, high thermal stability, and tunable molecular design. Despite advances in NHC surface engineering, the formation of ordered hydrogen-bonded NHC networks remains challenging. Such networks are of high interest, as they can modulate adsorbate orientation, charge distribution, and catalytic properties. Here, we investigate a hydroxyl-functionalized NHC, IMes-OH (4-(1-(4-hydroxy-2,6-dimethylphenyl)-1H-imidazol-3-ium-3-yl)-3,5-dimethylphenolate (3)), on Ag(111) to achieve controlled adsorption and extended hydrogen-bonding networks. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, non-contact atomic force microscopy with O-terminated copper tips, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, supported by density functional theory calculations, we reveal the formation of linear hydrogen-bonded chains at low coverage and extended two-dimensional networks at higher coverage. Within our measurements, an upright adsorption geometry and coexisting binding modes, direct surface bonding and adatom-mediated bonding, are observed. Our results demonstrate that hydroxyl-functionalized NHCs offer new opportunities for molecular surface ordering and functional interface design.

papers.title: Correlative X-ray spectromicroscopy for quantitative cerium speciation in mammalian cells
papers.abstract: Determining intracellular metal oxidation state and speciation in intact mammalian cells remains a major analytical challenge, as most imaging methods lack chemical specificity or require disruptive sample preparation. Using cerium (Ce) as a model lanthanide relevant to environmental and biomedical exposures, we introduce a correlative X-ray spectromicroscopy workflow enabling oxidation state determination and quantitative mapping of f-elements in whole cells. Ce toxicity, uptake, and homeostasis in human lung cancer cells (A549) were characterized by scanning transmission X-ray microscopy (STXM), ptychography, bright-field transmission electron microscopy (BF-TEM) and viability assays across three sample preparations-chemically fixed, cryogenically preserved, and resin-embedded/microtomed cells. Ce was found to be membrane-bound and internalized, predominantly in the +3 oxidation state. EXAFS analysis indicates mononuclear or cluster-like coordination without precipitate formation. Active uptake processes drive Ce internalization, with intracellular Ce localized in autophagosomes and autolysosomes after 24 hours. Beyond elucidating Ce toxicity mechanisms, this correlative workflow is broadly applicable to lanthanides, actinides, and other redox-active metals for studying intracellular metal speciation in biological systems.

papers.title: Tunable Lignin-Based Hydrogels for Enhanced Water Retention and Sustained Urea Release in Agriculture
papers.abstract: Agriculture hydrogels with high lignin content represent promising alternatives to synthetic hydrogels, aligning with the goals of sustainable agriculture. In this work, lignin macromolecules were modified with pendant hydrophilic chains through graft polymerization of vinyl monomers initiated by cerium (IV) ammonium nitrate. Grafted lignins with varying compositions of grafted hydrophilic fragments, such as grafted polyacrylamide (PAAm), polyacrylic acid (PAAc), or their copolymers in different monomer ratios, were used to form hydrogel materials. The synthesized hydrogels displayed a wide range of properties due to the varying nature of grafted chains and crosslinker content. Specifically, hydrogels containing different amounts of acrylic acid fragments in the pendant chain demonstrated higher swelling capacities, ranging from 265 g H 2 O g -1 to 400 g H 2 O g -1 , compared to those based on lignin grafted with PAAm, which exhibited swelling capacities of 240 g H 2 O g -1 to 300 g H 2 O g -1 . Additionally, the swelling kinetics of PAAc-containing hydrogels were faster, reaching 90% of maximal water swelling capacity after the first six hours, while hydrogels containing exclusively PAAm chains absorb only 75% of their maximal water uptake. Introducing 2.5 wt% of hydrogel into soil results in a 25% longer moisture retention, helping to prevent drought stress in plants. Furthermore, hydrogel samples with incorporated urea demonstrated a sustained release of fertilizer, which should provide sufficient levels of urea concentration for crop production under real conditions. The germination index of wheat seeds incubated in saturated lignin-derived hydrogels confirmed that these synthesized materials do not possess a phytotoxic effect. Together with the ability to tailor the performance characteristics of the resulting hydrogels during synthesis, these designed materials can be considered sustainable alternatives to agricultural hydrogels and fertilizer formulations based on synthetic polymers.

papers.title: TIPS-Benzene-Based Two-Dimensional Perovskites
papers.abstract: A novel bis(triisopropylsilylethynyl) (TIPS)-benzene-based amine and two-dimensional organicinorganic hybrid perovskite materials comprising TIPS-benzene-based ammoniums were successfully synthesized. This work reveals the applicability of TIPS-based component ions to the crystal lattice of perovskite materials for the first time, promoting the development of TIPS chemistry, chemical materials that leverage TIPS moiety characteristics, and perovskite materials.

papers.title: TIPS-Benzene-Based Two-Dimensional Perovskites
papers.abstract: A novel bis(triisopropylsilylethynyl) (TIPS)-benzene-based amine and two-dimensional organicinorganic hybrid perovskite materials comprising TIPS-benzene-based ammoniums were successfully synthesized. This work reveals the applicability of TIPS-based component ions to the crystal lattice of perovskite materials for the first time, promoting the development of TIPS chemistry, chemical materials that leverage TIPS moiety characteristics, and perovskite materials.

papers.title: Topology-Directed π-Extension of Helical PAHs: Tunable Energy Gap and Excited-State Dynamics
papers.abstract: The topology of π-extension critically dictates the physicochemical properties of helical systems. Herein, we report the synthesis and characterization of two novel helically π-extended polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (HPAHs), 1 and 2 , derived from per - peri -perbenzo[7]helicene ( PB[7]H ) via central and terminal ring fusion, respectively. Structural analysis reveals that terminal extension in 2 yields a unique dispersion-dominated "π-clamped" geometry. While optical energy gaps decrease monotonically with extension size, oscillator strengths exhibit a non-monotonic trend, a "decoupling" phenomenon rationalized by transition-moment density (TMD) analysis which visualizes spatial cancellations of transition densities. Furthermore, transient absorption spectroscopy demonstrates that the rigidified inner rim of 1 retards non-radiative decay compared to PB[7]H , highlighting the role of polyene-like electronic character in excited-state dynamics. Importantly, these topology-directed fusions bridge the discrete energy gaps of the homologous PB[ n ]H series ( n = 5, 7, 9). This work establishes a design strategy for the continuous fine-tuning of chiroptical properties and dynamics in HPAHs beyond the limitations of discrete homologous series.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Workflows to Compute Large-Scale Sets of Absolute Binding Free Energies Aiding Drug Candidate and Binding Pose Selection
papers.abstract: Large-scale Virtual Screening (VS) campaigns of compound libraries can significantly speed up candidate selection in the early stages of drug discovery. The most promising drug candidates are identified by Scoring Functions (SFs), which enable VS campaigns to rank candidate compounds according to their estimated binding affinities. These SFs are typically trained on experimental data reflecting binding affinities (e.g. Dissociation Constant (Kd) values), commonly used as proxies for protein-ligand binding free energies. Since experimental reference data are often inconsistent between laboratories or even unavailable, we developed two computational workflows using Molecular Dynamics (MD) and implicit-solvent calculations to provide consistent large-scale datasets of Absolute Binding Free Energies (ABFEs), addressing two complementary aspects of virtual screening: quantitative binding affinity estimation and binding pose assessment. Our Binding Affinity Prediction (BAP) workflow estimated protein-ligand binding affinities for 4000+ complexes from the PDBbind 2020 dataset. Our Pose Selector (PS) workflow computed non-converged ABFEs from reduced-time Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations estimating stability for 800,000+ related binding poses. To produce ABFE data at this scale, our free-energy workflows classify, check and repair input structures of protein-ligand complexes in a fully automated fashion. The workflow scripts, molecular dynamics data and ABFE labels are publicly available, creating an extendable database of reference values for the development of Scoring Functions for Large-Scale Virtual Screening campaigns.

papers.title: Structure of Layers Formed by [2-(3,6-Disubstituted-9Hcarbazol-9-yl)ethyl]phosphonic Acids on Metal Oxides
Evaluating Transport Mechanisms for Lignocellulosic Inhibitors in Zymomonas mobilis
papers.abstract: The conversion of lignocellulosic biomass to biofuels and bioproducts is limited by small inhibitory molecules generated during the pretreatment process. The diverse compounds within the cell wall hydrolysate include aldehydes, carboxylic acids, phenolics and alcohols inhibit microbial growth by disrupting microbial membranes. Although Zymomonas mobilis combines high ethanol productivity with hopanoid rich membranes that confer solvent tolerance, hydrolysate compounds still inhibit microbial growth. One proposed mitigation strategy is to pump these molecules out through active transport processes, reducing the direct toxicity. However, if passive permeation rates are high, active transport would create a futile cycle where the exported molecules diffuse back in, creating a net drag on fitness. To investigate this hypothesis, we measure the passive permeation for thirty-three lignocellulose derived compounds using atomistic molecular dynamics simulations with enhanced sampling. Permeability coefficients determined spanned more than eight orders of magnitude driven largely by the balance between hydrophobicity and polarity. Hydrophobic inhibitors such as aromatic acids, aldehydes and short chain alcohols readily partitioned into the membrane and showed high permeability consistent with rapid passive influx and strong toxicity. Most polar molecules have lower but still appreciable permeation rates, with only the most polar sugars having low permeabilities. By integrating these predictions together with hydrolysate composition information, we find that most of these molecules are so permeable that futile cycles where passive permeation overwhelms efflux is highly likely. These findings provide a predictive framework for strain engineering, highlighting that lowering hydrolysate inhibitor concentrations through dilution may be the most effective strategy to productivity in industrial biorefineries.

papers.title: Morphogenic electrochemical solid-state interfaces
papers.abstract: Solid-state batteries (SSBs) with lithium (Li) metal anodes have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation energy storage technologies, offering higher energy density and improved safety over conventional Li-ion systems. However, achieving a stable Li metal-solid electrolyte (SE) interface remains a persistent challenge, as nonuniform electrodeposition can lead to morphological instabilities, filament growth, and eventual short circuits. In this work, we demonstrate mechanics-driven morphogenesis of the Li-SE interface during plating at zero external pressure, where chemo-mechanical coupling drives self-organized patterns analogous to growth processes observed in biological systems. The change in reaction kinetics due to the mechanical overpotential alters the free energy landscape, lowering the deposition barrier at peaks and accelerating filament growth. In contrast, the stress gradients give rise to an additional ionic flux toward valleys, resulting in uniform morphology and reaction homogenization. By investigating the interplay between mechanics-dependent kinetics and stress-driven transport, we show how different electrochemical, thermodynamic, and mechanical descriptors can together bring a stability shift from unstable to stable evolution. Under optimized conditions, these mechanisms result in a self-regulating interface morphology and suppress the onset of filament growth. The insights from this study provide a mechanistic basis for designing stable Li-SE interfaces, offering guidance for SE selection and interface engineering in SSBs.

papers.title: Defeating Multi Drug Resistant ESKAPEE Pathogens with Polymer Nanomaterials
papers.abstract: The clinical efficacy of antibiotics has progressively declined over the past decades as a consequence of the global spread of antimicrobial resistance, a phenomenon that is particularly pronounced among the so-called ESKAPEE pathogens: Enterococcus species, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Enterobacter species and Escherichia coli. Collectively, these bacteria are responsible for more than 50% of infection-related deaths worldwide, and multidrug resistance is highly prevalent among them. This alarming trend poses a critical threat to global public health and underscores the urgent need for innovative therapeutic strategies. One such approach involves the use of polymers as drug delivery systems for both conventional antibiotics and novel antimicrobial compounds, in the form of nanoparticles or polymer prodrugs, to circumvent resistance mechanisms. Other promising strategies are polycations with intrinsic antibacterial activity that act through mechanisms not widely exploited yet and polymers exerting photodynamic and photothermal effects. In this review, we summarize and discuss the current evidence for the efficacy of polymer-based strategies against drug-resistant ESKAPEE infections.

papers.title: Non-metal ionic clusters as 'soft' high-connectivity secondary building units for crystalline porous organic salts
Aligned Insulating Cavities for Metal Atom Binding on Conductive Surfaces
papers.abstract: Precise control over multiple coordination sites is critical for directing molecular assembly on surfaces, a challenge well suited to N-heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) owing to their strong σ-donation and tunable steric properties. In previously reported bisNHC systems, on-surface carbene generation from salt precursors requires elevated temperatures, driving adsorption into thermodynamically favored flat-lying configurations that obscure intrinsic binding behavior. Here, we employ isolable bisNHC derivatives bearing isopropyl and tert -butyl substituents, enabling their direct deposition as unprotected molecular precursors. Scanning tunneling microscopy and near-edge X-ray absorption fine structure measurements reveal that both derivatives adopt flat-lying geometries; however, their lateral assembly behavior differs markedly. The isopropyl substituted derivative forms mutually repulsive chains, whereas the more sterically hindered tert- butyl derivative (bisNHC t Bu ) unexpectedly assembles into a close-packed, dipole-driven molecular lattice. The bisNHC t Bu lattice is stable at room temperature but thermally fragile, underscoring the difficulty of accessing this architecture via protected-precursor approaches. The bisNHC t Bu lattice exhibits a wide spectroscopic bandgap and contains aligned metal-binding cavities that enable observation of spin-flip excitations of deposited dysprosium atoms. This molecular lattice provides a versatile platform for probing emergent electronic and magnetic properties and the single molecule reactivity of surface-confined, low-coordinate metal complexes.

papers.title: Tuning The Structure of Synthetic Antimicrobial Polymers (SAMPs) for Optimum Therapeutic response
Towards Realistic Fuel Cell Catalyst Degradation via Automated Identical Location-SEM-PSD Analysis with GDE Half-Cell Setup
papers.abstract: A realistic evaluation of electrocatalyst stability requires experimental setups that accurately reproduce the coupled chemical and transport environments of membrane–electrode assemblies. Conventional GDE half-cells, however, are typically operated without a proton-exchange membrane, exposing the catalyst layer directly to liquid electrolyte and intensifying dissolution–migration–redeposition dynamics. Here we examine how the presence of a membrane alters degradation in PtCo/C catalyst layers and establish a quantitative workflow for tracking nanoparticle evolution under realistic conditions. Particle size distributions (PSDs) are extracted directly from low-kV identical-location SEM (IL-SEM) images of intact multilayer electrodes and validated against IL-TEM for surface-accessible particles. Automated segmentation enables robust, high-throughput analysis across large datasets. Applying this framework to accelerated stress tests reveals that membrane-free GDEs undergo pronounced coarsening driven by severe Pt dissolution and redeposition under direct acid exposure, whereas membrane-protected electrodes constrain transport pathways and therefore exhibit more moderate, representative degradation behaviour. These findings underscore the indispensable role of the membrane for realistic half-cell durability studies and demonstrate that automated IL-SEM-based PSD analysis provides a powerful framework for linking morphological evolution to electrochemical performance in complex, multilayer electrocatalyst systems

papers.title: How Tetrodotoxin Blocks Sodium Channels: A Docking and Geometric Perspective
papers.abstract: Voltage-gated sodium channels (VGSCs) are essential membrane proteins responsible for electrical signaling in excitable cells. Guanidinium toxins such as tetrodotoxin (TTX) and saxitoxin (STX) block these channels by binding to the extracellular pore region and have traditionally been understood to stabilize binding through multipoint electrostatic and hydrogen-bond interactions. However, the role of geometric constraints imposed by pore architecture in determining binding stability remains insufficiently characterized. Molecular docking of TTX and STX was performed under multiple grid displacement conditions, and the resulting pose ensembles were analyzed using spatial and geometric metrics. Center-of-mass clustering and distance-dependent affinity analysis revealed two distinct regimes: a deep pore region with convergent, stable poses, and an entrance region with dispersed, variable poses. Notably, the number of contact residues did not directly correlate with docking affinity, indicating that binding stability is not determined solely by anchor interactions. These results suggest that geometric convergence within sterically constrained pore regions plays a key role in stabilizing toxin binding. The rigid cage-like structures of TTX and STX appear to promote selective alignment with pore geometry, supporting a geometric constraint model of VGSC blockade.

papers.title: Antibody-Guided Proximity Labeling Enables Selective Chemical Modification of Exosome Surface Proteins
papers.abstract: Exosomes have emerged as promising diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic delivery vehicles, yet precise methods for their surface engineering without genetic manipulation remain limited. Here, we report an antibody-guided proximity labeling (PL) strategy for the selective chemical modification of exosome surface proteins. By employing an anti-CD63 antibody–HRP conjugate, we achieved localized oxidative generation of reactive species, specifically oxoammonium and iminoxyl radicals, that target tryptophan (Trp) and tyrosine (Tyr) residues in close proximity to the antibody. This approach enables efficient biotinylation of exosome surface proteins. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this PL platform can be applied directly to exosomes within cell-culture supernatants. This method provides a non-genetic tool for functionalizing native exosomes, facilitating their application in complex biological environments.

papers.title: Diffusion-Regulated Cathodic Electrodeposition of Cr-Fe-Co-Ni Multicomponent Amorphous Electrocatalysts on a Nickel Foam for Integrated Alkaline Water Splitting
papers.abstract: High-entropy and medium-entropy alloys are attractive electrocatalysts for alkaline water splitting, yet it remains difficult to fabricate compositionally uniform MEA coatings on porous nickel foams by conventional routes. Here, we address this challenge using a diffusion-regulated, potential-controlled electrodeposition strategy enabled by a microphase-separated 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride-H₂O mixture as the electrolytic solution, which restricts multi-ion mass transport and promotes synchronized co-deposition. By tuning the applied cathodic potential, we selectively obtain either an amorphous Cr-Fe-Co-Ni MEA coating or a Cr-Fe-Co-Ni hydroxide layer directly on a nickel foam within a single electrolyte bath. The electrodeposited Cr-Fe-Co-Ni exhibits a homogeneous amorphous structure with a coral-like porous morphology and a markedly increased electrochemically accessible surface area, leading to the efficient hydrogen evolution reaction activity (η₁₀ = 71.1 mV; η₁₀₀ = 193 mV). The Cr-Fe-Co-Ni hydroxide@nickel foam delivers the strong oxygen evolution reaction performance (η₁₀₀ = 220 mV). When integrated as a Cr-Fe-Co-Ni ǁ Cr-Fe-Co-Ni hydroxide electrolyzer, the device achieves low cell voltages (1.55 V at 10 mA cm⁻²; 1.84 V at 100 mA cm⁻²) and stable operation at 100 mA cm⁻² for 24 h. This work provides a simple and scalable route to integrated medium-entropy alloys/hydroxide electrodes for durable overall water splitting.

papers.title: A Mild and Site-Selective Nucleophilic C−H Functionalization of Pyridines via its Stable N-alkylated Salts
papers.abstract: Direct, site-selective C-H functionalization of pyridines offers an efficient approach to both streamlined synthesis and late-stage modification of bioactive and functional molecules. Existing approaches to direct nucleophilic substitution typically rely on highly reactive nitrogen-activating groups, which limit nucleophile scope and functional group tolerance and often suffer from poor site selectivity. Although milder activating groups address some of these limitations, they generally require additional installation and removal steps. Herein, we report a mild and general strategy employing designed alkyl halide activators that enables one-pot, site-selective functionalization of pyridines with synthetically valuable yet challenging nucleophiles. This strategy allows, for the first time, direct pyridine functionalization with a broad range of phosphites and amines, in addition to methoxide and cyanide. The mild and redox-neutral reaction conditions are particularly well suited for late-stage functionalization (LSF) of pharmaceutically relevant molecules, enabling site-selective modification with both phosphites and amines. The rational design of the alkyl halide activators, together with careful analysis of side-product formation, reveals the delicate balance required for success with electronically diverse nucleophiles and suggests broader applicability of this C-H functionalization strategy.

papers.title: Base-Free C-N Cross-Electrophile Coupling via a Nitrogen-First Mechanism
papers.abstract: Metal-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen (C-N) cross-coupling-a philicity-matched reaction of carbon electrophiles with nitrogen nucleophiles under basic conditions-is a foundational tool in modern medicinal chemistry. 1-4 Here we report a philicity-mismatched nickel-catalyzed C-N crosselectrophile coupling (XEC) that combines carbon and nitrogen electrophiles. This mild protocol exhibits broad functional group tolerance including base-sensitive substrates and is compatible with late-stage applications. The necessary nitrogen electrophiles can be accessed from diverse starting materials, including C-H bonds and olefins. Strategic implementation of C-N XEC enables synthesis of designer secondary and tertiary amines, unsymmetrical diamines, and native amine functionalization through a two-step, one-pot N-phenothiazination, C-N XEC sequence. Mechanistic investigations suggest a unique nitrogen-first pathway involving N-centered radical (NCR) intermediates, which enforces cross selectivity by avoiding metal aryl intermediates associated with homocoupling. These findings establish a paradigm for base-free C-N bond construction and introduce a mechanistic rationale for controlling C-X XEC selectivity.

papers.title: 2,7-Diazatriptycene: Acid-Responsive Ternary Fluorescence Switching via Modulation of Through-Space Conjugation
papers.abstract: An unexplored 2,7-diazatriptycene exhibits protonation-controlled ternary fluorescence switching (on/off, cyan/violet) through modulation of through-space conjugation. Protonation also reorganizes crystal packing from herringbone assemblies to chargesegregated layered structures.

papers.title: A minimal machine-learning correction of DFTB Mulliken charges towards DFT-level MBIS populations
papers.abstract: Density-functional tight binding (DFTB) enables efficient quantum-based simulations for large molecular systems, but atomic charges are typically reported via Mulliken population analysis and often deviate from density-based charge definitions at the density functional theory (DFT) level. Minimal basis iterative stockholder (MBIS) charges are attractive due to numerical stability and reduced basis-set sensitivity, yet MBIS is not available in standard DFTB workflows due to the lack of an explicit real-space electron density. Here we develop a minimal, physics-informed machine-learning (ML) correction that maps DFTB Mulliken charges to DFT reference MBIS charges at the atom-wise level. The model uses only atomic identity, DFTB Mulliken charge, and inexpensive local-geometry descriptors derived from the molecular structure, while enforcing exact molecular charge conservation at inference by a per-molecule shift. Using 5000 molecules from the QM9 database split into 4000/500/500 for training, validation, and testing, we show that nonlinearity alone provides limited improvement over an element-wise linear baseline, whereas incorporating local geometric descriptors yields a substantial accuracy gain, particularly for carbon and nitrogen. The proposed correction provides DFT-level charge quality at a computational cost comparable to standard DFTB calculations and can be readily integrated into existing DFTB-based workflows.

papers.title: Scoring-Function-Agnostic and -Dependent Outcomes in BCL-2 G-Quadruplex Ensemble Docking: Polar Interactions, Not Molecular Flexibility, Determine Rank Divergence
papers.abstract: NMR ensemble docking rankings depend on both conformer selection and scoring function choice, yet no framework exists for classifying which outcomes are robust to this choice (scoring-functionagnostic) and which are sensitive to it (scoring-function-dependent), and the molecular basis of scoring function discordance for nucleic acid targets remains uncharacterized. We address both questions through pocket-driven ensemble docking of the human BCL-2 promoter G-quadruplex (PDB: 2F8U, 10 NMR models), cross-validated with AutoDock Vina (7,469 compounds screened, 114 ensemble-validated) and rDock (7,296 screened, 113 validated). Scoring-function-agnostic results include: the analytical framework (pocket-defined docking, Kendall's W concordance, sigma-scaling calibration), G4 vs. negative control discrimination direction, the W category hierarchy (G4-specific > overall), and the G4-specific cross-scoring rank correlation (Spearman rho = 0.632, p = 0.009, n = 16). Scoring-function-dependent results include: discrimination magnitude (Vina AUROC = 0.748, p = 0.010 vs. rDock AUROC = 0.602, p = 0.162), compound rankings (overall rho = 0.263, p = 0.111, n = 38; ChEMBL subset rho =-0.450, p = 0.027), and model concordance patterns. Molecular descriptor analysis revealed that hydrogen bond donor count (rho = 0.647) and topological polar surface area (rho = 0.525) predict rank divergence, while rotatable bond count does not, indicating that polar interaction parametrization-not conformational sampling-drives scoring function disagreement. Single-model screening recovered only 29-74% of the ensemble top-20, with Quarfloxin/CX-3543 as the only compound maintaining top-5 placement across both scoring functions. Ensemble docking methodology generalizes across scoring functions, while compound prioritization requires multi-scoring-function consensus, particularly for polar compounds.

papers.title: Glass fiber paper-based Corrugated Catalyst Substrates: End-to-End Modeling Workflow to analyze the Impact of Mechanical Production Processes on the Mass and Heat Transfer Performance
papers.abstract: Corrugated substrates based on glass fiber sheets are an alternative to common cordierite honeycombs as support for automotive catalysts, offering significant advantages such as lower heat capacity, increased intra-wall diffusion, and higher active material uptake. Depending on the heterogeneity of the glass fiber sheets and depending on the tolerances of the involved corrugation and winding production steps, the channel geometry of corrugated substrates can exhibit variability. The impact of these variances on mass and heat transfer is not known. Finite Element Method (FEM) modeling is performed to analyze the mechanical impact during production on the channel geometry and its influence on mass and heat transfer. This requires highly detailed Computer Aided Design (CAD) models of corrugated sheets and substrates. Due to the inherent variability and complexity of the geometry, common CAD tools do not deliver satisfying results. We address this problem by creating the models programmatically by script-based CAD tools. To capture the heterogeneity of the glass fiber material, the CAD models are based on corrugated sheet point clouds recorded via laser scanning microscopy. The mentioned methods are combined to an End-to-End Modeling Workflow which covers the total span from corrugated sheet point cloud recording to mass and heat transfer simulation of corrugated substrates. The proposed workflow is sufficiently generic to be applied to a wide range of CAD-FEM studies across various technical fields beyond the scope of the present work.

papers.title: Armstrong's Hierarchical Molecular Graph Framework (AHMGF)
papers.abstract: Traditional molecular formulas and structural notations (e.g., SMILES, InChI) compress multi-scale or hierarchical chemical structures into flat strings, capturing composition and connectivity for discrete molecules while obscuring layering, surface oxidation, and multi-cluster assemblies. This paper presents Armstrong's Hierarchical Molecular Graph Framework (AHMGF), a nested notation that encodes hierarchical relationships between chemical units, permitting core-shell structures, molecular clusters, sheets, and surface layers to be represented independent of explicit spatial coordinates. AHMGF represents each chemical unit as a node, with nesting denoting hierarchical adjacency that may be chemically interpreted as containment without implying spatial enclosure, and includes multiplicities to quantify repeated subunits. I define the canonical syntax, demonstrate an algorithm for constructing nested representations from layered or clustered structures, and illustrate the framework with examples including oxidized iron sheets, nanoparticle clusters, and supramolecular assemblies. AHMGF is purely notational and hierarchical, yet fully computable, permitting automated parsing, analysis, and integration with materials-informatics workflows while preserving intuitive structural relationships that are inaccessible in traditional flat formulas.

papers.title: F bond as a Unified Measure of Electron Correlation: From Aromatic Clusters to Metallic Superatoms
papers.abstract: We present a unified study of electron correlation across molecular and cluster systems using the F bond descriptor derived from coupled-cluster natural orbital occupations. We define F bond through a direct occupation-number summation over all correlated natural orbitals, F bond = i n i (2 − n i), which captures the total deviation from idempotency in the one-particle density matrix. Computed at the CCSD/def2-SVP level, all systems studied exhibit substantial multiconfigurational character when the complete natural orbital space is included: aromatic Al 4 2-(F bond = 3.84), antiaromatic Al 4 4-(4.03), planar and icosahedral B 12 clusters (4.42 and 4.99), heteroatomic B 6 N 6 (5.11), and cesium-aluminum superatoms Cs 3 Al 8 and Cs 3 Al 12-(5.58 and 7.10, respectively). We show that F bond is an extensive quantity that scales with the number of correlated orbitals, and introduce the perelectron correlation density f e = F bond /N e as a complementary intensive measure. This intensive measure reveals a clear separation: small clusters (Al 4 , B 12 , B 6 N 6) exhibit f e ≈ 0.07, while metallic superatoms show f e ≈ 0.04, reflecting the diluted nature of correlation in large delocalized systems. We demonstrate that previous reports of "weakly correlated" behavior (F bond < 0.001) in aluminum clusters were artifacts of natural orbital space truncation, and that complete occupation data are essential for physically meaningful correlation diagnostics. This work establishes F bond and f e as complementary extensive and intensive measures bridging quantum information theory and electron correlation across fundamentally different bonding regimes. We further validate the framework using analog quantum simulation on a neutral-atom quantum processor, confirming that the topological entanglement signatures of aromaticity and superatomicity are reproducible on near-term quantum hardware.
