papers.title: Fibroprinting -Hybrid Fiber-Reinforced (Bio)fabrication via In-Situ Biomimetic Spinning and 3D Printing
papers.abstract: One major challenge in additively manufacturing soft materials such as thermoplastics, elastomers, and gels is their low mechanical stability. Nature solves this by embedding continuous fibers like collagen or cellulose into soft matrices. Integrating 3D printing with fiber spinning has remained difficult due to limited material compatibility, restricted deposition methods, insufficient control over fiber properties, and lack of interlayer reinforcement. We present a spider-inspired technology that combines 3D (bio)printing with in-situ biomimetic fiber spinning. Fibers are drawn from polymer solutions or melts and deposited via controlled oscillatory motion, enabling horizontal or tilted freestanding fibers, precise adjustment of pulling speeds, and fabrication of structures with unlimited thickness. This method surpasses existing spinning techniques and enables complex, fiber-reinforced architectures for biomedical and engineering applications.

papers.title: Gas Adsorption & Selectivity in Five Classes of MOFs: From CO2 to Hydrocarbon Separation
papers.abstract: The rational selection of metal organic frameworks for gas separation applications remains challenging due to the complex interplay between framework topology, pore chemistry, size, and intermolecular interactions under operating conditions. In this study, a comprehensive simulation-based screening is carried out to evaluate the gas adsorption and separation performance of five MOFs, namely IRMOF-1, HKUST-1, ZIF-8, ZIF-68, and ZIF-69. Industrially relevant systems, including CO 2 /CH 4 , N 2 /O 2 /H 2 , and C 2 H 4 /C 2 H 6 , are systematically investigated. Molecular simulations are performed across the pressure range, 1-40 bar for pure components and binary mixtures at 298K to assess adsorption capacity and selectivity. Notably, the selectivity was sensitive to the molar ratio and pressure, underlining the importance of evaluating MOFs across a broad range of conditions for industrial relevance. For CO 2 − light gas mixtures, ZIF-68, 69 showed a non-monotonic dependence of selectivity on molar concentration. In contrast, for binary mixtures of light hydrocarbons (C 2 H 4 /C 2 H 6 ), all MOFs exhibited poor selectivity across all concentrations and pressures, with little variation in performance. This insensitivity suggests the limited capability of the selected MOFs to distinguish 1 between structurally similar hydrocarbon gases, which is in stark contrast to their behavior for light gas separations.

papers.title: A Reinforcement Learning-guided Genetic Algorithm Integrating Medicinal Chemistry-inspired Molecular Transformations
papers.abstract: Achieving optimal target activity while maintaining synthetic accessibility and drug-likeness represents a major challenge in computational drug discovery. Existing de novo generative models often yield chemically invalid or synthetically intractable structures and struggle to optimize multiple objectives simultaneously. Here, we introduce ALCHIMIA, an interpretable hybrid framework combining reinforcement learning (RL) and a genetic algorithm (GA), built based on a vocabulary of 33 medicinal chemistry-inspired molecular transformations. The RL component trains a policy network to prioritize transformation sequences that improve synthetic accessibility (SA) and quantitative estimate of drug-likeness (QED) scores, embedding these constraints directly into molecular generation. The GA component applies the learned policy as a mutational operator within population-based optimization guided by molecular docking, enabling exploration of diverse chemical lineages while converging toward high-affinity ligands. ALCHIMIA was applied to two different pharmacologically relevant targets, human Cannabinoid Receptor 2 (CB2R) and human sigma non-opioid intracellular receptor 1 (S1R). We considered three different scenarios: i) unconstrained hit-identification; ii) scaffold-constrained lead-optimization and iii) design of dual modulators. Remarkably, the framework generated chemically valid molecules with better QED and SA scores compared to random baselines and state-of-the-art de novo design models. By codifying typical medicinal-chemistry actions as learnable transformations and coupling multi-objective optimization with GA-based diversity maintenance, ALCHIMIA provides a practical, interpretable, and scalable framework for molecular de novo design. The developed RL algorithm is freely available as GitHub repository (https://github.com/alberdom88/ALCHIMIA).

papers.title: Circularly Polarised Luminescence (CPL) as a Contingency Assay for 'Mirror Life' Bio-Hazards
papers.abstract: Life on Earth is predominately based upon a single chirality set, but so-called “mirror life” - speculated life of the opposite chirality, either of artificial or natural origin - presents a low-likelihood, but high severity global biosecurity threat. Such an existential risk necessitates that technologies for surveillance and containment of mirror life are developed as a contingency. In this perspective, we propose a method for screening against mirror life hazards via an optical chirality assay, based upon circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) generated either via achiral fluorophores (via supramolecular chirality effects) or intrinsically chiral molecular probes. When bound to biological molecules, CPL-generating probes enable Enantioselective Differential Chiral Contrast (EDCC) imaging to verify chirality of a biological specimen. We set out why a multi-reporter panel approach – incorporating many CPL generating fluorescent/luminescent complexes – in conjunction with testing on conventional life’s chirality set, would be necessary to avoid false positives, and thereby screen against mirror life with a high degree of confidence. The all-optical approach could be deployed via recently innovated optical technologies, i.e. rapid CPL spectroscopy, CPL EDCC microscopes, and CPL EDCC cameras. We envisage that this CPL-based approach to screening against mirror life could be a useful tool for safeguarding against mirror life biohazards in a complimentary manner to any future legislative controls.

papers.title: Dimensional Reduction of Perovskite-Derived Structures in Formamidinium-Rich Lead Iodide Compositions
papers.abstract: Formamidinium lead iodide FAPbI3 (FA+ = CH(NH2)2+) with a cubic perovskite structure is among the most-studied or-ganic-inorganic hybrid perovskites. Despite several reports only on thin films of FA-rich lead iodide perovskites, such as FA2PbI4, their structures remain unknown due to challenges in characterizing polycrystalline films. Here, we report two new phases of FA-rich lead iodide perovskite-derived structures, FA2PbI4 and FA3PbI5, in the bulk form. These materials feature two- and one-dimensional octahedral networks of perovskite, respectively, allowing for the bandgap tuning among FA-Pb-I compositions. This study presents a novel approach to controlling the structural dimensionality of perov-skites and their optical properties.

papers.title: Optimising thermal pressing of airlaids with machine learning
papers.abstract: Airlaying is a promising alternative to conventional papermaking that does not require extensive drying. The key limitation of airlaids is weak fiber bonding, which results in low strength. Strength can be improved with thermal pressing, which however involves multiple process parameters whose relationships with strength are not known. Here we combined the benefits of deterministic linear models and probabilistic machine learning to improve airlaid properties by optimizing the conditions in thermal pressing. Our approach starts with a fractional factorial design as the initial sampling strategy to quantify independent and interpretable variable effects and their interactions. We show how these resource-efficient designs can be easily complemented with few additional experiments to identify more complicated behavior using a formal statistical test. We then identified three main challenges in optimizing the pressing conditions for our airlaids and tackled them with Bayesian optimization. Bayesian optimization improved the mechanical and physical properties of our airlaids which showed tensile performance comparable or higher than traditional wet laid paper. Our work is an important contribution for improving airlaid properties by thermal pressing to decrease the energy consumption of the forest industry.

papers.title: Electrochemical Tryptophan-Selective Bioconjugation in Neutral Buffer via Cooperative N‑Oxyl Radicals
papers.abstract: Protein modifications targeting canonical, hydrophobic amino acid residues remain scarce under neutral, transition met-al‑free and biocompatible conditions. Here, we report an electrochemical tryptophan (Trp)‑selective bioconjugation that proceeds in a neutral buffer without external oxidants. The method relies on a cooperative dual N‑oxyl radical manifold, employing keto‑ABNO as the Trp‑reactive reagent and 4‑oxo‑TEMPO as an electron mediator, together with NaBr, which suppresses over‑oxidation and radical degradation while maintaining low operating potentials. Under the optimised condi-tions, diverse peptides and proteins are efficiently labelled. Systematic cyclic voltammetry (CV) and UV–visible absorption spectroelectrochemistry (UV/Vis-SEC) suggest a Trp···keto‑ABNO pre‑association that lowers the oxidation threshold and reveal distinct roles of the two radicals, while Br⁻ preferentially stabilises the oxoammonium species rather than mediating redox processes. This neutral‑buffer, electrocatalytic platform provides a practical route to Trp‑selective labelling under physiologically compatible conditions.

papers.title: Molecular Flexibility-Controlled Ion Solvation and Electrode Reaction Kinetics in Sulfite-Based Lithium-Ion Battery Electrolytes
papers.abstract: The effects of solvent molecular flexibility on Li⁺ solvation and graphite electrode kinetics were investigated in lithium-ion battery (LIB) electrolytes using dimethyl sulfite (DMS), a linear sulfite solvent with high molecular flexibility. Raman spectroscopy revealed that, in the dilute solutions, Li+ ions are solvated by three DMS molecules to form Li(DMS)3+ complexes, whereas the corresponding cyclic sulfite solvent, ethylene sulfite (ES), forms conventional four-coordinate Li(ES)4+ complexes. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that the Li(DMS)3+ complex consists of two monodentate DMS molecules and one bidentate DMS molecule, the latter adopting the trans–trans (TT) conformer, which is thermodynamically unfavorable in the bulk phase, but becomes stabilized within the Li+ solvation shell due to the strong electrostatic field of the Li+ ion. As a result, the Li(DMS)3+ complex is energetically less stable than the conventional four-coordinate Li(ES)4+ complex. In the highly concentrated region, Li+ ions formed similar ionically ordered structures interconnected through bis(fluorosulfonyl)amide (FSA) anions in both DMS and ES electrolytes. In the electrode reaction, the dilute DMS electrolyte exhibited an exceptionally low activation energy for Li+ insertion at the graphite electrode, attributed to the easier desolvation of weakly coordinated Li+ species. However, its reductive instability led to DMS-derived SEI films with poor stability and rapid capacity degradation. In contrast, the highly concentrated DMS electrolyte produced stable FSA-derived SEI films and improved cycling stability, albeit with higher activation energy due to dominant Li+–anion interactions. These results provide molecular-level insights into how solvent flexibility governs Li+ coordination structures and electrode reaction kinetics in LIB electrolytes.

papers.title: Programmable DNA folding modulates phase behavior and dynamics of DNA/peptide condensates
papers.abstract: Membraneless compartments formed by liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) regulate biochemical reactions and play a key role in both physiological and pathological processes, including viral replication. In retroviral systems, the extent of genome folding is critical for the efficient packaging of new viral particles, a process mediated by the nucleocapsid (NC) protein that chaperones RNA folding and assembly. Here, we sought to elucidate how nucleic-acid folding and structural folding influence LLPS, and whether an HIV NC-derived peptide (HNP) can modulate this process through chaperone-like activity. To this end, we designed a programmable single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) library spanning varying degrees of folding and palindromic architectures, enabling systematic investigation of how nanoscale structural order governs coacervation. Using circular dichroism, FRET, SAXS, and coarse-grained simulations, we correlate DNA conformations with phase behavior and emergent condensate material properties. We find that interactions with HNP promote DNA folding, and that increasing DNA order suppresses LLPS, whereas structural disorder and palindromic linkers that induce DNA dimerization enhance phase separation by facilitating multivalent interactions and in turn, increasing condensate viscosity. Together, these findings identify two programmable determinants, local structural order and palindromic dimerization, that govern DNA/peptide condensate behavior, offering mechanistic insight into viral genome organization and guiding principles for tuning the physicochemical and material properties of synthetic condensates.

papers.title: On topologically frustrated polymers and where to find them
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of graph-theoretic topological frustration in quasi-one-dimensional periodic bipartite lattices that are based on the two-dimensional honeycomb lattice. Then we provide insights into how to construct such structures on the basis of the Tutte-Berge formula, Gallai-Edmonds theorem and quasi-symmetries. We notice an anomalous nullity in the graphs of such structures and suggest a possible explanation.

papers.title: Armstrong’s Exclusion-Zone SASA Formula and Model
papers.abstract: Solvent-accessible surface area (SASA) is a central quantity in computational biochemistry, structural biology, and molecular modeling, with applications ranging from protein folding to ligand binding. Widely used approaches such as Shrake-Rupley, Lee-Richards, and LCPO estimate SASA through geometric sampling or surface tessellation, introducing discretization error and significant computational overhead. Here, I introduce Armstrong’s Exclusion-Zone SASA model, a closed-form analytical framework that approximates solvent-accessible surface exclusion without explicit surface tessellation, using a physically motivated steric metric derived from atomic radii, bond lengths, and solvent probe size. The model enables direct and effectively instantaneous calculation of sterically adjusted SASA values while preserving the expected physical scaling behavior across molecular sizes. Benchmarking across systems ranging from small molecules to large proteins demonstrates systematic recovery of solvent-accessible microenvironments in compact systems and smooth convergence toward Shrake-Rupley and Lee-Richards values at macromolecular scales, with quantitative agreement emerging within the expected resolution of classical tessellation-based methods. Because the exclusion metric depends explicitly on geometric parameters, the formulation naturally adapts to bond-length variations arising from temperature, pressure, or conformational change, making it well suited for dynamic simulations and high-throughput workflows. By uniting analytical efficiency, physical interpretability, and asymptotic consistency with classical methods, the Exclusion-Zone SASA model provides a computationally efficient, physically interpretable approximation for solvent accessibility estimation in molecular modeling and biomolecular simulation.

papers.title: Direct Ketone Conversion to Cyclohexynes for Alkyne-Ene Reactions
papers.abstract: Cyclohexynes are highly strained intermediates that are largely underexplored compared to benzynes as their aromatic counterparts. Previous strategies towards generating cyclohexynes include accessing precursors with specific functionality such as silyl vinyl triflates, vinyl halides, vinyl pseudohalides, diazirines, carbene precursors, or diacyl peroxides among others. Ultimately, the stepwise buildup of these starting materials and the transient nature of cyclohexynes has led to their synthetic utility being limited to specific classes of reactions including cycloadditions and nucleophilic trapping. To address these challenges, we envisioned accessing cyclohexynes directly from ketones, one of the most abundant and easy to install functional groups. In this work, we report forming cyclohexynes from ketones via a vinyl triflate intermediate formed in situ. These cyclohexynes then undergo a cyclohexyne-ene reaction, an unprecedented mode of reactivity for this strained intermediate. The work presented herein highlights an alternative strategy towards generating cyclohexynes and expands their synthetic utility.

papers.title: In situ observation of ultra-giant spherulites in perovskite hydrates

papers.title: Defect-Topology Control of Anisotropic Lattice Flexibility for High-Performance Fluoride-Ion Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Fluoride-ion conductors show promise for next-generation solid-state ionics, but achieving high room-temperature conductivity and strong thermal stability remains a significant challenge, especially in rareearth fluoride systems, where vacancy formation, clustering, and microstructure intricately influence ion transport. Here, we show that mechanochemical synthesis followed by moderate hot pressing within the effective temperature range of 200-300 °C yields a tysonite-type Ca-doped rare-earth fluoride with high room-temperature conductivity. Within the low-temperature processing route, vacancy topology, c-axis lattice expansion, and grain-boundary structure are collectively optimized, resulting in a 5-orderof-magnitude increase in room temperature (RT) fluoride-ion conductivity to approximately 10 −4 S cm −1 , while also lowering the activation energy to approximately 0.4 eV. Thermogravimetric analysis, combined with time-resolved Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) data, indicates that fluctuations in conductivity can be attributed to changes in defect chemistry, particularly the formation of vacancies at the fluorine site. Hot pressing at 400 °C results in vacancy clustering, c-axis collapse, the formation of intergranular glassy phases, and a sharp decrease in conductivity to approximately 10 −9 S cm −1 , highlighting a trade-off among processing, structure, and ion transport. Notably, pellets pressed at 300 °C show slow conductivity relaxation over approximately 30 days under ambient conditions, indicating metastable defect dynamics and long-term stabilization. We demonstrate that near singlecrystal ion conductivity in polycrystalline tysonite fluorides can be attained not via densification or equilibrium defect optimization, but by kinetically stabilizing an anisotropic defect network through low-temperature thermomechanical processing.

papers.title: Composite Electrolytes from Molecular Crystals and Polymer Gels: Absence of Interface Effects
papers.abstract: Composites were formed between the components of a molecular crystal, (Adpn)2LiPF6, and a polymer/polymer gel phase by dissolution of all components in a common cosolvent. Upon evaporation of the cosolvent, it was possible to form the molecular crystal phase in the polymer gel phase when the latter was polyethylene oxide (PEO), or PEO, succininitrile and LiPF6. The composites had a uniform distribution of the molecular crystals in the polymer or polymer gel phase, the molecular crystals stiffened the films and the conductivity (σ) was a linear combination of the weight percentages of the two pristine phases, indicating that there was minimal interfacial resistance between them. This effect was attributed to the known fluid grain boundaries of molecular crystals that can be swollen with excess low molar mass ligands, which allowed easy Li + ion migration between the fluid phase grain boundaries of the molecular crystal and the fluid phase of the polymer gel. The gel phase was strengthened (qualitatively) by incorporation of the molecular crystals in the composite. When the gel phase was composed of a block copolymer of polyacrylonitrile and polystyrene, PS-co-PAN, a trinitrile ligand, 1,3,6-hexanetricarbonitrile (HCTN), and LiPF6, the (Adpn)2LiPF6 molecular crystal dissolved in the gel phase, except for the composition with the highest (Adpn)2LiPF6 content. However, good elastomeric films were formed due to phase separation of the PS block in the polar gel matrix.

papers.title: Armstrong's Hierarchical Molecular Graph Framework (AHMGF)
papers.abstract: Traditional molecular formulas and structural notations (e.g., SMILES, InChI) compress multi-scale or hierarchical chemical structures into flat strings, capturing composition and connectivity for discrete molecules while obscuring layering, surface oxidation, and multi-cluster assemblies. This paper presents Armstrong's Hierarchical Molecular Graph Framework (AHMGF), a nested notation that encodes hierarchical relationships between chemical units, permitting core-shell structures, molecular clusters, sheets, and surface layers to be represented independent of explicit spatial coordinates. AHMGF represents each chemical unit as a node, with nesting denoting hierarchical adjacency that may be chemically interpreted as containment without implying spatial enclosure, and includes multiplicities to quantify repeated subunits. I define the canonical syntax, demonstrate an algorithm for constructing nested representations from layered or clustered structures, and illustrate the framework with examples including oxidized iron sheets, nanoparticle clusters, and supramolecular assemblies. AHMGF is purely notational and hierarchical, yet fully computable, permitting automated parsing, analysis, and integration with materials-informatics workflows while preserving intuitive structural relationships that are inaccessible in traditional flat formulas.

papers.title: C5-Halogenation of Pyridines via Zincke Iminium Intermediates
papers.abstract: Recently, several methods for pyridine halogenation have emerged, but a robust 5-selective platform has yet to be developed. Here, we report a ring-opening, halogenation, and ring-closing sequence for C5-pyridine iodination and bromination. The process exploits Zincke iminium salts that undergo C5-selective halogenation with N-halosuccinimides, thereby switching the selectivity from the C3-position in our previous work with NTf-Zincke imines. The reaction does not require blocking substituents at C3 to maintain 5-selective C-halogen bond formation and tolerates a range of functional groups. This process accommodates pyridines embedded in complex structures, and thus has implications for drug and agrochemical development, where positional selectivity can greatly impact structure-activity relationship studies.

papers.title: HBAT 2: A Python Package to Analyse Hydrogen Bonds and Other Non-covalent Interactions in Macromolecular Structures
papers.abstract: Hydrogen bonds and other non-covalent interactions play a crucial role in maintaining the structural integrity and functionality of biological macromolecules such as proteins and nucleic acids. Accurate identification and analysis of these interactions are essential for understanding molecular recognition, protein folding, and drug design. HBAT (Hydrogen Bond Analysis Tool) is software for analysing hydrogen bonds and other weak interactions in macromolecular structures. This paper presents HBAT 2, an updated Python reimplementation of the original HBAT tool published in 2007. HBAT 2 is a Python package for automated analysis of hydrogen bonds and other non-covalent interactions in macromolecular structures available in Protein Data Bank (PDB) file format. The software identifies and analyses traditional hydrogen bonds, weak hydrogen bonds, halogen bonds, X-H···π, π-π stacking, and n→π* interactions using geometric criteria. It also detects cooperativity and anticooperativity chains and renders them as 2D visualisations. The latest version offers improved cross-platform tkinter-based graphical user interface (GUI), a web-based interface, a simple command-line interface (CLI), and a developer-friendly API, making it accessible to users with different computational backgrounds.

papers.title: Generalization of Bleaney's Theory
papers.abstract: Here, we generalize and unify Bleaney’s theory and related inverse-temperature expansions of magnetic properties of paramagnetic species. Our approach is valid for different properties, including NMR chemical shifts beyond the point-dipole approximation, and for both transition-metal and lanthanide complexes. We derive an analytical equation for the 1/T³ term. Furthermore, we implement higher-order terms numerically to investigate the convergence behavior of 1/T expansions. For transition-metal complexes, the second-order and third-order expansions provide quantitatively accurate results for most commonly encountered zero-field splittings. For lanthanide complexes, the newly derived third-order term substantially improves the accuracy of calculated susceptibility anisotropies compared with Bleaney’s second-order theory.

papers.title: Chemical Synthesis of Mirror-Image Proteins Reveals Chirality-Dependent Cellular Uptake
papers.abstract: Mirror-image peptides and proteins are attracting interest as therapeutics, key building blocks for constructing mirror-image life, and as tools to probe the origin of life. Their resistance to proteolytic degradation and unique stereochemistry make D-peptides/proteins particularly appealing for biomedical applications, yet a critical unresolved question is how their intracellular uptake compares with that of natural L-forms. To address this, we systematically investigated the role of cargo chirality in cellular internalization while maintaining a constant delivery vehicle. Three model cargos of increasing size and structural complexity were synthesized in both L- and D-configurations and conjugated to an identical cyclic deca-arginine (cR10) cell-penetrating peptide (CPP). By keeping the CPP scaffold constant, we reduced delivery-related variability and directly assessed the influence of cargo chirality on uptake. Quantitative uptake analysis using flow cytometry, gel analysis, and confocal microscopy across multiple mammalian cell lines reveals that L-cargos are internalized more efficiently than their mirror-image D-counterparts, demonstrating that cargo chirality is a key determinant of uptake efficiency across the chiral biological membrane. Collectively, these findings provide a systematic basis for further exploration of chirality effects in CPP-mediated delivery and may inform the design of mirror-image peptides and proteins for therapeutic or synthetic biology applications.

papers.title: From Single Injection to Dual Insights: Integrating EAD and CID acquisition for Spectral Library Generation and EAD-CID Spectral Matching
papers.abstract: Mass spectral MS/MS libraries are essential in non-targeted metabolomics as they facilitate metabolite annotation and provide the basis for in silico annotation tools and fragmentation rules. While significant progress has been made towards more comprehensive MS/MS libraries, those efforts have focused mainly on collision-induced dissociation (CID) and higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) based approaches. In this work, we introduce a flow injection MRM HR-based acquisition strategy that acquires electron-activated dissociation (EAD) and CID across a wide range of fragmentation energies within a single injection. The workflow supports both nontargeted and targeted analysis, through efficient library generation and MRM HR-parameter optimization, respectively. We apply the workflow via a set of 40 steroid standards, known for their important role in human health, disease, and doping, expanding the coverage of public libraries for both CID and EAD. Finally, we utilize public MS/MS libraries and raw data to reveal that EAD MS/MS spectra can, to some extent, be annotated via existing MS/MS libraries, governed by CID and HCD, and show that the acquired CID library enables novel annotations in publicly available clinical data, demonstrating its utility for biological studies.

papers.title: Mitigating Residual FAI for Air-Stable FAPbI3 LEDs
papers.abstract: Formamidinium lead iodide ( FAPbI 3 ) perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) showing record external quantum efficiencies (EQEs) are typically fabricated in a n-i-p structure through the deposition of a precursor solution rich in FAI on top of ZnO/ITO substrates. The ZnO electron transport layer is known to interact with the precursor solution during the fabrication, which can help to remove most of the excess FAI to ensure good stoichiometry and crystallinity as well as promote the formation of films with strong emission. However, residual FAI often remains on the perovskite surface, where it compromises device efficiency and stability. In this study, we introduce a thiol-functionalized tertiary ammonium halide, 2-diethylaminoethanethiol hydrochloride (DEAET). Beyond acting as a passivation agent via synergistic hydrogen bonding and electrostatic interactions, DEAET effectively facilitates the regulation of excess formamidinium iodide (FAI). This dual functionality suppresses non-radiative pathways and promotes radiative recombination. The resulting DEAET-passivated LEDs exhibit increased EQE and an impressive 15-days air stability without encapsulation. The encouraging findings of this study lay the foundation for the utilization of thiol-based salts as efficient agents for interface engineering in FAPbI 3 perovskite, that opens new possibilities for air-stable perovskite light-emitting diodes.

papers.title: Developing an optimal path fluorescence scanning method for identification of PAHs in mixtures
papers.abstract: Fluorescence spectroscopy is among the most commonly used methods that for analytic studies. The quality of the measured fluorescence data is dependent on various technical parameters. Among them are the excitation intensity, the bandwidths of the slits, the sensitivity of the detector, and the number of scanned wavelengths where the analyte emits. The shortest scanning mode is a single point measurement, which is very short and has the lowest potential to inflict photodamage to the analyte. however, such method may be blind to measurements errors since it does not show the whole peak of the analyte. The most common scanning method is the emission scan, in which λEx is fixed and λEm is variable. A less common method is excitation scan in which λEx is variable and λEm is fixed. Both methods may be restricted by the light scattering of the lamp at wavelengths that are close to the excitation and its double value. A more advanced method is synchronous fluorescence in which λEx and λEm varies during the scan with a constant gap between them. This method is less restricted by the lamp scattering and also display narrower peaks. The most comprehensive scanning method is excitation-emission matrixes that measure the whole fluorescence map. However, while using a system with a photo-multiplier detector, the scan time may be relatively long and cause photodamage to the analyte. In this work, we demonstrate a new scanning method named optical path fluorescence in which the scanning path is conducted from the maxima of the peaks toward their shortest way down to the noise level. We show that upon addition of increasing artificial noise levels, the optimal path method can predict the concentrations of the 3-polyaromatic hydrocarbons in a mixture better than all other scanning methods.

papers.title: Sputtered Ni and Ni₄Mo Catalysts at Low Loadings for the Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution Reaction in AEM Water Electrolyzers
papers.abstract: Reducing catalyst material usage while maintaining high performance is critical for scalable green hydrogen production via electrolysis. In this work, low-loading alkaline hydrogen-evolution reaction (HER) cathodes are fabricated by direct current magnetron sputtering of Ni and Ni₄Mo, providing a one-step, solvent-free route to catalyst-coated substrates. By tuning sputter power and Ar pressure, the deposited layers are steered toward rough nanostructures with increased accessible surface area, which correlates with improved HER activity compared with denser reference films, as shown by three-electrode measurements. The sputtered Ni-Mo has the targeted Ni₄Mo composition and exhibits a nanocrystalline Ni-fcc-type structure rather than the equilibrium intermetallic phase. Process transfer from planar substrates to porous carbon paper yields catalyst loadings of 0.046-0.186 mg cm⁻² (Ni) and 0.053-0.318 mg cm⁻² (Ni4Mo). Three-electrode electrochemical benchmarking showed decreasing HER overpotential with increasing loading, reaching ~104 mV at 10 mA cm⁻² for a NiMo cathode with 0.21 mg/cm². Implemented in a PGM-free AEM electrolyzer, along with an uncatalyzed stainless steel anode, Ni4Mo outperforms Ni at high current densities, delivering 1.95 V at 1 A cm⁻² and 60 °C (1.88 V at 80 °C) and enabling a mass activity of ~4.7 A mg⁻¹ at 1.95 V. A 500 h steady-state durability experiment at 1 A cm⁻² demonstrates stable performance with a reduced degradation rate toward the end of the test.

papers.title: F bond as a Unified Measure of Electron Correlation: From Aromatic Clusters to Metallic Superatoms
papers.abstract: We present a unified study of electron correlation across molecular and cluster systems using the F bond descriptor derived from coupled-cluster natural orbital occupations. We define F bond through a direct occupation-number summation over all correlated natural orbitals, F bond = i n i (2 − n i), which captures the total deviation from idempotency in the one-particle density matrix. Computed at the CCSD/def2-SVP level, all systems studied exhibit substantial multiconfigurational character when the complete natural orbital space is included: aromatic Al 4 2-(F bond = 3.84), antiaromatic Al 4 4-(4.03), planar and icosahedral B 12 clusters (4.42 and 4.99), heteroatomic B 6 N 6 (5.11), and cesium-aluminum superatoms Cs 3 Al 8 and Cs 3 Al 12-(5.58 and 7.10, respectively). We show that F bond is an extensive quantity that scales with the number of correlated orbitals, and introduce the perelectron correlation density f e = F bond /N e as a complementary intensive measure. This intensive measure reveals a clear separation: small clusters (Al 4 , B 12 , B 6 N 6) exhibit f e ≈ 0.07, while metallic superatoms show f e ≈ 0.04, reflecting the diluted nature of correlation in large delocalized systems. We demonstrate that previous reports of "weakly correlated" behavior (F bond < 0.001) in aluminum clusters were artifacts of natural orbital space truncation, and that complete occupation data are essential for physically meaningful correlation diagnostics. This work establishes F bond and f e as complementary extensive and intensive measures bridging quantum information theory and electron correlation across fundamentally different bonding regimes.

papers.title: Conformation-Guided Meta-Selective C-H Borylation via Metal-Arene π-Complexation
Continuous Flow Chemistry and Microfluidics: AI/ML-Driven Workflows and 3D Printing
papers.abstract: Microfluidics and millifluidics researchers have focused on devices for reaction and flow studies that use small volumes of liquid. Fluid control in mono- and multiplexed micro-systems is a design space not only for investigating phenomena and sensor development but also for small-volume production. It has enabled engineering, machining, and lithography for applications in chemistry, physics, biology, biomedical engineering, and soft robotics. Beyond lithography, 3D printing has made significant progress in the fabrication of microfluidic devices. CAD-designed devices and modules provide high design flexibility and electronics integration. With the appropriate 3D printing method, this can be fabricated from polymers: thermoplastics, elastomers, and thermosets, and in combination with formative and subtractive manufacturing. The form factor can depend on scale, design complexity, and intended applications. This article describes the convergence of microfluidics and continuous-flow chemistry (CFC) devices fabricated using 3D printing, mechatronics, and robotics for high-throughput experimentation. We also focus on integrating these devices across various investigation and production platforms for chemistry and reaction engineering. Advances in microfluidic and CFC devices, printed with multiple materials and featuring surface functionality, are highlighted. More importantly, we review the potential for artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML)-driven workflows, including simulation, modeling, data analytics, and self-driving laboratories (SDL). The critical role of 3D printing is emphasized as a tool for high-throughput experimentation. It will also lead the way towards the democratization of microfluidics and CFC with SDL.

papers.title: Symmetric VSEPR Geometries from Energy Minimization on a Sphere
papers.abstract: The basic VSEPR molecular geometries are derived by treating electron domains as identical repelling charges constrained to a sphere. In order to minimize the total Coulombic repulsion under the constraint, Lagrange multipliers and the Gram matrix are used show to that the minimum-energy configurations for 𝑁 = 2, 3, 4 are linear, trigonal planar, and tetrahedral.

papers.title: Divergent [3+2] Photocycloadditions of Nitrones to Isoxazolines and Oxa-Aza-Bicycloheptanes: Controlling Entry and Exit from Flatland
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional, conformationally rigid molecular architectures are increasingly valued in chemical biology, and drug discovery, yet their syntheses often rely on step-intensive or metal-mediated methods. Herein, we report a metal-free, redox-neutral photocatalytic approach that enables divergent [3+2] cycloadditions of nitrones under mild conditions. Visible-light excitation of an acridinium photocatalyst promotes cycloaddition of nitrones with alkynes to furnish densely substituted 4-isoxazolines, prototypical "Flatland" heterocycles, while engagement of bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes trigger rapid skeletal reorganization to deliver oxa-aza-bicycloheptanes that escape Flatland into three-dimensional chemical space. Both product classes are challenging to access using conventional thermal or metalcatalyzed methods. The transformation tolerates a wide range of functional groups and provides access to bioisosterically relevant motifs. Mechanistic investigations, in correlation with density functional theory calculations, support a unified photocatalytic manifold and clarify the origin of the divergent reactivity, thereby providing a platform for various downstream transformations.

papers.title: Decoupling Shape Retention from Polymerization Kinetics Enables Ambient-Temperature 3D Printing of Polystyrene
papers.abstract: Polystyrene (PS) is a widely used polymer with numerous structural and functional 43 applications, yet its additive manufacturing remains highly constrained. Conventional fused 44 deposition modeling (FDM) relies on the extrusion of pre-polymerized thermoplastic 45 filaments at temperatures exceeding 230 °C, due to the high melting point of PS, and cannot 46 produce crosslinked architectures. This aspect limits design freedom, energy efficiency, and 47 material performance. Here, we introduce a paradigm-shifting approach for ambient-48 temperature extrusion of PS using an oil-in-water high internal phase emulsion (HIPE) ink 49 composed of styrene and divinylbenzene dispersed in an aqueous phase. UV irradiation 50 during deposition induces instantaneous crosslinking of the continuous phase, forming a 51 thin hydrogel scaffold that confers structural integrity, while subsequent thermal curing 52 converts the oil phase into dense PS. This dual-curing strategy decouples shape retention 53 from polymerization kinetics, allowing for the printing of complex constructs at room 54 temperature. Compression tests reveal exceptional mechanical performance, with a yield 55 stress comparable to that of benchmark FDM polymers (ABS and PETG) and a maximum 56 compressive stress exceeding their values by more than twofold, highlighting the robustness 57 of interlayer cohesion achieved through in-situ crosslinking. Beyond PS, this versatile 58 approach could unlock new possibilities for scalable, energy-efficient manufacturing of 59 advanced polymer architectures, redefining the boundaries of additive manufacturing.

papers.title: THE SYMMETRIC HIERARCHY A GROUP-THEORETIC FRAMEWORK FOR PREDICTIVE DESIGN OF REFRACTORY MATERIALS (First-Principles Insights into Carbides, Spinels, and Amorphous Ceramics for Extreme Environments)
papers.abstract: The design of materials for extreme environments requires predictive frameworks that transcend empirical trial-and-error. Here we establish a unified computational methodology that integrates abstract algebraic principles—crystallographic symmetry analysis, group-subgroup relationships, and representation theory—with first-principles density functional theory simulations to enable rational design of refractory materials. We demonstrate that the symmetric hierarchy provides a quantitative foundation for predicting solid-state reaction pathways, assessing phase stability, and engineering thermal transport properties. In transition metal carbide systems M-W-C (M = Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb, Ta), we show that the most probable reaction pathways minimise the symmetric gap between reactants and products, achieving 94% predictive accuracy against experimental observations. Formation energies follow the hierarchy M6W6C < M3W3C < M2W2C, with energy differences correlating directly with symmetric gap magnitudes: ΔEf = –2.12 + 0.43·Δsym (R2 = 0.94). Percolation analysis of interstitial carbon networks reveals that carbon diffusion becomes rate-limiting below the site percolation threshold pc = 0.311, explaining the transient appearance of M2W2C phases in group V systems. For entropy-stabilised spinel refractories (MgxZn(1–x)/2Cu(1–x)/2)(Al0.9Fe0.1)2O4, configurational entropy increases monotonically with x from 0.90R to 1.03R, producing a linear reduction in thermal conductivity at 1000°C from 3.20 to 2.78 W·m–1·K–1. The correlation κ = 3.85 – 1.04·Sconfig (R2 = 0.98) provides a quantitative design rule. Phonon mode analysis demonstrates that increased configurational entropy decreases phonon participation ratios from 0.88 to 0.70 for high-frequency modes, directly causing reduced thermal transport. In amorphous systems a-Si3N4 and a-SiBN, we establish that local coordination symmetry—96% tetrahedral Si sites (Td symmetry) and 92% planar N sites (D3h symmetry)—is remarkably preserved despite the absence of long-range order. BN domain segregation in a-SiBN creates symmetry-breaking interfaces that scatter phonons, reducing thermal conductivity beyond predictions from simple mixing rules: Δκ = –1.2·finterface (R2 = 0.94). For HfO2–SiO2 glasses, thermal conductivity decreases with HfO2 content despite increasing density, due to low-frequency vibrational modes from heavy Hf atoms (mass contrast mechanism). Based on these validated principles, we predict 23 new refractory compositions with projected use temperatures exceeding 2000°C, including 12 high-entropy carbides and 11 entropy-stabilised spinel oxides. The most promising candidates—(TiZrHfNbTa)C and (MgCoNiZnCu)(AlCrFeGa)2O4—have configurational entropies of 1.61R and projected thermal conductivities below 15 W·m–1·K–1 and 2 W·m–1·K–1, respectively. This work establishes symmetry analysis as a fundamental predictive tool for materials design, bridging abstract algebra and engineering applications, and provides a roadmap for the next generation of extreme-environment ceramics.

papers.title: Microenvironment Engineering as a Design Principle for Suppressing Catalyst Metal Loss
papers.abstract: Stability losses in platinum electrocatalysts arise from dissolution, redeposition, and restructuring processes that are strongly shaped by the catalyst microenvironment. Yet the degree to which ionomer chemistry and support porosity jointly govern the true Pt mass balance has remained unresolved. Here, by integrating operando ICP-MS with an ion-exchange approach that quantifies Pt species retained within the ionomer, we distinguish apparent dissolution from actual metal loss across model polycrystalline Pt and supported nanoparticles. We find that direct ionomer-Pt contact enhances intrinsic dissolution while simultaneously trapping dissolved Pt ions, leading to a pronounced mismatch between measured and actual Pt loss. Extending this framework to porous and non-porous carbon supports reveals that pore confinement fundamentally alters degradation pathways, promoting local redeposition and suppressing net metal loss through a permeable 'lid' effect at pore entrances. Our results show that managing ionomer access and nanoscale transport within the catalyst microenvironment is a key practical factor in improving electrocatalyst durability.

papers.title: pH-Responsive Halochromic Biobased Polyketones Incorporating a Bifuran Unit
Multi-Scale Transformation of Nitrous Oxide into Functional Materials under Extreme Conditions: A Framework from High-Pressure Polymerization to Radiation-Induced Synthesis
papers.abstract: Nitrous oxide (N₂O), a potent and chemically inert greenhouse gas, represents a dual challenge of environmental concern and untapped materials potential. This critical review establishes a unified, multi-scale framework for the forced transformation of stable small moleculesexemplified by N₂O-into functional nitrogen-oxygen-carbon (N-O-C) materials via extremecondition synthesis. We systematically evaluate and integrate four primary activation pathways: high-pressure polymerization, cryogenic matrix isolation, high-temperature molten salt transport, and radiation-induced synthesis. The review synthesizes foundational principles and recent advances in each domain, highlighting the indispensable role of multi-scale computational modeling (DFT, MD, GEANT4) in guiding and validating experimental discovery. Using N₂O as a detailed case study, we demonstrate how the convergence of these disparate techniques enables the coercive formation of polymeric (N₂O)ₙ phases, metastable isomers (ONCO), and radiation-modified hybrids. The proposed framework not only charts a viable route to valorize N₂O into materials for energy storage, catalysis, and sensing but also provides a blueprint for activating other recalcitrant molecules (CO₂, CH₄). We conclude by identifying critical challenges in metastability, scalable synthesis, and in-operando characterization, outlining a forward-looking research agenda that bridges environmental remediation with nextgeneration materials design.

papers.title: B2Pin2-Enabled Chemoselective Ni-Catalyzed Reductive Ar-Ar Coupling of Two Aryl Halides
papers.abstract: A versatile Ni-catalyzed reductive coupling platform has been developed for the chemoselective cross-coupling of two distinct aryl (and heteroaryl) halides. The method employed B2Pin2 as a non-single-electron-transfer (non-SET) homogeneous reductant. The use of specific 2,9-dimethyl phenanthroline ligands (L1 and L2) and additives allows the protocol to be modulated, according to the electronic nature of the coupling partners. This includes the 1:1 coupling of electron-deficient aryl bromides with electron-rich aryl iodides, the coupling of two electronically similar (either rich or deficient) aryl halides, and reactions involving heteroaryl halides. These equimolar reactions afforded the biaryl scaffolds in moderate to good yields. Notably, a directing effect from nitrogen-containing heterocycles, such as 2-chloropyridine, 2chloropyrimidine and 8-bromoquinoline, further enhances chemoselectivity. Two proposals were implemented for the formation of a key Ar 1-LnNi I intermediate. One concerns Ni(I) reduction of Ar 1-LnNi II X generated from oxidative addition of Ar 1 X to LnNi 0 , the other emphasizes B2pin2-invoked reduction of Ar 1-LnNi III (X)2 generated from addition of Ar 1 X to LnNi I X. This cost-effective reductive system minimizes the need for an excess of one coupling partner in constructing biaryl scaffolds, and the mechanistic insights offer valuable guidance for the future development of cross-electrophile coupling methodologies.

papers.title: Geometry-Driven Excited-State Intramolecular Proton Transfer-TADF Modulation in Phenoxazine Donor-Amide Systems
papers.abstract: We report the first comprehensive structure-property-device study of phenoxazine-spacer amide emitters: phenoxazine-phenyl (1), phenoxazine-pyridine (2), and phenoxazine-pyrazine (3). This phenoxazine-π-amide platform exploits spacer identity and donor-acceptor geometry to regulate intramolecular N-H⋯N hydrogen bonding, donor-spacer dihedral angles (34-85 °), and HOMO-LUMO coupling, thereby tuning local versus charge-transfer character.

papers.title: Linking Electrostatic-Induced Chain Stretching to Heat Flow in Amorphous Polymers
papers.abstract: Amorphous polymers are soft materials whose thermal properties are dominated by weak, nonbonded interactions that strongly suppress heat flow, limiting the thermal transport coefficient, κ, to below 0.40 W m −1 K −1. Recent experiments, however, show that electrostatic modification of poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) can increase κ beyond 1.00 W m −1 K −1 in highly ionized systems, compared to κ ≃ 0.33 W m −1 K −1 for uncharged PAA. Using molecular-dynamics simulations of a bead-spring polymer model, we study the effect of ionization on κ in amorphous polymers. In agreement with experiment, we observe a more than 2.5-fold enhancement in κ, driven by electrostatically induced, local chain stretching that increases stiffness and the bonded contribution to κ. These results identify a generic mechanism for tuning κ across a broad class of charged polymers.

papers.title: Digital infrastructure to support daily high-throughput experimental materials research
papers.abstract: High-throughput and autonomous experimentation generate complex, heterogeneous datasets whose reuse, large-scale analysis, and linking to data from first-principles calculations remain challenging. Here, we report on an operational deployment of the open-source NOMAD Oasis data infrastructure as a digital backbone for daily high-throughput experimental work in a materials discovery group at DTU Nanolab. The customized platform supports the complete experimental workflow in a thin-film laboratory, linking physical inventory items, automated synthesis logs, high-throughput characterization data, and cloud-based analysis within a unified data model. The platform preserves full sample provenance across multi-step workflows and uses unified sample coordinates to enable direct cross-technique correlation. We demonstrate the capabilities of the platform on a combined experimental-computational project centered on phosphosulfide thin-film libraries. The data consists of 12,000 experimental samples acquired during routine operation over 18 months, complemented by more than 800 first-principles calculations - all managed in a unified data platform. We show how an open, extensible data infrastructure system supports reproducible workflows, scalable analysis, and long-term data reuse.

papers.title: Post-fabrication Reconfiguration of Hydrogels through Thermodynamic Asymmetry in Dynamic Chemistry
papers.abstract: Designing soft materials with adaptive properties requires internal chemical processes that enable reconfiguration across multiple system levels. Dynamic covalent chemistry has provided powerful routes to dynamic polymer networks, yet it is typically employed in an equilibrium-based manner where the identity of the dynamic bond remains unchanged. Here, we introduce thermodynamic asymmetry in dynamic covalent chemistry to enable the replacement of network-defining linkages after material formation, rather than their mere bond shuffling. For combinations of hydrazones and oximes, we demonstrate near-quantitative hydrazone-to-oxime exchange in aqueous conditions. Kinetic modelling quantifies that the exchange is dominated by a hydrolytic pathway with a non-trivial concentration dependence. This chemistry enables diverse reconfigurations within hydrogels after their initial synthesis, achieving near-complete replacement at material scale. Treating pre-formed hydrazone gels with functional alkoxyamines enables topological, mechanical, and functional reprogramming without network deconstruction. This work establishes thermodynamically biased dynamic covalent exchange as a generalizable principle for materials, surface functions or self-assembling systems, illustrating how molecular reaction pathways can be harnessed to deterministically alter structural and functional identity.

papers.title: Integrated Au-Nanocomposite Microelectrodes for Dual Detection of Phenolic Endocrine Disruptors
papers.abstract: 17β-Estradiol (E2) and bisphenol A (BPA) widely co-occurr in industrial effluents, plastic manufacturing wastewater, landfill leachates, and polymer systems, typically at nanomolar to micromolar concentrations. Their concurrent presence poses analytical challenges, as most existing electrochemical sensors are designed for single-analyte ultra-trace detection rather than simultaneous, application-relevant monitoring. In this study, a silicon-based microelectrode array is developed for dual electrochemical detection of E2 and BPA on a single platform. The sensor integrates Au-graphitic carbon nitride (g-C₃N₄) and Au-reduced graphene oxide (Au-rGO) nanocomposites as selective sensing interfaces for E2 and BPA, respectively. Ultrathin g-C₃N₄ nanosheets provide nitrogen-rich active sites and enhanced surface area for efficient estrogen sensing, while rGO offers high conductivity and defect-assisted electrocatalytic activity for BPA detection. Unlike single-analyte sensors optimized for ultratrace detection, this platform prioritizes robustness, simplicity, and multi-analyte capability aligned with environmentally and industrially relevant concentration ranges. With eight independently addressable working electrodes, the platform offers a scalable foundation for multiplexed detection of diverse EDCs, supporting point-of-care and in-field environmental monitoring applications.

papers.title: Rational Rigid-Core Design Realises Efficient and Colour-Pure Sky-Blue MR-TADF Emission in Boron-Nitrogen Functionalised Dibenzo-Xanthene
papers.abstract: In this work, we report the strategic incorporation of a 14H-dibenzo[a,j]xanthene (DBX) unit into the BCz-BN framework, leading to the development of a novel DBX-BCz-BN multiresonance (MR) thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) emitter. Interestingly, this structural modification preserves the sky-blue emission colour while significantly narrowing the emission profile by reducing the full width at half maximum (FWHM) to 17 nm. Furthermore, the singlet-triplet energy gap (ΔEST) was notably lowered from 0.17 eV (BCz-BN) to 0.06 eV, which effectively promotes reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) and enhances exciton harvesting. As a result, the corresponding OLED device based on DBX-BCz-BN exhibited an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 22.2% without any change in the emission colour. These results demonstrate that the introduction of the DBX unit is an effective strategy for achieving a highly stable, narrowband sky-blue TADF emitter.

papers.title: Chromium(III) amino-bis(phenolate) catalysts for the ringopening copolymerization of epoxides and phthalic anhydride: effects of co-catalysts and cyclohexene oxide initiators on copolymerization activity
papers.abstract: The amino-bis(phenolate) chromium(III) "ate" complex {Na[CrCl2L1]}, Na[1Cl], where [L1] = 6,6′-((1,4-diazepane-1,4-diyl)bis(methylene))bis(2,4-di-tert-butylphenolato) and the similar amino-bis(phenolate) chromium(III) complex CrCl[L1], 2 where [L2] = 6,6′-((1,4diazepane-1,4-diyl)bis(methylene))bis(2,4-dimethylphenolato) both show good activity for the 2 ring-opening copolymerization (ROCOP) of epoxides with phthalic anhydride (PA). These complexes when pre-contacted with co-catalyst, bis(triphenylphospine)iminium chloride, form bis(triphenylphosphine)iminium chromium(III) dichloride ate complexes, PPN[1Cl] and PPN[2Cl], that show further control and selectivity for the ROCOP reactions. The influence of cocatalyst, solvent, catalyst loading, and presence of a second epoxide for initiation of the ROCOP reaction were studied. The pre-contacted PPN[1Cl] catalyzes a faster polyester formation using propylene oxide and PA by using the more reactive cyclohexene oxide as an initiator. These polyesters have moderate molar masses, high conversions of PA to polyester, excellent selectivity, and narrow dispersity values (e.g. Mn = 6.8 kg mol-1 and Đ = Mw/Mn = 1.13).

papers.title: Nonisothermal kinetics of polymer melting through the analysis of peak temperatures
papers.abstract: This study introduces a novel methodology for the kinetic analysis of polymer melting processes, based on the exponential model of Toda–Hikosaka–Yamada, which originates from nucleation theory. The proposed approach utilizes melting peak temperatures from nonisothermal experiments conducted at constant heating rates and employs linear regression to simultaneously determine the nonequilibrium melting temperature T m and the kinetic parameters of the exponential model. While a similar linear regression technique has been widely applied to the power-law model of the Toda–Hikosaka–Yamada model, its use in non-power-law melting processes yields inaccurate T m estimates. The accuracy of both power-law and exponential models was validated using simulated melting data, and the methods were subsequently applied to experimental polyethylene melting kinetics. Results reveal differences in estimated T m values between the models. Comparison with onset temperatures from fast scanning calorimetry curves indicates that the estimated T m by exponential model is more physically realistic, consistently lying below the observed melting onset temperatures. To facilitate implementation, GNU Octave/MATLAB scripts are provided for researchers to apply the methodologies to their kinetic datasets.

papers.title: MillerBind: A Harmonic Framework for Protein-Ligand Binding Affinity Prediction with State-of-the-Art Performance on CASF-2016
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of protein-ligand binding affinity remains a central challenge in computational drug discovery. We present MillerBind, a novel scoring function based on a proprietary mathematical framework-Miller Harmonic Mathematics (MHM)-that encodes atomic and amino acid interactions using periodic harmonic classification and compatibility scoring. Evaluated on the CASF-2016 benchmark (285 held-out complexes), MillerBind achieves a Pearson correlation of R = 0.890 and mean absolute error of MAE = 0.78 pKd units, surpassing established methods including RF-Score (R = 0.80), OnionNet-2 (R = 0.82), PIGNet (R = 0.83), IGN (R = 0.85), and DeepDTA (R = 0.88). The model uses an ensemble of gradient-boosted and bagged decision trees with 487 interpretable features, requires no GPU, and predicts in under 1 millisecond per complex. We further demonstrate that the framework extends to protein-protein interactions (PPI), achieving MAE = 0.985 kcal/mol on 15 historically "undruggable" PPI targets-outperforming PCANN (1.27), BindPPI (1.40), and PRODIGY (1.4). Applied to microtubule pharmacology, the framework classifies all 24 tested microtubule-targeting agents as stabilizers or destabilizers with 100% accuracy. Finally, we show that MHM principles applied as reasoning middleware to a 7B-parameter large language model improve TruthfulQA accuracy by +4.94 percentage points without model retraining. These results establish Miller Harmonic Mathematics as a unified framework for molecular interaction modeling with demonstrated applications across drug discovery, structural biology, and artificial intelligence.

papers.title: A Concise Enantioselective Formal Synthesis of the Second-Generation Oral Contraceptive Levonorgestrel
papers.abstract: A concise formal synthesis of levonorgestrel (LNG) precursor, a natural 18a-homoestrone, 13-ethyl-3methoxy-gona-2,5(10)-dien-17-one (11) is described, in which the steroid core of LNG is formed by enantioselective CRED bioreduction of prochiral secodione 4 followed by Torgov cyclization as the key steps.

papers.title: Ambient Photocatalytic Conversion of Atmospheric CO₂ and H₂O to Polyoxymethylene Via a Redox-Active Titanium-Phenanthroline Matrix
papers.abstract: A light-driven, ambient-temperature pathway is described for converting atmospheric CO₂ and water directly into polyoxymethylene-type (POM) oligomers containing up to ~30-CH₂O-units, enabled by a hydrolyzed titanium(IV) chloride-1,10-phenanthroline (phen) matrix. Spontaneous hydrolysis of phen•TiCl₄ by trace water generates a disordered but catalytically competent ensemble of Ti-oxo, Ti-hydroxy, Ti-Cl, and phen-supported species. Water plays a dual role, initiating hydrolytic assembly of redox-active titanium clusters while supplying the protons and oxygen incorporated during CO₂ activation and chain propagation. nucleophilic attack by Ti-bound hydroxyls or oligomer termini, enabling sequential CH₂O insertion and controlled POM growth. MALDI-TOF mass spectra display regular m/z spacing corresponding to CH₂O extension, supported by ¹H/¹³C NMR and FTIR signatures of hydroxyl-terminated acetal chains HCOO-(CH₂-O)-H. These results establish a radical-driven, acetal-forming mechanism that integrates CO₂ capture, reduction, and polymer construction directly from atmospheric inputs under visible light.

papers.title: Accelerating Superconductor Discovery with Disorder-Aware Multi-Fidelity Graph Transformers
papers.abstract: Discovering new superconductors with high critical temperature Tc remains challenging because reliable experimental data are scarce and real materials frequently exhibit crystallographic disorder that is difficult to represent faithfully in machine-learning models. We present FiDeTGraph, a disorder-aware, multi-fidelity SE(3)-equivariant graph transformer for predicting superconducting Tc from 3D crystal structures. FiDeTGraph addresses two practical bottlenecks in data-driven superconductivity: (i) the tendency of prior disorder handling to collapse substitutional/positional disorder into occupancy-weighted averages that obscure local variations, and (ii) the limited coverage of high-fidelity superconducting datasets. To capture disorder explicitly, we introduce virtual nodes placed at the centroid of each disordered cluster and connect them bidirectionally to the constituent atomic instances, enabling the network to learn higher-order disorder effects without linear mixing. To mitigate data scarcity, we propose a multi-fidelity learning strategy that combines high-fidelity SuperCon3D structures with low-fidelity 3DSCMP and supercell-permuted variants that sample plausible disorder realizations, and we condition predictions on a learned graph-level fidelity embedding. Across 10-fold cross-validation on SuperCon3D, virtual-node modeling improves performance over occupancy-summation baselines, and FiDeTGraph further benefits from low-fidelity augmentation, yielding consistent gains on both the full set and the disorder-only subset. Finally, we integrate FiDeTGraph into a high-throughput screening pipeline over the ICSD and Materials Project databases, applying stability and metallicity filters to prioritize synthesizable candidates for downstream first-principles verification. Our results show that jointly modeling disorder and exploiting multi-fidelity data can substantially improve Tc prediction and accelerate the identification of promising superconducting materials.

papers.title: Soft Specialization via Mixture-of-Experts Enables Accurate Prediction of Superconducting Tc from Crystal Structures
papers.abstract: Predicting superconducting critical temperature (T c) from crystal structure is challenging due to diverse material families with distinct physical mechanisms and structural complexities like siteoccupation disorder. We introduce Superconductor Mixture of Experts (SuMoE), a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture using multiple Graph Neural Network experts with learned routing, achieving MAE of 0.671 logK on the SuperCon3D dataset, significantly outperforming both a state-of-the-art single generalist Graph Neural Network (0.709 logK) and isolated family-specific specialists (0.683 logK). While traditional intuition suggests models should specialize in rigid material families, our analysis reveals a more sophisticated regime of soft specialization. We find that experts specialize in underlying physical mechanisms rather than arbitrary labels, for instance, a single expert dominates predictions for both Cuprates and Heavy Fermion systems, effectively capturing the physics of strongly correlated electrons across chemically distinct families. Crucially, the model couples this specialized knowledge with a diffuse routing mechanism that synthesizes insights from multiple experts, ensuring robustness through redundancy. Our work demonstrates that for complex structure-property relationships, the most effective paradigm is not specialization but integrative prediction, where the model learns to synthesize complementary insights to form a single, robust prediction.

papers.title: Harnessing the Reactivity of Sulfinate Salts with Cystine: An Umpolung Approach to Residue-Specific Peptide Modification
papers.abstract: The first use of sulfinate salts for the late-stage modification of peptidic disulfide bonds is reported. While the majority of cysteine-based peptide modifications rely on the nucleophilicity of the side-chain thiol functionality, umpolung approaches-exploiting instead the electrophilicity of the cystine disulfide-are underexplored. Using structurallydiverse sulfinate salts, we have optimized a mild, photochemical strategy for the generation and coupling of carbon-centered radicals with both symmetrical and electronically-distinct, unsymmetrical cystine disulfides using high-throughput experimentation techniques. A library of modified peptides was accessible, as confirmed by qualitative and quantitative analytical data, providing valuable insights into the matched reactivity of specific radical/disulfide substrate pairings. The method was broadly compatible with a range of unprotected amino acids, including His, Trp and Tyr, and can be used for the functionalization of biologically relevant peptides, as exemplified by the late-stage modification of a semaglutide analogue and the preparation of high-value macrocyclic peptides.

papers.title: Computational Progress of Designing Single Atom Alloy Catalysts for Methane Activation
papers.abstract: Nonoxidative coupling of methane to value-added hydrocarbons remains a major challenge in catalysis due to inert C-H bonds in methane and rapid catalyst deactivation caused by coke contamination. Single atom alloys (SAAs), atomically dispersing isolated metal atoms into a host metal surface, have emerged as promising catalysts for activating light alkanes. Here, we present a review of recent progresses on designing SAA catalysts for efficient and selective conversion of methane and other alkanes using computational modeling tools, including quantum mechanical simulations and machine learning models. First, we describe the various studies of applying firstprinciples simulations to discern reaction mechanisms, to understand the role of isolated dopant atoms in reducing C-H activation barriers, and to rationalize the synergy between dopant and host in improving selectivity towards desired products. Next, we present how the rapid development of machine learning models enables high-throughput screening of a large chemical space of SAA catalysts for methane transformation. We then extend the discussion from methane to the chemistry of activating other light alkanes, demonstrating the transferability of the synergy between dopant and host to activate multi-carbon hydrocarbons. Finally, we provide some perspectives on the future outlook for computational SAA catalyst design for methane activation.

papers.title: Topological effects of bottlebrush copolymers on their assembly at the water/air interface
papers.abstract: Amphiphilic bottlebrush copolymers offer exceptional tunability through their grafted side-chain architectures, yet the molecular principles linking topology to interfacial assembly remain incompletely understood. Here, we use coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the influence of three topological design parameters: block length (l), side-chain dispersity (Ð), and grafting density (f) on the assembly of PEG-PS (PEG: poly(ethylene glycol), PS: polystyrene) bottlebrush copolymers at the water/air interface. The assembled structures are characterized by three methods: the surface covered area, the average radius of gyration of PEG-PS chains, and the hydration of PEG. By varying each parameter while keeping overall hydrophilic and hydrophobic content fixed, we identify the distinct physical mechanisms by which topology dictates molecular organization at the interface. Increasing block length enhances PEG-PS segregation, producing a few-percent reduction in chain dimensions and a 1 tens-of-percent decrease in surface covered area, making block length the strongest determinant of packing. In contrast, the dispersity and grafting density of PEG and PS induces only minor changes (∼ 5 − 10%) in the surface covered area at the studied range. The hydration of hydrophilic chains varies differently with the three topological design parameters. The grafting density significantly impacts the hydration of PEG side chains, while the block length and the dispersity play a minor role in the local water structures. The simulations provide insights into the experimentally observed differences in the surface packing and interfacial tensions of bottlebrush copolymers. This work establishes a topology-assembly relationship and provides molecular-level design principles for bottlebrush copolymers.

papers.title: Aligning Mass Spectrometry with Molecular Representations for Guiding de novo Structure Prediction
papers.abstract: Interpreting mass spectrometry (MS) data is challenging because reconstructing molecular structures from fragment patterns is an inherently ambiguous task, even for experienced analysts. Recent advances in MS instrumentation and acquisition protocols have created new opportunities for data-driven structural elucidation by leveraging large amounts of experimental spectra. This work presents DeniMS, a deep learning framework for a de novo generation of molecular structures from tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) data. We use a contrastive learning strategy to train a model to produce a joint representation that aligns spectra with their corresponding molecular graphs, resulting in embeddings that organize MS data in a chemically meaningful manner. These MS embeddings then guide a discrete graph diffusion model to predict molecular structures directly from spectra. Rather than returning a single answer, the model produces a ranked list of plausible structures, which better reflects practical MS/MS analysis, where isomers and closely related compounds can yield similar spectra. The framework can also integrate multiple spectra per molecule, improving robustness by pooling complementary evidence across measurements. We train and evaluate the method on the open FragHub dataset and release the code and pretrained models at https://github.com/Milo-group/DeniMS.

papers.title: Computational Prediction of Moiré Superlattice Engineering in Magic-Angle Twisted Bilayer Graphene: A Literature-Validated Framework for Molecular Filtration and Electrochemical Applications
papers.abstract: We present a literature-validated computational framework for magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) heterostructures at θ = 1.05° ± 0.05° investigating two potential room-temperature applications through synergistic moiré engineering. The framework employs density functional theory (DFT-D3 with VASP 6.3.0, 600 eV cutoff, 18×18×1 k-mesh for ~15,500-atom supercell), molecular dynamics (LAMMPS with AIREBO/TIP4P/2005, 50 ns production), and grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations validated against 18 peer-reviewed experimental studies. For molecular filtration, we predict water flux 180-450 L/m²/h at 2-10 bar with >99.5% NaCl rejection through precision nanopores (3.0 ± 0.1 Å diameter, 10¹²-10¹³ pores/cm²) positioned at AA stacking sites with 13.4 nm moiré periodicity-representing 2.7-6.8× flux enhancement versus single-layer graphene literature baseline (66 L/m²/h per bar). For electrochemical energy storage, calculated 153× density of states enhancement (147 ± 15 states/(eV•cell) versus 0.96 for pristine graphene) produces quantum capacitance CQ ≈ 535 µF/cm², enabling predicted specific capacitance >300 F/g-representing conservative 1.2-1.5× enhancement over activated carbon supercapacitors (150-250 F/g) with simultaneous high energy density (50-90 Wh/kg) and power density (10-15 kW/kg). Complete experimental protocols disclosed for independent verification: CVD synthesis (1030°C, CH₄/H₂), angular alignment (±0.03° precision via crossed polarizers or ±0.05° via machine vision), electron beam nanopore drilling (STEM, 80-120 keV, controlled dwell), and performance characterization (ASTM E2550-17, IEC 62391-1). This computational methodology establishes a conservative framework for translating magic-angle TBG physics from cryogenic quantum phenomena into functional roomtemperature applications, with all predictions anchored to experimental literature benchmarks.

papers.title: Synthesis and Vibrational Identification of the Uranyl Peroxodicarbonate [UO2(O2)(CO3)3]4-: Insights into Peroxo-Carbonate Bonding from 18O Labeling, DFT and QTAIM analysis
papers.abstract: In carbonate-rich aqueous environments relevant to spent nuclear fuel storage, the coexistence of carbonate species and radiolytically generated H 2 O 2 is expected to promote the formation of uranyl peroxo-carbonate complexes under mild conditions. Despite their importance, reliable vibrational markers for uranyl peroxo-carbonate complexes remain scarce, and several reported spectral assignments remain controversial. Here, we report the first unambiguous solution-phase characterization of the peroxo-dicarbonate species M x [UO 2 (O 2 )(CO 3 ) 2 ] (4-x)- (M = Na + or K + ) by combining Raman spectroscopy with 18 O-labeled H 2 O 2 , Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Distinct vibrational fingerprints are identified for M x [UO 2 (O 2 )(CO 3 ) 2 ] (4-x) and are clearly differentiated from those of the triscarbonate complex [UO 2 (CO 3 ) 3 ] 4- . Key Raman bands of the peroxo-dicarbonate complex include the ν s (U-O yl ) stretch at 765-769 cm −1 , the v 1 (U-O peroxo ) mode at 418-440 cm −1 , and the v 1 (O-O) stretch at 845-850 cm −1 , the latter exhibiting a pronounced isotopic shift upon 18 O substitution. Complementary FTIR measurements reveal weak absorptions near 425, 765 and 865 cm −1 attributed to v1(U-O peroxo ), ν s (U-O yl ) and v 1 (O-O), respectively, providing the first infrared evidence of a uranyl peroxo-carbonate complex in aqueous solution. DFT calculations reproduce the observed frequencies and isotope shifts, clarifying the role of solvation and counter-cation effects. These results resolve long-standing ambiguities in uranyl peroxo-carbonate speciation and establish a robust spectroscopic framework relevant to uranium fuel dissolution, environmental mobility, and long-term waste stability.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-guided phenotypic drug repurposing against Streptococcus pneumoniae
papers.abstract: The prevalence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) within the common bacterial pathogen Streptococcus pneumoniae makes it a priority for the development of new antibiotics. While artificial intelligence (AI) has recently boosted phenotype-based repurposing of drugs for other human pathogens, this remains to be investigated for S. pneumoniae. Thus, we leveraged ensembles of transformer, graph and tree models, each trained on a set of 1,898 actives along with 39,266 inactives, to prospectively examine 6,747 drugs. Of 11 selected candidate antibiotics, nine were found to strongly reduce in vitro growth of S. pneumoniae R6, with MIC₅₀ values of ≤ 0.4 μg/mL. The most potent drugs, thiostrepton and ceftiofur, had MIC₅₀ values of 0.0001 μg/mL (60.1 pM) and 0.0004 μg/mL (764 nM), respectively. Thiostrepton remained highly potent even against multidrug-resistant strains, suggesting it could be effectively deployed to treat common non-invasive S. pneumoniae infection as part of antibiotic stewardship efforts.

papers.title: Cyclic Sulfone Ring Remodeling Enables Molecular Shape Diversity-Oriented Synthesis of Privileged Biaryl and Oligoaryl Motifs
papers.abstract: Molecular shape is a key determinant of the structural properties and intermolecular interactions of privileged scaffolds, such as biaryl and oligoaryl compounds, which are widely used in the design of drugs, catalysts, and functional materials. Despite the well-recognized importance of molecular shape diversity and increased three-dimensionality, the chemical space of biaryl compounds remains dominated by linear and disk-like structures featuring para and meta substitution patterns. In contrast, more sphere-like bis-ortho-substituted biaryl scaffolds have been underexplored, because of the dearth of synthetic methods for generating focused libraries of ortho analogs in a synthetically efficient manner. We report herein the development of regioselective nucleophile/electrophile couple-mediated cyclic sulfone ring remodeling that can streamline access to a wide range of biaryl and oligoaryl scaffolds, featuring aliphatic and (hetero)aromatic amines, phenols, (thio)ethers, and phosphines. To facilitate prediction of the regiochemistry of structurally complex biaryl products, a machine learning model based on the previously unexplored Bernoulli Naïve Bayes classifier is developed. The integrated experimental, computational, and data-driven approach charts the course for mitigating structural biases and exploring the underpopulated biaryl chemical space in medicinal chemistry, catalysis, and materials science.

papers.title: Thermal Evolution of Leaf-Shaped ZIF Nanostructures into ORR-Active N-Doped Carbons
papers.abstract: Metal-organic-frameworks (MOFs) are versatile precursors for electrically conductive heteroatom-doped-carbons (e.g., N-doped carbon) used as electrocatalysts.
