papers.abstract: Accurate quantification of molecular structural similarity through root mean square deviation (RMSD) is essential for protein-ligand docking validation, conformational analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations, yet current methods face a critical trade-off: polynomial-time algorithms sacrifice chemical correctness by ignoring molecular connectivity, while graph isomorphism approaches exhibit prohibitive computational costs for symmetric molecules. This limitation prevents routine exact symmetry correction in applications where distinguishing genuine conformational differences from atom labeling artifacts is essential, such as evaluating docking poses and pruning conformational ensembles. This work introduces the Hierarchical Neighborhood of Atoms (HNA) partitioning, a recursive classification of chemically equivalent atoms that enables fast computation of exact symmetry-corrected RMSD. Hierarchical decomposition reduces search complexity from the product of branch combinations to their sum, achieving computation time reductions of several orders of magnitude compared to existing topology-preserving methods. Comprehensive benchmarks on large molecular databases demonstrate mean execution times in the millisecond range across molecules ranging from small compounds to proteins, with complete success on all calculations without failures or timeouts. In contrast to linear assignment approaches that produce high rates of topologically invalid mappings, this algorithm ensures chemically correct atom correspondences, enabling practical exact symmetry correction across the full spectrum of molecular complexity relevant to drug discovery and biomolecular structure prediction.

papers.title: Improving Robustness of Fifth-Rung Functionals with Linearized Ladder Correlation
Quaternary ammonium–modified cellulose fibers can enhance wastewater treatment performance under challenging conditions
papers.abstract: Wastewater treatment is challenged by refractory contaminants and rising water demand, while conventional coagulation-flocculation suffers from low throughput and is sensitive to the influent water conditions. Cellulose fibers can act as super-bridging agents offering enhanced turbidity removal when used in conjunction with traditional coagulants and flocculants. However, the chemical modification of cellulose fibers and their performance under challenging influent conditions remain largely unexplored. In this study, recycled cellulose fibers are modified with cationic quaternary ammonium groups, imparting a positive charge that can improve treatment performance for a wider range of water matrices including varying influent pH, ionic strength, and turbidity. Modified fibers achieve turbidity below 5 NTU across all influent pHs (7.0–8.9) and turbidities (62–285 NTU) tested, while pristine fibers show that the target turbidity of 25 NTU is not reached when the influent pH or turbidity exceed 8.2 or 130 NTU, respectively. Additionally, modified fibers achieve the target turbidity of 25 NTU even in the presence of an additional 20 mM NaCl, while pristine fibers cannot reach this target at an additional 10 mM NaCl. Furthermore, the modified fibers enhance the removal of metals such as Zn, Cr, Fe, and Pb through the incorporation of metal hydroxide precipitates within fiber-based flocs. Overall, pristine and modified fiber-enhanced treatments remove 52 % and 65 % of metals, respectively, compared to 39 % with the conventional method. Therefore, modified cellulose fibers represent a promising strategy for enhancing coagulation-flocculation treatment performance.

papers.title: Space-Charge Effects in Lithium Garnet Solid Electrolytes: A Continuum Modeling Study Using the Poisson–Nernst–Planck Framework
papers.abstract: For next-generation solid-state micro-batteries, lithium garnet solid electrolytes like Li 7 La 3 Zr 2 O 12 (LLZO) are considered a promising material because of their high ionic conductivity, electrochemical stability, and mechanical robustness. Experimental data indicates that interfacial resistance, thickness-dependent conductivity, and currentinduced polarization can considerably restrict their performance, even though they are frequently regarded as Ohmic ionic conductors. Based on the coupled Poisson-Nernst-Planck (PNP) equations, we create a continuum-scale model in this work to study the transport of lithium ions in LLZO under applied potential difference. Physically motivated scales are used to nondimensionalize the governing equations, demonstrating that the problem is governed by a single dimensionless parameter: the squared ratio of the electrolyte thickness to the Debye length. Space-charge layers and nonlinear transport regimes can be resolved steadily by the use of an implicit Newton-Raphson approach to get numerical solutions. The findings underscore the significance of spacecharge effects in solid-state electrolytes by showing departures from electroneutral Ohmic behavior in thin electrolytes and under reduced electrolyte thickness. The framework offers a quantitative foundation for comprehending phenomena and for creating composite or interfacially designed electrolytes that perform better.

papers.title: Splitting-Domain Reformulation of Symmetric Strongly Coupled Four-Spin NMR Systems
papers.abstract: The analysis of strongly coupled ¹H NMR spin systems of the AA′BB′ and AA′XX′ type has remained one of the most challenging problems in spectral interpretation for over six decades. The classical Pople framework provides a complete closed-form solution, but requires the prior assignment of observed peaks to specific quantum-mechanical transitions, a combinatorial problem that has rendered the method impractical for routine use. Alternative approaches based on iterative quantum-mechanical fitting exist but remain computationally demanding and sensitive to initial parameter estimates, limiting their adoption for routine analysis. Here we demonstrate that both limitations can be bypassed by reformulating the analysis in the domain of pairwise frequency differences. We show that the coupling interaction between nuclei guarantees the existence of characteristic shared splittings within this set, reducing the problem from combinatorial assignment to pattern recognition. A Set Transformer extracts the relevant splittings from the unordered difference set, and a differentiable Pople inversion layer converts them into coupling constants through exact analytical equations, enabling end-to-end training with physics-informed loss functions. The approach is validated on two distinct four-spin topologies (ortho-and para-disubstituted benzenes), achieving sub-0.05 Hz mean absolute errors on synthetic data and sub-0.08 Hz on experimental spectra from six compounds spanning the full range from the AA′XX′ limit to the genuinely second-order AA′BB′ regime. The two models share an identical neural architecture differing only in the deterministic Pople layer, demonstrating the generality of the splitting-domain representation across coupling topologies.

papers.title: p-H 2 versus o-D 2 Clusters: from liquid-like to glass-like behavior
papers.abstract: Motivated by fascinating structural properties, as well as emerging numerical challenges, para-Hydrogen clusters have been explored in numerous publications in the past. Despite the enormous computational resources used by a number of groups, involving various methods, no consensus on the clusters' energetic and structural properties has been established. Most studies reported strong size dependencies, e.g., "magic number" clusters, while strongly disagreeing with each other quantitatively. Only a few studies claimed the lack of size sensitivity. That is, hardly more than a couple of reports could be considered numerically converged and/or physically meaningful. Unlike most of the previous studies, we focus on small size range of Lennard-Jones LJ34−39 clusters, for which using Diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) we attempt to capture the true behavior of the systems accurately. Not only do we demonstrate that the (p-H2)N clusters for the chosen sizes have the ground state wavefunctions strongly delocalized over thousands of structurally identical isomers, but we also vary the quantum delocalization parameter Λ in the effective range between the hydrogen (ΛH 2 ∼ 0.28) and deuterium (ΛD 2 ∼ 0.20) regimes. We show that for the o-D2 clusters the ground state wavefunctions are strongly localized, yet they are still disordered. In this regime, the system dynamics associated with the DMC method becomes non-ergodic, e.g., the random walkers get trapped in the potential energy minima, where they have been initialized. (It is ergodic for hydrogen clusters.) Consequently we suggest that the structural change induced by decreasing the quantum parameter Λ from p-H2 to o-D2 has the character of a "liquid-glass" transition.

papers.title: A preassembled backbone-anchored solubilizing tag to simplify native chemical ligation-based protein synthesis
papers.abstract: Chemical protein synthesis (CPS) has become an essential tool in chemical biology, offering access to homogeneous proteins bearing modifications beyond the reach of biological expression systems. At the heart of CPS lies native chemical ligation (NCL), which enables the chemoselective coupling of unprotected peptide segments under mild aqueous conditions. However, the scope and efficiency of NCL are often severely constrained by the poor solubility or aggregation propensity of certain peptide segments leading to inneficient ligations and challenging purifications. To address these limitations, a wide range of temporary hydrophilizing tags has been developed, yet existing systems frequently require trade-offs between ease of installation, stability, and cleavage efficiency. Backbone substitution strategies such as Liu's removable backbone modification (RBM) platforms, based on N-2-hydroxy-4-methoxybenzyl (Hmb) derivatives, offer additional advantages of disrupting secondary structures thus preventing aggreagtion. We report here a new class of backbone-anchored solubilizing tags, termed Hmb<K3>, designed for automated introduction by straightforward on-resin reductive amination during standard Fmoc-SPPS. This tag integrates a hydrophilic tri-lysine module, N-Boc-protected for compatibility with SPPS, preassembled with a Hmb-derived backbone modification, thereby eliminating the need for additional non-standard solid-phase assembly steps. O-GABAylation ensures its stability towards TFA cleavage to deprotect and release the peptide from the solid support. Neutral pH incubation triggers selfimmolative de-GABAylation, restoring the acid sensitivity required for tag removal after NCL. The utility of this strategy is demonstrated through the synthesis of the challenging protein target human SUMO-2, and its modularity is further demonstrated by the successful incorporation of multiple Hmb<K3> units within a single peptide segment.

papers.title: Catalyst-free hydrophosphination of alkenes enabled by protic solvents
papers.abstract: Under catalyst-free conditions, activated olefins are subject to hydrophosphination in Click-like efficiency unexpectedly in polar protic (alcohol) solvent. Hydrophosphination of more challenging styrene substrates can be achieved in polar protic solvents as well under irradiation. While the former reaction is apparent conjugate addition, the latter is still under consideration.

papers.title: Probabilities of phases. An algebraic approach in determining the exact phases II
papers.abstract: In this paper we give the exact linear equations to solve the phase problem for a point atom structure. The equations are written for P 1, but they are very easily extended to other spacegroups.

papers.title: Review of a Withdrawn Drug Candidate: Adipiplon
papers.abstract: Adipiplon is a benzodiazepine-site ligand developed for insomnia that was discontinued after phase II trials due to safety concerns. To extract structural insights relevant to drug design, we performed an in silico docking comparison of adipiplon and representative dual orexin receptor antagonists (DORAs) at two sleep-related targets: the GABA_A receptor benzodiazepine binding site and the orexin type 2 receptor (OX2R). Docking calculations using AutoDock Vina showed that adipiplon can form binding poses at both receptors, with intermediate predicted binding scores relative to reference ligands. At the GABA_A benzodiazepine site, adipiplon frequently formed polar anchor-like interactions, whereas at OX2R its anchoring patterns were less consistent. In contrast, DORAs showed more reproducible anchor interactions and more favorable score distributions at OX2R. These results suggest that adipiplon has structural flexibility across multiple receptor pockets but may lack a dominant anchoring mode associated with target selectivity. This docking-based analysis provides a structural hypothesis and illustrates the value of reassessing withdrawn drug candidates for structure-based drug design.

papers.title: Computational Prediction and Synergistic Performance Enhancement in Triple-Crosslinked Biopolymer Nanocomposites for Sustainable Food Packaging: A Literature-Validated Framework
papers.abstract: We present a literature-validated computational framework for predicting synergistic mechanical and barrier properties in biodegradable food packaging materials through hierarchical integration of three distinct crosslinking mechanisms in biopolymer networks. The composite architecture combines: (1) chemical crosslinking via citric acid thermal esterification (∆σ_chem = 20 MPa), (2) enzymatic crosslinking via transglutaminase-catalyzed isopeptide bond formation (∆σ_enz = 8 MPa), and (3) ionic crosslinking via calcium-mediated alginate egg-box coordination (∆σ_ionic = 6 MPa), with hierarchical reinforcement from exfoliated montmorillonite nanoplatelets (aspect ratio 100-300). Employing interpenetrating polymer network (IPN) theory with conservative synergy enhancement factors (α = 2.0-2.8), we predict tensile strength of 32.4 ± 1.8 MPa-representing 6.2-fold enhancement versus pure starch baseline (5.2 ± 0.8 MPa)-oxygen permeability of 318 ± 22 cc•mil/m²•day•atm (65% reduction via tortuous diffusion pathways), and complete aerobic biodegradation of 89.2 ± 2.1% mass loss within 120 days per ASTM D5338 protocol. The observed synergistic enhancement factor of 2.8× (measured 32.4 MPa versus interference-corrected additive prediction of 11.6 MPa) demonstrates non-additive performance characteristic of multi-mechanism hierarchical polymer architectures. This computational methodology, validated against 14 peer-reviewed experimental studies, establishes a framework for rational design of petroleum-plastic alternatives achieving mechanical properties exceeding low-density polyethylene (LDPE: 10-20 MPa) while maintaining environmental biodegradability under home composting conditions, addressing the sustainability challenge of 146 million metric tons annual global plastic production.

papers.title: Embedding-Guided Design Rules for Programmable Mitochondrial Protein Import and Modular Organelle Organization
papers.abstract: Mitochondria coordinate cellular energy conversion, metabolism, signaling, and survival through the coordinated action of thousands of proteins distributed across the outer membrane, intermembrane space, inner membrane, and matrix. Yet, a systems-level framework that links mitochondrial protein sequence space to sub-mitochondrial localization and import logic remains incomplete. Here, we use protein language model embeddings from ESM2 to analyze the human mitochondrial proteome curated in MitoCarta3.0. Low-dimensional projections of embedding space recover biologically meaningful structure, with proteins forming compartment-enriched groupings consistent with submitochondrial organization. Unsupervised clustering and bipartite network analysis identify oxidative phosphorylation, protein import, and mitochondrial translation as highly connected hubs that anchor mitochondrial functional architecture. To probe engineering principles, we perform in silico minimaledit mutagenesis of N-terminal targeting presequences and quantify shifts in embedding position and predicted import potential. These perturbation experiments show that modest changes in charge distribution, hydropathy, and helix propensity can tune import behavior, with a substantial subset of proteins exhibiting large, directionally consistent shifts in predicted targeting. Together, the results support a modular view of mitochondrial organization and indicate that targeting presequences behave as tunable control elements rather than fixed codes. This work provides an embedding-driven computational blueprint for programmable mitochondrial targeting, with applications in synthetic biology, therapeutic payload routing, and organelle engineering.

papers.title: Stereoinvertive Cross-Coupling for Trisubstituted Alkenes Enabled by Sulfoximine Leaving Group
papers.abstract: Although stereodivergent synthesis of alkenes is highly valuable in organic synthesis, its scope has been largely confined to disubstituted alkenes, and extension to multisubstituted alkenes remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a stereoinvertive cross-coupling enabled by alkenyl sulfoximines with aryl boronic acids in the presence of nickel catalyst, in stark contrast to typical cross-coupling reactions of alkenyl (pseudo)halides, which proceed with retention of stereochemistry of substrates. Given that our previously developed Pd-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling of alkenyl sulfoximines proceeds in a stereoretentive fashion, this Ni-catalyzed protocol paves the way for the stereodivergent synthesis of trisubstituted alkenes from a common precursor. Combined experimental and computational studies reveal that the sulfoximine group plays a pivotal role in achieving the stereoinvertive transformation with its coordinating ability.

papers.title: Elucidating the Molecular -Scale Mechanisms of Zinc Adsorption on Redox -Active Ligand Tethered to Mesoporous Silica
LC-MS FADE: Leveraging Untargeted Lipidomics Data for Fatty Acid Profiling
papers.abstract: Fatty acid (FA) profiling has historically been accomplished via gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and can be used in tandem with liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) untargeted lipidomics workflows to comprehensively investigate global FA and lipid dynamics. This approach requires both GC-MS and LC-MS platforms, adding expense, acquisition time, and sample consumption, yet lacks the ability to directly correlate fatty acid profiles to intact lipid molecules. To address this issue, we present a novel workflow to determine FA profiles from lipidomics datasets termed LC-MS fatty acid data extraction (LC-MS FADE). FA data were extrapolated from intact lipid peak areas and expressed as percent fractions. A total of eight disparate lipid extracts, including fetal bovine serum, nutritional yeast, beef liver, canola oil, Viral Producing Cells 1.0, Arabidopsis thaliana, Acheta domesticus, and Escherichia coli K12 were analyzed to assess the accuracy of this strategy. By comparing the LC-MS FADE profile to the GC-MS FAME profile, an average R 2 value of 0.89 was obtained, demonstrating that LC-MS FADE can successfully and accurately extract FA profiles. LC-MS FADE datasets displayed improved sensitivity by identifying more FAs with improved reproducibility compared to GC-MS FAME data. Significantly, novel lipid class-specific FA insights were obtained using LC-MS FADE that were not accessible with traditional GC-MS methods. LC-MS FADE can also be applied retrospectively to existing lipidomics datasets, enabling extraction of FA profiles from data not originally intended for FA analysis. This novel method provides additional insight into FA dynamics in complex untargeted lipidomics datasets and can be readily implemented into lipidomic workflows.

papers.title: Direct Electron Transfer-Type Gas Diffusion Electrode for Efficient CO 2to-Formate Bioconversion across Broad and Low CO 2 Levels
papers.abstract: Bioelectrocatalytic CO 2 reduction to value-added chemicals offers a sustainable route for carbon recycling; however, achieving high activity under low CO 2 conditions remains a major challenge. Herein, we report a direct electron transfer (DET)-type gas diffusion electrode (GDE) utilizing formate dehydrogenase 1 (FoDH1) from Methylorubrum extorquens AM1 for efficient CO 2 -to-formate conversion across a broad range of low CO 2 levels. The electrode surface was modified with pyrene derivatives using multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) to tailor the enzyme-electrode interface, enabling favorable enzyme orientation for rapid electron transfer. A 1-pyrenemethylamine (PyNH 2 )-modified GDE with FoDH1 exhibited a current density of-1.2 mA cm -2 at a reduction potential of-0.9 V, which was twice that of the pristine electrode, and generated formate with a Faradaic efficiency of 82 +/- 5%, outperforming previously reported GDE systems. Kinetic analyses under controlled CO 2 conditions (0.04-100%) revealed a notably low apparent Michaelis constant ( K M,app ) of 2.6 +/- 0.3%, which is less than one-third of that of the solution system, indicating high CO 2 affinity. This enhancement is attributed to the direct supply of gaseous CO 2 to the catalytic layer, avoiding equilibrium limitations in the electrolyte solution. These results lead to a promising tool for enzymatic CO 2 reduction using emission gases from industrial sources and provide key design principles for practical CO 2 -recycling technologies.

papers.title: Empirical Assessment of Energy Consumption and Chemical Productivity Across Diverse Mechanochemical Platforms
papers.abstract: Mechanochemical synthesis is frequently identified as a sustainable alternative to solvent-based methods, yet empirical data regarding the energy consumption of various milling platforms remains scarce. This study provides an assessment of the electrical power demand and chemical productivity across five distinct milling modes: vibratory, planetary, media-free, high-energy, and disc milling. We demonstrate that manufacturer reported power specifications consistently overestimate actual operational demand by up to a factor of 3.1x which can lead to inaccuracies in sustainability metrics. Through the investigation of two diagnostic probe reactions, we observed that power consumption is primarily determined by the mechanical inertia and frequency of the hardware-the platform's "Energy Fingerprint"-with the internal chemical payload exerting a negligible effect. The results show that increasing operational frequency beyond a certain threshold results in disproportionately high energy consumption relative to the incremental gains in chemical yield. By integrating yield and measured power into an energetic return metric (mmol/kWh), we compare the efficiency of different platforms at the laboratory scale. Furthermore, we observe that the fixed electrical overhead of high-capacity hardware, such as disc and planetary mills, becomes more efficient as reaction volumes increase. This work provides a standardized framework of measured energy values, enabling more accurate Life Cycle Assessments and supporting the optimization of mechanochemical processes for industrial applications.

papers.title: Functional Abiotic Metabolite Assembly: Hypothesis for the Early Events in the Origin of Life
papers.abstract: The RNA world hypothesis offers a compelling conceptual framework for the emergence of life, yet a fundamental gap remains between simple abiotic molecules and complex functional RNA polymers. Amyloid-like assemblies have been proposed as plausible earlier prebiotic scaffolds due to their ability to compartmentalize into microenvironments and catalyse chemical reactions.

papers.title: Identification of isotocyanozene at an Australian drug checking service
papers.abstract: Novel synthetic opioids of the 'nitazene' class, comprised of 2-benzylbenzimidazole opioids and related derivatives, present a growing threat to public health. Most recently emerging in European drug markets in 2019, the nitazene group of drugs has been associated internationally with adverse effects in drug users, overdose clusters, and significant mortality. The variable structure and high potency of many nitazene derivatives, which can exceed that of fentanyl, poses a significant challenge to the public health and early warning systems used to detect and respond to the emergence of new high-risk substances. This report describes the early identification of an emerging nitazene derivative, isotocyanozene (5-cyano isotodesnitazene), at Australian drug checking service in an expected opioid sample of uncertain identity presented by a member of the public. Close collaboration with affiliated university laboratories has provided characterisation data and evaluation of the in vitro µ-opioid receptor biological activity to support the assessment and monitoring of this emerging substance and related desnitazene and 5-cyano desnitazene derivatives. The study highlights the rapid response possible though engaging drug users with drug checking services as a market monitor and early warning system to alert health services and the broader community to the presence of unexpected, high-risk substances. Integration of well-resourced and supported drug checking services provides a powerful approach to tackle the public health threats associated with novel synthetic opioids and other drugs of concern.

papers.title: Decoding the Blood-Brain Barrier Permeation in CNS Drug Discovery: An Integrated Framework through High Fidelity Explainable ML and Low Dimensional Linear Discriminant Mapping
Single-crystalline 3D covalent organic frameworks with nbo topology
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (3D COFs) are promising crystalline porous materials, but the elucidation of their structure remains challenging, particularly for those featuring spiroborate linkages. Herein, we report the synthesis of a 3D single-crystalline COF (scCOF) with nbo topology, constructed from a rigid square-planar monomer, tetracyclopentatetraphenylene (TCTP), and spiroborate linkages. Theoretical calculations revealed that the TCTP core possesses higher rigidity than phthalocyanine, effectively suppressing structural fluctuations during framework formation. The structure of the resulting TCTP-COF was successfully determined using microcrystal electron diffraction (MicroED), revealing a non-interpenetrated cubic framework with space group Im -3 m . TCTP-COF exhibits high crystallinity, thermal stability up to 320 °C, and permanent porosity with a Brunauer–Emmett–Teller surface area of 1360 m 2 ·g –1 . To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first structural determination of a spiroborate-linked 3D scCOF using electron diffraction methods, providing a new design strategy for expanding the chemical space of highly ordered 3D COF architectures.

papers.title: Benchmark assessment of collinear, mixed-reference, and spin-adapted variants of spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory, for closed-and open-shell molecules
papers.abstract: Spin-flip methods provide access to certain electronic states having multireference character while retaining single-reference cost. However, conventional spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory (SF-TDDFT) often suffers from severe spin contamination that may engender inaccurate state ordering or ambiguous state character. For singlet excited states, this is largely rectified by a "mixed-reference" formulation (MRSF-TDDFT), while a spin-adapted formalism (SA-SF-TDDFT) addresses spin contamination in a general way for arbitrary multiplicities. Here, we revisit SA-SF-TDDFT and demonstrate that it significantly improves the agreement with reference data as compared to other variants of SF-TDDFT, and also relative to conventional (spin-conserving) TDDFT. However, the spin-adapted approach exhibits notable limitations in the case of linear and quasilinear doublet radicals, where improvement is less pronounced due to degeneracies in the high-spin quartet reference state.

papers.title: Development of a Practical Copper-Catalyzed C-N Cross-Coupling for Heteroaryl Chlorides and Base Sensitive Substrates
papers.abstract: We report a new ligand for Cu-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling of (hetero)aryl chlorides with a broad range of nitrogen nucleophiles. Nucleophiles include primary, secondary and α-branched amines, amides, hydrazines, ammonia surrogates, NH-heterocycles, and base-sensitive substrates such as aminomethyl-functionalized azoles. Aryl and heteroaryl halides, including pyridyl and pyrimidyl chlorides, are competent reaction partners. Key reactivity trends of azole methanamines as a function of its azole identity and isomer were elucidated in a head-to-head comparison of heterogenous and homogenous C-N cross-coupling conditions using 42 different nucleophiles in a parallel library synthesis. The modular nature of the investigated ligands enabled a systematic structure-activity relationship study to elucidate key design principles, as well as steric and electronic effects on catalysis.

papers.title: Computational Insights into O 2 Capture by Cobalt salen and Its Derivatives
papers.abstract: We present a detailed computational study of O 2 binding thermodynamics, spinstate preferences and redox properties of cobalt salen (Co(salen)) and its methoxy substituent analog (OMe-Co(salen)). Starting with a DLPNO-CCSD(T) benchmarking study, we used the r 2 SCAN-3c functional to quantify the energetics of superoxo and µ-peroxo adduct formation across various charge states, solvents, and ligand environments. We find that µ-peroxo species are consistently more stable than their superoxo counterparts, with binding free energies twice as exergonic under typical conditions. Our results show that weak-field ligands such as DMF promote slightly stronger binding O 2 than pyridine, particularly in the peroxo configuration. We show that methoxy substitution further enhances O 2 affinity, especially for the peroxo adduct, with increased stabilization on the order of 0.1-0.2 eV compared to Co(salen). Binding constants (K eq), derived from free energy calculations, elucidate the impact of various factors on the efficiency of capture and release of O 2. To facilitate the rational design of Co(salen) systems for O 2 separation, these insights are combined into thermodynamic schemes using reduction potentials and equilibrium constants.

papers.title: Amino donor-acceptor Stenhouse adducts as visible-light-responsive intrinsically emissive photoswitches for dynamic cellular imaging
papers.abstract: Combining efficient photoswitching with emission into a single chromophore remains a major challenge, as the structural requirements for one function are often antagonistic to the other. Here, we report amino donor-acceptor Stenhouse adducts (aDASAs) as a new class of intrinsically emissive photoswitches that overcome this limitation. By introducing a sulfonamide at the C2 position, we interrupt the full isomerization pathway and impact isomer distribution ratios under irradiation, enabling single-wavelength visible-light photoswitching and fluorescence to coexist within the same thermodynamically favored chromophore. Optimizations yield compounds with red-shifted absorption, record photoluminescence quantum yields representing a six-fold improvement over previous donor-acceptor Stenhouse adducts, and enhanced stability in biologically relevant solvents. These new intrinsically emissive photoswitches correlate fluorescence intensity with switching equilibria, allowing reversible light-induced dimming that creates a fluorescence winking effect. Optimized aDASAs enable robust cytoplasmic visualization in both fixed and live human embryonic kidney (HEK293T) cell imaging, and repeated on/off fluorescence dimming occurs with minimal irreversible photobleaching in fixed cells and with little to no impact on cell viability. This shared-chromophore design provides precise spatiotemporal control for dynamic biological imaging and establishes aDASAs as potential lightresponsive probes for confocal and super-resolution microscopy.

papers.title: Defect-Driven Local Structures in 3D Hollow Hybrid Perovskites Resolved by Solid-State NMR Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Metal halide perovskites (MHPs) are versatile semiconductors with high defect tolerance. Among emerging MHP architectures, the 3D "hollow" perovskites incorporating ethylenediammonium (en) dications represent a unique defect-stabilization paradigm by retaining structural order, stability, and performance. But the local chemical environments of defects that underpin bulk properties have remained unresolved, due to the inherently averaging nature of diffraction techniques. Here, we address this information gap by probing both crystallinity and defect-specific local structures in three representative hollow systems: enMAPbI 3 , enFAPbI 3 , and enFAPbBr 3 (MA: methylammonium; FA: formamidinium) using powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), periodic density-functional theory (DFT), and solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (ssNMR) spectroscopy. Specifically, ssNMR allows to identify and quantify two distinct vacancy regimes: a low-en (below 30%) regime with predominantly trans en conformers that stabilize the framework by simultaneously generating Pb vacancies; and a new high-en (above 30%) regime where conformationally tilted en dications lead to distortions in PbX6 octahedra and crystallinity features. Modulated by the non-covalent interactions, insights into defect sites can be obtained by analyzing 1D 1 H, 207 Pb, and 2D 1 H- 1 H and 1 H- 14 N correlation NMR spectra acquired at a high magnetic field (21 T) with fast magic-angle spinning (MAS). These findings help explain defect compensation mechanisms, reconciling correlated trends between bandgap evolution and stability across iodine-and bromine-based hollow perovskites. In addition, they provide a framework for rationalizing defectengineering strategies in hybrid perovskites and related metal halides.

papers.title: Predictive Modelling Enables Exploration of the Anticancer Potential of Ruthenium(II) Polypyridyl Complexes
Predictive Modelling Enables Exploration of the Anticancer Potential of Ruthenium(II) Polypyridyl Complexes
From Dirhodium to Monorhodium: Identification of the True Active Catalyst in Dirhodium Catalyzed Carbonyl Arylation
papers.abstract: Dirhodium(II) carboxylates play a central role in catalysis; nevertheless, achieving high enantioselectivity through the use of external chiral ligands in dirhodium systems has remained elusive until recent years. While these reports using chiral bisphosphines represent landmark breakthroughs, the nature of the active species has not been established, and the proposed coordination modes of phosphines have lacked direct experimental validation. Here, we unambiguously identify the true active catalyst in the dirhodium(II) tetracarboxylate/chiral Josiphos-catalyzed carbonyl arylation reaction. Through a rigorous combination of variable-temperature 31 P{ 1 H} NMR (VT-31 P{ 1 H} NMR) spectroscopy, electron spray ionization high-resolution mass spectrometry (ESI-HRMS), single-crystal X-ray diffraction (scXRD), and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we demonstrate that catalysis proceeds via an unprecedented additive-assisted cleavage of the Rh-Rh bond. Under the reaction conditions, the dirhodium(II) core dissociates to form a chiral, orthometalated Rh(III) complex that constitutes the catalytically competent species. This new complex exhibits higher reactivity and selectivity compared to dirhodium(II), Rh(I), and other Rh(III) complexes. DFT calculations elucidate the origin of high stereocontrol in the CC bond-forming event. This study reveals, for the first time, that dirhodium(II) catalysts can dissociate under catalytically relevant conditions to generate a highly active chiral monorhodium(III) species, thereby overturning the prevailing mechanistic model of dirhodium(II) catalysis. Such monomeric species may constitute the true active catalysts in other dirhodium(II)-catalyzed reactions, thereby opening new avenues for mechanistic exploration in dirhodium(II) catalysis. Moreover, the chiral orthometalated Rh(III) complex identified herein presents significant opportunities for the development of new asymmetric transformations.

papers.title: Mechanical Taming of Hardy-Cope Rearrangements
papers.abstract: Bullvalene is a fluxional molecule that rapidly rearranges via low-barrier [3,3] sigmatropic rearrangements, allowing each of its 10 carbon atoms to exchange such that they exchange rapidly at room temperature, accessing all possible configurational permutations with sub-millisecond half-lives. We previously demonstrated that the incorporation of this fluxional core into polymeric systems imbues materials with force-responsive properties, as bullvalene's fluxionality can reversibly "respond" to applied mechanical stress. However, direct observation of such rearrangements within the bullvalene core in response to applied force has remained elusive in soft materials, owing to the complexity of the resulting isomer distributions and the rapid thermal reversion of perturbed isomers. Herein, we utilize a polymer chain-centered fluorinated bullvalene core to provide direct spectroscopic evidence of changes to the bullvalene isomer distribution in response to mechanical force. These findings position bullvalene as the first example of a unique class of mechanophores capable of undergoing multiple mechanochemical reactions without needing an external stimulus for subsequent mechanochemical activity. We anticipate these results to provide key insights into the development of force-responsive materials with enhanced mechanical properties and macromolecular sensing capabilities.

papers.title: Prelithiated SiOₓ/Graphite-NMC811 Cells: Capacity loss, Impedance Rise and Hidden Degradation Pathways Revealed Using Three-Electrode Diagnostics
papers.abstract: Electrodes containing SiOx/graphite(Gr) materials are attractive as anodes for high-energy lithium-ion batteries. However, their mechanical deformation, electrochemical response, and impedance evolution during long-term cycling are strongly coupled, complicating accurate diagnosis of performance fade mechanisms. In this work, the behavior of electrochemically prelithiated SiOx/Gr anodes paired with NMC811 cathodes is systematically investigated using techniques that include in-situ dilatometry, three-electrode electrochemistry, and multiscale post-cycling microscopy. The SiOx/Gr electrode exhibits a maximum expansion of 49% upon lithiation to 10 mV vs. Li + /Li, with 84% of the expansion and 91% of the capacity being reversible. In full cells, relatively stable cycling with only 12% capacity fade over 500 cycles is observed. Three-electrode experiments reveal cell-level impedance growth, which is dominated by the NMC811 cathode: the SiOx/Gr anode exhibits minimal net impedance rise and an initial impedance decrease at low potentials. Despite this apparent electrochemical stability, crosssectional SEM, PFIB tomography, and cryo-STEM reveal irreversible anode thickening caused by the accumulation of an inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) permeating the anode bulk. Electrode potential-shift analysis further demonstrates that Li + ions released from lithium reservoirs in the prelithiated anode masks true lithium inventory loss during aging. These results demonstrate that low-expansion SiOx/Gr anodes can simultaneously exhibit favorable cycling and impedance metrics while undergoing substantial, hidden degradation, underscoring the importance of electrode-resolved diagnostics for evaluating prelithiated silicon-based anodes.

papers.title: Enhanced Chemical Reasoning Agent: Boosting Trustworthy LLM Performance in Chemistry via Multi-Stage Reasoning and Calibrated Confidence
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show immense promise in chemistry but struggle with deep knowledge comprehension, complex multi-step reasoning, and output trustworthiness, particularly overconfident predictions. Inspired by the ChemBench evaluation framework, we propose the Enhanced Chemical Reasoning Agent (ECRA). ECRA is an intelligent agent framework built upon existing powerful LLMs, integrating modules for structured problemsolving, leveraging external computational resources, and dynamically estimating and selfcalibrating confidence to address overconfidence. Fabricated experimental results on the ChemBench-Mini subset demonstrate ECRA's superior performance, achieving higher overall accuracy than state-of-the-art LLMs. Critically, ECRA significantly improves reasoning and intuition capabilities and dramatically reduces expected calibration error, indicating a groundbreaking enhancement in output trustworthiness. Ablation studies confirm each module's vital role. Human evaluations and detailed error analyses further underscore ECRA's ability to deliver more accurate, explainable, and reliably calibrated chemical insights, paving the way for safer and more effective LLM deployment in scientific applications.

papers.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Biology: Toward Unifying Models, Algorithms, and Modalities
papers.abstract: Rapid advances in generative artificial intelligence have revolutionized biological modeling across domains such as protein, genetics, and single-cell. However, existing works often organize applications by molecule types or specific research tasks, overlooking the methodological convergence and cross-modal innovations. This paper aims to present a unified methodological perspective that highlights the fundamental technical commonalities across biological modalities. We systematically organize recent advances in generative modeling for biology through the lens of core machine learning paradigms, from language models (LMs) and diffusion models to their emerging hybrid architectures. Our work reveals how techniques initially developed for one molecular type (e.g., protein design) can be effectively transferred to others (e.g., RNA engineering), and identifies the convergence trend where discrete diffusion models and iterative language models represent different facets of a unified generative framework. We cover the evolution from domain-specific models to multi-modal biological foundation models and agent-based systems. By emphasizing methodological connections rather than applications, this paper aims to accelerate cross-domain innovation and make the field more accessible to the broader machine learning community. We conclude by identifying promising research directions where successful techniques in one biological domain remain unexplored in others, offering a roadmap for future advances in generative biology.

papers.title: Synthesis and biological characterization of [3.1.0], [3.2.0], [3.3.0], and [3.4.0] bicyclic pyrrolidine analogs as D4 and sigma 1 receptor dual modulators
papers.abstract: Dopamine D4 (D4R) and sigma-1 (σ1R) receptors represent attractive targets for the treatment of neurological disorders, including L-DOPA–induced dyskinesias associated with Parkinson’s disease. Guided by prior work on D4R antagonists and σ1R modulators, we designed and synthesized a series of sp³-rich bicyclic pyrrolidine scaffolds ([3.1.0]–[3.4.0]) using a modular [3+2] cycloaddition strategy that enabled rapid exploration of structural diversity. In vitro profiling revealed pronounced structure–activity relationships driven by ring size and southern substituents, with the compact [3.1.0] and [3.2.0] scaffolds exhibiting optimal physicochemical properties and potent dual activity, including D4R Ki values of 1–5 nM and σ1R Ki values <10 nM for multiple analogs. Selected chemotypes delivered high σ1R selectivity, while others maintained strong D4R potency. Although high intrinsic clearance was observed across the series, several [3.1.0] and [3.2.0] compounds showed improved microsomal stability, moderate plasma protein binding, and robust in vivo brain penetration (Kp >3). Lead compounds 9b and 12b demonstrated favorable exposure and half-life in rat cassette studies, with discrete mouse pharmacokinetics confirming sustained brain concentrations well above D4R Ki values. Collectively, these findings establish bicyclic pyrrolidines as a versatile chemotype for dual D4R/σ1R modulation and identify 9b and 12b as promising in vivo tool compounds and leads for further optimization toward L-DOPA–induced dyskinesia.

papers.title: Ultrafast computation of exact symmetry-corrected RMSD of conformers
papers.abstract: Accurate quantification of molecular structural similarity through root mean square deviation (RMSD) is essential for protein-ligand docking validation, conformational analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations, yet current methods face a critical trade-off: polynomial-time algorithms sacrifice chemical correctness by ignoring molecular connectivity, while graph isomorphism approaches exhibit prohibitive computational costs for symmetric molecules. This limitation prevents routine exact symmetry correction in applications where distinguishing genuine conformational differences from atom labeling artifacts is essential, such as evaluating docking poses and pruning conformational ensembles. This work introduces the Hierarchical Neighborhood of Atoms (HNA) partitioning, a recursive classification of chemically equivalent atoms that enables fast computation of exact symmetry-corrected RMSD. Hierarchical decomposition reduces search complexity from the product of branch combinations to their sum, achieving computation time reductions of several orders of magnitude compared to existing topology-preserving methods. Comprehensive benchmarks on large molecular databases demonstrate mean execution times in the millisecond range across molecules ranging from small compounds to proteins, with complete success on all calculations without failures or timeouts. In contrast to linear assignment approaches that produce high rates of topologically invalid mappings, this algorithm ensures chemically correct atom correspondences, enabling practical exact symmetry correction across the full spectrum of molecular complexity relevant to drug discovery and biomolecular structure prediction.

papers.title: Scalable Modeling of Multi-Spin Ensembles in SABRE Hyperpolarization: A Symmetry-Based Framework for Zero and Ultralow Fields
papers.abstract: This work presents a theoretical framework for quantitative, scalable modeling of SABRE (Signal Amplification by Reversible Exchange) experiments under zero- and ultralow-field (ZULF) conditions. SABRE exploits the singlet spin order of parahydrogen to hyperpolarize nuclear spins of substrates without chemical modification, enhancing NMR signals. In ZULF SABRE method polarization transfer occurs in ultralow magnetic fields where Zeeman interactions are comparable to or weaker than scalar couplings, enabling coherent mixing of spin states and revealing interactions often suppressed at high fields. Our approach captures the full quantum dynamics of the SABRE complex, including coherent evolution, chemical exchange, and relaxation, within a Liouville-space formalism. We demonstrate that the Hamiltonian, relaxation, and exchange superoperators possess symmetry with respect to the total spin, allowing the dynamics to be rigorously restricted to the zero-quantum coherence subspace. This symmetry-based reduction yields a scalable framework for efficient simulation of multi-spin SABRE systems. The approach is validated against full Liouville-space calculations for small systems and is further applied to a 14-spin SABRE complex, demonstrating its ability to treat spin systems of a complexity well beyond the reach of conventional full Liouville-space simulations. The framework thus provides a predictive tool for optimal polarization fields, ZULF NMR spectra and the design of novel hyperpolarization experiments.

papers.title: Light-Induced Selective Control of Excitonic States in Supramolecular Nanotubes
Hyperfine Coupling Quantifies Hole Delocalization in Triarylamine Radical Cations of D–χ–A Molecules
papers.abstract: Spin-charge delocalization can reshape the hyperfine landscape that governs weak-field magnetic response in spin-correlated radical pairs (SCRPs), but delocalization is often hard to quantify experimentally. Here we show the isotropic 14 N hyperfine coupling ( A N ) of triarylamine radical cations provides an experimental metric of hole delocalization in donor–chiral bridge–acceptor molecules where triarylamine acts as an electron donor. We modulate delocalization through a donor series that varies the N-aryl π-manifold (extension/fusion) and its torsion control. Room-temperature cw-EPR resolves the 14 N three-line pattern for radical cations generated chemically and electrochemically at room temperature. A N decreases as spin density moves off the N-centered aryl and into distal rings, correlating with both DFT Fermi-contact terms and global delocalization metrics. In contrast, the visible–NIR radical-cation absorption contains two overlapping transitions that depend primarily on local N-bound aryl identity and therefore do not uniquely track delocalization. These findings provide a practical route to systematically tuning the effective hyperfine scale relevant to SCRP magnetic response.

papers.title: Deaminative 1,n-Difunctionalization of Alkenes Via Controlled Chain Walking
papers.abstract: The regioselective 1,n-difunctionalization of unactivated alkenes at remote positions is highly challenging due to the lack of thermodynamic driving force to arrest chain walking at a specific nth site. Herein we describe a new modality for controlling such regioselectivity by harnessing chain walking to activate remote leaving groups. We report that alkenyl ammonium salts can undergo a Pd-catalyzed deaminative 1,n-dicarbofunctionalization reaction with aryl iodides in which the ammonium group controls the remote nth site of functionalization. This transformation features a broad tolerance for electron-poor, elec-tron-rich, and reactive aryl coupling partners as well as linear and cyclic alkenes to generate 1,n-difunctionalized products in modest to excellent yields. Mechanistic studies provide insight into key steps, including the role of the ammonium group in controlling chain walking.

papers.title: α-Fluoronitroalkenes as Fluorinated Building Blocks: Solvent-Controlled Functionalization with Hydrazones
papers.abstract: While α-fluoronitroalkenes have been widely explored in annulation and cycloaddition chemistry, controlled intermolecular C–N bond formation through conjugate addition remains largely undeveloped. Moreover, solvent-controlled divergence between conjugate addition and cyclization from identical starting materials has not been systematically demonstrated for α-fluoronitroalkenes. Herein, we report a base-mediated 1,4-conjugate addition of hydrazones to α-fluoronitroalkenes under aprotic conditions, affording fluoro-substituted hydrazones. In contrast, protic acidic conditions divert reactivity toward 4-fluoropyrazole formation, highlighting a solvent-controlled divergence in reaction pathways. This one-pot protocol tolerates a wide range of aromatic, heteroaromatic, and aliphatic substrates, providing isolable fluorinated hydrazones in moderate to high yields. This study expands the synthetic utility of both hydrazones and α-fluoronitroalkenes as building blocks of interest for applications in organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry.

papers.title: Tuning the surface charge of cellulose super-bridging agents for improved performance during wastewater treatment
papers.abstract: Wastewater treatment is challenged by refractory contaminants and rising water demand, while conventional coagulation-flocculation suffers from low throughput and is sensitive to the influent water conditions. Cellulose fibers can act as super-bridging agents offering enhanced turbidity removal when used in conjunction with traditional coagulants and flocculants. However, the chemical modification of cellulose fibers and their performance under challenging influent conditions remain largely unexplored. In this study, recycled cellulose fibers are modified with cationic quaternary ammonium groups, imparting a positive charge that can improve treatment performance for a wider range of water matrices including varying influent pH, ionic strength, and turbidity. Modified fibers achieve turbidity below 5 NTU across all influent pHs (7.0–8.9) and turbidities (62–285 NTU) tested, while pristine fibers show that the target turbidity of 25 NTU is not reached when the influent pH or turbidity exceed 8.2 or 130 NTU, respectively. Additionally, modified fibers achieve the target turbidity of 25 NTU even in the presence of an additional 20 mM NaCl, while pristine fibers cannot reach this target at an additional 10 mM NaCl. Furthermore, the modified fibers enhance the removal of metals such as Zn, Cr, Fe, and Pb through the incorporation of metal hydroxide precipitates within fiber-based flocs. Overall, pristine and modified fiber-enhanced treatments remove 52 % and 65 % of metals, respectively, compared to 39 % with the conventional method. Therefore, modified cellulose fibers represent a promising strategy for enhancing coagulation-flocculation treatment performance.

papers.title: Orthogonal Solvent Mediation for Solid Composite Electrolyte Synthesis: Phase Integration via Particle Dispersion
papers.abstract: Ceramic-rich solid-composite electrolytes exhibit ceramic-like ionic conductivity and enhanced mechanical property, making them promising candidates for market-relevant solid-state batteries. In-depth knowledge of the microstructure within the composite electrolytes for ideal performances and their correlation with the choice of materials and processing methods are not well-understood. Herein, we report a solution-cast, free-standing composite film comprised of well-integrated ceramic (Li3InCl¬6) and binder (Styrene-Ethylene-Butylene-Styrene, SEBS) phase, which simultaneously provides Li+ transport pathways and the required mechanical support. In the formation of this unique microstructure, we mark the mediator role of dibutyl ether – a low polarity solvent that forms a non-invasive polar-ionic interaction with the electronegative metal elements at the surface of Li3InCl¬6 particles to suspend and disperse Li3InCl6 particles in the dissolved SEBS matrix, facilitating phase integration. This weak interaction only occurs at chosen conditions; increased solvent-to-ceramic ratio and interaction time can induce Li3InCl6 decomposition. Our results correlate the electrochemical performance of a ceramic-rich Li3InCl6-SEBS composite electrolyte film with its microstructure; the latter was demonstrated to be potentially tunable by altering the molecular structure of the solvent and the parameters used in composite electrolyte synthesis procedures. This work provides materials structural-level insights that underpin the design principle of solution-cast solid composite electrolytes.

papers.title: An Expert-Augmented Deep Learning Approach for Interpretable Synthesis Route Evaluation
papers.abstract: Selecting efficient multi-step synthetic routes is a central challenge in organic synthesis, particularly in medicinal and process chemistry, where route choice directly impacts feasibility, cost, and development efficiency. While computer-aided synthesis planning (CASP) tools can generate diverse pathways, the evaluation of these generated routes remains challenging. Existing heuristic or data-driven scoring systems often oversimplify the multi-objective nature of synthesis design and rely on proxy datasets (e.g., patent routes) rather than universal grounded criteria. To address this, we introduce an expert-augmented, data-driven scoring framework that integrates machine learning with chemists’ domain knowledge for both numerical and explainable route assessment. A DeepSets-based model is trained using tree edit distance between reference and machine-generated routes, then fine-tuned with expert evaluations to produce both quantitative scores and interpretable qualitative categories (Good, Plausible, Bad). Validated against expert assessments, the resulting system achieves a Spearman correlation coefficient of 0.78 ± 0.05 and a Pearson correlation of 0.77 ± 0.06 regarding its category assessment prediction. When ranking routes by predicted score, the model achieves an overall 60.2% top-1 accuracy (vs. a 17.5% baseline) relative to reference routes, while expert validation confirms that 75% of sampled top-1 selections are feasible, demonstrating the model correctly identifies diverse, expert-validated alternatives beyond the reference.

papers.title: Synthesis of two methylolanthanin derivatives and the investigation of their lanthanide and iron binding capabilities
papers.abstract: Lanthanides (Lns) have recently been recognized as essential cofactors for certain bacterial enzymes, such as the methanol dehydrogenase (MDH), yet their poor bioavailability under physiological conditions has long suggested the existence of Ln-binding metallophores termed lanthanophores. In this context methylolanthanin (MLL), a chelator which is potentially involved in Ln-uptake of methylotrophic bacteria, was recently isolated and characterized. Here, two novel MLL derivatives, ortho-and meta-MLL, were synthesized for comparative studies in order to gain a deeper insight of the unusual 4-hydroxy benzoate moiety of native para-MLL. UV-vis titrations and ion mobility spectrometry-mass spectrometry (IMS-MS) complemented by density functional theory (DFT) calculations were implemented to investigate metal-binding behaviour in both solution and gas phase. Binding studies revealed that the two artificial chelators also tend to precipitate Lns under biologically relevant conditions (pH 6.0) rather than solubilizing them. As MLL and its derivatives are closely related to the siderophore rhodopetrobactin B (RPB B) we also investigated iron binding. In this regard ortho-MLL stood out in our analysis and showed a distinctly different binding behaviour than the other two derivatives.

papers.title: Nanostructural Engineering for Optimizing Performance and Durability of Sputtered RuO <sub>2</sub> Oxygen Evolution Catalysts in PEM Electrolyzers
papers.abstract: Proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysis is a key technology for sustainable hydrogen production but is constrained by the cost, complexity, and durability of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalyst. Ruthenium oxide (RuO 2 ) is regarded as a promising alternative to the state-of-the-art IrO 2 catalyst, offering superior intrinsic OER activity at a lower material cost. However, structure–performance relationships in practical RuO 2 -based electrodes require deeper understanding, and their long-term stability in PEM electrolyzers is still unsatisfactory. In this study, RuO 2 thin films are fabricated by reactive magnetron sputtering and directly integrated as ionomer-free OER catalysts in porous transport electrodes (PTEs). By systematically varying deposition parameters, the nanostructure of the films is tuned over a wide grain-size range. Structural analysis by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and cross-sectional scanning electron microscopy (SEM) reveal a strong correlation between grain size and electrochemical behavior. Reduced grain size results in a higher electrochemically active surface area (ECSA), determined from evaluating the double-layer capacitance, which leads to an enhanced OER activity both in 3–electrode measurements in 0.5 mol L −1 H 2 SO 4 as well as in a PEM electrolyzer cell. Combining results from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) suggests that the higher ECSA in membrane electrode assemblies is presumably enabled by proton-conductive hydrated grain boundaries. Importantly, smaller grains also improve long-term stability in PEM electrolyzer tests. A cell with a low anode loading of 0.64 mg cm −2 operates for over 700 h at 1 A cm −2 , exhibiting a degradation rate of only 4 µV h −1 for more than 300 h. These results demonstrate that nanostructural engineering of sputtered RuO 2 enables efficient, durable, and scalable ionomer-free OER catalysts for PEM electrolysis.

papers.title: Enhancing All-Solid-State Batteries Performance through Thickness Control and Surface Passivation of Thermally Evaporated Lithium Metal Anodes
papers.abstract: Thin lithium metal anodes are key to realizing high-energy-density and enhanced safety in allsolid-state batteries (ASSBs). However, extruded lithium foils thinner than 50 µm suffer from poor structural integrity, rough surfaces, and resistive native passivation layers which severely limit cycling stability. Here, we demonstrate that thermally evaporated, highly pure lithium with smooth, grain-boundaries surfaces morphology significantly improves interfacial contact and electrochemical performance. For a fixed lithium thickness, replacing extruded lithium with a 50 µm evaporated lithium anode increases the critical current density (CCD) from 1.6 to 2.1 mA cm-2 in Li|Li symmetric cells using Li6PS5Cl (LPSCl) as solid electrolyte separator. In LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811)|LPSCl|Li full cells, this configuration enables 161 stable cycles at 1.5 mA cm-2 and 1.6 mAh cm-2. A systematic thickness dependence study reveals that reducing the evaporated lithium metal to 25 µm severely limits full-cell performance (~20 cycles), underscoring the need for a sufficient electrochemically active lithium reservoir to mitigate void formation and to compensate for the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) growth. To address this limitation, an ultra-thin 65 nm LiF passivation layer was applied to 25 µm evaporated lithium. The LiF coating suppresses chemical degradation during storage, stabilizes the lithium/LPSCl interface, limits SEI growth, and mitigates dendrite formation, thereby increasing the CCD to 2.6 mA cm-2. In full cells, LiF-coated 25 µm lithium delivers over 500 and 300 cycles at current density of 1.5 mA cm-2 and 3 mA cm-2 respectively. These results establish LiF-passivated thermally evaporated lithium as a high-performance anode design for next-generation ASSBs.

papers.title: Azeotropic Adsorption and Selectivity Reversals in Zeolites
Biomass-Derived 2-Cycloolefin-1-ones: A Key to Depolymerizable and Degradable Polymeric Materials
papers.abstract: The upcycling of polymeric materials, which enables the full recovery of carbon resources or energy from waste, is increasingly critical for mitigating the environmental impact of plastic disposal. However, endowing polymers with efficient depolymerization or degradation capability remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report a strategy based on the polymerization of 2-cycloolefin-1-one monomers characterized by low ring strain energies. The resulting polymers can be selectively depolymerized into their original monomers or otherwise degraded under mild conditions after use. This fully closed-loop, carbon-conserving recycling protocol offers a practical and sustainable solution. Notably, these monomers can be derived from biorefinery platforms, reducing the reliance of polymeric materials on fossil fuels. The polymers derived from 2-cycloolefin-1-ones exhibit material properties akin to conventional plastics. The precisely controlled C=C configuration and the presence of rigid cyclic units along the backbone impart high thermal transition temperatures, meeting the performance requirements for commodity materials. Beyond highly efficient depolymerization to monomers, which achieves true circularity, the strategic retention of evenly spaced carbonyl (ketone) groups adjacent to C=C bonds in the main chain provides versatile and complementary degradation pathways for polymeric plastics and thermosets.

papers.title: Malonic Ester Synthesis-type Polymerization: Precise Design of the Repeating Unit Structure in sp³ Carbon-Chain Polymers
papers.abstract: Repeating unit structures (RUS) govern polymer function, yet methods to diversify RUS in sp³ carbon‑chain polymers remain limited, particularly for systematic control of side‑chain spacing. Here, we report malonic ester synthesis–type polymerization (MESP), an A₂+B₂ polycondensation that exploits nucleophilic substitution between malonate enolates and alkyl bromides to access sp³ carbon‑chain polymers with single‑carbon increments in side‑chain spacing. Post‑polymerization decarboxylation converts gem ‑bis esters into mono‑ester side chains, yielding acrylate–ethylene copolymer analogues with controlled composition and sequence. Thermal analysis reveals polymer properties spanning amorphous to semi‑crystalline regimes, with odd–even effects arising from single‑carbon variations in gem -bis ester placement relative to methylene units. By unifying backbone and side‑chain design within a single strategy traditionally associated with polyesters and polyacrylates, respectively, MESP expands the accessible RUS landscape and provides a platform for the discovery of new functional carbon‑chain polymers through precise control of functional group arrangement and spacing within their RUS.

papers.title: DISSOLVR: An Interpretable and Fast Framework for Aqueous and Organic Solubility Prediction
papers.abstract: High-fidelity solubility prediction is fundamental to pharmaceutical development and environmental partitioning, where accurate modeling must couple molecular structure with thermodynamic behavior across diverse chemical environments. However, recent advancements have been dominated by deep learning architectures that often sacrifice physical interpretability for predictive power. We challenge this trend by showing that state-of-the-art performance does not require such non-transparent architectures. To address this, we introduce DISSOLVR, a transparent framework for molecular solubility prediction. In addition, we perform a comprehensive literature review and a benchmarking study against various methods. We show that DISSOLVR approaches the aleatoric limit of experimental uncertainty and achieves OOD generalization through structural invariance derived by mapping molecules to physically-grounded descriptors. Then, we present an LLM-assisted post-hoc explanation pipeline that bridges the gap between symbolic model artifacts and chemically grounded narratives. Finally, a comparative benchmark of a survey involving 22 expert chemists reveals that expert evaluators provide deep insights.

papers.title: Grand Banquet: A next-generation chemometrics framework for classification analysis on data matrix
papers.abstract: The advancement of high-throughput analytical instrumentation has placed analytical science into the "Fourth Paradigm" of data-intensive discovery. In this new era, the limitation of scientific insight is not merely data acquisition but the objective, reproducible interpretation of highdimensional data matrices. Conventional chemometric workflows remain fundamentally reliant on "try-and-trust" methodologies. These expert-assisted paradigms require analysts to manually select preprocessing filters, feature selection methods, and classification models based on intuition or limited resources. Such subjectivity introduces analyst bias, raising concerns about reproducibility when applied to biological or chemical signals. Inspired by the concept "there is no one silver bullet", a next-generation chemometrics framework, named Grand Banquet (GB), is designed to standardise the analytical pipeline in this paper. GB replaces manual selection with a near-exhaustive approach, evaluating 990 pipelines (combinations of 15 preprocessing, 6 feature selection, and 11 classification methods) using various performance indices. Beyond this automatic pipeline, Qwen series Large Language Models (LLMs) have been integrated to generate natural-language narratives of these results, bridging the gap between complex computational outputs and human interpretation. GB offers a near-standard baseline ("Glass-box") for data analysis and a practical step toward method governance and reproducibility. The operation of GB has been tested on four public datasets from the Chemometrics Group at Copenhagen University. GB generates near-exhaustive pipelines for each dataset, with validation accuracies ranging from 40% to 100%, highlighting its ability to systematically explore the data matrix rather than providing only best-performing results. To pay tribute to experts in this field and to promote the standardisation of data analysis practices, related Python files and manuals have been published on GitHub under the Apache License 2.0 licence (GitHub link: https://github.com/Omicsforever867/Grand-Banquet).

papers.title: EIS Prediction of degradation of Aluminum beverage can lids using LSTM neural networks
papers.abstract: Corrosion prediction in aluminum can lids is important to maintain the longevity and safety of beverage containers, with Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) serving as a helpful modern tool to assess coating performance. This study aims to develop a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network for predicting EIS spectra, enabling more efficient and real-time corrosion assessments. The impedance data was collected using a custom-designed experimental setup that replicated real beverage can environments, generating comprehensive EIS spectra under controlled conditions. This data was then used to train and validate an LSTM model tailored for time-series predictions. The model uses a three-dimensional input structure, incorporating frequency, real impedance (Z'), and imaginary impedance (Z'') as input features. This approach captured broader changes in the EIS spectra, allowing the model to simultaneously map changes in Nyquist plots, Bode magnitude, and phase angle plots. The results demonstrated good predictive accuracy, with the model capturing the complex dynamics of EIS spectra over conventional analytical methods. This study tries to integrate advanced machine learning with electrochemical analysis to enhance material evaluation. This approach can be expanded to predict corrosion not only in coated aluminum lids but also across broader applications involving aluminum and its alloys. By incorporating recurrent neural networks (RNNs) or advanced LSTM architectures, future work could further refine predictions of EIS spectra, advancing corrosion monitoring techniques in diverse industrial and environmental contexts.

papers.title: Quantification of Beverage Uptake in Aluminum Beverage Can Lid Liner: Effects of Alcohol Content and Tonic Water on Corrosion Resistance
papers.abstract: This study investigates the quantitative relationship between beverage penetration into aluminum can lid interior coatings and the protective effect of increasing alcohol content against corrosion. Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) was employed, and the coating capacitance (Cco) was specifically monitored to note the changes when the beverages are penetrated into the protective polymer coatings. The Brasher-Kingsbury equation was used to convert capacitance measurements into volume fraction of liquid within the coating. Results demonstrate that higher alcohol content in beverages, exemplified by wine, correlates with enhanced corrosion resistance in aluminum can lids, as evidenced by higher pore resistance (Rpo) and charge transfer resistance (Rct). This protective effect is attributed not only to alcohol and water-mediated oxide stabilization, but also to the presence of resveratrol in wine, a potent antioxidant and metal-chelating agent that further inhibits corrosion. On the other hand, alcoholic lemonade exhibited steadier uptake patterns and energy drinks maintained minimal penetration. In contrast, tonic water exhibited the most aggressive corrosion behavior among the tested beverages, likely due to the synergistic effects of quinine and chloride ions, which compromise the protective oxide layer and accelerate degradation. These findings contribute to a better understanding of beverage-coating interactions, particularly as the market for canned alcoholic beverages continues to expand.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Corrosion Resistance Between 424 and 824 Aluminum Beverage Can Lids when Exposed to a Carbonated Cola Beverage: A Blistering Study
papers.abstract: This study compares corrosion behavior and blister formation in aluminum can-lid variants 424 and 824 when exposed for 10 days to a pressurized, carbonated cola beverage (40 °C, 90 psi). Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), potentiodynamic polarization (PDP), EIS-derived beverage-uptake measurements, and optical microscopy were used to track coating degradation. Uptake results show that the 824 coating rapidly absorbed liquid, peaking at ≈19 vol % within the first 30 h, whereas the 424-coating stabilized at 3-5 vol % for most of the test. The high uptake in 824 coincided with lower pore resistance (Rpo) and charge-transfer resistance (Rct) and with higher double-layer (Cdl) and coating capacitances (Cco), indicating accelerated loss of barrier properties. No blister formation was detected on the outside surface of 424. The blisters were observed for both the lids in the rivet area and on the outside surface of the 824 lids. The combined electrochemical, uptake, and microscopic evidence demonstrates that variant 424 provides markedly superior corrosion protection under realistic beverage conditions.

papers.title: Automated EIS Data Acquisition and Analysis for Monitoring Degradation of Aluminum Beverage Can Lids
papers.abstract: Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) is a powerful, non-destructive tool for probing corrosion phenomena in metallic systems. In this work, we present an automated platform for highthroughput acquisition and analysis of EIS data to characterize corrosion in aluminum beverage can lids. Using a low-current potentiostat in combination with a multiplexer and custom-fabricated electrochemical reactors, EIS measurements were performed with the aluminum lid as the working electrode and a graphite rod as the counter electrode, directly immersed in commercial beverage solutions. To extract meaningful corrosion parameters, we applied 2D fitting techniques to the impedance spectra using a hybrid optimization strategy: global exploration via Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), followed by local refinement using gradient-based techniques. The automated workflow facilitates rapid, consistent measurement and analysis, providing detailed insight into coating breakdown and interfacial degradation. This framework significantly reduces manual effort and subjectivity in EIS interpretation and offers a scalable approach for corrosion testing in packaging applications.

papers.title: Uranocenium – The bis-[8]annulene Uranium Cation
papers.abstract: Uranocene, [U IV (η 8 -C 8 H 8 ) 2 ], is the actinide equivalent to ferrocene. While ferrocene is readily oxidised to the ferrocenium cation, higher oxidation states of uranocene are unknown. Here we report the elusive uranocenium cation, [U V (η 8 -C 8 H 8 ) 2 ] + , and demonstrate using electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy and magnetometry that this formal U(V) complex has a 5 f 1 ground state. The uranocene/uranocenium redox couple exhibits near-ideal electrochemical reversibility, and X-ray diffraction studies show minimal U-C bond length changes on oxidation. Enhanced uranium 5 f and 6 d mixing into filled δ-symmetry bonding orbitals in uranocenium, compared to uranocene, amplifies interorbital electron-electron repulsion, and offsets bond length contraction. This demonstrates a case where actinide electronic structure directs molecular structure and physical properties across both solid and solution phases.

papers.title: Trajectory Excited-State Dynamics Study of Pyrazine: Assessment of Potential Energy Surfaces and Simulation of Picosecond Timescales
papers.abstract: The femtosecond and picosecond excited-state dynamics of pyrazine are studied using full-dimensional trajectory surface hopping (TSH) dynamics simulations. We assess how different types of potential energy surfaces (PESs) influence the simulated dynamics; these include on-the-fly potentials versus those obtained by the linear vibronic coupling (LVC) model, calculated by multistate multiconfigurational perturbation theory (MS-CASPT2) and time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) as well as machine-learning (ML) PESs. We find that MS-CASPT2 delivers a reliable excited-state description utilizing on-the-fly and LVC PESs for short (fs) and long (ps) timescales, respectively. TD-DFT (B3LYP) provides qualitatively accurate dynamics for short timescales but is unable to account for the coupling with the ground state and is even qualitatively wrong for longer timescales (i.e., failing to account for the internal conversion to the ground state). We observe and rationalize the oscillations (with a period of ∼40 fs) in the populations of 1 B 3u (nπ*) and 1 A u (nπ*) excited states. Both MS-CASPT2 and TD-DFT-based TSH simulations identify significant singlet-triplet intersystem crossing (ISC) on picosecond timescales (∼10 ps). With our simulations, we established the excited-state mechanism both for the internal conversion to the singlet ground state and singlet-triplet ISC that involves the 1 B 3u (nπ*) and 1 A u (nπ*) states with similar weights. Finally, we successfully used pyrazine as a benchmark model for TSH carried out on ML-PESs.

papers.title: Evolution of the Composition and pH of Single Aqueous Aerosols Produced from Bulk Aqueous Sulfite Solutions
papers.abstract: Sulfur speciation and pH are important parameters in aerosol chemistry that influence the oxidation of S(IV) to S(VI), a critical process that contributes to haze pollution. Here, we monitor the evolution of the composition and pH of aqueous aerosols (radii ~4 μm) prepared from bulk solutions containing sulfite/bisulfite through quantitative spectroscopic measurements utilizing an aerosol optical tweezer coupled to cavity enhanced Raman spectroscopy. Under N 2 at ~80% relative humidity, individual, trapped aqueous aerosols are generated from solutions ranging from ca. pH 2 to 6 with a vibrating mesh nebulizer. Aerosols show a significant loss of sulfur relative to bulk solutions due to SO 2 evaporation with a concomitant increase in aerosol pH. An ambient pressure mass spectrometer confirms SO 2 partitioning from the aerosol into the gas phase. Most interesting is that the loss of sulfur from the aerosol due to the partitioning of gas-phase SO 2 occurs at a higher solution pH compared to bulk solutions, suggesting an enrichment of protons at the aerosol surface that plays a role in the protonation of bisulfite, a precursor to the formation of gasphase SO 2 . An electrical low-pressure impactor was used to determine that the aerosols have a slight positive charge. In air (21% O 2 in N 2 ), S(IV) is completely oxidized to S(VI), as sulfate, on the time scale of minutes and occurs several hundred times faster than for bulk solutions. In addition to soluble S(IV) oxidation, we also establish the time scales for gas-phase partitioning and aerosol pH changes.
