Overall, this study shows the need to quantify aqueous aerosol composition, pH, and charge following production from bulk solutions and the role of aqueous surfaces in driving compositional changes, highlighting the role of surfaces in multiphase sulfur chemistry for accurate representation in air quality models.

papers.title: Size-Dependent Reaction Pathways in Multiphase SO2 Oxidation Chemistry
papers.abstract: The paradigm for multiphase SO 2 chemistry in the atmosphere is traditionally based on bulk studies and involves a multistep process of uptake and hydrolysis of SO 2 followed by oxidation. Here we have investigated several processes relevant to SO 2 chemistry, including uptake, evaporation, hydrolysis, and oxidation, as a function of size in aqueous microdroplets. Our results reveal contrasting size dependencies for some of these processes. Most notably, SO 2 uptake is suppressed as the microdroplet radius ( r ) decreases, while oxidation to sulfate is strongly enhanced. The suppressed SO 2 uptake is explained by a size-dependent SO 2 evaporation rate scaling as 1/ r , driven by high interfacial proton activity that accelerates HSO 3 - protonation and SO 2 volatilization. The size dependence shows that oxidation proceeds over 100 times faster than uptake for typical atmospheric aerosols ( r ≤ 5 μm). Consequently, larger cloud and fog microdroplets follow the conventional multiphase pathway (i.e. surface SO 2 hydration and subsequent S(IV) (aq) oxidation) while smaller aqueous aerosols are dominated by direct oxidation at the surface. Overall, microdroplet size dictates the different reaction pathway, essentially acting as a mechanistic switch between them. This study highlights the complexity of multiphase chemistry and the critical roles of droplet size and the air/water interface, emphasizing how different size-dependencies in multistep processes can reshape our understanding of multiphase atmospheric processes.

papers.title: Twisted-Handle Terrylene Diimides Exhibiting Near-IR Circularly Polarized Luminescence
papers.abstract: Non-orientable molecular architectures are aesthetically pleasing but hard to attain due to structural flexibility and complex synthetic strategies. Herein, we report two novel rylene diimides with a twisted-handle topology, wherein the chirality originates from a non-orientable twisted 'basket-handle' arrangement, sans

papers.title: ThermoFAD® and in silico evaluation of Trypanosoma cruzi Trypanothione reductase (TcTR) inhibition by thiazolidine-2,4-dione derivatives
papers.abstract: Chagas disease, endemic to Latin America and caused by Trypanosoma cruzi , has spread to nonendemic regions worldwide due to globalization and migration. Currently, the treatment options for Chagas' disease are limited (two drugs approved) and with severe side effects. This led to a search for less toxic and more potent drugs exploring innovative targets, such as Trypanosoma cruzi Trypanothione Reductase (TcTR). In our study, we optimized the ThermoFAD® assay for TcTR, leading to the identification of a thiazolidine-2,4-dione derivative (specifically, 5-(3,4dichlorobenzylidene) thiazolidine-2,4-dione) that stabilizes TcTR. We also employed in silico methods, such as Docking and Molecular Dynamics, to gain a deeper understanding of the biological activity data of these compounds.

papers.title: DBTL Programming of Mitochondrial Inner-Membrane-Like ATP Modules
papers.abstract: The mitochondrial inner membrane (IMM) achieves efficient ATP production by combining a low-proton-leak barrier, vectorial proton pumping, and FoF1-ATP synthase-mediated conversion of proton-motive force (pmf) into ATP. Although ATP-generating proteomembrane assemblies have been repeatedly demonstrated in vitro , a persistent engineering gap remains, namely, a decision grade workflow that links controllable manufacturing variables, lipid composition, detergents, assembly route, protein ratios, and orientation control, to functional outputs such as pmf, ATP rate and yield, stability, and tunability, in a way that supports rapid iteration and scale-up. Here we present a proof-of-concept Design-Build-Test-Learn (DBTL) framework for IMM-like energy modules that couples a physics-informed simulation of build records and quality control (QC) outcomes to interpretable machine-learning surrogates for prediction and experiment selection. Output magnitudes for ATP rate and yield are benchmarked to published reconstitution regimes, and stability behavior is represented through literature-consistent decay dynamics, providing a realistic scale for evaluating process decisions. Using the simulated manufacturing dataset, we implement explicit QC gates, train a random-forest surrogate model with an uncertainty proxy, quantify feature effects by permutation importance and partial dependence, construct robustness maps across leak and dispersity, and generate algorithmic next-build proposals by scoring candidate designs within manufacturable constraints. This work provides a transferable computational operating system for programming mitochondrial-like energy conversion with emphasis on manufacturability, auditability, and closed-loop iteration.

papers.title: AutoSolveX: a Python-based pipeline for automated structure solution, refinement, and guest identification from diffraction data
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED) is a powerful technique for determining the structures from nanosized crystals. During a typical 3D ED data experiment, dozens of datasets can be acquired per single session. While data collection can be automated, structure solution and refinement remain key bottlenecks in structure determination and require monotonous manual work. A structure determination pipeline, AutoSolveX, with corresponding graphical user interface, was developed that automates structure solution and refinement for small molecules, and allows the identification and refinement of ordered guest molecules in porous materials with theoretical candidates. AutoSolveX provides phase separation and Laue group suggestion, supports atom-type reassignment and HKL transformations consistent with an input space group, and automatically generates refinement summaries and statistics tables for cross-dataset comparison. We demonstrate the functionality of AutoSolveX by batch structure solution and refinement of seven datasets of MOF-74 and guest identification based on MOF-520.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insight into the Effects of A-site Doping in Perovskite Nanorods on Interfacial Li-Ion and Na-ion Transport in Polymer-Perovskite Composite Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Composite polymer electrolytes (CPEs) offer a promising pathway to safer and higher energy density electrochemical energy storage yet optimizing interfacial ion transport remains a critical challenge due to high resistances and a lack of understanding of the complex interfacial electrostatic interactions. This work investigates the mechanistic origins of the interfacial ion transport enhancement in single-ion conducting (SIC) polymer electrolytes filled with A-site disordered perovskite LaxMyTiOz (LMTO) (M = Li, Na, K) nanorods. By integrating Density Functional Theory (DFT) with broadband dielectric spectroscopy (BDS) and pulsed-field-gradient NMR (PFG-NMR), we analyze the ion transport behavior in Li-based and Na-based SIC systems containing compositionally distinct LMTO fillers (LMTO800 and LMTO900). Specifically, we introduce the site-to-site energy difference (∆E) descriptor, which extends beyond single-site descriptors such as adsorption energy and ion binding energies. We demonstrate that ∆E together with ion binding energies provide a more comprehensive picture of the energy landscape at the polymer-ceramic interface. The combined DFT and experimental results show that that A-site doping in the ceramic filler can effectively modulates ∆E and ion binding energies, creating a favorable potential energy landscape that promotes enhanced ion transport along the interface. This comprehensive study illustrates the impact of ceramic compositional tuning on interfacial ion transport and provides materials design rules towards real-world applications.

papers.title: Catalytic Enantioselective Allenylation of Zincke Imine
papers.abstract: Zincke imine, with rich history since its discovery more than a century ago, is a versatile intermediate in organic synthesis. In recent years, there has been renewed interest in temporary dearomatization of pyridines through their redox-neutral ring opening to Zincke imines as this strategy allows for site-selective pyridine functionalization. Despite their growing popularity, no catalytic asymmetric transformation involving Zincke imines has ever been realized. In this work, we have harnessed the intrinsic push-pull dienamine reactivity of Zincke imines to achieve an enantioselective Ir-catalyzed allenylation for the synthesis of highly enantioenriched (up to >99 : 1 e.r.) meta-allenylic pyridines with complete regiocontrol. This transformation proceeds in an enantioconvergent manner using racemic allenylic alcohol as the electrophile. Ammonium acetate-mediated cyclization of the resulting 3-allenylic Zincke imines restored the pyridine core. Notably, this approach provides previously inaccessible 2-substituted 3-allenylic pyridine regioisomer and complements our recently reported strategy using oxazinopyridine. Control experiments combined with computational studies reveal the exclusive dienamine selective nucleophilic attack originates from a lower distortion in the corresponding transition state.

papers.title: Pili-based 'Toe-dipping' Phenomena Preceding Solid Surface-Associated Microbial Biofilm Formation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
papers.abstract: The review focuses on the molecular mechanisms surrounding bacterial pili triggered biofilm formation in a prime nosocomial infection pathogen i.e. Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Bacterial biofilm formation is a major biomedical challenge driving antibiotic resistance and persistent hospital-and biomaterialassociated infections, and existing antibiofilm strategies often show limited efficacy and poor cytocompatibility, highlighting the urgent need for improved antibiofilm strategies. We critically reviewed current antibiofilm strategies targeting biofilm-associated proteins in P. aeruginosa and found that none of the aforementioned strategies are entirely efficacious, highlighting the need to reexamine our understanding of the signaling pathways governing biofilm formation. therefore subsequently we reexamined the key pathways that were involved in biofilm formation and identifies surface sensing as a central regulatory mechanism influencing all extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) production-related pathways. Following this insight, we further examine the surface-sensing mechanism mediated by the Type IV pilus (T4P) tip protein PilY1. Upon surface contact, PilY1 triggers intracellular signalling that rapidly elevates cyclic-di-GMP levels, a key second messenger driving EPS synthesis and biofilm maturation. Further, the PilY1-mediated process of surface mechano-sensing plays a crucial role in coordinating biofilm formation through various interconnected regulatory pathways. However, the existing literature suggests that PilY1 has not been directly targeted therapeutically, revealing a critical gap in current pili-based antibiofilm intervention strategies. Addressing this unmet gap, our review, based on extensive literature analysis and mechanistic insights, we conclude that disrupting pilus-based surface sensing represents a highly effective strategy to inhibit EPS production and, consequently, biofilm formation in P. aeruginosa and other Gram-negative bacteria. In addition, this review provides insight into pilus-mediated surface-sensing strategies that could be key foundations for anti-biofilm coatings for biomedical and related anti-fouling applications.

papers.title: Fibroprinting -Hybrid Fiber-Reinforced (Bio)fabrication via In-Situ Biomimetic Spinning and 3D Printing
papers.abstract: One major challenge in additively manufacturing soft materials such as thermoplastics, elastomers, and gels is their low mechanical stability. Nature solves this by embedding continuous fibers like collagen or cellulose into soft matrices. Integrating 3D printing with fiber spinning has remained difficult due to limited material compatibility, restricted deposition methods, insufficient control over fiber properties, and lack of interlayer reinforcement. We present a spider-inspired technology that combines 3D (bio)printing with in-situ biomimetic fiber spinning. Fibers are drawn from polymer solutions or melts and deposited via controlled oscillatory motion, enabling horizontal or tilted freestanding fibers, precise adjustment of pulling speeds, and fabrication of structures with unlimited thickness. This method surpasses existing spinning techniques and enables complex, fiber-reinforced architectures for biomedical and engineering applications.

papers.title: Towards the conductivity-magnetism interplay in hydroxylated ethylene-coupled tetrathiofulvalenes and nitronyl nitroxides for magnetoresistance applications
papers.abstract: BTBN, a covalently linked tetrathiafulvalene-nitronyl nitroxide (TTF-NN) dyad, represents a prototypical purely organic system exhibiting magnetoresistance (MR). In this material, hole transport along the TTF π-stacks is modulated by ferromagnetic (FM) exchange with the NN radicals, rendering the hopping probability spin-dependent; magnetic-field-induced spin alignment thus leads to reduced resistance. Building on this mechanism, we computationally investigate three in silico designed BTBN derivatives (E1-E3) in which the benzene coupler is replaced by a hydroxylated ethylene unit previously predicted to enhance FM coupling. Using density functional theory and multiconfigurational methods, we compute key charge-transport parameters, including reorganization energies, electronic couplings and rate constants. All three derivatives, E1-E3, exhibit higher hole mobility than BTBN along the π-stacks, a result validated by their larger valence-band dispersion, reaching the same conclusion from both hopping-based and band-structure analyses. Regarding hole injection, Fermi-level alignment with gold electrodes shows that E1 and E3 require voltages similar to BTBN, while E2 requires only a slightly higher bias. Magnetic exchange interactions, evaluated through multiple models, consistently reveal strong intramolecular FM coupling in all compounds. Intermolecular interactions vary, with weak FM or AFM character depending on the system, suggesting potential for MR even in weakly coupled systems. Under appropriate external magnetic fields, weak AFM interactions may convert to FM, further supporting the MR viability of E1-E3. Overall, the results highlight the potential of molecular design to enhance spin-dependent transport and identify E1-E3 as strong candidates for future organic MR materials.

papers.title: Borane Catalysed Annulative Sulfenylation of Internal Alkynes: Towards the Synthesis and Study of Highly Unsaturated Heterocycles
papers.abstract: Herein, we disclose a B(C₆F₅)₃-catalysed intramolecular cyclisation reaction of N-protected alkynyl amines and phenols to generate 5-membered heterocycles, including 3-sulfenyl indoles (17 examples, up to 91% yield) and benzo[b]furans (9 examples, up to 90% yield), in good yields with a broad functional group tolerance. This protocol was adapted into an annulative πextension (APEX) reaction when using diyne derivatives of aniline and phenol, which effectively led to sulfenylated polyaromatic heterocycles, such as benzo[a]carbazole or naphtho[1,2-b]benzofurans. These products exhibit fluorescence from locally excited states, consistent with their large singlet-triplet energy gaps. Additionally, the cyclisation of aryl propargyl ethers, 4-diphenylbut-1-yne and a tosyl-protected propargylaniline afforded sulfenylated 6-membered products (7 examples, up to 94% yield). Extensive density functional theory (DFT) calculations were conducted and support a mechanism in which thiirenium ions are involved as key intermediates in the formation of the observed products.

papers.title: Greatly Enhanced Photocatalytic Hydrogen Peroxide Production over Titanium Dioxide using Anthraquinone-based Co-Catalysts
papers.abstract: In this study, anthraquinone derivatives were explored as cocatalysts on titanium dioxide nanoparticles (P25) for the photocatalytic production of hydrogen peroxide from oxygen. The screening of anthraquinone derivatives revealed that 1-hydroxyanthraquinone is the most effective cocatalyst on P25 and increases the reaction rate greatly, by a factor of 30. In addition, the impact of various reaction parameters on the kinetics of hydrogen peroxide formation such as light intensity, wavelength, the amount of cocatalyst on P25, oxygen flux and the pH value, were investigated. Using this data allowed optimization of the reaction with respect to high reaction rate (1.9 mM min -1 ), quantum yield (26.7%) or turnover number of the AQ co-catalyst (2300). In particular, the extremely high formation rate represents a new benchmark for this reaction.

papers.title: Atomic Layer Deposition of Textured ZnO on 200 mm Wafers for Device Applications
papers.abstract: Zinc oxide (ZnO) is a technologically important wide-bandgap semiconductor used in optoelectronics, sensing, and transparent electronic devices. Implementing ZnO thin films in such devices requires scalable, uniform, and compatible thin-film deposition methods. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) provides precise control over film thickness, composition, and conformality, and is a well-adapted process in the semiconductor industry. ALD processes for growing ZnO primarily rely on the pyrophoric diethylzinc (DEZ) precursor. Recently, Bis-3-(N,N-dimethylamino)propyl zinc ([Zn(DMP) 2 ]) has emerged as a promising non-pyrophoric alternative, providing improved handling safety and enhanced thermal stability. However, its use has so far been limited to growth on small substrates in proof-of-concept experiments. In this work, a thermal ALD process using [Zn(DMP) 2 ] with H 2 O as precursors was developed on industrially-relevant 200 mm silicon wafers and compared to an established thermal process with DEZ and H 2 O. The effects of deposition temperature (150-300 °C), film thickness, and the underlying substrate material on film growth were systematically investigated. Structural, morphological, chemical, and electrical properties were evaluated using complementary and advanced materials characterization techniques. Across the entire 200 mm wafer area, ZnO films deposited from [Zn(DMP) 2 ] exhibit excellent thickness uniformity and a nearstoichiometric composition comparable to those obtained with DEZ. While slightly higher resistivity and reduced crystallinity are seen at lower deposition temperatures, higher deposition temperatures yield comparable resistivity and an improved c-axis oriented crystalline texture. Importantly, successful lithographic patterning and electrical characterization of van der Pauw devices confirm compatibility with advanced fabrication workflows. These results demonstrate that [Zn(DMP) 2 ] can compete with DEZ in film quality on large-area wafers and is safer to handle, which is a significant advantage overall.

papers.title: Microbial synthesis of stereoirregular poly(3-hydroxybutyrate)
papers.abstract: Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) (PHB) is the most extensively studied polyhydroxyalkanoate and has long been promoted as a sustainable alternative to petrochemical polymers due to its excellent biocompatibility and biodegradability. Despite decades of research, PHB has not achieved broad commercial adoption, in part because its ( R )-isotactic microstructure leads to undesirable material properties such as high crystallinity and poor processability. This stereoregularity is widely assumed to be a consequence of the strict stereoselectivity of PHA synthases. Here, we provide the first evidence that challenges this long-standing assumption. In a proof-of-concept study, we demonstrate that stereoirregular PHB containing 6.84% ± 0.04% ( S )-3 hydroxybutyrate with a m dyad fraction of 11.8% ± 0.7% can be produced in fed-batch fermentation at a productivity of (58 ± 9) mg L −1 h −1 . Importantly, the material properties of the resulting stereoirregular PHB align with improvements predicted from chemically synthesized PHB. Notably, the melting temperature reduced from 179.3°C ± 0.7°C to 154.3°C ± 1.1°C, which was accompanied by decreased molar mass decomposition during processing, suggesting improved recyclability of the stereoirregular polymer. These findings overturn key assumptions about PHA synthase stereoselectivity and open the door to microbial production of PHB with tunable material properties.

papers.title: Gauging the Double Lewis Acidity of Dicationic Molecules with Oxide and Fluoride Ion Affinities
papers.abstract: The hunt is on, but the tools are lacking: exciting main group dications were recently isolated and more will come. With increasing access to such exotic compounds, their applications in synthesis quickly draw interest. Dicationic acceptors can bind two donors or directly form double bonds, highlighting the need for specialised metrics of double acidity. We propose the oxide ion affinity ( OIA ) as ideal metric for the strength of double acids. We compare the OIA with the fluoride ion affinity ( FIA ), a widely used measure for hard Lewis acidity. OIA s and first and second FIA s values were obtained from a series of 164 double Lewis acids involving carbon, silicon, sulphur and selenium central atoms. Ion affinities were computed using DFT at the DSD-BLYP-D3BJ/def2-QZVPP level of theory. An isodesmic anchoring scheme to obtain precise absolute energies of oxide ions is presented. Solvation was considered with a polarizable continuum solvation model. OIA s were found to be more than twice as large as FIA s with the values varying strongly depending on the acidic atom. We found strong linear correlations (R 2 > 0.97) between FIA and OIA values for each element. This study provides a conversion scale that unlocks conventional FIAs as convenient predictor for the reactivity of double acids. An application to recent experimental findings on dicationic diphosphonium salts demonstrate that the OIA values provide a reliable measure of oxophilicity that can be used to understand and predict oxide abstraction reactions.

papers.title: How spin conductive are oligo(p-phenylenes) in trityl-based biradicals
papers.abstract: The relationship between structure and exchange coupling constant J is of interest for the rational design of molecular open-shell systems in the context of molecular magnetism, dynamic nuclear polarization, and quantum information science. However, even for the basic relationship between J and the distance r between two spin centers for the archetypal oligo( p -phenylene) bridge, there are only a few and contradicting experimental and theoretical data. We therefore synthesized a series of six trityl-[( p -phenylene) n=1-5 ]-trityl biradicals and used Electron Paramagnetic Resonance methods to extract J values in the range from 17.5 MHz to 235 GHz. We find a distance dependence parameter β of 0.11 Å -1 for unsubstituted and 0.67 Å -1 for substituted oligo( p -phenylene) bridges. This places unsubstituted oligo( p -phenylene)-bridges into the spin-conductor regime and highlights the tunability of conductance by substitution, i.e., increase of the dihedral angle between the phenylene units. DFT calculations employing low Fock-exchange fraction functionals exhibit some limitations in reproducing the experimental J value, particularly in the weak coupling regime. Furthermore, biradicals with n = 3-5 exhibit spin coherence of 1.2 µs at room temperature in the liquid state. These long coherence times, combined with the modular bridge design, position bistrityl systems as promising candidates for applications in quantum information technology.
