Here, we report a fabrication strategy based on randomly dispersed carbon nanotubes (CNTs) grown by chemical vapor deposition (CVD), in which the surface density and electrode design are co-optimized to maximize the probability of CNT interception, the feasibility of singling an isolated CNT and the operation of the device array in fluidics. This process results in an average device yield >70%, limited primarily by the selection of CNT with excellent conductivity and contacts, rather than by the interception or singling processes. These results position 1-CNTFETs as a more accessible platform for the exploration of chemical and biological mechanisms at the single-molecule level.

papers.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Biomolecules: Toward Unifying Models, Algorithms, and Modalities
Improved antifouling properties of a carbon fiber microelectrode modified with a graphene oxide-silicate matrix composite
papers.abstract: Carbon fiber microelectrodes (CFMEs) are widely used as implantable probes for real-time in vivo neurotransmitter monitoring via fast scan cyclic voltammetry, but suffer from electrode fouling, resulting in a continuous signal loss. To prevent fouling, high switching potentials (>+1.3 V vs. Ag/AgCl) are commonly used to renew the electrode through anodic etching of the carbon surface, although this practice precludes long-term implantation and introduces background drift. Therefore, surface modifications providing enhanced fouling resistance while avoiding electrode etching protocols are vital to continual neurotransmitter monitoring. Herein, we demonstrate CFME modification using a composite containing graphene oxide and a tetramethoxysilane-derived silicate matrix (GO-SM-CFMEs). Electrochemical reduction of GO used for its deposition increased the amount of defect sites, while its subsequent oxidation increased the amount of surface oxides, thus reducing the spread of a response towards oxidation of inner-sphere dopamine from ±65% to ±25% for an unmodified CFME and GO-SM-CFME, respectively, under hemispherical diffusion conditions. An increased resistance to fouling by dopamine oxidation byproducts at a reduced switching potential of +1.0 V vs. Ag/AgCl is also reported, maintaining 83% of the initial response toward dopamine over 72 hours. Finally, GO-SM-CFMEs were also shown to be less susceptible to extracellular fouling in a mouse striatum, sustaining 21% higher responses to dopamine after one hour than an unmodified CFME. This article reports the first use of GO-SM-CFMEs and highlights the advantageous antifouling properties of GO-SM modification, allowing for reduced biofouling at CFMEs and potentially clearing the path to quantitative, real-time, in vivo neurotransmitter monitoring.

papers.title: The Curious Case of Dual Emission in 9,10-Bis(phenylethynyl)anthracene
Why Seeding Works When Nucleation Barriers Vanish
papers.abstract: Crystallization is a process governed by the interplay between nucleation and growth. While crystalline seeds are known to reduce nucleation barriers and accelerate crystallization under nucleation-limited conditions, their influence when nucleation is not the limiting step remains poorly understood. This creates a mechanistic puzzle in systems where nucleation barriers are already negligible, yet seeding still accelerates crystallization. The synthesis of zeolites is a quintessential example of growth-limited crystallization that can be directed by seeds that promote heterogeneous nucleation. Using coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations, we show that crystalline seeds direct crystallization pathways by enforcing heteroepitaxial growth, effectively shortening the time required to develop long-range order. This explains why seeded zeolite syntheses can reach XRD-detectable crystallinity earlier, even when nucleation barriers are negligible. We conclude that under growth-limited conditions, while seeds still provide favorable interfaces for heterogeneous nucleation, their primary function is not to accelerate crystallization via barrier reduction but to enforce coherent growth, thereby shortening the time required to develop long-range order detectable by X-ray diffraction.

papers.title: UV response of the green fluorescent protein chromophore: Insights from ab initio non-adiabatic simulations
papers.abstract: The Green Fluorescent Protein (GFP) is widely used in imaging organisms at the sub-cellular level. However, upon exposure to UV or intense visible light, GFP undergoes irreversible reactions, altering its photocycle, which are believed to precede via photooxidation of the chromophore. The mechanism of this process is not well understood, even in the gas phase, with competing interpretations of photoelectron experiments on the isolated chromophore arguing either for nonadiabatic decay or vibrational energy relaxation and autoionization from an initially populated S 3 shape resonance. To address the controversy, we simulated the excited-state dynamics and time-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (TRPES) of the GFP chromophore with ab initio multiple spawning and on-the-fly multiconfigurational electronic structure using our dynamically weighted complete active space self-consistent field method. Our simulations show excellent agreement with experimental TRPES and reveal that S 3 -S 2 non-adiabatic transitions do occur on an ultra-fast timescale that can compete with autoionization; however, the conversion between the shape and Feshbach states occurs primarily adiabatically on the S 2 state. Furthermore, the threshold energies of the shape and Feshbach resonances are very similar, with a low barrier separating these regions of the PES, leading to both states being populated and reversibly inter-converting within 50 fs of the initial photoexcitation. As a result, rapid autoionization still precedes via the shape resonance. The picture that emerges thus reconciles the two competing views of the GFP chromophore's UV response: both internal conversion and vibrational energy relaxation from the shape resonance state are operative. Our findings of the involvement of the Feshbach state suggest new strategies to engineer FP chromophores with tailored photostabilities.

papers.title: Multiscale Computational Discovery of an Indole-Based CK2α′ Inhibitor for Huntington's Disease Therapy
papers.abstract: Selective inhibition of CK2α′ presents a therapeutic opportunity in Huntington's disease. Using an integrated computational approach, we report the indole-based ligand T-21 as a high-affinity CK2α′ inhibitor. Structurebased docking identified a unique hinge-binding motif. Ensemble MD simulations (triplicate of 100 ns each) demonstrated stable, convergent binding. MM/GBSA calculations yielded strong binding free energies (ΔGbind ≈ −25 kcal/mol), primarily driven by hydrophobic interactions with Met158, Leu40, and Ile111. Quantum mechanical analysis confirmed the structural integrity of the indole scaffold upon binding. With favourable predicted CNS permeability and safety, T-21 represents a promising lead for CK2α′-targeted Huntington's disease therapeutics.

papers.title: Stormwater infrastructure as landscape hydrology: Contrasting runoff-fed and groundwater-fed urban ponds reveals design-driven harmful algal bloom risk
papers.abstract: Residential stormwater ponds are common features of urban and suburban landscapes, yet their vulnerability to harmful algal blooms (HABs) remains insufficiently understood despite their close proximity to residential communities. This study examined how stormwater routing pathways and pond water-level dynamics influence underwater light conditions and subsequent bloom development, to inform stormwater management strategies beyond nutrient source control. From July to November 2024, we monitored four groundwater-fed residential stormwater ponds and one surface-runoff-fed lake in Florida, USA, during a hydrologically active, warm season. Field observations were integrated with geochemical, optical, and microbiological measurements, including chlorophyll-a, water level, cyanobacterial community composition, nutrients, calcium, and colored dissolved organic matter (CDOM), to identify environmental conditions associated with bloom occurrence. Substantial HABs developed exclusively in the groundwater-fed ponds, where chlorophyll-a concentrations reached up to 21 times Florida's algal bloom threshold and were dominated by toxin-producing genera such as Microcystis and Dolichospermum. In contrast, no blooms were observed in the runoff-fed lake despite similar nutrient concentrations. Groundwater-fed ponds consistently exhibited lower CDOM and shallower, hydrologically stable water columns, resulting in enhanced underwater light availability that promoted rapid phytoplankton growth. These results indicate that stormwater designs that increase groundwater connectivity and maintain clear, shallow, and stable water columns can elevate HAB susceptibility independent of nutrient enrichment. Bloom risk should therefore be recognized as an emergent consequence of hydrologic routing and optical conditions, underscoring the need for management approaches that reduce light exposure, avoid prolonged stable stages, and support routine monitoring and risk communication in residential environments.

papers.title: Hybrid NMR Reveals Loop-Modulated Substrate Recognition in Multicopper Oxidases
papers.abstract: Decoupling substrate binding from catalysis remains a central challenge in mechanistic enzymology, particularly for metalloenzymes in which metal cofactors intrinsically couple molecular recognition to electron transfer. Here, we introduce a hybrid nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) strategy that isolates binding thermodynamics by exploiting metal-free (apo) variants of multicopper oxidases that abolish turnover while retaining structural integrity and binding competence. By combining ligand-based saturation transfer difference (STD) NMR with protein-centered methionine-selective methyl NMR, we resolve substrate-binding interactions at atomic resolution and directly interrogate how dynamic structural elements shape molecular recognition independently of catalysis. Using the metallo-oxidase McoA, its evolved laccase-like variant 2F4, and their Met-looptruncated counterparts, ligand-centered NMR reveals a conserved aromatic binding epitope for the reporter substrate ABTS across all enzyme backgrounds, while distinguishing specific contacts from transient, nonproductive encounters. Quantitative analysis shows that 2F4 binds ABTS more weakly than wild-type McoA despite exhibiting higher catalytic activity, indicating that directed evolution enhances turnover rather than binding. Methionine-selective methyl NMR identifies substrate-induced perturbations in the Met-loop and adjacent surface residues consistent with heterogeneous, multi-site binding. NMR-guided filtering of ensemble docking models supports two adjacent substrate-access cavities that accommodate multiple transient ligand orientations, validating mechanistic features previously inferred only 2 computationally. Collectively, these results define substrate recognition in multicopper oxidases as tunable, with the Met-loop modulating accessibility, promiscuity, and conformational sampling rather than dictating catalytic chemistry. By decoupling binding from catalysis and quantifying loop-modulated interactions, this hybrid NMR framework provides a generalizable strategy for dissecting substrate-recognition mechanisms in multicopper oxidases and other loop-regulated metalloenzymes.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Design and Optimization of Bio-electrocatalytic CO2 Conversion Pathways
papers.abstract: Unlocking the potential of CO 2 as a renewable carbon resource is paramount to achieving economy-wide decarbonization. Emerging bio-electrocatalytic CO₂ conversion (BECC) platforms, such as microbial electrosynthesis (MES) and related Biohybrid (electro-biological) systems, offer exceptional precision for synthesizing multi-carbon products. Yet, after many years of research, their progress remains hindered by the slow pace and expensive nature of wet-lab research. Building on recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML), this perspective highlights a new data-driven paradigm in BECC innovation. We begin by outlining recent advances and persistent challenges of MES and Biohybrid systems. We then provide an overview of AI/ML workflows that show potential to accelerate BECC research with an emphasis on biocatalyst engineering, electrode and catalyst design, and reactor optimization. Through this wide-ranging analysis, we aim to catalyze the integration of AI/ML tools into BECC studies, supporting a new frontier in CO 2 conversion research and development.

papers.title: Generalization of the Discrete Valence Operator: Unification of the s, p, d Blocks and Noble Gases under Electronic Parity Constraints
papers.abstract: The mathematical formalization of chemical valence is an essential step in the development of stoichiometric prediction algorithms and automated teaching tools. In a previous work, a discrete operator capable of reproducing the valences of representative elements under electronic parity constraints was introduced. In the present note, this formalism is extended to include noble gases and transition metals ( d block). Systematic algebraic expressions are defined for the counting of valence electrons ( e ) as a function of orbital occupation ( s , p , d ). The unified model rationalizes the reactivity of heavy noble gases and explains the maximum oxidation states in transition metals through orbital saturation constraints. The notion of electronic promotion employed in this work is introduced exclusively as a formal resource for counting orbital availability and should not be interpreted as the existence of real excited atomic states. The operator is grounded in the conservation of electronic parity and does not aim to replace quantum mechanical bonding models.

papers.title: Chemoselective Reductive Deuteration and Deuterodefluorination of Trifluoromethyl Ketones with D2O
Fluorescence-Detected Two-Dimensional Electronic Spectroscopy: A Coarse-Grained Simulation Approach
papers.abstract: Fluorescence-detected two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy (F-2DES) offers superior sensitivity compared to the traditional coherent two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy (2DES) technique. However, theoretical modeling remains essential to interpret F-2DES spectra specially for multi-chromophoric systems. While widely used to study excitation energy transfer in molecular assemblies, even conventional 2DES faces computational challenges for large systems. To address these challenges, we extend a recently developed coarse-grained method for 2DES to simulate F-2DES and account for signatures of exciton-exciton annihilation events, that affect cross-peak intensities in F-2DES. We then apply this approach to the light-harvesting II complex of purple bacteria, a well-studied benchmark system, we find that F-2DES simulations reproduce experimental cross-peaks at zero and early waiting times. Moreover, disabling exciton-exciton annihilation recovers results identical to standard 2DES simulations, confirming that the observed cross-peaks arise from annihilation events, as hypothesized earlier. The implemented method opens the door for future exploration of waiting-time dynamics and extends the possibility of predicting F-2DES spectra to extensive photosynthetic systems.

papers.title: Compatibility of Additives with Organic Semiconductors: Bis(fluorosulfonyl)imides with Hole-Transport Materials in Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract: Organic semiconductor-based hole-transport materials (HTMs) play a crucial role in fabricating high-performance perovskite solar cells (PSCs). In particular, for n–i–p structured PSCs, the development of additives for HTMs is imperative. While bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (TFSI)-based HTM additives are commonly used, various other HTM additives are still in their infancy; for instance, the effects of a series of bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide-containing compounds, to which TFSI belongs, have remained unelucidated. Moreover, HTM additives have typically been explored with spiro-OMeTAD HTMs, the most widely known HTMs. However, the compatibility of additives can differ among the different HTMs used. Therefore, the compatibility of a series of bis(fluorosulfonyl)imides with other HTMs is of interest, and establishing the difference in the compatibility of different additives among the base HTMs can facilitate further development of PSCs. In this study, the effects of bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide HTM additives on PSCs based on poly[bis(4-phenyl)(2,4,6-trimethylphenyl)amine (PTAA), a widely used HTM, were investigated. Although bis(pentafluoroethanesulfonyl)imide (PFSI) degraded the uniformity of spiro-OMeTAD layers, the PFSI HTM additive was compatible with the PTAA HTM. In addition, extension of fluorocarbon (C-F) moiety in bis(fluorosulfonyl)imides, used as HTM additives, significantly modulated energy alignment in spiro-OMeTAD-based PSCs, whereas the modulating the size of C-F moiety in bis(fluorosulfonyl)imides negligibly changed energy alignment in PTAA-based PSCs. As a result, PSCs with bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (FSI)-based, TFSI-based, and PFSI-based HTM additives exhibited similar photovoltaic performances. Meanwhile, in terms of thermal stability, only PSCs with the FSI-based additives resulted in a significant performance drop, which differed from the properties of spiro-OMeTAD HTMs. Consequently, the compatibility difference of additives among the base HTMs was elucidarted. This study revealed the importance of developing additives tailored to different HTMs and may pave the way for discovering HTMs and their additives from a novel aspect.

papers.title: Tensor Train Compression of Molecular Orbitals
papers.abstract: This work systematically investigates the tensor train (TT) compressibility of gridrepresented Hartree-Fock and Density Functional Theory orbitals across a range of molecular systems and TT formats (standard, quantized, and z-permuted quantized). To overcome limitations of current TT solvers, we employ a novel orthogonal tensor train cross approximation (TT-Cross-Orth) to decompose Hartree-Fock and DFT orbitals into TTs, enabling the study of large molecules. We find that the approximation error decreases exponentially with TT-rank for all systems studied and identify QTT as the most efficient TT format. Furthermore, we identify quasi-periodic and symmetric structures-including graphene, graphite layers, and polyalanine helices-as particularly favorable candidates exhibiting sublinear rank growth with system size. The tensor train approach automatically compresses quasi-symmetries and systems with symmetry defects, which makes it an attractive approach for materials science applications. TT-Cross-Orth enforces orthogonality during the decomposition, thereby improving stability and reducing the number of function evaluations compared to standard TT-Cross. These findings establish an empirical foundation for the development of scalable tensor network methods for HF and DFT.

papers.title: The Pathfinder: Adaptive Learning for Hydrogen Storage Material Optimization
papers.abstract: Progress in solid-state hydrogen storage is critically constrained by the time consuming experimental measurements. While machine learning offers a promising route to accelerate materials screening, its accuracy is fundamentally limited by the scarcity of quality experimental data. To overcome this bottleneck, we introduce an adaptive learning (AL) framework that integrates uncertainty quantification into a closed-loop workflow for targeted material optimization. Unlike static models, this framework actively guides the selection of high-value compositions to maximize information gain and improve model predictability. As a proof of concept, we apply the framework for the prediction of pressure-composition-temperature (PCT) isotherms of Mg-Ni-La compositions using literature-reported data. Starting with a baseline model trained solely on PCT isotherms of Mg-Ni compositions, the model is iteratively refined through ten adaptive learning cycles. The uncertainty-driven composition selection effectively 1 identifies informative data points spanning Mg fractions from 92% to 4% and temperatures from 300 K to 633 K, demonstrating strong exploration capability across the chemical space. For ten unseen Mg-Ni-La compositions evaluated sequentially, the model accuracy converges upto 80% within the first five cycles, with predictions aligning well with experimental observations. This work demonstrates adaptive learning as a robust, data efficient predictive framework for accelerating the screening and optimization of hydrogen storage materials while minimizing experimental efforts.

papers.title: Reaction Intermediates Modulate Framework Flexibility in Zeolite ZSM-5 during the Methanol-to-Hydrocarbons Reaction
papers.abstract: Understanding how zeolite frameworks evolve during catalytic reactions is critical for improving their performance. Framework flexibility (the ability of zeolite T-O-T linkages to undergo angular and bond length variations that transiently adapt pore geometries) is increasingly recognized as key factor in adsorption and diffusion, yet its role remains unclear. Here, we investigate the dynamic behavior of zeolite ZSM-5 during the methanol-to-hydrocarbons (MTH) reaction, focusing on how reaction intermediates affect framework flexibility and pore accessibility. Using polarization-dependent attenuated total reflection infrared (ATR-PDIR) spectroscopy on b-oriented ZSM-5 thin films, where the straight channels align perpendicular to the substrate, we directly separated the responses of straight and sinusoidal pores. We correlate framework distortions and molecular orientation with catalytic function. The formation and orientation of key intermediates (methoxy, carbonyl, allylic carbocations, and aromatic precursors) coincide with zeolite stiffening within minutes on stream, while external pore blockage continues even after internal stiffening stabilizes. These effects are absent in silicalite controls. These findings indicate that early-formed intermediates modulate zeolite flexibility and initiate the formation of coke intermediates and hence the deactivation process. Flexibility thus emerges as an underexplored parameter for designing more resilient, adaptive zeolite catalysts.

papers.title: Boron-Centered Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer
papers.abstract: Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer (PCET) has been well-established in transition metal complexes, biomolecules, and organic compounds. In the majority of PCET reagent systems, hydrogen-atom equivalents are toggled predominantly at transition-metal centers or at heteroatomcontaining basic sites, most commonly amines, hydroxyl groups, or phosphines, where welldefined X-H bonds (X = N, O, P, or metal hydrides) provide the thermodynamic and kinetic framework for coupled proton-electron transfer. In this work, we demonstrate that a deliberately designed perfunctionalized redox-active boron cluster ( closo -B 6 Ph 6 2- ) can intrinsically mediate PCET, with the coupled proton and electron transfer events confined exclusively to boron atoms rather than being mediated by metals or heteroatom based functional groups, thereby representing the first unequivocal example of a purely boron-centered PCET process.

papers.title: Phase-Locked Dynamics: Decoupling Mechanical Stability and Reprocessability in Vitrimer Elastomers
papers.abstract: Vitrimers have emerged as a powerful class of dynamic polymer networks, yet their design has been largely governed by chemical exchange kinetics. This chemistrycentric view, however, falls short of rationalizing the persistent trade-off between mechanical stability and reprocessability in vitrimer elastomers. Here, we introduce Phase-Locked Dynamics (PLD) as a physics-based framework in which dynamic covalent bond exchange is hierarchically confined by multiphase architectures, including crystalline domains, supramolecular clusters, entanglement networks, and filler-induced physical locks. In PLD systems, relaxation processes are deliberately separated across length and time scales, enabling dynamic bonds to remain chemically active while mechanically latent under service conditions. We further discuss how nonequilibrium processing fields selectively activate exchange pathways by coupling multiscale relaxation modes, offering a route to program vitrimer topology and anisotropy without altering intrinsic bond chemistry. By integrating polymer physics, simulation-guided insights, and emerging experimental evidence, this Perspective establishes Phase-Locked Dynamics as a general design principle for vitrimer elastomers with decoupled mechanical stability and processability.

papers.title: REACTION ENUMERATION BASED ON NBO-INFORMED MOLECULE GRAPHS
papers.abstract: Enumeration of reaction products and pathways is essential for understanding chemical reactivity and for the rational design of new chemical technologies. Traditional graph-based enumeration methods represent molecules through atomic connectivity and simple valency rules, with bond breaking and formation encoded as edge modifications. However, this representation becomes ambiguous for many important classes of chemical systems, including transition-metal complexes, hypervalent compounds, and molecules with extensive resonance or delocalization. Here, we introduce a molecular graph representation constructed at the level of valence orbitals rather than atomic connectivity alone. When combined with quantum-mechanical Natural Bond Orbital (NBO) analysis, the method automatically detects delocalized bonding motifs and adaptively increases reaction-step complexity when chemically warranted. This integration enables systematic and computationally efficient identification of chemically meaningful reaction pathways that lie beyond the practical scope of conventional graph-based approaches. We demonstrate the robustness of the method across challenging bonding environments, including organometallic catalytic cycles, pericyclic reactions in highly delocalized systems, main-group hypervalent chemistry, and multicomponent reaction networks.

papers.title: Sensor arrays built with a single sensor element: complexity conferred through simple co-assembly achieves sensitive, information-rich outputs
papers.abstract: Differential sensing with macrocyclic host molecules has enabled the detection of diverse chemical structures and complex mixtures, quickly advancing towards clinical applications. However, current systems are typically constrained by the binding properties of their individual sensor components, limiting practical implementation. In this work, we introduce a fundamentally different strategy: functional complexity is conferred onto a single reporter host through non‑covalent co‑assembly with a second host that brings both high potency and inherently high promiscuity — sulfo‑pillar[n]arene. This co-assembly approach augments the performance of a DimerDye-class sensor by increasing its sensitivity (>100-fold in some cases) and by creating dramatic variations in its responses to different analytes. We present evidence that the co-assembled sensor forms ternary complexes with certain analytes, and that its new emergent properties include increased signal intensity and unique changes in fluorescence output. This means the performance typically achieved by sensor arrays built from several distinct host-type sensors can now be achieved using only a single DimerDye sensor that is simply mixed with unadorned sulfo-pillar[n]arenes under two different conditions. We report the mechanisms by which this emergent sensing occurs and demonstrate that a simple co-assembly enables differentiation of complex biological mixtures, reliably distinguishing between illicit drugs and whole-tissue samples of wild mushrooms.

papers.title: De Novo Chemoenzymatic Synthesis of Asymmetric N-Glycans Empowered by Sulfate and Phosphate as Novel Orthogonal Protecting Groups
papers.abstract: Glycoproteins often exist in nature as heterogeneous glycoforms, and it has been difficult to obtain pure homogeneous samples to study the role of specific N-glycans in a glycoprotein. Despite various chemical and enzymatic methods developed for the synthesis of N-glycans, access to highly diverse N-glycans remains a challenge. Herein, we report a concise strategy for the synthesis of multi-antennary N-glycans from designed common core structures with phosphate and sulfate protecting groups, which can be selectively deprotected by respective phosphatase and sulfatase, thereby enabling enzymatic elongation to install a desired glycan chain at a specific antenna. We also explored the directing effect of galactose sulfation for enzymatic fucosylation of the neighboring GlcNAc, further expanding the structural diversity of multi-antennary N-glycans. Starting from sulfate and phosphate-terminated core structures, this synthetic strategy in aqueous solution provides an efficient and practical route for the enzymatic assembly of a diverse array of complex N-glycans for biological study.

papers.title: Femtosecond Soft X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy Identifies Metal-Centered S1 Excited State of Cyanocobalamin
papers.abstract: Time-resolved X-ray absorption spectroscopy (TRXAS) at the Co L 3 -edge was used to identify metal-centered (MC) character in the S 1 excited state of cyanocobalamin (CNCbl). Cobalamins have UV/visible spectra that are dominated by intense corrin-based excitations, but these ligand-centered states energetically overlap with charge transfer and MC excited states that may be populated following photoexcitation. Ultrafast optical and hard X-ray spectroscopy have shown that CNCbl forms a structurally distorted S 1 state, but these probes lack a clear signature of the S 1 electronic identity, which theory has suggested is a ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) state. Femtosecond soft X-ray TRXAS offers greater state-selectivity than many optical or hard X-ray probes, but has, so far, been limited to highly concentrated (≥100 mM) samples. A new experimental setup at the European X-ray Free Electron Laser (EuXFEL) that enables studies of sub-10 mM samples and provides ∼100 fs time-resolution is used to measure the TRXAS of CNCbl at the Co L 3 -edge. Comparison of the L 3 -edge XAS spectrum measured at 0.8 ps with ligand field multiplet simulations indicates that the S 1 state is primarily a MC excited state. The sub-20 µOD detection sensitivity achieved in this study demonstrates the possibility of applying this method to a wide range of naturally-occurring and synthetic transition metal complexes.

papers.title: SPHERE-MS: Hybrid Fragment-Vocabulary Modeling for Accurate and Efficient Tandem Mass Spectra Prediction
papers.abstract: Identifying known compounds and elucidating unknown chemical structures from mass spectra remains a significant challenge due to the limited size of experimental reference libraries. Enhancing these libraries with predicted mass spectra through computational methods offers an opportunity to resolve unmatched spectra. In this paper, we present SPHERE-MS (Secondary-loss Powered Hybrid Edge Removal Engine for predicting Mass Spectra), a graph neural network model designed to predict mass spectra from molecular structures. The hybrid approach, combining bond-breaking and vocabulary-based strategies, enables SPHERE-MS to efficiently simulate multi-level fragmentation processes without the need to enumerate all possible bond combinations. Evaluations on the NIST-20, MSnLib, and CASMI2022 datasets demonstrate that SPHERE-MS outperforms baseline models that rely on single fragment generation strategy, showing higher prediction accuracy and library retrieval success rates. Notably, SPHERE-MS also maintains reasonable accuracy even when applied to molecules with low structural similarity to the training set. This strong generalization capability makes SPHERE-MS a valuable tool for mass spectra prediction across large libraries, including those containing uncommon structures.

papers.title: Enzymatic Nylon degradation: enzyme discoveries, engineering and challenges
papers.abstract: Nylons are among the most widely produced synthetic polyamides, prized for their strength, versatility, and durability across textiles, packaging, and engineering applications. However, their petrochemical precursors and high energy demand make Nylon production a significant source of greenhouse gas emissions, highlighting the need for more efficient and circular solutions. Conventional recycling methods, either mechanical and chemical, achieve only partial material recovery and remain limited by efficiency, material degradation, and the need for costly sorting. Enzymatic depolymerization offers a promising low-energy and selective alternative, capable of recycling mixed feedstocks under mild conditions. While enzymatic recycling has advanced for polyesters such as polyethylene terephthalate (PET), the enzymatic breakdown of polyamides remains in its early stage. The discovery of Nylon hydrolases, notably NylC, revealed that microbial systems can evolve catalysts to degrade synthetic polyamides. However, enzymatic Nylon depolymerization is still inefficient, with typical reported yields below 1%. These low yields are due in part to the inherent structural complexity and semicrystallinity of Nylons but also demonstrate the need for additional effort on discovering, characterizing, and engineering Nylon hydrolases. This review examines the progress, challenges, and future directions of enzymatic Nylon recycling, outlining its potential role enabling mixed polymer waste to be used as a green feedstock for remanufacturing.

papers.title: Cyclic Block Copolymers via Living Ring Expansion Metathesis Polymerization
papers.abstract: Cyclic block copolymers are a captivating class of macromolecules with the potential for advanced materials applications due to their distinctive self-assembly behavior. Ring expansion metathesis polymerization (REMP) is a promising method towards such high molar mass cyclic polymers, but uncontrolled intermolecular ring-transfer processes have precluded its extension to cyclic block copolymers synthesis. As a result, the synthesis of cyclic block copolymers remains exceedingly rare. In this work, we develop a novel controlled living REMP method using cyclic Ru-benzylidene initiator Pyr-CB6. Using an operationally simple sequential monomer-addition strategy followed by thermally triggered intramolecular backbiting, we produce cyclic multiblock copolymers of low dispersity (<1.2) and high yields (up to 97%). Mechanistic analyses elucidate the delicate role that pyridine plays as a secondary metathesis inhibitor, preventing intermolecular ring-transfer while permitting backbiting, when triggered. Overall, this study demonstrates the power of REMP with Pyr-CB6 as a vehicle towards a diverse future of cyclic block copolymer materials and applications.

papers.title: Microscopic origins of hysteresis and conduction mechanisms of defective MoS 2 /Au(111)-based devices
papers.abstract: We present a first-principles investigation of vertical Au(111)/monolayer MoS 2 /Au(111) heterostructures that links atomic-scale structural evolution, defect energetics, and bias-dependent transport barriers to memristive switching behavior. Three distinct and concurrent hysteresis mechanisms are revealed: (i) sliding-induced hysteresis of the MoS 2 layer, which also occurs in the absence of defects, (ii) defect-driven hysteresis associated with adatom motion and registry changes between MoS 2 and Au, and (iii) electronic-based hysteresis arising from reversible transitions between different conduction mechanisms (electron-barrier limited, defect mediated, Ohmic) due to band bending. Our calculations reveal how these mechanisms of hysteresis act through a nonlinear modulation of the effective electron injection barriers at the metal-semiconductor interface. This barrier modulation directly controls charge injection, trap occupation, and the activation of different conduction regimes. To connect to transport characteristics, we employ a non-equilibrium Green's function approach within an effective-mass model using the bias-dependent barrier profiles extracted from first-principles calculations and find a switching ratio of two orders of magnitude, consistent with measurements. The resulting framework provides a unified microscopic description of hysteresis in vertical memristors based on defects in monolayer materials.

papers.title: Decoding C-O vs C-C Bond Selectivity in Nickel-Metallaphotoredox Carboxylic Acid Cross-Coupling
papers.abstract: Understanding how catalytic systems dictate product selectivity is crucial for advancing sustainable cross-coupling chemistry. While nickel-photoredox dual catalysis has unlocked CC and CO bond formation from carboxylic acids and aryl halides, the mechanistic origins of this divergence have remained elusive. Here, we combine systematic experimentation with density functional theory (DFT) calculations and electrochemical analysis to uncover the key parameters that govern whether CC or CO bonds are formed. We show that the halide identity of the aryl electrophile exerts a decisive influence: iodides strongly favor esterification via a low-barrier reductive elimination pathway, bromides promote decarboxylative CC coupling, and chlorides, with prohibitively high CO barriers, yield exclusively CC products. Complementary experiments reveal that both photocatalyst loading and halide additives modulate selectivity, in direct agreement with computed energy landscapes. Together, these insights establish a unified mechanistic framework that explains divergent reactivity across seemingly similar conditions. By demonstrating how subtle changes in halide, photocatalyst, and additives toggle reaction outcomes, our study provides predictive design principles for exploiting carboxylic acids in nickel-photoredox catalysis.

papers.title: EEM fluorescence data-driven determination of cell density in adherent cell cultures
papers.abstract: Accurate, precise, and non-invasive determination of cell density is a critical challenge in cell culture research, directly influencing experimental reproducibility and reliability of biological interpretations. Conventional methods, such as cell counting and colorimetric assays, are invasive and often unsuitable for continuous monitoring. This study evaluates excitation-emission matrix (EEM) fluorescence spectroscopy (multispectral fluorescence) combined with chemometric analysis as an innovative, data-driven approach for quantifying cell density in adherent cultures. The experiments were performed using two adherent cell lines, i.e., HaCaT and A375, simultaneously, to verify if the observed trends might extend beyond a single cell line and thus not be cell-line specific, which could further support the general applicability of the proposed cell number determination strategy. The number of cells in culture was determined using two reference methods, i.e., classical cell counting or the MTT assay providing information on the number of metabolically active cells. Unfolded partial least squares (PLS) regression was used to develop models for predicting cell numbers based on information encoded in excitation-emission spectra of cell cultures. Statistical analysis shows that multispectral fluorescence surpasses cell counting in sensitivity, while the MTT assay exhibits the highest precision. By enabling label-free, non-destructive, and repeatable measurements with applicability across different cell lines, multispectral fluorescence can be proposed as an interesting alternative, especially for automated and dynamic monitoring of cell cultures.

papers.title: Bioinspired Diversification of Short Peptides via Tyrosine Umpolung
papers.abstract: Herein, we report a bioinspired strategy for the selective modification of tyrosine residues in short peptides based on a formal umpolung of the phenolic side chain. Mild oxidation with a hypervalent iodine(V) reagent enables the in situ generation of ortho-quinone intermediates, effecting a polarity inversion. These electrophilic intermediates can be selectively intercepted by external nucleophiles, enabling diversification of tyrosine residues either through skeletal modification of the phenolic core into phenazine scaffolds, or via peripheral modifications through the formation of tyrosine-cysteine cross-links.

papers.title: How spin conductive are oligo(p-phenylenes) in trityl-based biradicals
papers.abstract: The relationship between structure and exchange coupling constant J is of interest for the rational design of molecular open-shell systems in the context of molecular magnetism, dynamic nuclear polarization, and quantum information science. However, even for the basic relationship between J and the distance r between two spin centers for the archetypal oligo( p -phenylene) bridge, there are only a few and contradicting experimental and theoretical data. We therefore synthesized a series of six trityl-[( p -phenylene) n=1-5 ]-trityl biradicals and used Electron Paramagnetic Resonance methods to extract J values in the range from 17.5 MHz to 235 GHz. We find a distance dependence parameter β of 0.11 Å -1 for unsubstituted and 0.67 Å -1 for substituted oligo( p -phenylene) bridges. This places unsubstituted oligo( p -phenylene)-bridges into the spin-conductor regime and highlights the tunability of conductance by substitution, i.e., increase of the dihedral angle between the phenylene units. DFT calculations employing low Fock-exchange fraction functionals exhibit some limitations in reproducing the experimental J value, particularly in the weak coupling regime. Furthermore, biradicals with n = 3-5 exhibit spin coherence of 1.2 µs at room temperature in the liquid state. These long coherence times, combined with the modular bridge design, position bistrityl systems as promising candidates for applications in quantum information technology.

papers.title: Air-tolerant solar reforming of pre-treated biomass and plastics in viscous sustainable solvents
papers.abstract: We report an air-tolerant solar reforming (SR) system for the valorisation of pretreated biomass and plastic waste streams. This process operates in low O2-diffusivity solvents such as the robust deep eutectic solvent (DES) ZnCl2-acetamide in water to prevent O2 from interfering with the photocatalytic reaction. This approach sustains SR performance under aerobic conditions using a carbon nitride photocatalyst, enabling photooxidative valorisation of depolymerised cellulose and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) while generating H2 fuel. SR using low O2-diffusivity solvents is scalable and also adaptable to non-innocent viscous liquid wastes such as glycerol, which can act as both the low O2-diffusivity solvent to exclude O2 and the organic waste source to produce valuable chemicals.

papers.title: A Hydrazoic Acid Adduct of Rh 2 : Synthesis, Characterization, and Imidogen-Transfer Photochemistry
papers.abstract: Metal-imidogen (i.e., M-NH) are proposed to mediate bond cleavage and construction in an emerging family of metal-catalyzed NH-transfer reactions. Transition metal complexes of hydrazoic acid (HN3) could serve as precursors to these transient intermediates; however, the coordination chemistry of HN3 is essentially unknown. Here, we report the synthesis and characterization of Rh2(esp)2(HN3)2, the first crystalline transition metal complex of HN3 (esp = α,α,α′,α′-tetramethyl-1,3-benzenedipropionate). Temperature-dependent multi-nuclear NMR, UV-vis, and IR spectroscopies demonstrate that HN3 is a weakly coordinating ligand (Keq = 1100 ± 100 M-2 at 243 K). Photolysis of Rh2(esp)2(HN3)2 in the presence of olefinic substrates results in stereospecific imidogen transfer to afford N-H aziridines. Cryogenic photolysis (77 K) enabled observation of a non-steady state intermediate, which we assign to be a triplet Rh2-NH complex. The nitrene photochemistry of Rh2(esp)2(HN3)2 was corroborated by in crystallo synthesis and cryogenic spectroscopic characterization of a family of N-aryl nitrene complexes. Together, these results establish the coordination chemistry of HN3, confirm the triplet ground state of the Rh2-NH intermediate responsible for catalytic NH transfer, and demonstrate a photochemical platform to study NH-transfer catalysis.

papers.title: Structure-free generation of transition state conformations with Bayesian flow networks
papers.abstract: Transition state (TS) conformation prediction is crucial for understanding reaction mechanisms and guiding catalyst or enzyme design yet remains challenging due to the intrinsic instability and structural sensitivity of TSs. Conventional determination relies heavily on expert intuition and computationally intensive quantum chemistry methods. Existing 3D-input search approaches are sensitive to initial conformations, while other methods tend to yield high-variance and imprecise results, limiting their practical application. Here, we introduce TSBFN, a structurefree transition state conformation generator based on Bayesian flow networks, directly from reaction SMILES and graphs. TSBFN achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming other machine learning methods with a median structural deviation of 0.064 Å and a 93.4% intrinsic reaction coordinate (IRC) validation rate. Notably, TSBFN generates inherently compact conformational distributions that naturally coalesce into a handful of high-quality candidates per reaction, substantially mitigating the challenge of TS selection. Furthermore, the structure-free design demonstrates enhanced robustness and efficacy in challenging multi-component systems. In an out-of-distribution Claisen rearrangement case, TSBFN efficiently generated two distinct classes of mechanistically relevant and valid TSs at millisecond speed, achieving 100% IRC validation and underscoring its potential for automated reaction exploration.

papers.title: Unified Mechanistic Insights into Hydrogen Evolution and Oxidation from Homogeneous to Heterogeneous Electrocatalysis
papers.abstract: Direct comparisons between homogeneous and heterogeneous electrocatalysis using the same molecular system remain rare, despite their importance for catalyst design and device integration. Here, we investigate the heterogenization of the DuBois-Shaw nickel catalyst [Ni(P Cy ₂N Arg ₂)] 2 ⁺ (NiCyArg), a well-characterized molecular electrocatalyst for reversible H₂/H⁺ interconversion, and assess whether its established homogeneous mechanistic framework can be extended to surface-confined conditions. The catalyst was successfully immobilized onto edge-plane graphite electrodes via noncovalent interactions. Cyclic voltammetry over a range of pH values under Ar and H₂ demonstrates that the heterogenized catalyst retains its reversibility and bidirectional catalytic activity near the thermodynamic H₂/H⁺ potential, with a pronounced bias toward hydrogen oxidation. Pourbaix analysis reveals redox potentials and pKₐ values of key intermediates that closely match those obtained under homogeneous conditions, indicating minimal perturbation of the thermodynamic landscape upon immobilization. Kinetic analysis using a simplified ECrECr model shows that the same chemical step remains rate-limiting in both regimes, while internal proton transfer processes are modestly slowed upon surface confinement. Overall, this work provides a quantitative bridge between homogeneous and heterogeneous systems and demonstrates that solution phase mechanistic models can in some conditions be applied to surface immobilised systems.

papers.title: Synthesis and biological characterization of [3.1.0], [3.2.0], [3.3.0], and [3.4.0] bicyclic pyrrolidine analogs as D4 and sigma 1 receptor dual modulators
papers.abstract: Dopamine D4 (D4R) and sigma-1 (σ1R) receptors represent attractive targets for the treatment of neurological disorders, including L-DOPA–induced dyskinesias associated with Parkinson’s disease. Guided by prior work on D4R antagonists and σ1R modulators, we designed and synthesized a series of sp³-rich bicyclic pyrrolidine scaffolds ([3.1.0]–[3.4.0]) using a modular [3+2] cycloaddition strategy that enabled rapid exploration of structural diversity. In vitro profiling revealed pronounced structure–activity relationships driven by ring size and southern substituents, with the compact [3.1.0] and [3.2.0] scaffolds exhibiting optimal physicochemical properties and potent dual activity, including D4R Ki values of 1–5 nM and σ1R Ki values <10 nM for multiple analogs. Selected chemotypes delivered high σ1R selectivity, while others maintained strong D4R potency. Although high intrinsic clearance was observed across the series, several [3.1.0] and [3.2.0] compounds showed improved microsomal stability, moderate plasma protein binding, and robust in vivo brain penetration (Kp >3). Lead compounds 9b and 12b demonstrated favorable exposure and half-life in rat cassette studies, with discrete mouse pharmacokinetics confirming sustained brain concentrations well above D4R Ki values. Collectively, these findings establish bicyclic pyrrolidines as a versatile chemotype for dual D4R/σ1R modulation and identify 9b and 12b as promising in vivo tool compounds and leads for further optimization toward L-DOPA–induced dyskinesia.

papers.title: H NMR Chemical Shift as an Index of UV-Vis Absorption/Emission Maxima in Aromatic Dyes
papers.abstract: We have demonstrated that experimental ¹H NMR chemical shifts can serve as direct indicators of absorption and emission maxima within families of structurally related molecules. Notably, predictions of optical maxima based on chemical shifts have proven to be more accurate than excitation energies obtained from time-dependent density functional theory employing long-range corrected functionals such as CAM-B3LYP. This proof of principle has first been established using experimental data for a series of pyrrolo[3,2-b]pyrroles, for which a linear correlation between the absorption maximum and the ¹H NMR chemical shift has been identified for the first time. The scope of the study has then been extended to diketopyrrolopyrroles, additional pyrrolo[3,2-b]pyrroles, and thieno[3,2-b]thiophenes using density functional theory calculations. Across all investigated compound families, the correlation has remained close to linear. We have shown that two key criteria must be fulfilled to preserve this linearity: steric similarity among the compared molecules and full π-conjugation of the molecular framework. These conditions arise from the dependence of magnetically induced ring-current strengths, i.e., the most influential factor on the ¹H NMR chemical shifts of conjugated molecules, on frontier-orbital energy gaps, together with symmetry selection rules formulated by Fowler and Steiner. These findings have provided new insight into the electronic structure of quadrupolar dyes and have established a practical framework for the rapid and efficient design of optoelectronic materials.

papers.title: Environmental Stability of Alkyl Phosphate and Sulfate-Containing Membranes as Early Cell Models
papers.abstract: The ability of simple amphiphiles to assemble into stable membranes is central to understanding how protocells may have formed on the early Earth. In this work, we examine how small structural differences, specifically hydrocarbon chain length and headgroup identity, influence membrane formation, stability, and permeability in mixed-amphiphile systems exposed to diverse conditions to understand the role of the environment in protocell evolution. Using automated sample preparation and confocal microscopy, we characterized eight compositions containing decyl sulfate (DS), dodecyl sulfate (DDS), or dodecyl phosphate (DDP) across a range of pH values in ultra-pure 1 water, sea salt, or sea salt mixed with a complex prebiotic organic solution. Longer chain and phosphate-containing amphiphiles formed more vesicles, particularly at low pH and high ionic strength. DS exhibited consistently low and environment-insensitive critical vesicle concentration (CVC), whereas DDP displayed the highest sensitivity to alkaline conditions. DDP-containing vesicles were the least permeable, highlighting the lipid packing influence of the phosphate headgroup. Together, these findings show that small modifications in amphiphile composition strongly affect membrane properties in across early Earth-like environments, demonstrating the role of anionic surfactants in protocell emergence.

papers.title: Unexpected Chemistry of Molecular Precursors to Boron Arsenide Materials
papers.abstract: Simple arsine-boranes were explored as precursors to the semiconductor ceramic cubic boron arsenide (BAs). In preparing Ph 2 AsHBH 3 , spontaneous hydrogen loss was observed to give cyclo -arsine boranes, (Ph 2 AsBH 2 ) n , and other products. At low temperature, Ph 2 AsHBH 3 could be isolated and observed to engage in spontaneous hydrogen to form (Ph 2 AsBH 2 ) n rings. These rings exhibit dynamic behavior through varying ratios of n = 3, 4, but n = 5 could be observed and promoted under non-equilibrium conditions. Interestingly, the arsine substrate appears catalyze the decomposition of THF-borane, and simple boranes are catalysts for the dehydrocoupling of Ph 2 AsH. However, the most chemically odd observation was the relative lability of As–C bonds under mild conditions. While (Ph 2 AsBH 2 ) n and Ph 3 AsBH 3 are competent substrates for the formation of boron arsenide products under pyrolysis conditions, particularly in air, ceramic yields suffer from volatility of the substate under pyrolysis conditions and competitive arsenic oxidation occurred unpredictably. Arsenic chemistry aside, this overall strategy is valid for the production bulk boron arsenide substrates, through further substrate development is needed.

papers.title: Polyoxometalate-Assisted Crystallization: A General Strategy Enabling Structural Characterization of Molecular Radium Complexes
papers.abstract: A fundamental understanding of radium (Ra) coordination chemistry has been hindered by the scarcity and radiological hazards of 226 Ra, leaving the structural characterization of molecular Ra complexes almost entirely unexplored. Here, we present a polyoxometalate (POM)-assisted crystallization strategy that enables single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis of Ra–chelator complexes from microgram-scale samples. Employing the Keggin anion [SiW 12 O 40 ] 4– , we isolate and structurally characterize Ra 2+ complexes of 18-crown-6 and the bis-picolinate macrocycle macropa, together with their Sr 2+ and Ba 2+ analogues. The resulting structures reveal systematic, size-dependent trends in coordination number and metal-donor distances across the alkaline earth series, notably this series also features the first reported Ra–N and Ra–O COO bonds. This work establishes POM-assisted crystallization as a robust approach for obtaining solid-state structural information on Ra 2+ complexes of organic chelators and provides a generalizable route for advancing the coordination chemistry of scarce, highly radioactive elements accessible only in trace quantities.

papers.title: Leveraging Hidden-Space Representations Effectively in Bayesian Optimization for Experiment Design through Dimension-Aware Hyperpriors
papers.abstract: Hidden-space molecular representations derived from pretrained graph neural networks, Transformer models, and large language models offer an appealing alternative to conventional encodings for Bayesian optimization (BO) in chemical experiment design. However, their performance benefits in BO remain poorly understood and difficult to assess in practice, and, when deployed within current chemical BO frameworks, they often do not yield clear advantages over traditional representations. Here, we show that this behavior arises from a previously underappreciated interaction between representation dimensionality and Gaussian process kernel hyperpriors, rather than from limitations of the representations themselves. We demonstrate that different chemical representations induce substantial variations in search-space dimensionality, which, when paired with fixed or mismatched lengthscale hyperpriors, lead to flat marginal likelihood landscapes and severely degrade surrogate learning and acquisition optimization. To address this issue, we introduce a dimension-aware adaptive hyperprior, tailored to reaction optimization, whose characteristic lengthscale scales with the square root of the search space dimensionality. Benchmarking across multiple reaction optimization datasets and molecular representations shows that this adaptive hyperprior consistently restores and amplifies the performance advantages of hidden-space featurizations over traditional representations, such as Mordred or one-hot encoding. Our results identify hyperprior calibration as a critical requirement for fair evaluation and effective deployment of modern molecular representations in chemical BO.

papers.title: Perdefluorinative borylation of perfluoroalkyl and gem-difluoroalkenes
papers.abstract: Polyfluorinated organic molecules including perfluoroalkyl substances (so-called PFAS) are broadly used as water-repellents and flame retardants, in paper coatings, fire extinguishing chemicals, agrochemicals, and drugs. However, these compounds are resistant towards degradation and known to bioaccumulate in the environment and organ tissue with numerous associated negative health effects. This persistence further renders the chemical treatment of PFAS highly challenging. We herein report a “zipper” reaction that strips off all fluorine atoms from a perfluoroalkyls bound to an alkene and converts these PFAS compounds into synthetically useful boronate building blocks without destruction of the carbon framework. This is achieved by a combination of pinacolborane and lithium methoxide that iteratively removes the fluoride substituents from the attached perfluoroalkyl chain through repeated hydroboration/β-F-elimination steps. The reaction then installs a boronate function at the chain terminus, which overall turns the problematic PFAS into useful synthesis reagents. Yields of up to >99% are achieved per fluorine atom and the isolation of LiF by simple filtration is demonstrated. The reaction also works on gem -difluoroalkenes, which we conclude to be intermediates of the PFAS perdefluoro-monoborylation reaction.

papers.title: Non-enzymatic Raman sensing of lactic acid in microbial cultures: applications in resolving protonation states
papers.abstract: Lactic acid is a key microbial metabolite with widespread industrial applications in food preservation, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, polymer industries, and others. The detection of lactic acid directly in complex microbial culture remains a challenge. Enzymatic assays and high-performance liquid chromatography are traditional methods for lactic acid detection which require extensive sample preparation. In this study, we report a non-enzymatic Raman sensing framework for the direct detection and mapping of lactic acid in microbial culture. We used Lactobacillus plantarum and Lactobacillus acidophilus as representative lactic acid producing microbes, and the characteristic Raman signal of lactic acid was detected from microbial culture supernatants. An additional multiplex advantage of the approach is that both protonated and deprotonated forms of lactic acid were detected under varying culture pH conditions across species. Raman imaging was also performed directly on microbial cultures, making it possible to visualise the spatial distribution of lactic acid. Raman images revealed a diffuse distribution of lactic acid within the culture matrix, consistent with metabolic secretion by actively growing cells. This work pipeline highlights the analytical utility of Raman spectroscopy for a reagent-free, non-invasive, and minimal signal processing sensing platform for lactic detection and spatially resolved analysis for the future integration for in-line monitoring in bioreactor systems.

papers.title: Reversible layered-disordered transitions enabled by entropic stabilization
papers.abstract: High configurational entropy was shown to impart emergent physical and structural functionalities to various oxides, with the notable exception of transition metal layered lithium oxides which were observed to possess poor electrochemical performance associated with secondary impurity phases. Through a combined thermal analysis using operando X-ray diffraction and calorimetric techniques with scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) measurements, we reveal the crystallization pathway of compositionally complex lithiated oxides and show how entropystabilization can be manipulated to enable enhanced electrochemical performance associated with reversible structural transitions in layered oxides. Screening various high-entropy and mediumentropy layered oxides and studying their thermal behavior, we show how precise control of synthetic conditions yields co-existing layered and disordered rock salt (DRX) nano-domains and the formation of antisite defects, both enabling enhanced electrochemical performance with reversible layered to spinel and layered to DRX structural transitions upon Li (de)intercalation. By comparing oxides with similar configurational entropy but different enthalpy of mixing, we show that large configurational entropy, as calculated assuming an ideal mixing, cannot be used as sole criterion for designing enhanced intercalation materials, with transformation energies and non-ideal enthalpy and entropy of mixing offsetting the stabilization effect of configurational entropy. The fundamental insights gained in this work regarding the thermal and electrochemical behavior of high entropy layered materials constitute a crucial step towards the choice of synthetic conditions to control the complex interplay between thermodynamics and kinetics in stabilizing compositionally complex layered oxides.

papers.title: Comparative Molecular Dynamics Analysis of Dopamine Receptors in C. elegans and Human Reveal Common Domains and Ligand Interactions with Implications for Parkinson’s Disease
Chirality transfer in nematic liquid crystals via octahedral coordination compounds with Δ and Λ chirality
papers.abstract: Nematic (N) liquid crystals (LCs), characterized by long-range orientational order, readily transform into chiral nematic (N*) phases upon the incorporation of optically active substances known as chiral dopants. While the ease of N* induction has driven the extensive development of organic chiral dopants, coordination compounds possessing Δ/Λ chirality have emerged as compelling alternatives, offering distinct structural and functional attributes. This review highlights not only the advantages of the "metallodopants", such as their high twisting power (HTP) and predictable structure, but also discusses their current limitations. Future perspectives regarding the design of multi-functional chiral materials are also provided. A defining feature of metallodopants is their exceptionally high helical twisting power (HTP). For instance, early studies demonstrated that the simple complex Δ- or Λ-[M(acac) 3 ] (M = Co, Cr, Ru, Ir, Rh, acac = acetylacetonate) exhibits remarkably high HTP. This efficiency is attributed to the rigid coordination framework, which facilitates robust chirality transfer to the host LC. However, metallodopants often face challenges regarding miscibility with nematic hosts and intrinsic coloration, potentially complicating their integration into optical devices; consequently, systematic investigations have been limited compared to organic dopants. Nevertheless, metallodopants offer unique advantages. In tris(chelate) metal complexes, the sense of the induced helix ( P or M ) is strongly correlated with ligand orientation; for example, a 90° rotation of a ligand’s elongation axis can reverse the helical sense. This predictable inversion, supported by theoretical models, underscores the critical role of structural rigidity. Furthermore, the intrinsic absorption of these complexes, once viewed as a drawback, is now being harnessed for resonance Raman enhancement and chiroptical modulation. By combining high HTP, predictable helix inversion, and spectroscopic utility, metallodopants are positioning themselves as versatile competitors to organic dopants, serving as both functional inducers and optical probes for next-generation photonic and sensing technologies.

papers.title: Armstrongs Probabilistic Electron Phase-Space Overlap Model (APEPM)
papers.abstract: Context Assessing whether a bonding interaction is geometrically possible, that is, whether the probabilistic electron clouds of two atoms spatially overlap at a given internuclear separation, is a fundamental but often implicit aspect of molecular modeling. Conventional electronic structure methods address this question indirectly through wavefunction optimization and energetic analysis, which can obscure the underlying geometric constraints and limit scalability. Here, Armstrong’s Probabilistic Electron Phase-Space Overlap Model (APEPM) is introduced as a geometry-driven, wavefunction-free framework for evaluating geometric bond feasibility by explicitly determining whether nonzero electron cloud overlap exists for any specified atomic separation. The model provides closed-form expressions for the size and extent of the shared electron phase-space and tracks how this overlap evolves continuously under bond compression or extension. By mapping the overlap region onto radially partitioned orbital shells, APEPM identifies which atomic orbital regions are geometrically involved in the mandatory shared phase-space, yielding an interpretable description of spatial orbital involvement that is independent of energetic weighting or bond strength assignment. Methods APEPM represents bonded atoms as interacting probabilistic electron volumes characterized by effective electron cloud radii derived from atomic electron cloud extents. Geometric overlap is determined analytically using closed-form expressions for the intersection of two spheres as a function of internuclear distance, yielding overlap radius, cross-sectional area, and overlap volume, with zero overlap defining the geometric infeasibility limit. Orbital participation is evaluated by projecting the overlap region along the bond axis and identifying intersections with predefined radial orbital shells. Admissible electron participation within intersected orbitals is constrained using Armstrong’s Range Exponent Electron Configuration Model (AREECM), which assigns minimum and maximum probability bounds consistent with normalization and exclusion principles and incorporates a discrete bond-interaction constraint for each bonding interaction. All calculations are analytic and geometry-based and are implemented in Python using custom software developed for this work.

papers.title: Quantum Tunneling On Water I. General framework for microdroplet redox chemistry
Topology-Enabled Many-Body Reinforcement Mechanisms in Toroidal Graphene–Bronze Composites
Artificial Intelligence for Direct Prediction of Molecular Dynamics Across Chemical Space
papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) is a powerful tool for exploring the behavior of atomistic systems, but its reliance on sequential numerical integration limits simulation efficiency. We present a novel neural network architecture, MDtrajNet, and a pre-trained foundational model, MDtrajNet-1, that directly generates MD trajectories across chemical space, bypassing force calculations and integration. MDtrajNet combines equivariant neural networks with a transformer-based architecture to achieve strong accuracy and transferability in predicting long-time trajectories. This approach accelerates simulations by up to two orders of magnitude and yields better accuracy than MD propagated with established machine-learning interatomic potentials trained on the same data. Remarkably, the errors of the trajectories generated by MDtrajNet-1 for various seen and even unseen small-sized molecular systems are close to those of the conventional ab initio MD. The current limitations of MDtrajNet-1 are attributed to the relatively small size of the chemical space in its training data; however, even for bigger, unseen systems, MDtrajNet-1 provides a good starting point for fine-tuning and obtaining system-specific models. The architecture’s flexible design supports diverse application scenarios, including different statistical ensembles, boundary conditions, and interaction types. By overcoming the intrinsic speed barrier of conventional MD, MDtrajNet opens new frontiers in efficient and scalable atomistic simulations.

papers.title: Structure Prediction of Organic/Inorganic Interfaces with Genarris
papers.abstract: Organic/inorganic interfaces perform critical functions in organic electronic devices and their structure can affect device performance. In addition, interactions with the substrate can promote the growth of otherwise metastable thin film structures by epitaxial templating. Predicting the structure of organic/inorganic interfaces by computer simulations can aid in the design of interfaces with desirable properties. We present Genarris Interfaces, a structure generator for organic/inorganic interfaces. Genarris uses epitaxy matrices to impose commensurism with the substrate. Film structures are generated in all layer groups that are compatible with the substrate symmetry and the requested number of molecules per unit cell. Clustering and down-selection are performed to reduce the number of structures while maintaining the diversity of packing motifs. Finally, relaxation and stability ranking are performed using dispersion-inclusive density functional theory (DFT). We demonstrate the application of Genarris for the interfaces of PTCDA on Ag(111), TCNE on Au(111), and naphthalene on Cu(111). In all cases, we find generated structures that resemble experimental scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) images. The electronic structure agrees well with spectroscopy experiments, where available. We envision Genarris Interfaces being used to predict the structure of organic/inorganic interfaces, to generate initial populations for other structure prediction algorithms, and to generate datasets for training machine learning models.

papers.title: Polyoxometalate-Assisted Crystallization: A General Strategy Enabling Structural Characterization of Molecular Radium Complexes
papers.abstract: A fundamental understanding of radium (Ra) coordination chemistry has been hindered by the scarcity and radiological hazards of 226 Ra, leaving the structural characterization of molecular Ra complexes almost entirely unexplored. Here, we present a polyoxometalate (POM)-assisted crystallization strategy that enables single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis of Ra–chelator complexes from microgram-scale samples. Employing the Keggin anion [SiW 12 O 40 ] 4– , we isolate and structurally characterize Ra 2+ complexes of 18-crown-6 and the bis-picolinate macrocycle macropa, together with their Sr 2+ and Ba 2+ analogues. The resulting structures reveal systematic, size-dependent trends in coordination number and metal-donor distances across the alkaline earth series, notably this series also features the first reported Ra–N and Ra–O COO bonds. This work establishes POM-assisted crystallization as a robust approach for obtaining solid-state structural information on Ra 2+ complexes of organic chelators and provides a generalizable route for advancing the coordination chemistry of scarce, highly radioactive elements accessible only in trace quantities.

papers.title: Fully bio-based precursor for photocurable networks: synthesis and photopolymerization of furan-vegetable oil derivative
papers.abstract: The development of fully bio-based photocurable resins represents a promising sustainable alternative to conventional petroleum-derived materials. In this study, novel furan-based macromonomers were synthesized via a two-step synthetic route. The first step involved the transesterification of dimethyl 2,5-furandicarboxylate (DMFDCA) with dilinoleic diol (DD) using various catalysts, followed by methacrylation with methacryloyl chloride to introduce terminal vinyl functionalities. The chemical structures of the intermediates and final macromonomers were confirmed by 1 H NMR and FT-IR spectroscopy. Rheological characterization was conducted to evaluate flow behavior and processability. Thermal properties and phase behavior were investigated by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), revealing an amorphous and flexible polymer architecture with thermally induced crosslinking at elevated temperatures. Photopolymerization kinetics were analyzed using photo-DSC with different type-I photoinitiators under controlled UV irradiation conditions, while network formation was further evaluated through gel fraction analysis of photocured samples prepared under ambient conditions. Additionally, cytocompatibility studies were performed to assess the potential suitability of the materials for biomedical applications. Overall, this systematic investigation provides valuable insights into the design and synthesis of renewable, photocurable furan-based materials for advanced biomedical applications and sustainable manufacturing.

papers.title: Ultrafast Excited-State Proton Transfer Dynamics Using Linearized Pair-Density Functional Theory †
papers.abstract: Accurate simulation of excited-state bond rearrangement dynamics remains a major challenge since photoinduced reactions can often involve significant changes in electronic structure along excitedstate reaction pathways. Describing such processes requires an electronic structure method that provides balanced descriptions of all electronic states across nuclear configuration space, while remaining computationally feasible for molecular dynamics. Linearized pair-density functional theory (L-PDFT) provides an efficient multireference framework for excited-state simulations by enabling an accurate multi-state treatment of excited-state potential energy surfaces. In this work, we assess the performance of L-PDFT for excited-state bond-breaking dynamics using excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) as a stringent benchmark. Ab-initio molecular dynamics simulations are performed for 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline, a prototypical ESIPT system that undergoes ultrafast proton migration following photoexcitation. L-PDFT predicts that ESIPT for the molecule occurs within 16 fs, in close agreement with latest ultrafast time-resolved fluorescence experiments. Trajectory analysis reveals an active role of the proton in driving the ESIPT. These results demonstrate that L-PDFT can describe excited-state photodynamics involving bond rearrangements, highlighting its potential for broader light-driven chemical processes, including excited-state reactivity in photocatalytic transition metal-based systems

papers.title: Influence of dilinoleic succinate segments on the biodegradation of poly(butylene succinate-co-dilinoleic succinate) copolymers under composting and anaerobic digestion conditions
papers.abstract: Growing environmental and human health concerns associated with the persistence of nondegradable polymeric materials have intensified the global demand for sustainable alternatives. Consequently, research has increasingly focused on the development of bio-based and biodegradable polymers as a means to mitigate plastic pollution. In this context, the present study investigates the biodegradation behavior of poly(butylene succinate) (PBS) and poly(butylene succinate-co-dilinoleic succinate) (PBS-DLS) copolymers under mesophilic anaerobic digestion (AD) and thermophilic aerobic composting conditions. After 99 days of anaerobic incubation, the tested materials exhibited negligible mineralization and no significant mass loss, indicating limited biodegradability under oxygen-deficient conditions. In contrast, all materials underwent substantial degradation during thermophilic composting (97 days), with PBS-DLS 70-30 demonstrating the highest extent of mineralization-nearly twice that of PBS-and approximately 30% greater mass loss. Gel permeation chromatography (GPC)

papers.title: Recent Contributions of Organic Synthesis from Brazil. An Overview of the Period 2019-2025
Programmable chemical sensitivities scale with extent of reaction, not time
papers.abstract: The programmable oscillation of external energetic stimuli to drive a catalytic surface between distinct regimes of kinetic control has emerged as a strategy to surpass steady-state Sabatier limitations, yet experimental probes of the underlying kinetic origins of rate enhancement remain limited. Here, we demonstrate that chemical sensitivities such as apparent reaction orders, activation energies, and the Gibbs free energy, scale with reaction events (extent of reaction) under oscillatory conditions and not time. Using formic acid electro-oxidation on polycrystalline Pt as a model system, an analytical framework demonstrating that transient kinetic parameters are governed by reaction event weighting was developed, rather than time-weighted averages based on duty cycle. Experimentally observable charge transfer during potentiodynamic oscillations provided a direct and quantitative measure for the extent of reaction, enabling prediction of dynamic chemical sensitivities across a wide range of oscillation timescales (10 -3 - 10 1 Hz) and reaction conditions (285-305 K, 0.05-2.5 M HCOOH). The extent of reaction formalism accurately reconciled experimentally observed potentiodynamic reaction orders and activation barriers with steady-state behavior. Although developed for electrochemical potential oscillations, the extent of reaction weighting framework is universal and readily applicable to any catalytic system driven by programmable energetic stimuli (e.g. electrical, photonic, mechanical).

papers.title: Catalyst-Free, Autoinductive Photochemical Upcycling of Aromatic Polymers and Mixed Plastics via Autosensitization
papers.abstract: Photochemical upcycling of polymers is a promising strategy for mitigating the plastic-waste crisis; however, many recent advances have centered on developing new and often costly photocatalysts. In contrast, the auto-sensitized photoreactivity of aromatic polymers such as polystyrene (PS)-albeit documented for decades-has remained essentially unexploited for practical upcycling. Here we leverage this overlooked reactivity to develop a catalyst-free, autoinductive platform that converts PS into benzoic acid under visible light irradiation in air. The approach extends to other aromatic polymers including polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polycarbonate, polyether sulfone (PES), and epoxy resins, as well as biomass feedstocks such as lignin.
